commits.message:
test(plugins): split launcher and linked-home tests out of test_plugin_host

Move launcher selection, env expansion, multiplexing, and extraction-launcher
cases (18 test functions, 26 collected ids, plus _tagging_launch_host) into
tests/hermes_cli/test_plugin_host_launcher.py, and move linked, relative,
renamed, and repointed profile-home cases (22 test functions, 35 collected
ids, plus _marked_profile_linked_out_of_the_root and repointed_profile_link)
into tests/hermes_cli/test_plugin_host_linked_homes.py.

Keep core host RPC, import isolation, managed-scope pin, hosted provider,
async callback, subagent lifecycle, and failed/abandoned-load tests (12 test
functions, 15 collected ids) in tests/hermes_cli/test_plugin_host.py.

Every moved test, helper, fixture, constant, and platforms() marker moves
verbatim with no production or assertion changes. The 76 collected test ids
before and after map one to one across the three suites.

Refs #159450

test(plugins): extract shared plugin-host test setup into plugin_host_support

Move PROBE_PLUGIN, _home_with_plugins, MODEL_PROVIDER_PLUGIN, and
_hosted_model_provider out of tests/hermes_cli/test_plugin_host.py into
tests/hermes_cli/plugin_host_support.py so sibling plugin-host suites
and other tests no longer import helpers from a test module.

Update tests/hermes_cli/test_plugin_host.py and all five existing
importers (test_cron_plugin_api, test_plugin_home_moved,
test_plugin_host_prompt_sections, test_plugin_session_client,
test_plugin_session_turn_origin) to import from plugin_host_support.
No re-export shim is left in test_plugin_host.py.

fix(cli): decode raw arrows at the read, keep every other key as it was

Review of the first approach found two regressions from routing every
non-printable key through the menu-action decoder: a quick second Esc
was swallowed as an unknown sequence (the sessions filter stayed and a
later Enter picked a filtered row), and Ctrl+D became cancel (the plugins
checklist saved and exited on it).

read_key() now translates only ESC-prefixed input into the curses key it
encodes and leaves every other code untouched, so both pickers keep their
original dispatch. The delete confirmation prompt gets decoded arrows too.
The shared ESC decoder pushes a second ESC back instead of eating it.
The plugin test fake carries real KEY_UP/KEY_DOWN so base fails at the
assertion, not at constructing the nav table.

test: keep one raw-arrow invariant per picker

The up-arrow twins exercise the same decoder path as the down-arrow
cases; one red-on-base invariant per picker is enough.
fix(cli): decode raw CSI arrows in sessions and plugins pickers

test(plugins): share the dashboard moved-home tests' setup

The launch route, queued-request and Hermes-root dashboard tests each
installed the same plugin, wrote the same host config, linked the same
profile names and reset the same caches. One context manager,
_launch_dashboard_profiles, now does that and the manager cleanup;
each test keeps only its own link move (Greptile on #159450).

Test-only. The file collects the same 32 test ids before and after, all
pass, and the dashboard mutants of the launch route, the plugin-home
check and the host's load-time check are still caught.

fix(plugins): lend a start's launcher to an extraction its env build runs

3adc70d33b moved the child-env builder's import into the host's base
context. The first import reads the provider registry, which can run a
cold hosted-provider extraction. Outside a lent launcher, that
extraction picks its own in the base context, which binds no launch
scope for a single-profile TUI or dashboard start. It then ran under
the process env's launcher, not the one the start chose from the
launch scope.

The env build now runs under lending_launcher, as the ambient-credential
scan already did. The launch-body extraction test gains the case where
the start is the env builder's first importer.

Found by Sol (gpt-6.2-sol) reviewing 65528e060d.

fix(plugins): check a dashboard plugin's name after the host's queued releases

4560099171 checked a dashboard plugin path's home name before calling
_call, but _call first sends the releases queued by collected object
proxies, a blocking round trip to the host. A repoint during that wait
still sent the host the stale path.

_call takes a before_send hook that runs once the releases are flushed,
right before the method goes out, and asgi_request checks the path
there.

Found by Sol (gpt-6.2-sol) reviewing 4560099171.

fix(plugins): read the provider registry for the host's home at a cold env build

_env imported the child-env builder in the caller's context. The first
import of that module builds its provider blocklist from the registry,
which imports an in-process home's provider plugins. A start that was
that first import, called from a context bound to another profile whose
link had since been repointed, imported the other directory's provider
code, although the host's own home had just passed its check.

The import now runs inside the host's base context with the env build,
so the registry is read for the home the start checked.

Found by Sol (gpt-6.2-sol) reviewing 4560099171.

fix(plugins): check a dashboard plugin's home name right before the host loads it

A forwarded dashboard request looks its plugin up, then waits in its
profile's queue (up to 60 s), and the host may start cold, before the
host loads the plugin's path. The lookup's checks run at lookup time.
If the request came through a second live name for the home and the
name the path was read through was repointed meanwhile, the host
loaded the other directory's plugin code, while the request's own name
still passed (Greptile on #159450).

PluginHost.asgi_request, which both hosted routes call, now runs
refuse_moved_plugin_dir() on the path after the host is up and right
before it hands the host the path. Reading the plugin from the
verified directory instead is the structural fix, left for a
follow-up.

fix(dashboard): judge a launch plugin by the name its own path went through

2c729a11c0 refused the launch profile's hosted plugin whenever the
process's own home name had moved. Launch discovery also scans the
Hermes root's plugins, whose paths never go through that name. After
the launch link ops is renamed to ops2, a request through ops2 for a
plugin installed in the root was refused even though its path still
leads where it did (Greptile on #159450).

plugin_isolation.refuse_moved_plugin_dir() checks the home a dashboard
plugin's directory was read through. Discovery builds that directory
as <home>/plugins/<plugin>/dashboard from the name it scanned. A
profile-local copy is still judged by the process's home name, and a
root or bundled copy by its own tree.

fix(plugins): check a host start's name again before its provider scan

7b27aec0c7 moved _env's check from before the ambient-credential scan
to before the child's env is built, leaving the scan itself unchecked.
The build reads through the name, and the provider layer rereads the
plugin dirs once its stamp check is due (1 s). A link repointed while
the build ran therefore let the scan import the other directory's
provider code into Hermes before the start's final check refused it
(Greptile on #159450).

_env keeps both checks: before the build and again before the scan.
The ambient-credential test gains a repoint during the build, with the
stamp check made due as a long build would.

fix(plugins): refuse a host start before it builds the child's env

22970d3213 checked a start's home name before the ambient-credential
scan, but building the child's env reads the provider registry
earlier. The first import of tools.environments.local builds its
blocklist from PROVIDER_REGISTRY, and the registry's first read lists
the bound home's provider plugins. Either read imports them through
the name, in Hermes for an in-process home, so a link repointed before
the start loaded the other directory's provider code before the start
refused (Greptile on #159450). The test also showed it for a process
whose registry had not been read yet.

_env now checks the name first, before it imports the env builder or
builds anything. The ambient-credential test is parametrized for a
process that has not imported the env builder yet.

fix(dashboard): check the launch home's name after the plugin lookup

2c729a11c0 checked the launch discovery name before the lookup read
the plugin list through it. When the launch home has a second live
name and a request comes through that one, the discovery name can be
repointed after the check while the lookup reads through it. The
lookup then picks the other directory's plugin, and the request's own
name still passes requested_plugin_host().

The check now runs after the lookup's last read through the name, just
before the paths go to a host, so it catches a repoint before the
lookup or during it. The reads before it only stat and parse manifests.

Found by Sol (gpt-6.2-sol) reviewing 2c729a11c0.

fix(dashboard): forward no launch plugin once the launch home's name moved

The dashboard's hosted plugin routes forward the launch profile's copy
of a plugin, which discovery always reads through the process's own
home name (get_process_hermes_home). Suppose the launch link ops is
renamed to ops2 and ops is reused for another directory. A request
through ops2 still counts as launch-profile traffic, because both
names share the remembered key, and it passes 72d4f17a4b's check on
its own name. Discovery meanwhile reads the other directory through
ops, so that directory's plugin code ran in ops2's host with its
environment.

_hosted_plugin_for_request now refuses with PluginHomeMoved when the
process's home name leads elsewhere than the directory the process
opened it as, whichever name the request came through.
plugin_isolation's check takes the home to check
(refuse_moved_home), so the active-home callers and this one share it.

Found by Sol (gpt-6.2-sol) reviewing 2a337e908e.

fix(dashboard): rescan a profile's plugins cached through a moved name

The dashboard caches a secondary profile's plugin list under the key
the process remembered for its home, with each plugin's path read
through the name it scanned. After a linked profile ops is renamed to
ops2 and the name ops is reused for another directory, a request
through ops2 passes 72d4f17a4b's check, since ops2 leads where it
always did, and is then handed the cached paths through ops: the other
directory's plugin code, run in ops2's host with its environment. The
cache predates this PR; 72d4f17a4b closed the same harm only for a
request through the reused name.

Each cached list now keeps the home it was scanned through, and a
lookup rescans when that name leads elsewhere than the directory the
process remembered. A profile reached through two live links keeps
its cache.

Found by Sol (gpt-6.2-sol) reviewing a342cfe657.

fix(plugins): treat a home removed before its first discovery as removed

ae4c106072 refuses a name that leads to no directory once the manager
has seen its directory, but only a lookup recorded that. A manager
opened for an existing directory that was removed before discovery
first looked it up (the background discovery thread) still took it
for a home not created yet, and discovery ran there (Greptile on
#159450).

The manager now records whether its directory exists when it opens.
A home that has never existed still discovers plugins.

test(plugins): share the moved-home extraction tests' provider setup

Both extraction tests wrote the same stand-in launcher, installed the
hostmodel provider by hand and wrote the same host config. Only the
moment the link moves differs. _hosted_provider_behind_a_launcher now
does that setup, reusing test_plugin_host's _hosted_model_provider
(Greptile on #159450). The file still runs the same 14 tests (20
cases), all passing before and after, and the re-check before
subprocess.run still fails a test when removed.

fix(plugins): give no shared host to a request through a moved profile name

Since 20d19b4537, managers are found by the key the process remembered
for a name. A linked profile renamed while the process runs (ops to
ops2) keeps its manager, which runs under the new name with that
profile's environment. If the old name is then reused for another
directory, a request through it reaches that same manager.

Callers that take the manager's host also hand it plugin paths read
through their own name, which is now the other directory's: the
dashboard's hosted plugin API (both the secondary-profile route and
the launch route) and the category loaders' user_plugin_host(). That
ran the other directory's plugin code in the renamed profile's host,
with its environment (Greptile on #159450). transient_plugin_host()
keyed the remembered directory the same way.

plugin_isolation.requested_plugin_host() now refuses with
PluginHomeMoved when the active home's name leads elsewhere than the
directory the process opened it as. user_plugin_host() and both
dashboard sites go through it, and transient_plugin_host() runs the
same check first. The renamed profile still reaches its host.
Lookups that hand the host no request paths (discovery, loads and
hooks of already loaded plugins) are unchanged.

fix(plugins): refuse a profile directory removed or renamed after it was seen

_leads_here compares a name's real path with the manager's directory.
os.path.realpath does not need the path to exist, so a plain profile
directory's name still resolved to itself after the directory was
removed or renamed away. It therefore read as leading to the manager's
directory, and discovery ran there with no profile left: bundled and
project plugins loaded under a home that no longer exists. A link's
target directory removed from under it passed the same way.
PluginHomeMoved says "renamed or removed"; for those it never fired.

Once the manager has seen its directory through a name, a name that
leads to no directory no longer leads there, and owner_home refuses.
A home not created yet (a first run, a profile being created) is still
accepted, as before.

Found by Sol (gpt-6.2-sol) reviewing 513e598f2e.

fix(plugins): refuse a host start before it scans a moved home's providers

A host start reads which providers take ambient credentials with
list_providers() in the host's context, which this PR binds to the
profile's name. That call rescans the home's provider plugins through
the name and imports them, into Hermes itself for a home whose
plugins.isolation is in_process. 5954d9f98c checks the name only after
the child's env is built, as reads have no effect until Popen. This
read runs code: a link repointed before the scan imported the other
directory's provider plugins into Hermes, and the start then refused.

The start now checks the name right before that scan and refuses with
PluginHomeMoved. A repoint landing during the scan itself is left, like
the window between the start's last check and Popen. Provider lookups
by other bodies bound to a moved name are left as well (restart
required).

Found by Sol (gpt-6.2-sol) reviewing 513e598f2e.

fix(plugins): keep a host context stale until a check after its build passes

513e598f2e marked a host's base context stale only when a start's last
check refused. A context is built through the profile's name, so it
holds the other directory's secrets whenever the link was repointed
during the build. Two more paths kept such a context:

- The rebuild cleared the flag as soon as it finished. A start that then
  failed before its last check, because the other directory's
  plugins.host.launcher did not parse, left a context marked fresh.
- The context built with the host was never checked. The first start
  then refused in owner_home while the link led elsewhere, and once it
  led back the start reused the context.

In both cases, once the link led back, the next start kept the context
and parent-side plugin calls with no caller ran with the other
directory's secrets.

A rebuild now marks the context stale until the start's last check
passes. Construction checks the name right after its build, so a host
built through a moved name rebuilds at its first start. The refusal no
longer sets the flag itself, because every context it could find is
already marked. An unmoved host still builds its context once.

Found by Sol (gpt-6.2-sol) reviewing 513e598f2e.

fix(plugins): rebuild a host's context after a refused start

A start that moves to a new profile name rebuilds the host's base
context, whose secret scope under multiplexing is read from the
profile's .env through that name. When 5954d9f98c refused such a start
because the link was repointed meanwhile, the rebuilt context still
held what the other directory's .env held. Once the link led back, the
next start found the same name and skipped the rebuild. Parent-side
plugin calls with no caller then ran with the other directory's
secrets.

A refused start now marks the context stale, and the next start
rebuilds it.

Found by Sol (gpt-6.2-sol) reviewing 5954d9f98c.

fix(plugins): check an extraction's home again after it picks its launcher

83a679ba48 refuses an extraction whose home name already leads
elsewhere when it starts. Picking the launcher still reads the home's
config and .env through that name, so a link repointed during the
pick ran the chosen launcher, and the extraction child, on the other
directory. That includes an extraction a host start runs while it
builds its child's env, before the start's own check.

The extraction now checks the name again right before subprocess.run
and refuses the same way.

Found by Sol (gpt-6.2-sol) reviewing 83a679ba48.

fix(plugins): refuse a host start whose name moved while it read through it

ensure_started checks that the profile's name leads to the manager's
directory once, when it reads owner_home. Its context, launcher and
child env are then built by reading through that name. A link
repointed in between made the start read the replacement directory's
config and .env, and launch a host there with the original profile's
credentials (Greptile on #159450).

The start now re-checks the name after its last read (the child's env)
and before Popen, and refuses with PluginHomeMoved if the name leads
elsewhere. No host process starts. A host already running keeps
reading through its name. That is a separate design question and is
not changed here.

fix(plugins): refuse a provider extraction whose home name was repointed

A model-provider extraction outside a host start takes get_hermes_home()
as its home and never goes through the plugin manager, so 843ea093ee's
refusal never reached it. is_launch_home compares the name's remembered
key with the launch key. After the launch profile's link is repointed,
the name still counts as the launch home, and launcher_for expanded the
new directory's plugins.host.launcher with the launch profile's values
and ran it (Greptile on #159450).

_extract now refuses with an error payload when the name leads to
another directory than the one the process remembered it by
(plugin_isolation.home_moved_refusal). providers logs the error as it
does any failed extraction, and the failure is not cached.

test(plugins): a sibling name served elsewhere is not taken over

_leads_here requires a name's remembered key to equal the manager's
directory as well as its real path, so a renamed profile's manager
never takes a name the process already serves another directory
under. The test that guarded that clause pinned the old fallback and
was replaced in 843ea093ee. Without the clause, a manager whose own
name is gone adopts such a sibling, and plugin code bound to it
registers under the other directory's key.

The new test catches the clause's removal. The rest of the plugin host
and moved-home suites pass without it.

fix(plugins): test a name against the manager's directory, not its scope key

A profile-hook manager from transient_plugin_host suffixes its
scope_key with "#transient-<id>" so overlapping hook loads never share
registry slots. Its home_path stays the profile's directory. The
equality shortcut that 8b662c58fd removed was the only thing that
accepted that manager's name. Without it, _leads_here compared the
name's real path with the suffixed key, so every hosted profile hook
was refused with PluginHomeMoved. That failed 8 tests in
test_memory_provider_seams_hosted.py.

_leads_here now compares against home_path, the directory's key.

docs(plugins): say where a reused profile name's plugin requests go

The manager lookup's docstring said a repointed name always reaches a
manager that refuses. When a linked profile is renamed and its old name
is reused for another profile, the old name instead reaches the renamed
profile's manager, which runs under the new name, until a restart. Say
so.

Raised by Sol (gpt-6.2-sol) reviewing 20d19b4537.

fix(plugins): key a relative home by the directory it names now

hermes_home_key remembers a key per path text. A relative home, such as
a symbolic profile id bound as a home, therefore kept the directory it
named from the first working directory. A lookup from another working
directory reused that first manager and its plugins.

The manager lookup now makes the home absolute (links left unresolved)
before taking its key, so each working directory gets the directory the
name means there.

Found by Sol (gpt-6.2-sol) reviewing 20d19b4537.

fix(plugins): check a plain profile directory's live target too

owner_home accepted the name a manager was opened by without checking
it whenever that name equalled the manager's directory, meaning the
home was a plain directory. Now that managers are found by the
remembered key, a profile directory replaced by a link while the
process runs reached its old manager, which then read the link
target's plugins under the replaced directory's key.

Every name now has to lead to the manager's directory, so that manager
refuses (PluginHomeMoved). An unmoved plain directory still passes,
because its real path and remembered key both equal the directory.

Found by Sol (gpt-6.2-sol) reviewing 20d19b4537.

fix(plugins): find a repointed profile's manager by the key it was opened under

get_plugin_manager() cached managers under the active home's live
target. A profile link repointed while the process ran therefore never
reached the manager it was opened by, which now refuses. If the new
target had been opened as its own home, the moved name reused that
home's manager and ran plugin work under the other home's name. If not,
the moved name created a refusing manager under the target's key, and
the target's own requests were then refused.

Managers are now cached under the home's remembered key
(hermes_home_key), the key the rest of the process already serves that
spelling by. A request through a repointed link finds the manager it
was opened by, which refuses, and the target's manager is untouched in
both orders.

Found by Sol (gpt-6.2-sol) reviewing 843ea093ee.

fix(plugins): refuse plugin work once no profile name leads to its directory

A linked profile's plugin manager runs plugin code under the profile's
name, because a marked profile whose directory is a link out of the
Hermes root is found by that name only. When no name led to the
manager's directory any more, owner_home fell back to the directory
itself. That happens when the link is repointed after the process
remembered its key, renamed out of the root, or removed. The directory
alone reads as an unmarked profile, so the run-elsewhere marker went
unseen and a marked profile's own launcher ran (Greptile on #159450).

owner_home now raises PluginHomeMoved in that state. Discovery, loads,
plugin ctx calls and host starts are refused until a restart opens the
profile again. Unloading still runs, under the directory, because it
stops plugin work. A host restarted after a crash unloads its plugins
and logs the refused reload instead of raising from its thread.

The tests that pinned the fallback now pin the refusal. The test of a
start's launcher check moves the start's name mid-start instead,
because a start with no name is now refused before it builds anything.

refactor(env): resolve names kept live in the one dotenv line loop

9911054aa0 added _resolve_pinned_assignments, a second copy of
_resolve_dotenv_assignments' line-by-line ${VAR} expansion with a live
chain beside it, so a fix to one loop could leave startup and plugin
host starts expanding a .env differently. _resolve_dotenv_assignments
now takes the optional live_env and live_names itself: each line is also
expanded the way a load against live_env would, a marked name takes
that value, later lines see it, and live_env takes the file's live
values for the next layer. A bare key (no value) is recorded as None
before any lookup is built, as the old loop did. Callers that pass
neither are unchanged.

The kept-live test gains a marked name both set in the environment and
assigned by an earlier line, then referenced: the earlier line wins.
Without it, a mutant letting the environment beat earlier lines
survived in the live chain and in the plain override order.

refactor(plugins): choose a host's launcher in plugin_isolation

b5e2a1dd03 had plugin_host_profiles import plugin_host for the
extraction's launcher, while plugin_host already imports
plugin_host_profiles: a cycle, where the repo's rule puts a shared name
in a lower module. The launcher choice moves next to host_launcher in
plugin_isolation, which both already import: is_launch_home,
launcher_for (no longer handed host_launcher, which now lives beside
it), extraction_launcher, and the start's lend as lending_launcher. No
behaviour changes.

fix(plugins): ask the marker again before an extraction takes its start's launcher

A host start lends the launcher it chose to the cold provider
extraction it runs while building the child's env (f8c6a0bab7). The
extraction used it without asking the run-elsewhere marker, where the
extraction on main and on b5e2a1dd03 asked it at extraction time. A
profile marked between the start's choice and the extraction had its
extraction run under its own plugins.host.launcher.

extraction_launcher now takes the lent launcher only while the home
still runs here; a marked home gets a fresh choice, which is the
managed overlay's launcher alone.

test(plugins): share the hosted model-provider setup in the host tests

A host start with no extraction cached extracts the profile's hosted

there. Inside a launch-profile body that is not multiplexed (the TUI
gateway binds one even single-profile), the start reads its launcher
through the launch scope, the .env as it is now, while the host's
context binds no scope and the second choice read the process env, as
loaded before a .env edit: two launchers for one start.

still chooses for itself.

fix(plugins): extract hosted providers under the launcher their host start chose

A host start with no extraction cached extracts the profile's hosted
model providers while it builds the child's env, from the host's own
context. That extraction called host_launcher() there, while the start
itself chose its launcher through _launcher_for. The host's context
holds the profile's secret scope only while multiplexing is
process-wide, so under task-local multiplexing (the desktop cron ticker)
the extraction expanded the profile's launcher ${VAR}s against the

value built from ${HERMES_HOME} could point into another profile while
its host child starts in the selected home.

resolves, in the lookup and in a marked line's live expansion, as the

The previous commit kept a process-global key's live expansion only when
the .env assigns it. A line naming a global the .env never sets, one the
process env holds alone, still resolved it against the frozen launch env,
while the launcher and the host child read the live value.

With live_names, resolve_home_dotenv now takes every marked name in its
lookup from the live env, set or unset there, before the file's lines.

fix(plugins): let a launch .env line see a process-global key's live value

profile's .env on the live env with a second pass, after the frozen pass
had already expanded the lines naming it. RUNNER_CWD=${TERMINAL_CWD}
therefore held the frozen expansion while TERMINAL_CWD held the live one,
in the host child's env and in the launcher's scope alike.

resolve_home_dotenv takes live_names: with a lookup env, a name it marks
takes the value the plain live resolution gives it (through earlier lines
and the home layer before the managed one), and later lines see that
value. _expand_dotenv_templates marks the process-global names when it
resolves against a template env, in place of the second pass.

fix(plugins): keep a host child's process-global .env keys on the live env

The previous commit gave the launch host's child env the frozen launch
env its launcher's .env templates resolved against. That also froze a
templated process-global key (TERMINAL_*, say), which the launcher reads
from os.environ through get_secret, as the last dotenv reload resolved
it: after a reload the child held the frozen value and the launcher the
reloaded one.

_expand_dotenv_templates resolves a process-global key against the live
env even when a template_env is given, so the child holds what the
launcher's read returns. Only the plugin host passes a template_env.

fix(plugins): resolve a launch host's .env once for its launcher and child

Under multiplexing the launch profile's host launcher resolved the
profile's .env templates against the launch env frozen when multiplexing
began, while the host child's env, built a moment later for the same

that another profile's task changed since gave the launcher and its child
two values for one setting.

the start passes that same mapping to served_profile_child_env and the
ambient-credential overlay (template_env=). launch_secret_scope takes
the mapping (template_env=) instead of deciding it from a flag, so the
plugin host reads the frozen env once per start.

launch_template_env peels the frozen launch env by the dotenv record
frozen with it: a name whose value equals what the launch .env once
published goes back to its pre-dotenv value. A secret source that holds
the name in the snapshot and rotates to that same value was taken for

fix(plugins): freeze the launch env and its dotenv record under the loader's lock

capture_launch_env copied os.environ and then the dotenv publication
record without the dotenv loader's lock. A launch .env reload landing
between the two copies paired the frozen env with the reload's record,
which no longer recognises the frozen values, so the launcher's .env
templates resolved against stale dotenv output until the process
restarted (Greptile on 9eb6c81a6c; Sol's S8 nit on 6509e6c1ce, which I
had declined).

both copies, taken before the module's own _lock; env_loader documents
that order and never calls into launch_profile_policy while holding its
lock. Later captures return the snapshot under _lock alone, as before.
dotenv_publication_record copies under the same re-entrant lock.

caller the choice is unchanged: the process env for the launch profile
outside multiplexing, its own scope otherwise.

test_a_host_started_inside_the_launch_profiles_bound_scope_takes_its_
launcher_value_from_it fails on 6d69a64015 ('${PLUGIN_RUNNER}' not found)
and passes on main and here. test_a_caller_bound_to_another_profile_lends_
its_scope_to_no_other_profiles_launcher pins the other side: both rows
fail on main and on a mutant that lends any bound scope; the launch row
fails on one that lends an unstamped scope to every profile.

test(plugins): wait for the restarted host to reload before counting launchers

The crash-restart test stopped waiting once the launcher script logged its
run, before the Python child answered hello or reloaded the plugin, so it
could pass with a host that never came back (Greptile on 7bb619bb8a).

Wait for the plugin's reload instead, check it carries no error and that
hostprobe_pid answers from a new pid, then compare the counts. The rows
still fail where they did: [secondary] on 270e37621f ((1, 1) == (2, 0)),
[launch] on ab028cc238 ('${PLUGIN_RUNNER}' not found).

fix(plugins): read the launch profile's launcher files through its current name

d91acd10e8 built a renamed launch profile's launcher scope with
owner_secret_scope(<the process's own path>), so after the rename its
files were read through the old name, which leads nowhere: a value only
the launch profile's .env held stayed a literal ${VAR} on a crash
restart, and an .env edit was ignored for the frozen env value (Sol on
5e8d9a7038).

Build launch_secret_scope(home) once the start's directory is known to be
the launch profile's: the launch env, with the files read through the
name that leads there now.

The rename test now also takes a launcher value only the launch profile's
.env holds: red on 18510dfbf2 (the restart passed '${RUNNER_TAG}'), green
here. It fails on main at the first start, whose multiplexed launcher read
only the process env (a real process loads that file into it at start).

fix(plugins): read a sibling profile's launcher from its own files outside multiplexing

4450d0a128 chose the launcher scope by is_multiplex_active() inside the
fresh context. A process that is not a multiplexer still serves a sibling
in a task (the desktop backend's cron ticker marks it with
set_multiplex_context), and that task-local flag does not reach a fresh
context: such a host start read the sibling's launcher against the
process env, the launch profile's value for the name (Sol on 5e8d9a7038).
Main kept the caller's scope there.

Decide by whose profile the start is for instead: a profile a plugin runs
elsewhere, and the launch profile outside multiplexing, read the process
env; any other profile expands through its own secrets whatever the
flag; the launch profile under multiplexing through its own scope.

The test starts a sibling's host under task-local multiplexing with its
variable in its .env and a different value in the process env: red on
0d64a03a7b (the launch value ran), green on main and here.

test(plugins): pin a single-profile launcher to the process env

7bb619bb8a expanded every launcher through owner_secret_scope, so outside
multiplexing the launch profile's launcher read its .env again at each
host start: an .env edited after the process loaded it picked a
different launcher for a crash restart (Greptile on 7bb619bb8a).
4450d0a128 already restored main's lookup there (the process env, with
only the home bound); this pins it.

The test starts a single-profile host whose launcher variable differs
between the process env and the .env file: red on 7bb619bb8a (the file's
runner ran), green on main and here.

test(plugins): pin the absolute name of a manager opened by a relative one

The relative-home test passed with the .absolute() in
PluginManager.__init__ removed: once the working directory moved, the
relative name led nowhere, the manager fell back to the resolved
directory, and that is all the test looked at (Sol on 7bb619bb8a).

Open a marked profile linked out of the root by a relative ops, move the
working directory, and assert plugin code still finds the marker, which
only the name under the root leads to. With .absolute() removed it reads
False; the old test still passes there.

fix(plugins): keep the launch profile's launcher keys after its link is renamed

Under multiplexing 7bb619bb8a expands a launcher through owner_secret_scope
of the start's home, which decides the launch profile by comparing that
path with the process's own. After the launch profile's link is renamed,
the manager answers to the new name, the process still names its profile
by the old path, and owner_secret_scope took the new name for another
profile: the launch env was dropped, so a crash restart left an env-only
${VAR} literal (Sol on 7bb619bb8a). Main read the process env there.

Decide the launch profile the way serves_routed_profile does, by the
process's remembered key for its own path, and build the launch profile's
scope (launch env plus files) when the start's home keys the same
directory.

The test renames the link of a multiplexed launch profile whose launcher
variable only the launch env holds, then kills its host without updating
the process's own path: red on 4450d0a128 (the restarted host's load fails
on '${PLUGIN_RUNNER}'), green on main and here.

fix(plugins): expand a marked profile's managed launcher against the process env

7bb619bb8a expanded every launcher's ${VAR}s through a scope built for the
start's home. For a profile a plugin runs elsewhere, host_launcher takes
the launcher from the managed overlay alone, and #156725 specifies that its
refs expand against the process env, as for any profile
(test_a_managed_launcher_expands_its_env_refs_for_a_marked_profile_too).
Under multiplexing a variable only the process env held therefore stayed
literal: FileNotFoundError '${PLUGIN_RUNNER}' at the host start (Sol on
7bb619bb8a).

Bind a profile's own secrets for the launcher only where the process env
is the wrong source: under multiplexing, for a profile run on this host.
A marked profile, and every start outside multiplexing, expand against
the process env again, with only the home bound, as on main. That also
keeps single-profile launchers on the values main read (the managed and
project dotenv layers the process loaded), which a rebuilt scope does not
replay.

The test starts a marked profile's host under multiplexing with the
managed launcher's variable in the process env only: red on 7bb619bb8a,
green on main and here.

fix(plugins): read a host launcher's variables from its own profile

270e37621f chose the host launcher in the caller's context with only the
home rebound, so its ${VAR}s expanded through whatever the caller had
bound. A crash restart runs on a bare thread with nothing bound, where
config expansion reads os.environ: under multiplexing a secondary
profile's launcher variable from its .env stopped expanding, or took the
launch profile's value for the same name (Greptile on 270e37621f; the
same as main, whose launcher read the caller's context too).

Choose the launcher in a fresh context bound to the start's home and its
own secrets (bind_state with owner_secret_scope, not hydrated, no
terminal policy): the launch profile's env-only keys and files, any other
profile's own files. The answer no longer depends on who started the host.
Single-profile values are unchanged: the user .env already overrides shell
exports in os.environ, as launch_secret_scope does.

The test runs a real crash restart under multiplexing in two rows: a
secondary with the variable in its .env and a different launch value (red
on 270e37621f and main: the launch runner ran) and the launch profile with
an env-only variable (red on ab028cc238: '${PLUGIN_RUNNER}' not found).
It replaces the test that bound a hand-built caller scope.

fix(plugins): expand a host launcher's variables in the caller's scope

ab028cc238 chose the host launcher inside the host's own context so its
config would be read in the home the start took. That context holds only
the profile's own secrets (build_profile_secret_scope), so under
multiplexing a launcher written as ${VAR} whose value only the caller's
scope holds (a launch profile's env-only keys: systemd Environment=, op
run) no longer expanded, and the literal placeholder reached
subprocess: FileNotFoundError '${PLUGIN_RUNNER}' (Greptile on ab028cc238).

Choose it with only the home rebound to the one the start took
(_plugin_home_scope, the binding plugin code runs under): config is still
read there, and ${VAR}s expand through the caller's secret scope as they
did before ab028cc238. Not
owner_secret_scope() per start, which would rebuild the profile's secrets,
external sources included, at every host start and crash restart.

fix(plugins): read a host's launcher config in the home it starts in

_argv chose the launcher with host_launcher(home=...), which reads
plugins.host.launcher (and expands its variables) through the caller's
binding. A load binds the profile name it read, and a rename can retire
that name before the load starts the host: the start then took the new
name for its context, environment and working directory, but the launcher
lookup still read config under the old name, which now fails with
"Named profile home does not exist". Main bound the resolved directory
for loads, so its caller binding never went stale.

Run the launcher choice in the start's own context, which binds the home
the start took. Found in the sol-loop review of 01b93a32c5.

fix(plugins): bind a profile name only while its remembered key agrees

hermes_home_key remembers the key each path text first resolved to. When a
profile's link is repointed from one directory to another in a running
process, the new directory gets its own manager (managers are keyed by a
fresh resolve), but owner_home still returned the link's name, whose
remembered key is the old directory's. Plugin code bound to that name ran
under the old directory's key: implicit registry lookups and anything else
keyed by hermes_home_key() went to the wrong profile. Main bound the
resolved directory there and got the new key.

A name now leads to the manager's directory only when the process's
remembered key for it agrees as well; otherwise owner_home falls back to
the directory, as main binds. Found in the sol-loop review of 01b93a32c5.

fix(plugins): ask about a host's launcher for the home its start took

ensure_started reads the manager's owner_home once and builds the host's
environment and working directory from it, but _argv read owner_home
again for the launcher's run-elsewhere check. Since owner_home follows a
profile's name, a name that appeared between the two reads (a link made
while the host was starting) gave one start two homes: the launcher was
judged for the new name, the environment for the directory.

Use the home the start took. Reported by Greptile on 9e7a40f2f8.

test(plugins): give the uppercase rename case no extra sibling link

The uppercase case also fell into the branch that adds a sibling link
leading to the profile's directory, so it did not need adoption of Ops2 to
pass on every volume. Add sibling links only for the cases about them; the
case is still red on 248ff26dea and green after 2aba283105.

fix(plugins): read a renamed profile's name as the marker lookup does

60cfaa1f03 matched profile ids against the on-disk name. The marker lookup
lowercases a name first (a case-insensitive volume opens any case), so a
link renamed to Ops2 and marked as ops2 was rejected as a candidate, the
manager fell back to the directory, and the restarted host used the
profile's own launcher. Check the lowercased name, and keep the on-disk
path for binding.

fix(plugins): keep looking for a profile name after a lookup found none

ec62cbb8cb remembered the directory itself when no name led to it, so
after a lookup that ran while the profile's link was missing, the manager
never looked again. A link that came back and was marked under a new name
went unseen, and the restarted host used the profile's own launcher.

Keep the old name on a fallback, so a later lookup searches again. Only a
name that was found is remembered.

fix(plugins): adopt only a live profile id as a renamed profile's name

ec62cbb8cb took the first entry under profiles/ that leads to the
manager's directory as the profile's new name. An entry the marker lookup
does not read as a named profile (an id it rejects, such as _backup, or
default) sorted ahead of the real name gave the marker check the wrong
root, so a profile marked under its new name was told it runs here and the
restarted host used its own launcher again. A tombstoned entry made every
config load under the binding fail, and the restart never served.

Adopt only an entry whose name is a profile id (PROFILE_ID_RE), not
default and not deleted.

fix(plugins): resolve only the profile home in a hosted provider's address

2c8046d88d addressed a hosted model provider by its fully resolved
directory. That also followed a plugin's own install link, so after such a
plugin was removed (its link deleted, its target left behind) the
restarted host loaded it again from the target. Main failed there, at the
missing install path.

Resolve only the profile home's own spelling and keep the plugin's path
below it as installed. A plugin outside the home keeps its path as given.

fix(plugins): compare install-record parents by canonical path, not file id

b65a110095 compared a plugin's parent with the plugins dir by
os.path.samefile. A filesystem that reports file id 0 for every directory
(FAT, some network mounts) would equate two distinct directories on one
volume and attach the wrong installer record. Compare canonical paths
(realpath, normcase) instead. No red test on Linux, which has no such
filesystem in a temp dir; the linked-profile recall test still covers the
comparison.

fix(plugins): follow a linked profile's new name after a rename

After a linked profile is renamed while a process keeps its manager,
`owner_home` fell back to the profile's directory. A marker is found by
name only, so when the profile was then marked to run elsewhere under
its new name, the restarted plugin host asked about the directory, was
told the profile runs here, and started under the profile's own
launcher with its own `.env`.

When the name the manager was opened by no longer leads to its
directory, take the other named profile under the same `profiles/` dir
that does, which is the name a rename left. Fall back to the directory
only when no name leads there, and remember the answer so a name that
is gone for good isn't searched for at every bind. The rename test now
also covers a removed link.

test(plugins): drop the directly called lambda in the rename test

Python lints failed on 9e61d03cfc with ruff's unnecessary-direct-lambda-call
in the wait for the restarted host. Use a named helper instead.

fix(plugins): retry a host's new home after its context failed to build

A start that moves the plugin host to the manager's current home set
`_home` before building that home's context. When the build raised (the
profile's secret scope unreadable), the next start saw the home
unchanged, skipped the build and started the host with the context of
the home it had left: the old link name, gone after a rename.

Put the previous home back when the build raises, so the next start
builds the context again.

fix(plugins): tell a plugin its profile from the host it loads into

`PluginHost.load` computed the plugin's `ctx.profile_name` from the base
context before `ensure_started`, which is where a start now takes the
manager's current home. After a linked profile is renamed and the host
crashes, the first plugin the restart reloads was told the old profile
name while the new host, and every later load, ran under the directory.

Compute it after the host has started, in the context of that host.

fix(plugins): address hosted provider overrides by the resolved plugin dir

A hosted model-provider profile's overrides run in the plugin host,
addressed by the plugin's directory, and the host loads the plugin from
that path on first use after each start. The proxy kept the directory as
discovery spelled it. Once this PR binds the host's start to the
profile's name, a provider first discovered there carries the link
spelling, so after the link is renamed the restarted host is sent a path
that no longer exists and every override call fails. Main has the same
gap for providers discovered outside a manager's scope through a link
spelling, which is the path the new test takes.

Address the proxy by the resolved directory, as the extraction already
does for its argv and cache key.

fix(plugins): give the provider extraction child the home as named

The one-shot model-provider extraction imports the provider plugin in a
child process started with `HERMES_HOME` set to the resolved home. For
a marked profile whose directory is a link out of the Hermes root, code
in that child asked the run-elsewhere marker about a directory with no
marker folder above it and was told the profile runs here, while the
plugin host and the parent ask by name.

Pass the absolute home with links kept. It is still absolute, which the
child needs because it starts in the home.

fix(plugins): find a linked profile's install records from its plugin paths

Since the previous commit, discovery records user plugins under the
manager's resolved directory while plugin code runs under the name the
profile was opened by. `_install_record` compared the plugin's parent
with the plugins dir as text, so for a profile whose home is a link the
two spellings never matched and every installer record was missed. The
load-time kill-list check then skipped recalls matched only by the
recorded repo or catalog name, and the login-backend gate refused
verified catalog installs. Main and the PR's earlier heads used one
spelling on both sides.

Compare the parent as a directory (`os.path.samefile`). The record is
still keyed by the plugin directory's own name, and only a direct child
of the current home's plugins dir qualifies.

fix(plugins): stop binding a linked profile's old name after a rename

A process keeps one plugin manager per resolved directory. When a
profile whose home is a link is renamed while the process runs (the
dashboard, a multiplexed gateway), the next request for the new name
gets the same manager, still holding the old name. The manager kept
binding that name for discovery, a plugin's calls and the plugin host,
and discovery had recorded each user plugin's path through it. After a
host crash, the restart reloaded every plugin from a path that no
longer exists, and the plugin's tools were gone until the process
restarted. On main the manager bound the resolved directory and
recovered.

- `owner_home` is now a property. It returns the name while that name
  still leads to the manager's directory, and the directory itself
  once it doesn't. A marked profile is still found by its name, and a
  marker does not follow a rename by design.
- The plugin host takes its home at each start, not only when it is
  first built.
- Discovery reads user plugins from `home_path`, so a plugin's path
  survives a rename of the link, as it did on main.

A host already running when the link is renamed keeps the old name in
its environment until it restarts.

fix(plugins): keep a manager's owner home on the directory it opened for

`owner_home` kept the home exactly as given. A symbolic profile id bound
as a home is a relative path, so each scope the manager bound later
resolved it against the working directory of that moment, while
`home_path` (the registries' key) was resolved once, when the manager
opened.

The gateway tests that open sessions for symbolic ids run in tmp_path
(`authority_cwd_in_tmp`). Plugin loads that ran once the working
directory was the checkout again bound `<checkout>/<id>`, and the
checkout-home guard failed five gateway test files on CI. A local run
also left `owned/` and `fixture/` home skeletons in the checkout.

Make it absolute at construction with `Path.absolute()`, which leaves
links unresolved, so a marked profile linked out of the root is still
found by its name.

fix(plugins): run a marked profile's plugin code under the name it was opened by

#156725 refuses to run a profile that a plugin runs elsewhere, and asks the
marker by the home's name. b912bfb00e7 passed that name (owner_home) to
host_launcher() for the plugin host's argv only. The plugin manager still
bound home_path, the resolved directory, around discovery, loading,
unload and a plugin's calls, and PluginHost._home was home_path too. For
profiles/<name> linking to a directory outside the Hermes root, code under
those bindings asks the marker about a directory with no marker folder
above it, and is told the profile runs here:

- A model-provider plugin's extraction (plugin_host_profiles._extract)
  started the launcher the profile's own config.yaml names. It runs while
  a bundled plugin loads (its imports list the providers) and when the
  host starts (_hosted_ambient_credentials). `hermes -p ops tools list`,
  `profile list` and `memory status` each started it once with a cold
  extraction cache.
- The host child's environment was built from that directory's .env,
  which reads as empty for a marked profile: a PYTHONPATH there ran a
  module from it in the host child.

Bind owner_home wherever the manager or its host runs code. home_path
stays the registries' key; for a home that is not a link both name the
same directory.

fix(agent): look up git from the repo in @diff context references

_expand_git_reference gated on resolve_usable_git(), which searches
PATH from Hermes's own cwd, and then launched bare git with cwd= set to
the session's repo. The same gap 85a3be0c3b closed for three other
bare-git readers: with a relative PATH entry (PATH=bin:<stub dir>) and
a working bin/git only under Hermes's cwd, the gate approved git and
the child, searching from the repo, ran the macOS CLT stub.

Ask inspect_git(cwd=...) instead. A missing git still reports
"git is not available".

fix(platform): look up git from the child cwd in bare-git readers

dump._git_output, trace_upload._git_branch and host_supervisor._build_sha
gate on resolve_usable_git(), which searches PATH from Hermes's own cwd,
and then launch bare git with cwd= set to another directory. With a
relative PATH entry (PATH=bin:/usr/bin) and a working bin/git only under
Hermes's cwd, the gate approved git and the child, searching from its own
cwd, launched the macOS CLT stub.

Ask inspect_git(cwd=...) instead, the cwd-aware lookup the guard already
uses for bounded_probe_run, web_git, version_info and source_check. It
still refuses a missing git, as resolve_usable_git did.

(cherry picked from commit c1133734657e315849ad155d3394ddae6c13ef63)

refactor(platform): drop the unused cwd parameter from resolve_usable_git

577d8524e1 threaded cwd through resolve_usable_git as well as the
guard's inspect_git path, but no caller passes it. It also invites a
misuse: with a relative cwd the returned path is relative to the
parent, so launching it with cwd= would resolve it a second time from
the child. The cwd-aware lookup stays on inspect_git and
is_usable_git_command, which only classify.

test(platform): pin an empty PATH as missing even when the cwd holds git

The cwd half of test_empty_path_reports_missing_not_clt_stub used an
empty cwd, so it still passed with _locate_git's empty-PATH guard
deleted: the lone "" entry joins to <cwd>/git, which did not exist.
Put an executable git in the cwd so the test fails unless PATH=""
keeps searching nothing.

fix(platform): keep a colon in the child cwd inside one PATH entry

The cwd-aware lookup joined each relative PATH entry onto cwd and then
re-joined the results into a PATH string for shutil.which. A checkout
directory containing os.pathsep (/tmp/a:b) was split back apart, so
PATH=bin:/usr/bin missed /tmp/a:b/bin/git, fell through to /usr/bin/git
and refused a working git as the macOS CLT stub.

On POSIX with a cwd, _locate_git now tests each PATH entry on its own,
the way subprocess tries each entry after chdir(cwd), and never builds
a PATH string. Without a cwd, and on Windows, the lookup still goes
through locate_command unchanged, and PATH="" still reports missing.

fix(platform): resolve relative PATH entries against child cwd in the CLT git guard

On POSIX, subprocess resolves relative PATH entries (such as bin or an
empty segment) after chdir(cwd). When PATH=bin:/usr/bin and only the
parent directory had a working bin/git, the CLT guard resolved git from
the parent cwd, approved it, and let the child fall through to the Apple
stub.

Accept optional cwd in inspect_git, resolve_usable_git,
is_usable_git_command, is_git_command, and _git_argv0_unusable,
resolving relative PATH entries and relative argv[0] paths against cwd
on POSIX (preserving PATH='' as missing). Pass cwd from
bounded_probe_run, web_git, version_info, and source_check.

Follows up on Greptile's relative-PATH finding on #159834, confirmed by
@unsupportedpastels.

test(platform): exercise the xcode-select -p timeout in the CLT git resolver

Add a POSIX regression test that runs a real fake xcode-select script
returning a valid developer directory immediately (usable) and after 3s
(rejected as clt_stub by the 2s deadline). Dropping timeout=timeout in
_probe_xcode_select_developer_dir fails the test with 'usable' != 'clt_stub'.

Follows up on @unsupportedpastels's m2 review finding on #159834.

fix(cli): refuse review_push and review_revert on the macOS CLT git stub

When macOS only provides the uninstalled /usr/bin/git CLT stub, the
guard skips the branch probes inside _review_push and the checkout/clean
calls inside review_revert, so both direct routes previously returned
{"ok": True} without running git.

Preflight both mutations with _git_argv0_unusable(["git"]) and raise
RuntimeError("git is not available"), matching review_create_pr.

Follows up on @unsupportedpastels's m1 review finding on #159834.
fix(pm): an unmeasurable volume still records the fallback, and seed sizing counts files linked out of the cache
test(pm): pin the rebuild headroom once the uv cache is merged; document the restart fallback
fix(pm): the refresh fallback records a stale stamp so the selection rebuilds once its cause clears
fix(pm): a failed refresh check boots the image environment, never the previous generation
fix(docker): an image upgrade no longer fills the data volume rebuilding the image's own extras

fix(cli): resume a source launch through this install's own command

A `python -m hermes_cli.main` or `python cli.py` launch reported
`sys.executable -m hermes_cli.main`, which depends on the old shell's
PYTHONPATH and fails with ModuleNotFoundError from a fresh terminal outside
the checkout. It now reports chat_launch.hermes_command(): the install's
launcher, or this interpreter with the inline bootstrap, which runs from any
directory with no extra environment (checked by replaying it under `env -i`).

Tests: a file-backed `display.program_resume: false` through the real config
loader writes no report; the gateway chat SIGCONT test is marked
platforms("posix") instead of skipping by hand, so macOS CI runs it.

Review: Greptile on #160797.

fix(tui): OSC 7577 follow-ups for the Ink TUI

Follow-ups to freqyfreqy's OSC 7577 support, from review:

- `--resume ID` is reported only for a session the gateway confirmed saved:
  an inline turn's prompt.submit `streaming` answer (tui_gateway writes the
  row before answering) or a resume with stored history. Token usage, a built
  agent or a pending submit no longer count; an isolated compute-host turn,
  a queued prompt and a shared gateway's admission receipt do not either.
  Saved ids are tracked only when the pane reports. Nothing is reported while
  attached to a named gateway (HERMES_TUI_GATEWAY_URL).
- The record is cleared on exit only after a user quit (die(): /quit, Ctrl+C
  or Ctrl+D at an idle prompt; or SIGINT). /update (exit 42), a crash, a
  signal and a dead output stream keep it.
- The launcher's bypass flag (--safe-mode / --ignore-user-config) rides in
  the resume prefix, and such a launch reports only a saved session
  (HERMES_TUI_RESUME_SESSION_ONLY).
- SIGCONT reports again; turning display.program_resume off at runtime asks
  the reporter whether a record is out. argv[0] follows the Python rule.

fix(cli): OSC 7577 follow-ups for the classic CLI and gateway chat

Follow-ups to freqyfreqy's OSC 7577 support (previous commit), from review:

- One ProgramResumeReporter (hermes_cli/program_resume.py) replaces the two
  copies of the report/clear bookkeeping in the classic CLI and gateway chat.
  It orders its writes under a lock, the classic CLI choosing its session
  under the same lock: the SIGCONT re-report runs on its own thread and must
  not land after the user's clear or a session switch.
- The reported command reaches the same home: `-p NAME` when the profile
  resolves to this HERMES_HOME (a real profile named "custom" included),
  nothing for a home outside the profiles root or under a custom root
  (Docker's /opt/data, where `-p default` means ~/.hermes in a fresh
  environment), and nothing while attached to a named gateway
  (HERMES_TUI_GATEWAY_URL: a fresh launch would open this machine's store).
  A --safe-mode or --ignore-user-config launch repeats its flag (gateway chat
  takes it from its args: such a launch sets no env opt-in) and is reported
  only with a saved session, since a bare restart would need its explicit
  model again.
- `--resume ID` is reported only once the session store holds the row; a
  fresh session reports the bare command until then.
- The record is cleared only when the user ends Hermes (/quit, Ctrl+D; in
  gateway chat Ctrl+D on an empty line is now a /quit binding). A signal,
  terminal loss, an exception, a bare EOF and the /update relaunch keep it.
  Both clients report again after SIGCONT.
- The token leaves os.environ in load_hermes_dotenv, every entry point's first

fix(pm): spell deep copy/remove paths long-form on Windows

`pm install` and `pm gc` are permanently broken on a default Windows host. A pm
workspace lives at `installs/<key>/environments/<32-hex>/workspace/` (132 chars before
any content) and the deepest bundled plugin fixture path adds another 132, so
destinations reach 263. With `LongPathsEnabled = 0` (the Windows default):

- `shutil.copytree` in `_copy_core_inputs` raises `[WinError 3]`, so every install
  fails and `venv_is_current()` stays False forever - the "install out of sync"
  warning can never clear.
- `shutil.rmtree` in `collect_generations` raises `[WinError 145]` on installed
  wheels whose paths reach 276, leaving the tree half-deleted so `pm gc` fails on
  every run and generations accumulate (19 GB observed on one host).

`pm/filesystem.py` already ships `long_root()` for exactly this, and its docstring
says every path joined onto the result inherits the spelling - these four call sites
just never adopted it. Route them through it.

Verified on a 263-char destination: plain `copytree` raises `WinError 3` while the
long-form call copies all 50 files; plain `rmtree` raises `WinError 145` while the
long-form call removes the tree. tests/pm/test_long_paths_windows_live.py,
test_long_path_exits.py and test_workspace.py pass (20 tests). The 9 failures in
test_filesystem_inherit_acl.py / test_workspace_output_encoding.py are pre-existing

for the card id, and the admission inserted one whose model line was the
plugin's own card id.

The replay is now an AdmissionReplay(existing_only=True) wake: the store
decides inside its one write, on the conversation the route names then,
between the existing row (duplicate), another digest (card_conflict) and
no row, which the admission gate refuses (not_found) at the point a new
row would be written. The legacy line cannot create a row on any
conversation; the plugin's plain retry lands on the new conversation
under the opaque reference.

Tests: the real /resume between the two admissions (red before: the
legacy line queued), the existing-only wake primitive, and the legacy
line reaching the admission only after a conflict. The helper equality
assertion in the upgrade test is dropped.

fix(plugins): replay cards admitted before the opaque reference

A card row admitted by the previous version carries the plugin's own
card id in its model line, and that line is part of the row's durable
payload digest. After the opaque reference change an unchanged retry of
such a card was refused as card_conflict instead of answered as its
duplicate.

When the opaque-line admission meets an existing row with another
digest, replay the card under the exact legacy line. The admission still
digests everything else, so changed content remains a conflict, and the
row exists, so the legacy line is never queued as new model content.
Rows are not rewritten and newly admitted cards keep the opaque
reference. Pin queued and completed legacy retries, legacy changed-
content refusals and current-version duplicate/conflict controls.
style(desktop): keep overlay module within line cap
style(tests): separate card overlay fixtures

fix(plugins): mark ambiguous card results as uncertain

Expose certain=false for cancelled, post_failed and timeout outcomes.
Document that cards may have landed and consumers must not inject a
fallback turn. Exercise both entrypoints with errors after real durable
admission and assert exact retries do not deliver twice.

fix(desktop): dedupe live cards against fetched history

Filter immutable live cards by structured plugin and card identity before
the concurrent message overlay. Preserve the durable row and distinct
plugin/card pairs. Cover the event-before-history-response race through
the real event builder, hydration and overlay.

fix(plugins): use opaque card references in model history

Derive a stable short reference from the structured dedupe identity and
persist it as the model line next to the renderer descriptor. Keep the
plugin card id for dedupe and display only. Pin malicious id absence at
the real history boundary, exact retry and restart persistence.

fix(memory): scrub card metadata after history repair

Remove display-only card keys independently of the repaired row kind.
Cover session-end, legacy pre-compress and checkpoint evidence egress
through repaired history while preserving stored display data.

test(plugins): pin atomic card rate admission

Exercise concurrent distinct card posts at the window boundary so the
per-plugin-session posting lock remains load-bearing.

test(plugins): pin closing an unscheduled card coroutine

Assert the coroutine is closed when the gateway loop drops its queued
callback before the card task starts.

fix(memory): keep plugin card display data host-only

Strip plugin-card text and directive metadata before session-end and
pre-compress memory-provider hooks while preserving the bounded core line.

test(plugins): a cross-profile card is refused by the ownership check itself

The two-profile matrix asserted only no_conversation, which the admission layer
also returns when it finds no route in the plugin's own scope. Pin the ownership
check's own detail for local and messaging keys, so a bypass of that check alone
fails the test instead of being caught one layer later.

test(tui): a hydrated plugin card plus its replayed plugin.card event prints once

Reconnect through the real Ink lifecycle and shared gateway client against a fake socket: the
resume snapshot carries the stored card row (as the gateway persists it: content, display_kind,
display_metadata) and the fanout replays the card's plugin.card frame at a seq the snapshot
covers, plus a later card's frame. Hydration renders the stored card once as its own text, never
the model's line; the covered frame is dropped by the attach fence and the later card prints
once from its event. Removing the fence makes the stored card print twice and fails the test.

test(plugins): ctx.post_card on a multiplexed gateway, two live profile authorities

Two served profiles with their own session authorities, state.db, live local session and a
Discord bot holding one committed human DM, in one process. A plugin posts by local key, by
messaging key and by origin from a sessionless task into its own profile only: the other
profile's keys and an origin naming the other profile are refused, and the other profile's chat
is not reachable through the plugin's own bot. Each card row lands in the plugin's own authority
and never in the other store. The same card id from two plugins is two cards, each with its own
replay.

fix(plugins): a card's idempotency receipt comes from the atomic admission

queued versus duplicate was read from a find() before the admission and rate limiting, so seven
concurrent posts of one card returned several queued receipts for one row, and exact retries
spent rate-limit slots before the dedupe settled.

admit_automation takes an AdmissionReplay sink the write stamps with the store's
created-versus-existing flag (as TranscriptRewrite.applied is stamped); admit_route_wake forwards
it for a producer that names its request_id. gateway/plugin_cards.post reads the status from that
flag, serializes posts per (plugin, session) with an asyncio.Lock, spends a rate-limit slot only when
its admission created the row, and consults find() only to let an exact replay through a full window.

Tests: seven concurrent same-content posts give one queued, six duplicate, one row and one stamp;
seven concurrent conflicting posts give one row and six card_conflict with no slot spent; a full
window still answers an exact replay as duplicate and a new card as rate_limited.

fix(plugins): ctx.post_card never raises across a gateway shutdown

post() created the coroutine and called asyncio.run_coroutine_threadsafe outside its only exception
handler, which caught concurrent.futures.TimeoutError alone. A gateway loop that closed between the
lookup and the scheduling raised RuntimeError("Event loop is closed") into the plugin and leaked the
coroutine ("coroutine '_post' was never awaited"); a cancelled task raised CancelledError.

Coroutine creation, scheduling and the wait are now one guarded operation. A loop closed before the
scheduling closes the coroutine and answers gateway_unavailable. The wait polls the loop while it
waits: a loop closed before the scheduled task ran answers gateway_unavailable and closes the
never-started coroutine; a cancelled task answers cancelled; the deadline answers timeout as before.
apost() answers the gateway's cancellation of the task with cancelled and a loop that refuses the
task with gateway_unavailable, while the caller's own cancellation still propagates
(Task.cancelling()).

Tests (tests/hermes_cli/test_plugin_cards_shutdown.py, RuntimeWarning turned into an error): closed
loop before scheduling, loop closed after scheduling and before the task ran, task cancelled from the
loop, timeout with the admission still landing, and the three apost cases.

docs(plugins): specify ctx.post_card, a durable card with no model turn

Background plugin work can only show the user an actionable card by
injecting a user turn the model must answer with a tool call. That costs
a full model call over the whole session, waits behind the background
review, and depends on the model cooperating. ctx.post_message cannot do
it either: it needs a session bound in the calling context and, on a
local session, is a transient notice rather than a transcript row.

Document the contract for ctx.post_card: a card (text, optional
transcript directive, optional id) admitted into the session's FIFO and
written as a note at the turn boundary, never a turn. It needs its own
consent capability, targets only the plugin's own profile, is
idempotent by id, and shows the model one factual line. Desktop renders
the plugin's registered directive. Other surfaces show the text, and
messaging platforms keep the plugin's own native card.


Also folds, while rebasing onto main (their intermediate trees predate merges of main):
- feat(plugins): ctx.post_card admits a card as a note, with no model turn
- test(plugins): ctx.post_card lands one note, in FIFO order, own profile only
- fix(desktop/tui): render plugin cards
- fix(plugins): a card is admitted from the gateway context, never the caller's
- docs(plugins): mark ctx.post_card experimental and state the plugin-host behaviour
- refactor(desktop): plugin card row and its claim check in a thread sibling module
- fix(plugins): a card is display-only, the model is told it exists and never reads its text
test(dashboard-auth): pin the loop marker on the move; docs say which sign-ins move
test(dashboard-auth): pin the desktop start, the Webapp's own public URL and the first forwarded host
test(gateway): auth fixtures start sign-in on the public host, as the proxy in front forwards it

fix(credential-pool): a spent plan window reads as a rate limit on every surface

Review follow-up on the plan-window bench:

- is_rate_limited_auth_error also recognises the `model_rate_limited` AuthError
  code (now MODEL_RATE_LIMITED_CODE in auth_constants) that
  _anthropic_token_or_raise raises for a benched Anthropic seat. It knew only
  `codex_rate_limited`, so the messaging gateway replaced the cooldown text with
  "Use /login to sign in again", the API server and fallback logs said "auth
  failed", and Kanban took the non-transient exit. The same applied to the
  existing per-model cooldown error.
- The pool-wide cooldown branch fires only when every live Anthropic row is a
  429 bench (pool_cooldown_message(rate_limited_only=True)). A pool benched by
  a 401 or 402 keeps the missing-credentials diagnostic and its sign-in remedy
  instead of being reported, and classified, as a rate limit.
- Docs (en, zh-Hans): any rejected plan window rotates on the first 429, the
  429 table row names that exception, and only an account-wide window benches
  every model.
- Comments and test docstrings say what the code does (reset precedence, the
  aux context, env-key coverage); the scope test also asserts that the refused
  model never goes back to the spent seat.

fix(credential-pool): rotate on the first 429 for a rejected family plan window too

A 429 whose unified headers say `rejected` for a model-family window
(seven_day_opus, ...) cannot succeed on the same seat before that window's
reset either, which is days away, yet it still took the single
min(Retry-After, 600 s) retry before rotating. A field report on #160488 shows
exactly that: 600 s on the spent seat, the same 429 again, then rotation
(about 13 minutes for one turn).

usage_allowance_spent now treats any rejected plan window as spent. Scope is
unchanged: an account-wide window benches the whole credential, a family window
only the requested model. A 429 without the unified headers (API-key per-minute
limits) keeps its one retry.

fix(credential-pool): a spent plan window holds env tokens too and is reported as a cooldown

Follow-up to the account-wide plan-window bench (salvage of #160488):

- token_is_blocked now honours a credential-wide 429 bench, not only per-model
  cooldowns. ANTHROPIC_API_KEY / ANTHROPIC_TOKEN / borrowed claude_code-source tokens
  skip pool selection, so before this they got the spent account back for every
  model, including the one that was just refused (on main the per-model cooldown
  at least held that model). Non-429 benches still leave an env key alone.
- _anthropic_token_or_raise reports a fully benched Anthropic pool with the
  existing pool_cooldown_message ("its only credential is cooling down ...
  resets at <time>") instead of "No Anthropic credentials found. Run 'hermes
  auth add anthropic'", which a sole spent seat hit on every new session until
  the reset.
- record_plan_window lets an account-wide window's future unified-reset replace
  a shorter request-level reset (retry-after), so the bench lasts until the
  window reopens; a stale unified-reset never replaces a live one.
- extract_api_error_context no longer raises TypeError on a non-scalar body
  reset_at (the auxiliary recovery path now goes through it).
- credential-pools docs (en, zh-Hans) describe the account-wide exception.

fix(credential-pool): bench a spent Claude plan window for every model and rotate on its first 429

A Claude subscription 429 names the refusing plan window in Anthropic's unified
rate-limit headers. An account-wide window (five_hour, seven_day) refuses every
model, but the pool benched only the requested model, the first 429 slept up to
600 s on the spent account, and the auxiliary path dropped the reset so its bench
lapsed after an hour.

extract_api_error_context now records the claim (subscription_window) and the
unified reset; a spent account-wide window benches the credential until that
reset and rotates on the first 429. Family claims and 429s without the headers
keep the per-model cooldown and single retry. The auxiliary recovery builds its
context with extract_api_error_context like the main loop.

Fixes #149112

refactor(backup): restore loop uses _import_skipped for its skip rules

The restore loop re-listed every rule _import_skipped already holds
(runtime names, host-managed root trees, PM-local roots, SQLite
sidecars), so each new rule had to be added twice to keep the integrity
pre-flight and the restore in agreement. Call it once instead; the
keep-host skips stay beside it. Same members are skipped as before.

Also word the host-managed note as "imports skip them": a hand-built
archive can still reach the tree through _external/, as it can for any
root entry.

fix(backup): match host-managed dirs at the Hermes root only, skip them on import

Follow-up to the portal-recovery/lost+found exclusion (#158231).

- One HOST_MANAGED_ROOT_DIRS constant in home_data_layout, matched at the

  profiles/<name>/portal-recovery/ from backups while keep-host still
  overwrote it, so the undo point lost a copy main could restore.
- Plain and keep-host imports skip root portal-recovery/ and lost+found/
  (restore loop and _import_skipped). Older Cloud archives carry readable
  portal-recovery/ files, and writing them into the root-owned folder
  ended the import incomplete. keep-host's _HOST_ROOT_DIRS goes back to

- Tests: shared deny-reading helper, the archived lost+found member is

- Document the exclusion in the backup reference (en + zh-Hans).

fix(gateway-migrate): quote launchd recovery commands and handle edge states

Harden printed launchd manual stop and rollback commands across four
recovery edge cases:
- Build all printed launchd commands (`mv`, `launchctl enable`,
  `launchctl bootstrap`, `launchctl kickstart`, `launchctl bootout`,
  `launchctl disable`) with `shlex.join()` so plist paths or labels
  containing spaces stay intact while clean paths remain unquoted.
- When a legacy manifest lacks `old_backend_disabled` and
  `stop_old_backend` was entered, include `launchctl enable` before
  recovery while keeping explicit `old_backend_disabled=False` free of
  unnecessary `mv` and `enable`.
- When `unit_path` is absent and the job was booted out (or stop state
  is unknown), instruct the operator to locate the original plist and
  run `[sudo ]launchctl bootstrap <scope> <plist-path>` instead of
  emitting an unusable `launchctl kickstart`.
- When `unit_path` is already back on disk and `<unit_path>.disabled`
  is gone (e.g. restore renamed the plist before `launchctl enable`
  failed), omit `mv` while keeping `launchctl enable` and `bootstrap`.

Match Linux systemd-system parity for macOS system-domain LaunchDaemons

Make _manual_rollback_steps() for launchd privilege-aware (sudo for system
