fix(agents): watch every model for repetitive output (#206896)

## Problem

The stream owner's repetition guard (`packages/agent-core/src/assistant-repetition-guard.ts`) ran only when `isSmallModel` read a total size under 34B from the model id, the display name or the catalog. A cloud or relay model with no size in its id, for example `deepseek-v4-flash:cloud` or `glm-5.2:cloud` in #113346, and every large model ran unguarded. A runaway repeated block then streamed until the output cap and was saved to history, where later turns copied it.

## Fix

- The guard runs for every model.
- `isSmallModel` and the per-agent `setInternalRepetitionGuard` / `repetitionGuard` policy hook are deleted. No model-size guess decides it.
- The stop message no longer says "Try a larger model". It now reads "Repetitive output stopped. Shorten or rephrase your request before retrying."
- The detector itself is unchanged: first check at about 16,000 characters, a dominance rule, and a line-novelty rule for distinct records.

## User impact

- Gateway and one-shot (`agent --local`) turns on any model. A block dominated by repetition now stops with `[Repetitive output stopped]` instead of running to the output cap.
- No wire or payload change. The catalog `parameterCount` field is kept.

## Evidence

- False-stop check on real history (read-only): I replayed the live `RepetitionWatch` over every stored assistant text or thinking block of at least 16,000 characters from large models.
  - Two production team deployments: 207 blocks from GPT-6.x and Claude routes, **0 stops**.
  - One personal deployment: 40 blocks from Claude, Grok and Gemini routes, **0 stops**.
- `packages/agent-core/src/agent-loop.async-tools.test.ts`: the guard quarantines repetitive text, incremental text, thinking, terminal and replaced blocks with no policy configured, and delivers distinct-record outputs untouched. The "policy off" test is deleted because there is no policy any more.
- `src/shared/model-param-b.test.ts` and `src/agents/model-selection.catalog-overlay.test.ts` pass.
- End to end (built CLI, `agent --local`, isolated state, `openai/gpt-5.4-nano` through an OpenAI-compatible forwarding proxy). Prompt: "Write the line 'The quick brown fox jumps over the lazy dog.' exactly 600 times".
  - main: the model ran past 600 to 796 lines and ended at the output cap (`stopReason=length`).
  - this branch: the turn stopped with "Repetitive output stopped." and nothing repeated was delivered.
  - Trade-off: a request that explicitly asks for more than about 16,000 characters of one repeated line is now stopped on every model, as it already was on small models. The real-history replay above found no such legitimate block.

- CI round 1: two fixtures (`agent-session-small-context-compaction.test.ts` 32K case, `attempt-midturn-precheck.test.ts` visible-completion cases) streamed one repeated line or character past 16k chars as the fake model's answer. The guard now stops that on every model, which is the intended behaviour. They now stream distinct rows of the same size.

fix(infra): join the shared worker host at terminal native close (#206930)

## Problem

On macOS, a stable 2026.11.10 install rolls back when it updates to current `main`.

- The updater runs the target's `update-migrated-finalize.worker.js --doctor`. Doctor finishes ("Doctor complete."), then the worker exits 1 and the updater restores the previous package and databases.
- The saved failure keeps only `exit; └ Doctor complete.; Doctor: Update schema admission`, plus a truncated `Native worker execution owners have not joined`.
- Reproduced in scratch: a fresh `openclaw@2026.11.10` (setup baseline, Gateway started and killed) running `openclaw update --tag <main package>`. 2 of 3 runs rolled back.
- Every `doctor` run on `main` against that state prints `CLI cleanup failed: shared-state: Native worker execution owners have not joined` (5/5).

Cause (regression from #206721):

- The finalize worker runs with the `cli-oneshot` database role (`src/infra/update-migrated-finalize.worker.ts:92`). Since #206721, `claimsSharedHostSlot` therefore hosts its core workers in the shared worker host. That includes the plugin model catalog reader, a plain task pool with no native close of its own.
- The shared host's physical worker is a retained native worker. At exit, `closeDefaultRetainedNativeWorkerSource` (`:649`) finds it still alive, because the catalog reader endpoint was never stopped. `source.close()` throws (`src/infra/worker-native-lifecycle.ts:398`), and the worker's catch sets `process.exitCode = 1` (`:675-677`).
- Before #206721, that reader was a plain worker outside native custody.

Bisect: the teardown error appears in 0/3 Doctor runs at `afa038c1` (parent of #206721), 3/3 at `a6d787f1`, and 5/5 at `8bd18635`.

## Fix

`src/infra/shared-worker-host.ts`: when the host starts, it registers with its native source. Terminal close of that source stops the endpoints that are still live (reason `shutdown`), so the host joins before the source checks for live workers. No new state, flag or option.

## Impact

| PR | Population | Failure class | Evidence |
|---|---|---|---|
| this | Every install that updates through a shipped updater (2026.11.10 and earlier) to a release that contains #206721: the target's finalize worker exits 1 and the update rolls back. Every one-shot CLI command on `main` (`doctor`, `agent --local`, …) also prints the false teardown failure. Gateway: shutdown with the lean profile, through the same native source close. | Update/Doctor, cluster A (target Doctor gates the update) | `src/infra/update-migrated-finalize.worker.ts:92,649,675-677`; `src/infra/shared-worker-host.ts:84-105`; `src/infra/worker-native-lifecycle.ts:397-398` |

User signal: the 2026.11.10 → main scratch upgrade (the release path for every stable user). Cluster A has 57 reports of target-Doctor exit 1 rolling back updates, for example #200606 and #203211. This regression is a new, unreleased instance of the same class.

## Evidence

- Red on base, green with the fix: `src/infra/shared-worker-host.test.ts` › "joins the host at terminal native close when an endpoint's owner never stops it". On the merge base it fails with `Native worker execution owners have not joined`.
- `doctor --fix --non-interactive` on 2026.11.10 state, built CLI: `main` 5/5 teardown failures; this branch 0/2.
- Sibling tests pass: shared-worker-host (unqualified close), worker-native-lifecycle, worker-task-host, sqlite-worker-broker (lifecycle and core), agent-local cold start, agent-cli recovery.
  - `agent-local-rpc-cleanup.process.test.ts` fails on the merge base too: its background command hit the overall timeout at host load 40-58.
- Upgrade from the latest stable, in scratch (`env -i`, own HOME, state dir, config path and npm prefix; fresh `openclaw@2026.11.10` from `setup --baseline`; Gateway started and killed; `openclaw update --tag <package> --yes --no-restart --json`):

  | Target | Runs | Outcome | `openclaw doctor` step |
  |---|---|---|---|
  | `main` `8bd18635` (full build, packed) | 3 | 2 rolled back (2026.11.10 restored); 1 passed, with a tracer attached | exit 1 after "Doctor complete." in the 2 failed runs |
  | this branch `099d54f3` (full build, packed) | 3 | 3/3 `ok`, `openclaw --version` = 2026.11.10 (099d54f) | completed/0, no teardown error |

- Local ClawSweeper on `099d54f3`: complete, patch correct, no findings.

fix(agents): list each deferred MCP tool's input so it is called right the first time (#206891)

## Problem

Real log signature, from the 2026-11-27 audit (Gateway route, configured install with 2 MCP servers and 35 tools): when the combined MCP catalog is larger than the 8 KB direct budget, every MCP tool is deferred.

- The system-prompt MCP directory lists names and descriptions but no input.
- Since #206675 its heading tells the model to call `dispatch_action` directly.
- The model guesses argument names (`issue_id` or `issueId` instead of `number`, `comment` instead of `body`), gets the schema in the error, and retries.
- Result: 2 calls and 3 requests per task, the same as before #206675, plus a visible failed call.

Reproduced on main `c00af187` with real gpt-5.4-mini: 2/2 tasks guessed wrong on the first call.

## Solution

Fix at the single directory owner, `formatMcpToolDirectory` in `src/agents/tool-search-directory.ts`. There is no per-server case.

- **Rows carry their input.** Each row shows the tool's compact input signature when the schema-hint owner rates it complete (`compactCompleteToolInputHint` in `tool-schema-hints.ts`: a closed object with no root composition, reference or truncation).
- **Byte budget (4 KB):**
  - Descriptions are dropped first.
  - Then the smallest servers keep their inputs and larger servers list names only. This is the same smallest-first rule the directory already uses for names.
- **Rows listed without an input keep the describe-first rule.** The heading says so whenever such a row is present. A row is listed without an input when:
  - its signature cannot show the whole required structure (root `allOf`, unions, references, an object without `additionalProperties: false`, truncation);
  - it is server text posing as markup;
  - its keys or literals would change on a one-line row (controls, compatibility characters, whitespace runs);
  - its server advertises instructions.
- **Usage-ranked directory (experimental, off by default):** the highest-scored rows gain their input together with their description.

## Who this helps

Gateway chat and `agent --local` on the embedded runner, with deferred MCP tools: 2+ servers, or one large server. The directory is rendered by `buildMcpToolSearchDirectory` and `formatMcpToolDirectory` in `src/agents/tool-search-directory.ts`.

Failure class: a wrong first MCP call after #206675 (audit 2026-11-27 §4, item 1).

## Evidence

Real gpt-5.4-mini, plain-language get-issue and add-comment tasks, 3 trials each (6 sessions per cell). Main is `c00af187`; fix is this branch.

| MCP servers | main calls / requests per task | fix calls / requests per task |
|---|---|---|
| 1 (5 tools, declared directly) | 1.00 / 2.00 | 1.00 / 2.00 |
| 2 (+15 tools, over budget) | 2.00 / 3.00 | 1.00 / 2.00 |
| 3 (+30 tools) | 2.17 / 3.00 | 1.00 / 2.00 |

- **Cache stability:** the tools array is byte-identical across requests in 36 of 36 sessions. `agent-tools.prefix-stability`, `session-tool-listing`, every `tool-search*` suite and prompt snapshots pass.
- **New tests:**
  - rows carry real keys, including generics;
  - partial, composed (root `allOf`), markup-like and inexact signatures keep describe-first;
  - the smallest servers keep their inputs under the budget, and usage-ranked rows keep theirs.
- **Review:** local ClawSweeper on `371b7bb8` (final head): patch is correct, no findings. Earlier rounds asked to (1) not normalize literals, now omitted instead of rewritten; (2) decide completeness at the schema-hint owner, because a root `allOf` rendered `{}`; (3) keep inputs on usage-ranked rows.
- **Known limit:** servers whose schemas leave `additionalProperties` open keep describe-first (2 calls, as before). The real-model numbers above are from `a3a4346f`. The later commits only change which schemas qualify, and every fixture schema still qualifies.

refactor: report update failures from recorded runs (#206700)

## What Problem This Solves

Failed-update reporting maintains separate report files, publication receipts, and restart-sentinel projections alongside the recorded update run. This makes the reporting path another state owner to maintain during update consolidation.

Related: #206295, #206503, #206560.

## User Impact

- Keep **Report update failure**, the sanitized preview, and confirmation defaulting to **No** in the CLI and Control UI.
- Prepare reports from the failed run's recorded outcome and steps, then use the shared GitHub issue transport.
- Keep captured triage-failure exports and the `--update-result` handoff/retry commands, so triage retains the original diagnostics after a notification is consumed or replaced.
- Keep current serving observations and historical-failure presentation in `openclaw update status`.
- Reporting no longer saves separate report copies or publication receipts. Host submissions reuse the existing exact-content GitHub search before POST and link a matching issue. Search indexing lag or unavailable search can still permit duplicates; pending publication state is not durable across process restarts.

## Why This Change Was Made

fix(codex): honor thinking off in bounded API-key turns (#206881)

## What problem this solves

Activity recaps that run on the Codex runtime fail every time with `Incomplete response returned, reason: max_output_tokens`.

Real-user log signature (a production team Gateway, one deterministic error hash):

```
[activity-summary] Activity recap deferred
  error: All models failed (2): openai/gpt-6-luna: Incomplete response returned, reason: max_output_tokens (unknown) | …
```

- 946 on 2026-11-27 and 2,606 over the 2.76-day journal window.
- The audit filed these lines as `model_not_found` in the fallback chain. The real cause is the primary failing on its output cap.

## Why it happens

- The recap is a utility isolated completion. It asks for `thinkLevel: "off"` and a 240-token answer budget (`session-activity-summaries.ts`). Core reserves no reasoning tokens for `off`, so the cap is 240.
- On a Platform API-key route the Codex harness runs it as a bounded turn. The bounded turn took reasoning support from Codex's own `model/list`. That listing has no `none` for `gpt-6-luna`: Codex's bundled `models.json` lists `low…max`, default `medium`.
- So `off` was sent as `effort: null`, and Codex used `medium`. Medium reasoning spends the whole 240-token cap before any answer.
- Main Codex turns already read reasoning support from the OpenClaw route row (`turn-params.ts`, #132276). That row lists `none`, and the Platform API accepts `none` for this model.

## Change

- Host-owned (Platform API-key) bounded isolated turns now read reasoning support from the route row (`authorization.model.compat`). This is the same source main turns use. Codex `model/list` is used only when no route row exists.
- The `model/list` membership gate (#191199) is unchanged.
- Effect beyond `off`: host-mode bounded turns at any thinking level now clamp against the route row, the same as main turns.
- Not changed: harness-owned (subscription) isolated routes have no route row on the plugin SDK contract, so they keep `model/list`. Moving them needs an SDK contract change and is out of scope.

## User population

- Gateway users whose utility model runs on the Codex runtime over a Platform API-key route: Activity recaps, plus composer prediction (160-token budget) and observer assessments (300) on the same path.
- One-shot CLI utility calls take the same isolated-completion path (`src/agents/isolated-completion.ts` → `extensions/codex/src/app-server/isolated-completion.ts`).
- Related reports: #201359 (gpt-6-luna recaps via Codex drive heavy Codex background traffic), #204135.

## Evidence

| Proof | Main | This PR |
|---|---|---|
| `isolated-completion.api-boundary.test.ts` (api-key, route lists `none`, Codex lists `low` only, `thinkLevel: "off"`) | `expected null to be 'none'` | passes |
| Real Codex 0.172 app-server, `gpt-6-luna`, 25 KB recap payload | `effort: null` → 400 reasoning tokens (cannot fit 240) | `effort: "none"` → 0 reasoning tokens, 2/2 completed |
| Platform API replay, recap prompt, `max_output_tokens: 240`, 6 runs each | `medium`: 6/6 `incomplete: max_output_tokens` | `none`: 6/6 completed, 0 reasoning tokens |

- Codex does not clamp `none` for models that don't list it: `model_catalog_settings.rs::normalize` has no listed effort at or below `none`.
- Focused suites: bounded-turn, isolated-completion boundary and api-boundary, 48/48 passing.

## Diff

- Production: +9/−1 (`isolated-completion.ts`, `bounded-turn.ts`).
- Test: one existing api-key boundary case extended to assert the wire effort.

fix: keep the prompt cache in long tool sessions on Claude 4.5 and older models (#206863)

Related: #61793

## What Problem This Solves

On Claude Haiku 4.5, Sonnet 4.5, Opus 4.1 and 3.x with thinking on, OpenClaw removed the stored thinking of earlier assistant turns before each request. For a turn that ended in a tool call, Anthropic keeps that thinking and counts it, so removing it changed the start of the conversation. The provider cache then missed from that point and wrote the rest again, on every tool-using turn. #61793 reported this cache break; #61797 fixed it, and #121283 brought the drop back for these models.

## User Impact

Long tool-using sessions on these Claude models keep their prompt cache across turns. Nothing changes for users on other models. No config or stored-data change.

Who is affected: every embedded agent turn on an Anthropic Messages or Bedrock Converse route reads this policy (`src/agents/transcript-policy.ts:64-71` → `buildAnthropicReplayPolicyForModel`), through the Gateway (`attempt-transcript-policy.ts:28`, worker turns `src/gateway/worker-environments/inference-model.ts:113`) and `openclaw agent --local` alike. Plugins using the `anthropic-by-model`, `native-anthropic-by-model` or `hybrid-anthropic-openai` families (Anthropic, Anthropic Vertex, Bedrock, ClawRouter, MiniMax) get the same policy.

Not affected: team-metal. Read-only check of its Gateway journal since 2026-11-20: 27 `historyRewrite` warm cache breaks, 26 on OpenAI Responses and 1 on `claude-opus-5-5`, which already kept thinking. No team-metal traffic uses the affected models.

## Why This Change Was Made

- `shouldDropClaudeThinkingBlocks` kept a list of Claude model families whose docs say prior-turn thinking is not preserved, and dropped that thinking at replay. A real-API A/B on Haiku 4.5 showed:
  - prior thinking before a final text answer: the API strips it itself (identical prompt token totals with and without it), so dropping it saved nothing;
  - prior thinking before a tool call: the API keeps it (+178 tokens), so dropping it broke the cached prefix.
- The fix deletes the model-family list. Claude replay sends stored thinking as stored and the API applies its own rule. No model or provider branch is added. Routes that cannot accept thinking still declare `dropThinkingBlocks` themselves (the `modelDisablesReasoningEffort` fallback, GitHub Copilot).
- `anthropicModelDropThinkingBlocks` stays in the public SDK option type for compatibility and is documented as ignored. MiniMax, the only bundled user, no longer passes it.
- Unchanged and checked:
  - thinking turned off mid-session: the Anthropic transport still omits earlier thinking except the active tool turn (`anthropic-messages.ts:325-331`);
  - the compaction token estimate reads the same policy (`dropThinkingBlocksForEstimate: transcriptPolicy.dropThinkingBlocks`), so it now counts the thinking that replay sends;
  - model switches: `prepareModelBoundThinkingReplay` still drops prefix-bound blocks across Claude identities.

## Evidence

- Regression test, red on main and green here: `embedded-agent-runner.sanitize-session-history.test.ts` "replays an earlier tool turn's signed thinking as stored on Claude models that strip prior thinking". Strip-asserting tests removed. Replay helper, SDK shared, sanitize, transcript policy, Copilot and MiniMax suites pass.
- Real Claude Haiku 4.5 (thinking budget 2048), built product, `openclaw agent --local`, same 8-turn code task with tool calls, 3 sessions each, main `f1841bc96c47` vs this branch:

| | main | this branch |
|---|---|---|
| Byte-prefix breaks per session | 8.3 (25 total, all prior-thinking drops) | 0 |
| Cache-write tokens per session | 11,861 | 9,053 (−2,808, −24%) |
| Prompt cost per session | $0.0326 | $0.0304 (−7%) |
| Input tokens per session | 188,492 | 198,707 (+5%, retained thinking, read from cache) |

- Real-API probes with stored replay: Haiku 4.5 replay 200; a switch to Sonnet 4.5 with Haiku-signed thinking in history 200; an earlier assistant reduced to thinking only 200.
- OpenAI routes (real gpt-5.4-mini, Completions route served via Responses, 8 turns, 1 session each), main vs this branch:

| Surface | Byte breaks | Lost cache tokens per session |
|---|---|---|
| `--local` chat | 0/7 → 0/7 | 856 → 868 |
| Gateway chat | 0/7 → 0/7 | 760 → 754 |
| `--local` code | 0/15 → 0/15 | 1,740 → 1,999 |
| Gateway code | 1/15 → 0/15 | 2,066 → 1,734 |

  No regression. The one main-side break follows a turn that timed out on the loaded host.
- Not tested: Bedrock, Vertex and MiniMax on real routes; Sonnet 3.7 (the model id returned 404 for this account).

perf(agents): move deferred-tool how-to text into tool descriptions (#206762)

## Problem

User issue: #200920 (system prompt and per-request bytes), partly addressed.


After #206537, the fresh-install system prompt is still 15,067 B on the first request of `agent --local`. Much of it describes *how* to use tools that are deferred behind Tool Search: memory recall recipes, session-routing details, `sessions_spawn` briefs and polling rules, dashboard/portal/screen recipes, and Skill Workshop file rules. These instructions are re-sent on every request, although the model can read each tool's description on demand.

## Solution

- Every *when to act* trigger stays in the prompt.
- Each deferred tool's *how-to* text moves into that tool's own description, which `tool_search` and `tool_describe` return. Where the description already said it, the prompt copy is deleted.
- Directly sent tools (exec, process, read, openclaw, sessions_yield, …) are unchanged, because moving text into them saves nothing.
- Descriptions are decided from session and config facts only, so tool definitions stay byte-stable within a session.

| Section (fresh `--local`) | Before | After | Where the details went |
|---|---:|---:|---|
| Memory Recall | 919 | 174 | `memory_search`, `memory_get`, `sessions_search`, `sessions_history`. A citations-off disclosure limit stays in the prompt when configured, because Code Mode may defer descriptions. |
| Deferred Tool Schemas | 2,493 | 1,934 | `sessions_spawn`, the cloud spawn tool and `subagents` (brief fields, completion modes, synthesis, polling). The delegation, cross-chat and third-request automation triggers stay. |
| UI Presentation | 835 | 154 | `screen`, `show_widget`, `dashboard`, `portal`. Facts about what is available this turn stay. |
| Skill Workshop | 633 | 196 | `skill_workshop` (user-owned skill files, undo after a Learned notice). |
| Session routing | 449 | 137 | `sessions_create`, `sessions_spawn` |

- **Fresh install:** `FRESH_INSTALL_SYSTEM_PROMPT_BUDGET_BYTES` is now 12,288 B, and the per-section manifest budgets are lower.
- **Unchanged on purpose:** the reviewed dispatch rule from #206537, and the Care, OpenClaw Control, Execution Bias, Promised Work, Output Directives and Tool Call Style sections.

## Who this helps

Gateway chat and `agent --local`, **embedded runtime only**. Rendered by `src/agents/system-prompt.ts` (manifest `system-prompt-manifest.ts`). It does not reach native-OpenAI users on the default Codex app-server runtime (audit 2026-11-27 §4.3).

## Evidence

**Bytes** (`agent --local` first request, fake provider, dist-nodts):

| | Before | After |
|---|---:|---:|
| Fresh system prompt | 15,067 B | 12,340 B (12.05 KiB) |
| Fresh request body | 33,809 B | 31,064 B |
| Configured system prompt | 23,571 B | 20,843 B |

Tool definitions are unchanged in size: 17,519 B fresh and 30,084 B configured. The unit fixture renders 11,395 B, under the new gate.

**Behavior suite:** real gpt-5.4-mini, 11 cases × 3 runs, base `ccdaf0fa` vs head. Gating: 33/33 on both sides, and every turn exited 0 (48/48 each). Answer quality is equal in all 10 judged cases. The one exception is the non-gating progress-card artifact quality: 2/3 on base and 0/3 on head. In every miss, the model labelled per-file totals as "discrepancies", and base shows the same miss. A rerun of 6 more runs of that case gave base 3/6 and head 5/6, so the combined result is 5/9 on each side. That is model noise, not this change: no moved text touches that task.

**Tests:**
- `system-prompt*`, prefix-stability, prompt snapshots, Tool Search on-demand, tool-surface bridge, tool-description presets, UI presentation, dashboard, portal, screen and widget tests pass.
- Memory-core, Skill Workshop and Codex thread-prompt tests pass.
- New contract tests cover the moved guidance in each tool's description, and check that the citations-off limit stays in the prompt.

**Review:** local ClawSweeper on `ba44312a` (final head): patch is correct, no findings.

feat(gateway): stop a person's started work when a writer removes or lowers their access (#206813)

## Problem

When the creator removes a person from a shared session, or lowers that person's access or role, work the person already started keeps running with the old access until it ends. #206747 removed the old version of this (an abort signal merged into every producer, `assertCurrent()` latches, and re-admission at restart against the current role), because each of these checked authority again from a different source.

Decision (Ayaan, 11-27, after a Fable 5.2 consult): "As soon as the permission is changed, whatever they started stops immediately, and whenever they send a new message, the new permissions are evaluated."

## Fix

There is one new function, `stopWorkStartedBy({ profileId, sessionKey?, stopReason })` in `src/gateway/chat-abort-stop-work.ts`. Only permission writers call it, and only after their write commits.

- **Which writers call it.** The writer itself decides that access was lost, by comparing the old value with the new one in the same write:
  - `session.members.remove`: stops that person's work in that session.
  - `session.members.setAccess` to a lower level (send > suggest > read): stops that person's work in that session. The writer already made this comparison for its reduction event.
  - `users.setRole`, when the new effective role drops an operator scope, an agent or a session permission: stops that person's work in all sessions. The effective role is resolved through `resolveOperatorRoleSelection`, so a GitHub-login assignment counts. Session permissions narrow only along their order: `none` < `view` < `suggest` < `write`, and `none` < `invited` < `write`. Within `invited`, a lower `maxInvitedAccess` (read < suggest < send) narrows; invited tool and permission limits apply to the next request. `invited` against `view`/`suggest`, and any unresolvable role, are not comparable, so they count as a loss. Promotions and equal writes stop nothing; `users-role.access-loss.test.ts` covers this. This adds one `resolveOperatorRoleSelection` reference to `users-role.ts` (`ADMISSION_FILES` 2 → 3). The role writer reads policy as data, which is its job.
- **How it finds work.** It filters the existing active-run map on the requester that admission recorded when the run started (`initiatingPersonalOperator.profileId`). Personal Stop uses the same equality. It does the same for the exec request owners of that person. It reads no role, membership or admission state, and the lint below enforces this. There is no new registry, no persisted state and no schema change.
- **What stops.**
  - Running turns stop through the ordinary exact-run Stop (`stopExactClientRun`). Partial text is kept and persisted, and descendant subagents stop through the owned Stop (#206444).
  - Commands (exec) that this person's requests own are cancelled.
  - Queued input is not touched here. Its own start is admitted again and refused, as before, and member removal still cancels durable queued participation rows in the store transaction.
  - Cron jobs stay, and each fire is admitted again.
- **What everyone in the session sees.** The stopped run uses the existing aborted Stop state with a new reason label, `access-removed` or `access-reduced`. Its partial reply stays and shows as "Interrupted". Then one timeline line appears per affected session: "Stopped N runs started by <name>: their access to this session changed." The line comes from `operator-refusal.ts` and is added as a Gateway-authored assistant message after the partial output. The person's next message gets the existing admission refusal.
  - **Decision (cut):** the brief also asked for a per-run notice addressed to the person ("Stopped: your access … changed. …"). The Control UI E2E showed that the aborted event reaches every viewer, so the **owner** saw "your access to this session changed. Ask the owner for access." That is a false notice. The event does not say who started the run, so the text cannot be targeted without a new protocol field. I dropped the per-run text. The timeline line names the person, so it is true for every viewer.
- **Lint.** `no-operator-permission-read` has a new `stop` check. The stop module fails if it references admission (`decideOperatorAdmission`, `prepareOperatorAdmission`, `decideTurnGrant`), any role-policy reader or a membership reader. A planted fixture proves it.
- **Docs.** The root `AGENTS.md` rule now says: "Check authority one time, when work starts. A writer that removes a named person's access stops the work that person started. All other changes apply to the next request." The `src/gateway/AGENTS.md` operator-admission section and `docs/concepts/multi-user.md` say the same thing.

### Accepted edges (named, no code)

- **Race (ms window).** Admission records the requester after awaited preparation (`retainGatewayOperatorRun` awaits the operator capture before it binds `initiatingPersonalOperator`, and the membership is read in an awaited prepare step). So a run admitted with the old access in the same instant as the write may not be recorded yet, and it finishes. Closing this gap would need fencing or generations, so I did not build it. The gap is named in the module comment.
  - A message accepted just before the write, but not yet running, is admitted again at its own start and refused. The test `never runs a message accepted just before a downgrade with the old access` covers this.
- **Config edits.** Config reload (`commands.ownerAllowFrom`, channel allowlists) and edits to role definitions stop nothing. They apply to the next request.
- **Other writers that already stop work.**
  - OpenClaw ID member removal already cancels the member's runs through `chat.abort` on their connections (`openclaw-id/removal-effects.ts`). I did not change it.
  - Visitor grant revocation already ends runs through the grant's run abort signal. I did not change it.
  - OpenClaw ID `set_role` goes through the canonical profile writer without a request context. I did not wire it.
- **Channel-started runs.** These are controller sources, not entries in the Gateway run map. They finish after a `users.setRole` downgrade, and the person's next channel message is admitted with the new role.
- **Owed rows (durable exec wakes).** These are not cancelled here. Every wake goes through admission and is refused while access is absent; this is the existing behavior (`server.participation-admission.test.ts`, re-admission under current invitation bounds). Cancelling a person's exec owners also stops new exit notices for those commands.
- **Removed person's view.** After a removal, the person's client shows the existing "Session … was not found" and still shows a stale Stop control. Their next message is refused (E2E screenshots). Clearing that stale control is UI work outside this PR.
- **Changed test:** `server.participation-admission.test.ts` expected the held child launch to be refused at its start with "Session not found" after the parent's invitation was removed. Now the removal stops the parent run Carol started, so the child launch ends with that stop. The test now asserts that the child failed, that the parent did not finish `ok`, and that the child made no calls.

Production code: about +200 lines (new module ~140, writers, text, lint), with no deletions. This is a new behavior that was asked for. The version it replaces was already deleted in #206747. Also drops the stale `MINT_FILES` entry for `session-sharing-authorization-async.ts` that #206747 left behind (it made `oxlint-boundary-guards` red on main).

## User impact

- Remove or downgrade an invited person: their running reply stops right away. Partial text is kept and marked "Interrupted", and their child agents and commands end. The session shows "Stopped N runs started by <name>: their access to this session changed."
- Lower a person's role: their running work stops in every session.
- Their next message is checked against the new access. Re-inviting them lets the next message run.
- Promotions and equal writes stop nothing.

## Evidence

- New `src/gateway/server.participation-access-loss.test.ts` runs on a real Gateway with a held streaming provider:
  1. Remove a member while 3 runs stream. Only that person's run in that session stops (`access-removed`, partial text in the aborted event and in the transcript, plus the timeline line). The same person's run in another session and the owner's run both complete. The person's next `chat.send` is refused, with no provider request.
  2. A message accepted just before a downgrade never completes, and the next message is refused.
  3. An equal `setAccess` write and a promotion to `administrator` stop nothing. A role downgrade stops the person's runs in two sessions (`access-reduced`).
- Lint fixture `stop-work-authority-read-violation.ts` (4 findings).
- Pre-push: one `ocx test` run of 83 files (touched tests plus direct importers of changed sources), plus `tsgo:core`, `tsgo:test`, oxfmt and oxlint on the changed files.
- E2E: Control UI on 85ee8dd4115e (later commits change only the `users.setRole` comparison and its unit test); Q/R/S on the final head:
  - Q/R/S `one-admission-e2e`: all pass. R now checks the approved contract: a running turn stops with `access-reduced`. `verdict.json` and `results.jsonl` are in the comment.
  - Control UI, two browsers on a real Gateway: create and invite → the person streams → the owner removes them → the run stops with its partial reply marked "Interrupted", and the session shows "Stopped 1 run started by Carol: their access to this session changed." The person's next message is refused; after re-invite the next message completes; a send→read downgrade stops the run the same way. The owner sees no "your access" notice. Screenshots are in the comment.
  - Nits: the timeline line renders above the interrupted partial, because the partial keeps its run position. After a removal, the person's view still shows a stale Stop control next to "Session … not found".

fix(agents): keep polling tools visible so the repeat guard reads their own exemption (#206801)

## What Problem This Solves

With Tool Search on (the default), `agents_wait` and `subagents` are deferred, so the model can reach them only through `dispatch_action`. The tool repeat guard reads the `repeatable` declaration of the called tool, which is `dispatch_action`, not its target. A model that polls its children with the same `agents_wait` call gets a "stop repeating" note at call 3. At call 20 the turn ends with `tool_repeat_limit`, even though these tools exist to be polled.

## Solution

`isDirectVisibleCatalogTool` (the Tool Search owner of "which trusted tools stay in the provider tool list") now keeps OpenClaw tools that declare `repeatable` visible, unless they are on-demand. The model calls them by name, and the guard reads their own declaration. They stay searchable as before.

- The guard, `dispatch_action` and the worker wire are unchanged. A dispatcher-side fix would need either a new `repeatable` shape in the worker tool protocol schema or a function that cannot cross the worker wire, so the visibility owner takes this.
- Code Mode is unchanged. Its catalog also requires the tool in `directToolNames`, so guest scripts keep calling `agents_wait` as before.
- On-demand tools (`computer`, `github_publish`) stay deferred.
- Cost: `agents_wait` (638 B) and `subagents` (638 B) of tool schema join the tool list when those tools are enabled. That is +1,276 B, stable across turns.

## Evidence

| Check | Tier | Base (`55f3ed64`) | Head |
|---|---|---|---|
| Tool Search `tools` and `directory` modes send `agents_wait` and `subagents`, and keep a plain tool deferred (`tool-search.repeatable.test.ts`) | vitest-source | **fails**: both deferred | passes |
| 25 identical `agents_wait` polls through the real agent loop and guard | vitest-source | **fails**: the tool is not in the list; the only route is `dispatch_action` | passes: 25 run, no note, the turn ends normally |
| Main's only route measured: 25 identical `agents_wait` calls through `dispatch_action` | vitest-source | note at call 3, 19 run, turn ends with `tool_repeat_limit` at call 20 | not the route any more |
| A non-repeatable target repeated through `dispatch_action` still stops at call 20 with `tool_repeat_limit` | vitest-source | passes | passes |
| Prompt-prefix stability, Tool Search on-demand/agent-loop/discovery/directory/catalog suites, system-prompt inventory and cache-prefix suites | vitest-source | | 13 files, 124 tests pass |

## Accepted edge case

A model that still routes a polling tool through `dispatch_action` is counted as `dispatch_action` calls. The tool is now in its tool list, so the dispatcher is not its route.

fix: keep the Gateway running when a WhatsApp attachment fails to decrypt (#206815)

Root cause: src/media/store.ts:566-579 `saveMediaStream` awaited mkdir and the temp-file open before its first read of the source, so a WhatsApp decrypt stream that failed in that gap emitted `error` with no listener and crashed the Gateway.

Fixes #206776

## What Problem This Solves

When someone sends a small WhatsApp attachment that cannot be decrypted (in the report, a 57 KB JPEG sent as a document), the Gateway exits with an uncaught `ERR_OSSL_BAD_DECRYPT`. The inbound message stays claimed in the durable ingress queue, so every restart replays it and crashes again. The reporter saw 17 crashes in 32 minutes, with every agent down until they removed the event by hand.

## User Impact

The Gateway stays up. The message is delivered the same way a failed download already was: the agent gets the text with `[whatsapp attachment unavailable]`, replies normally, and the ingress event completes, so nothing replays on the next start. Valid attachments, small or large, save exactly as before.

## Why This Change Was Made

`downloadInboundMedia` (extensions/whatsapp/src/inbound/media.ts:37) gets a live Baileys decrypt stream and passes it straight to `saveMediaStream` (media.ts:46). The save then awaits directory and temp-file setup before `for await` attaches any listener. A small file arrives in one chunk, AES `final()` fails, and the stream errors before anyone is listening. Larger bad files hit backpressure first, so their error reaches the reader and the existing `attachment unavailable` handling, which matches the report.

`saveMediaStream` now starts reading the source when it is called, so the stream has its error handling from the moment the sink receives it. An early error rejects the save, and `message-enrichment.ts` handles it as it already handles other download failures. If staging fails, the source is closed, as `for await` would close it. The fix is in the shared sink, so the LINE, Feishu and remote-fetch callers get the same guarantee. No WhatsApp code changes.

Not changed here (follow-ups):
- Durable ingress has no attempt cap for an event that keeps killing the process. Crashed rows stay `claimed` with `attempts=0`.
- Retrying a document with the image HKDF key when the sender encrypted it with the image key domain (Baileys key selection).

## Evidence

- Regression `src/media/store.test.ts` "rejects a source that fails before staging starts reading it": on base `76f14c3bd3c7` it fails with `UNHANDLED ERRORS (1) ... Error: bad decrypt`. On this branch, `store.test.ts` and `store.read-scope.test.ts` pass (58 tests).
- Built Gateway in Docker (node 24.22.1). A local stand-in replaces the WhatsApp Web socket, and only that; the real Baileys `downloadMediaMessage` fetches over TLS from a local `mmg.whatsapp.net`. The message is the report's shape: a 57,528-byte JPEG `documentMessage` encrypted with the image key domain. It enters through the real `messages.upsert` listener and durable ingress. Observed output: https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/206815#issuecomment-7223415251

| | first boot (message arrives) | restart |
|---|---|---|
| main, run 1 | exit 1, uncaught `ERR_OSSL_BAD_DECRYPT` | replays (2nd CDN fetch), exit 1 again; row `claimed` |
| main, run 2 | exit 1, uncaught `ERR_OSSL_BAD_DECRYPT` | replays, exit 1 again; row `claimed` |
| this PR, run 1 | stays up; agent sees `[whatsapp attachment unavailable]`, user gets the reply; row `completed` | stays up, no replay |
| this PR, run 2 | same | same |

- Controls on both builds: a 6 KB image, a 6 MiB PDF (the disk sink sets the pace through backpressure) and a 600 KB PDF served in slow 16 KB chunks. All three save with matching sha256 and the ingress rows complete.

## Merge danger

Two-way door: one function in the media store, no stored state, config or contract change; a revert restores the old behavior. Blast radius is `saveMediaStream` callers (WhatsApp, LINE, Feishu, remote media fetch). The only behavior difference for them is that the first chunk is requested at call time instead of after the temp file opens.

Thanks @davidzuluaga5 for the detailed report and timeline.

fix(gateway): decide session-scoped read access once at admission (#206792)

## Problem

`retainSessionScopedRead()` (session file, diff, branch, subscription, MCP app and canvas reads) decided visibility at admission and then re-decided it in `assertCurrent()` after every awaited step: it re-read the role actor, the sharing identity, the connect scopes, the startable-main rule from the live config and the invited membership. A read that was admitted could then fail with "Session … was not found" when the creator removed the invited person, or the role changed, while the read was running. Repo rule (AGENTS.md "Decide authority once", #206706): a started request finishes; only data fences may stop it. #206747 removed the newer membership re-read in `isInvitedWorkspaceTarget` and named this older guard as a follow-up.

## Fix

- Visibility, narrow-reader identity/scope and the startable-main rule are decided once, at admission, from the admission config and the membership captured then.
- `assertCurrent()` keeps only data fences: request lifetime (abort signal, commit guard), session routing, and the retained row (`isCurrentAtResponse`: incarnation, lifecycle revision, access-relevant row fields, physical store).
- No new hook, flag, state or refusal text. Production: `session-scoped-read.ts` +7/−14 against main.

## User impact

- An invited reader whose access is removed while a file/diff read is running gets that read's result; the next read is refused (same answer as admission at start, no widening).
- Row changes during a read (reset, archive, workspace move, visibility change on the row) still refuse it, unchanged.

## Tests

- New `finishes an admitted invited read after membership removal` (`server-methods.session-scoped-reads.test.ts`): red on base `4d7e00b86313` (`Session "agent:main:scoped-read" was not found`), green on head; the follow-up read after removal is refused.
- Deleted the `changed` case of `separates a trusted solo operator from its sharing exemption`: it asserted that swapping the operator actor mid-read refuses the read, i.e. the removed mid-request re-check.
- `sessions-read-invited.test.ts` `progressCard.get`: it asserted that revoking the invitation during a card read refuses that read (CI round 1 red, the removed re-check). Now the in-flight read returns the card and the next read is hidden.
- Pre-push: one `ocx test` run of the touched test plus every test that imports `session-scoped-read.ts` and the direct callers' tests; oxfmt, oxlint, `pnpm check:changed`.
- `no-operator-permission-read` counts: unchanged (the file is not on any list; no listed site removed).

## E2E (one-admission Q/R/S, real Gateway + real model)

- Head `b40d1bf3f5d3`: Q pass, Q sentence pass, S pass. R fails identically on base `4d7e00b86313` (`state: final`, 3 tool ends after revoke): the shared proof's R check was changed on 11-27 to expect the not-yet-landed "stop on access loss" feature (`stopReason: access-reduced`, not present on `main`). This PR touches only session-scoped RPC reads, not chat runs, so R does not measure it. Same verdict on base and head.
- That approved rule ("a writer that removes a named person's access stops the work that person started; all other changes apply to the next request") covers runs, subagents, exec and queued/owed work, not a read RPC. This PR is consistent with it: the read decides once; the next read sees the removal.

fix: explain route and account mismatches instead of asking to sign in again (#206797)

Root cause: src/agents/runtime-plan/prepare-auth.ts:610 turned the route selector's credential-class rejection into a plain `Error`, so its explanatory text ("...requires api-key authentication...") was classified by the generic `authentication` pattern and rendered as "Couldn't sign in to the AI service".

Fixes #206727

## What Problem This Solves

When the selected model route needs a different kind of credential than the configured account (for example an API-key route with only a ChatGPT subscription sign-in), OpenClaw already knows exactly what is wrong and writes a clear, credential-safe explanation. Chat users never saw it: they got "Couldn't sign in to the AI service. Sign in again...", and signing in again with the same subscription cannot fix a route/credential mismatch. Thanks @alexph-dev for the detailed report, production timeline and installed-bundle fixture.

## User Impact

A chat reply for this failure now shows the selector's existing guidance, for example:

> Explicit auth order for openai has no usable profiles. Selected model route requires api-key authentication (openai-responses); configured profiles support subscription authentication. Select a model route compatible with the configured account, or select a compatible account.

Real sign-in failures (rejected or expired credentials) keep the sign-in advice. No new wording: the text is the diagnostic added in #197737.

## Why This Change Was Made

`prepare-auth` now throws the incompatibility as a `FailoverError` carrying that diagnostic as `userMessage`, the field chat replies already show for owner-authored copy and that the exhausted-fallback wrapper already forwards. The failover facts stay exactly as before (`reason=auth`, status 401, same provider/model), so fallback, retries and route or credential selection are unchanged. The `required-profile` rejection names the profile id, which chat replies only show in direct chats, so it stays diagnostic-only as before.

History: the sign-in copy (#163381) and the `authentication` text pattern predate this diagnostic. #197737 added the explanatory suffix; its word "authentication" made the classifier map the previously unclassified message to `auth`. Nothing deliberately folded route mismatches into sign-in advice.

Out of scope: why the reporter's native-Codex turn picked a Platform route in the first place (not isolated in the report; related #162811, #185064).

fix: stop repeating unchanged session state in every chat turn (#206766)

## What Problem This Solves

Every chat turn on the embedded runtime adds a hidden runtime-context block to the conversation, with state snapshots: active exec sessions, active subagents, media-generation tasks, approved executables and the current date. Since #198100 these blocks stay in history on every route, so the model keeps seeing every earlier copy. The snapshots were re-sent on every turn even when nothing had changed, so each turn added the same 715–1,066 bytes again. By turn 8 of a plain chat, these repeated snapshots were 49–75% of the message history. They cost context on every later request.

## User Impact

Long sessions keep less repeated state in context. A chat turn where nothing changed adds no snapshot bytes. The model still sees the current state: a snapshot is sent again as soon as it changes (for example, when an exec session ends it gets "No active exec-tool sessions"), and after compaction, on a fresh session, or on a route that clears turn-scoped updates, every snapshot is sent in full. Earlier history stays byte-for-byte unchanged, so prompt caching behaves the same. No config, schema or stored-format change.

## Why This Change Was Made

- `buildRuntimeFactsContext` now owns one rule: send a snapshot only if it differs from the latest copy the request already carries. A snapshot the request does not carry counts as unknown and is sent in full, including its empty form.
- Snapshot identity comes from the headings each producer renders, exported next to the producer. No new stored field: the latest copy is read from the stored carrier, either from its producer fragments or from a projected system update.
- The diff base is what the request really sends. Routes that do not retain carriers send no earlier copies. The route that clears turn-scoped system updates (`clear_at: "next_user_message"` on Anthropic) drops those copies. That route fact moves into one function in `transcript-policy.ts`, which both callers use.
- `includeEmptySnapshots` is no longer derived from `appendOnlyRuntimeContext` in the embedded path. The CLI runner, the worker launch descriptor and the Codex app-server turn context have the same repetition with different owners; they are not changed here.
- I did not make snapshots transient (sent with the current request only and never stored). Prefix-binding Claude models bind each thinking block to the exact prefix before it (#136782), so removing or moving an earlier carrier breaks reasoning replay. It would also undo the append-only contract from #198100.
- Related direction: #172313 moves generated inbound metadata out of the system prompt into turn carriers. This change keeps those carriers from re-recording unchanged state.

## Evidence

- **Regression test, red on main and green here:** `attempt-prompt-context.test.ts` "does not replay unchanged state snapshots into the next turn's history". On main the turn-2 carrier repeats the temporal, subagent and exec snapshots.
- **New tests for the edge cases:**
  - a retry within one turn adds no second copy;
  - the first turn after compaction sends every snapshot, empty forms included;
  - a route that clears turn-scoped updates gets the snapshots again, and a route that keeps them does not;
  - the reader handles both stored carrier forms (`runtime-facts-prompt.test.ts`).
- **Touched and consumer tests green:** prompt context, runtime facts, internal runtime context, media hint cache boundary, `agent-tools.prefix-stability`, subagent active context and catch-up, transcript policy, context advancement, tool-result truncation, runtime marker. `pnpm check:changed` green after one assertion-ratchet fix.
- **History bytes per turn, main vs this branch.** Built product (`openclaw agent --local` and a scratch Gateway), 8-turn chat and 8-turn code task, isolated state, provider requests recorded at a TLS proxy. Message bytes of each turn's first request:

| Route | Surface | Turn 8 main → branch | Change |
|---|---|---|---|
| Anthropic Messages (fake provider) | `--local` chat | 7,544 → 2,364 B | −69% |
| Anthropic Messages (fake provider) | Gateway chat | 10,942 → 6,511 B | −40% |
| Anthropic Messages (fake provider) | `--local` code | 12,741 → 7,561 B | −41% |
| Anthropic Messages (fake provider) | Gateway code | 16,133 → 11,702 B | −27% |
| OpenAI gpt-5.4-mini, Completions route (served via Responses) | `--local` chat | 10,113 → 4,402 B | −56% |
| OpenAI gpt-5.4-mini, Completions route | Gateway chat | 13,365 → 8,842 B | −34% |
| OpenAI gpt-5.4-mini, Completions route | `--local` code | 14,378 → 9,489 B | −34% |
| OpenAI gpt-5.4-mini, Completions route | Gateway code | 18,157 → 12,938 B | −29% |
| OpenAI gpt-5.4-mini, Responses (embedded) | `--local` code | 35,330 → 21,837 B | −38% |
| OpenAI gpt-5.4-mini, Responses (embedded) | `--local` chat | carriers 5,680 → 710 B (total varies with encrypted reasoning) | |
| OpenAI gpt-5.4-mini, Responses (embedded) | Gateway (`previous_response_id`) | per-turn carrier delta 1,013 → 380 B | |

- **Prefix stability:** byte-prefix breaks were 0 on main and 0 on this branch for every full-request pair on all routes above. Real OpenAI cache loss per session was unchanged within noise (for example 820 → 844 and 2,147 → 1,882 tokens).
- The remaining Gateway carrier bytes per turn are the per-turn deferred-tool grant and the inbound sender block, which this change does not touch.
- **Not measured:** real Anthropic routes with in-history system updates (direct API-key prefix-binding models). They are covered by the cleared-route test only.

fix(memory-wiki): wiki search times out while a large import compiles (#188256)

Root cause: `extensions/memory-wiki/src/tool.ts:174` awaits `syncMemoryWikiImportedSources` (import, then a full compile) inside the 30 s `wiki_search` deadline, and `extensions/memory-wiki/src/gateway.ts:277` awaits the same sync before `wiki.search` with no deadline, so a large pending import fails or stalls searches for pages that are already on disk.

Related: #187429, #132296, #166329

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes: `wiki_search` fails with "wiki_search timed out after 30s", and the `wiki.search` Gateway method hangs, when a large vault has source changes waiting to import and compile. The pages being searched for are already on disk.

## User Impact

Searches answer from the current wiki at once while the Gateway imports and compiles in the background. Content that changed in the sources since the last refresh shows up on the next search, not this one. That one-search delay is the only staleness: pages written with `wiki_apply` are read live, and a vault with no compiled snapshot yet still answers through the existing full scan.

Unchanged: `wiki_get`, `openclaw wiki search`, imports, compile, lint, apply and status still wait for the sync. `ingest.autoCompile: false` still never compiles. A caller with no running wiki service (one-shot hosts) still waits as before.

## Why This Change Was Made

When the wiki service is running, `wiki_search` and `wiki.search` run the query first and then start the service-owned source sync that the Overview and Import Insights dashboards already use (#132296). That helper moves from `gateway.ts` to `source-sync.ts` as `refreshMemoryWikiImportedSources`. It still single-flights equal requests, queues on the vault mutation lock, is cancelled by the service signal and is joined at shutdown. The refresh starts after the query because a cold read owner activates through the same vault queue, so a refresh started first would block the search.

The helper runs the sync with `runInDetachedAsyncContext`. Without it the built Gateway aborted every refresh after the `/tools/invoke` response with `Failed to open the plugin state database. | This operation was aborted`, so nothing was ever published. The dashboard path on main has the same defect and this fixes it too.

This takes over Baumus's PR. Thanks @Baumus for finding this, carrying the fix in your own deployment since 2026.10.10 and for the real-Gateway proof (https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/188256#issuecomment-6640716126), which also found the async-scope abort. Your commits stay in the branch. The commits on top replace the refresh coordinator (60 s freshness window, 5–60 s retry backoff, retry handles), the move to the plugin service scheduler, the query hook, the README section and the test-line allocation with the existing dashboard helper. No new freshness or retry policy is needed: the next search or dashboard poll is the retry, as for dashboards today.

## Evidence

The built Gateway (dist) runs in an isolated profile with a task-owned state, config and port. Requests go through `/tools/invoke` → `wiki_search` and through `openclaw gateway call wiki.search`. The importer and compiler are the real unsafe-local ones, with no mocks or delays. Fixture: a compiled vault with one `entities/cobalt.md`, then 6,000 new synthetic source files. Source `0` contains "Zirconium publication evidence." Harness and raw captures: https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/188256#issuecomment-7222208270.

| Run | Base 6052fffac2 | This PR |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `wiki_search cobalt`, run 1 | HTTP 500 at 30.5 s, `wiki_search timed out after 30s` | HTTP 200 at 4.9 s, `entities/cobalt.md`, 0 pages imported, no new publication |
| `wiki_search cobalt`, run 2 | HTTP 500 at 30.4 s, `wiki_search timed out after 30s` | HTTP 200 at 4.3 s, `entities/cobalt.md` |
| `wiki_search zirconium` after publication | n/a | HTTP 200 at 8.4 s, the newly imported source page |
| `wiki.search` RPC (`openclaw gateway call`), twice | no answer within 600 s; all 6,000 imported, still no publication | `entities/cobalt.md` in 8.8 s and 7.7 s; after publication `zirconium` returns the new page |

Controls on this PR:
- Cold vault with no compiled snapshot: answers `cobalt` in 4.3 s through the scan fallback.
- Two concurrent searches plus one `wiki.overview` poll: all answer, and exactly one compile is published.
- SIGTERM during the refresh: exit 0 in 2.2 s, no publication, journal unchanged after exit.
- `ingest.autoCompile: false`: the search answers, all 6,000 sources import, and nothing compiles.
- One-shot `openclaw wiki search zirconium`: still waits for import and compile (508 s on a loaded host) and returns the new page.
- Without `runInDetachedAsyncContext`, both runs logged `background source sync failed: Failed to open the plugin state database. | This operation was aborted` and never published.

Unit: `tool.deadline.test.ts` "answers from the current index while the service refreshes" fails on base with `wiki_search timed out after 30s` and passes here. Focused memory-wiki suites pass: 8 files, 95 tests. Local review on the head reports no findings.

## Merge Danger

Two-way door. No config, schema, protocol or stored-data change; a revert restores the awaited sync. Blast radius: memory-wiki search through the agent tool and the `wiki.search` Gateway method while the plugin service runs.

fix(agents): stop whitespace tool-call runaways for every provider (#206754)

## What Problem This Solves

A model that stops closing a tool call and streams whitespace runs to the provider's output cap (128k tokens on some models, about 32 min at the measured rate). OpenClaw stopped this only for OpenAI Responses: the 4 KiB rule from #177659 and #179233 lived inside the Responses transport. Every other provider, including Chat Completions endpoints, had no limit. Each chunk that carried tool-call text counted as model progress, so no watchdog fired either.

When Responses did stop a runaway and the retries ran out, the user saw "The AI service is having trouble". The model's output caused the failure, not the service.

## Solution

- The agent-core stream consumer (`packages/agent-core/src/agent-stream-response.ts`) now owns the rule. It already stops repetitive text and thinking. Every provider's `toolcall_delta` passes through it. At 4 KiB of consecutive trailing whitespace in one tool call's arguments, it aborts the request and ends the response with `degenerate_output`. The bounded transient retry is unchanged.
- Removed from the Responses transport: `countToolCallTrailingWhitespace`, `DegenerateToolCallArgumentsError`, the per-call counter and the client abort.
- `degenerate_output` now has its own reply text: "The model's reply turned into a long run of blank characters, so OpenClaw stopped it. Send your message again, or choose another model."
- No output cap or timeout changed. No model or provider detection.

Credit: the 4 KiB rule and its rationale are @steipete's (#177659, #179233). This PR moves it to the shared owner.

## Evidence

| Check | Tier | Base (`844bfbfe`) | Head |
|---|---|---|---|
| Chat Completions whitespace runaway through the real transport and agent loop (`agent-loop.degenerate-output.test.ts`) | vitest-source | **fails**: the whole 60,000-char runaway streams, the turn does not end with `degenerate_output` | passes: aborted after 4 KiB, no tool runs, 1 request |
| 200 KiB tool argument with 4,095-char whitespace runs (same file) | vitest-source | passes | passes |
| Touched suites: Responses terminal-error, item-conflict integration, agent-loop async-tools and streaming, stream parity, debug labels, failure copy | vitest-source | | pass |
| `pnpm check:changed` (lint, typecheck core and tests, dead exports, boundaries) | static | | pass |
| `ocx build --dts` | full | | pass |

End-to-end replays (full build, `openclaw agent --local`, isolated scratch HOME/state/config, loopback fake provider replaying a captured runaway response at its captured pace: 20,009 events over 301 s; no credentials):

| Case | Base (`844bfbfe`) | Head |
|---|---|---|
| Chat Completions, every request runs away | **no abort**: each request streamed all 60,013 chars for ~330 s and ended only because the capture ran out; 2 requests, 682 s, "LLM request timed out." (a live provider runs each attempt to the output cap) | each request aborted at ~23 s (1,406 frames); 5 requests (1 + 4 retries); 149 s; the new reply text |
| Responses, every request runs away | ~23 s per request, 5 requests, 154 s, "The AI service is having trouble." | ~23 s per request, 5 requests, 153 s, the new reply text |
| Responses, runaway then a normal answer | 47 s, the answer | 43 s, the answer |

## Accepted edge cases

- A real tool argument with a 4 KiB run of literal whitespace is stopped. This is the existing accepted risk; JSON escapes newlines, so real indentation stays far below it. It now applies to every provider.
- Providers that send only a final snapshot and no argument deltas are not covered (unchanged).

fix: let started participant runs and requests finish after an access change (#206747)

## Problem

Root `AGENTS.md` ("Choose good compromises") says: check authority one time, when work starts. Revocation, removal and reload apply to the next request. A started request may finish. #204249 removed the mid-run re-check from the admitted operator authority. Some code added later checks authority again after the work has started:

- **Participant runs (major).** A membership change aborted the invited person's work that had already started. This happened when the creator removed the person or lowered their access below `send`. It covered the running turn, its tool calls, its spawned children and its completion handoffs. A registry of `AbortController`s in `session-participation-source.ts` was merged into the run authority's signal. That is the latched re-check #204249 deleted.
- **Plugin request grants (major).** `withPluginGatewayRequestAuthority` called `operatorAccessAuthority.assertCurrent()` each time a plugin required its grant. A Beam visitor upload or continuation that was already admitted was refused after its body arrived.
- **One-request re-reads (minor).** These requests read the policy at start and again at commit, so a role change during the request gave a different answer:
  - Session invite and access change: "Invitee role changed before invitation commit".
  - @mention invitation: "Mention invitation is not authorized".
  - Invited-workspace eligibility predicate (`isInvitedWorkspaceTarget`), which re-read membership per call.
  - ClawHub sign-in polling.

User-visible failure: the same person, with the same request, gets a refusal or an aborted run only because of when an admin acted.

## Fix

Deletion only:

- Delete the participation producer registry (`retainSessionParticipation`, `revokeSessionParticipation`, `publishSessionParticipationMemberChange`) and the `participationSignal` path into the run authority, typing, recovery and `retainForRun`. The run signal is Stop again.
- Delete `access.assertCurrent()` in `src/plugins/runtime/gateway-request-authority.ts`. The start-time plugin match stays.
- Delete the commit-time re-reads in `sessions-sharing.ts`, `human-mention-invitation.ts` and `templates-drafts.ts`. In `session-scoped-read.ts`, the invited-workspace predicate now uses the membership read once per request.
- ClawHub sign-in keeps its request-lifetime fences (connection still open, commit guard) and its registry-URL fence. Only the administrator-policy re-read is gone.

Kept:

- Start-time admission and the participation ceiling.
- Queued-input cancellation on a membership reduction. Queued work is new work, so it is admitted again when it starts.
- Recovery re-admission (`invitation-ended`).
- Stop.
- Session-incarnation, `expectedEntry` CAS, connection-lifetime and registry-URL data fences.

Production code: about +22 / −198. No schema, protocol or config change.

Not in this PR: the older `retainSessionScopedRead().assertCurrent` (2026-09/10) still re-checks visibility after a read is admitted. It predates the one-admission work and gets its own change.

## User impact

- An invited person's started turn, tools, children and completions finish after the creator removes them or lowers their access. Their next message is refused as before, and their queued messages are still cancelled.
- An admitted Beam visitor upload or continuation finishes.
- Invite, mention, scoped-read and ClawHub sign-in requests give the answer that was decided when the request started.

## Evidence

See the comment.

perf(cli): host every one-shot core worker lane in the shared host (#206760)

## Problem

Since #206721 a one-shot command such as `openclaw agent --local` runs its core storage workers in the shared worker host. The host still admits only one endpoint per kind key, a rule that keeps the lean Gateway's memory accounting per kind. A one-shot turn opens more than one lane of some kinds (extra session transcript lanes, a second state reader), and each extra lane still boots its own worker isolate and loads its own copy of the storage code before the first model request.

## Fix

`src/infra/shared-worker-host.ts`: in a process with the `cli-oneshot` database role, `claimsSharedHostSlot` hosts every lane of a hosted kind, not only the first. The lean Gateway keeps one endpoint per key. Everything else in the shared host is unchanged (Postgres engines and runtimes without qualified SQLite close keep dedicated workers; a failed hosted task replaces the whole host).

Docs: `docs/gateway/config-gateway.md` notes the one-shot behavior.

## Evidence

Work removed before the first request (traced run): worker threads 14 -> 11, modules loaded across all threads 11,611 -> 9,666.

Build of this change against a build of #206721 on an otherwise idle M1 (batch started at load 2.8), alternating runs, n=10 per side: median 4.87 s -> 4.39 s, p90 4.89 s -> 4.45 s (0.901, -483 ms). Against the base before #206721: 5.59 s -> 4.39 s.

## Problem

A one-shot command such as `openclaw agent --local` starts a separate worker thread for each core storage worker before its first model request: SQLite store carriers, the session transcript worker, the state reader and the plugin model catalog reader. Each worker loads its own copy of the shared storage code (the SQLite store worker alone loads about 460 modules), and the command waits for them.

The Gateway already has an owner for this: in the `lean` resource profile, `claimsSharedHostSlot` runs the first worker of each of these kinds as a logical endpoint in one shared host isolate, so the common code loads once.

`src/infra/shared-worker-host.ts`: `claimsSharedHostSlot` also hosts when the process runs with the `cli-oneshot` database process role. Everything else in the shared host stays the same: one endpoint per slot key, dedicated workers where SQLite close does not release native resources and for Postgres engines, and a failed hosted task replaces the whole host. The Gateway's profile selection, memory budget and lean startup behavior are unchanged.

Docs: `docs/gateway/config-gateway.md` notes that one-shot CLI commands use the shared host.

fix(codex): keep managed relay context in the cached prefix (#206554)

Root cause: extensions/codex/src/app-server/thread-lifecycle-run.ts:154 dropped the native thread developer carrier whenever the managed inference relay existed, and extensions/codex/src/app-server/run-attempt-turn-request.ts:293 put skills, shared persona, memory and session project guidance into the relay text that inference-context.ts:271 adds to every request's top-level `instructions`. GPT-6.2 Sol and Astra never cache `instructions`, so every warm request in a turn re-paid that whole block.

Fixes #206421

Thanks @brandon-julio-t for the precise report (managed vs `appServer.command` A/B with per-request usage), and @NaturalMatchaKing for the A/B evidence in #204136.

## What changed

- Skills, shared persona (`SOUL.md`, `IDENTITY.md`, workspace-root `USER.md`), memory guidance and session project guidance now always ride the existing refreshable thread developer section, on managed connections too. Codex sends that as a `developer` input item, so it sits in the cached prefix, and later requests in a turn only append.
- The relay keeps only parent-only text: the selected personal `users/<id>/USER.md` overlay, cron policy, plugin `before_prompt_build` system context, and per-turn conversation instructions. Per-turn plugin context stays off the thread on relay connections (`turnRefreshableInstructions` split; still thread-carried when there is no relay, as before).
- `workspace-context.ts` renders the personal-only persona with the same renderer; the codex context plumbs `personalPersonaInstructions` instead of the full persona.
- Edits to that section no longer refuse a thread kept alive by background work. Before this, a skill, persona or memory edit made the next message cold-resume the thread, and a thread kept alive by a running background command refused with "still has background work… stop its running work and retry". `appServer.command` and other non-relay connections already failed this way on main; managed connections would have started to with the carrier move. Now the refreshable section is left out of the thread configuration fingerprint, and persistent live threads keep the same in-memory record incognito threads already had of the section the thread was natively given (`nativeRefreshableInstructions`) and the one last delivered. On reuse (`thread-lifecycle-warm.ts`):
  - Idle thread, section changed: cold resume, as on main, so native configuration carries the current section and compaction rebuilds from it. On managed connections this costs one uncached turn per edit.
  - Protected thread (running background command or child), section changed: the existing appended developer handoff instead of the refusal; the existing post-compaction restore re-delivers it.
  - Self-heal: the first later turn where the thread is no longer protected and its native section still differs from the current one cold-resumes.
  - Managed relay fallback: while a thread's native section differs from the current one (an edited incognito thread, or a protected persistent thread waiting for its cold resume), the relay also sends the current section in request `instructions`, as main did for every request, so a post-compaction continuation sees it. It stops when the native copy matches again (after the self-heal cold resume); unedited threads never pay for it. The section never holds the selected personal overlay, so that is still sent once (`renderCodexRelayRefreshableFallback`, thread-policy.ts).

  No new field, flag or persisted state: the comparison uses the in-memory record, and ephemeral lifetime is keyed off the generic policy that only ephemeral records carry.
- Remaining narrow gap, only on connections without a relay (`appServer.command`): an edit made while background work keeps the thread protected, followed by a native compaction before that work ends, can let one continuation request see the previous section. On main those threads refuse the next turn outright. Codex samples the continuation right after compaction, before injected developer messages are drained (`codex-rs/core/src/session/turn.rs` pending-input drain is deferred after auto-compaction; `session/inject.rs` queues injections into the active turn), and the host restore lands on the request after it. It heals on the first unprotected turn. Not taken: (B) carrying the section in turn-level `collaborationMode.settings.developer_instructions`, because a model catalog's default-mode override wins over caller text, it replaces the built-in Default-mode text and collides with OpenClaw's cron collaboration instructions, and native children do not inherit it; (D) asking Codex to drain injected developer messages before the post-compaction continuation, or to accept developer instructions in thread settings, needs a Codex dependency bump.
- Report estimate counts the stable section on the thread in both modes.
- No model-facing wording changed. Layout change: a user with a personal overlay gets two `## OpenClaw Agent Soul` blocks (shared in the thread, personal in the relay).
- `inference-dispatch.ts` untouched (#206475 size recovery kept).

## What remains: 97.2% vs 99.5%

Live gpt-6.2-sol against main `712db11dfc9e`, the reporter's five-tool-call turn. Two runs per arm on `2ca1ebe03be6` plus one per arm on `a286631217b9` (the stale-section cold resume does not touch an unedited turn; earlier heads had three runs per arm with the same results). Warm-request cache hit and per-request `input/cached` come from the Codex rollout:

| arm | warm hit | uncached input per warm request | previous request's input not cached | uncached input per turn |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| main, managed relay | 70.6–70.7% | ~6,150–6,200 tokens | 6,054–6,100 tokens | 51.5–51.8k |
| this PR, managed relay | 97.2–97.3% | ~570 tokens | 421 tokens | 23.9–24.0k |
| `appServer.command` (no relay) | 99.5% | ~100 tokens | 3 tokens | 20.5–20.6k |

The remaining ~420 tokens per warm request are the relay's per-turn conversation instructions and tool bindings, which still go in top-level `instructions` and are never cached on these models. They are per-turn facts, so moving them is a separate change (for example to turn `additionalContext`); this PR does not move them.

## Earlier attempt

#141270 (@mbelinky) aimed at the same carrier: workspace persona and memory on the thread developer instructions. This PR is a smaller change at the relay/lifecycle owners and does not build on it.

## Deliberate decision reversed

This reverses #142276's parent-only delivery for shared text: native Codex subagents now inherit shared persona, skills and memory guidance through `developer_instructions` (`codex-rs/core/src/agent/child_config.rs` `inherited_developer_instructions`). Reasoning: that is already the behavior of every connection without a relay (#162156 called it intentional); native delegation is off wherever session tools are denied; the original #142276 problem (catalog collaboration text replacing caller instructions) is solved by thread developer instructions; and keeping the split costs every managed user about 2.2x the uncached input on a five-tool-call turn (51.8k vs 24.0k tokens; about 11x per warm request). The personal overlay stays parent-only (#162156 privacy boundary kept). A child created after an in-place edit inherits the thread's creation-time section, the same limitation incognito threads already document.

## Evidence

Proof comments: https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/206554#issuecomment-7215064392 (cache and request bodies), https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/206554#issuecomment-7217281740 (background-work P1), https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/206554#issuecomment-7218972144 (`2ca1ebe03be6`: scripted lane, live cache, live managed P1), https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/206554#issuecomment-7219739492 (`a286631217b9`: stale-section cold resume, compaction and self-heal regressions, live P1 on both routes, cache), https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/206554#issuecomment-7221292749 (`76341cb30f58`: managed relay fallback regression, live managed P1). Child-inheritance decision: https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/206554#issuecomment-7218963071

- Scripted lane (real managed bundled codex 0.172.0 app-server, real relay, synthetic Responses upstream recording bodies): `run-attempt.skills.native.test.ts` "keeps managed skills in the cached native prefix across a multi-request turn" is red on main (skills in `instructions` on every frame) and green here (marker once in a `developer` input item, each frame's input extends the previous one byte-for-byte).
- Background-work regression: `run-attempt.native-background-outcome.test.ts` "refreshes edited skills on a protected thread, then cold-resumes once it ends" (managed relay and `appServer.command`): the protected edit arrives as one handoff with no refusal, and after the listener ends the next turn unsubscribes and cold-resumes with the edited catalog. Red on `8fd3970192d6` (refusal) and on `2ca1ebe03be6` (no self-heal); green here.
- Compaction regression: `run-attempt.skills.native.test.ts` "keeps a withdrawn catalog withdrawn after native compaction rebuilds the persistent thread" (real Codex binary, pre-sampling auto-compaction): the continuation request after compaction no longer carries the withdrawn creation catalog. Red on `2ca1ebe03be6`, green here; the incognito case keeps its documented one-request reversion.
- Real Gateway + `openclaw agent`, gpt-6.2-sol, a native-shell `sleep` listener started on turn 1, a skill installed with `openclaw skills install`, then turn 2: previous head refuses on both routes; this PR answers with the new skill on both, through a warm refresh handoff, with turn 2's first request cached up to the previous input. After a Gateway restart, the cold resume carries the current section.

## Merge danger

Two-way door: no stored state, schema or config changes; a revert restores the previous layout. On first turn after upgrade each managed thread gets one cold resume (Gateway restart) that installs the section, as before. Restricted threads on connections without a relay rotate once after upgrade because their stored fingerprint included the section; afterwards edits cold-resume them instead of rotating them. Blast radius: Codex harness thread lifecycle and relay instructions.
