fix: keep workspace Changes visible while it refreshes after a run (#206720)

Root cause: ui/src/pages/chat/components/chat-session-workspace-state.ts:408 (`delete workspace.diffContent` in `refreshSessionWorkspaceState`) drops the last accepted Uncommitted totals on every post-run refresh, so the Changes row (and Environment when it is the only fact) unmounts until the replacement summary read returns.

Fixes #206367

## What Problem This Solves

In a chat whose workspace has uncommitted changes, the Details sidebar's Environment → Changes row disappears every time the agent finishes a turn, then comes back when the Gateway answers the new totals read. With a large checkout or a slow read the section is gone for seconds, and with an agent that keeps working it flickers in and out, as @alexph-dev reported on 2026.11.10 with 110 modified files.

## User Impact

The Changes row stays visible while it refreshes and its numbers update in place when the new totals arrive. Switching to another session or a replaced checkout still starts empty, a late answer for the previous workspace is still ignored, and a clean workspace still shows no Changes row.

## Why This Change Was Made

#125785 made a run's refresh replace the diff content so an open Review panel and the Environment totals re-read the checkout. It also threw away the totals the old content had accepted. The refresh now returns the content it retired, and `refreshSessionWorkspace` seeds the replacement with those totals only when both belong to the same workspace owner. The new loader replaces them on its first accepted result. The retired loader's late results still fail the existing `current.load !== content.load` check. Checkout retirement and session changes still create a fresh workspace with no totals. No new state: the existing `uncommitted` field carries the value.

Production +19/-13, tests +40/-0 (one regression, red on base: `expected undefined to be 4656`).

## Evidence

Built Gateway + Control UI from both commits in a secretless `node:24.22.1` container, real Chromium 156, real git workspaces (agent edits 110 tracked files: `110 files changed, 4730 insertions(+), 110 deletions(-)`; a second workspace with 3 files; a clean one). Each real agent turn ends with a terminal chat event that refreshes the workspace. Environment and its Changes row were sampled every 100 ms, plus DOM transitions. Two runs per build.

| Phase | main (ecfd42f8d0) x2 | this PR (319da32c7a; 22f9134d01 only narrows types) x2 |
|---|---|---|
| refresh after agent edit 1 | row and Environment unmount 47 ms / 352 ms | never hidden, `+4730 −110` |
| refresh after agent edit 2 | unmount 71 ms / 1055 ms | never hidden, updates to `+4725 −228` |
| same refresh, summary read held 2 s | unmount 2079 ms / 2546 ms ("No session details to show.") | never hidden, `+4725 −228` then `+4733 −287` |
| switch to other workspace while main's read is held, held answer lands after switch | shows only `+129 −3` | shows only `+129 −3` |
| clean workspace | no Changes row | no Changes row |

Observed lines: https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/206720#issuecomment-7220260017. Before/after screenshots: https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/206720#issuecomment-7220262213.

Unit: `chat-session-workspace-loading.test.ts` plus every test file importing the changed modules (41 files, 589 tests) pass. `pnpm check:changed` passes except the dead-export scan, which flags `src/cli/gateway-cli/run-loop-startup.ts` and `src/update/gateway-trial.ts` (not touched here).

Thanks @alexph-dev for the report and the 110-file shortstat.

## Problem

`openclaw-boundaries/no-operator-permission-read` (#204823) blocks new live permission reads in files outside its allowlist. Since then, post-start authority re-checks landed through three paths the rule cannot see:

- A started run's authority rebuilt with a separate revocation signal: `createAdmittedRunOperatorAuthority({ ...authority, signal })` in new files (`session-sharing-authorization-async.ts`, `operator-run-invocation.ts`).
- `client.internal?.operatorAccessAuthority?.assertCurrent()` after a request was admitted (`question-session-access.ts`, `session-communication-approval.ts`).
- New reader calls in files that were already allowlisted. The allowlist was per file, so any number of new reads passed.

Each one gives one person different answers depending on timing, which the root `AGENTS.md` rule "Decide authority once" forbids.

## Change

Tooling only. No runtime code changes.

`scripts/lib/no-operator-permission-read.mjs`:
- Every list now maps a file to its reference count today. A file in a list fails on the reference after its count, so a new read in a listed file fails too.
- New check: `createAdmittedRunOperatorAuthority` outside its definition and the 7 current callers (`MINT_FILES`).
- New check: `….operatorAccessAuthority.assertCurrent` outside the 2 current files (`ACCESS_RECHECK_FILES`).
- Messages start with `Permission read:`, `Run authority minted:` or `Access re-check:`.

`test/scripts/oxlint-boundary-guards.test.ts`:
- The stale-entry test now requires each listed count to equal the references found. When a reference is removed, its count must be lowered in the same change.
- New fixture `run-authority-mint-violation.ts`: 4 findings (one access re-check, three minter references).

The lists start at today's callers and can only shrink. Some of those call sites are post-start re-checks that a separate change removes; that change lowers these counts.

`src/gateway/AGENTS.md`: the Lint bullet names the new checks and per-file counts.

## Evidence

- `test/scripts/oxlint-boundary-guards.test.ts`: 40/40 pass. The new fixture reports lines 1, 4, 8, 9, and the counts match all 58 + 7 + 2 listed files exactly.
- `node scripts/run-oxlint.mjs --openclaw-focused-config --config config/oxlint/boundary-guards.json src extensions packages`: 0 errors.

## Problem

#206675 declares small MCP catalogs directly in the tool list. It decided which tools are direct in two places:

- **The default embedded runner:** the session's tool-listing pin decides. The tool list is byte-stable.
- **Runners that do not pin a session tool listing** (plugin-SDK agent harnesses): the decision came from each run's MCP inventory. The tool-overhead brief rules this out: tool lists are decided from session and config facts, never per turn.

- When it is unset, every MCP tool stays deferred.
- Only the embedded runner sets it, in `installToolListingPin`. It sets it to the established pin, or, on a series' first request, to the tools chosen by size.

perf(agents): declare small MCP catalogs directly and call deferred tools without describe (#206675)

## Problem

Every MCP tool is deferred behind Tool Search. Even for a name listed in the system-prompt directory, the model is told to call `tool_describe` first and then `dispatch_action`. That is two model round trips per tool use. On the HF GH Sol run, 2 of every 3 tool calls were this discovery overhead.

## Solution

1. **Small MCP catalogs are declared directly.** On the first request of a prompt series, if the run's MCP tools need at most 8,192 bytes (name, description and input schema together), they are listed with full schemas next to the controls, and the model calls them by name.
   - **How the threshold was chosen:** a direct catalog costs its size on every request. Each discovery step it avoids saves one re-sent request (about 51.5 KB on a fresh install) plus a `tool_describe` result (about 1 KB). Over an 8-request session these break even near 8.2 KB.
   - **Measured MCP catalogs:** 5-tool tracker 2.1 KB and server-everything 7.8 KB are declared directly. filesystem 14 KB, github 16 KB and playwright 19 KB stay behind search.
   - **Stability:** later turns keep exactly the MCP tools the session's tool listing already sends (`catalogRef.sessionPinnedToolNames`, installed by `installToolListingPin`). The provider tool list stays byte-stable. A tool a server adds mid-series goes to the directory.
   - **These stay deferred:** names that another tool also uses (a lookalike never shadows a trusted direct tool), and tools of a server that advertises instructions (`tool_describe` returns those instructions). Configured `include`/`exclude` selectors keep their own split.
2. **Call by name without `tool_describe`.** `dispatch_action` now validates MCP input after hooks, without coercion, the same way it already validates OpenClaw tools. When arguments are invalid, the error carries the tool's full input schema (up to 8,192 characters), so the model can retry in one step. An MCP schema that OpenClaw cannot compile still reaches the server.
3. **Wording.** These texts no longer require `tool_describe` before a call: the MCP directory heading, the `dispatch_action` and `tool_search` descriptions, and the unknown-id recovery hint. The exception is a server that advertises instructions: its directory rows are marked `[instructions]`, and the heading tells the model to call `tool_describe` first for them, because that is where the instructions are returned. fix(gateway): continuation turns keep the admitted owner grant (#206665)

## Problem

In the owner's own Control UI session, a turn the Gateway starts for that session (a background `exec` completion after a Gateway restart, a scheduler turn, a tool handoff whose sender flag was unset) lost the owner's authority. The model then got `portal needs the owner's authority, and this turn was not started by the owner` and told the owner to "send any message" to get it back. The same person got a different answer depending on how the turn started.

Root cause: `buildSessionEventContext` (`src/auto-reply/reply/session-event-context.ts`) bound the command-owner authority only when the admitted grant said owner **and** the turn kind was `restart`, a scheduled run, or the target carried an `ownerContinuation` flag. Only the live same-session exec notifier and some tool handoffs set that flag. A durable exec wake (`captureOwedRequesterTarget`, used for a process restored after a restart and for stored owed rows) re-admits the requester through `restoreGatewayQueuedOperatorRecovery`, gets `grant.owner === true`, and then lost it at this gate: `senderIsOwner` became `false`, owner-only tools were refused.

Observed on main (`39b6a89d2984`, real isolated Gateway, real model, token-auth Control UI owner session): after `gateway.restart.request`, the wake for the interrupted command ran with the admitted owner grant but `senderIsOwner: false`, and its tool surface treated it as a non-owner turn.

## Fix

The admitted grant is the only producer of the owner decision for a session-event turn (`decideOperatorAdmission` → `grant.owner`). Turn kind no longer narrows it.

- `session-event-context.ts`: bind owner authority when `operatorAuthority.grant.owner`; no turn-kind condition.
- Delete the `ownerContinuation` flag and every producer and reader: `session-event-target.ts` (scope field, option, reader, batch check), `bash-tools.exec-notify.ts`, `session-tool-handoff.ts` (and the `senderIsOwner` pass-through in `github-publish-tool.ts`, `session-project-tool.ts`, `sessions-send-self-hold.ts`), `cron-job-turn-target.ts`.
- `portal-tool.ts`: delete the local `senderIsOwner === false` refusal. The turn's owner-only tool gate (`resolveTurnToolSurface` → `gateAgentToolExecution`, and the HTTP/loopback `ownerOnlyDeny`) already refuses a non-owner call without a conversation worker.
- The owner-only gate's refusal comes from the cause table: new `owner-only` cause in `src/gateway/operator-refusal.ts` with a next step ("Ask the Gateway owner to do it."). The text no longer says "this turn was not started by the owner", which led the model to ask the owner to send another message.

Production: +14 / −54.

Decisions recorded (standing authority):
- A completion that a requester's command routed to another chat (`cross-session` row in `bash-tools.exec-notify.owner-continuation.test.ts`) now runs with that requester's admitted grant, like every other continuation. Before, it already carried that grant for control-plane tools; only the sender flag differed. Test row updated.
- A scheduler turn about a job (`cron`, `cron_failure_repair`) now takes the owner bit from its restored source's grant (admin scope), not from the extra `automationAdmin` delegation flag. The `automations` capability itself is unchanged.
- No widening beyond the recorded principal's own grant: a member's or guest's continuation still has `owner: false` and gets the cause-table refusal.

Other tools that still refuse locally on `senderIsOwner` (outside this PR, OA2 PR 6 sweep): `src/agents/tools/conversation-tools.ts:71`, `session-project-tool.ts:67`, `sessions-tool.ts:194,387`, `openclaw-delegate-tool.ts:293`, `extensions/codex/src/{command-diagnostics.ts:63,native-plugin-tool.ts:46,native-thread-tool.ts:166,supervision-tools.ts:706}`, `extensions/discord/src/actions/handle-action.guild-admin.ts:64,77`, `extensions/imessage/src/actions.ts:291`, `extensions/matrix/src/tool-actions.ts:348,422`, `extensions/visitor-access/src/tools.ts:84`, `extensions/whatsapp/src/agent-tools-login.ts:41`.

## User impact

After a Gateway restart, the owner's session can open portals and use other owner-only tools again from the automatic completion turn. A real non-owner continuation is refused with "I did not run portal. It needs the Gateway owner's authority, and this turn does not run with it. Ask the Gateway owner to do it."

## Evidence

- Regression: `src/gateway/owed-exec-requester.test.ts` reads the woken turn's own owner decision (the context the session event builds, as commands and owner tools read it) for `exec`, `restart` and `tool_handoff` on the same admitted target. Red on the merge base (admin and configured channel owner cells: `owner: { exec: false, restart: true, tool_handoff: false }`), green on head. Member cell stays `owner: false`.
- Matrix note in `src/gateway/operator-admission.table.test.ts` points at those continuation cells.
- E2E: see the comment below (real isolated Gateway, real model, owner Control UI session, `gateway.restart.request`; plus the one-admission Q/R/S run).

perf(cli): reuse startup plugin metadata in one-shot commands (#206677)

## Problem

A one-shot command such as `openclaw agent --local` scans every plugin manifest twice before its first model request. The startup config preflight builds the plugin metadata snapshot in a private plugin cache and discards it. The command then loads the CLI plugin registry in its own invocation cache and scans the same manifests again, with the same cache key. Gateway startup does not have this problem because it adopts the preflight cache itself (`src/cli/program/config-guard.ts`).

## Fix

`src/commands/startup-config-preflight.ts`: when the preflight is not Gateway startup, read plugin metadata into the current plugin cache. In a CLI command that cache is the invocation cache that `withCliPluginInvocation` owns, so the plugin registry load reuses the snapshot. Gateway startup keeps its private preflight cache, its migration lease and its adoption.

Accepted edge case: after an in-process `doctor --fix` from the invalid-config prompt, the retried validation reads the same invocation cache that the command already used after the repair. The cache key still includes the config policy, so a config change always scans again.

## Evidence

Workload: cold `openclaw agent --local --message "Reply with exactly: ok" --json`, fresh 0700 HOME, state and config per run, empty caches, local fake OpenAI Responses server. Metric: process start to the first request byte at the provider.

Work removed (diagnostics timeline, same turn): `plugins.metadata.scan` spans before the first request, 5 -> 3 (main: 725, 196, 20, 17, 249 ms; this change: 198, 22, 18 ms on a loaded Studio host). Besides the duplicate registry scan, the run's prepared model runtime no longer scans again.

Time on mbp-m1 (M1, Node 24.22.1, load 2.5-4.0), ABAB interleaved, n=10 per side, one build with the change switched by environment:

| | median | p90 |
|---|---|---|
| main | 5.82 s | 5.86 s |
| this change | 5.64 s | 5.65 s |

Ratio 0.968 (-187 ms).

Tests: `src/commands/startup-config-preflight*`, `src/commands/config-preflight-snapshot.test.ts`, `src/cli/program/config-guard*`, `src/cli/command-execution-startup.test.ts`, `src/cli/invalid-config-recovery*`, `src/commands/doctor-config-preflight*`, `src/cli/agent-local-cold-start.process.test.ts`.

fix(ui): keep pre-final assistant text visible after a completed turn (#140835)

Root cause: `ui/src/pages/chat/chat-turn-presentation.ts:150` (`isCollapsibleWorkGroup`) treats every assistant text group that is not an explicit final answer as foldable work in a completed OpenAI turn. Text written before a tool call over Chat Completions has no phase label, only `stopReason: "toolUse"`, so a long explanation the user already read folds into **Worked for…** with the tools, and only the short closing line stays.

## What Problem This Solves

Reported by @leapdragon on 2026.9.2 with an `openai-completions` transport: the agent streams a long reply, calls a tool, then writes a short final line. When the turn completes, the long reply disappears behind the **Worked for** row. Current main still does this for OpenAI models over Chat Completions (OpenAI-compatible proxies such as LiteLLM/OpenRouter-style providers).

## Why This Change Was Made

Rule: assistant text folds into **Worked for…** only when the model labels it `commentary`. Unlabeled text stays visible below the one **Worked for** row, in source order. Tools, reasoning and labeled commentary still fold; there is still one rollup per turn (#188045).

Why this rule:
- The label is the model's own signal. OpenAI models that emit `phase` are told commentary may be hidden, so folding it loses nothing.
- A length cut-off or other guess about whether model text is "just status" would be a heuristic judge on model output. An absent label is unknown, not commentary, as #197429 argued.
- Where no label exists, the text stays visible, which is what every non-OpenAI model already does since #197429. This makes OpenAI-over-Chat-Completions consistent with that, not a new layout.

Where the label comes from:

| Path | Pre-tool text labeled `commentary`? | Source |
|---|---|---|
| OpenAI Responses, models that emit `phase` | Yes, folds | `packages/ai/src/transports/openai-responses-stream-internal.ts` stores `item.phase` as the text signature |
| Codex app-server harness | Yes, when Codex sends a phase | `extensions/codex/src/app-server/transcript-history-projection.ts` keeps the item phase |
| OpenAI Responses, models without `phase` | No, stays visible | Same transport; no phase to store |
| Chat Completions, any model | No, stays visible | The format has no phase field |

Known cost: on Chat Completions and on Responses models that don't emit `phase`, short status lines such as "Let me check the notes file." now stay visible under **Worked for** instead of folding.

This ports @leapdragon's fix from the old `chat-thread-grouping.ts` (now a thin wrapper) to the current presentation owner. The old review finding (tool batches on either side of kept text) doesn't apply here, because the current owner partitions work and answers separately instead of scanning backwards.

## User Impact

- Text written before a tool call without a commentary label stays visible after the turn completes and after reload.
- Labeled commentary, reasoning and tool activity still fold into **Worked for…**.
- Turns without tools and non-OpenAI turns don't change.

## Evidence

Built Gateway and Control UI (Docker, `node:24.22.1`), scripted models (`proxy/openai/gpt-5.4` on `openai-completions`, `resp/openai/gpt-5.5` on `openai-responses`), real Chromium. Each scenario runs in its own dashboard session: during streaming, after completion, then after reload.

| Build | Wire | Long pre-tool text | Short unlabeled status line | Labeled commentary | No-tool turn |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| main `41fcd490fb4d` (2 runs) | Chat Completions | folded away | folded | n/a | visible |
| main `41fcd490fb4d` | Responses | n/a | folded | folded | n/a |
| fix `77ec6f2633f5` | Chat Completions | visible (after and reload) | visible | n/a | visible |
| fix `77ec6f2633f5` | Responses | n/a | visible | folded | n/a |

Proof lines: https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/140835#issuecomment-7218726163. Screenshots: https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/140835#issuecomment-7218723412.

Regression test `keeps unlabeled pre-tool text visible while labeled commentary folds` in `chat-thread-grouping.test.ts` covers the boundary. Tests that covered other folding rules now use labeled commentary fixtures. Tests that asserted unlabeled text folds now expect it to stay visible. Focused chat presentation suites pass (17 files, 310 tests, plus browser shards).

## Merge danger

Two-way door: display grouping only, with no stored history, config or protocol change. A revert restores the previous folding. Blast radius: completed dashboard turns answered by OpenAI models without a commentary label.

fix: observer fallback models get time after a primary timeout (#191669)

Root cause: src/gateway/session-observer-completion.ts:131 arms one observer timer of 30 s × candidates that covers preparation, both JSON attempts and every utility candidate, while isolated completion already gives each model call its own hard 30 s deadline; time spent before and between candidates comes out of the observer timer only, so the last configured fallback is aborted inside its own budget (`caller_signal_aborted`) and the notice loses the "fallbacks exhausted" detail.

Related: #191600 (closed by #191653, still reproducible per the 2026-11-20 follow-up), #191653, #196345

Thanks @Marvinthebored for the original report, @dankarization for the detailed follow-up on the N×30 s build, and @he-yufeng for the fix this builds on.

## What Problem This Solves

With `utilityModel.fallbacks` configured, Control UI session assessments stop for the run even though a fallback answers inside its own 30 s. The observer's outer timer ran out first, the chain stopped as `caller_signal_aborted`, and after two rounds the chat showed "add capable utilityModel.fallbacks", the setting the user already had.

## Why This Change Was Made

`runIsolatedCompletion` owns each call's deadline (fresh per candidate and per JSON attempt) and enforces it without provider cooperation. The observer now keeps a flat 30 s timer for preparation only and clears it as soon as preparation finishes; caller cancellation (run end, demotion, dispose) still aborts the shared controller. #191653 scaled the observer timer by candidate count; that keeps two owners with equal budgets, so overhead always lands on the last candidate. This removes that arithmetic (`resolveObserverDeadlineMs`).

## User Impact

- A fallback that answers within its own 30 s produces a digest instead of the warning.
- When every candidate times out, the chain still ends (about N × 30 s per attempt), and the existing notice now names each attempted model with `timeout`, because the real `FailoverError` reaches it.
- Worst case for a fully hung chain is 30 s preparation plus 30 s per call per JSON attempt. The per-call 30 s is unchanged and not configurable here.

## Changes

- `session-observer-completion.ts`: delete `resolveObserverDeadlineMs`; 30 s timer bounds preparation only (he-yufeng's `clearTimeout` after preparation kept).
- Tests: one regression through the real `runUtilityCompletion` (2 s preparation, primary times out at 30 s, fallback answers at 29 s), red on main; the stuck-completion and settlement tests no longer depend on the observer aborting the call; removed the candidate-budget test, the duplicated `it.each` cases and the test-lines allocation file.

## Evidence

- New regression fails on main `28dbf4784175` (`expected { headline: "Recovered" }`, received `session observer model call timed out or was cancelled`) and passes here; observer suites 84 passed.
- Isolated Gateway with the real Control UI in Chromium and a loopback OpenAI-compatible stub: primary hangs, fallback answers 27 s into its own 30 s, 5 s local pre-call time per call. Main, twice: fallback cut at about 24 s with `caller_signal_aborted`, no digest, banner without fallback details. This PR, twice: fallback answers at 27.0 s, digests arrive, no banner.
- Controls on this PR: all three candidates hang -> each closes at 30.0 s, chain ends at 90 s, banner names every candidate with `timeout`; Stop mid-candidate -> chain stops 15 ms after `chat.abort` and the next run is observed; a preparation that never returns stays held by the existing physical-settlement rule (unchanged).
- Proof: https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/191669#issuecomment-7218498742 · screenshots: https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/191669#issuecomment-7218502084

## Merge danger

Two-way door: one production file, no config, schema or stored state; a revert restores the previous timer. Blast radius: background session-observer assessments only; chat replies are not affected.

fix(memory): remember an implicit endpoint that refuses embeddings (#206582)

## Problem
With `memory.search.provider` unset or `auto`, memory search embeds through the OpenAI provider's endpoint. That endpoint is often a custom `models.providers.openai.baseUrl`, such as a proxy, router or metering meter, with no `/v1/embeddings` route. Each new process asked again and got refused; one public benchmark logged 56–449 refused calls per cell. Worse, on `main` the first refusal leaves an fts-only index behind. Every later search in that workspace then answers "memory search is paused because the current memory configuration no longer matches the index", so keyword results are lost too. Supersedes #206478, which guessed from the URL and would have broken proxies that do serve embeddings.

## Solution
Probe once and remember, owned by the Memory Core provider lifecycle:
- The first real embedding request is the probe. When the implicit endpoint answers 404, 405 or 501, the lifecycle records the refusal for that embedding identity (provider, baseUrl, model), logs one warning, and degrades to keyword-only through the existing bootstrap-failure path.
- In later processes, provider initialization finds the record and treats it like a missing credential: no provider is created, so no embedding calls are made.
- 401, 403, 429 and 5xx degrade only until the existing 30 s readiness window and are never recorded.
- An explicitly configured provider never uses this path (`providerRequirement` stays `required`).
- The record clears when the endpoint or model changes, or when `openclaw memory status --index` (a writable check) re-checks the endpoint and it now serves embeddings. Read-only readiness checks (`memory status --deep`, Control UI **Memory → Test**, `doctor.memory.status probe`) report the recorded refusal rather than a success they cannot record. Status shows a refusal only while the current configuration still resolves to that endpoint.
- The refusal key is the provider's own cache identity: provider, base URL, model and its credential-free routing headers (record or `[name, value]` pairs).
- With `memory.search.fallback` set, nothing is recorded: each process tries the primary and hands off to the fallback, as on `main`. (A configured fallback is an explicit embeddings config; remembering refusals there let a fallback hide or overwrite the primary's record.)
- Storage reuses the existing `memory_index_meta` table (key `memory_embedding_refusal_v1`). No new table and no schema change. It is read in the existing `index.facts` snapshot and the status snapshot, and written through a new `index.writeEmbeddingRefusal` publication command in the SQLite worker and the PostgreSQL publication path. It always goes to the published database, never to a reindex shadow.
- Visible: `openclaw memory status` prints `Embeddings: keyword-only: <host> refused embeddings for <model> (404); set memory.search.provider or memory.search.remote to use embeddings`, and status reports the keyword-only identity instead of a false "index paused" fix.
- `markLocalEmbeddingProviderDegraded` becomes `markEmbeddingProviderFailure`, because it now owns remote implicit failures too.

## Impact
- Custom chat endpoints without embeddings: at most the first sync's concurrent requests are refused, then nothing more, and keyword search keeps returning results.
- Proxies that serve embeddings keep semantic search (the round-3 case of #206478).
- Not changed: after an auth outage is fixed, the keyword index built during the outage still needs `openclaw memory status --index` to return to semantic search. That is existing behavior.
- Follow-up, not in this cut: `auto` is hard-coded to `"openai"` in core, and `autoSelectPriority` has no runtime reader.

## Evidence
Real CLI (`ocx build --dist`, dist-nodts), `env -i` scratch install. A fake endpoint is `models.providers.openai.baseUrl`; `memory.search` is unset. Each agent run makes N `memory_search` calls with distinct queries in a fresh session:

| case | embedding requests | searches with results |
|---|---|---|
| main, 404, 2 processes × 10 searches | 2 | 1 / 20; 19 paused ("index was built for model fts-only") |
| this PR, 404, 2 processes × 10 searches | 2 (both from the first sync's two files, sent concurrently), 0 afterwards | 20 / 20 |
| this PR, endpoint serves embeddings, provider unset | 6, all 200 | 3 / 3, with vector scores |
| this PR, 401 | 2, nothing recorded (`memory_index_meta` has no refusal key) | keyword results |

- After the 404 run, `openclaw memory status` prints the `Embeddings: keyword-only: 127.0.0.1:… refused …` line. With the endpoint switched to serving, `openclaw memory status --index` re-checked (4 requests, 200), printed `Embeddings: ready`, and deleted the record (measured before the read-only-probe change).
- `extensions/memory-core/src/embedding-refusal-real-transport.test.ts` runs a real HTTP endpoint and real managers:
  - 404: the first search refuses; later searches across closed managers and databases make no calls and return hits; status shows the line.
  - A serving endpoint keeps working.
  - 401 is not recorded.
  - The 404 case fails on base `d78611d842e5` (later searches paused) and passes here.
- Related suites pass: provider lifecycle, leases, retry, keyword retrieval, generic provider, status state, publication generation, probe, fallback, chunking-upgrade real transport. `cli.test.ts` "fails index --force after full verification records orphaned provenance" fails on base `d78611d842e5` too.

## What Problem This Solves

A healthy update can remain running while plugin maintenance is pending or aborted. Core readiness should finish the run; plugin downloads and result-notice failures must not hold it open.

## User Impact

Core settles at Gateway ready, and the CLI can exit. Plugin maintenance and Doctor inspections continue afterward through the existing watcher. The result notice remains independent.

## Why This Change Was Made

- Record the terminal result directly in `settleRunFromTrial`, then schedule the existing maintenance job before awaiting notification.
- Delete the plugin-gated completion closure, its in-progress plugin phase, and unused maintenance return values. No new status, phase, notice, record, flag, timer, retry or boot trigger.

fix(bedrock): tool-returned images fail on non-Claude routes such as GPT-6/6.1 Sol and Kimi K3 (#186834)

Root cause: `extensions/amazon-bedrock/stream.runtime.ts:970` moved tool-returned images out of `toolResult.content` only when `model.id.includes("openai.gpt-5.6-sol")`, so every other route sent them nested, a layout AWS documents only for Claude and Nova and that GPT-6/6.1 Sol and Kimi K3 reject with `ValidationException`.

Fixes #186753

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes: on Amazon Bedrock, a turn fails with "The agent run failed before producing a reply." after a tool such as `read` returns an image, on GPT-6 Sol, GPT-6.1 Sol, Kimi K3 and any application inference profile that points at them.

## User Impact

User impact: image-returning tools work on every non-Claude Bedrock route, including opaque application-inference-profile ARNs and models that ship later, without a code change per model. Claude requests are byte-for-byte unchanged. No config or migration.

## Why This Change Was Made

#149336 added the sibling layout (tool results first, then a labeled user image group per result, no history rewrite) for one route name. Each new route that rejects nested images was a user-visible failure until someone added its name, and opaque ARNs never matched.

This flips the default: only Claude keeps images nested, using the `isAnthropicClaudeModel` predicate this file already uses for signatures and caching. Every other route gets the sibling layout, which the reporter's 24-request Converse matrix shows every tested route accepts. A wrong guess now still completes the turn instead of failing it. Production change: one line, net 0.

Two consequences, named on purpose:

- **Nova moves from nested to sibling.** AWS documents nested images for Nova, and only Nova Pro has been seen to accept the sibling layout (#187159's live run). I chose not to add an `amazon.nova` name match: sibling user images are documented for Converse, and the tool-free replay path in this file already sends tool images as plain user images on every model.
- **`isAnthropicClaudeModel` also matches a model whose `name` contains "claude".** A non-Claude profile named, say, "claude-replacement" would keep the nested layout. That is the same exposure signature replay has today.

A non-Claude session that already holds a tool image gets one prompt-cache miss on its next request, because the replayed layout changes once.

Credit: @beezly reported this with the full route matrix and proposed this exact inversion (#187159); @yousan opened the first fix and ran a live Kimi K3 ConverseStream turn with the sibling layout. This PR keeps yousan's commit and replaces its name list with the inverted default.

## Evidence

- Regression: `stream.runtime.test.ts` › "lifts non-Claude tool images into user content, keeping result associations" now uses an opaque application-inference-profile ARN for the lifted case (red on base: images stay nested) and a Claude id for the nested control.
- End to end, built `dist/` on both sides, isolated Gateway, one `openclaw agent` turn whose `read` returns a PNG, against a local ConverseStream server that enforces the observed rule (nested image on a non-Claude/non-Nova model -> 400 `ValidationException` with AWS's message; otherwise the reply carries the SHA-256 of each image it received). Results: https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/186834#issuecomment-7217213380
- Limit: the local server encodes the observed rule, so it cannot prove that Nova accepts the sibling layout; only a live AWS call can.

Merge danger: two-way door. A revert restores the old layout; nothing is stored or migrated (transcript rows are unchanged; only the request built from them differs). Blast radius: Bedrock ConverseStream requests that replay a tool result containing an image, on non-Claude models.

fix(gateway): retire the local session projection with its maintenance scope (#206628)

## Problem

`openclaw agent --local` sometimes exits 1 after a correct answer:

```
[openclaw] OpenClaw hit an unexpected runtime error.
[openclaw] Reason: Database maintenance resource admission is closed
```

Seen in 3 of 21 runs of a real `session_status` task, and in a `skill-load` run on the older base, so the bug was already there before this PR.

Cause: the local command creates the in-process session-row projection inside the CLI's database maintenance scope (`runWithLocalStateOwner`). But `local-request-context.ts` gave the job of releasing it to the outer CLI resource host, and that host closes after the maintenance scope. While the scope is closing, a late fact publication queues `ensureMaterialized()`. That calls `hasWork()`, which reads subagent facts through the closed scope (`snapshotIdentity` -> `assertAdmission`). The read throws synchronously inside a microtask, so the `.catch` never attaches and the error is uncaught.

## Solution

When a maintenance scope is present, it owns the projection in its `agent-resources` phase. The scope closes in this order: it waits for pending work, disposes the projection, then closes admission. `openclaw-agent-db-resources.ts` already uses this pattern. Callers with no maintenance scope still release through the resource host, as before.

## Evidence

- New test `local-request-context.test.ts` › "retires the session projection before its database maintenance scope closes". It fails on main with `Database maintenance resource scope is closed` and passes with the fix. Production reads subagent facts from SQLite, so the test turns that on too.
- `local-request-context*.test.ts` (3 files, 37 tests) pass.
- Real `agent --local` runs (gpt-5.4-mini, fresh install, `session_status` task): main 1 failure in 15, fix 0 failures in 20 (dist-nodts build). The failure is rare, so the deterministic test is the main proof.
- Local ClawSweeper review on `866e7490`: patch is correct, no findings.

perf(agents): render the system prompt from one manifest and halve it (#206537)

## Problem

On a fresh install, the first request of `openclaw agent --local` carries a 29 KB system prompt (about 3x Pi). One large function builds it, helped by scattered section builders, and nothing limits its size. The Tool Search directory alone repeats 11.6 KB of tool descriptions on every request, and the skills catalog adds 4.2 KB. `tool_search`, `tool_describe` and `skills_search` already supply those details on demand. The 2.6 KB `message` tool is also sent in runs that have no channel to send to.

## Solution

The change has three parts:

1. `test(agents)`: byte snapshots of the fresh-install and configured system prompts, generated on the base commit.
2. `refactor(agents)`: one owner renders the prompt from a declared manifest, `src/agents/system-prompt-manifest.ts`. Each section has an id, an owner file, a region (stable, dynamic or runtime), an inclusion condition and a byte budget. `buildAgentSystemPrompt` renders only through one renderer per manifest id, in manifest order. The output is byte-identical: the base snapshots pass unchanged, and dist `agent --local` first requests match the base byte for byte for fresh, bootstrap and configured installs.
3. `perf(agents)`: shrinks the prompt, largest sections first. Each cut has its reason:
   - The deferred Tool Search directory lists names only. Descriptions come from `tool_search` and `tool_describe`. The lean-only description tier is gone, so lean and default agents render the same directory.
   - The skills catalog lists names only when `skills_read` and `skills_search` are both usable; search matches descriptions on demand. Without search, the compact catalog keeps descriptions.
   - Directory tools marked `[loads on lookup]` keep their own call rule; the `dispatch_action` rule covers the other names.
   - `message` is omitted when the session has neither a supported source nor a configured messaging route, also on fixed listings. Availability is a session and config fact, so the pinned tool list stays fixed for the session.
   - Wording is tightened in Execution Bias, Promised Work, Runtime Context, Tool Call Style, Care, OpenClaw Control, Session routing, Documentation, UI Presentation, Memory Recall and Skill Workshop. No rule is removed.
   - Gate: `system-prompt.inventory-snapshot.test.ts` fails when the fresh-install fixture exceeds `FRESH_INSTALL_SYSTEM_PROMPT_BUDGET_BYTES` (13,500 B; the fixture renders 12,864 B) or when any section exceeds its manifest budget.

## Impact

First request, fake provider, `agent --local`:

| | before | after |
|---|---:|---:|
| fresh install: system prompt | 29,157 B | 15,015 B |
| fresh install: tools array | 20,108 B | 17,542 B |
| fresh install: request body | 50,554 B | 33,780 B |
| configured agent: system prompt | 37,534 B | 23,491 B |
| configured agent: request body | 69,061 B | 54,959 B |

Per section on a fresh install: Deferred Tool Schemas 11,596 -> 2,483 B; Skills 4,249 -> 1,047 B; OpenClaw Control 2,199 -> 1,803 B; Memory Recall 1,202 -> 812 B; Skill Workshop 848 -> 633 B; Session routing 562 -> 404 B; the `message` tool section 558 -> 0 B. Other sections shrink 5-10%.

Each change to the stable sections starts one new prompt series per session after upgrade (one cache miss). Pinned series keep their bytes until then.

## Evidence

Behavior suite: real gpt-5.4-mini, `agent --local`, 3 trials per case. Base is `ca15e2952f` (manifest only); head is `c5752270fb`, the shave before review restored a few dropped qualifiers (base wording, +341 B). Pass/fail is judged structurally from the recorded provider calls; answer quality is judged by a model against a written rubric.

| Case | Base | Head |
|---|---:|---:|
| read a file | 3/3 | 3/3 |
| shell command | 3/3 | 3/3 |
| skill discovery and load | 3/3 | 3/3 |
| deferred tool (`session_status`) | 3/3 | 2/3 |
| MCP tool call | 3/3 | 3/3 |
| reply directive | 3/3 | 3/3 |
| safety confirmation | 3/3 | 3/3 |
| memory recall | 3/3 | 3/3 |
| subagent spawn | 3/3 | 3/3 |
| compaction recall | 3/3 | 3/3 |
| progress card | 3/3 | 3/3 |

- The head `session_status` miss made the correct calls and gave the correct answer. Then the CLI exited 1 at shutdown with `Database maintenance resource scope is closed`. Over all runs this happened in 3 of 21 head trials and 0 of 15 base trials, and only in this case. It looks like an existing `--local` shutdown race and is tracked separately.
- Skill loading now goes through `skills_read` in every head trial. Base read SKILL.md from the filesystem in 2 of 3 trials.
- Local ClawSweeper on `1ebe079678`: patch is correct, no findings. Earlier rounds found and fixed: keep skill descriptions when `skills_search` is unavailable; keep the on-demand exception in the directory's dispatch rule; keep the one-skill limit scoped to initial selection; restore other qualifiers the wording pass dropped.
- Green: system-prompt, tool-search, attempt-bundle-tools, memory-core, copilot and codex thread-prompt suites; prompt snapshot drift; `agent-tools.prefix-stability`; `tsgo`; lint; format; line cap.

## Not in scope

- Plugin and SDK prompt contracts stay as declared slots: provider `transformSystemPrompt` and promptContribution, `before_prompt_build` contexts, context-engine `systemPromptAddition`, and the permission notice.
- `progress_card` stays listed. Its plan-completion check and channel plan updates work without a UI.
- `toolSearchDirectoryLean` stays an accepted optional field in the worker presentation schema. Core no longer reads it; removing it is a protocol change.

fix(gateway): keep a subagent paused on sessions_yield unfinished (#206548)

## Problem

A subagent that called `sessions_yield` and waits (on its own background `exec`, on its children, or on nothing) reads as finished in Control UI:

- The Subagents panel files it under **Done / "Completed"**.
- The parent's sidebar row depends on whether the paused child's row is loaded. The incident Gateway returned the parent with no `hasActiveSubagentRun`, so with the child unloaded the parent row showed no running child. (In the scratch-Gateway run below the child row was loaded, and the existing loaded-child case already showed "Subagents working" on base.)

In the incident, a hidden child yielded three times on background commands (last one a 25-minute `sleep 1500`). Live `sessions.list` returned the child with `subagentRunState: "paused"`, `backgroundProcessCount: 1`, no `status` and no `hasActiveSubagentRun`, and the parent with no `hasActiveSubagentRun`. The user could not find the subagent.

## Root cause

No single owner answers "is this child still unfinished?".

- A `sessions_yield` wake adopts the paused run under a new run id, so between wakes the run has ended. `projectGatewaySessionRunState` (`src/gateway/session-utils-display.ts`) sets `hasActiveSubagentRun` only for live runs and live descendants. It already computes `subagentRunState: "paused"`, but nothing used that for "unfinished".
- The parent rollups (`session-utils-row.ts` inline path and `session-row-child-activity.ts` resident path) both read `projectPreparedSessionChild`, which used only `hasActiveSubagentRun` → a paused child made the parent idle.
- In the UI, `isUnfinishedSubagent` (`ui/src/pages/chat/chat-spawned-subagent.ts`) = active run || `hasActiveSubagentRun`, so the desktop `groupFor` and the mobile panel status filed the paused child as done.
- `chat-subagent-wait.ts` built its own paused taxonomy as "paused && !isUnfinishedSubagent".

## Solution

One fact, owned by the Gateway row projection, read by every UI reader:

1. **Gateway** (`projectPreparedSessionChild`): a child's contribution to its ancestors is active when `hasActiveDescendantRun || hasActiveSubagentRun || subagentRunState === "paused"`. Both rollup paths read this one function, so every ancestor row gets `hasActiveSubagentRun: true`. The paused child's **own** row is unchanged: `hasActiveSubagentRun` still means "live work under this row", so readers can still tell "paused alone" from "paused with live descendants" (handoff `pausedOnly`/`pausedNote`, header running count, native Swarm dots, public session cards). No new field, schema, protocol or stored-row change.
2. **UI**: `isUnfinishedSubagent` adds `|| subagentRunState === "paused"`. That one definition drives the desktop panel group, the mobile panel status and launch cards.
3. `chat-subagent-wait.ts` no longer derives "yielded" from `!isUnfinishedSubagent`. `isYieldedChild` tests the row facts directly (paused, not active, no live descendants), and yielded children stay out of the running count, so the paused/background handoff lines keep working.
4. **Status text** (`pausedSubagentStatus`, Subagents panel module) for a paused child in the panel (existing strings, no new i18n): "Running in background" when `backgroundProcessCount > 0`, the existing "Waiting for/on subagents" when it has live descendants, else "Paused".

`childShowsParentWorking` keeps its paused-with-background-process case. Reason: with loaded children, the parent-flag fallback in `app-sidebar-session-tree.ts` adds 1 only when no loaded child counts as running. Without the special case, a parent with one live child and one paused child would show 1, not 2. `hasRunningDescendant` (home glyph) also reads loaded children only.

## User impact

- A paused subagent now shows under **Waiting** in the Subagents panel (desktop and mobile), with what it waits on ("Running in background", "Waiting for subagents" or "Paused"). It moves to Active when it wakes and to Done when it finishes.
- The parent's sidebar row shows "Subagents working" while a child is paused, whether or not the parent is open.

Stricter than before (intended): while a child is paused, the parent shows a working state and **Stop**. Stop on the idle parent stops the paused child (new test: `sessions.abort-yielded.test.ts`). Goal resume (`chatGoalResumeBusy`) and archive of the parent are blocked while a child is paused, the same as while a child waits on its own descendants today.

## Accepted edge cases

- A paused child whose background process died (for example in a Gateway restart) shows **Paused** until someone stops it. It is visible and recoverable. No reaper.
- On the inline (non-resident) rollup path, a paused grandchild under a finished, non-paused middle child does not mark the top parent: that path reads direct children only.
- The iOS chat wait line shows a wait without naming the paused child.

fix: finish release updates after a slow launcher response (#206503)

## What Problem This Solves

A plain `openclaw update --yes` can keep printing `restarting: restarting` after the new release is healthy and its launcher has committed the trial. The CLI is following a run that never receives its terminal history entry.

## User Impact

The serving release completes the activation run through the existing readiness and update-watcher owners. No new setting, status, stored format, timer, retry loop, or flag is introduced. This change belongs in the candidate release; an older installed CLI can keep following the same run.

## Why This Change Was Made

On base `bad21b1eba43`, `src/gateway/stale-install.ts:269-275` sets `trialSettled` before a detached `announceReady` finishes. In `src/update/gateway-trial.ts:363-371`, a two-second timer can end the IPC wait while the resident launcher has not yet written its committed receipt. The file fallback then sees an active trial, `settleRunFromTrial` returns at lines 311-315, and the one-shot prevents another settlement. The serving Gateway owns the terminal `update_runs` write at lines 259-290; the old updater CLI only polls it.

Move that same announcement into the existing core-readiness owner and delete the redundant `trialSettled` marker. Await the launcher's existing receipt, using the same single file fallback only when the IPC channel disconnects. Required plugin work and the terminal write remain on the existing Gateway update watcher, so readiness does not wait for plugin downloads.

`6d863890e965` added the separate format-1 legacy recovery path but left the resident one-shot intact. `da6ec1a0d0cb` bounds CLI requests and polling; it does not move settlement ownership.

Production delta: **6 added / 13 removed; net -7 lines**. Tests: net +82 lines. The existing persisted trial receipt and readiness lifetime replace the removed one-shot.

## Evidence

Read-only evidence from a macOS Git-release update from `93ce03aada9f` to `af91b89f6524` on 2026-11-27 (private paths and hostnames omitted):

- Gateway log line **4447**: run `947dcd09…` admitted at **07:13:25.815Z**.
- Lines **4845-4847**: managed restart begins at **07:27:07.903Z**.
- Line **4908** identifies the newly serving `af91b89f6524` build; lines **4967-4968** report Gateway ready at **07:27:44.435Z**.
- The resident `.trial` receipt is `committed`, with `outcome.status=succeeded` at **07:28:10.009Z**, but has no `reported` receipt. Log line **5017** and later lines continue `update.runs.get`.
- At **08:14:20Z**, `sqlite3 -readonly` still showed `status=running`, `phase=restarting`, `finished_at_ms=NULL`, last updated **07:22:05Z**. No live Gateway or state was modified.
- The precise timeout/commit interleaving is reconstructed from those durable facts; it was not directly logged. A deterministic regression reproduces it by advancing the candidate clock three seconds before the launcher acknowledges the committed trial.

Local proof:

- **Red on main/base `bad21b1eba43`** before production edits: the delayed-acknowledgment and delayed-disconnect cases both retain a running run instead of succeeding. The core-readiness activation cases also fail before the fix.
- **Green on the fix:** all 20 `gateway-trial.test.ts` tests pass, including both delayed-launcher cases, readiness success/rollback, plugin finalization, and watcher shutdown. All 17 `stale-install.test.ts` tests pass.
- The 10-file consumer run passed 198 tests and failed `server-startup-legacy-completion.test.ts` at its existing 120-second timeout. An isolated diagnostic replay also timed out: it reached “starting HTTP server” but never reached `http.bound` or the changed readiness owner. Both failures remain recorded; no assertion or timeout was weakened. This host-side startup proof is incomplete.
- Targeted typechecks passed: `node scripts/run-tsgo.mjs -p test/tsconfig/tsconfig.core.test.gateway-root.json --incremental` and the `tsconfig.core.test.other.json` leaf.
- Targeted Oxlint: zero errors or warnings. Oxfmt: all five changed files pass.
- `ocx build --dist` passed (**dist-nodts**). It reported existing Control UI budget warnings; declarations and packaging were not part of this runtime proof.
- `pnpm check:changed --delegate-compilers` is running; canonical production compiler graphs remain delegated to PR CI. Local ClawSweeper review will be attached for this exact head.

The live affected installation was deliberately left untouched. No release was deployed and no PR was merged.

fix(setup): leave starter files to the first conversation (#206517)

## Problem
`openclaw setup --baseline` wrote the starter workspace files (AGENTS.md, SOUL.md, IDENTITY.md, USER.md, BOOTSTRAP.md) and ran `git init` into whatever directory was named as the workspace. Scripted installs often name the task or project directory (`--workspace .`). They got persona files and a `.git/` in the project, and every later run carried a "Bootstrap Pending" directive plus about 19 KB of persona text in its prompt. Baseline cannot finish the bootstrap ritual, because it has no conversation.

## Solution
Baseline setup now creates config, the workspace directory and the session directory only. Seeding keeps its one owner (`ensureAgentWorkspaceOwned`) and one moment: the agent's first persistent conversation (Gateway or chat) or interactive onboarding. It follows the rule from #206477: seed only when a later turn can finish the ritual.
- `src/commands/setup.ts`: the offline path creates the directory instead of calling `ensureAgentWorkspace`. A fresh install creates the first agent with `skipBootstrap`, through a new optional `ensureOnboardingAgent({ skipBootstrap })`. The Gateway-owned path never seeded; only its message changed.
- Visible non-outcome: `Workspace OK: <dir> (starter files are created by the first conversation)`; `--json` adds `"starterFiles": "first-conversation"`, or `"skipped"` (with a matching text note) when `agents.defaults.skipBootstrap` is in effect.
- `--skip-bootstrap` keeps its meaning: it persists `agents.defaults.skipBootstrap: true`, so the first conversation does not seed either. No config shape change, so no Doctor migration.

## Impact
- Starter files now appear at the first conversation, not at baseline. Existing workspaces are untouched.
- Scripts that edit the generated templates right after baseline must ship their own files; seeding keeps existing files. This is noted in the changelog and `docs/cli/setup.md`.

## Evidence
Real CLI, `ocx build --dist` (dist-nodts), `env -i` scratch HOME/state/config, fake OpenAI-compatible endpoint:
- **Task-directory shape** (`setup --baseline --workspace . --json` on a fresh install, then the task config, then `agent --local`): the sha1 listing of the task directory is identical before and after, for both a non-empty directory (main.py, README.md) and an empty one. System prompt 30,888 B. Before this change, the same flow added AGENTS/SOUL/IDENTITY/USER/BOOTSTRAP.md and `.git/` (21 files).
- **Gateway first chat after baseline:** after `setup --baseline` the workspace is empty. Then `gateway run` and `openclaw agent --message hello` (through the Gateway). The workspace then holds AGENTS.md, BOOTSTRAP.md, IDENTITY.md, SOUL.md, USER.md and `.git/`, and the request carries `## Bootstrap Pending`. The Linux app first run (`apps/linux/src-tauri/src/runtime_action.rs`) calls `setup --baseline --json`, checks only `ok`, then starts the Gateway, so this is the same path.
- **Upgrade from latest stable (2026.11.10):** old `setup --baseline` seeded the workspace and I edited USER.md. Then the new `setup --baseline`, `doctor --fix` and `agent --local` ran. The workspace sha1 listing (23 files) stayed identical.
- `src/commands/setup.test.ts` "initializes local setup": the workspace is empty after baseline and the JSON carries `starterFiles`. It fails on base `fd681ab8786e` (2 failures) and passes here.
- `pnpm check:changed` green.

perf(state): keep one-shot CLI state readers between reads (#206504)

## Problem

A one-shot CLI (`openclaw agent --local`) boots a fresh shared-state reader worker for every state read: since #204868, each successful one-shot read retires its worker so that no SQLite handle outlives the read (Windows `EPERM` on a release switch). The handle release is required; the worker exit is not. Each boot re-imports the reader's module graph (~90-880 modules, ~140 ms CPU per boot measured with per-thread `--cpu-prof`).

## Change

`src/state/openclaw-state-read-worker.ts`: in the `cli-oneshot` role, a successful read no longer retires its reader. It closes the task, then joins `closeReadResources(pool)` before the result returns:

- Node (`explicitSqliteCloseReleasesNativeResources`): native handles close in place and the isolate stays for the next read.
- Runtimes without explicit native close: `closeReadResources` rotates the pool, which joins worker exit, as before.

The kept reader exits when the command closes shared state at CLI cleanup (`withCliCommandCleanup` resets the state-database lifecycle, which closes the read pools). Other roles are unchanged.

The #206466 gate budget drops from 19 to 17 worker threads before the first request.

## Guarantee kept

No SQLite handle outlives a successful one-shot read: the result still settles only after the native release completes. `src/state/openclaw-state-read-source.test.ts`:
- `releases CLI reader handles before a successful read returns and keeps the reader`: replaces the per-read exit assertion. The read result stays pending until the handle release settles, the task closes without retiring, one pool is created for four reads, and `closeOpenClawStateDatabaseAsync()` (the CLI cleanup path) closes that pool.
- `uses the cli-oneshot process lifetime for early awaited reads`: tasks close without retirement in `cli-oneshot`.

## Evidence

- Worker threads started before the first provider request, `src/cli/agent-local-cold-start.process.test.ts` (Node, macOS arm64): 18 -> 16. Linux CI was 19 before; the budget is 17.
- Per-thread CPU profile of one fake-provider turn (3 runs, median): 4 state-read worker boots per turn at 137 ms boot CPU each; this change removes 2 of them in the measured turn (one stays, admission reads keep their worker).
- Tests: the 26 test files under `src/state/openclaw-state-read*` plus every importer of `openclaw-state-read-worker.js`, `src/cli/agent-local-cold-start.process.test.ts`, `src/cli/agent-local-rpc-cleanup.process.test.ts`, `src/cli/one-shot-exit.cleanup.process.test.ts` pass locally.
- Wall-time ABAB is owed: host load stayed above 20 during this work; it will be appended to the W4 status at load < 10.

fix(browser): keep the user's color scheme on extension relays (#193911)

Root cause: `extensions/browser/src/browser/pw-session-cdp-transport.ts:361` calls Playwright's `connectOverCDP` without `noDefaults`, so every extension-relay connection applies Playwright's default-context overrides to the user's own tabs, including `prefers-color-scheme: light`.

## What Problem This Solves

When OpenClaw drives your own Chrome or Dia through the OpenClaw extension, sites that follow the system theme switch to light mode as soon as OpenClaw touches a tab, even when the system is dark. They go back to dark when the debugger detaches. secondfoxgit reproduced this on 2026.11.1 in the comments below (macOS Dark, Chrome, Proxmox on "Default (auto)").

## User Impact

- Tabs OpenClaw works in through the extension keep your light or dark mode. `browser emulate colorScheme=...` still overrides on request, and `none` restores your setting.
- Clicks in background tabs keep working, as on main.
- Browsers OpenClaw launches itself (managed profiles) and remote CDP profiles are unchanged.

## Why This Change Was Made

- Owned and borrowed extension relays now pass Playwright's `noDefaults` (upstream added it for "attaching to a user's daily-driver browser", microsoft/playwright#40185). The owned relay is recognized from its internal relay credential in the profile URL (`isExtensionRelayCdpUrl` in `config.ts`).
- `noDefaults` also drops Playwright's `Emulation.setFocusEmulationEnabled`. Chrome stops `requestAnimationFrame` in a hidden tab, and Playwright's click waits on it ("stable" check), so clicks in background relay tabs timed out. The relay bridge now sends that one command itself when it attaches a tab. It runs after the target is recorded, so if it fails the existing `detachUnusedAttachments` path releases the debugger. The extension already allows the method; no extension update is needed.
- `toErrorPayload` moves from `relay-bridge.ts` to `relay-protocol.ts` to keep `relay-bridge.ts` within its line-cap ratchet.
- This takes over jorge-monalee's PR and keeps his commit. The idle-detach part (60 s idle disconnect, connection holds) is removed: it is a separate lifecycle policy and needs its own decision.

## Evidence

Real Chromium with `--force-dark-mode`, the unpacked extension, and a probe tab behind an active tab, through the real browser routes. main is 277b251bfa80; head is f33eb47178ba; owned and borrowed relays.

| Step | main | this PR |
|---|---|---|
| `matchMedia('(prefers-color-scheme: dark)')` after `/tabs` and two `/snapshot` | false | true |
| Click in a background tab | 200 | 200 |
| New background tab / popup / cross-origin navigation, then click | 200, page light | 200, page stays dark |
| `emulate colorScheme=light`, then `none` | light, then dark | light, then dark |
| Managed profile after `/snapshot` | light | light (unchanged) |
| Download through the relay | same result | same result |

Without the relay-bridge focus call (`noDefaults` alone), background-tab clicks time out on Playwright's stable check; the new `bootstrap.chromium.test.ts` click case catches that. Headed macOS Chromium for Testing shows the same main/head results; real Chrome/Dia was not driven.

- Proof lines: https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/193911#issuecomment-7213396709
- Screenshots (background tab after OpenClaw, before light / after dark): https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/193911#issuecomment-7213387976
- Tests: `bootstrap.chromium.test.ts` theme case (red on main) and background click case (red without the focus call), owned and borrowed; relay-bridge unit tests updated for the extra command.

## Merge danger

Two-way door: no stored state, config or contract change; a revert restores the old behavior. Blast radius: extension-relay connections only (owned and borrowed). A non-Playwright client of the relay now also gets focus emulation on tabs it attaches, as Playwright clients had on main.

Thanks @jorge-monalee for the original fix and @secondfoxgit for the reproduction.

fix: keep chat photo previews sharp within their byte limits (#206461)

Root cause: `src/gateway/managed-image-thumbnail-cache.ts:46` forced lossless WebP (the in-process encoder has no WebP quality) and `:50` only tried 1/2 and 1/4 of the width, so photos that missed the byte budget losslessly came back at half or a quarter of the requested width.

Closes #206404

## What Problem This Solves

Photos looked blurry in chat and in the enlarged viewer. The Gateway reduced their dimensions to meet the preview byte limit, and Chromium enlarged those small images to fill the available space.

## User Impact

Photos can use the full requested preview width within the existing download budget. The updated preview URLs let browsers fetch the sharper renditions even if they cached an older version.

## Why This Change Was Made

The Gateway keeps a full-width WebP when it fits. For larger opaque images, it searches JPEG quality levels at the requested width before stepping down in size. Transparent images keep an alpha-capable format. The existing HEIC path still produces JPEG.

## Evidence

I ran the same 1920 × 1920 photograph through separate loopback Gateways built from upstream `66b2e244acf2` and the candidate. A local fixture supplied the model reply with the image. OpenClaw created the attachment and served it to the real Control UI in Chromium 156 on macOS arm64, Node 26.13.1, at 1440 × 960 and device scale 1.

| Requested width | Before, decoded | After, decoded | After, bytes | Limit, bytes |
| ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| 480 | 120 | 480 | 89,449 | 98,304 |
| 960 | 240 | 960 | 212,225 | 262,144 |
| 1920 | 480 | 1920 | 500,056 | 524,288 |

Chromium rendered the inline photo at 360 × 360 CSS pixels and the enlarged viewer at 868 × 868 in both runs. The viewer decoded 480 × 480 before and 1920 × 1920 after. The browser requested the new cache version. The full 919,421-byte JPEG matched the input in both runs. A small transparent PNG retained its alpha and dimensions.

The committed photo regression failed on upstream at 480 decoded pixels for a 960-pixel request and passed with this change. The affected Gateway, artifact download, UI, and managed-image end-to-end tests passed, along with core and UI typechecks, targeted lint, formatting, and the documentation link check.

fix: show typing while a queued follow-up turn runs (#201920)

Root cause: src/auto-reply/dispatch.ts:358-359 seals the source message's typing controller and src/auto-reply/reply/reply-dispatcher.ts:706-709 stops its channel typing callbacks (src/channels/typing.ts `closed`) when the enqueuing dispatch returns, and the queued follow-up turn reused both (agent-runner-run.ts createFollowupRunner `typing`, followup-turn-execution.ts `defaults.typing`), so its typing starts were no-ops.

Fixes #201885

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes: a message that waits behind a running turn (queue mode `followup`, or a busy session) never shows "typing…" while the agent works on it, even though the docs promise typing once the model loop starts.

## User Impact

User impact: a queued message now shows typing from the moment its own turn starts until its reply arrives, the same as a message sent to an idle session. `typingMode: "never"` and `/stop` behave as before.

## Why This Change Was Made

Each queued turn now owns its typing: the follow-up runner builds a fresh typing controller per turn and stops it in the existing `finally`. An explicit typing start on the channel callbacks opens a new cycle instead of being ignored after an earlier stop; stops still win over in-flight keepalive ticks.

This replaces the earlier version of this PR, which kept the source controller open with hold/release flags. That skipped channel idle work (Feishu preview finalization), removed the typing pulse at enqueue, and could leave holds open in collect mode or on retries. Thanks @chessing234 for the PR and @Davidnovarro for the precise report.

## Evidence

- Live Telegram Test Server, real model (anthropic/claude-haiku-5-5), `messages.queue.mode: "followup"`; M1 runs a ~12 s exec, M2 is sent 3 s later; the QA userbot records the bot's typing updates. Details: https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/201920#issuecomment-7212718999
  - main (6d2cb0379cb6), twice: no typing between M1's reply and M2's reply (11.4 s and 10.8 s without typing).
  - this PR, twice: typing within 2 s of M2's turn start and every ≤6 s until its reply, none afterwards.
  - Controls: idle message shows typing on both builds; `/stop` during M2's turn ends typing; `/stop` while M2 waits shows no typing afterwards; `typingMode: "never"` shows none.
- Regression in `followup-runner.test.ts` with real `createTypingCallbacks`: fails on main, still fails with only the runner change (the stopped callbacks ignore the start), passes with both.

Merge danger: two-way door. No stored state, config or contract change; a revert restores the old behavior. Blast radius: typing indicators for queued turns on all channels; channel plugins that call `onReplyStart` directly now restart typing after an earlier stop (checked: Discord, Matrix, Feishu, MS Teams and ACP call it only at turn or block start, before their own stop).

fix: let owners fork a chat with exec after a subagent or exec completion (#206483)

## What Problem This Solves

A plugin that forks the current chat with `exec` (for example better-prompt's `/better`, which calls `api.runtime.subagent.runForkedTurn({ tools: ["read", "ls", "exec"] })`) is refused with "This chat's tool policy does not allow read, ls and exec" when the owner uses it in a chat where the latest input is an internal wake: a subagent completion, an exec completion, a cron or `sessions_send` delivery, or a restart continuation. In an orchestrator chat that is most of the time.

Cause: the fork took its owner flag from the latest stored user row (`__openclaw.senderIsOwner`). The host stores every internal wake with `senderIsOwner: false`, whoever started the work. The transcript records who typed an input (attribution), not the authority a run holds. Introduced by #204411.

## User Impact

- An owner (a caller with the `operator.admin` scope) can fork any chat with `exec`, whatever the latest input is. `/better` works after a subagent or exec completion.
- A caller without owner authority (for example a session writer with `operator.sessions.write`) still never gets `exec`. `read` and `ls` stay under the session's own policy, unchanged.
- Sender, group and channel tool policy still follow the anchored turn.

Two plugin-visible behavior changes:

1. **Forks with no admitted operator caller no longer get `exec`, even on owner turns.** A fork started from background work that no Gateway request started (for example an `agent_end` hook) has no operator grant, so `exec` is refused there. Before, such a fork got `exec` when the anchored turn was the owner's. The bundled `skill-workshop` review requests only `["skill_workshop"]` and is unaffected. `plugin-sdk-impact` for `runtime-member:runtime.subagent.runForkedTurn`: 0 static references across 2,768 eligible ClawHub releases (2,333 complete, 432 partial, 3 failed coverage); the only bundled consumer is `skill-workshop`.
2. **An admin calling through a `sessionAccess` method on another person's owner turn now gets `exec`.** #204411 refused it with a `senderId === caller` clause. That clause closed nothing: the same admin already ran `exec` on that turn through a plain `operator.write` method (its own e2e asserted it). The assertion that refused it is replaced with one that admits it.

Deferred, not written: an `ownerAllowFrom` decider for channel callers that arrive without an operator grant. No such fork entry point exists today; it lands when one is proven.

## Why This Change Was Made

Authority is checked once, when the work starts, by the owner of that check. `runPluginForkedTurn` already admits the caller (`execution.operatorAuthority`); `forkPluginSession` now sets `requester.senderIsOwner = operatorAuthority?.grant.owner === true` and passes that requester to both `prepareSessionFork` (exec admission) and `runSessionFork` (capability profile, sandbox session tools, plugin tool context, memory-write provenance). The flag is an explicit boolean: several consumers restrict only on `=== false`, so a missing flag would widen access.

- `readSessionForkRequesterFromTurn` no longer returns `senderIsOwner`; the anchored turn supplies conversation facts and the model only.
- `prepareSessionFork` loses the `caller` parameter and the `senderId === caller` clause; its single producer is gone.
- Prompt-cache keep-warm prewarms (no caller, no tools) pass an explicit `false`.
- No SDK type change. `SubagentForkedTurnResult` is unchanged.
- Docs: `docs/plugins/sdk-runtime.md` says `exec` follows the caller's admitted authority, not the anchored turn.

Production code: +28 / −27 lines (flat). Tests: +135 / −23.

## Evidence

**Reproduction on the base (merge base 313b2112f6b6):**
- vitest-source: the new test `runs exec on the caller's admitted authority when the latest input is an internal wake` fails at its first fork with `{ status: "refused", reason: "tool_policy" }` (owner `operator.admin` caller, latest user row a stored `inter_session`/`subagent_announce` wake with `senderIsOwner: false`). The session-writer wake case passes on the base, as expected.
- dist-nodts real Gateway E2E: isolated scratch Gateway on a random port, owner Control UI client (trusted-proxy identity with `operator.admin`), real Anthropic `claude-sonnet-5-5`, scratch plugin calling `runForkedTurn` with `["read", "ls", "exec"]` from a `sessionAccess` method. The agent spawned a real subagent; its completion wake became the latest user row (`provenance: inter_session / subagent_announce`, `senderIsOwner: false`, `requesterOrigin.operatorProfileId` set). Fork result: `{ status: "refused", reason: "tool_policy" }`.

**Head:**
- vitest-source, one `ocx test` call, all green: `gateway-plugin-forked-turn-session-tools.e2e.test.ts` (4), `gateway-plugin-forked-turn.e2e.test.ts` (7), `session-fork-run.test.ts`, `prompt-cache-keep-warm.test.ts`, `session-manager-model-context-limits.test.ts`, `cron/maintenance-lifecycle.test.ts`, `cron/maintenance-snapshot.test.ts`.
  - Owner caller forks with `read`/`ls`/`exec` after a subagent-completion wake and after an exec-completion (`internal_system`) wake, through a plain operator method and through a `sessionAccess` method: settled, exec output present.
  - Session writer (`operator.sessions.write`) after a wake: `exec` refused, `read`/`ls` settled.
  - A non-admin `operator.write` caller's fork reaches the plugin tool with `senderIsOwner: false` (explicit, not missing); the admin caller's fork with `true`.
- dist-nodts real Gateway E2E, same script as the base: the latest user row was again a real subagent completion wake (`inter_session` / `subagent_announce`, `senderIsOwner: false`). Fork result: `{ status: "settled", value: { text: "FORK_EXEC_OK" } }`. The recorded provider requests show the fork's `exec` tool call (`echo FORK_EXEC_OK`) and its tool result `FORK_EXEC_OK`, so the command ran, not only the model text.

Live Gateway check after both E2E runs: the `ai.openclaw.peanutto` pid did not change, and the live config was last written on 2026-11-24, before these runs.

test(cli): gate agent --local cold-start processes and workers (#206466)

## Problem

Cold time-to-first-request of the one-shot `openclaw agent --local` turn (the path benchmark boards run) has no regression gate. A measured turn on `b0a6e8cd` took 6.05 s median to the first provider request (warm Gateway: 0.69 s). Most of it is fan-out: every Node process and worker thread boots its own module graph before the first request. Nothing stops a change from adding another one.

## Change

Add `src/cli/agent-local-cold-start.process.test.ts`: one real `agent --local` turn from source, run on Node (the default install's runtime, also when Vitest runs on Bun), against the local fake OpenAI Responses server (`test/helpers/openai-responses-model-fixture.ts`). A ledger preload, carried by `NODE_OPTIONS` into every descendant process that inherits the environment and into every worker thread, counts up to the moment the fake provider receives the first request:

- `nodeProcesses`: Node processes that started (CLI, respawns, inheriting children),
- `nodeSpawns`: Node spawn calls from any process or thread (covers children that start with a clean environment),
- `workerThreads`: worker threads constructed in any process or thread.

The test asserts ceilings `{ nodeProcesses: 4, nodeSpawns: 5, workerThreads: 19 }`, measured on the Linux CI runner (macOS starts 18 workers). Counts, not wall time: they do not move with host load. A PR that removes work lowers the budget in the same change.

The fixture keeps the default startup (`OPENCLAW_NO_RESPAWN` unset) and marks host CA discovery done (`OPENCLAW_NODE_EXTRA_CA_CERTS_READY=1`), because that respawn depends on the host's Node install. Windows is skipped: it always respawns for its stack size, so its topology differs by design.

## Evidence

- Red on the merge base before #206448 (`b0a6e8cd`, first version of this test): the warning-only respawn adds a CLI process. Green on main with #206448.
- Counts: Linux CI (Node CLI under the Bun Vitest lane) 4 / 5 / 19; macOS arm64 Node 24.22.1, 3 runs, 4 / 5 / 18 each.
- Review round 1 findings fixed: Windows topology (skipped, documented) and descendant work (ledger now propagates through `NODE_OPTIONS` and counts in every thread; process starts and spawn calls are separate counters).
- Cost: one CLI turn from source, about 16-31 s test time locally (88 s once under host load 40); same 120 s timeout as `agent-local-rpc-cleanup.process.test.ts`. No cheaper layer proves the processes and workers a real turn starts before its first request.

fix(agents): skip the bootstrap ritual in one-shot runs (#206477)

## Problem
A one-shot `openclaw agent --local` run seeded the first-run bootstrap ritual into its workspace: AGENTS.md, SOUL.md, IDENTITY.md, USER.md, BOOTSTRAP.md and a `git init`. The run then got a `## Bootstrap Pending` directive and about 19.5 KB of persona text in its system prompt. When the workspace is the task directory (`agents.defaults.workspace: "."`), these files and `.git/` go into the user's project. A one-shot run has no later turn, so it can never finish the ritual.

## Solution
`prepareAgentCommandExecution` (`src/agents/command/prepare.ts`) is the owner that seeds the workspace for every agent command. It now passes `ensureBootstrapFiles: false` when the run is one-shot (`oneShotCliRun`, already set by `agent --local` and `exec`). Existing workspace files are still injected. The Gateway and chat path (`get-reply.ts`) is unchanged, so the first interactive run still seeds and starts the ritual.

## Impact
- `agent --local` on a fresh install: system prompt 50,548 B → 30,899 B, with no Bootstrap Pending section.
- With `workspace: "."`, the task directory is byte-for-byte unchanged after a run. Before the fix, the run added 5 persona files and `.git/` (21 files).
- Interactive and Gateway first runs still bootstrap.
- Not changed: `openclaw setup --baseline` still seeds by its documented contract (`--skip-bootstrap` opts out).

## Evidence
- Real CLI (`ocx build --dist`, dist-nodts), `env -i` scratch HOME/state/config, fake OpenAI-compatible endpoint that records every request:

  | run | system prompt B | cwd after run |
  |---|---|---|
  | base, default workspace | 50,548 | unchanged; persona files in `$STATE/workspace` |
  | base, `workspace: "."` | 50,527 | +AGENTS/SOUL/IDENTITY/USER/BOOTSTRAP.md, `.git/` |
  | fix, default workspace | 30,899 | unchanged; nothing seeded |
  | fix, `workspace: "."` | 30,878 | sha1 listing identical before and after |
- `src/commands/agent.bootstrap-seeding.test.ts`: the one-shot run seeds nothing, and a persistent first run still seeds all five files. It fails on base `d6d289ee` (one-shot case) and passes with the fix.
- `pnpm check:changed`: all gates green except the dead-export scan. That scan reports existing unused exports in `src/agents/subagents/announce/*`, which this PR does not touch.

## Accepted edge
A sandbox with `sandbox.mode` set and `workspaceAccess: "none"` seeds its own private copy of the workspace under the state dir (`ensureSandboxWorkspaceLayout`). It follows `skipBootstrap` only. That copy is never the user's project directory. Carrying the one-shot fact into sandbox preparation would need a new parameter through the sandbox context, so this PR leaves it. The docs say so.

## Problem
