The second Node boot is pure waste.

## Change

- Delete the warning-only respawn branch from `src/entry.respawn.ts` and its skip policy `shouldSkipRespawnForArgv` from `src/cli/respawn-policy.ts`.
- Respawn stays for the two cases that need a fresh process: auto-discovered `NODE_EXTRA_CA_CERTS` (Linux version-manager Node) and the Windows stack size.
- Tests: the respawn tests now assert that common commands run in process unless Node must reload its trust store. Tests that used the warning respawn as a vehicle now use a CA respawn, or run on Windows only (`node-runtime-recovery` startup-respawn cases: POSIX no longer respawns there).

Acceptance rule (written before the run): cold `openclaw agent --local` one-shot turn, built `dist`, fresh scratch state per run, real OpenAI `gpt-5.4-nano`; metric = process start to `provider.request.started` (diagnostics timeline) and the CLI entry stage; ABAB with the base build, 8 samples each, same load band. Win = one fewer Node process per CLI call and a lower entry stage, no metric worse.

| metric (ABAB n=8, load 15-21) | base b0a6e8cd | this PR |
|---|---|---|
| Node processes per CLI call | 2 | 1 |
| node boot + entry wrapper, median | 311 ms | 154 ms |
| node boot + entry wrapper, p90 | 352 ms | 174 ms |
| start -> first provider request, median | 8769 ms | 7440 ms |
| start -> first provider request, p90 | 9777 ms | 9640 ms |

The total is noisy at this load (shared host); the entry stage drop (-157 ms median) is the attributable part.

- No warning: an `OPENCLAW_NO_RESPAWN=1` `agent --local` turn on Node 24.22.1 printed no `ExperimentalWarning`. `node -e "require('module').registerHooks(...); require('node:sqlite')"` prints nothing.

fix(models): back off consecutive catalog expiry renewal failures (#206415)

## Summary

- **Problem:** when a provider's model listing expires and its background renewal keeps failing, catalog discovery restarts with no delay. Only the first failure advanced the retry backoff: the failure counter in `createCatalogAttemptReporter` ran from a `beforeProviderFailure` callback that fired only when the failure *notification* was not deduplicated. Background (expiry) acquisitions set no pending scope, so every failure after the first was deduplicated, `discoveryFailures` stayed 1 and `expiresAt` stayed in the past. Each later expiry read started discovery again while the provider kept failing.
- **Fix:** the acquisition records its own failure. `acquireCatalog` records exactly one discovery failure per failed provider acquisition (worker recovery callback and rejection share one flag), then reports it. The reporter only reports; the `beforeProviderFailure` callback is removed. Notification dedupe is unchanged.
- **User impact:** a provider that keeps failing now retries at 30 s → 60 s → 120 s (capped at 30 min) instead of on every expiry read. Less CPU and fewer provider calls; no visible UI change.

Reported by @DonnieFi in #206097 (section 3). Split out of #206122; fix and regressions start from DonnieFi's branch commit 9620e47a48.

## Evidence

Two regressions, red on the merge base `fbba71f65223`, green on this head (vitest-source, `ocx test`):

- `src/agents/prepared-model-catalog-worker.pool.integration.test.ts` "backs off expiry reads across consecutive real worker failures" (real catalog worker pool, terminated workers). Base: `expected { discoveryFailures: 2, … }`, received `discoveryFailures: 1`.
- `src/gateway/server-chat-metadata-lifecycle.catalog-renewal.test.ts` "backs off consecutive expiry renewal failures instead of spinning at 0ms" (Gateway metadata lifecycle with fake timers: 1 → 2 → 3 failures at 30 s / 60 s, one broadcast). Base: same mismatch.

Head: those two files plus every test file that imports the changed sources (27 files) pass.

## Merge danger

Two-way door: in-memory retry bookkeeping only; no stored state, config or published contract changes. A revert fully undoes it. Blast radius: catalog discovery retry timing for providers whose listing fails.

fix: keep models.json loading when one configured provider has no api (#206390)

Related: #206097 (section 2)

## What Problem This Solves

One configured provider whose models have no `api` (for example a legacy `models.providers["google-antigravity"]` entry with only `baseUrl` and `models`) was still written into the agent's `models.json`. The model registry then rejected the **whole** file with `Provider google-antigravity, model …: no "api" specified. Set at provider or model level.` Every other provider in `models.json` stopped loading from it, and each catalog load logged the same warning again (about 118k lines a day in the report).

## User Impact

- Valid providers in `models.json` load again when one configured or discovered provider has no `api`.
- The provider that cannot load is left out of `models.json`, and its stale row from an older version is removed. OpenClaw logs one warning when `models.json` or a provider-plugin catalog changes, for example: `Model catalog omits a provider the model registry cannot load: Provider google-antigravity, model gemini-4-neon-high: no "api" specified. Set at provider or model level.` Catalog loads do not repeat this warning.
- Config stays valid. Users do not need a migration. Set `models.providers.<id>.api` to load that provider again.
- A provider that a user added only to `models.json` is never deleted. As on base, it stays in the file, and the registry reports it if it cannot load.

## Why This Change Was Made

The models.json planner (`isWritableProviderConfig`) and the registry (`validateProviderModels`) each had their own rule for a valid provider. The planner checked only `baseUrl` and `apiKey`. The rule now lives in one function, `findProviderModelsError` in `models-config.merge.ts`. The registry calls it through `validateProviderModels`, which throws. The planner calls it through `findUnwritableProviderReason` for every provider it builds (config, discovery, generated plugin catalogs) while it routes them to root or plugin catalogs. A skipped root provider also removes its stale row from the existing file, as a valid entry would replace it.

Decisions:
- **Entries that exist only in `models.json` keep base behavior.** `mergeWithExistingProviderSecrets` and its retention check (`isWritableProviderConfig`, now private) do not change. Deleting a user-authored file entry would lose data that exists nowhere else, and setting `api` later could not restore it. The issue's case is a config provider, which config rebuilds on every write.
- **Warning owner: the `models.json` writer, not Doctor.** Only the planner knows whether a provider plugin filled in `api` during normalization. A Doctor check on raw config would give false positives for plugin-owned providers (for example `models.providers.openai` with no `api`). The warning shows only when `ensureOpenClawModelsJson` changes `models.json` or a plugin catalog, so it appears once per change and not on each catalog worker run.
- **No `openai-completions` default in `models.json`.** The embedded runner still defaults a config provider with a `baseUrl` and no `api` to `openai-completions` (`resolveConfiguredProviderDefaultApi`). That runtime path does not change. To write this default into `models.json`, the planner would need a second copy of that rule.
- Accepted: the warning repeats whenever `models.json` or a plugin catalog actually changes, even for an unrelated change (a live `models list --refresh` on a host with live discovery logs it once per refresh). It does not repeat on catalog loads or unchanged rewrites.
- Accepted edge case: an `apiKey` that existed only in the old file row of a skipped config provider is removed with that row. The provider cannot load until `api` is set, and the key belongs in config or an auth profile.

## Evidence

- Base e9f9556bca5f, scratch profile, `openclaw models list --refresh` with the reporter's config shape (one provider without `api` plus one valid `openai-completions` provider): `models.json` contained `google-antigravity` with no `api`, and the log had `model catalog load issue: Failed to load models.json: Provider google-antigravity, model gemini-4-neon-high: no "api" specified. Set at provider or model level.`
- Head, same profile, starting from the base-written `models.json` (the upgrade case): `models.json` keeps only the valid provider. The log has one `… omits a provider the model registry cannot load …` line and no `model catalog load issue`. A second run added no new warning.
- Regression test `models-config.applies-config-env-vars.test.ts` › "omits configured providers the registry rejects and keeps the rest loadable": it plans `models.json` from a config provider with no `api`, with an old file row for it and a stale malformed row under a valid key. It then loads the planned contents in `ModelRegistry`. It fails on base (`expected [ 'valid', 'legacy' ] to deeply equal [ 'valid' ]`) and passes on head. "keeps a provider that exists only in models.json" checks that a rewrite does not delete user data.
- `models-config.model-input-presence.test.ts` and `test/openai-model-discovery-auth-order.test.ts`: their fixture providers had no `api`, so the registry would have rejected the `models.json` they produce. The fixtures now set `api`, as the real chutes catalog does.
- `ocx test` on the touched tests plus every test file that imports a changed module (15 files): all pass on the final head. `tsgo:core`, the core test-type shards, `test/tsconfig/tsconfig.test.root.other.json`, oxfmt and oxlint: clean. Earlier `check:changed`: the dead-export scan fails on `readUpdateDatabaseEngineConfig`, `DoctorContributionPending` and `formatUpdateSnapshotCapacity`. This PR does not touch those files.

## Merge danger

Two-way door: a revert restores the old behavior completely. The change writes no stored state beyond the regenerated `models.json` and makes no config, schema or protocol change. Blast radius: models.json planning and the registry's provider validation messages. The messages stay the same.

fix: keep answering your first message after the agent replies to a second one mid-task (#206412)

Root cause: src/agents/embedded-agent-runner/run/message-tool-terminal.ts:184 returns `terminate: true` for any delivered final message-tool send, without checking whether an earlier input of the same run is still waiting for its answer.

Fixes #202669

Thanks @Davidnovarro for the detailed report and trajectory.

## What Problem This Solves

In a chat with the default `steer` queue, you send message A, the agent starts working on it with tools, and you send message B while it works. If the agent answers B with the message tool (no `final`, which means final), OpenClaw ends the whole run. A never gets an answer and you get no notice, so you have to ask again.

## User Impact

- The answer to B is delivered and the run continues, so A still gets its answer.
- When the agent then sends A's final answer, the run ends there with no extra model request.
- A single message with a final send behaves as before (same number of model requests). Progress sends (`final: false`), a new message after A is fully answered, and follow-up queueing are unchanged.

## Why This Change Was Made

The hook that decides "a final send ends the run" already keeps per-input reply state. It now also tracks inputs that ran a tool and have no final reply yet. A final send completes its own input first (else the oldest open one), and ends the run only when no input stays open. The Code Mode nested-send completion uses the same rule. The model still decides whether one message answered both requests: if it did, its next turn simply ends.

`docs/concepts/agent-loop.md` now says that a final reply completes only one input, which matches the existing sentence in `docs/concepts/messages.md`.

Other runtimes:
- Codex app-server runtime: not affected. After a steer, a delivered final reply loses its terminal authority (`run-attempt-lifecycle-controller.ts`, `hasSubmittedMessages()`), so the turn runs to the model's own end.
- CLI runner (Claude CLI live sessions with steering): same pattern. `execute-tool-tracking.ts` interrupts the turn after the latest delivered final send and does not track earlier inputs. Not changed here; it needs its own per-input bookkeeping and live CLI proof.

## Evidence

Base is `d877e8007fba` (merge base); candidate is this branch head. Full captures: https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/206412#issuecomment-7210719550

- **Unit regression** (`message-tool-terminal.test.ts`, "ends the run only once the input before a steer has its own final reply"): fails on base (`expected { terminate: true } to be undefined`), passes here. The four test files that import the hook pass.
- **Agent loop, real `Agent` + real message tool + scripted model** (A runs `exec`, B is steered in, send for B with no `final`, then send for A):
  - base: 2 model requests, 1 delivery (`4`), run ends at `toolUse`.
  - fix: 3 model requests, 2 deliveries (`4`, then A's answer), no extra request.
  - Controls, same on both: single input with a final send (2 requests); `final: false` progress (3 requests); B after A was fully answered (new run, 3 requests); B queued as a follow-up (3 requests).
- **Telegram Test Server DM, real Gateway, deterministic provider** that replays the reported trajectory (Code Mode off, default steer queue):
  - base: the user sees only `2+2 = 4`; the provider gets no further request and A is never answered.
  - fix: the user sees `2+2 = 4`, then `notes.txt contains PELICAN-…`; 3 tool requests, no failure notice, no duplicate.
- **Telegram Test Server DM, real Claude (Sonnet 5.5 and Opus 5.5)**: 21 completed runs (13 base, 8 fix), including 6 per side where B asks for the message tool directly. The reported model choice (a send for B with no `final`) did not occur: in 20 runs the model sent B's answer with `final: false`, and in one it wrote B's answer as text beside a tool call. So the live gap is the model's choice, not the product path; the deterministic Telegram run above covers the reported path. The live runs show the unchanged progress path: A's answer arrives on base and on the fix, with no duplicate.

## Merge danger

Two-way door. No stored state, config, or contract change; a revert restores the old behavior. Blast radius: embedded (`openclaw` runtime) runs where a message-tool final send happens while an earlier input of the same run ran tools and has no final reply yet. Cost in the rare case where one send answered both inputs: one extra, normally empty, model request.

fix(exec): charge shared pages once in the host memory budget (#206396)

Root cause: src/process/child-memory.ts:165 `readMemory()` charged each process its full `VmRSS`/`VmSwap`, and `totalUsage()` adds every distinct PID, so a page shared by N processes in an exec tree was charged N times.

Fixes #206082

## What users see

- Before: headless Chromium (about 425 MiB real) and forked worker pools were killed in about 1.5 s with "Command killed because the shared host exec memory budget was exceeded".
- After: each process is charged its proportional share (`Pss`/`SwapPss` from `/proc/<pid>/smaps_rollup`), so a shared page counts once. Real private growth is still killed.
- A process whose `smaps_rollup` is unreadable or has no `Pss` line (non-dumpable, old kernel) keeps the full `VmRSS` charge. A parse miss never charges 0.

## Change

- `src/process/child-memory.ts`: read `smaps_rollup` first, fall back to `status`. Comment on the remaining overcount updated.
- `docs/tools/exec.md`: describe PSS charging and when shared pages can still count more than once.
- Test: one new case (PSS under budget with RSS over budget: no kill; PSS grows over: cancelled once, swap from `SwapPss`). The degraded-read case now rejects both reads.
- No config, flag or state.

## Evidence

Observed lines: https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/206396#issuecomment-7210339681

Real agent `exec` turns through an isolated Gateway built from base and this head (secretless Linux container, scripted model), two passes each. Budget 593-624 MiB.

| Workload | main | this PR |
|---|---|---|
| Python 200 MiB + 5 idle forks (RSS 1234, PSS 207) | killed, RAM 1294/601 | exits 0 |
| `chromium --headless=new about:blank` 60 s (RSS 1023, PSS 425) | killed in 1.5 s | alive at 60 s |
| 900 MiB private hog | killed | killed |
| 900 MiB hog with `PR_SET_DUMPABLE=0` | killed | killed (RSS fallback) |
| 2 fork trees + 400 MiB hog | both trees killed | only the hog cancelled |
| 700 MiB + 9 `setsid` copies, `background: true` | killed, RAM 7114 | killed, RAM 729 (copies stay charged) |

Poll cost: `smaps_rollup` takes about 6-7 ms per GiB resident per process on a libuv pool thread (8 GiB touched + 7 forks: 442 ms per poll; base `status`: 1 ms). An 8 GiB shared tree ran 45 s through a real Gateway exec with `/readyz` p50 1.0 ms, p95 2.3 ms.

Thanks @jzmudzinski for the report, the measurements and the proposed fix.

Real occurrence: I found no user report of this one. GitHub issue searches and the Discord archive (keyword and semantic) turned up nothing. The bug was found while proving #197108. It has the same root cause as #197024 and the same user harm, reproduced below on current main.

Evidence (Control UI, before/after screenshots and controls): https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/206403#issuecomment-7210517388

## What Problem This Solves

In Code Mode, if an agent asks for an API key with `secrets({action: "request", ...})` in an ordinary cell, the secret card disappears about 10 s after it appears. The transcript then says "API key: Skipped" although nobody skipped it, and the agent never gets the key.

## User Impact

The secret card stays open until the owner enters the value, skips it, the request's `timeoutSeconds` runs out, or the run is stopped. Entering the key through the card stores it and returns `status: "stored"` to the agent. The agent no longer has to remember `wait` or `awaitResults` to keep the card alive.

## Why This Change Was Made

#197108 made native `ask_user` required Code Mode work so a pending question is never cancelled at turn end. A secrets `request` is the same kind of call: it opens a question card and waits for the human. This change treats only the native core binding `openclaw:core:secrets` with `action: "request"` as required. `list` and `delete` return immediately and stay as they were. A client tool named `secrets` resolves to a different binding id, so it doesn't match.

## Evidence

Built in secretless `node:24.22.1` Docker (base `2bacc4a6e9`, current main including #197108; candidate `04c20a9ba4`). The Gateway runs in the container, real Chromium drives the built Control UI, and a scripted model runs one ordinary cell that calls `secrets({action: "request"})`. On `waiting` the model ends its turn and never calls `wait`.

| Case | Build | Card | Question | Agent got |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| request, run 1 | main | gone at t+10 s, "API key: Skipped" | `cancelled` after 11 s | `waiting` (handed back) |
| request, run 2 | main | gone at t+10 s, "API key: Skipped" | `cancelled` after 9 s | `waiting` (handed back) |
| request, run 1 | fix | visible at t+5/20/64 s, key entered via the card at t+66 s | `answered` | `completed`, `status: "stored"` |
| request, run 2 | fix | visible at t+5/20/64 s, key entered via the card at t+66 s | `answered` | `completed`, `status: "stored"` |
| Stop at t+20 s | fix | gone after Stop | `cancelled` | run stopped |
| `timeoutSeconds: 30` | fix | visible at t+20 s | `expired` at 30 s | `completed`, `no_answer` |
| `timeoutSeconds: 30` | main | gone at t+10 s | `cancelled` | `waiting` |
| `action: "list"` | main / fix | no card | n/a | `completed` in 1-2 s (unchanged) |

The secret was a fresh random fake per run, typed into the masked field. It does not appear in the page after the reply, `chat.history`, the Gateway log, the model requests, or any other run output. The only place it is stored is the secret store row (`secret_store_entries.value`), where it belongs.

Unit: the #197108 regression in `src/agents/code-mode.wait.test.ts` now runs for both `ask_user` and `secrets` `request`. On base the `secrets` case fails (`status: "failed"`) and on this branch it passes. `code-mode.wait` plus the tests that import `code-mode-bridge.ts` pass. oxfmt and oxlint are clean.

Merge danger: two-way door. One predicate branch and one doc line; a revert fully undoes it. No state, config or contract change. Blast radius: Code Mode cells that call native `secrets` with `action: "request"`. Such a cell now stays open until the request is answered, skipped, times out or the run is stopped. Like `ask_user` since #197108, `secrets` request followed by `yield_control` now fails as unfinished required work, where before the card was silently cancelled.

fix: let a per-call timeoutMs reach closed-schema Codex tools instead of failing after the gate passes (#206400)

Root cause: `extensions/codex/src/app-server/dynamic-tools.ts:337` (main 2237f16b7e27). The Codex bridge forwards `call.arguments` unchanged after the dynamic-tool watchdog has already used the per-call `timeoutMs`/`timeoutSeconds` (`dynamic-tool-execution.ts:506-518`). Hooks run before validation (`src/agents/agent-tools.before-tool-call.wrapper.ts:382` then `:429`). So a tool whose schema allows no extra properties rejects the call only after its `before_tool_call` gate has finished.

Fixes #206056

## What Problem This Solves

The Codex harness docs say a per-call `timeoutMs` gives a slow dynamic tool more time than the 90 s default. For tools with a closed schema, such as `workboard_complete`, the override does extend the timer. But the call then fails with `Invalid arguments for tool "workboard_complete": <root>: must not have additional properties: "timeoutMs"`, and only after a `before_tool_call` gate (for example a 2–10 minute test run) has passed. The card is not completed and the passing test run is lost. A hook cannot remove the field, because returned `params` are merged into the original arguments.

## User Impact

`workboard_complete({ ..., timeoutMs: 600000 })` behind a slow gate now completes the card, both as a direct call and from a Code Mode `exec` cell. These calls are unchanged:

- A tool that declares `timeoutMs` or `timeoutSeconds` (for example `image_generate`, `tts`, browser) still receives it.
- Open-schema tools and external MCP tools get the same arguments as before.
- Any other undeclared key is still rejected.
- Without `timeoutMs`, the 90 s default still applies.
- Stop and a failing gate still keep the card open.

## Why This Change Was Made

The bridge already reads these two fields as its own control arguments. It is also the one place that knows the tool's schema before hooks and validation run. `handleToolCall` now removes the two fields once, through `omitUndeclaredTimeoutArguments` in `dynamic-tool-catalog.ts` (next to the schema validator). It removes them only when the schema sets `additionalProperties: false` and does not declare the field, and never for external MCP tools (the same exemption `validateArguments` uses). Hooks, validation and `executedArguments` therefore see the arguments the tool accepts. The watchdog and abort path are not touched.

Rejected: adding `timeoutMs` to Workboard schemas (one tool at a time, and it changes the model-facing schema), and letting hooks delete keys (that reverses #142700).

`dedupeQuarantinedDynamicTools` moves from `dynamic-tools.ts` to `dynamic-tool-catalog.ts`. The body is byte-identical and it has the same single caller. This is only to stay under the file line-cap ratchet; behavior does not change.

Docs: `docs/plugins/codex-harness-reference/timeouts.md` now says a closed-schema tool that does not declare the timeout argument does not receive it.

Not in this PR: a gate longer than 90 s without `timeoutMs` still times out. That belongs with #154733 (the watchdog counts approval and hook time).

## Evidence

Gateway proof: main 2237f16b7e27 and this branch e8c9082b7748 were each built in a secretless `node:24.22.1` container and run as an isolated Gateway with the Codex harness, Workboard, and a plugin `before_tool_call` gate on `workboard_complete` (registered with `timeoutMs: 1830000`). The gate runs `sleep 120` with `ctx.abortSignal` and blocks the call if the sleep fails. A stand-in Codex app-server sent the `item/tool/call` requests that Codex sends: `workboard_create`, then `workboard_claim`, then `workboard_complete({ id, summary, timeoutMs: 600000 })`. These ran as top-level calls and nested inside an `exec` Code Mode cell item. Full observed lines: https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/206400#issuecomment-7210456853

| Case | main | this branch |
|---|---|---|
| direct call, `timeoutMs: 600000`, 120 s gate passes (×2) | gate passes at ~120 s, then `Invalid arguments ... "timeoutMs"`; card not done | card `done` |
| same call inside a Code Mode `exec` cell (×2) | same error; card not done | card `done` |
| `timeout_echo` (closed schema that declares `timeoutMs`) | receives `timeoutMs: 600000` | receives `timeoutMs: 600000` |
| `timeoutMs` + undeclared `foo` | rejected (`"timeoutMs", "foo"`) | rejected (`"foo"`) |
| no `timeoutMs`, 120 s gate | times out at 90 s, gate abort signal fires, card open | same |
| Stop 20 s into the gate | gate's sleep killed, card open | same |
| gate exits 1 | blocked, card open | same |

Tests: one new case in `extensions/codex/src/app-server/dynamic-tool-execution.test.ts` (closed schema, passing hook, `timeoutMs: 600000` and `timeoutSeconds`; declared and undeclared variants). It fails on main with `must not have additional properties` and passes here. The touched test file and the 17 Codex test files that import the changed modules pass (437 tests).

Not covered here: the same calls through the real `codex` 0.172.0 binary against a scripted local Responses endpoint fail at ~10 s on both main and this branch, with `Tool call blocked by PreToolUse hook: Native hook relay timed out`. The reason is that Codex also sends `PreToolUse` for dynamic tools, so the native hook relay runs the same gate under its fixed 10 s hook timeout before the call reaches the bridge. This PR does not change that. It is tracked separately.

Merge risk: low, two-way door. A revert fully undoes it. No stored state, config or schema changes. Only arguments to closed-schema, non-MCP tools change, and only the two timeout keys those tools would have rejected.

fix: stop an idle Control UI tab from relisting models in a loop (#206122)

Fixes #206097

## What Problem This Solves

With a Control UI chat tab open and idle, the Gateway can list models thousands of times per minute. Each `models.list` reply says the catalog is still pending, the Gateway broadcasts `chat.metadata.changed`, and the tab asks for `models.list` again, forever. The trigger in the report: two agents share one OAuth sign-in, and the catalog worker uses newer credentials than the ones the agent's runtime started with (OAuth refresh or adoption from the main agent, or an external CLI credential).

## Root cause

`acquireProviderCatalog` (`src/agents/prepared-model-runtime.catalog-access.ts:314` on main) records each completed provider's credential key from the auth the worker discovered. `listChangedPreparedCatalogProviders` (`prepared-model-runtime.catalog-source.ts`) compares that key with the generation's startup `params.agentFacts`. When the two differ, every `changedOnly` read marks the provider pending (`modelCatalogStatusChanged: true`), and the tab reads again.

## Why This Change Was Made

1. Completed discovery now records the generation input it satisfied, `preparedProviderCatalogCredentials(params.agentFacts, …)`: the same input the comparison reads. The worker-discovered auth still owns the published catalog auth and account retention. A real credential change starts a new generation with different facts, so it is still rediscovered once.
2. The credential key and `hasSamePreparedModelCatalogAuth` now use one identity function, `preparedModelCatalogAuthIdentity` (extracted, not new logic). For an OAuth profile with an account identity, the volatile `access`/`refresh`/`expires`/`idToken` fields are left out, so a hot reload after a token rotation of the same account keeps the learned catalog instead of rediscovering.

Removed from this PR: the expiry-failure backoff change (`failProvider`, the moved `recordFailedDiscovery`, the `beforeProviderFailure` parameter removal) and its two tests. That path has no observed occurrence in #206097. Both backoff tests are red on the merge base `36395007cf` (second consecutive failure stays at `discoveryFailures: 1`, `expiresAt` unchanged), so the defect is real; it moves to its own fix. The `models.json` missing-`api` warning in the report is handled in a separate PR.

## User Impact

An idle Control UI tab no longer drives a `models.list` / `chat.metadata.changed` loop and the CPU and provider `/v1/models` traffic it caused. A real credential change still refreshes the model list once. No config, schema or protocol change.

## Evidence

Regressions (vitest-source, merge base `36395007cf` vs head):

- `prepared-model-catalog-worker.integration.test.ts` "settles models.list follow-up reads after real worker external-auth discovery" (real catalog worker, through the `models.list` handler and the metadata lifecycle): fails on the base, passes on head.
- `prepared-model-runtime.scoped-refresh.test.ts` "retains discovery across a hot reload with rotated identified OAuth": fails on the base, passes on head.
- Head: touched tests plus every test importing a changed source, 46 files, all pass. `pnpm check:changed`: all lanes pass except the dead-export scan, which reports two untouched files (`src/agents/btw-runtime.ts`, `src/agents/subagents/registry/subagent-control.types.ts`) also reported on the base.

End to end: built Gateway (`pnpm build:docker && pnpm ui:build`) in a secretless `node:24.22.1` container, a real Chromium Control UI tab, and a local stand-in OAuth provider (plugin loaded from `plugins.load.paths`; sign-in, refresh and `/v1/models` go to a local server; no real credentials). Setup from the report: agents `main` and `helper`; `helper` holds an older copy of the same sign-in, `main` signs in later; the first token is inside the refresh window when discovery runs; tab on `/chat/helper`. Counts over 60 s idle after the tab loads.

| Build | Scenario | `models.list` | `chat.metadata.changed` | stand-in `/v1/models` |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| base `36395007cf` run 1 | reporter topology | 2467 | 2467 | 2466 |
| base `36395007cf` run 2 | reporter topology | 3060 | 3060 | 3061 |
| head `081b1405b1` run 1 | reporter topology (OAuth adoption logged 1×) | 0 | 0 | 0 |
| head `081b1405b1` run 2 | reporter topology (OAuth adoption logged 2×) | 0 | 0 | 0 |
| head `081b1405b1` | real key change after startup (`openclaw models auth paste-api-key --provider standin`) | 4 in the action window, then 0 over 60 s idle | 7, then 0 | 2 at the action (OAuth + new key), then 0 |

The base also relists once on a real key change and then stays at 0 (base-side comment below).

Base-side runs: https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/206122#issuecomment-7203236168

Thanks @DonnieFi for the report, the root-cause analysis and the original fix.

## Merge danger

Two-way door: a revert fully undoes it; nothing is written to state or config. Blast radius: model catalog rediscovery decisions for `changedOnly` reads and hot reloads of identified OAuth accounts.

fix(ollama): uncurated cloud models fail every request with a window-sized max_tokens budget (#199930)

Root cause: `extensions/ollama/src/defaults.ts:78-82` used an uncurated Ollama Cloud model's context window (for example 1,048,576) as its output budget, and `stream.runtime.ts` sends that as `num_predict`. Ollama Cloud caps output lower (393,216 for `deepseek-v4.1-flash`, 65,536 for `deepseek-v4-pro`) and rejects every request with HTTP 400.

Fixes #199928

Thanks @kybrcore for the report, the diagnosis and this fix.

## What Problem This Solves

Since 2026.11.3, every reply through an Ollama Cloud model outside OpenClaw's short curated list fails with "The reply length is set too high for this model", even though the user set no reply limit. OpenClaw asks for as many output tokens as the model's whole context window, and Ollama Cloud rejects that. Fallback models do not take over, so the model is unusable.

## User Impact

- Uncurated Ollama Cloud models (`:cloud` rows through a local Ollama, or `ollama-cloud/<id>`) now send `num_predict` 32,768 instead of their context window. Turns that failed with "The reply length is set too high for this model" now reply.
- `ollama-cloud/deepseek-v4-pro` and `deepseek-v4-pro:0813` no longer carry a manifest `maxTokens` equal to their context window (1,048,576). They now take the same 32,768 default.
- Unchanged: curated cloud models (`minimax-m3` 131,072, `kimi-k3`, `glm-5.2`, `minimax-m2.7`), authored `maxTokens`, `params.num_predict` (including `-1`), and local models (16,384 for the 32K local context).

## Why This Change Was Made

Ollama's API reports no per-model output limit, and server caps vary by model (65,536, 131,072, 393,216), so no number derived from the context window is safe. 32,768 is the shared unknown-limit default (`resolveDefaultModelMaxTokens`) that the config path already gives these models. The first commit fell back to the local 32K-context clamp (16,384) for discovered rows; the follow-up commit sizes remote rows on their full window so discovery and config agree and cloud thinking models keep the headroom #173844 wanted.

This reverses the context-window fallback from #173844. Its goal (do not truncate cloud thinking models at 8,192) stays: 32,768 is 4x the old placeholder.

## Evidence

Built Gateway, `openclaw agent -m "Reply with exactly: OK" --model <ref> --json`, against a local stand-in of the Ollama daemon that enforces the hosted output caps and returns Ollama Cloud's 400 body. Base: main `d877e8007fba`. Candidate: this branch. Full lines: [proof comment](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/199930#issuecomment-7209864581).

| Model | main | this PR |
|---|---|---|
| `ollama/deepseek-v4.1-flash:cloud` (x2) | 400, `num_predict` 1,048,576 | reply, 32,768 |
| `ollama/deepseek-v4-pro:cloud` (x2) | 400, 1,048,576 | reply, 32,768 |
| `ollama-cloud/deepseek-v4-pro` (manifest row, x2) | 400, 1,048,576 | reply, 32,768 |
| `ollama/minimax-m3:cloud` (curated) | 131,072 | 131,072 |
| authored `maxTokens: 2048` | 2,048 | 2,048 |
| `ollama/qwen3:8b` (local) | 16,384 | 16,384 |
| `params.num_predict: -1` | -1 | -1 |

Known gap: a user who ran setup on 2026.11.3-11.6 with an uncurated cloud model has `maxTokens` equal to the context window saved in config. Setup on v2026.11.6 then an in-place upgrade to this build still sends 1,048,576 and fails. Re-running setup or setting `maxTokens` fixes it. Repairing saved config is a separate change.

Tests: the existing output-budget rows flip from 262,144 / 1,048,576 to 32,768 (red on main); tests net 0.

## Merge danger

Two-way door. No config, state or schema writes; a revert restores the old budgets. Blast radius: output caps for uncurated Ollama Cloud models and the two `deepseek-v4-pro` catalog rows.

fix(agents): Code Mode ask_user questions are cancelled when the turn ends (#197108)

Root cause: `src/agents/code-mode-bridge.ts:206` `requiresCodeModeCompletion` made a cell required only for `exec`/`agents_wait` with `awaitResults: true`. So an ordinary cell that called `ask_user` parked as `waiting` after the 10 s cell budget, and turn teardown closed the parked cell and cancelled the pending question.

Fixes #197024

Thanks @migelizaga-rgb for the report and @harjothkhara for the fix.

Maintainer follow-up on top of the contributor's commits: dropped the `config/test-lines-allocations` file, because main's per-PR test-line allowance now covers the 18-line regression.

Control UI proof with before/after screenshots and controls (Stop, `timeoutSeconds`, client tool named `ask_user`, `exec({awaitResults: true})`): https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/197108#issuecomment-7209819578


## What Problem This Solves

Fixes: in Code Mode, an `ask_user` question asked from an ordinary cell (without `awaitResults: true`) is cancelled when the turn ends, so the owner never gets an answerable card and the agent never receives the answer.

## User Impact

User impact: agents using Code Mode can call `ask_user` normally and the question stays open until the owner answers, the question times out, or the run is cancelled. Same outcome as `awaitResults: true` today, without the model having to remember the flag.

## Why This Change Was Made

Code Mode already has a required-completion owner that keeps the exec call open while off-VM tool results are pending. Previously only `exec`/`agents_wait` with `awaitResults: true` entered it. A native `ask_user` call was not covered, so a slow human answer let the cell return `waiting`, and turn teardown then aborted the pending question. This change makes every native core `ask_user` call required work. Client-provided tools named `ask_user` and the existing `awaitResults` rules are unchanged; deadlines, Stop and owner replacement still end the call.

One deliberate consequence: a cell that calls `ask_user` and then `yield_control()` now fails explicitly as unfinished required work, instead of parking a handle whose question would be silently cancelled at turn end.


## Evidence

### Real Gateway proof (isolated local Gateway, real agent and model)

Setup: `pnpm build:runtime` of each commit, then `openclaw gateway run` on loopback with a fresh state dir. The model is `openai/gpt-6-astra` via ChatGPT OAuth, pinned to the OpenClaw runtime. `tools.codeMode = { enabled: true, timeoutMs: 2000 }`. The question is driven over Gateway RPC:
1. `chat.send` asks the agent to run one ordinary Code Mode cell, `const answer = await ask_user({...}); return answer;`, with no `awaitResults` and no `yield_control`.
2. `question.list` finds the pending question, which is held unanswered for 30s (15x the 2s cell budget). `question.get` is checked every 10s.
3. `question.resolve` submits `Amber`. `chat.history` must then show `PROOF-197024 ANSWER=Amber`.

The "end turn" scenario tells the model to reply `PROOF-197024 HANDED-BACK` and end its turn if `exec` returns `waiting`, instead of polling `wait`. That is the hand-back that loses the question in #197024. Both builds got the identical prompt. Base = this branch with only `src/agents/code-mode-bridge.ts` reverted to 3031a32908b (scratch build `3197a25`). Head = `dc3c9c0` (both from `dist/build-info.json`).

| Scenario | Build | `exec` result | Model `wait` polls | Question after 30s | Answer reached the agent |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| End turn on `waiting` | base | `waiting` (`pending_tools`) | 0, replied `HANDED-BACK` | **`cancelled`** within 10s of being asked | **no** |
| End turn on `waiting` | head | `completed`, value `{status:"answered", proceed:["Amber"]}` | 0 | `pending` at 10s, 20s and 30s, then `answered` | yes: `PROOF-197024 ANSWER=Amber` |
| Model keeps polling | base | `waiting` | 9 | `pending`, then `answered` | yes, only because the model polled `wait` 9 times |
| Model keeps polling | head | `completed` with the answer | 0 | `pending`, then `answered` | yes: `PROOF-197024 ANSWER=Amber` |

On head, the Code Mode tool result in `chat.history` is `{"status":"completed",…,"sources":{"openclaw":64,"mcp":0,"client":0},…}`, so the native core `ask_user` was used. ### Unit regression and checks

- Regression in `src/agents/code-mode.wait.test.ts`: an ordinary cell awaits a core `ask_user` whose answer arrives only after the clock is advanced 60s past a 1s cell budget.

- Treat [ as an ordinary word character unless it opens an array subscript,

  backslash-newline continuation does not end it.

- Read aliases and extensions from gh's config/data directories on every

  stay invisible, and a broken config must not stall the pass-through.

* fix(tools): keep a backslash inside a shell comment from hiding commands

The heredoc body-start scan treated every trailing backslash-newline as a
bash line continuation. A backslash at the end of a shell comment is data,
so bash ends the command line there. The validator instead skipped the
newline and pushed the body start past real command lines, blanking them as
heredoc data. For 'cat <<echo # \' followed by 'echo', 'echo echo PROOF | sh'
and 'echo', bash ends the heredoc at the first 'echo' and runs the pipeline,
while is_allowlisted returned True and is_denylisted returned False.

Detect comment context for the backslash and stop the continuation scan
there. Regression tests cover the validator verdicts and run the payload
under bash to pin the real behaviour.

Git-Session-Id: 06c9da40-b348-5b99-b8b5-47fdbd0d1a7b

* fix(tools): ignore quotes inside heredoc bodies when finding a comment backslash

A quote character in an earlier heredoc body set the quote state for the rest
of the command, so a later heredoc header's comment was not recognised and its
trailing backslash was treated as a line continuation. The body start then
moved one line down and hid a real pipeline from validation.

Also resolve gh's config and data directories from the Windows locations, so an
existing shell alias or installed extension is still refused there.

Git-Session-Id: 0e876bac-46fa-5050-b96c-b6b22062bc6e

* fix(tools): stop skipped heredoc openers from hiding commands

An opener whose delimiter is not modelled (``, `$`, `(`, unterminated quotes) was skipped with `continue`, so its body was scanned as shell text and a `<<` inside that body was accepted as a new opener. That region blanked lines bash executes: `cat <<$x / echo <<Z / $x / curl … | sh / Z` was auto-approved. Stop modelling openers after an unmodelled one.

A bare `[` was pushed onto the nesting stack whenever the previous char was alphanumeric, so `echo a[ <<EOF` suppressed a real heredoc and reopened the same hole. Require a same-line closing `]` for a subscript, and track `$[...]` explicitly so its multi-line form still suppresses.

Also catch `ValueError` in the gh alias reader: `read_text` raises `UnicodeDecodeError` on undecodable bytes, which crashed the pass-through instead of skipping the config.

Git-Session-Id: 22b292b5-ec9d-592f-9817-41266d845541

- _has_closing_bracket scans past a << inside an array subscript, so

  forbidden pipeline.
- _gh_alias_values reads config.yml as UTF-8 and returns None when an
  existing config cannot be read or parsed; _local_exec_reason then refuses

- Tests: non-vacuous array-shift payload, UTF-8 non-ASCII alias, and

Git-Session-Id: 606465d5-554e-5d4e-9c5f-98f8946e1be1

* fix(tools): stop modelling heredocs where `<<` may be an array shift

An open `[` after a word, or an open `name=(` compound assignment, can make

than guess, so later lines stay visible to validation. This replaces the
closing-bracket lookahead, which missed spaced subscripts and compound
assignments and misread `echo a[<<EOF]`.

implement, refuse `gh copilot`, and isolate the Windows extension test
from the host's gh config.

A `]` from a nested `[` inside `$[...]` closed the outer bracket, and `$'\''` lost quote tracking so a quoted `)` closed `name=(`. Both let a shift read as a heredoc opener.

fix(browser): carry cookies across allowlisted redirect hops (#5271)

* fix(browser): carry cookies across allowlisted redirect hops

With a host allowlist each redirect hop is its own lynx process, and a
Set-Cookie sent with a 30x was lost before the next probe and the final
fetch. Servers that set a session cookie on the first redirect and check it
on the next looped until "Too many redirects", or bounced the final fetch
back to a redirect that -noredir then dumped instead of the page.

lynx can read a cookie jar but only when PERSISTENT_COOKIES is enabled in
its config, it drops rows whose expiry is 0, and it never writes the jar
back in -dump mode. So the harness owns the jar: each probe's Set-Cookie
headers are parsed into a per-request Netscape jar (session cookies get a
short real expiry) that every later hop and the final fetch read.

Verified locally: lynx sends jar cookies under -mime_header -source as well
as --dump -noredir, and a two-hop redirect that requires its own cookie now
resolves under an allowlist.

fix(server): keep ACP runtime transport on a dedicated long-lived event loop (#5185)

* fix(server): keep ACP runtime transport on a dedicated long-lived event loop

Each server ACP step ran in its own asyncio.run() loop, but the runtime's
GptmeAcpClient (subprocess transport + spawn_agent_process async context) was
bound to the first step's loop. When that loop closed, the async generator was
finalized from the wrong loop ('athrow(): asynchronous generator is already
running'), the subprocess was torn down, and the next step failed with
'ConnectionError: Connection closed'.

AcpSessionRuntime now owns a dedicated event loop thread and marshals
start/prompt/close onto it, so the transport outlives the per-step loops.
terminate_subprocess_sync() closes gracefully on that loop before falling
back to signalling the process; stopping the loop cancels in-flight calls.

Fixes #5177

* fix(server): never fall back to another provider for an explicit model

Startup treated every model-config error as 'no model configured' and called
_pick_fallback_model(), even when the operator pinned --model/MODEL. With only
OPENAI_API_KEY present, a server started for openrouter/... silently ran every
conversation on openai/gpt-4o-mini for a day.

one is pinned, never substitute another provider: log an error naming the model
and the missing key and start in the same degraded setup mode as with no keys
(require_llm=False, provider_configured=false). The no-model first-run path is
unchanged.

model, picked a fallback provider, and sent conversations there despite the
operator pinning one. Load .env before the resolution so the pin is honoured.

* fix(tools): key browser logs per conversation and skip log tests without playwright

read_logs() read the process-wide _last_logs slot twice: once for the
ownership check and again to build the response. A concurrent page load in
another conversation could replace the slot between those reads, so a caller
could receive another conversation's private console logs.

Key the logs by conversation and read the caller's entry once, which also
stops one conversation's load from discarding another's logs. A blocked
landing page now records its navigation errors against the caller's own
entry with the console output dropped, so read_logs() after a failed load
no longer returns the previous page's logs.

The new isolation tests import _browser_playwright, which imports
playwright.sync_api at module level, so they need the same has_playwright()
skip as the other Playwright-backed classes; without it they fail with
ModuleNotFoundError on installs without the browser extra.

A blocked load stored its navigation and page errors for the caller, and
those can carry internal host names or token-bearing text from the page
that was refused. Drop the caller's entry instead, so a read_logs() after a
failed load reports nothing rather than echoing blocked-page detail or the

fix(server): fall back to the cookie when Authorization carries another scheme (#5296)

Behind a basic-auth reverse proxy, browsers attach the cached basic
credentials to every request to that origin, including EventSource, which
cannot set its own header. require_auth rejected any non-Bearer Authorization
header outright, so the webui's event streams got 401 and kept reconnecting
while ordinary fetches (explicit Bearer) worked.

A foreign scheme is now ignored and authentication falls through to the auth
cookie / query token, which still has to hold the server token. With no other
credential the response stays 401 'Invalid authentication scheme'; an empty
or wrong Bearer token still never falls back.

Because browsers also attach those Basic credentials to forged cross-origin
requests, the cookie Origin check (validate_cookie_origin) now exempts only
Bearer Authorization headers, so a Basic-carrying request authenticated by
the cookie gets the same origin check as any cookie request.

fix(config): honor XDG_CONFIG_HOME for the user config path (#5297)

config_path was hardcoded to ~/.config/gptme/config.toml while
dirs.get_config_dir() follows platformdirs, so XDG_CONFIG_HOME could not give a
process its own user config (and with it, its own prompt files, user profile
and API keys). This matters for a dev or shared server that must not load the
operator's personal prompt files.

XDG_CONFIG_HOME is honored on every platform; when unset the path is still
~/.config/gptme/config.toml, including on macOS.

* fix(webui): show server-unreachable guidance once a probe fails, even while auto-connect retries

deriveConnectionStatus treated the whole auto-connect loop (isAutoConnecting$,
which stays true through the exponential retry back-off) as an in-flight
attempt and returned 'connecting' before looking at the failed probe or the
grace period. Against an unreachable server that held "Connecting…" for ~182 s,
through all 10 retries, before any "Cannot reach" guidance appeared.

Pass the auto-connect loop separately: while it runs, report 'connecting' only
until a probe has actually failed and the grace period has expired. Explicit
connect() attempts and the auth-code exchange still count as in flight, and an
un-probed client (first probe still pending) still shows 'connecting', so the
no-flash behaviour from #4028 is preserved.

relied on to be a live probe because every path that bumped the generation
also installed a newer probe or nulled it via stopAutoConnect.

  converter could place tool output in developer input or top-level
  instructions. Send unmatched results as labelled user text instead, so

  Track pending calls so only a result that can pair stays native.

fix(api-gateway): map statusless context-overflow errors to 400 instead of 500 (#25614)

### What this PR does

Before this PR:
- In `src/main/features/apiGateway/errors.ts`,
`normalizeProviderError()` only mapped statusless errors for
`AI_InvalidArgumentError` (`400`) and timeout/abort shapes (`504`).
- Any context-window overflow arriving without an HTTP status/statusCode
(for example, a stream error frame or statusless `Error` /
`SerializedError` such as `Your input exceeds the context window of this
model.`) fell through to `HTTP 500` (`Internal server error` in
production builds for public clients, and `500 api_error` without
`category: 'context_length'` or `Prompt is too long:` for internal
runtimes).
- Because callers saw a retryable `500` instead of a deterministic `400`
context-overflow error, agent runtimes retried repeatedly (including
failing compaction requests with `500`) instead of triggering overflow
handling or surfacing the real cause.

After this PR:
- When a statusless, non-local, non-JS-runtime error carries
`providerErrorCategory: 'context_length'` or its message / structured
error code classifies as `context_length` via `classifyErrorCategory()`,
`normalizeProviderError()` maps it to `statusCode: 400` with `category:
'context_length'`.
- Public HTTP and SSE clients receive a bounded, redacted
`context_length_exceeded: <sanitized message>` payload (dropping
embedded JSON/HTML containers and redacting credentials) across
Anthropic, OpenAI Chat, OpenAI Responses, and Gemini dialects.
- Authenticated internal runtimes (`internalGatewayError` /
`objectGatewayError`) receive `400` with `Prompt is too long:`
(including `N tokens > M maximum.` when token counts are present) on the
Anthropic dialect and `code: 'context_length_exceeded'` on OpenAI
dialects, enabling Claude Code reactive compaction and preventing retry
storms.
- Genuine internal errors, JS runtime exceptions (`TypeError`, etc.),
local errors (`errorSource: 'local'`), and non-overflow rate-limit
messages remain `500` without leaking internal text in production.

Fixes #24258

### Why we need it and why it was done in this way

Statusless provider stream errors (such as OpenAI Responses
`response.failed` / SSE error events) do not carry an HTTP status code
when they reach `normalizeProviderError()`. Flattening a deterministic
context overflow into `500 Internal server error` hides the cause and
causes clients to treat it as a transient server failure.

The following tradeoffs were made:
- Restricted statusless 4xx classification specifically to
`context_length` (the confirmed failure class in #24258) rather than
mapping every error category from message text, preserving the existing
no-leak boundary for statusless transport, database, and internal
errors.
- Excluded `errorSource === 'local'` and native JS runtime error names
(`TypeError`, `ReferenceError`, `SyntaxError`, `RangeError`, `URIError`,
`EvalError`), and ran public messages through
`getSafeProviderErrorMessage()` so credentials and raw payloads cannot
leak.
- Reused `classifyErrorCategory()` rather than calling
`isContextOverflowMessage()` directly so precedence rules stay unified

production.

the same `normalizeProviderError()` fallback.

fix(plantuml-preview): prevent worker timeout after unbundled stdlib include error (#25665)

<!-- Template from
https://github.com/kubevirt/kubevirt/blob/main/.github/PULL_REQUEST_TEMPLATE.md?-->
<!--  Thanks for sending a pull request!  Here are some tips for you:
1. Consider creating this PR as draft:
https://github.com/CherryHQ/cherry-studio/blob/main/CONTRIBUTING.md

### What this PR does

Before this PR:
In `@plantuml/mcp-js/engine.js`, optional standard-library / resource
bundles (`!include <C4/C4_Context>`, `!theme`, emoji, openiconic) fall
back to `document.createElement('script')` inside
`nsptjb_ScriptLoaderJs_loadOnce$js_body$_0` when
`globalThis.PLANTUML_STDLIB_LOADER` is undefined. Because
`plantUml.worker.ts` runs in a Web Worker where `document` is undefined,
the first call throws `ReferenceError` and settles as an error, while
leaving `globalThis.__pl_script_state[name].state` stuck at `'loading'`.
Any subsequent render of the same resource bundle on the reused worker
(for example after switching away and back or opening Split View) waits
indefinitely in `'loading'` until `PlantUmlRenderService` hits its
10-second `TimeoutError`.

After this PR:
`plantUml.worker.ts` defines `globalThis.PLANTUML_STDLIB_LOADER` to
immediately call `fail('Unbundled PlantUML resource: ' + name)`. TeaVM
marks the resource state as `'error'` instead of `'loading'`, so
repeated renders fail immediately with the expected unbundled include
error and never wedge the worker or subsequent valid diagrams.

Partially addresses #25650 (fixes the re-entry and split-view 10-second
timeout; unbundled C4 stdlib support remains out of scope per
`.agents/notes/implemented/feature/2026-11-27-plantuml-local-render.md`).

<!-- (optional, in `fixes #<issue number>(, fixes #<issue_number>, ...)`
format, will close the issue(s) when PR gets merged)*: -->

Fixes # None

### Why we need it and why it was done in this way

The following tradeoffs were made:
- Fails unbundled optional resource loads immediately at the worker
loader boundary rather than bundling large extra standard-library JS
assets or terminating the worker after every error.

The following alternatives were considered:
- Terminating and recreating the TeaVM worker on every PlantUML error,
which wastes cold-start initialization time on subsequent valid
diagrams.
- Patching `@plantuml/mcp-js` in `patches/`, unnecessary because
`@plantuml/mcp-js` already provides the
`globalThis.PLANTUML_STDLIB_LOADER` hook.

Links to places where the discussion took place:
https://github.com/CherryHQ/cherry-studio/issues/25650

DSH reads local multi-frame Zstandard JSONL archives from the Harness
home and imports selected conversations into an existing Pi Durable
Agent. It groups archive versions by header ID, preserves visible
inherited history once, and keeps tool calls and results together in the
task history. DeepSeek account export ZIPs use their existing route. DSH
implementation #25497 targets #23626. It reads the complete child
archive in order, including parentless and nested forks. The goal
driver’s automatic rounds remain system history.

Related to #22728.

### Why we need it and why it was done in this way

The following tradeoffs were made:

- Users select an existing Pi Agent for each batch. Each source
conversation becomes a separate Agent Session with its own recorded or
explicitly mapped workspace. The importer does not create or reconfigure
Agents.
- Shared discovery, validation, persistence, and continuation ship with
the first source; subsequent sources add adapters through the existing
gh-stack sequence.
- WorkBuddy uses a separate reader. Its desktop records differ from
Claude's nested message layout, and SQLite index rows alone do not
contain conversation bodies. Cloud-only histories are outside this
local-file import scope.
- The inspected WorkBuddy transcript has five tool timestamp decreases
of 8–191 ms despite a continuous parent chain. The revised design stores
session identity and per-message source order in app_state, keeps an
imported prefix, and leaves original times unchanged. The 2026-11-06
revision replaced the earlier column-based draft. In #23441 the
import-specific migration, columns, and index have already been
withdrawn. Each selected branch uses Cherry’s native session root,
message parent links, and active head. Ordinary sources keep their
existing time-order rejection rules.
- Windows format inspection is only initial evidence. macOS/Linux
defaults, source layouts, packaged SQLite loading, and native
import/continuation remain to be verified. Linux coverage must name its
distributions and architectures.

The following alternatives were considered: ordinary Assistant Topics,
automatic Agent creation, merged histories, name-based destinations,
display-only import, incremental synchronization, treating WorkBuddy as
Claude, and automatically downloading WorkBuddy cloud history.

fix(mcp-oauth): fall back to in-memory storage when OAuth directory is not accessible (#25620)

### What this PR does

Before this PR:
- When `{cherryHome}/config/mcp/oauth` is on an isolated, encrypted, or
read-only volume (such as Windows portable mode when `%USERPROFILE%` on
`C:` is blocked by corporate policy), connecting an OAuth MCP server
fails immediately on the first cold read (`ENOENT` →
`writeStorage(initial)` → `EPERM` / `EACCES` / `EROFS`) with `Failed to
write OAuth storage`, preventing MCP server activation before browser
OAuth can even start.
- Deleting or clearing OAuth storage under the same
inaccessible-directory condition also throws on `fs.rm`.

After this PR:
- `JsonFileStorage` gracefully degrades to process-scoped in-memory
storage (`volatileStorage` alongside the existing `volatileSecrets`)
when reading, creating, writing, or deleting the OAuth storage path
fails with `EPERM`, `EACCES`, or `EROFS`.
- Full OAuth state (`tokens`, `clientInfo`, `codeVerifier`, `state`, and
`discoveryState`) round-trips across
`McpOAuthClientProvider.reloadCredentials()` (fresh `JsonFileStorage`
instances) for the lifetime of the session, while `clear(...)` and
`deleteOAuthStorage(...)` still reset all in-memory entries cleanly.
- If a previously persisted OAuth file is readable on a now read-only
disk and `saveDiscoveryState()` degrades to memory before secrets are
loaded, existing `encryptedCredentials` are preserved.
- Non-permission errors (such as `ENOSPC` or malformed JSON) continue to
throw as before.

Fixes #24088

### Why we need it and why it was done in this way

This implements Option A from the investigation in #24088: degrading
cleanly inside `src/main/ai/mcp/oauth/storage.ts` rather than relocating
`{cherryHome}`.

The following tradeoffs were made:
- Credentials kept in memory after an `EPERM`/`EACCES`/`EROFS` fallback
do not persist across app restarts (users re-authorize per session),
matching the existing `volatileSecrets` behavior when OS secure storage
(`safeStorage`) is unavailable.
- Only filesystem access/read-only errno codes (`EPERM`, `EACCES`,
`EROFS`) trigger fallback; other I/O or schema parse failures still fail
loudly.

The following alternatives were considered:
- Relocating `{cherryHome}` in packaged portable builds (Option B):
rejected for this minimal fix because `{cherryHome}/boot-config.json` is
read before `userData` is resolved
(`docs/dev/references/data/boot-config-overview.md`), making relocation
a larger architectural decision.
- Leaving activation broken and only documenting the boundary (Option
C): leaves users in isolated Windows portable environments unable to use
OAuth MCP servers at all.

### Agent Note / Spec

Agent Note: N/A — localized storage resilience fix in
`src/main/ai/mcp/oauth/storage.ts` extending the existing
`volatileSecrets` in-memory fallback.

Spec PR: N/A — direct bug fix for #24088 (Option A).

Acceptance criteria:
- Cold read, full OAuth save/reload round-trip (`tokens`, `clientInfo`,
`codeVerifier`, `state`, `discoveryState`), `clear(...)`, and
`deleteOAuthStorage(...)` succeed in-memory when `fs.readFile` /
`fs.mkdir` / `fs.writeFile` / `fs.rm` fail with `EPERM`, `EACCES`, or
`EROFS`.
- Existing persisted `encryptedCredentials` survive read-only
`saveDiscoveryState()` updates.
- Non-permission write errors (e.g. `ENOSPC`) still reject with `Failed
to write OAuth storage`.

### Verification

- TDD red run before fix: `vitest run --project main
src/main/ai/mcp/oauth/__tests__/storage.test.ts` — 4 new
`EPERM`/`EACCES`/`EROFS` cases failed reproducing `Failed to write/read
OAuth storage`.
- Post-fix OAuth test suites: `vitest run --project main
src/main/ai/mcp/oauth/__tests__/storage.test.ts
src/main/ai/mcp/oauth/__tests__/provider.test.ts
src/main/ai/mcp/oauth/__tests__/callback.test.ts` — **PASS** (3 files,

- `git diff --check` — **PASS**.

`EPERM`/`EACCES`/`EROFS` paths degrade to session-scoped in-memory
storage instead of failing MCP server activation.

if maintainers prefer relocating `{cherryHome}` later (Option B), this
fallback remains safe and non-conflicting.

fix(plantuml-preview): default to source view and require consent before remote render (#25582)

### What this PR does

Before this PR:
- Rendering any `plantuml` fenced code block in `CodeBlockView`
defaulted immediately to the `special` preview view, mounting
`PlantUmlPreview`.
- `PlantUmlPreview` compressed the full diagram source and automatically
sent `GET https://www.plantuml.com/plantuml/svg/<encoded>` after a 300ms
debounce with no user click and no third-party host disclosure.

After this PR:
- `plantuml` code blocks default to `source` view (including when a
streamed block transitions from another language to `plantuml`), with
both `Edit` and `Preview` actions available in the toolbar.
- Opening `Preview` or `Split View` for a `plantuml` block displays an
explicit notice disclosing that diagram source will be sent to
`www.plantuml.com`, and makes zero network requests until the user
clicks **Render via PlantUML**.
- Local renderers (`mermaid`, `svg`, `dot`, `graphviz`, `echarts`,
`latex`) keep their existing default preview behavior unchanged.

Fixes #25579

### Why we need it and why it was done in this way

`PlantUmlPreview` is the only diagram renderer in
`SPECIAL_VIEW_COMPONENTS` that transmits diagram source to an external
third-party service (`www.plantuml.com`). Making `plantuml` default to
`source` view AND gating `PlantUmlPreview` behind an explicit
host-disclosing confirmation button provides defense in depth: neither
passively viewing a message nor opening Split View / Preview can
exfiltrate diagram content before the user consents.

The following tradeoffs were made:
- Confirmation is kept as local component state per preview mount
(resetting when leaving preview/split view) rather than adding a new
persisted preference, keeping the fix minimal and avoiding silent future
sends across unrelated conversations.

The following alternatives were considered:
- Only defaulting `plantuml` to `source` view without an in-preview
confirmation gate: rejected because clicking `Preview` or `Split View`
would still send diagram source to `www.plantuml.com` without disclosing
the external destination.
- Adding a configurable self-hosted PlantUML server setting: out of
scope for this privacy bug fix and can be addressed separately if
desired.

### Agent Note / Spec

Agent Note: N/A — localized privacy bug fix for PlantUML code block
preview.

Spec PR: N/A — direct bug fix for #25579.

Acceptance criteria:

triggers zero outbound requests.
- Streaming transitions to `plantuml` remain in `source` view.
- Opening `Preview` or `Split View` discloses `www.plantuml.com` and
triggers zero outbound requests until the user explicitly clicks the
render action.
- Clicking the render action fetches and renders the SVG from
`www.plantuml.com` as before.

fix(agent-approval): preserve root permissions and surface subagent approvals (#24382)

### What this PR does

Before this PR:

Pi and Pi Durable children receive Full Access instead of the root
session's permission mode. Child approvals can lack the input and origin
needed to render a decision. Unresolved dynamic tool approvals can also
leave a turn waiting without approval controls.

After this PR:

- Children inherit the root's live permission mode, interaction state
and tool restrictions.
- Foreground/background child approvals carry complete tool input and
the spawning task identity into the root stream and composer.
- Unresolved dynamic approvals remain actionable even while the native
part is `input-available`.
- Approval cards show the requesting Agent/task, background status, task
navigation and a full copyable command preview. Rejection reasons expand
on demand; Enter on disclosure/navigation controls does not approve.
- Tools called from `codemode` follow the same gate as direct calls. The
approval identifies the actual nested operation; the script has no added
mandatory outer confirmation.

Fixes # N/A — scoped follow-up to the endpoint report; command-policy
and parser work is tracked separately in #24419.

### Why we need it and why it was done in this way

The following tradeoffs were made:

This PR repairs approval inheritance, routing and presentation while
preserving the existing permission policy. First-use Shell consent,
session-wide grants, expanded command patterns and mandatory code-mode
dispatch approval are excluded from the final diff. The approval-rule
core, Pi approval-facts implementation, built-in tool descriptors and
destructive detector match the merge base. Ordinary auto Bash still runs
automatically; this PR does not fully resolve the original ordinary-Bash
endpoint report.

Code mode executes JavaScript in QuickJS without direct
Node/filesystem/network access. File and shell effects use nested tools,
each with its own policy checks. A separate script confirmation
duplicates the actual operation's approval, so the native regression now
requires exactly one request naming Bash, including when called from a
child script.

The following alternatives were considered:

Mandatory outer code-mode approval, first-use consent and session
grants, expanded string patterns, endpoint tool suppression, OS
sandboxing and independent classification. The bilingual Agent Note
records their rationale and limits. Structured parsing, selectors and
the single JSON policy belong to separate work.

Links to places where the discussion took place:

https://github.com/CherryHQ/cherry-studio/pull/24419

### Agent Note / Spec

Agent Note:
`.agents/notes/implemented/bug-fix/2026-11-12-agent-shell-approval-boundary.md`
and its reviewed Chinese counterpart.

Spec PR: N/A — direct subagent approval-routing/presentation bug fix.
#24419 owns the separate command-policy redesign and is not implemented
by this PR.

Acceptance criteria:

- Regression — children honor the root's live mode and cannot bypass
required approval by delegating.
- Regression — foreground/background requests retain complete input and
correct task origin, without effects before approval or after
denial/responder loss.
- Regression — direct Bash and code-mode-nested Bash use the same
policy; one approval identifies the actual Bash call, with no mandatory
script-level prompt.
- Regression — dynamic approvals render, resolved parts do not
re-prompt, and origin/command/keyboard behavior remain usable.
- Regression — ordinary auto shell execution and the existing
destructive-command checks retain their behavior.

### Verification

fix(usage): preserve entries on cost sort and link chart point filtering (#25502)

### What this PR does

Before this PR:

1. In `AiUsageRecordService.list`, sorting the Usage requests table by
`cost` (`settings.usage.entry_sort_by = 'cost'`) added `cost_currency =
query.costCurrency` to the `WHERE` filter. When records in the active
window were unpriced (`cost_currency IS NULL`) or in a different
currency before/without a matching selection, the query returned `0`
entries and `total = 0`. Because `UsageEntriesTable` omits
`<TableHeader>` when `entries.length === 0`, the persisted `'cost'` sort
choice trapped the user on `0` entries with no header control to switch
back, while `useUsageEntriesData` also swallowed list errors as `0`
entries and issued a redundant initial-mount `reset()` call.
2. After the ECharts redesign (`#19084`), `Echarts`, `Chart`, and
`UsageDistributionChart` did not emit data-point click events, and `GET
/ai-usage-records` had no group-dimension filter parameters, so clicking
a point on the line/bar/pie chart could not filter the Requests table
below.

After this PR:

1. `AiUsageRecordService.list` keeps all records when `sortBy ===
'cost'` by ranking matching-currency rows via `CASE WHEN cost_currency =
? THEN cost ELSE NULL END` and sorting unpriced / non-matching-currency
rows after them (with matching `getListSortValue` keyset cursors).
`useUsageEntriesData` skips the redundant initial-mount `reset()` and
surfaces list errors via an error alert in `UsageEntriesTable`.
2. `Echarts` / `Chart` expose `onDataPointClick` (including
`timelineIndex` tracking via `timelinechanged`),
`AiUsageRecordListQuerySchema` / `AiUsageRecordService.list` accept
optional group-dimension filters (`providerId`, `modelId`, `sourceType`,
`sourceId`, `apiKeyId`, `apiKeyAttribution`, `authMethod`), and
`UsageDistributionChart` + `UsageSettings` + `UsageEntriesTable` filter
the Requests list by the clicked point's date/period and group identity
(with toggle-off on repeat click, clear chip in the Requests header, and
reset on window change).

Fixes #25467

### Why we need it and why it was done in this way

The following tradeoffs were made:

- Scoped cost sorting ranks matching-currency entries first and treats
non-matching/unpriced entries as `NULL` rather than filtering them out,
so `total` and row visibility stay consistent with the overview and
chart metrics while still preventing unlike currencies from competing
numerically.
- Clicking a chart data point filters only the Requests entries table
(session-local state, cleared on window change) rather than overriding
the chart's own `windowRange`, preserving the chart context so users can
click between points freely.

The following alternatives were considered:

- Filtering only to `costCurrency = query.costCurrency OR costCurrency
IS NULL` was rejected because users with mixed-currency records sorted
by cost would still see fewer total entries than the overview/chart
request counts.
- Having chart clicks mutate the page-wide `windowRange` was rejected
because it collapses the multi-day trend chart to a single day.

Links to places where the discussion took place:
https://github.com/CherryHQ/cherry-studio/issues/25467

feat(agent-sandbox): add the base sandbox policy and its Claude Code translation (#25559)

### What this PR does

Before this PR:

The Spec (#25512) defines a runtime-neutral base sandbox policy with
per-Agent overlays and a Claude Code adapter, but none of it exists in
code.

After this PR:

- `src/main/ai/toolApproval/sandboxPolicy.ts` —
`resolveSandboxPolicy(overlay, platform, homeDir)` merges an Agent
overlay into the base. It returns no policy without an overlay or off
macOS. List fields are unioned and de-duplicated; a denied domain is
removed from the allowed list. Writable paths are expanded (`~`), and
any path that is the home directory, an ancestor of it, a shell startup
file in it, or relative is dropped. Only `allowedDomains`,
`deniedDomains` and `writablePaths` are read, so an overlay has no way
to express the base invariants.
- `src/main/ai/runtime/claudeCode/sandboxSettings.ts` —
`toClaudeCodeSandboxSettings(policy)` produces the SDK `sandbox` option:
enabled, `failIfUnavailable`, `autoAllowBashIfSandboxed`,
`allowUnsandboxedCommands` (escapes stay possible, behind approval),
strict network allowlist, and `filesystem.allowWrite`. It never emits
Apple Events, Unix socket or nested-namespace options.

Nothing consumes either function yet; no runtime behavior changes. The
next layer wires the Support overlay, the escape approval guard and
effective-settings verification.

Fixes #

### Why we need it and why it was done in this way

The following tradeoffs were made:

- The invariants are structural rather than validated: the policy type
has no field for strict mode, escape approval or the escape hatches, and
the adapter hard-codes them. A later overlay cannot weaken them by
adding a key.
- Network tiers and the Cherry preset list from the Spec are left out
until an overlay needs them (Assistant / user Agents); Support uses the
empty base.
- The session workspace, Agent data directory and temp directory are not
listed in the policy because the SDK already makes the cwd,
`additionalDirectories` and `$TMPDIR` writable (probe evidence in the
Spec).

The following alternatives were considered:

Rejecting an overlay that carries forbidden fields instead of ignoring
them; per-Agent full SDK configs. See the Spec.

docs(agent-sandbox): specify a base shell sandbox policy for Cherry Support (#25512)

### What this PR does

Before this PR:

Cherry Support asks before every interactive Bash or PowerShell call
outside Full Access, because command detection cannot see what a script
or raw API call submits. Users approve many harmless local diagnostics
to reach the few commands that leave the machine.

After this PR:

Adds a proposed Spec (Agent Note) for a runtime-neutral base sandbox
policy with per-Agent overlays and a Claude Code adapter. Cherry Support
on macOS is the only consumer for now. The sandbox has no network
access, so local commands run without approval, and an explicit
`dangerouslyDisableSandbox` escape is the single approval point.
Overlays may only widen what the base allows; strict mode, escape
approval, and the base's other invariants cannot be overridden.

No code changes. Implementation layers will stack on this PR.

Fixes #

### Why we need it and why it was done in this way

The following tradeoffs were made:

- No network inside the sandbox, rather than an allowlist containing the
feedback hosts. Every networked command (including read-only `gh`) still
needs one approval. In exchange, a script cannot reach the submission
hosts without that approval, the unverified `lark-cli` host set does not
matter, and allowing `github.com` does not open a domain-fronting path.
- macOS only. Linux needs bubblewrap/socat and Windows needs an elevated
`claude sandbox install`, so neither is zero-setup; both keep per-call
approval.
- Full Access keeps its "no prompts" meaning: escapes run without a card
there, while commands that stay in the sandbox still have no network.
- The sandbox only turns on after its effective configuration is
verified, using `resolveSettings()` with the same options as the query
and including managed settings. If verification fails, the turn fails
instead of running unsandboxed.

The following alternatives were considered:

Per-Agent full sandbox configs without a shared base; strict allowlist
with feedback hosts; non-strict per-host prompts (`SandboxNetworkAccess`
has no matching tool part and is silently allowed under Full Access);
`excludedCommands: ["gh *"]`; `enableWeakerNetworkIsolation`;
`CLAUDE_CODE_SUBPROCESS_ENV_SCRUB` for built-in sessions (tried in
#25513 and closed: it only hides the loopback internal gateway
credential and breaks `npx skills` global installs by stripping
`CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR`); sandboxing the Assistant now; Linux/Windows now;
wrapping the whole CLI in a VM. Rationale is in the note.

Links to places where the discussion took place: Follow-up to #25488
(feedback submission guard). Prior art reviewed: Codex, Cursor, Claude
Code, VS Code Copilot, Zed, Gemini CLI, Claude Cowork sandboxing docs.

### Agent Note / Spec

Agent Note:
`.agents/notes/proposed/feature/2026-11-26-builtin-agent-sandbox.md` (+
`.zh.md`, `.i18n.yaml`)

Acceptance criteria:

- AC1 — macOS Support runs allowed local Bash in the sandbox without an
approval card (Default / `acceptEdits`).
- AC2 — sandboxed Support Bash cannot reach any host via `curl` or

- AC3 — a `dangerouslyDisableSandbox` call shows the existing Bash card

### What this PR does

Before this PR: Responsive SVGs with extreme aspect ratios could have
their short preview edge rounded to `0` after the upscale and long-edge
cap, leaving the preview dialog blank.

After this PR: Preview dimensions derived from a positive `viewBox` are
clamped to at least one pixel while preserving the existing upscale and
4096-pixel long-edge cap, so extreme-aspect SVGs remain renderable.

The following tradeoffs were made: Extreme-aspect previews may have a
one-pixel short edge, which minimally distorts the mathematical aspect
ratio but keeps the preview renderable instead of blank.

The following alternatives were considered: Leaving fractional
dimensions unrounded was rejected because the existing preview contract
uses integer pixel dimensions; removing the upscale/cap was rejected
because those behaviors bound memory use and improve fullscreen preview
readability.
