commits.message:
feat(cua-driver): share one local IPC client (#8448)

* fix(cua-driver): read daemon presence from one probe

Add DaemonPresence { Absent, Stale, Starting, Serving { pid, gate } } and
probe_presence, which reads the daemon's metadata answer, its socket lock
(tried and released at once) and its socket file together. Daemon
metadata gains an additive permissions_pending field so a daemon that
answers but refuses every tool call reads as Serving with a
PermissionsPending gate.

* fix(cua-driver): keep stop truthful while a daemon is starting

`serve` now claims its socket lock before it builds the desktop runtime,
and a disclaimed macOS relaunch inherits that claim, so a launch reads
as Starting from its first moments. `stop` waits (bounded) for a Starting
daemon to answer and then shuts it down instead of reporting "not
running" and leaving it alive. `serve`'s already-running refusal,
`status` and `wait_for_release` all read probe_presence: status reports
starting, stale socket files and a permissions-pending gate, and a stale
socket file no longer counts as unreleased.

* fix(cua-driver): close the stop race before serve claims its socket

`serve` claims its socket at the top of the serve command, and `stop`
keeps looking for half a second when it finds no daemon, so a launch
that has started but not yet claimed is still waited for and stopped.
The Windows presence probe now bounds its metadata reply, and a
relaunch validates an inherited lock descriptor and marks it
close-on-exec before adopting it.

* fix(cua-driver): clear a stale socket only once serve validates

The early socket claim now takes only the lock. A standalone daemon
removes a dead daemon's socket after startup authorization passes and
before it binds, and removes it only when it is a socket, so a rejected
launch leaves the path alone. `run_serve` is a Unix test helper and the
Unix serve body no longer keeps an `embedded` binding only macOS reads.

* fix(cua-driver): count only a socket as a stale daemon socket

probe_presence reports Stale only when the path is a Unix socket, so a
regular file at --socket is no longer promised to the next launch.
`status` and `stop` name such a file as occupying the path instead.

* fix(cua-driver): name only a non-socket path as occupied

A daemon that binds between the presence probe and the message no longer gets its live socket called a non-socket.

* fix(cua-driver): keep stop waiting while a Windows daemon's pipe still listens

A late metadata reply left the probe reading Starting, which the Windows
branch of is_released counted as released even with the pipe still up.
Count it released only once the pipe stops listening, and cover it with a
Windows test.

* fix(cua-driver): bound Windows daemon replies by REPLY_DEADLINE

Windows clients opened the daemon pipe with std::fs and then blocked in
ReadFile with no limit, so a stalled daemon hung the CLI, MCP proxy and
SDK service sessions forever. Open the pipe for overlapped I/O, wait on
each read and write for at most its timeout, and cancel with CancelIoEx
when it expires. The Unix exchange and service-session deadline loops
now run over it unchanged, and the presence probe no longer leaves a
blocked thread behind.

* fix(cua-driver): let only a closed pipe count as released on Windows

An embedded daemon holds no lock, so a late metadata reply read as Absent
and counted as released while its pipe still listened. On Windows every
state but Serving now asks the pipe. The Windows release test covers the
no-lock case too, and shard 1 runs it.

* fix(cua-driver): hold Windows pipe exchanges to one reply deadline

The service-session reader now checks its deadline after every buffer,
so a peer that trickles bytes without a newline still times out. A
daemon exchange spends one deadline on connect, write and read, which
keeps the presence probe within its two seconds. The overlapped pipe
calls pass one raw OVERLAPPED pointer and never take a reference while
the kernel may write to it.

* fix(cua-driver): count a busy Windows pipe as still held

The probe can hold the only pipe instance while it waits for a late reply,
so a free-instance check read a held pipe as gone. Release and the launch
refusal now ask whether any instance of the pipe exists, free or busy. A
launch beside a lockless embedded daemon that answers late is refused again,
as on main. The Windows test holds the only instance busy.

* fix(cua-driver): keep Windows stop and status truthful while a pipe is held

A lockless embedded daemon that answers late read as Absent, so stop said
the daemon was not running after its short settle and status agreed. On
Windows a held pipe now counts as a daemon that is not answering yet: stop
waits for it as for a starting daemon, and status says the endpoint exists
but is not answering.

* fix(cua-driver): stop Windows pipe reads and writes at the reply deadline

PipeStream takes an absolute deadline that caps every operation's
timeout, so neither a retried write nor a read after a partial reply
waits a further slice past it. The daemon exchange and the service
session set it on their pipe handles; Unix sockets are unchanged.

* fix(cua-driver): treat a Unix socket that still listens as held, not stale

A lockless embedded daemon that answered metadata late read as Stale, so a
standalone launch took the lock and unlinked its live socket, and
wait_for_release reported success while it still held the path. A socket
that still accepts connections now counts as a held endpoint on Unix, as a
held pipe does on Windows: launch refuses it, stop waits for it, status says
it is not answering, release waits for it, and the stale-socket cleanup
leaves it alone.

* fix(cua-driver): take only repeated refusal as a dead Unix socket

macOS refuses a connection while a live listener's accept queue is full,
so one refused connect read a held socket as dead. The socket probe now
retries a refusal for half a second, and treats any error other than a
refusal or a missing path as a listener that is still there.

* fix(cua-driver): build every Windows crate against windows 0.61

cua-driver-core, cua-driver-sdk (dev-dependencies) and platform-windows
were still on windows 0.58 while cua-driver, the testkit and the e2e crate
used 0.61. Move the three to 0.61 and port the API changes:

- BOOL moved to windows::core.
- VARIANT moved to Win32::System::Variant (new Win32_System_Ole and
  Win32_System_Variant features); its fields are read directly, and the
  owned BSTR is read in place instead of rebuilt and forgotten.
- PROPERTYKEY moved to Win32::Foundation.
- Nullable handle, string and flag parameters are Option<_>; null handles
  pass None, and HBITMAP/HMODULE convert into HGDIOBJ/HINSTANCE.

windows 0.58 leaves the driver lockfile. windows 0.59 stays: clipboard-rs
0.3.5, its latest release, still requires it. The cua-spacesd lockfiles
pick up platform-windows and cua-driver-core on 0.61.

* fix(cua-driver): never block a presence probe on a full Unix accept queue

On Linux a blocking connect to a listener whose accept queue is full waits
indefinitely, which left the metadata probe, wait_for_release and the
socket check without a bound. The presence probe now connects without
blocking and retries a full queue only until its reply deadline, and the
socket check treats a full queue as a listener that is still there.
send_request keeps its blocking connect.

* feat(cua-driver): share one local IPC client

Add cua_driver_core::ipc with LocalIpcClient, ConnectPolicy, exchange_line
and the async LocalIpcStream. The daemon request path and the SDK trusted
service session send one line through LocalIpcClient on every OS, with the
same connect retry, 10 s read poll and deadline. The MCP proxy control
connection and the MCP envelope relay connect through LocalIpcStream. The
Windows pipe client is written against windows 0.61 and replaces
pipe_stream and socket_io.

* fix(cua-driver): never hang on a FIFO lock or miss a symlinked live socket

A FIFO left at the lock path blocked the presence probe on open. The lock
now opens without blocking and only a regular file counts as a lock.

A symlink to a socket that still listens read as Absent and so as
released. A probe that finds no answer now follows the path and counts a
live socket behind it as held.

* fix(cua-driver): keep IPC reads, writes and connect retries inside their bounds

A blocking macOS socket write could run past the exchange deadline, and a
connect retry could sleep past its budget. Unix sockets are now nonblocking
and each read or write waits in poll for at most what is left of its slice;
the Windows pipe client takes the same per-operation timeout. A retry pause
is cut to the budget that is left.

* fix(cua-driver): refuse a Windows launch whose pipe was taken after its check

A standalone launch checks for a daemon before it builds its runtime. A
lockless embedded daemon could take the pipe name in between, and the
launch then opened a second instance beside it. Every daemon now takes
its first instance with the first-instance flag, so that launch fails
and says the pipe is already held.

The macOS unit lane now also runs the daemon presence tests.

* fix(cua-driver): record a Windows daemon's PID only once it holds its pipe

A launch that lost the pipe race wrote its PID file before the first
pipe instance was refused, so status named the rejected process. The PID
file is now written after the first instance is created, as on Unix.

The macOS and Windows unit lanes now run the whole cua-driver binary
suite instead of a module filter.

* fix(cua-driver): compare perception worker paths as paths in the extension test

The Windows binary suite now runs whole, which exposed a test that
matched worker arguments with string suffixes using forward slashes.
Windows joins those paths with backslashes, so the test compares them
as paths.

* fix(cua-driver): remove the Windows pipe tests' lock files when they end

* fix(cua-driver): wait out a pipe operation's whole timeout on Windows

WaitForSingleObject can end a timed wait up to a clock tick early, so a
read or write could report a timeout before its slice had passed.

* fix(cua-driver): format the Windows pipe wait

* fix(ci): retry the rootless Xwayland harness's first sway IPC request

sway's IPC socket appears before sway answers on a loaded runner, and
swaymsg waits only 3 s for a reply, so the Linux X11 capture step failed
before its test ran. Retry until the harness's existing deadline, and
print sway's log if it never answers.

fix(cua-driver): keep consent grants inside the session episode that approved them (#8287)

* test(cua-driver): a grant approved after end_session must not reach the next episode

A history call waits on a blocking consent provider while end_session
lands, the person approves, and the label is started again. The next
call reuses the stale grant instead of prompting.

* fix(cua-driver): keep each session's lifecycle in one episode map

LifecycleRecord and the ended, idle-ended, explicitly-ended, closed
transport, suspended scope and cleanup-progress collections become one
Lifecycle under one lock. Each session id maps to an Episode with an
EpisodeId and a Live, Ending or Ended phase; the id grows on every new
episode, including a revival or a recreation by the next call.

Admission and start_session share one claim check. A closed transport
is recorded before its sessions end and refused on every label, so a
call it sent before the close cannot bind a label afterwards; closed
owners no label names are forgotten after the idle TTL.

* fix(cua-driver): drop a consent grant whose episode ended during approval

ResourceGrantKey carries the EpisodeId the grant was approved in, so a
later episode of the same label never finds it. authorize stores an
approval only when the episode it started in is still live; otherwise
it revokes it and returns authorization_canceled. A session already
ending or ended gets an approval for that call only.

* fix(cua-driver): admit a call into its session before asking for consent

begin_session_dispatch now runs ahead of the protected-resource
adapters, so a call waiting on a person counts as in flight: end_session
and the idle sweep defer instead of ending the episode under it. An end
that arrives meanwhile still wins, and the call is refused before it
acts.

* fix(cua-driver): settle the closed-transport refusal and clippy in the episode map

A closed transport's late call on its old label is refused as
TransportClosed, the refusal admission now gives a closed owner on any
label.

* test(cua-driver): expect TransportClosed for a closed owner's late call on its label

Admission refuses a closed owner on any label as TransportClosed before
it looks at the label's ended episode.

* fix(cua-driver): close the revive-hook, grant-insert and closed-transport gaps

Revive hooks hold a separate end-order lock instead of the lifecycle
lock, so a hook that reads session state cannot deadlock while an end
still waits for the hooks to finish.

authorize checks the episode and stores the grant under the grant lock.
The session-end hook revokes under that lock after the end is recorded,
so an end that lands after the check still revokes the grant.

A closed transport's late call on its label is refused as
session_unavailable from the same claim check admission uses, instead of
the session_ended hint to restart or pick a new label.

* fix(cua-driver): cancel a consent request queued behind another once its episode ends

authorize rechecks the episode after it gets its turn at consent
admission, so a call queued behind another prompt when end_session lands
is canceled without asking anyone, and the end completes when the
in-flight calls return.

* test(cua-driver): pin the consent-queue cancellation to its exact refusal

The queued-behind-another consent test now expects the queued call to
be canceled without a prompt, and the registry test asserts both calls
end in authorization_canceled rather than any error.

fix(cua-driver): give authorization one AuthorizationPhase clock (#8304)

* fix(cua-driver): give authorization one AuthorizationPhase clock

The authorization context and the capability manifest each kept their own
idle lease and sticky expiry flag, and a call could refresh one while the
other refused it. The context now owns a single AuthorizationPhase
(Active, IdleExpired, Expired, Revoked) that merges its own TTLs with the
manifest's declared expires_after and idle_timeout. The manifest keeps
only those declared limits.

Dispatch reads the phase before any lifecycle work, so start_session
refuses with the phase instead of reviving an episode that every later
call would be denied in. Refusals keep their existing codes and add
authorization_phase.

* fix(cua-driver): read the authorization lease time under its lock

A dispatch that read the time before taking the phase lock could commit
an older last_dispatch over a newer one and idle-expire an active context
early.

fix(cua-driver): carry call identity as a typed DispatchIdentity (#8348)

* fix(cua-driver): carry call identity as a typed DispatchIdentity

The dispatch boundary resolved a call's session identity by stamping
`_session_id`, `_transport_session_id` and `_public_session_label` into
the arguments, returning a `runtime_prefix` string, and then reading the
keys back out of the JSON for ended-session checks, lifecycle admission,
consent, process ownership, recording and history.

Resolve it once, from trusted evidence, the authorization context and the
public `session` label, into a `DispatchIdentity { runtime, lifecycle,
transport, public_label }`. Core code reads the typed value, and the
platform tool's arguments are stamped from it in one place. Reserved keys
in caller arguments are still stripped at the outer boundary, and the
stamp replaces or removes them in any case.

Protected-resource grant keys now come straight from the identity
(runtime, lifecycle session, transport) instead of a public-session then
transport string fallback, and `revoke_session` matches the lifecycle id.

* fix(cua-driver): keep an empty trusted transport id in DispatchIdentity

The old dispatch kept a context's empty transport id as the call's owner. resolve dropped it and fell back to the lifecycle id.

feat(cua-driver): persist get_window_state max_elements and max_depth defaults (#8563)

* feat(cua-driver): save get_window_state walk defaults in core

get_window_state.max_elements and get_window_state.max_depth persist in
~/.cua-driver/config.json and replace the built-in default on a plain read
that omits the argument. A per-call argument always wins; query, full_output
and observation reads keep the platform cap.

* feat(cua-driver): read saved walk defaults in every get_window_state backend

macOS, Windows and Linux load get_window_state.max_elements and
get_window_state.max_depth at startup, accept them in set_config, report the
effective and saved values in get_config, and resolve each read through the
shared ViewOptions rules. The since view key now records the depth the walk
used, so changing the saved depth falls back to a full read.

* feat(cua-driver): list the get_window_state walk defaults in cua-driver config

config get and set name get_window_state.max_elements and
get_window_state.max_depth, and config reset clears them.

* docs(cua-driver): regenerate references for the saved walk defaults

The macOS MCP snapshot and CLI spec come from the native dump; the Windows
and Linux snapshots carry the same source strings for their tools.

* fix(cua-driver): refuse the whole set_config call on a bad walk default

A refused get_window_state.max_elements or max_depth value used to leave
cursor keys from the same call saved. Each backend now validates the walk
keys before writing anything.

* fix(cua-driver): advertise the saved walk defaults as plain integers

The Vertex AI schema lint rejects a list of types, so set_config now
advertises get_window_state.max_elements and max_depth as integers from 0 to
the platform cap. 0 clears a saved value, as default and null still do.

* fix(cua-driver): restore the saved walk defaults in the macOS tool spec

The merge from main took main's copy of the generated macOS spec and
dropped this branch's max_elements and max_depth descriptions and the
get_window_state set_config keys.

* fix(cua-driver): name only 0 as the MCP clear value for saved walk defaults

The set_config schema types both keys as integers, so a client that
validates arguments against it rejects "default" and null. The parser
still accepts them, and the CLI keeps `config set <key> default`.

feat(mobile): start a chat from an artifact with it attached (KRTX-5255) (#13231)

## Review in 60 seconds

- **Ask AI on mobile artifacts.** The artifact `···` sheet gets an **Ask
AI** row, in the viewer and on a long press in the Artifacts list. It
opens a new chat on project home with the artifact shown as a chip on
the composer before any message. The chip's X removes it. Leaving home
drops it: a page or thread covering home, or closing the project, which
unmounts home (review item, `ProjectHome.tsx` unmount cleanup).
- **Same context as desktop.** The send uses the desktop Ask AI sheet's
first prompt: the person's words, then the artifact's Files path as a
`Referenced files` block, so the agent reads the current artifact rather
than its name. The session gets the `artifact:<id>` label, so web's Ask
AI history lists it. `lib/artifacts/artifact-chat.test.ts` pins the
block to the web builder byte for byte. Web code is unchanged.
- **No silent send without it.** Home reads the artifact again. While
that read loads, or after it fails, Send refuses with a toast ("Couldn't
attach “…”. Tap it to try again, or remove it.") and keeps the draft.
Tapping the failed chip retries.
- The native mobile app cannot run in this sandbox. There is no iOS
simulator, no Android SDK and no `/dev/kvm`. The Expo web build fails on
the app's Skia hero (`MakeSurface`), and the artifact viewer is a
`react-native-webview`, which has no web target. The flow is covered by
render tests of the real `ProjectHome` and `ArtifactActionsSheet`, and
the create body was posted to the local API (below).
- **Risk:** low, mobile only, behind an explicit tap. Unverified here:
the on-device look of the chip, and a live agent reply. The local stack
could not start a sandbox (platinum provider over its template quota,
Daytona 401), so the session was created but never ran a turn. Desktop
Ask AI was not re-run in a browser; its code is untouched.
- **Verified:** `bun test --isolate` of the 5 touched/new test files: 47
pass, 0 fail. Whole mobile suite `pnpm test` (after `npx
patch-package`): 3950 pass, 0 fail. `tsgo` typecheck: only the
pre-existing `ProjectScreen.tsx(996,9)` error. New tests go red at
origin/dev. The local API `POST /v1/projects/:id/sessions` accepted the
mobile-built body and stored the label. Unrun: device/simulator demo and
a live agent reply (environment, see above).
- suna-skills: contributing, learnings, worktree and testing (headings
and key sections), apps/mobile/AGENTS.md (read in full);
apps/mobile/design.md and kortix-design-system not read: the chip reuses
the composer's existing staged-command chip markup
- ponytail: full · review: Lean already. Ship. · markers: 0
- Self-review: 4 items found and fixed (the sheet row had no test →
`artifact-actions-ask-ai.test.tsx`; an unused export; G9 item: the
attachment survived an unmount → cleared on unmount; the body called the
markdown-keys failures pre-existing, but they came from this sandbox's
install skipping mobile's `patch-package` → re-run with the patches
applied, 0 fail)
- Linear: KRTX-5255 (mobile version 1.6.61 → 1.6.62 via `set-version.mjs
--next`)

## Demo video

No demo video: a mobile simulator in this sandbox is unavailable (no iOS
simulator, no Android SDK, no /dev/kvm), and the app's Expo web build
cannot render the Skia hero or the WebView artifact viewer. The
behaviour is pinned by render tests of the real screens; the reviewer's
device check is listed below.

## Quick verification

- Outcome: on mobile, Ask AI in an artifact's `···` sheet opens a new
chat with that artifact attached. The first send carries the artifact
exactly as the desktop Ask AI sheet does, and refuses to send while the
artifact is loading or unreadable.
- On a device (TestFlight after merge): open Artifacts, open a doc, tap
`···` → Ask AI. Home shows the doc's chip. Type a question about it and
send: the agent answers from the doc. Tap X instead: nothing is sent.
- Tests: `bun test --isolate` of the 5 touched test files → 47 pass, 0
fail; red at origin/dev before the change. Whole mobile suite → 3950
pass, 0 fail.
- Review fix: leave the project with an artifact attached, come back:
home shows no chip and the next chat carries no artifact (`leaving the
project unmounts home …` test, red without the cleanup line).
- Pre-existing: `cd apps/mobile && pnpm typecheck` fails the same at
origin/dev (`components/session/ProjectScreen.tsx(996,9)`,
`openSpringConfig`).

fix(mobile): artifact pages keep their momentum after a flick on iOS (KRTX-5256) (#13230)

## Demo video

No demo video: the Linux sandbox has no iOS simulator or device, so the
iOS native scroll view this fixes is unavailable to record. The local
stack's web app does not run this code path (the change is in
react-native-webview's iOS component). Proof below is the regression
test that renders the artifact viewer through the real library
component, and the shipped iOS bundle containing the patched default.

## Quick verification

Outcome: on iOS, a flick in the artifact viewer (and every other in-app
web view) keeps scrolling after the finger lifts and slows down at the
system rate, instead of stopping dead. Closes KRTX-5256.

- **Root cause.** react-native-webview 14.0.1 never initializes
`decelerationRate` on iOS. Under the new architecture an unset prop
reaches the native view as the codegen default `0`, and the library
writes that rate to the WKWebView scroll view on every drag
(`scrollViewWillBeginDragging`). A rate of 0 means no momentum. Upstream
fixed it natively in 17.x (`_decelerationRate =
UIScrollViewDecelerationRateNormal` in the init); 17.x is a major
upgrade, so this PR patches 14.0.1 instead.
- **Fix.** `apps/mobile/patches/react-native-webview+14.0.1.patch` (the
app's existing `patch-package` flow: `postinstall`, the
`eas-build-post-install` hook that store builds use, and the TestFlight
workflow's `patch-package --error-on-fail`): an unset rate becomes
`'normal'` = 0.998, UIKit's and Safari's default. An explicit rate
passes through unchanged. No app component changes. Android is untouched
(the prop is iOS only).
- **Who else gets it.** Every `WebView` in the app sets no rate, so the
Browser page, the HTML file preview, the sandbox preview sheet and
`show` content also get normal momentum. AppsPage and Mermaid set
`scrollEnabled={false}` and are unaffected.
- **Unchanged:** the sheet (`enableContentPanningGesture={false}`, title
row drags it), the close and `···` controls, drag tracking, and
horizontal scrolling of wide tables (an inner WebKit scroller, not this
rate). Mobile version 1.6.61 → 1.6.62 (`set-version.mjs --next`).

A worktree stopped sooner leaves nothing to copy. Tests: `turbopack-portable-loaders.test.ts` (4) and `turbopack-seed.test.ts` (3). Studio Translate: preserve cue boundaries in CR-delimited WebVTT files (#19473)

Closes #19472.

Studio reads uploaded subtitle files with `TextDecoder`, which preserves
carriage returns. A WebVTT file using CR for its line endings therefore
reached the parser intact, but the parser only split on LF and CRLF.
With no cues found, Translate sent the document through its plain-text
path.

The parser now recognizes all three WebVTT line terminators and keeps
the source separators when rebuilding the file. A single CRLF still
counts as one line ending. The numbered translation path also recognizes
CR inside a multiline caption.

I used a two-cue file with an identifier, an alignment setting and a
multiline caption. Chromium read both cues. On `0443880` the Studio
parser returned `null` for the CR version and two cues for the LF and
CRLF versions. With this change all three produced the same caption-only
translation request and kept the original timestamps and separators on
export.

The regression test runs the parser and translation code with a
deterministic reply. All 102 Translate tests passed locally on Windows
with Node 24.16.0.

Studio: live denoise preview for MiniMax-H3 video (fitted latent map, no slowdown, bit-identical output) (#20094)

## Summary

MiniMax-H3 video renders now show the same live denoise preview as
LTX-2.5, Wan 2.2 5B and HunyuanVideo-1.5: a rough picture of the first
frame, refreshed while the clip denoises.

It is a fitted linear latent to RGB map, the same mechanism #12692
added. No tiny decoder and no downloaded weights. The final video and
audio are unchanged.

## How it works

- **The map.** H3's video VAE has 24 latent channels at 16x spatial
compression. A ridge least-squares fit maps each latent pixel to RGB (24
weights + bias per colour). It is fitted against H3's own VAE decode
(`unsloth/MiniMax-H3`, `vae/`), on latents normalised exactly as the
denoiser sees them (`(z - latents_mean) / latents_std`).
- **Where it sits.** The transformer packs latents into `(1, 2, 2)` rows
of 96 features, so the per-pixel map is placed block-diagonally into a
`96 -> 12` token map (`layout: tokens`, `down: 32`, `patch: 2`). It is
the `minimax_h3` entry in `diffusion_preview_factors.py`, selected
through `preview_factors` on the `minimax-h3` family.
- **The hook.** H3's modular loop has no step callback, so `video.py`
already wraps `pipe.scheduler.step` with `scheduler_step_preview` for
it, exactly as for HunyuanVideo-1.5. That wrapper hands the previewer
the step's video rows as one unbatched `[N, 96]` sequence. `latent_grid`
now takes that 2-D sequence as a view (`unsqueeze(0)`), which is the
only change to `diffusion_preview.py`.
  - Only the video scheduler is wrapped, never `audio_scheduler`.
- Conditioning rows are never stepped, so they never reach the preview.
- The Euler x0 estimate reads the video scheduler's own device `sigmas`.
- **When it stays off.** Nothing changes on the API, chat-tool and MCP
routes: they pass `live_preview=False`, so no previewer is created and
`scheduler.step` is not wrapped. The UI toggle and
`UNSLOTH_DIFFUSION_PREVIEW=0` turn it off as before. The GGUF path
renders through the native sd.cpp server and is not affected.

## Fit quality (held-out photos, never seen in training)

Data: 60 COCO val photos at 384x512, each as a static 22-frame clip and
as a 22-frame slow pan + zoom clip. Training used 28 static and 16
moving clips; 8 static and 8 moving clips were held out. Each held-out
clip's linear preview of latent frame 0 was compared with the VAE's real
decode of frame 0.

| held-out set | PSNR, native preview size | PSNR, as shown (with
smoothing) | LPIPS (alex), as shown | first 3 channels min-max baseline
|
|---|---|---|---|---|
| static clips (8) | 30.45 dB (min 28.95) | 25.07 dB | 0.227 | 8.91 dB |
| moving clips (8) | 29.02 dB (min 27.06) | 22.91 dB | 0.289 | 10.96 dB
|

Fitting on frame 0 only beat fitting on every latent frame of the first
chunk: 29.0 vs 24.0 dB on the moving held-out clips. The token map
matches the per-pixel map on diffusers' own `patchify_video_latents`
rows to 3e-16.

## GPU check (RTX PRO 6000 Blackwell 96 GB, interleaved fresh processes,
Studio defaults)

Setup: `unsloth/MiniMax-H3` text to video, 960x544, 124 frames, 20
steps, one seed. Studio resolved INT8 transformer + INT8 text encoder,
compiled, resident (no offload). Each process does one 4-step warm
render, then one measured render. Per-step time comes from CUDA events
recorded at each video `scheduler.step` (never synchronised during the
render). Host syncs were counted with
`torch.cuda.set_sync_debug_mode("warn")`.

| arm | runs | s/step (median of steps 2..20) | wall s | host syncs
(whole render / denoise) | previews published | video sha256 | audio
sha256 |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| this PR, preview off | 3 | 2.0540 / 2.0672 / 2.0683 | 46.21 / 46.57 /
46.59 | 148 / 4 (all three) | 0 | `256dd5c3af70` | `a3f906fefd19` |
| this PR, preview on | 3 | 2.0650 / 2.0678 / 2.0672 | 46.51 / 46.59 /
46.57 | 148 / 4 (all three) | 19 / 19 / 19 | `256dd5c3af70` |
`a3f906fefd19` |
| main, preview requested | 1 | 2.0677 | 46.57 | 148 / 4 | 0 (no map on
main) | `256dd5c3af70` | `a3f906fefd19` |

- **Speed.** Every preview-on run falls inside the preview-off spread,
for both s/step (2.054 to 2.068) and wall time (46.21 to 46.59 s).
- **Syncs.** The host-sync count is identical in every arm, both over
the whole render and inside the denoise window.
- **Output.** Video frames and the audio track are bit-identical across
all seven runs.
- **Preview.** Each preview-on run published a picture on 19 of its 20
steps; the first step has no partner step for the x0 estimate yet.

Studio: live denoise previews do no work unless a visible page is watching the render (#20081)

## Summary

Live denoise previews now cost nothing when nobody is looking. Until
now, a render started from the Images or Video page did its preview work
on every planned step: a projection or tiny VAE decode, a pinned copy
and a JPEG encode. That happened even when the tab was in the
background, the page was closed, or the only thing polling was an MCP or
status client that never shows the preview.

With this change the work runs only while a visible page is polling that
render's progress.

- `LatentPreviewer` takes a new `watch` kind (`"image"` / `"video"`).
`on_step` returns before any GPU op or copy unless a progress poll that
asked for the preview arrived after this render started and within the
last 5 s (`WATCH_WINDOW_S`). When it skips, it also drops its stored
previous step, so a viewer who comes back mid-render gets a fresh x0
pair at the next planned snapshot instead of a stale one.
- `GET /images/generate-progress` and `GET /video/generate-progress`
accept `preview` (default `false`). A watch is recorded only on the path
that answers with the running job's own progress. Hidden,
foreign-account, reservation-handoff, finished-outcome and batch-rider
replies never count, and riders never get the job's preview anyway.
- The Images and Video pages add `preview=1` to their progress poll only
while `document.visibilityState === "visible"`. A hidden tab keeps
polling progress as before but no longer asks for the preview. The next
visible poll turns it back on.
- `watch=None`, the default, keeps the old always-on behaviour for any
other caller.

Things that do not change:
- Output bytes. The previewer only reads the latent, and skipping it
does less of that.
- Host syncs. The gate is a dict read and a monotonic clock compare on
the denoise thread.
- An explicit `live_preview=false` still builds no previewer at all, so
it wins over any watcher.
- API, chat tool and MCP renders still pass `live_preview=False`.
- The `UNSLOTH_DIFFUSION_PREVIEW=0` kill switch.

## UI

What a visible page shows does not change. After a hidden tab becomes
visible again, the preview it shows can be a few steps old until the
next planned snapshot lands, at most one snapshot interval. UI evidence
for that resume path is still needed.

## Images page switch

The Images page's "Live preview" switch now also gates the poll: with it
off, `preview=1` is never sent, so turning it off mid-render stops the
per-step work, not only the display (`tests/preview-watch.test.ts`).

## Tests

Backend, all on CPU:
- `tests/test_diffusion_preview_watchers.py`
  - Builds a real previewer with pinned memory and CUDA events stubbed.
- An unwatched render never reaches the step body and drops its stale
partner.
- A watcher opening mid-render resumes it, and leaving for longer than
the window stops it.
- A poll for the other kind, or one made before this render started, is
not a watcher.
- `watch=None` keeps the old behaviour, and `requested=False` returns no
previewer even with watchers.
- An AST check confirms both engine `LatentPreviewer.create` sites pass
their kind.
  - The headless `live_preview=False` paths are still present.
- `tests/test_diffusion_routes.py`: only `preview=1` on the image
progress route records a watch.
- `tests/test_account_video_progress_handoff.py`: only `preview=1` on a
reply carrying the running job's progress records a watch. A reservation
handoff does not.

The new tests fail on main and pass here. Every existing test that
mentions previews or generate-progress (54 files) gives the same result
on main and on this branch.

Frontend: `tests/preview-watch.test.ts` loads both `api.ts` modules with
stubs. It asserts that `preview=1` is sent only when the document is
visible, is appended correctly after `video_id`, and is absent when
hidden or when there is no document. `npm test` gives the same single
pre-existing failure on main and here (the Vite KaTeX stylesheet test).

## Not covered

- A real GPU render with the tab hidden and then shown was not run here,
only CPU stubs.
- Creating the previewer itself (pinned slots, its worker thread, and
loading the tiny decoder for Wan) still happens once per render that the
UI starts, even if nobody watches. Only the per-step work is gated.

Studio images: per-row layout for Qwen-Image-2.1 batches (mixed prompt lengths in one forward, 2.12x streamed on A100) (#20072)

Follows #19837 (merged), which added the batch adapters and the measured
race.

## Problem

Qwen-Image-2.1 lays out a batch from row 0. Prompts of different lengths
are right-padded to the longest, so a shorter row's image tokens took
the longest prompt's RoPE positions, which is a cross-row effect. To
keep rows correct, `text_length_runs` split every mixed-length batch
into calls of one length. As a result, #19837's adapter treats a
Qwen-Image-2.1 load as `batched_forward = False` and concurrent requests
render one at a time, even when the denoiser streams from host memory
and a shared call would save most of the weight transfer.

## Change

- `diffusion_qwenimage21_rope.py` / `diffusion_qwenimage21.py`: when the
rows' text masks differ, each row gets its own RoPE table, exactly the
table it would get alone at its real positions. This applies on every
Studio attention path (stock, eager fused, ConvRot fused, ROCm, bounded
math, TP2) and under CUDA graphs. Padded text stays a masked key.
Uniform batches and a single row take the unchanged path.
- Policy: a mixed-length batch needs the key mask, which the int8
attention kernel does not take, so mixed lengths share one call only
when the denoiser streams from host memory. With a resident denoiser,
rows keep the split by length. On compiled blocks a mixed batch is a new
graph signature, so it is only admitted at a batch size that an
off-request warm (`warming_mixed_lengths`, run by the batching race or
an idle worker) has already run. A user request never compiles it; until
the warm has run, the rows render apart.
- `diffusion_families.py`: `DiffusionFamily.batched_forward` (None = not
stated, the existing default rules). The Qwen-Image-2.1 record sets it
to True, so #19837's adapter admits the load and `layout_key` is the
coalescer's match key.
- Kill switches: `UNSLOTH_DIFFUSION_Q21_ROW_LAYOUT=0` restores the row-0
layout. `UNSLOTH_DIFFUSION_Q21_MIXED_BATCH=1/0` forces the mixed-length
policy either way.

## What Auto does by default

Nothing changes for a single user. With concurrent requests:

- **Streamed denoiser** (Low VRAM / group offload): requests share a
call, including prompts of different lengths once the warm has run. This
is the 2.12x placement below.
- **Resident weights**: requests stay serial, as they do today. #19837's
race only promotes a size where it measures a win, and that win serves
only with a passing offline G2c verdict for this family, card and
execution path (the gate ships with none). A forced resident mixed batch
measured 0.74x, so we expect resident loads to stay serial anyway.

## Gates

G1: an N=1 single-image request is byte-identical to the base; a request
with `batch_size` > 1 shares one forward across its images, so its bytes
may differ by floating-point batch-shape effects and that path is gated
by G2a and G2c instead. G2a: a row's bytes do not change when its
neighbours change. G2c: paired LPIPS against a bf16 speed-off reference,
upper bound of (batched minus solo) at most +0.01. G4: speed lower bound
at least 1.05x with p95 at most +3%. 1024 px, 25 steps, Studio Auto
(int8).

| Gate | Result |
|---|---|
| G1 | Solo images byte-identical to the base tree, resident and
streamed (A100-80). A/A repeat identical. |
| G2a | Target first / middle / last in a batch of 3. Bit-identical (max
px 0) against an identical rerun, against neighbours of another token
length with other seeds, and against a same-length neighbour swap. |
| Activations | One captured transformer step, prefill and cached
decode, with the neighbours' latents scaled x1e4: the target row is
exact. |
| G2c | Mixed lengths (26 / 32 / 34 / 40 tokens): upper bound +0.0025,
n=32, PASS (A100-40). An earlier 12-pair run had mean +0.0016 but an
upper bound of +0.0138 (underpowered, over eps). |
| Streamed batch-4 | 2.12x (60.2 s to 28.4 s per 4, A100-80) and 2.14x
(A100-40), Low VRAM, 25 denoiser calls per batch instead of 100. |
| Resident batch-4 | Policy keeps it serial: 1.00x, 100 calls. Forced
mixed-length batch: 0.74x, which is why resident stays serial. |

G4: streamed clears 1.05x by a wide margin. Resident does not, and stays
serial.

**G4 (RTX PRO 6000 Blackwell), through #19837's route and race, this
branch merged with #19837, streamed (Low VRAM)**:

| Gate | Result |
|---|---|
| G1 | N=1 single-image requests byte-identical to #19837: 10/10 |
| G2a (race neighbour check) | exact, max diff 0; A/A exact |
| Row 0 vs its own solo render (same path) | byte-identical (max 0 px) |
| G2c | batched rows bit-identical to their solo renders: upper bound
0.000 vs the eager reference and vs solo (n=8) |
| Race | size 2 lost on speed (lower bound 1.001x): on this card
streaming costs little, so a shared call saves nothing; size 4 skipped
(no static-compile graph at 4) |
| Auto after the race | no admitted batch size at this shape; concurrent
requests render one at a time (17.6 images/min either way) |

So on G4 the batched path is exact but not faster, and the measured race
keeps it off; the A100 table above shows where it pays (2.12x streamed).

## Tests

CPU, `studio/backend`:

- New `tests/test_diffusion_qwenimage21_row_layout.py`. It checks that
the stock layout puts a short row out like the long one and per-row
layout fixes it, that a row is bit-identical whatever its neighbours
hold, that per-row tables are each row's solo table, one forward per
step, the kill switches, that uniform batches stay bit-identical to the
stock forward, that the graph plan replays the per-row decode
bit-identically, that layout groups merge equal lengths, mixed-length
admission when streamed or forced, and compiled blocks only on a warm
graph.
- Updated `test_diffusion_qwenimage21.py`, `_eager.py` and `_graph.py`.
- Run together with `test_image_batch_infra.py`,
`test_image_batching_followups.py`, `test_diffusion_batched.py`,
`test_batch_sizes_per_load.py`, `test_openai_images_batching.py`,
`test_take_rows_batched.py`, `test_diffusion_cfg_batch_policy.py` and
every `test_diffusion_qwenimage21*` file, plus the quality gate tests
(`test_image_batch_quality.py`): 724 passed, 38 skipped.

## Not proven here

- The table above comes from earlier builds of this change on an earlier
base (before #19837's latest commits).
- The quality gate ships with no G2c verdicts, so no family is promoted
beyond today's rules until verdicts are measured and added.
- These probes call the engine directly. The race endpoint, including
its `warming_mixed_lengths` warm, has not been run on GPU for this
family (on CPU, routing through the adapter and race is covered by
`test_image_batch_infra.py`).
- Resident uniform-length batches were not timed separately from the
policy run. Qwen-Image-2.1 Turbo was not measured separately.
- No G4 lower bound or p95 was computed. Only medians of repeated runs.
- No AMD, Apple Silicon or Windows GPU runs. The ROCm attention path is
covered by CPU tests only.

Studio images: batch FLUX.3 requests in one modular call (streamed klein 2.69x per 4 images on A100), Anima kept serial (#20071)

Follows #19837 (merged), which added the batch adapters and the measured
race.

## Problem

FLUX.3 klein, FLUX.3 klein base and Anima render every image of a list
as its own modular pipeline call: the text step encodes one prompt per
call, so #19837's request batching has to treat both families as
`batched_forward = False` and runs concurrent requests one at a time.
When the denoiser streams weights from host memory, every image pays the
full weight transfer again, so four queued requests cost four full
passes of streaming.

## Change

- **FLUX.3** (`diffusion_flux3.py`): rows that share a text window run
as one modular call. Each row is encoded alone, so its embeddings are
exactly what its own call would produce; the text step returns the
stacked rows, each row's noise is its own seeded reference noise, and
the denoiser runs one forward per step over all rows. Rows land in
separate calls when they differ in text window, per-row negative prompt
or per-row reference size, and also for caller latents, unseeded rows,
or a denoiser whose activation scale is computed from the whole call. A
single image takes the unchanged call.
- **FLUX.3 edit, shared reference**: within one request (one prompt, a
seed list), rows that share the request's reference still run as one
call. A neighbour swap on that path was bit-identical (see the follow-up
section). The route never coalesces separate edit requests: only plain
text-to-image requests share a call.
- **FLUX.3 per-row references** (`row_images`, references per image):
held back. Rows that carry their own references always render one at a
time until a GPU run shows neighbour invariance.
`UNSLOTH_DIFFUSION_FLUX3_ROW_REFS_BATCH=1` enables batching for
measurement only.
- **Anima** (`diffusion_anima.py`): the facade can run rows with the
same conditioned text length as one modular call, but the Anima record
keeps `batched_forward = False`, so Anima requests stay serial on every
card (one chunk per image, never coalesced at the route). On an RTX PRO
6000 its batched rows drifted about 0.13 LPIPS from their own solo
renders; batching turns on only after a like-for-like G2c passes.
- Quality gate (`diffusion_batch_quality.py`, merged in from the infra
side): a measured race win serves only with a passing offline G2c
verdict for the family, the card's device class and the execution path;
missing or failing keeps the serial rule. The race's replay check now
compares row 0 with its solo render on the same execution path
(`b_exact`: bit-identical, or within the same-shape rerun noise), and
seeded joins need it.
- `diffusion_families.py`: `DiffusionFamily.batched_forward` (None = not
stated, the existing default rules). Both FLUX.3 records set it to True,
so #19837's adapter (`diffusion_batch_adapters.batched_forward` /
`adapter_for`) admits them, `_generation_chunks` keeps their rows in one
chunk, and the race no longer refuses them.
- Kill switches: `UNSLOTH_DIFFUSION_FLUX3_BATCH=0` and
`UNSLOTH_DIFFUSION_ANIMA_BATCH=0` restore one call per image.

## What Auto does by default

Nothing changes for a single-image request. With concurrent requests,
#19837's policy decides:

- **Streamed denoiser** (Low VRAM / group offload, no CUDA graphs):
requests with the same settings share a call (the existing rule for a
family that fuses its rows).
- **Resident weights, CUDA graphs, or a static compile**: requests stay
serial, as they do today, unless #19837's idle race measures a win on
that load, card and shape **and** an offline G2c verdict passes for that
family, card and execution path (eager or graph). Without a passing
verdict a race win is persisted but not served. The gate ships with no
verdicts, so out of the box these placements stay serial; the race
decides speed per card, the G2c verdict decides whether that speed may
be served.

## Gates

- G1: an N=1 single-image request is byte-identical to the base. A
request with `batch_size` > 1 now shares one forward across its images,
so its bytes may differ from the base by floating-point batch-shape
effects; that path is gated by G2a and G2c instead.
- G2a: a row's bytes do not change when its neighbours change.
- G2c: paired LPIPS against a bf16 speed-off reference, upper bound of
(batched minus solo) at most +0.01.
- G4: speed lower bound at least 1.05x with p95 at most +3%.

1024 px, Studio Auto settings.

apart from a change) | exact (max diff 0), A/A exact; row 0 vs its solo
max 227 px | +0.036 vs eager reference (n=8, FAIL); +0.207 strict vs
solo | size 2 lost on speed, lower bound 1.036x; size 4 skipped | 22.2
vs 22.2 images/min (no change: stays serial) |

On G4 a streamed klein render is already fast (1.85 s per image), so
streaming saves little and the speedup is small; the measured race
decides per card. This PR ships the klein G2c PASS for this card (RTX
PRO 6000 Blackwell, eager and graph path) as a stored quality verdict,
so a klein race win there may serve, and only where that card's own race
measures a lower bound of at least 1.05x. Every other card, and klein
base, still needs its own verdict.

Like for like on G4 (n=24): solo renders are byte-identical on the eager
and the graph path, and batched rows score the same on both, so the
earlier drift was not a path mix. Batched rows are not byte-identical to
their solo renders (mean LPIPS 0.010), so seeded requests do not join:
the first batch-shape divergence is the bf16 timestep embedder and the
text input projection, both run at M = batch rows. Running those row by
row is being measured as an exact path and is not part of this PR. On G4
the Anima race also found no speedup, and its batched rows drift far
from their solo renders, so this PR keeps Anima serial everywhere (see
Change).
## Follow-up: edit batching

Batching edits across requests, and rows with per-row references, is
left for a follow-up. Evidence so far, kept for that PR:

- FLUX.3 klein edit, shared reference, batch 4: G1 identical 4/4; G2a
bit-identical (max diff 0, RTX PRO 6000); G2c upper bound +0.00003
(n=12, PASS); resident 1.018x; streamed not measured.
- Per-row references: own-row LPIPS at most 0.0044, but in one earlier
run one of four targets changed bytes when a neighbour's reference was

Studio ROCm: prebuild the Triton conv3d kernels off the first decode (gfx1151 Wan first 480p decode 284 -> 42 s on Windows) (#20065)

## Summary

On AMD gfx1151 the Wan 2.2 VAE decode routes `nn.Conv3d` through the
vendored Triton conv3d kernels (#19873). With an empty Triton cache the
first decode compiled them inline: the first 480p decode took 135 s on
Linux and 277 s on Windows, against 39 to 42 s for MIOpen. This PR
removes that stall: a decode never compiles a conv3d kernel any more,
and a cold call runs MIOpen instead.

- A conv3d call routes to Triton only when its compiled variants are
known to be in the Triton disk cache. Otherwise it runs MIOpen (new
`fallback_cold` counter) and its variant is queued.
- Right after the video load (`diffusion_vae_prebuild.maybe_kick_video`,
which skipped ROCm until now), a child process compiles every wrapped
conv's variants on tiny zero inputs, with no weights. The direct kernels
take N / D / H / W / OD / P / Q / M as runtime ints since #19873, so a
tiny input builds the same binary a real decode loads. The tuned literal
table shapes (the 704x1280 entries) are built at their exact size. The
router self-check also runs in the child first.
- The child appends each built variant to a manifest next to the Triton
cache
(`<TRITON_CACHE_DIR>/unsloth_vae_prebuild/rocm_conv3d_<hash>.json`). The
hash covers the kernel sources, torch, HIP, Triton, the arch and
`TRITON_*` env, so wiping the cache drops the manifest, and anything
that changes Triton's own cache key starts a new one. The parent
re-reads the manifest at most once a second while calls are cold. A
partially built manifest routes the convs that are ready.
- A variant first seen during a decode (an encoder conv, a resolution
with a tuned literal shape) is handed to a child 3 s after the last new
one, so the next decode routes it.
- The variant key mirrors what Triton specialises for these launches:
route, channels, kernel, stride, padding, dilation, dtype, bias, the
table config (the `any` entry or a literal shape), input pointer
alignment, and `D*H*W % 16` for the NCDHWc pack (the only size int left
specialised). Winograd (opt-in) keys on the exact shape.
- The child reuses the existing prebuild machinery: a spawn child that
is adopted for teardown, cancelled by `cancel_all("video")` on unload
(which now also drops queued variants), and stopped by `yield_to_render`
when VRAM is tight. Its timeout is 1500 s, and partial progress is kept.
- Opt out with `UNSLOTH_DIFFUSION_ROCM_TRITON_CONV3D_PREBUILD=0` or
`UNSLOTH_DIFFUSION_VAE_PREBUILD=0`, which restores the old inline
compile. Nothing changes off ROCm gfx11 or for the kernels themselves,
and no binaries are shipped.

Triton cache per cold arm)

| prebuild child done, after load | | 475.5 s (49 variants plus
self-check) | |

kernels compiled | |
| first 720p decode, same process | 100.3 s (5 more compiled inline) |
83.5 s, 713 routed, 0 compiled | |

## Tests

`tests/test_diffusion_rocm_triton_conv3d.py`: 7 new tests. They fail on
main and pass here.
- tiny inputs plus literal shapes cover every variant of real 480p and
720p Wan decodes (42 recorded conv shapes)
- a cold call runs MIOpen and queues the self-check and the variant, and
a child that died leaves it on MIOpen
- a manifest-listed variant routes and matches stock
- a failed child self-check keeps MIOpen with nothing compiled
in-process
- the child compiles only specs whose key it reproduces and writes the
manifest
- both opt-outs compile inline as before

Load hook guard: require the hook to be the first statement that does work (red on main since #20022) (#20077)

## Summary


`tests/test_import_keeps_plain_model_backends.py::test_every_from_pretrained_starts_with_the_load_hook`
has failed on `main` since #20022 (`Train LoRA on packed GGUF weights`).
It fails in the `Repo tests (CPU, rest-2)` shard, most recently on
#20071's staging run:

```
AssertionError: ('unsloth/models/loader.py', 'FastLanguageModel')
assert '_unsloth_load_begins' in []
```

The guard makes sure `_unsloth_load_begins()` (the cuDNN SDPA switch for
Unsloth loads) runs before any loading work in each `from_pretrained`.
It looked for the call among the first three statements. #20022 added a
third local import (`from .gguf_packed import
check_gguf_packed_request`) to `FastLanguageModel.from_pretrained` and
`FastModel.from_pretrained`, which pushed the hook to the fourth
statement. Nothing runs before the hook: the statements ahead of it only
bind names. So #20022 is correct, and the guard was counting statements
rather than checking the property it is named for.

docstring. It then requires the first remaining statement to be the
`_unsloth_load_begins()` call. This is stricter than before about real
work: an assignment or call ahead of the hook now fails, where the old
check let up to two of them through. It is also indifferent to how many
imports a load path needs.
- The test now asserts that it found all four `from_pretrained` methods
(`FastLanguageModel`, `FastModel`, `FastLlamaModel`, `FastBaseModel`),
so a rename cannot make it pass vacuously.

no hook at all.

Mac torch floor workflow: check the merge base arm against its own route (red on staging since #20038 landed) (#20069)

## Summary

`Studio macOS torch floor upgrade` (`existing torch 2.10 home`, both
Python legs) now fails on every staging run of a PR that touches
`install.sh`. #20066 is the current example. The failing step is arm A,
which re-runs the merge base's `install.sh` on a home seeded with torch
2.10:

```
grep -q "existing install has torch 2.10.0 -- keeping it" "$LOGS/A_base_rerun.log"
##[error]Process completed with exit code 1.
```

#20038 added this workflow to show its own change: its merge base kept a
2.10 home, and its head moves it to the 2.13 route. Arm A hard-coded
what that pre-#20038 base does. Since #20038 merged, every merge base
contains the 2.13 route, so the base re-run correctly says:

```
existing install has torch 2.10.0 -- moving to torch>=2.13.0,<2.14.0 for the fused MPS attention kernel (set UNSLOTH_TORCH_UPGRADE=0 to keep it)
```

It then installs 2.13.0, and arm A fails. The installer is right and the
arm's fixed expectation is out of date. A second, hidden problem follows
from the first: once A moves the home to 2.13, arm B no longer starts
from a 2.10 home. B's `moving to torch>=2.13.0` check would then fail
too, even with a correct head.

## Changes

- `.github/scripts/mac-torch-floor-upgrade.sh` gains `check-route T
INSTALL_LOG PROBE_LOG`. A re-run of a home on torch `T` must either:
  - say `keeping it` and leave the probe on `T`, or
  - say `moving to torch>=LO,<HI` and leave the probe inside that range.

Anything else fails: no route line, a route line the probe contradicts,
or a missing probe line.
- Arm A runs `check-route 2.10.0`. It now checks the merge base against
the route its own log names, so it holds before and after a routing
change lands.
- Arm B reseeds the home to torch 2.10 before re-running the head
installer, so it always starts from the state it is meant to test,
whatever A did.

Arms B, B2, C and D (the head's own expectations) are unchanged.

## Verification

- `check-route` against fixtures built from the failing job's real log
lines:
- pass: `moving to >=2.13.0,<2.14.0` with the probe on 2.13.0, and
`keeping it` with the probe on 2.10.0;
- fail: `moving` with the probe still on 2.10.0, `moving` with the probe
on 2.14.1, `keeping` with the probe on 2.13.0, no route line, and no
probe line.
- `shellcheck` is clean, and the script is `bash -n` clean. The
version-regex escape uses `sed` rather than `${var//}`, so it does not

- The workflow runs on the staging repos (it is skipped on
`unslothai/unsloth` pull requests). This change touches the workflow, so
the staging run of this PR exercises the edited arms on `macos-15` for

Studio images: family batch adapters, measured batching race and per-size CUDA graphs (#19837)

## Summary

Builds on #19667 (merged). Concurrent image requests from different
accounts now share one pipeline call only where it is measured to help,
and the batching decision moves from blanket per-family refusals to a
per-family capability plus a measured verdict per card, load and shape.
Unmeasured loads keep the #19667 rules, so nothing changes until a race
on that card proves a win.

**Where Auto now batches.** In the measured runs, Auto batched only
HiDream-I1-Fast streamed on an A100 40GB. Its race promoted batch 4
(median 1.44x, lower bound 1.40x) and batch 2 (lower bound 1.06x), and
16 concurrent users went from 6.4 to 8.0 images/min with p95 down from
149 s to 120 s. FLUX.2 klein 4B resident on RTX PRO 6000 measured 1.037x
at batch 2 and 1.055x at batch 4, below the 1.05 lower bound, so it
stays one request at a time, byte-identical to before.

**Klein accuracy.** At batch 4, klein's rows are 0.064 LPIPS from the
eager reference, against 0.028 for solo renders, so the paired gate
fails at eps 0.01. This is the existing batch-shape behaviour of the
INT8 path: neighbour invariance is bit-identical at batch 2 and 4, and a
single request with `batch_size` 4 gets the same drift today. Auto does
not batch klein.

**Family capability.** `batched_forward` is read from the family object
with `getattr`. `DiffusionFamily` is unchanged here; families opt in by
setting the attribute in their own PRs.

## What changed

**Family capability (`core/inference/diffusion_batch_adapters.py`,
new)**
- A family says whether its pipeline call fuses a list of prompts into
one forward with `batched_forward` (bool) on the family object. Unset
keeps today's answer: FLUX.3, Anima, layered, MiniMax-H3-Image, MOSS and
Qwen-Image-2.1 render one image per forward; everything else uses the
diffusers list call.
- `BatchAdapter` (`prepare` gives the row layout key, `compatible`,
`denoise_batched`, `split`) with `DefaultAdapter` for the list call
(FLUX.1 T5 bucket, SD / SDXL CLIP chunk counts). A family can set
`batch_adapter` for its own row layout.
- The route refusal (FLUX.3 / Anima / layered), the key refusal (H3 /
MOSS / Qwen-Image-2.1) and the in-request chunking rule now read the
capability, so a family that gains a batched forward is admitted without
touching the batching code.

**Measured race (`core/inference/diffusion_batch_race.py`, new)**
- `POST /api/inference/images/batching/race` (owner only) races k
requests served one at a time against the same k in one call, at sizes 2
and 4 by default, each arm including encode, denoise and decode,
interleaved in random order over several repeats. With CUDA graphs on it
also races the batched call with the graphs bypassed (`set_bypass`).
Static compile races only sizes already compiled.
- It runs only on an idle engine: it is refused when a request holds or
waits for the slot, and it stops (persisting nothing for that size) as
soon as one starts waiting.
- A size is promoted only when the one-sided 95% lower bound of the
speedup is at least 1.05x (the smaller of a Student t bound on the log
ratios and a percentile bootstrap) and the batched p95 request latency
is at most 3% above serial. Losers are persisted too.
- Verdicts go through `diffusion_probe_cache.Namespace("batch_race")`:
keyed by torch, driver, card and env (the probe fingerprint) plus model
and revision, family, denoiser class, precision, speed mode, attention
backend, offload placement, graph and compile state, step cache, canvas,
guidance, step count and batch size.
- The step count is in the key because the fixed per-call cost of encode
and decode weighs more at few steps.
- It also checks neighbour invariance at the batch shape (the target row
first and last, only the neighbours' prompts and seeds changed, plus an
A/A repeat) and whether a member equals its solo render.
- Each verdict stores its winning arm (graph replay at that batch size,
or batched eager). User requests never record a batched graph, so a
verdict won by graph replay admits its size only while the load holds
that batch-size graph. After a restart, a LoRA reset or an OOM drop, the
size is admitted only if the eager arm passed the 1.05x bound on its
own. Seeded joins are then off, because the neighbour check ran on the
graphed arm.

**Policy (`diffusion.py`)**
- `request_batching` keeps per-call dynamic NVFP4 serial and serves
families without a batched forward serially. Resident and CUDA-graph
loads stay serial unless a race promoted a size on this load (new mode
`measured`). In that mode only the winning sizes and shapes are
admitted.
- `coalesce_batch_sizes` drops measured losers and adds measured winners
at that shape. A request that cannot be part of any admitted size at its
shape no longer waits to coalesce.
- Seeded requests may join only where the measured path is
neighbour-exact and replays bit for bit from the seed
(`coalesce_seeded_ok`), at every batch size the request could render at.
A streamed load that still admits unmeasured sizes keeps seeded requests
alone. The env switch still opts every seeded request in.
- The eager arm runs under a `forced_eager()` scope that the per-chunk
graph re-arm in `generate()` cannot undo.
- A verdict won by graph replay records the prompt layout it was raced
at (the batch key's T5 bucket or chunk count) and holds only for
requests in that layout. Any other layout gets the eager arm's verdict.
- An out-of-memory error at one batch size is persisted as a loss with
its reason, that size's graphs are dropped and the cache emptied, and
the race goes on to the smaller sizes.
- When the eager arm wins a size, the race drops that size's recorded
graphs, so dispatch runs the arm that was measured. On a static compile,
the race only tries batch sizes that are already compiled, whatever the
policy mode, so resident and graphed loads are covered too.

**Row coupling outside the denoiser**
- FBCache decides whether to skip the remaining blocks from one mean
residual over the whole call, so in a shared call one request's image
would decide whether another's blocks run.
  - An explicit FBCache load now serves serially.
- An AUTO cache admits no batch size at a step count where it would
engage FBCache.
  - The race refuses such a load.
  - The static schedule decides by step only and still batches.
- The Qwen-Image single-frame VAE path decoded every image of a call in
one pass. Inside a call carrying several requests it now decodes one
image per pass, so the peak is one feature map and each image decodes
exactly as its own request would. A single user's multi-image call keeps
its one batched pass.

**Out-of-memory retry (`image_request_batching.py`)**
- A batch that ran out of memory was split into halves while its
exception was still alive. The traceback pinned the failed call's frames
and the tensors they held, so the halves started with that memory still
allocated.
- The tracebacks are now dropped before the halves run.

**Re-coalescing (`image_request_batching.py`)**
- When only some sizes are admitted, a fired batch takes the longest
admitted prefix. The members it leaves out used to render one at a time.
- They are now told as the batch fires and coalesce again behind it, at
most 3 rounds.

**CUDA graphs per batch size (`diffusion_cuda_graph.py`)**
- A coalesced call runs under `batch_rows(k)`. It may record a graph of
its own only at sizes 2 and 4, only during the race (never on a user's
request), at most 2 per module, and within the pool budget
(`UNSLOTH_DIFFUSION_BATCH_GRAPH_POOL_MB`, else free VRAM minus 1 GiB).
The estimate is k times the size-1 graph's own pool growth, measured
around its capture, not the whole shared pool. Free VRAM is read on the
card the call's operands are on.
- Batched graphs are recorded only on resident loads. Under an offload
placement a failed recording poisons the whole load, so batched calls
there run eager.
- A key recorded by a batched call that a size-1 call later replays
(true CFG gives a size-1 call 2 rows, the same shape as 2 coalesced
requests without CFG) counts as a size-1 graph from then on, so dropping
batched graphs never takes it.
- A placement change clears the batched and edit labels together with
the graphs.
- A full cache never evicts for a batched key, and a planned eviction
takes a batched graph first.
- On a resident load, running out of memory while recording a batched
graph drops only the batched graphs and stops batched recording for the
load. That call runs the way other unrecorded shapes run beside live
graphs, and the size-1 graphs keep replaying, where before any capture
failure poisoned the wrapper.
- Batch-size graphs record into their own pool, one shared by every
batched graph and both DiTs of a dual-DiT family. torch frees a pool's
blocks only once no graph uses it, so with a single pool, dropping the
batched graphs (a lost race, an OOM) gave nothing back while the size-1
graphs lived. `UNSLOTH_DIFFUSION_BATCH_GRAPH_POOL=shared` keeps one
pool, and with it dropping batched graphs returns no VRAM until the
size-1 graphs go too.
- Batched graphs also have their own budget, so they never take a size-1
prompt-length variant's slot. The race records the largest size first.
- Edit scopes are covered by the same rule. The image scope keys on
reference shapes, and a full planned cache (Qwen-Image-2.1's step)
evicted the least recently replayed graph. With true CFG, three edit
reference sizes evicted both text-to-image graphs, so the next plain
render recorded again on the user's request. A full planned cache now
drops a batched graph first, then an edit's; an edit that would have to
drop a text-to-image graph runs ungraphed instead.

**Trace (`core/inference/diffusion_batch_trace.py`, new; status
`batch_trace`)**
- Always on: admitted requests, idle direct dispatches, leads and joins,
realized call sizes, why a request rendered alone, and rows per pipe
call.
- With `UNSLOTH_STUDIO_IMAGE_BATCH_TRACE=1`: denoiser invocations, rows
and block executions per call. A pipeline that loops over the rows of
one call shows up as invocations growing with the rows.

**Unchanged**
- One request on an idle engine dispatches before any key, policy or
status read.
- Dynamic NVFP4 (per-call amax scales) stays serial. LoRA and
textual-inversion requests stay private to their account.
- The FIFO slot order is unchanged.

## Tests

`tests/test_image_batch_infra.py` (new) and the batched-graph tests
added to `tests/test_diffusion_cuda_graph.py`. They cover:
- the capability defaults and overrides, including the lifted key, route
and chunk refusals;
- unmeasured loads keeping today's rules;
- a measured win lifting the resident and graph rules to the winning
sizes, and a measured loss dropping that size;
- per-call NVFP4 staying serial whatever was measured;
- the seeded-join gate;
- the promotion statistics;
- verdict persistence (losers included, a new process reading them back,
another precision missing);
- race idle refusal and abort, neighbour-leak detection, and
static-compile sizes;
- batched graphs: no recording on a user's request, sizes 2 and 4 only,
no eviction of size-1 graphs, OOM dropping only batched graphs on
resident loads, none recorded on placed loads, the pool budget priced
from the size-1 graph's own growth on the operands' card, relabelling on
a size-1 replay, and placement changes clearing the labels;
- a graphed verdict admitting its size only while that graph exists,
else the eager arm's verdict;
- the idle path touching no key, policy, status or timer;
- the trace telling a fused call from a looped one.

## GPU evidence

Every arm ran in its own fresh process on the same VM, through the real
`/api/inference/images/generate` route, with one account per client. The
arms were:
- `main` at the #19667 merge base;
- #19667;
- `fair`: #19667 with `UNSLOTH_STUDIO_IMAGE_BATCH_MAX=1`;
- this branch;
- `ref`: an eager reference (speed mode off);
- a repeat of #19667 at the end (A/A).

Images are 1024x1024. N is the number of concurrent clients in one
synchronized burst, 3 repeats each.

- **Single user:**

**Graph pool probe (L4, synthetic 6-block MLP DiT, 4608 tokens x 3072,
fp16)**

Each row captures size 1, then sizes 2 and 4. It then drops the batched

| pool, capture order | reserved with sizes 1/2/4 (MiB) | after drop and
release (MiB) | freed (MiB) | eager batch-4 peak after (MiB) |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| one pool, ascending | 3000 | 2622 | 378 | 4190 |
| one pool, descending | 2676 | 2190 | 486 | 3758 |
| batched pool, ascending | 3270 | 1326 | 1944 | 2894 |
| batched pool, descending | 3216 | 1326 | 1890 | 2894 |

size-1 level.

descending order.

batched pool.
- With one pool, every lost race leaves its batched graphs' memory stuck
for the life of the load, which is why the batched pool is the default.
- The trade-off: losing the race is the common case, and there the
batched pool gives the 1.4 to 1.6 GB back. Only loads that won pay its
270 to 540 MiB steady cost. `UNSLOTH_DIFFUSION_BATCH_GRAPH_POOL=shared`
keeps one pool for anyone who prefers the lower steady cost.
- Caveat: these numbers come from a synthetic MLP DiT on L4, not a real
model. A real DiT's activation layout may move both the freed and the
steady figures.

- The idle path dispatches directly on every first request of a burst.
- Denoiser invocations per pipe call equal the step count for 1, 2 and 4
rows: the call is fused, not looped.
- On HiDream, block executions per call stay at 768 for any row count,
so the streamed weights upload once per step for the whole batch.

- **Out-of-memory recovery:** dropping only the batched graphs after an

- **Multi-card:** the verdict key now includes the card topology: card

Studio: stop empty replies when long OpenAI chats compact (#19620)

Long chats on an OpenAI connection could come back with an empty reply
once they passed the Auto-compact setting. Studio asked OpenAI to
compact inside the same response, and OpenAI spent the reply's output
budget compacting, sometimes several times in a row, then stopped with
no text. On gpt-5-nano with Auto-compact after at 2,000 tokens, 8 of 12
turns of a long chat came back empty. /compact returned a long summary
dump in place of the answer.

Studio now compacts OpenAI and Claude chats itself, as it already does
for every other connection, and no longer asks the provider to compact
as well. The context meter marks where Studio compacts, and the
connection settings no longer mention a 200,000 token cap.

Compaction state saved in older chats is still sent back, so those
threads keep their earlier context. Claude summaries on models that take
a temperature rely on #19596.

install.sh: move existing Apple Silicon homes below torch 2.13 to the fused-MPS-attention release on re-run (#20038)

## Problem

New Apple Silicon homes get torch 2.13 (#18428), because 2.13 is the
first release with the fused MPS prefill attention kernel. Studio only
enables that kernel on torch 2.13 or newer (`mps_prefill_supported` in
`diffusion_attention.py`). An existing home keeps whatever torch it has,
from 2.4 up to 2.14, unless the user sets `UNSLOTH_TORCH_UPGRADE=1`. So
every Mac that was installed before #18428 keeps its old torch and runs
diffusion on the math-only attention path.

On a MacBook Pro M5 Max with the same Studio backend and the same
prompts, warm time per 1024x1024 image was:

| Pipeline | torch 2.10.0 (that Mac's existing home) | torch 2.14.1 |
|---|---|---|
| FLUX.2 klein, bf16 | 8.60 s | 3.69 s |
| FLUX.2 klein, GGUF | 11.30 s | 6.39 s |
| Z-Image, GGUF | 64.37 s | 18.00 s |

Peak memory was also 3 to 5 GB lower on the newer torch. A large-linear
check showed no corruption on either version. The images are not
pixel-identical across versions, because the MPS random generator stream
changed between those releases. Within a single version, repeated runs
are bit-identical.

## Change

The change is in `install.sh`, on the macOS arm64 route only. On a
re-run, an existing home whose resident torch is a plain release below
`_MACOS_TORCH_MOVE_FLOOR` (2.13.0, the release Studio's fused MPS
attention gate needs) now takes the same `torch>=2.13.0,<2.14.0` /
`torchvision>=0.28.0,<0.29.0` constraint that a new home gets.
torchaudio resolves to 2.11.x, as it does on a new home. This happens
only when every gate of the new-install route already holds:

- the package is `unsloth`;
- the index is the default cpu index (an index set with
`UNSLOTH_TORCH_INDEX_URL` or `UNSLOTH_TORCH_INDEX_FAMILY` never moves);
- macOS 14 or later, with a GIL-enabled Python 3.10 to 3.14;
- the released `unsloth` on PyPI admits torch 2.13. An unreachable or
capped PyPI keeps the resident release.

These cases are unchanged:

- A home already on 2.13 or 2.14 is kept.
- A home whose torch cannot be read, or holds a nightly, takes the same
path as before.
- `UNSLOTH_TORCH_UPGRADE=0` (any value other than empty or `1`) keeps
the resident release.
- `UNSLOTH_TORCH_UPGRADE=1` behaves as before.

The move floor is its own literal, not derived from
`_MACOS_NEW_INSTALL_TORCH`. A later bump of the new-install pin (for
example to 2.14) therefore never moves a 2.13 home. Homes below 2.13
move to whatever the pin is at that point.

The installer prints `existing install has torch X -- moving to
torch>=2.13.0,<2.14.0 for the fused MPS attention kernel (set
UNSLOTH_TORCH_UPGRADE=0 to keep it)`.

This follows the rule the installer already uses for a raised floor
(#7250): a release below a route's floor is outside the preservation
window, so it moves. On ROCm 7.2 and Strix, that floor is 2.11. Here it
is 2.13.

Linux, WSL, Windows (`install.ps1` is untouched), Intel macOS, CUDA,
ROCm and XPU take exactly the same decisions as before. The new code
runs only inside the macOS arm64 branch, and the shared pin block skips
`_previous_torch_pin` only when that branch has decided to move.

### Why existing homes were preserved, and why this is safe on Apple
Silicon

- #6959 / #7250: a re-run should keep the torch release a user has
validated. The trigger was a silent 2.10 to 2.11 move on a CUDA host.
That still holds at or above 2.13 here.
- #12150: on CUDA, the torch release is tied to prebuilt flash-attn,
causal-conv1d and mamba-ssm wheels. `studio update` can also re-resolve
torch under an older release's cap. Apple Silicon has no such prebuilt
kernels. The PyPI gate is kept, and #18659 freezes the resident torch
through `studio update` on Apple Silicon, so a moved home stays on 2.13
there.
- torchcodec is chosen from the resident torch on every
`install_python_stack.py` pass, so it follows the move.
- A re-run rebuilds the venv anyway. A failed install rolls back to the
previous environment, unless `--no-rollback` was passed.

## Tests

- `tests/sh/test_macos_torch213_route.sh`: 132 checks. 22 fail on main.
3 more fail on a version of this branch that derived the floor from the
pin: the floor literal, and a pin bumped to 2.14 still keeping 2.13.0
and 2.13.1 homes.
- Existing 2.6 / 2.10 / 2.11 / 2.12.1 homes, and 2.10.0+cpu, move to the
2.13 constraint and announce the opt-out.
- These homes are kept: 2.13.0 / 2.13.1 / 2.14.0 / 2.14.1;
`UNSLOTH_TORCH_UPGRADE=0|false|no`; a pinned index; macOS 13;
