Studio GGUF: keep the exact Q2_K / Q3_K / Q6_K dequant at rank 4 (Z-Image GGUF 2.2x faster on Apple MPS, bit-identical) (#20034)

## Summary

Studio's llama.cpp-exact GGUF dequant made Z-Image-Turbo Q4_K_M about
2.25x slower on Apple MPS than diffusers' stock dequant (64.3 s vs 28.6
s per 1024px image, 8 steps, M5 Max, torch 2.10). With synced timers,
57.0 s of a 78.1 s render went to dequant. FLUX.2 klein Q4_K_M on the
same path ran at its microbenchmark rate.

The difference is the quant type mix. Klein's file has only Q4_K and
Q5_K. Z-Image's file also has 10 Q6_K tensors, which make about 22
dequant calls per step. At the measured Q4_K, Q5_K and Q8_0 rates,
Z-Image should spend about 1.0 s per step in dequant. It spent 7.1 s.
`dequantize_blocks_Q6_K` is the only exact dequant that builds rank-6
tensors. Q2_K and Q3_K reach rank 5, while Q4_K, Q5_K and the 32-wide
types stay at rank 4 or lower.

This PR lays out the same Q2_K, Q3_K and Q6_K codes and scales as `(n,
16 scale groups, 16)`, so every tensor stays at rank 4 or lower. Every
code, scale and product is the same value computed in the same order.
Only the shape that holds them changes, so the output is bit-identical.

## Changes

- `diffusion_gguf_exact.py`: `_k_codes` returns `(n, chunk, shift, 32)`
instead of `(n, chunk, shift, half, 16)`. A new `_groups16` helper views
contiguous codes as `(n, 16, 16)`. Q2_K and Q3_K scales are `(n, 16,
1)`. Q6_K builds its low nibbles as `(n, 2, 2, 64)` and its high bits as
`(n, 2, 4, 32)`, and multiplies `(n, 16, 1)` scales into `(n, 16, 16)`
codes.
- `test_diffusion_gguf_exact.py`: a new test records every aten op
`dequantize_cast` runs and asserts that no tensor exceeds rank 4. It
covers every exact type, fp32 and bf16, and both `_emit` branches
(cast-on-store for CPU / CUDA, and the `scale * q` then `.to(dtype)`
path MPS takes). It also checks the output against gguf-py.

## Testing

- `tests/test_diffusion_gguf_exact.py`,
`tests/test_diffusion_gguf_fused_cast.py`,
`tests/test_diffusion_gguf_fused_q8_0.py`: 229 passed on CPU (torch
2.14.1, diffusers 0.42.1, gguf-py). This includes the vendored ggml
oracle digests, the NaN / inf / subnormal / -0 scale cases, and the
compiled no-graph-break, one-graph-per-type checks.
- The new rank test fails on main for Q2_K, Q3_K and Q6_K, and passes on
this branch.
- Main vs branch bit comparison on 4099 random blocks per type (every
bit pattern, so special scales are included), in fp32, bf16 and fp16, on
both `_emit` branches: identical for all 11 types.

## Apple M5 Max results

MacBook Pro M5 Max, 128 GB, macOS 26.6.2, torch 2.10.0, 1024x1024. Main
and this branch ran in interleaved fresh processes, 2 runs each.

| | main | this PR |
|---|---|---|
| Q6_K exact dequant, one 3840x3840 tensor | 275-276 ms | 2.6-2.8 ms
(about 100x) |
| Z-Image-Turbo Q4_K_M dequant per render (8 steps) | 57.14 s, of which
Q6_K 49.42 s (176 calls) | 8.36 s, of which Q6_K 0.47 s |
| Z-Image-Turbo Q4_K_M s/image | 64.29 / 64.24 | 29.64 / 28.13 (2.2x) |
| FLUX.2 klein 4B Q4_K_M s/image (no Q6_K tensors) | 10.80 / 11.48 |
11.01 / 11.78 (unchanged, within run-to-run spread) |

- **Hashes:** all 7 per-type dequant output sha256 digests are identical
between main and this PR.
- **Images:** every rendered PNG is identical to main's (max abs 0) for
both models and both runs.
- **Weights:** the loaded weights have the same placement and layout in
both trees: on MPS, contiguous, uint8, bf16 compute.

Q4_K, Q5_K and Q8_0 per-call costs are unchanged.

## CUDA check

NVIDIA L4, torch 2.14.1+cu130, one 3840x3840 tensor of random blocks per
type. The test called main's and this branch's dequant functions
directly:

- **Output:** all 11 types are bit-identical in bf16, in fp16, and under
`torch.compile`, with 0 mismatches.
- **Eager:** Q6_K 0.665 vs 0.666 ms and Q2_K 0.402 vs 0.402 ms, so CUDA
eager speed is unchanged.
- **Compiled:** Q6_K 0.186 vs 0.200 ms. That is within the run-to-run
spread on a shared card: Q5_K, which this PR does not touch, moved from
0.154 to 0.177 ms in the same run.

Studio: keep recipe edits made just before leaving the editor (#19610) A data recipe autosaves 800 ms after the last change, and that pending save was dropped when the editor closed. Leaving within that window (sidebar, Back, reload or closing the tab) lost the change, as did a newer edit made while an earlier save was still on its way. The editor now saves a pending change at once when it closes, when the page is hidden and when it unloads. Nothing is sent twice, and content another window rejected is not retried. A newer edit made during a save is based on the version that save creates, so it lands after it and never overwrites a change from another window. WebKit browsers cancel ordinary requests on unload, so a recipe over 64 KiB reloaded within 800 ms of an edit can still be lost there. ## Backend `PUT /api/data-recipe/recipes/{id}` accepts an optional `alsoBaseUpdatedAt` list. The write is admitted when the stored version matches `baseUpdatedAt` or any listed version, checked in the same UPDATE statement. The editor uses it when a previous save's answer was lost, so one request covers every version that save may have left. Clients that send no list keep the single-base check. ## Studio before and after (merge base vs this PR, two isolated installs) Two seeded recipes are renamed in the editor and left inside the autosave delay, one with the browser Back button and one with a reload. On the merge base both keep their old `Draft ...` names; with this PR both renames are stored. Studio MiniMax-H3: load only the text-encoder layers the read uses (bf16 encoder 66.7 -> 51.5 GB, bit-exact) (#20021)

## Summary

MiniMax-H3 (video) and MiniMax-H3-Image condition on `hidden_states[50]`
of the Qwen3-VL-32B text encoder. The hosted int8 conditioner is already
built with only the layers that read needs (50 decoder layers, a
pass-through 51st slot, no final norm, no `lm_head`). The bf16 path,
which is used when the int8 file is not engaged (an explicit bf16
request, a broken or missing hosted file, a local `text_encoder/`
folder), still loaded all 64 decoder layers plus the final norm and the
`lm_head`, none of which affect the read.

This PR loads the bf16 encoder with the same layout as the int8 one:

- `video_minimax_h3_te.h3_read_layers_text_encoder_class()`: a
`Qwen3VLForConditionalGeneration` subclass that sets `num_hidden_layers
= 51` before the model is built, then puts the existing pass-through
terminator in slot 50 and replaces the norm and `lm_head` with
`Identity`. Under `from_pretrained` the model is built on the meta
device, so the checkpoint tensors for layers 50-63, the norm and the
head have no destination and are never read or allocated. They are
listed in `_keys_to_ignore_on_load_unexpected`, so loading prints no
unexpected-key warning.
- H3 video: the modular pipeline's `load_components_strict` call runs
under `h3_read_layers_spec(pipe)`. This swaps the `text_encoder` spec's
class only for the duration of the call, and only when the spec names
stock `Qwen3VLForConditionalGeneration`, the pipeline reads layer 50,
and no encoder has been seeded yet (the int8 path seeds its encoder
before this call, so it is unaffected).
- H3-Image: the bf16 fallback in `load_h3_image_text_encoder` (which the
H3-Image LoRA trainer also uses) and the local `text_encoder/` folder
load both use the read-layer class.

Nothing else reuses this encoder. The H3-Image prompt enhancer is a
separate Qwen3.5-9B GGUF on llama-server.

## Memory

At the released config (64 layers, hidden 5120, intermediate 25600, 64 q
heads and 8 kv heads of 128, vocab 151936, untied head):

| | params | bf16 bytes |
|---|---|---|
| one decoder layer | 487.6M | 0.975 GB |
| layers 50-63 (14) | 6.83B | 13.65 GB |
| `lm_head` + final norm | 0.78B | 1.56 GB |
| total not loaded | 7.60B | 15.21 GB |

That is 66.7 GB down to about 51.5 GB of host memory, and the same
amount less on the device wherever the encoder is resident.

## Memory planner

The read-layer size is derived from the released config, not typed in:
`h3_te_unread_bytes()` counts the bytes above from `H3_TE_RELEASE_SHAPE`
(the `text_encoder/config.json` fields), and
`h3_te_read_layers_gb(stock)` subtracts them from a whole-encoder
budget. It is used only where the read-layer class is what loads:

- H3-Image: `te_gb_for(None)` (placement plan, pre-load estimate, LoRA
trainer) and the bf16 fallback check price `H3_IMAGE_TE_BF16_READ_GB`.
Every bf16 encoder this backend loads itself goes through
`load_h3_image_text_encoder`. The refusal messages name the read-layer
size.
- H3 video: `h3_bf16_te_gb(stock, pipe=..., module=...)` returns the
read-layer size when the loaded encoder has the read-layer layout, or,
before the load, when the pipeline's `text_encoder` spec is one
`h3_read_layers_spec` swaps. It is used in the unified-memory refusal,
the rotating and resident set sizing (`_h3_others_bytes`,
`_h3_residency_budget_bytes`, pin deferral), and the runtime VRAM floor
and host RAM checks.
- The whole 66.7 / 66.8 GB stays where the stock class can load or
nothing is known yet: a spec naming another class or another read layer,
a loaded stock encoder, a local `text_encoder/` folder (still priced
from its file sizes), and the pre-load checks that run before a pipeline
exists (the fp16 GPU host check, the auto-precision table).

Effect, for example: an H3-Image load with an 80 GB card and 60 GB of
free host memory that was refused at 66.7 GB now keeps the encoder on
the host, and at 70 GB the encoder is no longer re-read for every
prompt.

## Output

The removed modules all run after the read, and the final norm only ever
followed the last layer, so `hidden_states[50]` is unchanged bit for
bit. On a tiny random Qwen3-VL (56 text layers, DeepStack on layers 0
and 1), with text-only and image inputs, `torch.equal` holds against the
whole encoder through the raw `output_hidden_states` read, the H3-Image
hook read (`qwen3vl_hidden_state`), and a diffusers `ComponentSpec.load`
under the spec swap.

A probe that wraps `safe_open` shows that the read-layer load reads data
for 0 of the 68 dropped tensors, on transformers 5.17.0 and 4.57.6.

## Tests

`studio/backend/tests/test_h3_te_read_layers.py` (24 tests, CPU):

- Loading: layout, exact set of dropped tensors, bit-exact
`hidden_states[50]`, the H3-Image bf16 loader, spec swap engagement,
restore and stay-off cases, the video loader wiring.
- Budgets: the byte formula against the real config and against a tiny
model's measured parameter bytes; read-layer pricing where that class
loads and whole pricing for another spec class, another read layer, a
loaded stock encoder and an unknown pipeline; an H3-Image plan refused
at 66.7 GB admitted at the read-layer size; an H3 video unified-memory
plan and a host RAM check that refuse the whole encoder and admit the
read-layer one; the video runtime checks all pricing the loaded encoder.

All 24 fail on `main` and pass on this branch (transformers 5.17.0). The
loading tests also pass on 4.57.6.
`test_the_plan_sizes_the_encoder_the_request_takes` now expects the
read-layer size for a bf16 request. The other H3, H3-Image and memory
planner tests pass, apart from failures that fail the same way on `main`
(`test_offload_planner_seam.py`, four GGUF layout tests in
`test_offload_planner.py`,
`test_diffusion_memory.py::test_the_pin_budget_leaves_the_reserve_free`).

## Not covered here

- The fp16 GPU host check and other pre-load checks that run before a
pipeline exists still price the whole encoder.

## Real weights

`unsloth/MiniMax-H3` `text_encoder/` (66.7 GB, bf16), loaded on a 96 GB
card. Each arm ran in its own process with the same short prompt:

| | full (main) | read layers (this PR) |
|---|---|---|
| decoder layers built | 64 | 51 (layer 50 is a pass-through) |
| parameter bytes | 66.71 GB | 51.51 GB |
| peak device memory | 66.8 GB | 51.6 GB |
| peak host RSS during the load | 79.1 GB | 51.2 GB |
| `hidden_states[50]` | reference | `torch.equal` True |

The saving is 15.21 GB, the same as the config-derived figure the
planner uses.

Studio: read safetensors with pread on ROCm integrated GPUs when host memory is tight (#19936)

## Summary

Extends #19905 (safetensors through `pread` instead of `mmap` on
integrated GPUs) to ROCm integrated GPUs such as Strix Halo (gfx1151),
but only when the load would put host memory under pressure. When memory
is free the loader keeps `mmap`, so default load speed does not change.

On a unified-memory APU, `pread` costs a little load time and saves a
lot of peak host memory. That trade is worth it only when memory is
tight, so the reader is chosen per load.

## Measurement (gfx1151, Linux, ROCm 7.13, torch 2.11, safetensors
0.8.0)

Qwen-Image-2.1 cold load (24.3 GB checkpoint). 8 mmap arms, 7 pread arms
and 3 pread + WILLNEED arms, all on one runner. "Quiet" leaves out the
arms that runner noise pushed to 62 to 70 s (2 to 3 per reader). Peak
RSS and page cache were the same in every arm, within 0.02 GiB.

| reader | quiet cold load | peak RSS (VmHWM) | page cache after load |
|---|---|---|---|
| mmap (main) | 49.3 s | 30.3 GiB | 28.5 GiB |
| pread + page drop (forced on) | 52.4 s (+3 s, +6%) | 17.5 GiB (-12.8
GiB) | 15.4 GiB (-13 GiB) |
| pread + POSIX_FADV_WILLNEED readahead | 52.6 s | 17.5 GiB | 15.4 GiB |

- `pread` is about 6% slower. The extra 3 s is the `pread` read of the
transformer shards. That fails a +5% speed bar, which is why this is not
on by default.
- Peak RSS falls by 12.8 GiB (42%) and page cache by 13 GiB. On an APU
that memory is also the GPU's pool.
- WILLNEED readahead does not recover the time, so it is not included.

## Gate rule

On a ROCm integrated GPU with `UNSLOTH_SAFETENSORS_PREAD` unset or
`auto`, the reader is chosen once per load, at its first shard:

```
pread  if  MemAvailable - checkpoint_bytes < max(16 GiB, 25% of MemTotal)
mmap   otherwise
```

- `MemAvailable` / `MemTotal` come from `/proc/meminfo` on Linux and
`psutil` elsewhere. If they cannot be read, the loader keeps `mmap`.
- `checkpoint_bytes` is the size of every `.safetensors` file in the
snapshot: the root plus its component dirs, one level deep. Variants are
counted too, so the estimate leans towards `pread`.
- Why this headroom: on the measured load, `mmap` needs about 12.8 GiB
more resident memory than `pread` (30.3 vs 17.5 GiB for 24.3 GB of
weights). The 16 GiB floor covers that extra plus margin for a
checkpoint of that size. 25% of RAM scales the margin on larger boxes
(32 GiB on a 128 GB Strix Halo), where checkpoints and the inference
working set are also larger. Example: a 128 GB box loading
Qwen-Image-2.1 uses `mmap` while 56.3 GiB or more is available, and
`pread` below that.
- Once `pread` is chosen, diffusers shards also drop each tensor's clean
file pages after reading it (`POSIX_FADV_DONTNEED`). This is what
produces the page-cache drop above. `UNSLOTH_SAFETENSORS_FADVISE=0`
turns it off. It never runs on the NVIDIA path.
- The server log says which reader was chosen and why, for example:
`safetensors reader: pread on a ROCm integrated GPU (MemAvailable 40.0
GiB - load 24.3 GiB = 15.7 GiB < headroom 32.0 GiB)`.

## Unchanged

- Integrated NVIDIA (DGX Spark, Jetson): always `pread` for every shard,
exactly as in #19905. Memory is never read.
- Discrete NVIDIA, discrete ROCm, CPU, MPS: unchanged (`mmap`, plus the
existing Windows converting-load rule).
- Intel iGPU and Windows rules: unchanged.
- On Linux, the ROCm gate's answer applies to every shard. When it picks
`mmap`, the fp32 conversion rules do not switch a shard to `pread`, so
`last_reader_decision` matches the reader that was actually used. On
Windows ROCm, converting loads still use `pread` to save commit
(#14513), and the logged reason says so.

## Override

`UNSLOTH_SAFETENSORS_PREAD` now takes `auto` (default), `pread` (also
`1/on/true/yes`) or `mmap` (also `0/off/false/no`). `pread` forces the
ROCm integrated path on. `mmap` turns `pread` off everywhere, as `0` did
before.

## Tests

`studio/backend/tests/test_safetensors_pread_rocm_igpu.py` (CPU only,
device and memory stubbed) covers:

- the decision table: integrated NVIDIA uses `pread` with plenty of
memory and under pressure; ROCm integrated uses `mmap` with plenty of
memory and `pread` under pressure; unreadable memory gives `mmap`;
discrete ROCm and discrete NVIDIA give `mmap`; unclassifiable devices
give `mmap`; `pread`/`1` and `mmap`/`0`/`auto` override as described
- checksums: every tensor read through the scope equals what was
written, on both readers
- the rule's boundaries, a 16 GiB floor against 25% of RAM
- the log reason, page drops only under the ROCm pressure path, and the
`UNSLOTH_SAFETENSORS_FADVISE=0` kill switch

The existing pread suites (`test_safetensors_pread.py`,
`test_safetensors_pread_igpu.py`,
`test_safetensors_pread_integrated_cuda.py`) pass, with their call-site
expectations updated for the new `integrated_rocm` argument.

## Not covered yet

- An AMD CI run of this exact gate on gfx1151 (one where the pressure
path fires and one where it does not) is still pending. The table above
was measured with `pread` forced on.
- Windows ROCm on Strix Halo: the gate uses `psutil` there, but it has
not been measured.

Studio sd.cpp: direct conv for the Metal VAE by default on FLUX.2 and FLUX.1 VAEs (#20003)

## Summary

On Apple Silicon, Studio now passes `--conv-direct off,vae=on` to sd.cpp
by default for the families whose VAE has been measured on real
hardware. Only the VAE switches from im2col to the implicit GEMM Metal
`CONV_2D` (unslothai/stable-diffusion.cpp#103). The denoiser and the
text encoders keep the argv they had before.

#19054 added this path as an opt-in
(`UNSLOTH_SD_CPP_METAL_VAE_CONV_DIRECT=1`). It was off by default
because the only numbers came from a virtualized `macos-15` M1 runner.
That PR named the missing evidence: speed, memory and GPU watchdog
behaviour on physical Apple Silicon. It was not opt-in because of a
hang, a crash or a quality problem. Intel Macs were excluded because
their old scalar Metal `CONV_2D` was about 5x slower than im2col and
tripped the GPU watchdog. That exclusion stays.

## Measurement on physical Apple Silicon

MacBook Pro M5 Max, 128 GB, macOS 26.6.2, on AC power. Studio's shipped
prebuilt `master-982-0518b34-u9455ee1`, FLUX.2 klein 4B Q4_K_M,
1024x1024, 4 steps. Each figure is the median of 2 runs, and every
sd-cli process includes the model load:

| arm | VAE decode s | wall s/image | PSNR vs default |
|---|---|---|---|
| Studio default (no `--conv-direct`, sd.cpp auto) | 2.33 | 14.73 | |
| `--conv-direct off,vae=on` | 0.84 to 0.89 | 13.4 to 13.6 | 71.65 dB
(max pixel diff 1) |
| speed mode (`--conv-direct off`) | 2.34 | 15.27 | 70.91 dB |

- The A/A wall spread is at most 0.38 s, and every arm was deterministic
run to run (A/A PSNR inf).
- There was no hang and no abort on either the prebuilt or a build of
the fork's current main.
- sd.cpp's own auto logs `conv2d direct auto: MTL0 -> off (no implicit
GEMM path)`, so with no flag it leaves the VAE on im2col.
- Speed mode passed `--conv-direct off`, which turned the lever off
explicitly. With this change speed mode keeps the VAE on direct conv.
- The earlier virtualized M1 numbers point the same way on memory. The
SD-Turbo VAE compute buffer went from 1664 to 640 MB at 512 px, and 1024
px decoded untiled in 2.56 GB where im2col asked for 8.5 GB.

## What changed

- `DiffusionFamily.sd_cpp_metal_vae_conv_direct` (default False). It is
True for `flux.2-klein` and `flux.2-dev`, which use the FLUX.2 VAE, and
for `flux.1`, `flux.1-kontext` and `z-image`, which use the FLUX.1 `ae`.
Every other family (Qwen-Image, FLUX.3, Krea 2, MOSS-Image, H3, SDXL and
the others) keeps im2col unless the user opts in.
- `native_speed_flags` returns `--conv-direct off,vae=on` with speed
mode off as well, which is Studio's default mode. Speed modes `default`
and `max` now send `off,vae=on` instead of `off` for these families.
- It applies only when every one of these holds, the same gates as the
opt-in:
  - the machine is an Apple Silicon Mac that is not a paravirtual VM
- the VAE stays on Metal (not `--vae-on-cpu`, not `--backend
...,vae=cpu`)
- the binary is an Unsloth prebuilt with the kernel (tag allowlist, or
master build 983 or later)
  - the binary's `--help` lists `--conv-direct`
  - the user passed no conv flag of their own
- The backend passes the family default to sd-server and sd-cli
(`_family_start_kwargs`, `metal_vae_conv_direct=`) on macOS only. Other
hosts call them with the same kwargs as before.
- The native status field `metal_vae_conv_direct` reports the family
default, and it is no longer forced off in speed mode off.

Kill switches:
- `UNSLOTH_SD_CPP_METAL_VAE_CONV_DIRECT=0` (or `off` / `false` / `no`)
restores the previous argv.
- `UNSLOTH_SD_CPP_CONV_DIRECT=0` still turns off all direct conv.
- `UNSLOTH_SD_CPP_METAL_VAE_CONV_DIRECT=1` still opts any other family
in, and `force` still skips the build check.

CUDA, Vulkan, ROCm, HIP, CPU, Intel Mac and macOS VM argv do not change.

## Tests

- New `studio/backend/tests/test_sd_cpp_metal_vae_conv_default.py` (42
cases), covering:
- speed off / None and default / max on Apple Silicon with the family
default
  - the kill switch values and the global conv kill switch
  - old, upstream and unrecorded builds
- a CPU VAE, a CPU backend, a user `--conv-direct` flag, and a build
without the module flag
- CUDA, Vulkan, ROCm and CPU on Linux, CUDA on Windows, an Intel Mac and
a macOS VM, all identical with and without the family default
  - the sd-server and sd-cli paths
- the family set, and that each of those families uses one of the two
measured VAE files
  - the backend start kwargs and the status field
- All 42 fail on `main` and pass on this branch.
- `test_sd_cpp_metal_vae_conv_direct.py`: one assertion changed. With
the opt-in, speed mode off now reports enabled, which matches the argv.
- `tests/test_sd_cpp_*.py`, `test_h3_sd_cpp_parity.py`,
`test_diffusion_family_data_freeze.py` and
`test_diffusion_more_families.py`: 2280 passed, 5 skipped.

## Not proven here

- Z-Image-Turbo, FLUX.1, Kontext and FLUX.2 dev have not been timed on

-> 0.86 s | 71.65 dB, max diff 1 | bit-identical |

Studio images: honour output_format and output_compression on /v1/images/generations (#19992)

## Summary

`POST /v1/images/generations` now honours the OpenAI `output_format`
(`png`, `jpeg`, `webp`) and `output_compression` (0-100) fields. A
request that does not send them gets exactly the bytes it gets today.
The PNG path also stops reading the gallery file back from disk to
base64 it.

On one 1024x1024 image, 8 CPU cores, the response path drops from about
60-69 ms (PNG encode, write, read back, base64) to about 8 ms for `jpeg`
at the default compression of 100, and about 3.3 ms at 75. The PNG
encode still runs, but after the response is sent.

## What the spec says

From the OpenAI Images API (`CreateImageRequest` /
`CreateImageEditRequest` and `ImagesResponse` in the OpenAPI spec and
the official Python SDK types, `image_generate_params.py`,
`image_edit_params.py`, `images_response.py`):

- `output_format`: "The format in which the generated images are
returned." Values `png`, `jpeg`, `webp`. Default `png`. Nullable.
- `output_compression`: "The compression level (0-100%) for the
generated images. This parameter is only supported for the GPT image
models with the `webp` or `jpeg` output formats, and defaults to 100."
Nullable.
- `ImagesResponse.output_format`: "The output format of the generated or
edited image."

References:
- https://platform.openai.com/docs/api-reference/images/create
-
https://github.com/openai/openai-python/blob/main/src/openai/types/image_generate_params.py
-
https://github.com/openai/openai-python/blob/main/src/openai/types/images_response.py

## Behaviour

- `output_format` is omitted, `null` or `png`: same path as today. The
response is the gallery PNG (filtered, zlib level 1, parallel strips),
base64'd from the bytes already in memory. I checked the default
responses byte for byte against `main`, with the clock, ids and link
secret pinned: the raw HTTP bodies for `url`, `b64_json` and `b64_json`
with `n=2` have identical sha256 on both trees, and so do the gallery
files.
- `output_format` is `jpeg` or `webp`: each image is encoded with Pillow
at `quality = output_compression` (100 when omitted). There is no
metadata in the response bytes. The response carries `output_format` at
the top level. JPEG drops alpha (the images are RGB anyway). WebP uses
libwebp method 0, because the default method 4 takes about 120 ms on a
1024x1024 image, which is slower than the PNG it replaces, for about 25%
fewer bytes.
- `output_compression` outside 0-100 is a 400 with `param:
output_compression`. With `png` it is accepted and ignored, as the spec
describes.
- `output_format` values other than the three (for example `gif`, `svg`)
are a 400 with `param: output_format`.
- `jpeg` / `webp` together with an explicit `response_format: "url"` is
a 400. A URL always links the gallery PNG, so the result would not be in
the format asked for. When `response_format` is omitted, a `jpeg` /
`webp` request is answered inline as `b64_json`, which is what the GPT
image models do. That also lets keyless callers use it.
- `ImagesResponse.output_format` is only echoed when the request set
`output_format`, so a default response keeps its current keys
(`created`, `data`).

## Gallery

The gallery always stores the lossless PNG with the full recipe in its
text chunks, whatever the response format. History, restore, re-download
and the signed URL route keep working unchanged, and a lossy copy never
replaces the original.

For `jpeg` / `webp` the response does not need the PNG, so the PNG
encode and write run in a background task after the response:

- The write runs in a task started inside the route. The task raises
`_diffusion_persist_active` as its first statement and drops it in its
own `finally` once the records exist, and the handler yields once before
returning so that hold is already taken when the response goes out.
Liveness and the gallery refresh probe therefore never read idle between
the response and the gallery record, as with `/images/generate`.
- The task copies the request's context, so the account context and the
gallery directory are the caller's. It also enters
`media_generation("diffusion")`, like the inline persist does.
- The write path is the existing one: a dotted temp file then
`os.replace` onto a new uuid name. No other reader can hold the file
open on Windows before it exists, and a crash mid-write leaves no
truncated PNG in the listing.
- A failed gallery write is logged and does not fail the request,
because the client already has its image. A process exit between the
response and the write means that image is not in the gallery. That is
the one behaviour change, and it only applies to clients that opted into
a lossy format.

The PNG `b64_json` path was not moved off the request path. The PNG
encode is the response itself, and what remains after it (write,
`os.replace`, mtime nudge, record) measured about 0.5-1 ms, too little
to justify a second code path with weaker crash semantics. URL responses
must have the file before the link is handed out, so they are unchanged.

## Measurements

CPU microbench on a real 1024x1024 RGB output from the FLUX.2 klein
benchmark, pinned to 8 cores (`taskset`), using each tree's own
`image_gallery`. Three repeated runs of 15-20 iterations each. Each cell
gives the median wall time with the range of the three run medians:

| Path | Wall ms | Process CPU ms | Payload (base64 chars) |
|---|---|---|---|
| main, `b64_json` png (encode, write, read back, base64) | 60.3-69.3 |
117-126 | 2,308,856 |
| this PR, `b64_json` png (bytes from memory) | 60.0-68.1 | 109-125 |
same bytes |
| this PR, `jpeg`, compression 100 (default) | 7.7-8.6 | 7.7-8.6 |
990,100 |
| this PR, `jpeg`, compression 75 | 3.3-4.6 | 3.3-4.6 | 159,232 |
| this PR, `webp`, compression 75 | 25.5 | 25.5 | 128,188 |
| this PR, `webp`, compression 100 | 79.5 | 78.2 | 666,600 |
| gallery PNG write, after the response (jpeg/webp) | 65.9 | 121 | n/a |

- PNG default: dropping the read-back is within run-to-run noise here
(the file is still in page cache). Its value is one less disk read and
file open on the request path, and no window in which the file could
vanish between write and read.
- `jpeg`: about 52-61 ms less server time per 1024x1024 image at
compression 100, and about 57-65 ms less at 75. On top of that, client
decode falls from about 30 ms (PNG) to about 2.6 ms (q75) or 8.4 ms
(q100), and the payload is 7 to 14 times smaller.
- `webp` is only worth asking for at lower compression values. At 100 it
costs more than PNG.

## Considered and not done

- **Stored (unfiltered, level 0) PNG as the default response.** It would
cut the default encode to a few milliseconds and keep pixels lossless.
But a 1024x1024 image grows from about 1.7 MB to about 3.1 MB (4.2 MB
base64). Over a remote link or tunnel, the extra transfer costs more
than the encode saves, so the default stays the compressed PNG. Clients
that want speed can now ask for `jpeg`.
- **Writing a lossy file to the gallery.** Rejected so the gallery stays
a lossless record with an embedded recipe.

## Scope notes

- Studio does not serve `/v1/images/edits`. Image edits go through the
Studio `/images/generate` route, whose response is a gallery record, not
base64. So these fields apply to `/v1/images/generations`. The encoder
helper (`image_gallery.encode_lossy`) is ready for an edits route to
reuse.
- The Studio UI never sends `output_format` (it uses
`/images/generate`), so there is no frontend change.

## Tests

New `studio/backend/tests/test_openai_images_output_format.py`, against
the real gallery in a tmp dir with real PIL images:

- A default `b64_json` response equals the gallery file bytes, with
`image_b64` patched to raise (proves there is no read back), and no
`output_format` key.
- An explicit `png` gives the same pixels and a gallery file, and echoes
`output_format`. A `null` `output_format` is PNG.
- `jpeg` and `webp` with `n=2` round-trip with the right format and
size. The gallery gets lossless PNGs with the recipe and the original
pixels.
- `jpeg` without `response_format` answers inline. Keyless `webp` works.
- Compression changes the size. The bounds 0 and 100 are accepted. -1,
101 and a string are a 400 on `output_compression`. `gif`, `bmp` and
`jpeg` with `url` are a 400 on `output_format`, with no generation run
and nothing written.
- A `url` response links a PNG that is already on disk, and the link
serves it.
- A failing background gallery write still returns 200 and releases the
liveness counter.

- The liveness hold is already taken (or the file already written) when
a jpeg response returns.

On `main` (b78af6d3c0) the new file gives 14 failed, 5 passed: the
passes are the paths main already serves the same way (null
`output_format`, URL responses, explicit png with url, and the
compression bounds cases, which main accepts by ignoring the field). On
this branch the new file plus the existing images route, keyless,
batching, LoRA, load swap, liveness persist-marker, gallery, PNG encode,
media auto switch and OpenAPI description suites give 534 passed, 1
skipped.
Kernels: do_not_specialize per-call sizes, eager int4 self-check, ROCm gates via is_rocm_torch (#19939)

Studio ROCm gfx1151: vendored Triton conv3d for the Wan VAE (about 11% faster decode, Winograd opt-in), MIOpen fallback (#19873)

## Summary

On ROCm gfx11 cards, Studio can now route a video VAE's `nn.Conv3d`
calls through a Triton direct conv3d instead of MIOpen. The vendored
H,W-Winograd routes are opt-in only
(`UNSLOTH_DIFFUSION_ROCM_TRITON_CONV3D_WINOGRAD=1`), since their bf16
error is 1.45-1.48x MIOpen's. The kernels are vendored from ROCm/aiter
(MIT), so there is no runtime dependency on an aiter checkout. It is on
by default only for gfx1151 and the Wan VAE (`AutoencoderKLWan`), the
arch and VAE class measured end to end on Linux and Windows. Other gfx11
cards and other VAE classes, LTX-2.5 included, need
`UNSLOTH_DIFFUSION_ROCM_TRITON_CONV3D=1`.

## What changes

- `studio/backend/core/inference/rocm_triton_conv3d/`: the Conv3D subset
of `aiter/ops/triton/conv` and `aiter/ops/triton/_triton_kernels/conv`
at ROCm/aiter commit `9e5e0362`, plus the gfx1151 conv3d tables from
ROCm/aiter PR #6973 (`065f9f99`) inlined as Python dicts.
- Edits against upstream: import paths; code removed for unused cases
(Conv2D, the NDHWC layout, the logger, the sigmoid / silu activations);
Winograd routing gated behind `ALLOW_WINOGRAD` (off by default, 3x3x3
then runs the direct cblocked kernel); and in the 1x1x1, general and
cblocked kernels the spatial sizes (N, D, H, W, output sizes) are
runtime arguments with `do_not_specialize`, so a new resolution does not
recompile them. Each file's header lists its changes.
- The weight-pack LRU now holds a weak reference to its source weight. A
pack is therefore freed with its module, and a weight that moves device
replaces its old pack.
- Each file keeps the AMD MIT notice and attribution next to our AGPL
header.
- `diffusion_rocm_triton_conv3d.py`: wraps `Conv3d._conv_forward` per
instance on `pipe.vae`.
- It covers diffusers' `WanCausalConv3d` and the plain `nn.Conv3d`
inside `LTX2VideoCausalConv3d`.
  - A call stays on MIOpen in any of these cases:
    - tracing under torch.compile;
    - autograd would record the call;
    - the tensor is fp32, or not on the GPU;
    - `groups != 1`, or `padding_mode != "zeros"`;
    - an index could pass int32;
- the estimated workspace (input packs, weight packs, output, plus the
Winograd V/M buffers when opted in) does not fit in driver-free memory
with a margin;
    - the shape already failed to compile or launch (it is not retried).
  - Out-of-memory and `torch._dynamo` errors are re-raised.
- A one-time self-check per device and dtype compares every enabled
route with `F.conv3d` in fp32 (rel L2 < 1e-2, including a strided 3x3x3
and a strided (3,1,1) case). If any route misses, MIOpen stays for that
device. `uninstall()` also clears the weight packs, which are otherwise
freed with their weights.
- Engagement is counted in `COUNTS` (`routed`, `fallback_error`,
`fallback_shape`, `fallback_memory`), and the install logs one line.
- `diffusion_speed.apply_speed_optims`: installs it on ROCm targets
only.

Env:
- `UNSLOTH_DIFFUSION_ROCM_TRITON_CONV3D=1` routes on any gfx11 card.
Archs other than gfx1151 borrow the gfx1151 tables.
- `UNSLOTH_DIFFUSION_ROCM_TRITON_CONV3D=0` turns it off, and wins over
the Winograd opt-in.
- `UNSLOTH_DIFFUSION_ROCM_TRITON_CONV3D_WINOGRAD=1` adds the Winograd
routes for 3x3x3 convs.
- Unset follows `DEFAULT_ON_ARCHES` (`gfx1151`) and `DEFAULT_ON_VAES`
(`AutoencoderKLWan`).
- `UNSLOTH_DIFFUSION_ROCM_AITER_CONV3D=1` is accepted as an alias.
- `UNSLOTH_DIFFUSION_ROCM_TRITON_CONV3D_SELFCHECK=0` skips the
self-check.

Coverage:
- Wan 2.1 / 2.2 VAE: every decoder conv.
- LTX-2.5 VAE (`AutoencoderKLLTX2Video`, `decoder_spatial_padding_mode`
zeros): every decoder conv, since they are plain `nn.Conv3d` reached
through `_conv_forward`.
- MiniMax H3: not applicable. Its decoder is a ViT, and its encoder's
causal convs use reflect padding and call `F.conv3d` directly. Only the
1x1x1 `quant_conv` / `post_quant_conv` are wrapped.

## Measurements (AMD CI Linux gfx1151, measuring branch with the same
kernels and configs)

All numbers in this section and the next were measured with the Winograd
routes on, before the default changed to direct-only with runtime sizes.
The direct-only default is being re-measured on gfx1151 (speed, first
render at a new resolution, per-conv error and peak memory) and this
section will be updated.

Stack: torch 2.11.0+rocm7.13.0, Triton 3.6.0. Every arm ran in a fresh
process, ABBA, 3 rounds; values are medians.

| | MIOpen | Triton conv3d |
|---|---|---|
| Wan 2.2 TI2V-5B VAE decode, 704x1280x49 | 51.9 s | 32.3 s (1.61x) |
| First (cold) decode | 1004 s | 35 s |
| Decode peak memory | 11.8 GiB | 18.7 GiB |
| PSNR vs MIOpen | - | 54.7 dB |
| Conv calls routed | - | 1323 / 1323 |
| Studio Wan 832x480x49 render, wall | 66.4 s | 58.2 s (-12.3%) |
| Studio Wan 832x480x49 render, VAE + post | 23.5 s | 15.4 s |

- Per-conv accuracy vs fp32 `F.conv3d`: rel L2 3.4e-3 (Winograd) and
1.7e-3 (direct), the same order as bf16 MIOpen.
- Render LPIPS against main: any GEMM-solution change gives about
0.10-0.12 on Wan after 8 steps, even when exact. Same-arm repeats are
LPIPS 0, so exactness evidence stays at the decode level (PSNR).

## AMD CI at the current head (direct conv default, Winograd opt-in)

AMD CI Linux gfx1151 (torch 2.11.0+rocm7.13, Triton 3.6.0). The workload
is a Wan 2.2 VAE decode of real latents. Each arm runs in a fresh
process, with A run 4 times and C and D 3 times each. A is main

## Kernel checklist

Checked against the kernel ship rules and the review checklist; GPU rows
come from the AMD CI gfx1151 runs above.

- **Exactness / tolerance, gfx1151 GPU, all 21 Wan decoder conv shapes,
bf16, rel L2 against fp32:**
- Winograd routes: 3.45e-3, 1.45-1.48x MIOpen's own bf16 error. That
misses the 1.05x per-op bar for a non-exact default kernel, so Winograd
is opt-in only.
- Direct routes (1x1x1, general, cblocked): 1.66e-3, 0.70x MIOpen's
error, so more accurate. These are the default.
- Whole decode: PSNR 54.7 dB against MIOpen. Same-arm repeats were
byte-identical.
- **CPU oracle sweep** (`TRITON_INTERPRET=1`, fp64 reference): 16 cases
per dtype across every route. They include batch 2, odd H / W,
non-contiguous and channels-last inputs, a DC offset, x100 magnitude, no
bias, stride 2 and dilation 2.
- fp16: every direct route has the same error as stock `F.conv3d`.
Winograd is 3.2e-3 (inherent to F(4,3)).
  - A perturbed negative control fails every fp16 case.
- bf16 under the interpreter is void (the interpreter truncates fp32 to
bf16), so bf16 accuracy comes from the GPU rows only.
- **Fallbacks:** every declined call runs the module's own original
`_conv_forward`, so the output is byte-identical to main. Unit-tested
cases:
  - fp32;
  - groups > 1;
  - reflect padding;
  - autograd recording;
  - torch.compile tracing;
  - HIP / CUDA graph capture;
  - CPU tensors;
  - int32-overflowing sizes;
  - low free memory;
  - a launch failure (that shape is not retried);
  - a Triton older than 3.6, or a stub Triton.
- **Errors:** OOM and `torch._dynamo` errors are re-raised. A failed
self-check keeps MIOpen for that device.
- **Kill switch:** `UNSLOTH_DIFFUSION_ROCM_TRITON_CONV3D=0` installs
nothing.
- **Device:** every launch runs under `torch.cuda.device(x.device)`, and
arch eligibility is read per operand device at call time.
- **Memory:**
- The workspace estimate covers the output, input / weight packs and the
Winograd V / M buffers.
- A call falls back to MIOpen when the estimate plus a margin exceeds
driver-free memory. Reserved-but-unallocated allocator blocks are not
counted as free.
- Calls under 64 MiB of workspace skip the driver memory query (about
0.2 ms each).
  - The weight-pack cache is bounded and holds weights weakly.
  - Measured cost: decode peak +3.6 GiB at 480p and +7.0 GiB at 720p.
- **Traceability:** eager only. Under torch.compile tracing the router
returns the stock conv, so a compiled VAE decode keeps MIOpen with no
graph break. Studio does not compile the Wan VAE decode on gfx1151: 1764
of 1764 calls were routed in the product flow.
- **Engagement:** the `COUNTS` counters and the install log line,
checked on both OSes through Studio's real load path. Results: 1764
routed, 0 fallbacks.
- **Platforms:**
  - Linux Triton 3.6 and Windows `triton-windows` 3.8 are measured.
  - Other gfx11 cards borrow the gfx1151 tables and are opt-in.
  - CUDA, CPU and MPS never install it (ROCm gate, CPU-tested).
- **Licence:** every vendored file carries the AMD MIT notice and the
source commit next to the AGPL header (tested). Nothing imports aiter.

Gaps:
- **Recompile budget:** upstream specialises every spatial size as
`tl.constexpr`. With those kernels, the first render at each new
resolution paid about +25 s on its VAE (48.5 vs 23.4 s, Linux). The
default-path kernels now take spatial sizes at runtime, so only a new
channel / kernel configuration compiles; the opt-in Winograd kernels
still specialise on size. The first-render cost of the new default is
part of the pending re-measurement.
- **Not run:**
  - the compute sanitizer, which is CUDA-only;
  - a compiled-arm oracle, since the kernels are never traced;
  - backward, since inference only routes and training stays on MIOpen;
  - gfx11 cards other than gfx1151;
  - torch versions other than Studio's 2.11 ROCm wheels.

## Tests

`studio/backend/tests/test_diffusion_rocm_triton_conv3d.py` (CPU, no
GPU), 27 tests. They fail on main (the module does not exist) and pass
here. They cover:
- gating: on by default only for gfx1151 and the Wan VAE class, env on /
off, legacy alias, ROCm gfx11 only;
- MIOpen paths: autograd, fp32, torch.compile, reflect padding, groups;
- failure handling: a launch failure falls back and is not retried; OOM
is re-raised;
- the low-free-memory fallback against driver-free memory;
- default routing to the direct kernels, the Winograd opt-in and
kill-switch precedence, runtime (non-specialised) size arguments, and
the self-check bound;
- the Winograd workspace estimate, and the int32 guard;
- `WanCausalConv3d` reaching the router, and the ROCm-only wiring;
- both license headers in every vendored file, and no aiter import;
- the vendored kernels for the 1x1x1, general, cblocked and Winograd
routes against `F.conv3d` under `TRITON_INTERPRET=1`.

## Not covered here

- Archs other than gfx1151 run with gfx1151 tables and are untested.
- No backward: training keeps MIOpen.

When Studio auto-detects an Alpaca dataset, it formats the rows with
generic Instruction and Response headings even when the selected
instruct model has a native chat template. Studio Chat and exports then
use the native turns, which differ from the ones used in training.

Studio: recall summarised details when a cloud chat is also trimmed (#19628) On an API connection with auto-compact set to summarise, a chat with a large fixed overhead (a long system prompt or many tools) can still be over the limit after the summary is written, so the oldest remaining turns are dropped as well. In that case the automatic recall only searched the turns dropped after the summary and skipped the turns the summary replaced. Asking about an exact value from early in the chat (a code, a number, a name the summary left out) got a recalled block about an unrelated recent turn (or none), and the model made a value up or said it did not know. The same happened when a saved summary was reused after a new summary call failed. The turns a summary replaces are now archived together with the trimmed ones before recall runs, and recall searches the full conversation, so the newest question gets the earlier wording it asks about, within the same recall budget as before. Chats that only need the summary, chats that are only trimmed, and chats that fit are unchanged. ## Screenshots | Before (main) | After (this PR) | |---|---| | | | --------- Co-authored-by: Daniel Han <23090290+danielhanchen@users.noreply.github.com>

Studio diffusion offload: follow diffusers' generic wrapper-tensor group offload helpers (#20016)

## Summary

Make Studio's diffusion group-offload code work on diffusers main after
[huggingface/diffusers#15383](https://github.com/huggingface/diffusers/pull/15383)
("[hooks] support generic wrapper subclass tensors in group offloading",
merged as 644aa884). Behaviour on the pinned diffusers (0.42.1 / 0.41.0
/ 0.36.0) is unchanged: when the old torchao helpers exist they are used
exactly as before.

## Upstream change

`diffusers/hooks/group_offloading.py` dropped the torchao-only helpers
`_is_torchao_tensor`, `_swap_torchao_tensor`, `_restore_torchao_tensor`,
`_record_stream_torchao_tensor` and `_get_torchao_inner_tensor_names`.
It now moves any traceable wrapper subclass with
`is_traceable_wrapper_subclass`, `_swap_wrapper_tensor`,
`_record_stream_wrapper_tensor` and `_apply_to_inner_tensors` (rebuild
through `__tensor_flatten__` / `__tensor_unflatten__`, nested wrappers
included). The restore on offload is inlined as
`_swap_wrapper_tensor(param, _apply_to_inner_tensors(host_copy,
identity))`.

Studio read those names with `getattr(go, "_is_torchao_tensor", lambda
t: False)` or wrapped them on the module, so on diffusers main every
torchao weight silently became a plain tensor to Studio, and the
wrappers no longer wrapped anything diffusers calls.

## What broke on diffusers main (reproduced on CPU, torch 2.14.1,
torchao 0.18.0)

Same script, base (`main`) vs this branch, on diffusers 0.42.1 and on
diffusers main at 644aa884:

| Check | 0.42.1 base | 0.42.1 head | main base | main head |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `torchao_group_offload_supported()` | True | True | **False** | True |
| `_return_module_tensors` on an `Int8Tensor` weight | moves
qdata/scale/zero_point | same | **RuntimeError:
`variable.set_data(tensor)` incompatible tensor type** | moves all inner
tensors |
| swap retry installed / wraps | `_swap_torchao_tensor` |
`_swap_torchao_tensor` | **not installed** | `_swap_wrapper_tensor` |

Consequences on diffusers main before this change:

- `torchao_group_offload_supported()` returning False turns off
`stream_prequantized_module`, hides the streamed MiniMax-H3 INT8 tier,
and makes an H3 INT8 load that has to stream raise "group offloading is
not available in this install".
- `_return_module_tensors` took the `.data` path for torchao weights,
which raises for `Int8Tensor` (`set_data` refuses a different subclass;
executed above). `_keep_groups_resident` and the prefetcher's
`_point_at` use the same `.data =` move: by reading, the first swallows
the error and keeps no group resident (every block streams), the second
raises in the prefetch issue path. Those two were not executed on a
card.
- The weakref swap retry no longer wrapped the helper diffusers calls,
so the compiled-weight `Cannot swap ... weakref` failure it guards
against was unguarded again.
- `install_torchao_v1_int8_pin_ops` hit an `AttributeError` on
`_restore_torchao_tensor` and returned False, so torchao 0.17 v1 INT8
fell back to synchronous (no copy stream) offload.
- The buffer restore patch fell back to `buffer.data = host` for wrapper
buffers.

Harmless: `_pin_top_level_group` / `_skip_top_level_copy_back` (wrapper
weights are refused by `_top_group_tensor_ok` anyway) and
`_install_group_offload_torchao_host_copy` (diffusers main's `_to_cpu`
always builds a new wrapper, so the aliasing it fixes cannot happen).

## The change

- New `studio/backend/core/inference/diffusion_go_compat.py` resolves,
for the installed diffusers, `is_wrapper_fn`, `swap` / `swap_fn` /
`swap_name`, `restore` / `restore_fn` / `restore_name`, `record_stream`
and `wrapper_swap_supported`. The torchao names win whenever
`_is_torchao_tensor` exists, and the same function objects are returned,
so the pinned diffusers keeps today's code path exactly. On diffusers
main it returns diffusers' own `is_traceable_wrapper_subclass` and
wrapper helpers, so Studio classifies a tensor exactly as the installed
diffusers does (GGUF parameters are not wrapper subclasses and keep the
`.data` path on both).
- Every Studio call site goes through it: `_keep_groups_resident`,
`_return_module_tensors`, the buffer restore, the top-level group
checks, the prefetcher issue path and top-level stream, and
`torchao_group_offload_supported`.
- The swap retry wraps whichever swap helper the installed diffusers
calls.
- The torchao 0.17 v1 INT8 pin ops still install on diffusers main; the
`_restore_torchao_tensor` / `_record_stream_torchao_tensor` wrappers are
only installed where those helpers exist (diffusers main rebuilds the
nested v1 wrappers itself).
- `_install_group_offload_torchao_host_copy` stays keyed on the torchao
helpers on purpose.

## Tests

`studio/backend/tests/test_diffusion_go_compat.py` (11 tests): API
resolution for both shapes (fake namespaces plus the installed
diffusers), generic restore not mutating the host copy, the capability
probe, `_return_module_tensors` with a real torchao `Int8Tensor`, the
swap retry on the real module and on a generic-API module, and the v1
pin ops install. Run against the old call sites, the new tests fail on
diffusers main and pass on 0.42.1; on this branch they pass on both.

New tests against the old call sites (compat module copied in, nothing
else changed):

| | diffusers 0.42.1 | diffusers main |
| --- | --- | --- |
| base call sites | 9 passed, 2 failed (the two fake generic-API cases)
| 5 passed, 6 failed |
| this branch | 11 passed | 11 passed |

Existing suites (84 files touching group offloading, prefetch, prequant,
int8 streaming and memory; CPU, `-o addopts=`), base vs head, compared
by failing test ID:

| | diffusers 0.42.1 | diffusers main |
| --- | --- | --- |
| base | 6403 passed, 5 failed | 6391 passed, 15 failed, 2 errors |
| head | 6403 passed, 5 failed | 6391 passed, 15 failed, 2 errors |

The failing IDs are identical base vs head in each venv, so none are
new. On 0.42.1 they are host-dependent or pre-existing
(`test_the_pin_budget_leaves_the_reserve_free` reads live host RAM,
three `test_integrated_gpu_no_host_pin` audits, one
`test_diffusion_cfg_pair` compile test). The extra ones on diffusers
main are separate forward-compat gaps, unrelated to group offloading:
`diffusers.utils.state_dict_utils._load_sft_state_dict_metadata` is gone
(`test_diffusion_lora_files`), and the Qwen-Image 2.1 fast step no
longer installs (`test_diffusion_qwenimage21_graph`,
`test_diffusion_cfg_pair`).

(streamed INT8 group offload with Studio's kwargs, bit-exact vs
resident, offloaded inner tensors on the host, resident groups) plus the
CUDA-gated offload / prefetch / precision / keep-cpu / CUDA graph / H3
suites, base vs head:

| | diffusers 0.42.1 | diffusers main |
| --- | --- | --- |
| base | smoke PASS, 382 passed, 2 failed (the new compat tests) | smoke
FAIL, 19 failed |
| head | smoke PASS, 384 passed | smoke PASS (bit-identical streamed
INT8), 8 failed |

The 8 head failures on diffusers main were all
`test_quantised_blocks_survive_group_offload_under_no_grad[*]` with
`Failed: DID NOT RAISE` at its `pytest.raises(Exception),
torch.inference_mode()` check: the no_grad streamed forward matched, and
diffusers main no longer rejects the streamed forward under
inference_mode, because it moves the inner tensors and swaps in a fresh
wrapper instead of calling `aten.to` on the torchao wrapper. That test
is now version-aware: it keeps expecting the raise where
`_is_torchao_tensor` exists, and on the wrapper-subclass API asserts the
inference_mode output equals the resident one and that a later no_grad
forward still does.

## Not proven here

- torchao 0.17 v1 INT8 on diffusers main is covered only with stand-in
classes; the bit-exact CUDA test for it needs torchao 0.17.
- diffusers 0.41.0 and 0.36.0 were not installed; they keep the old path
because the compat layer returns the same objects whenever
`_is_torchao_tensor` exists, and resolves nothing (the old `getattr`
defaults) when neither API exists.
- Studio still renders offloaded quantized pipelines under no_grad
(`_torchao_render_needs_no_grad`, `_move_groups_outside_inference_mode`
and the video / text-encoder residency equivalents). Those guards also

Studio loads: upload rings wait for the current stream before writing reused blocks (#20008)

## Summary

Two direct-to-GPU upload paths allocate their target tensors on the
current stream, then fill them from a side stream through a pinned ring
without waiting for the current stream first:

- `read_safetensors_to_device` in `video_ltx2.py` (the LTX-2.3 / LTX-2.5
direct checkpoint read)
- `_ring_copy` in `diffusion_fast_load.py` (the fast `.to(device)`
upload)

The caching allocator hands a freed block straight back to the same
stream, so a target can be a block whose previous owner still has a
write queued on the current stream. The side stream then writes the
checkpoint bytes first, and the queued write lands on top of them
afterwards. Each path now calls
`stream.wait_stream(torch.cuda.current_stream(device))` before its first
side-stream write. This costs nothing when the current stream is idle,
which is the normal case at load time.

## Evidence

The new GPU tests make the hazard deterministic. They queue
`torch.cuda._sleep` and then `fill_(7)` into a block, free the block,
and run the upload into the reused block. They assert that the block
really was reused, then compare the bytes.

Colab L4, torch 2.14.1+cu130, 3 runs per arm, base = this PR's merge
base plus the new tests:

| Test | base | head |
|---|---|---|
|
`test_video_ltx23_direct_load.py::test_the_device_read_waits_for_work_queued_on_the_current_stream`
| 3 / 3 failed (bytes overwritten) | 3 / 3 passed |
|
`test_diffusion_fast_load.py::test_the_ring_waits_for_work_queued_on_the_current_stream`
| 3 / 3 passed | 3 / 3 passed |

The fast-load ring passes on base because its pinned staging allocation
happens to synchronize the device before the first copy. The fence makes
the ordering explicit instead of relying on that, and the test catches a
regression if the staging allocation ever stops synchronizing.

## Tests

- CPU: `test_diffusion_fast_load.py` and
`test_video_ltx23_direct_load.py` pass. The new tests skip without CUDA.
- `test_integrated_gpu_no_host_pin.py` has 3 failures on main as well,
in files this PR does not touch.

## Not covered

- ROCm and multi-GPU were not run. The call is the same stream API on
ROCm.

Studio: finish tool runs when a provider refuses a too-long prompt (#19598)

When a cloud connection's real context window is smaller than the one
Studio was told, the provider can refuse a prompt in the middle of a
tool run. Studio then summarised only the turns before the current
request and resent the request with all of its tool results. The summary
often cost more than it saved, the second prompt was bigger than the
refused one, and the chat ended with a provider error (OpenRouter,
Gemini, Anthropic, DeepSeek and others).

Now the older tool results of the current request are cut to their
opening lines and stay cut for the rest of the run, while the request
and the newest result stay whole. A retry is only sent when it is
smaller than the refused prompt, otherwise the provider's error is shown
once, and a long run can recover again if a later step overflows. Plain
chats recover as before.

MOSS-TTS-Nano attention test: hold on Windows, where SentencePiece is disabled by default (#20015)

## Problem


`studio/backend/tests/test_native_audio.py::test_moss_nano_overrides_flash_attention_on_cpu`
fails on Windows:

```
RuntimeError: MOSS-TTS-Nano requires SentencePiece, which is disabled in this Unsloth process. Restart Unsloth with UNSLOTH_DISABLE_SENTENCEPIECE=0 to enable its native tokenizer.
```

The latest example is the `windows-latest` leg of the #19751
cross-platform staging run.

Studio disables SentencePiece on Windows by default
(`utils/sentencepiece_guard.py` leaves a `None` sentinel in
`sys.modules`). Since #14693, `_load_moss_nano` refuses up front when it
sees that sentinel. That refusal is correct, and it has its own test
(`test_moss_sentencepiece_preflight.py`).

This test, from August, is about something else: that the MOSS load
passes `eager` attention on CPU. It never cleared the sentinel, so on
Windows it stops at the refusal before it reaches what it checks. It
only runs on Windows in the cross-platform legs, so this has gone unseen
since #14693.

## Fix

The test drops the `sentencepiece` sentinel for its own duration
(`monkeypatch.delitem`), the same way
`test_moss_sentencepiece_preflight.py` controls it. It then checks the
attention kwargs on every platform. The refusal stays covered by its own
test.

## Verification

- `test_native_audio.py` and `test_moss_sentencepiece_preflight.py`, on
Linux: 53 passed.
- Windows simulated on Linux by setting `sys.modules["sentencepiece"] =
None` before running the test:
  - Main's test fails with the same `RuntimeError` as the Windows job.
  - This version passes.
- Not run on a real Windows runner in this PR.

Studio diffusion training: record per-process GPU and host memory peaks like LLM training (#19995)

## Summary

#19922 records per-process GPU and host memory peaks for LLM training
runs. Diffusion training never did, so diffusion A/Bs still had to read
whole-device memory. This PR makes the diffusion trainer report the same
fields with the same names and units (bytes), on the live status and on
the persisted run record.

Reporting only: no change to the training loop, losses, or the existing
`peak_memory_gb` figure.

## What changes

- `run_diffusion_training_process` wraps its event queue in the existing
`PeakStampingQueue`, so `progress`, `complete` and `error` events carry
`memory_peaks` for every diffusion family (SDXL, the DiT trainers, H3),
including the error event from a crashed trainer.
- `DiffusionTrainingService` folds those samples with
`merge_memory_peaks` (field-wise max, junk ignored) into
`status()["memory_peaks"]`, and `_persist_run_record` writes the flat
fields `gpu_peak_allocated_bytes`, `gpu_peak_reserved_bytes`,
`host_peak_rss_bytes`, `host_peak_commit_bytes`, as on the LLM run
record.
- API models: `DiffusionTrainingStatusResponse.memory_peaks` uses
`TrainingMemoryPeaks`, and `DiffusionTrainingRunSummary` (so also the
run detail) gains the four flat fields. Older run records without them
still load, with the fields set to null.
- `utils/process_memory_peaks.py`:
- `bank_gpu_peaks()`: the diffusion trainer resets the CUDA peak
counters at loop start and after each preview, so its own
`peak_memory_gb` leaves out model load and previews.
`reset_training_peak_memory` now saves the counters first, so the
process peak still covers the whole run, like the LLM worker, where
nothing resets them.
- MPS: torch has no peak counter there, so `current_allocated_memory`
(allocated) and `driver_allocated_memory` (reserved) are sampled on each
call and the running max is reported. CUDA and ROCm go through
`torch.cuda` as before. With no GPU, the GPU fields are null.
- `include_children=True`: the host RSS peak is the larger of the
process's own peak and a sampled sum over the process and its live
descendants. Multi-GPU diffusion runs start ranks 1..N-1 as child
processes, so this covers the whole training process tree. When there
are no children the value equals the LLM worker's own-process peak.
Without psutil it falls back to the own-process peak. The LLM worker
keeps the default (`include_children=False`) and behaves as before.
- `PeakStampingQueue` takes optional `event_types` and
`include_children`. The defaults keep the LLM worker unchanged.

## Limits

- The GPU fields come from rank 0's process. In a multi-GPU diffusion
run, ranks 1..N-1 are separate processes, and their torch counters are
not visible from rank 0.
- The tree RSS is sampled at log steps and terminal events, so it is a
lower bound on the true tree peak. Summed RSS counts shared pages once
per process.
- The frontend does not show the per-process peaks for LLM runs either,
so there is no UI change. The diffusion panel still shows its existing
`peak_memory_gb`.

## Tests

`studio/backend/tests/test_diffusion_train_memory_peaks.py`, CPU only:

- progress peaks reach the status and never go down; complete and error
peaks reach the persisted record, the list, and the detail; junk values
are dropped; old records still load; a new job starts with no peaks
- the trainer child stamps progress, complete and crash error events on
a CPU host (GPU fields null, host RSS set) and never imports torch to
measure
- MPS running max, MPS unavailable or raising, CUDA peaks banked across
the trainer's reset, CPU reset is a no-op
- tree RSS includes a live 300 MB child and keeps the peak after the
child exits; without psutil it falls back to the own-process peak

The existing `tests/test_training_memory_peaks.py` (LLM) and the
diffusion service and trainer suites pass unchanged.

Evaluate per-module LoRA scaling on vLLM releases that apply it (#19537)

`unsloth eval --backend vllm` refused every LoRA adapter whose
rank_pattern or alpha_pattern gives some module a different scale, on
the grounds that vLLM applies one lora_alpha / r scale to all modules.
That stopped being true in vLLM 0.32, which resolves rank_pattern and
alpha_pattern per module the same way PEFT does, so on current vLLM
these adapters were turned away even though vLLM scores them correctly.

The refusal now only applies when the installed vLLM is older than 0.32
(or its version cannot be read), and its message also suggests upgrading
vLLM. On vLLM 0.32 and newer such adapters are evaluated normally. Plain
adapters and the rank limit check are unchanged.

Studio diffusion: one module walk per CFG replica check (#19254)

## Problem

On multi-GPU hosts that run classifier-free guidance with a replica on a
second card (#18421), `CfgParallelRouter.__call__` re-checks the replica
on every denoise step, on the host:

- `_drop_if_stale` runs `weights_fingerprint` (which calls
`named_parameters()`, `named_buffers()` and `named_modules()`, so three
full walks of the denoiser) and then `_hooks_present` (a fourth walk).
In that fourth walk, `getattr(sub, "_hf_hook", None)` raises and catches
an `AttributeError` inside `Module.__getattr__` for every submodule.
- `_launch_prediction` runs `_mirror_hook_state` and `_take_prediction`
runs `_hook_state`, which call `startswith("_unsloth_")` on every
`__dict__` key of every source and replica submodule.

torch's `named_*` walks are nested generators, so each yielded name
passes through every enclosing generator. Real DiTs have 1,300 to 4,700
submodules, and all of this runs on the host before the step's branches
are queued.

## Change

The checks are the same and give the same answers on every step. Nothing
is cached across steps or renders.

- `_named_modules`: a single recursive walk that returns exactly
`list(module.named_modules())`, with the same order, names and
de-duplication. If a module's type or instance replaces `named_modules`,
the walk asks that module for its own subtree, the same way torch's
recursion does.
- `weights_fingerprint`: parameters, buffers and adapter attributes are
collected in one pass over that walk, following torch's `_named_members`
rules (separate de-duplication sets, `None` skipped). The parts tuple is
built in the same order, so the hash is identical to before. If the
root's type or instance replaces `named_parameters`, `named_buffers`,
`named_modules` or `_named_members`, the previous code path runs
unchanged.
- `_hooks_present`: a submodule is skipped only when every check would
provably find nothing. That requires torch's attribute lookup, no
class-level hook slots, no registry, no `_hf_hook` in the instance dict
or in the parameter, buffer or submodule fallback, empty forward hook
dicts, and no instance `forward`. Every other submodule goes through the
original checks. The first offending submodule and the reason string are
unchanged.
- `_hook_state` / `_mirror_hook_state`: before the exact per-key scan, a
dict's keys are joined and searched once. Only dicts that can hold a
`_unsloth_*` key are scanned. A non-string key falls back to the exact
scan, which raises exactly as before.

## Results

Host CPU time per call: `time.thread_time`, median of 40 interleaved
reps, p10 to p90 in brackets, torch 2.14.1, CPU only. Models are built
on the meta device from real transformer configs, with a deepcopy as the
replica. `old2` is a second run of the old code, used as the A/A noise
check. The host was heavily oversubscribed (load average about 700 on 96
cores), so absolute numbers are inflated. The ratios hold across runs.

| Model (modules) | Function | old ms | old2 ms | new ms |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| SD3.5 Large (1456) | weights_fingerprint | 10.73 | 9.34 | 4.96 |
| | _hooks_present | 4.77 | 4.62 | 2.73 |
| | _mirror_hook_state | 6.56 | 6.12 | 3.70 |
| | _hook_state | 2.53 | 2.45 | 1.66 |
| | per step | 24.59 | 22.53 | 13.05 (0.53x) |
| FLUX.1-dev (1279) | per step | 19.19 | 18.27 | 10.74 (0.56x) |
| Qwen-Image (2297) | weights_fingerprint | 12.93 | 11.89 | 6.25 |
| | _hooks_present | 6.04 | 5.68 | 4.05 |
| | _mirror_hook_state | 8.47 | 7.56 | 4.54 |
| | _hook_state | 3.68 | 3.59 | 2.30 |
| | per step | 31.12 | 28.72 | 17.14 (0.55x) |
| Qwen-Image + LoRA r16 (4697) | per step | 80.70 | 75.95 | 44.63
(0.55x) |

The A/A gap between `old` and `old2` is 2 to 9 percent of the per-step
total. The cut is 44 to 47 percent. On a less loaded run, today's
Qwen-Image total was 25.9 ms of wall time per step (56 ms with a LoRA).
At a 0.25 to 0.5 s step, that is roughly 5 to 10 percent of the step (10
to 20 percent with a LoRA), and this change removes about half of it.
The harness also checks that old and new give equal results on every
model before timing.

## Tests

- New `studio/backend/tests/test_diffusion_multigpu_walk_identity.py`
keeps the previous implementations verbatim and asserts equal answers
through these mutations: a parameter replaced, in-place parameter and
buffer edits, adapter state added, an adapter scale changed, the active
adapter changed, a pinned scale tensor edited in place, adapter modules
injected and removed, an inference-tensor buffer, a callable adapter
attribute, tied parameters, shared submodules, `None` children,
parameters and buffers. Hook cases: offload, trusted and foreign forward
/ pre hooks on the root and on children, `_hf_hook` as an attribute and
through the buffer fallback, a class-level `_hf_hook`, a custom
`__getattr__`, a missing `_forward_hooks` slot, step-cache and empty
registries, instance forward overrides. State cases: `_unsloth_*` added,
changed, retyped, removed and non-scalar, stale and kept replica keys, a
separator inside a key, a non-string key. Traversal cases: overridden
`named_modules` on a child, an instance and the root, and an overridden
`named_parameters` on the root. Also a real PEFT-injected model and a
tiny diffusers FLUX transformer. 9 passed.
- All 39 existing test files that touch `diffusion_multigpu` were run on
the merge base and on this branch: 1602 passed on both, with the same 92
failing / erroring test IDs on both arms (environment: diffusers and

`UNSLOTH_CPU_THREADS` caps threads for native Studio workloads, but GGUF
chat still starts llama-server using the host’s physical core count. On
a shared machine, a chat can use more CPU threads than the operator set
aside for Studio.

configuration. Explicit launcher flags and smaller platform limits still
take precedence.

Keep Claude Code parallel tool results in call order (#19809)

Claude Code can return the results of parallel tool calls in a different
order from the calls themselves. Studio forwards that order to the local
model. Chat templates that omit tool call IDs then pair the results by
position, so the model can read one tool’s output as another’s.

When a complete result batch matches the preceding assistant tool calls,
Studio uses the IDs to put the results back in call order before passing
them to the chat template. Partial batches keep their original order.

going to More > Audio > Music starts downloading the whole repo, often
hundreds of GB.

The Audio page stays mounted after its first visit and takes `active`
from the pathname. It read `?model=` with `useSearch({ strict: false
})`, which resolves the root match. While `/audio`'s async
`requireAuth()` guard runs, that match still belongs to the page being
left. So the Hub's `?model=<chat GGUF repo>` reached the Audio model

checkpoint repo that also publishes quants plans the checkpoint without
them. Single-quant repos (split parts count once, `mmproj` doesn't
count) plan as before, and picks that name a GGUF file or quant don't
use this plan.

When a Decision API request sent its picture inside a chat-message state
(an image part in `messages`) instead of the separate `images` field,

text only. That happened under Auto when the PyTorch model was already

restarted for the next one.

when nothing here can read them the API says so (images need llama.cpp,

answering without them. Text-only requests are routed exactly as before.

Studio: keep sentence spacing in long Chinese and Japanese translations (#19619)

Long text on the Translate page is sent to the model in passages of
about 1,000 characters. Chinese and Japanese paragraphs have no space
after a full stop, so when a long paragraph was cut after 。 and
translated into English, the passages were glued back together with
nothing between them and the result read "end of one sentence.Start of
the next" at every cut. The same happened to long text blocks in the
image translation overlay. The reverse also showed up: English
translated into Chinese or Japanese kept the English space after each
cut, leaving "。 " in the middle of a paragraph.

Passages are now joined the way the target language writes:

- One space between two passages of English, French, Korean and other
spaced languages, only where the source was cut after Chinese or
Japanese text with no space. A hard cut inside a long link or word of a
spaced language stays glued as before.
- No space before a passage of Chinese or Japanese output, unless the
source itself had a space there (for example a name such as 田中 太郎 inside
English text).
- A cut after 。, ！ or ？ now keeps the closing quote or bracket that
follows (”, 」, 』, ）) with its sentence, so no passage starts with a
stray closing mark.
- Only the last few characters of the output are inspected when joining,
so the join stays constant time per streamed token on long documents.

Line breaks and blank lines between passages are kept exactly as before,
and short texts that fit in one passage are not affected.

Before and after, a 1,383 character Chinese paragraph translated to
English (same two passages and same model output on both sides; the
boundary falls between sentences 17 and 18):

![Translate before and
after](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/danielhanchen/unsloth-staging-2/pr-media/pr/19619/pr19619_output_rows-d95291ace6cd.png)

an `AudioContext`, and waited on `context.resume()` before `play()`.
When the context can't start (no output device, an autoplay policy, a
stuck device), the elements play into a suspended graph: every stem is
silent while the transport shows "playing". The source preview, a plain
element, still plays. I reproduced this in headless Firefox with no
audio device, using real HTDemucs stems.

gain to 0..1, sets `volume` and sets `muted` at zero. On iOS Safari
`volume` is read-only (always 1), so a one-time probe
(`volumeIsWritable`) keeps the original `MediaElementSource` +
`GainNode` path there so partial levels still work.

Gain changes on the element path are instant. The old graph had a 15 ms
ramp, so moving a slider on loud material can click.

The playback and seek crashes in #19131 weren't reproduced here. This PR
doesn't claim to fix them.

probe with a pinned-volume fake, and checks that the graph is built only

```
[banner] FAIL 921x534 new chat expanded: the bottom card is on the corner, not floating above it lastPaintedFromBottom=4 (want 16)
[banner] FAIL 390x500 new chat collapsed: the bottom card is on the corner, not floating above it lastPaintedFromBottom=9.1 (want 16)
```

The other four failures are the same check on the Train and Model hub
pages, at the same two sizes. The cards in the corner rail (update,
llama.cpp update, downloads, loaded models) are supposed to sit 16 px
above the corner. At these two window sizes the bottom card lands 4 px
and 9 px from the edge instead.

#19970 made the rail `overflow: visible` while its cards fit, and scroll
only once they outgrow it (`data-rail-scrolls`), so WebKit can blur
glass cards against the page. That part is right. But `overlayRailScope`
decided "outgrow" with `scrollHeight > clientHeight`, and for an
`overflow: visible` box Chromium leaves the end padding out of
`scrollHeight`. Cards that run into the rail's 16 px bottom padding, but
not past its border, read as `scrollHeight == clientHeight`: the rail
never starts scrolling, and the bottom card sits in the gutter.

The same 921x534 layout on a bare page in Chromium, cards running 12 px
into the bottom padding:

| rail | `scrollHeight` / `clientHeight` | bottom card from the corner |
|---|---|---|
| `overflow: visible` (main) | 534 / 534 | 4 px, and the rail does not
scroll |
| `overflow: auto` (before #19970) | 546 / 534 | scrolls |

Before #19970 the rail was always a scroll container, so the same layout
scrolled.

## Fix

`railOverflows()` in `studio/frontend/src/lib/toast-offset.ts`:
- It keeps the `scrollHeight` test.
- It also measures the span of the rail's in-flow cards plus its top and
bottom padding against `clientHeight`. Dragged cards are `fixed`
elsewhere and are left out.
- `overlayRailScope` uses it, so the rail scrolls whenever its cards do
not fit.
- While they fit, the rail stays `overflow: visible`, so #19970's WebKit
glass fix is unchanged.

On the bare page above:
- Cards 12 px into the padding: the old test reports no overflow,
`railOverflows` reports overflow.
- Cards that fit with room to spare: both report no overflow, and the
bottom card sits at 16 px.

## Verification

- `tests/toast-offset.test.ts`, new case: cards running into the bottom
padding with `scrollHeight == clientHeight` count as overflow; a fitting
stack, a stack with a dragged `fixed` card, and an empty rail do not; a
real `scrollHeight` overflow still does. `toast-offset.test.ts` and
`glass-floating-cards.test.ts`: 27 passed.
- `npm run typecheck` and `eslint` on both files: clean.
- The browser check itself,
`tests/studio/playwright_update_banner_layout.py`, run against a local
Studio install of main (`6047d3b980`) with the same driver CI uses:
- Before, main: `2159 checks, 6 failed`. The same six as CI: 921x534
expanded and 390x500 collapsed on New chat, Train and Model hub,
`lastPaintedFromBottom=4` / `9.1`.
- After, the same install with only this PR's `toast-offset.ts` rebuilt
in: `2153 checks, 0 failed`.
- The six corner checks are not run in those six layouts any more,
because the rail now scrolls there, exactly as it did before #19970. The
check only judges the corner while the rail is not scrolling. Every
other check, including "can be scrolled into the rail's view" for each
card, passes on both sides.

Let the Docker llama.cpp updater repair a missing install (#19630)

If a container is stopped, killed or restarted while
`unsloth-llama-update` is swapping in the new llama.cpp, the old bundle
can be left at `/opt/unsloth/llama.cpp.old.<pid>` with nothing at
`/opt/unsloth/llama.cpp`. Studio then has no llama-server, and every
later run of the updater fails right away with a `mktemp` error, so the
only way back was to move the folder by hand or pull a new image.

The updater now puts a bundle a killed run left aside back in place
before it starts, then updates as usual. If the download fails, the
previous llama.cpp is still back and working. If the folder is missing
with nothing to restore, it installs a fresh bundle instead of failing.
Normal updates, `--check` and volume-mounted installs behave the same as
before.

Studio: keep a chat's summary when forking it (#19627) Forking a chat that was compacted with /compact gave the fork none of the parent's saved summary. With auto-compact off, the parent kept sending its summary plus the recent turns, but the fork sent the whole history again, so the next message in the fork failed with the provider's context length error. With auto-compact on, the fork first hit that error and then wrote a second summary of the same turns. A fork now carries the parent's saved summaries along with its messages. A summary only applies when the turns it covers are the start of the fork's own history, so a fork taken before the compacted point, or one that goes a different way, still sends its own turns as before. Deleting the parent leaves the fork's copy in place. ## Screenshots | Before (main) | After (this PR) | |---|---| | | |

Studio: let Deep Research try a failed page fetch again (#19538)

When a Deep Research run failed to read a page (a timeout, a 5xx from
the site, a page that came back unreadable), that page was never tried
again. The URL was marked as read before the fetch ran, so the page
linked in the question was skipped from then on and a later decision to
read it again was swapped for a seed search. A single hiccup on the page
the question was about left it out of the report.

A page that fails to load now gets one more try: the linked page is
fetched again on the next step, and the model may pick it again. A page
that fails twice is left alone, so a dead link costs at most one extra
step.
