Windows AMSI/Defender CI: actually ask AMSI, and turn the runner's Defender back on (#19680)

## Windows AMSI/Defender CI: actually ask AMSI, and turn the runner's
Defender back on

`windows-amsi-defender-differential-ci.yml` has never produced an AMSI
verdict. Every run reports "the AMSI positive control did NOT fire ...
COULD NOT MEASURE", and the Defender half reports "LOCAL SIGNATURES
ONLY". Two separate causes, plus one false negative in the cloud check.

### Causes

1. **The probe never reached AMSI.** `Probe-AmsiParse.ps1` called
`[scriptblock]::Create`, which only parses. PowerShell hands a script
block to AMSI when it is first invoked, so the control could not fire
even where AMSI is live. On `windows-11-arm`, where Defender is on, a
command containing the AMSI test sample is refused with
`ScriptContainedMaliciousContent`, while the old probe reported the same
sample as "compiled".
2. **The Windows Server image turns Defender off.**
`actions/runner-images` (`Configure-WindowsDefender.ps1`) disables
real-time protection, script scanning, behaviour monitoring, IOAV and
MAPS, and excludes `C:\` and `D:\`. Server runners have no Tamper
Protection, so those settings can be turned back on inside the job. On
the Windows 11 ARM images Tamper Protection keeps real-time protection
on, but MAPS cannot be enabled there.
3. **The cloud check misread success.** A successful `MpCmdRun
-ValidateMapsConnection` prints the legend `(... other - failure)`,
which matched the old `-notmatch 'fail'` test.

### Change

- `Probe-AmsiParse.ps1`: after parsing, invoke a wrapper that only
defines a function holding the text. AMSI scans every byte and none of
the script's statements run. Docstring corrected.
- Workflow: a first step removes the image's `C:\`/`D:\` exclusions and
turns real-time protection, script scanning, behaviour monitoring, IOAV
and MAPS back on, with `SubmitSamplesConsent=2` so files are never
submitted. The existing per-directory exemption still keeps a detection
from being quarantined before it is measured.
- Workflow: the MAPS check succeeds on exit 0 without the literal
`ValidateMapsConnection failed`.

### Evidence (staging, `windows-latest`, only this workflow in the tree)

| | Before (main) | After (this PR, run 45746669259) |
|---|---|---|
| AMSI control (Microsoft test sample) | did not fire, "COULD NOT
MEASURE" | BLOCKED in all 6 probe processes |
| AMSI on `install.ps1`, `studio/setup.ps1`, `scripts/uninstall.ps1` |
not measured | accepted by a live provider, base and head |
| EICAR file-scan control | fires | fires |
| Cloud-delivered protection | "NOT available" | reachable, connection
validated |
| Defender verdict | clean by local signatures only | clean with cloud
protection reachable |

Runner state was probed separately: `windows-latest` (Server 2025)
starts with real-time protection off, script scanning off, MAPS 0 and
`C:\;D:\` excluded; `windows-11-arm` and `windows-11-vs2026-arm` start
with real-time protection and Tamper Protection on.

### Tests

- `tests/security/test_amsi_parse_probe.py`,
`tests/security/test_lint_av_shapes.py`: 63 passed.
- `scripts/lint_av_shapes.py`: 0 new errors (one new warning for the
probe's own `[scriptblock]::Create`, which is the measurement).
`scripts/lint_workflow_triggers.py` clean.

### Not covered

- The job now runs with real-time protection on, so it may take a little
longer.
- AMSI on PowerShell 7 is not part of this workflow, as before.
- One vendor's verdict, as before; this says nothing about other AV
products.

Read a WoA companion wheel's METADATA through ZipFile instead of ranged reads (#19979)

## Installer (Windows on ARM): read a companion wheel's METADATA through
ZipFile, not hand-rolled ranged reads

`install.ps1` on main is flagged on VirusTotal by Skyhigh as
`BehavesLike.PS.Suspicious.jr` (1/61) since #19952. The parent commit is
clean. Supersedes #19967.

### Cause

#19952 added a reader for a torchvision wheel's own `METADATA`. It uses:
- `Invoke-WoaHttpBytes`: raw `System.Net.WebRequest` byte ranges into a
`MemoryStream` loop;
- a hand-written zip parser: end-of-central-directory search, central
directory, local header, hex magic numbers, bit shifts;
- manual `DeflateStream` inflation.

The detection is a score over that block, not one string:
- Swapping the bit shifts for multiplication (#19967) cleared it.
- It came back once the comments were made ASCII-only (#19976).
- Decimal constants did not help.

### Change

In `install.ps1` and its parity copy in `studio/setup.ps1`:
- `Invoke-WoaHttpBytes` is removed; nothing else used it.
- When the index advertises PEP 658 metadata, `<wheel>.metadata` is
fetched with `Invoke-WebRequest -UseBasicParsing -OutFile` (20 s, 1 MB
cap). As before, the wheel is the fallback.
- Otherwise the wheel is downloaded to a temp file (120 s) and
`*.dist-info/METADATA` is read through
`[System.IO.Compression.ZipFile]::OpenRead`, the same API `install.ps1`
already uses near line 290. A `try/finally` disposes the zip and deletes
the temp file.
- `Get-WoaWheelTorchRequirement` keeps its contract, its memo cache, and
"" on any failure. That "" falls back to the offset rule, as before.

Cost: the NVIDIA index (`pypi.nvidia.com/nvtorch_oot`) serves no
`.metadata`, so a stable companion is now downloaded whole, about 6.5 MB
for torchvision win_arm64. That happens only for candidates sharing
torch's local tag, next to a multi-GB torch install.

`tests/studio/test_installer_av_shapes.py` banned any `Add-Type` text in
`studio/setup.ps1`. The setup copy needs `Add-Type -AssemblyName
System.IO.Compression.FileSystem` on PowerShell 5.1. That only loads a
framework assembly and never runs csc.exe, so the assert now uses the
same "no `Add-Type` except `-AssemblyName`" rule the file already
applies to every script. The `StudioVTNative` ban is unchanged.

### Evidence (VirusTotal, fresh uploads)

| File | Detections |
|---|---|
| main `install.ps1` | 1 / 61, Skyhigh |
| this PR `install.ps1` / `studio/setup.ps1` | 0 / 61 / 0 / 61 |
| this PR merged with #19976 (ASCII-only), `install.ps1` /
`studio/setup.ps1` | 0 / 61 / 0 / 61 (the merged tree hashes `3e3fde2c`
/ `c6ee35b1`, the files scanned) |

### Tests

- `tests/studio/install/test_woa_companion_metadata_pairing.py`: 38
passed (PowerShell functions under pwsh, network mocked by copying
fixture files to `-OutFile`).
  - The two range-specific cases are removed.
  - Added cases:
    - a wheel downloaded and read;
    - a wheel without METADATA reads as "";
    - a non-zip file reads as "";
    - advertised but missing `.metadata` falls back to the wheel;
    - temp files deleted.
- The full probe decisions are unchanged: stable, cu134 driver, nightly,
stable over nightly, walk-back, setup repair and parity.
- `tests/studio/test_installer_av_shapes.py`: 254 passed, 1 skipped.
- `scripts/lint_av_shapes.py`: 0 new errors.
`scripts/lint_exec_literals.py`: all recorded. Pre-commit clean.

### Not covered

- Not run on Windows on ARM or under Windows PowerShell 5.1; the tests
run under pwsh 7 on Linux.
- No test reaches the real NVIDIA index.

## Problem


`tests/utils/test_dataset_num_proc.py::test_the_two_copies_have_not_drifted`
fails on every `Core` leg, for example on the #19837 and #19781 staging
runs on current main:

```
AssertionError: unsloth/dataset_num_proc.py and unsloth_zoo/dataset_num_proc.py have diverged; the zoo copy is the source of truth
```

unsloth-zoo #2909 taught `unsloth_zoo/dataset_num_proc.py` to keep
`Dataset.map` in-process while `offload_layers` holds model layers
page-locked in host RAM. Linux copies that memory into every forked
worker at fork time, and a 120 GB host tier with 6 workers stalled the

Port the same `_offload_reason()` into `unsloth/dataset_num_proc.py` and
return it from `_workers_unusable_reason()`, matching the zoo code
exactly. Like the zoo version, it reads
`unsloth_zoo.block_swap.offload_active` only if that module is already
loaded, so nothing new is imported.

Keep the PowerShell installers ASCII-only so their signature verifies on every locale (#19976)

## Keep the PowerShell installers ASCII-only so install.ps1's signature
verifies in every locale

Addresses the HashMismatch half of #19908.

### Cause

The Desktop release signs the bundled `install.ps1`
(`release-desktop.yml`, "Sign the bundled install script"). The file has
no BOM, and Windows reads a BOM-less script in the machine's ANSI code
page. That applies when PowerShell 5.1 runs it and when Authenticode
hashes it.

- **Reported file:** I extracted `install.ps1` from the v0.1.925-beta
x64 installer. Its sha256 is `3eee5a81...`, matching the report, and its
first 663,907 bytes are the repo file.
- **What was signed:** the signed digest (`SpcIndirectData`, PowerShell
SIP) is SHA-256 of the script decoded as **Windows-1252** and re-encoded
as UTF-16LE. It is not the UTF-8 or Windows-1251 decoding.
- **Reproduced on staging:** I signed main's `install.ps1` with a
throwaway certificate on `windows-latest` (ACP 1252). The digest again
matches the Windows-1252 decoding.
- `install.ps1` contains 202 non-ASCII bytes (`─`, `→`, `ß`, an em
dash), all in comments. On any machine whose ANSI code page is not 1252
(Cyrillic, CJK, Central European, the UTF-8 locale option) those bytes
decode to different text. The hash then differs and the signature
reports HashMismatch. The release's own "Valid" check runs on a 1252
runner, so it cannot see this.

### Change

- In `install.ps1`, `studio/setup.ps1` and `scripts/uninstall.ps1`: `─`
to `-`, `→` to `->`, the em dash to `-`, `(ß)` to `(the German sharp
s)`. Comments only: with comments removed, the PowerShell token stream
of each file is identical to main. 0 parse errors.
- The tests and `scripts/sync_shared_ps1_helpers.py` that locate
sections by those headings now use the ASCII headings, including the
`BEGIN/END SHARED WITH studio/setup.ps1` markers.
- New `tests/studio/install/test_ps1_scripts_are_ascii.py` fails on any
non-ASCII byte in the three scripts. Main's `install.ps1` fails it at
line 175, as a negative control.

A UTF-8 BOM added at signing time would also fix the hash. ASCII-only
fixes it without touching the release workflow. It also stops PowerShell
5.1 from running these comments as gibberish on non-1252 systems.

### Tests

- Every test file that reads one of the three scripts (117 files):
11,610 passed, 163 skipped. The 5 failures were regexes in
`tests/python/test_windows_xformers_installer.py` that still matched the
old heading, now updated. That file plus the new test: 45 passed.
- Pre-commit clean.

### VirusTotal

- `studio/setup.ps1`: 0 / 61.
- `scripts/uninstall.ps1`: 0 / 61.
- `install.ps1`: 1 / 61, Skyhigh `BehavesLike.PS.Suspicious.jr`. This is
not from this PR: main's `install.ps1` has the same detection since
#19952. It is being fixed separately by replacing the hand-written wheel
zip reader #19952 added.

### Not covered

Studio: recognize raw text columns in streams without feature schemas (#16122)

## Problem

Studio recognizes a single string column such as `body` or `content` as
raw training text, but preparation rejects that same dataset when its
streaming loader has not populated `features`.

This occurs with the Studio-pinned `datasets==4.3.0` and the supported
`3.4.1` floor: loading a local JSONL with `streaming=True` leaves
`features=None`. `is_plain_text_dataset` returns `True`, then
`prepare_raw_text_dataset` raises `Raw text training requires a string
'text' column but none was found ... (columns: ['body'])`. The same rows
load and prepare normally without streaming. With datasets 4.8.5, the
JSON loader supplies the schema and this particular load already
succeeds.

This is a gap in the arbitrary text-column handling from #15899 and
#12790, not a new dataset format or a change to pre-tokenized input
validation.

## Change

When feature metadata is absent, identify string columns from at most
the first 100 rows, the same prefix length already used to choose
between candidate text columns. A candidate must contain a string and no
non-null non-string values in that prefix. Then use the existing rename,
column selection, explicit eval-column override, blank filtering and EOS
append logic.

Declared feature metadata remains authoritative. Datasets already
containing `text` do not use the new probe. Numeric-only columns are not
coerced to text, and training re-iterates the source rather than losing
sampled rows. This does not scan an entire stream or claim to infer
columns whose first string only appears after the sampled prefix.

## Validation

Real production imports and Hugging Face datasets; no replacement
production modules or model downloads:

```sh
HF_HOME=/tmp/unsloth-offline-test-cache \
HF_HUB_OFFLINE=1 TRANSFORMERS_OFFLINE=1 \
python -m pytest \
  studio/backend/tests/test_raw_text_column_choice.py \
  studio/backend/tests/test_raw_text_blank_rows.py \
  studio/backend/tests/test_raw_text_batched_parity.py \
  studio/backend/tests/test_plain_text_dataset.py -q
```

- On datasets 4.3.0, original production code plus the final tests: **6
failed, 40 passed**. With this change: **46 passed**.
- On datasets 4.8.5: **46 passed**.
- New cases cover `body`/`content`/`passage`, null and blank prefixes,
EOS append, multi-column selection, explicit eval selection, bounded
probing, numeric rejection, and a real streamed JSONL load.
- Ruff 0.16.10, the project's pinned ruff-unsloth formatter, and `git
diff --check` pass for both changed files.

The full repository suite and GPU/model training were not run. This
validates dataset preparation, not a model-quality or throughput claim.

AI assistance was used for investigation, implementation and testing.

Studio MLX: count spliced image columns before VLM generation (#19911)

> **Depends on #19909.** This branch is stacked on it and includes its
commit (`fix(studio): count spliced media columns in MLX VLM chat
usage`) until #19909 merges. Only the top commit belongs to this PR.

## Problem

Some MLX VLMs splice an image's features in place of a single
placeholder id. FastVLM (`llava_qwen2`) does this: the processor emits
about 30 ids for an image prompt, but the model embeds 285 columns.
#19909 fixes the usage reported after generation. The counts taken
before generation still used processor ids:

- `count_chat_tokens`
- `image_tokens` (the computer-use screenshot cost)
- `_prompt_within_window` (the context-window guard)
- `_generation_limit` / `_media_generation_limit`

On a splicing model this has two effects. The window guard can admit an
image prompt that does not fit, and an unset generation limit is
computed from a prompt about 255 columns too small. The chat context bar
is unaffected, because the frontend never recounts media chats, but the
backend guards are.

## What changed

- **Truth source.** The width `get_input_embeddings` produces for the
prepared inputs is the ground truth. It is read off the unevaluated MLX
graph, so it costs about 2 ms on FastVLM, against 96 ms for evaluating
the embedding.
- **Measured once per load.** Some families run their vision tower even
while the graph is only being built (Qwen3-VL-30B: about 97 ms). So the
width is not probed on every request for every model. Instead,
`load_model` measures once, on a blank image, whether the model splices
(`_media_splices`). This costs 6–122 ms per load.
- **Splicing models.**
  - `_count_media_prompt_tokens` returns the embedded width.
- The width is used even when it is below the id count, because FastVLM
truncates its embedding at `tokenizer_model_max_length` and the width is
what is actually fed.
- `_generation_limit` prepares the media and counts the columns even
without a KV context budget.
- **Processor-expanding models are unchanged.** They never build the
embedding again after load. They also keep the existing rule that
unbudgeted generation never prepares media
(`test_media_is_prepared_only_under_a_budget_and_only_once`).
- **Dead Metal queue.** A dead Metal queue (`is_metal_queue_dead`)
raised while counting is no longer swallowed by the count path's broad
`except`. This covers the load-time probe, `prepare_inputs` (some
processors evaluate on the GPU), the generation limit, the budget check
and the window guard. Such an error now propagates, as it already does
from the load warm-up, so the orchestrator still retires the worker.

## Not changed

- A caller-supplied `prompt_ids` with images still uses
`len(prompt_ids)`.
- Distributed loads skip the measurement and keep id counts.
- On an unbudgeted load, the window guard for processor-expanding models
still counts placeholder text without preparing media. This is the
existing behaviour for every family.
- Only images are probed. No known model splices audio or video.

## Validation

Unit tests:

```text
studio/backend/tests/test_mlx_inference_backend.py: 591 passed
```

The new tests are:

- `test_pre_generation_counts_take_the_columns_a_spliced_image_fills`
(spliced and unspliced, with and without a budget)
-
`test_a_spliced_count_is_the_embedding_even_truncated_and_a_dead_queue_fails_the_load`
- `test_a_vision_load_records_whether_the_model_splices_images`

Each guarantee was mutation-checked by reverting or weakening the
production line it covers, and all 15 mutants are caught by the named
test. The mutants covered:

- the column count;
- the measurement;
- the stale flag across loads;
- unbudgeted media preparation, for splicing and for expanding models;
- pixel forwarding;
- truncation;
- each dead-queue re-raise.

Real weights on Apple Silicon:

```text
FastVLM-0.5B-bf16 (splicing):
  _media_splices = True
  count_chat_tokens = 285   (was 30)   = columns fed (285) = reported usage (285)
  image_tokens(1280, 800) = 257
  served window 200: single, resident and batch image requests all refused
    ("286 tokens exceeds the 200-token context window")
  with a KV budget of 295: unset generation limit = 10

12 processor-expanding families (LFM2.5-VL, GLM-4.6V, Kimi-VL, Molmo2, DeepSeek-VL2,
Phi-3.5-vision, Qwen2.5-VL, Qwen3-VL-30B-A3B, SmolVLM, Gemma 4, Qwen3.5, Gemma 3n):
  _media_splices = False
  count_chat_tokens identical to before the change, and equal to columns fed and reported usage
```

Studio diffusion: Krea-2 block frees its norm outputs before attention and the feed-forward (#19935)

## Summary

Studio's eager Krea-2 block patch (`_krea2_block_forward` in
`diffusion_arch_patches.py`) binds the two norm outputs to names, then
passes them into `torch.addcmul`:

```python
norm1 = self.norm1(hidden_states)
attn_out = self.attn(torch.addcmul(preshift, norm1, 1 + prescale), ...)
...
norm2 = self.norm2(hidden_states)
ff_out = self.ff(torch.addcmul(postshift, norm2, 1 + postscale))
```

A named local stays alive until the function returns. So `norm1` (`[B,
S, D]`) is held through all of `self.attn`, and `norm2` through all of
`self.ff`. Stock diffusers inlines `self.norm1(hidden_states)` in the
expression, so the patch holds one more activation than the code it
replaces.

This PR inlines both norms into the `addcmul` calls. The ops, their
order and their dtypes do not change, so the output is bit-identical.
The out-of-place `addcmul` fusion stays as it is; nothing becomes
in-place.

## Evidence (CPU, eager, `torch.inference_mode`, bf16)

Setup:
- A tiny random `Krea2Transformer2DModel`: 3 layers, 4 heads x 32 dims,
intermediate 256, S = 32 text + 1024 image tokens.
- Peak live bytes come from the profiler's CPU allocation events, summed
in time order.
- 3 repeats per arm; the A/A spread was 0 bytes in every arm.

| Arm | Full forward vs main | Peak live bytes |
|---|---|---:|
| stock diffusers block | - | 84,176,640 |
| main patch | - | 84,446,976 |
| this PR | `torch.equal` = True | 84,176,640 |

- main minus this PR = 270,336 B, exactly one `[1, 1056, 128]` bf16
buffer.
- This PR's peak equals stock diffusers'.
- The patch differs from stock only by the existing `addcmul` rounding,
on main and on this PR alike.

## Estimate at full size

Krea-2 config (`krea/Krea-2-Turbo` `transformer/config.json`): hidden 48
x 128 = 6144, intermediate 16384. The Qwen-Image VAE (/8) with 2x2
packing gives 4096 image tokens at 1024x1024 and 16384 at 2048x2048.
Inside a block the peak is in the SwiGLU feed-forward or in attention,
and `norm2` or `norm1` is live in each of them. So the block peak drops
by one `[B, S, D]` bf16:

| Size | S (128 text tokens) | saved at B=1 | saved at B=8 |
|---|---:|---:|---:|
| 1024x1024 | 4224 | 49.5 MiB | 396 MiB |
| 2048x2048 | 16512 | 193.5 MiB | 1.5 GiB |

These are estimates from the shapes. I did not measure them on a GPU.
Under torch.compile the traced graph has the same ops in the same order,
so compiled runs are unchanged.

## Tests


`studio/backend/tests/test_diffusion_arch_patches.py::test_krea2_forward_is_bit_equal_to_named_norms_with_one_less_buffer_live`:
- A bf16 `Krea2TransformerBlock` runs the patched forward and the old
named-norm body.
- The outputs must be `torch.equal`.
- The profiled CPU peak must drop by exactly `hs.numel() *
hs.element_size()`.
- The test fails on main (peak delta 0) and passes here.

Suites: `test_diffusion_arch_patches.py` and the 11 `*krea*` test files.
- In the default workspace venv (diffusers 0.40.0.dev0 with
huggingface_hub 0.36.2), 46 tests fail with the same IDs on main and
here. Every one of them is `from diffusers.pipelines...` raising
`ImportError: get_cached_repo_tree`.
- In a venv where the pipeline imports (diffusers 0.42.1, torch 2.13
CPU): 206 passed, 3 failed, the same 3 IDs as on main.
`test_install_idempotent_and_reversible` installs 0 patches against
diffusers 0.42.1's changed block bodies, and the two
`test_diffusion_lora_krea2_fused_qkv` cases fail.
`test_krea2_forward_matches_stock` passes there.

## Device results

NVIDIA A100-SXM4-80GB (Colab), torch 2.14.1+cu130, diffusers 0.42.1,
transformers 5.17.0, unsloth_zoo 2026.11.8. Base is the merge base
`532afbed81` and head is `be774a6aab`, run on the same VM with a fresh
process per arm, base/head order alternating, 3 processes per arm.

Each process loads `unsloth/Krea-2-Turbo` through Studio in eager mode
with no compile; Studio auto-picked an int8 text encoder and everything
stays resident. Each process does a warmup render, then 2 timed renders
at 1024x1024 for each batch size: 8 steps, guidance 0, seed 42.

Peak is `torch.cuda.max_memory_allocated()`, reset at the first
transformer call of the render and read after the last one, so it covers
the denoise only. s/step comes from CUDA events over the transformer
calls.

| batch | peak during denoise, base (MiB) | head (MiB) | saved (MiB) |
saved per row (MiB) | s/step base (A/A spread) | s/step head (A/A
spread) | image |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | 29609.8 | 29510.8 | 99.0 | 99.0 | 0.5727 (0.0028) | 0.5727
(0.0018) | byte-identical |
| 2 | 30360.4 | 30160.4 | 200.0 | 100.0 | 1.1254 (0.0027) | 1.1264
(0.0015) | byte-identical (both images) |

- In both arms the patched `_krea2_block_forward` was installed on
`Krea2TransformerBlock`. Base has the named `norm1` / `norm2` locals and
head has them inline.
- Peaks repeat to within 2.25 MiB across processes.
- The saving is about 99 to 100 MiB per batch row, roughly twice the
estimated 49.5 MiB. Head's denoise peak matches the stock diffusers
block forward measured on the same card type (604.4 vs 603.4 MiB working
set at batch 1), so the change gives back what the named norms cost.
- s/step is unchanged: both deltas are inside the A/A spread.
- Images are byte-identical across all 6 processes: batch 1 sha256
`64d6300cf555f79c...`; batch 2 `700fdf1c2390c7b8...` and
`ee8492c687fa537c...`.

fix(studio): split Inkling 2's thought at effort none, honor enable_thinking false, keep literal think tags (#19859)

## Problem

At `reasoning_effort: "none"`, Inkling 2 (`Inkling-2-Mini`) still writes
a thought. Unsloth Studio returned that thought as raw
`<think>…</think>` inside `content`, and `reasoning_content` was empty.
The bug showed on both backends:

- **Safetensors/MLX.** The MLX normalizer rewrites Inkling's
special-token thought channel (`<|content_thinking|>…<|end_message|>`)
into textual `<think>`. The chat route's think gate
`_sf_parse_think_markers` turns parsing off at effort "none" for
`reasoning_effort`-style templates.
- **GGUF.** llama-server's Inkling parser returns the thought as
`reasoning_content` even at "none", and the backend wraps it in
`<think>`. The GGUF gates `_think_parsing_expected` /
`_responses_should_parse_think_markers` then leave it in `content`.

Two related problems turned up while fixing this:

- **`enable_thinking: false` didn't turn thinking off.** Inkling's
template reads only `reasoning_effort` (none..max maps to 0.0..0.99) and
ignores `enable_thinking`. So `enable_thinking: false` rendered the
template default, effort 0.9, on MLX/Transformers, and "low" (0.2) on
GGUF.
- **Literal tags in answers were read as reasoning.** Because the route
re-parses textual tags, a literal `<think>…</think>` in an Inkling
answer was moved into `reasoning_content`. For example, a regex that
strips such tags would lose them. This happens at every effort, on main
too.

## Changes

One commit per change:

1. **`fix(studio): split Inkling's thought at reasoning effort none`.**
`_sf_parse_think_markers` returns True when the rendering template
carries Inkling's thinking channel, checked with
`replays_reasoning_content(template=…)`.
2. **`fix(studio): keep the GGUF Inkling thought out of content at
effort none`.**
- A new helper, `_llama_inkling_channel`, checks the rendered GGUF
template. The chat and Anthropic GGUF gates parse the thought for
Inkling.
- The chat route's provenance ledger starts with `split=True` for
Inkling. llama-server's default reasoning format always extracts
Inkling's thought, so an inline `<think>` from Inkling on GGUF is never
a real thought.
- The Responses gate keeps its effort rule, because it re-reads chat
output without a ledger.
3. **`fix(studio): turn Inkling thinking off for enable_thinking
false`.** When the rendering template carries Inkling's channel and
never reads `enable_thinking`, and no effort was sent, `enable_thinking:
false` becomes `reasoning_effort: "none"`.
- On MLX/Transformers this happens per render attempt inside
`apply_chat_template_for_generation`, so token counting and generation
render the same prompt. The swap replaces the keyword rather than adding
to it, so a processor that rejects `enable_thinking` still gets the
effort. The injected effort is fitted to the attempt's own allowlist.
- On GGUF, `_thinking_off_effort` covers both the request and the launch
default.
- Other effort templates are unchanged: gpt-oss still gets "low", and
Mistral Small 4 already got "none".
4. **`fix(studio): keep literal think tags in Inkling answers on MLX`.**
- `InklingMessageNormalizer` records the offset and body length of each
`<think>` it writes.
- MLX snapshots carry these spans as a `str` subclass, `ThoughtSpans`.
It survives the worker queue's pickling, so the worker and orchestrator
need no change.
- The chat route mirrors the spans into the extractor's existing
`think_provenance` ledger, the same mechanism GGUF uses. Only the
channel's thought becomes reasoning; any other tag stays text. This
covers streaming and non-streaming chat, including batched `n>1`
choices.
- A turn with a textual prefill emits no spans and keeps the previous
tag parsing, because the prefill is text that no span covers.

## Risks and tradeoffs

- **Inkling detection.** It relies on the template carrying Inkling's
channel tokens, which is how the codebase already identifies Inkling.
- **Paths that still parse tags.** The server tool loop, the tool-call
nudge retry, the Responses stream adapter and the Transformers backend
keep today's tag parsing. A literal `<think>` in an Inkling answer is
still read as reasoning there, as on main. The tool loop rewrites text
at many yields and would need its own offset bookkeeping.
- **Later thoughts.** The normalizer turns only an Inkling reply's first
thought into `<think>`; later thoughts already show as text. With spans,
literal tags inside that later text now stay text.

## Validation

Route-level tests (JSON and SSE) were added for each change. Each test
was checked by reverting or weakening the production change it covers
and confirming that the test fails.

```bash
cd studio/backend
python -m pytest -q tests/test_inkling2_transformers_reasoning.py tests/test_safetensors_reasoning_stream.py \
  tests/test_orchestrator_unload_cancel.py tests/test_mlx_inference_backend.py \
  tests/test_gguf_chat_literal_think_tags.py tests/test_reasoning_effort_allowlist.py tests/test_anthropic_messages.py
```

Real `mlx-community/Inkling-2-Mini-oQ4e-mtp` on MLX (mlx-vlm 0.8.1),
through the REST API:

- **Effort "none".** The thought lands in `reasoning_content`. Checked
for:
  - chat JSON and SSE;
  - an image prompt;
  - the server tool loop;
  - `/v1/responses` and `/v1/messages`;
  - and effort "high" for comparison.
- **`enable_thinking: false`.** It renders the same 44-token prompt and
the same reply as effort "none"; "high" renders 46 tokens.
- **Literal tags.** A prompt asking for a Python line containing
`<think>.*?</think>` keeps the line verbatim in `content`, with the
thought in `reasoning_content`. Checked at none and high, in JSON and
SSE.

Studio: count an MLX chat of instructions alone, and refuse a speech model's count by name (#19910)

## Problem

On an MLX load, `/api/inference/chat/count_tokens` had two refusals in
its MLX-only path that were wrong for the request they refused.

**A chat of instructions alone could not be counted on some templates.**
Before the first message, the chat's context bar recounts the chat,
which is then only the system prompt, the date line and the tool
schemas. Qwen3.5's chat template raises `No user query found in
messages.` (or `No messages provided.`) when there is no user turn. The
count fell into the generic `Unable to count tokens with the loaded
model tokenizer.` 503, so on Qwen3.5 the context bar showed "–" until
the first message was sent. Generation and llama-server fail on the same
prompt, because the template itself rejects it. Templates that do render
it (Qwen3) priced the bare instructions, which is also not a prompt any
request sends: the completion refuses a chat with no non-system message
(`At least one non-system message is required.`).

**A speech or transcription load answered a count with "No GGUF model
loaded".** `_mlx_count_chat_tokens` returned `None` for `is_audio`
entries (TTS and Whisper; `audio_vlm` models keep the flag off). The
endpoint then reported `No GGUF model loaded. Load a GGUF model first.`
with a `not_loaded` problem code, although a model is loaded.

## Change

- In `_mlx_count_chat_tokens`, a render whose conversation has no
non-system message gets one empty user turn appended. That is the prompt
the next send renders, without the user's text.
- It is decided per render, so the total and no-tools renders of a
breakdown price the same conversation. The history-only part has no
history to price and stays 0, as before.
- Chats with any non-system turn, assistant-only included, render
exactly as before. A template that cannot render such a chat still
refuses, as generation would.
- `is_audio` loads now get a 503 naming the reason: `Token counting is
not available for speech or transcription models.`

The other MLX-path refusals are unchanged, and are correct as guards:
- MCP tools not yet discovered: a count must not spawn the servers, and
pricing without their schemas would undercount.
- A pending turn that would retrieve documents: the retrieved text is
unknown before the run.
- An empty prompt: nothing to price.
- The generation-in-progress re-check: the count needs the orchestrator
lock, and a count taken mid-run is stale.

## Tradeoffs

- Templates that already rendered an instructions-only chat (Qwen3) now
count it a few tokens higher: the empty user turn's framing. The new
figure is what the first send costs besides the typed text.
- `/v1/messages/count_tokens` delegates to the same count on MLX, so a
request with `messages: []` follows the same rule: on Qwen3 it rises by
the same framing, and on Qwen3.5 it returns a count instead of a 503.
`/v1/messages` refuses that request for generation, so no generated
prompt exists to disagree with.
- GGUF counting, the media refusals and the frontend are unchanged.

## Validation

Live on an isolated Unsloth Studio server: the count of each chat is
compared with the `prompt_tokens` that generation reports. For
instructions-only chats, generation was sent the same chat plus an empty
user message.

```text
                           Qwen3.5-0.8B (MLX)       Qwen3-0.6B (MLX)
                           count  / generation      count / generation
system only                 40   /  40               35   /  35
tools only                 574   / 574              449   / 449
system + tools             581   / 581              455   / 455
empty (date line only)      33   /  33               29   /  29
assistant only, as sent    both fail (template)     42   /  42
user "hi" (control)         41   /  41               36   /  36
```

In the web UI with Qwen3.5 loaded and Unsloth Studio's default tools on,
an empty chat's recount returned 1984 tokens (bar `2.0k / 8.2k`,
previously "–"). The first message's own payload counts 1985 tokens, the
difference being the `hi` token.

```bash
cd studio/backend
python -m pytest tests/test_mlx_inference_backend.py -q -k "mlx_count or speech_load or mlx_breakdown"
python -m pytest tests/test_managed_engines.py tests/test_mcp_images.py tests/test_openai_tool_passthrough.py tests/test_anthropic_messages.py -q -k "count or breakdown"
```

The new tests cover:
- instructions-only chats on a template that refuses them and on one
that renders them;
- assistant-only chats priced as sent, or refused where the template
cannot render them;
- the breakdown pricing the same conversation in every part;
- a failing count not being retried on another conversation;
- the audio-model refusal.

Each was mutation-checked: removing or narrowing the behaviour it guards
makes it fail.


## Follow-up commit (maintainer)

The same two refusals had wider reach than the MLX path:

- **Any resident model the count cannot serve is named, not reported as
unloaded.** A transformers load (the CUDA safetensors path, whose worker
declines counts) also fell through to `No GGUF model loaded. Load a GGUF
model first.` with the `not_loaded` problem code, which the MCP hint
turns into "load a model". It now gets `Token counting is not available
on the transformers backend.` Speech and transcription loads get the
speech message on either backend. With nothing resident the endpoint
still answers `not_loaded`.
- **GGUF: instructions a template will not render alone are priced
behind an empty user turn.** The existing retry covered only an empty
chat or a lone assistant turn. The stock Qwen3.5 template (`No user
query found in messages.`) also refuses a system-only chat, so on such a
GGUF the context bar showed "-" before the first message. The retry now
inserts the empty user turn after the leading instructions, and only
after the template refuses, so a template that renders the chat
(Unsloth's Qwen3.5, Qwen3, ...) is counted exactly as before. The
per-load "empty chat refused" memo is not applied to instruction-only
chats.

Studio: round the decision warmup ratio up like transformers (#17231)

Decision training turned the warmup ratio into steps with `round()` in
`studio/backend/core/training/decision_trainer.py`. `round()` takes
anything below .5 down and .5 to the nearest even number, while
transformers' `get_warmup_steps` rounds up with `math.ceil`. So a small
ratio could give no warmup at all.

Decision training vs transformers: warmup for 0.05 at 10 steps is 0 vs
1, for 0.1 at 25 steps 2 vs 3, and for 0.15 at 30 steps 4 vs 5.

This is the fix from #16827, applied to decision training: `math.ceil`
on that line, so it matches transformers, the MLX schedule and
`multi_lora_trainer.py`. An explicit `warmup_steps` still wins. The
Studio UI already sends `warmup_steps`, so this shows up when
`warmup_ratio` is sent directly, through the training API or the MCP
training tool.

`tests/test_decision_dataset_prefetch.py` drives `_run` with the
existing fake runtime up to `TrainingArguments` and checks
`warmup_steps` for the same five cases as the MLX test. 5 failed before
(`assert 0 == 1`, `0 == 1`, `2 == 3`, `4 == 5`, `4 == 5`), passes after.

Studio: let a resident MLX batch reply carry a video clip (#19913)

## Problem

On the MLX backend a lone chat reply decodes through the resident batch,
but `resident_unavailable_reason` refused any reply that carries a video
clip ("a reply carries a video clip"). Every clip therefore fell back to
the one-at-a-time decode, although the multi-reply batch path already
accepts clips (`_video_batch_gap`, unsloth-zoo
`GenerationRequest.videos`) and reports exact usage for them.

## What changed

- **Resident gate.** `resident_unavailable_reason` now applies the same
clip checks as the multi-reply batch (`_video_batch_gap`) instead of
refusing every clip. Whether a clip fits the open batch is still decided
once its frames are decoded: unsloth-zoo's `BatchStream.add` prepares
the row and raises `BatchRowRefused` when it prepares unlike the batch's
other rows, `_VisionBatchSession.admit` turns that into `RowRefused`,
and the worker holds the reply and decodes it alone once the batch
drains (or on the single path at once when nothing else is in flight).
- **A clip's row cache.** A clip's row now gets its own
`VLMBatchRowCache` wherever other rows get one
(`_vlm_batch_row_cache(..., has_video=True)`), but without the snapshot
store: the store is keyed by token ids, which do not vary with the clip,
so a clip's row must neither resume nor bank by them. It prefills cold
on the load's prepared cache layout, so it keeps the load's KV window
(for example `RotatingKVCache(8192)` on Qwen2.5-VL) and shares the
layout of the other rows.
- **KV window.** mlx-vlm's own batch cache ignores `max_kv_size`, so on
a load with a KV window a clip whose row would get no row cache
(snapshot store off and no KV quantization, a zoo that cannot resume
rows, or a diffusion load) stays on the single path, which bounds its
cache at the window. The rule for "this load's rows get a row cache" is
now one helper, `_vlm_row_cache_available()`, shared with
`_vlm_batch_row_cache`.
- **Quantized KV cache.** `_video_batch_gap` now keeps clips out of any
batch on a load that quantizes its KV cache, not only a speculative one.
On the fixed multi-reply path a non-speculative quantized load was
already refused by `_kv_policy_batch_reason`, so only the message
changes there.
- **Temporary clip files.** A row's clip files are removed as soon as
`stream.add` returns or raises (unsloth-zoo decodes the frames inside
`add`), instead of living until the resident batch closes, where a
long-lived batch would accumulate them.

## Risks and tradeoffs

- A clip that does not fit the open batch has its frames decoded twice:
once on admission, where the fit is decided, and again when it decodes
alone.
- Two existing behaviors of the batch paths now also apply to resident
clip replies, as they already do to resident text and image replies.
Once a single reply grows past the KV window, mlx-vlm's
`BatchRotatingKVCache` evicts from the first token, where the single
path's `RotatingKVCache(keep=4)` keeps four. Rows with no row cache of
their own get mlx-vlm's unbounded batch cache. Neither is changed here.

## Validation

Usage of a resident clip reply against the columns the model embeds,
with one clip, greedy, 24 new tokens, on unsloth-zoo `main`. In every
case the reply text is identical to the single path's:

| Model | Embedded columns | Resident prompt tokens |
|---|---|---|
| Qwen3.5-0.8B-bf16 | 193 | 193 |
| Qwen2.5-VL-3B-Instruct-4bit | 224 | 224 |
| Qwen3-VL-30B-A3B-Instruct-3bit | 189 | 189 |
| gemma-4-e2b-it-4bit (speculative) | 301 | 301 |

Text and image resident replies are unchanged on all four models.

Through the worker's `_ResidentBatch` at width 2:

- On Qwen3.5, a clip next to a text or image row (and a text row next to
a clip) is refused once its frames are prepared, with zoo's signature
reason. The open row finishes, and the refused one decodes alone with
exact usage.
- On gemma-4 (speculative batch), the clip joins the other row and both
report exact usage.
- With the snapshot store off (`prompt_cache_mib=0`), Qwen2.5-VL (window
8192) keeps the clip off the resident batch, and it completes on the
single path with 224 prompt tokens. Qwen3.5 (no window) admits it.

its input latents through every denoising step, so any change in the
encoder's rounding moves the render:

- `diffusion_vae_single_frame.install()` gives the VAE a 2D path for
one-frame, uncached causal convolutions. It patched both `_decode` and
`_encode`. The 2D form is exact in exact arithmetic, but rounds
differently in bf16. With the encoder folded, Qwen-Image-Edit renders
moved by up to 0.037 LPIPS against an otherwise bit-identical rerun, to
save about 14 ms (768x768) to 38 ms (1024x1024) per input image.

fix(studio): count spliced media columns in MLX VLM chat usage (#19909)

## Problem

Unsloth Studio's chat context bar on an MLX VLM load showed far too
little context for image chats on models that splice vision features in
place of one placeholder id. FastVLM (`llava_qwen2`) is the example: one
`<image>` id becomes about 256 embedding columns. The single-path reply
(`_generate_vlm`, used when a reply cannot join the resident batch)
reported mlx-vlm's `prompt_tokens`, which counts input ids. An image
turn therefore reported 27 prompt tokens while 282 were fed and the KV
cache ended at 291. The prompt-processing rate was also computed from
the smaller count.

## Root cause

mlx-vlm's `stream_generate` reports the length of the processor's
`input_ids`, not the width of the `inputs_embeds` the model's
`get_input_embeddings` builds. The two differ only for models that
splice.

## Changes

- `_spliced_columns(model)`: a context manager that wraps
`model.get_input_embeddings` for one generation. It records how many
columns the widest prompt embedding filled past its ids. The widest call
is the full prompt; later decode calls embed single tokens. On exit it
restores the model's own attribute, or removes the wrapper if the method
came from the class. Models without `get_input_embeddings` are left
alone.
- `_generate_vlm` adds those columns to the reported prompt tokens. It
recomputes the prompt rate over the tokens actually prefilled,
consistent with how cache hits and produced-token time were already
folded in.

The resident and batched paths are fixed in the companion unsloth-zoo
change: unslothai/unsloth-zoo#2883. This PR works on its own for the
single path.

## Risks

- For models that do not splice, the recorded difference is 0 and
nothing changes.
- A warm single-path prompt-cache hit on a splicing model reports what
the cached resume actually fed. That resume path has a separate,
pre-existing alignment issue for splicing models, addressed in its own
PR.
- Pre-generation counts (`count_chat_tokens` and the window guards) are
not changed here. They are covered by a follow-up PR built on this one.

## Validation

```text
studio/backend/tests/test_mlx_inference_backend.py -k vlm: 111 passed
```

- The new test is
`test_mlx_vlm_usage_counts_the_columns_an_image_was_spliced_into[0,255]`.
It uses partial-prompt, full-prompt and decode embedding calls with
different expansions, and checks the prompt count, the rate, and that
the model's embedding method is restored. Each production line was
mutation-checked: dropping the add, the rate recompute, the widest-call
selection or the restore each fails the test.
- Real models on Apple Silicon:
- FastVLM-0.5B on the single path reports 282 prompt tokens, equal to
the embedding columns, with KV 291 = 282 + 9 completion. Before this
change it reported 27.
- A sweep of 15 VLM families shows prompt usage equal to the embedded
columns for image, video and audio input, on the single, resident and
batch paths, including MTP, DFlash and n-gram speculative loads. The
families are GLM-4.6V, Kimi-VL, LFM2.5-VL, Molmo2, Phi-3.5-vision,
SmolVLM, DeepSeek-VL2, Qwen2.5-VL, Qwen3-VL, Qwen3.5, Gemma 3n, Gemma 4
and FastVLM.

Studio RAG: re-embed with one stale-document scan and one vector-row scan per scope (#19891)

## Problem

A re-embed job (every embedding model switch, every Re-embed click,
every connection server change) did two scans per document, each over a
whole table, so a job over N stale documents cost O(N^2):

1. `reembed._run` called `_stale_documents` before every document. That
query reads every `documents` row with three correlated subqueries and a
sort. Archived conversation turns count as documents, so N grows with
chat history.
2. `store.replace_document_vectors` found the document's old vectors
with `SELECT rowid FROM chunks_vec WHERE scope=? AND chunk_id > ? AND
chunk_id < ?`. vec0 does not index `chunk_id`, so this reads every
vector row in the scope, for every document.

With the first fixed, the second was about 70% of the job's time.

## Change

`reembed.py`:

- The job takes the ordered stale snapshot once and keeps the ids in a
queue. Before each document it re-reads only the next id with the same
predicate plus `d.id=?` (`_stale_document`) and the same failed /
refused filter.
- The full query still runs when the embedding identity changes, when
the queue runs out (documents that went stale meanwhile are picked up;
the job only completes after a full scan finds nothing), and at most
once per second otherwise (`_RESCAN_SECONDS`).
- One `chunks_vec` partition scan per scope and job
(`store.vec_rowids_by_document`) maps each document to its vector
rowids.

`store.replace_document_vectors`:

- New optional `known_rowids`. Under the write lock the rowids are used
only if every one is present, in the document's scope, and they hold
exactly the document's chunk ids; otherwise it falls back to the
partition scan. After a swap the map takes the new rowids, so a model
switch mid-job stays linear.
- A document whose verified stale identity carries the
`vectors-dropped:` prefix has no rows to delete: `ensure_vec` sets the
prefix only when it drops the table, and it is cleared in the same
transaction that writes the document's vectors into the current table.
The lookup is skipped.

Unchanged: processing order, retired-scope and linked-folder guards, the
swap guard, refusal and redo, the failure streak, the download-required
stop, cancellation and retirement, the automatic-job identity stop,
final counts. Between full scans `remaining` counts the queued snapshot,
so it can lag the database by up to one second, and a document that went
stale mid-job and sorts ahead of the queue waits for the next scan.

## Results

Colab CPU High-RAM VM (8 vCPU, load under 1.5), stub encoder, one
knowledge base scope, one chunk per document. Base is the merge base
`84fe850`; "PR v1" is the first commit of this PR (stale scan only);
"PR" is the head. Arms interleaved in rotating order, median of 3
rounds, spread under 3% in every cell.

Model switch that changes the vector width (old vectors dropped):

| Documents | Base | PR v1 | PR | Speedup vs base |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| 1,000 | 25.2 s | 20.6 s | 11.3 s | 2.2x |
| 3,000 | 162.9 s | 119.1 s | 35.1 s | 4.6x |

Same vector width (old vectors replaced in place):

| Documents | Base | PR v1 | PR | Speedup vs base |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| 1,000 | 33.5 s | 29.5 s | 10.7 s | 3.1x |
| 3,000 | 238.1 s | 197.2 s | 32.8 s | 7.3x |

Work counts over 300 documents: full stale scans 302 -> 6; `chunks_vec`
partition scans 300 -> 1 (2 after a width change, for the document
`ensure_vec` exempts). `chunks_vec` ends with exactly 300 rows in every
arm.

## Tests

- `test_rag_reembed.py`: one job runs one full scan plus primary key
rechecks; documents deleted or added mid-job end in the same state as a
scan per document (`_RESCAN_SECONDS` 0 and 3600); an identity switch
mid-job scans again. With `_run` reverted to base, the scan-count tests
fail (8 scans vs 3 for 6 documents) and the scan-per-document case
passes.
- `test_rag_vec_cache.py`: a swap replaces exactly the document's
vectors whether the rowid hint is right, points at another document's
rows, or is absent; a swap after a width change writes the dropped
document's vectors.
- All `tests/test_rag*.py`: no new failures vs base (the remaining
failures are missing optional captioning / OCR dependencies on both
sides).
- Staging: Linux and Windows green. macOS 15 fails
`test_the_builder_opens_and_closes_through_the_connection_gate`, which
this PR does not touch and which fails the same way on main (that
runner's Python cannot load sqlite extensions).

FSDP2 auto GA: replicated gradients wait for the last micro-batch again (red on main since #19942) (#19990)

## Problem


`tests/test_fsdp2_replicated_grad_sync_gloo.py::test_replicated_sync_follows_the_ga_sync_flag`
fails on main (`0076415307`), in the `Repo tests (CPU, fsdp2-2)` shard.
On a staging run (#19657) and locally:

```
(1, 'auto', {... 'calls': {'old': [1, 1, ...], 'new': [1, 1, 1, 1, ...], 'oracle': [0, 0, 0, 1, ...]}})
```

In `auto` mode the trainable parameters FSDP2 leaves unsharded (the
replicated ones, here `norm`, `norm16`, `branch`) are now all-reduced on
every gradient accumulation micro-batch, not once per accumulation
cycle.

This comes from #19942. Under auto GA with no fit layout,
`_no_grad_sync` turns gradient sync off on the root, then turns the
reduce-scatter back on for units whose own parameters are mostly
trainable. That is what #19942 is for: it avoids holding their whole
fp32 gradients on every rank between micro-batches.

`fsdp2_save._fsdp_grad_sync_deferred` decides whether the replicated
all-reduce can wait. It reads "non-final micro-batch" as "every FSDP2
param group has `reduce_grads == False`". Once any unit reduce-scatters
again, that never holds, so the replicated gradients are all-reduced on
every micro-batch.

The test model is fully trainable, so all of its units fall in that set.
For replicated parameters, the per-micro-batch all-reduce buys nothing:
their gradients are whole on every rank either way, so it is only extra
communication. #19942 is right for the sharded units. The replicated
predicate just needed to follow it.

## Fix

- `fsdp2_native._no_grad_sync` marks the root model while a non-final
micro-batch runs (`_unsloth_ga_no_sync`). It does this only in the modes
that skip a reduce: `skip`, `defer`, and `auto` when it resolves to one
of those. It clears the mark in the `finally` that already restores
gradient sync. `each` still returns early and sets nothing.
- `fsdp2_save._fsdp_grad_sync_deferred` treats that mark as a non-final
micro-batch. Without the mark it reads the param groups as before, which
covers a direct `set_requires_gradient_sync(False)`.

## Verification

- `tests/test_fsdp2_replicated_grad_sync_gloo.py`: 9 passed, 2 skipped.
Before: `test_replicated_sync_follows_the_ga_sync_flag` failed on main
as above.
- The FSDP2 GA suites together (`test_fsdp2_native_ga_auto_rule`,
`test_fsdp2_native_ga_sync_gloo`,
`test_fsdp2_native_ga_trainable_units_gloo` from #19942,
`test_fsdp2_replicated_grad_sync_gloo`,
`test_fsdp2_native_empty_cache_sync`): 21 passed, 2 skipped. #19942's
own trainable-units tests still pass, so mostly trainable units keep
reduce-scattering every micro-batch.
- Sabotage: with the mark removed from `_no_grad_sync` and the reader
kept, `test_replicated_sync_follows_the_ga_sync_flag` fails again.
- Only the CPU gloo tests ran here, not a multi-GPU training run.

fix(studio): rebuild @skill manifests into the system prompt on every turn (#19529)

Fixes #19212

## Problem

An explicit `@skill` mention adds the complete `SKILL.md` to the system
message. This happened only on the turn that held the mention, because
the loader read `messages[-1]`.

On the next turn, the system prompt fell back to the client's original:

- llama.cpp's prefix cache missed at token 0 and re-processed the whole
prompt (about 33k tokens in the report).
- The skill's instructions were gone from context, although the user
expects them to keep applying.

## Change

`load_mentioned_skills` now rebuilds every user mention in the thread
into the system message on every request.

- **Ordering:** oldest mention first, one block per skill.
- **Reads:** each skill is read once per request.
- **Budget:** one thread-wide budget, charged in first-mention order, so
a later mention never changes an earlier outcome.
- **Result:** later turns resend the same system prompt, and a newly
mentioned skill only extends it.

Some behaviour stays on the latest user message only:

- **Activation:** the latest message alone activates a mention. It emits
`skill_load` events, asks for Ask approval and gets the full-access
upgrade.
- **Continue:** Continue and partial-assistant resumes rebuild without
activating anything.
- **Tool results:** only the latest turn can reuse a complete
`read_skill` tool result instead of injecting, and only when the caller
pins that result through native fitting (local GGUF). Every other path,
and every earlier mention, uses the system message, because a tool
result can be compacted away.
- **Ask:** under Ask, earlier mentions are not rebuilt, since their
approval is not on record. This matches the current behaviour.

`dedup_tool_context` is removed. Its only caller (safetensors) passed
`False` and supplied no pins, so the new rule already covers it.

## Why not move skill bodies into the user turn (#19233)

Moving the bodies into the user turn also keeps the system prompt
stable, but it has two costs:

- **Many readers have to change:** every reader of user text must strip
the injected head. That includes retrieval, titles, transcripts,
compaction and attachment fitting.
- **Skills can still be lost:** a skill can still disappear when
provider or cloud compaction summarizes the user turn, or when a
`SKILL.md` quotes its own end marker.

Every fitter and compactor already keeps the system message, so this
change keeps the bodies there and makes the message deterministic.

## Trade-offs

- **First mention:** the turn that first mentions a skill still
re-prefills once, as it does today.
- **Context space:** a mentioned skill now keeps using its share of the
budget on later turns. That is the point of the fix, but it leaves less
room for history on small context windows.
- **Re-reads:** each request re-reads every mentioned skill: about 11 ms
per skill on a 39-skill catalog.
- **Ask, then Auto:** a mention denied under Ask is rebuilt if the
thread later runs under Auto, which permits the read.

## Validation

Live two-turn check against `llama-server` with Qwen3.5-0.8B
(`cache_prompt`). The loader output was sent directly to the server:

```text
main:     turn 2 cache_n=0     (system prompt fell back to 35 bytes; skill lost)
this PR:  turn 2 cache_n=3352 of 3375 prompt tokens (system prompt identical)
```

Tests run:

```bash
python -m pytest -q studio/backend/tests/test_skill_mention_semantics.py \
  studio/backend/tests/test_explicit_skill_loading.py \
  studio/backend/tests/test_tool_full_access_upgrade.py \
  studio/backend/tests/test_sandbox_level.py studio/backend/tests/test_skills.py \
  studio/backend/tests/test_refactor_guard.py studio/backend/tests/test_llama_cpp_tool_loop.py
```

Each new assertion was mutation-checked: weakening the code it guards
makes that test fail. This covers:

- latest-only activation;
- Ask skipping;
- the upgrade applying only to the latest turn;
- budget consistency across turns;
- tool-result reuse only on pinned latest turns;
- the single read per request.

Studio images: skip the coalescing tokenizer copies on resident loads that can never batch (#19886)

## Problem

Every diffusion render calls `prime_coalesce_tokenizers` inside the
generation slot, after `render_t0`. On the first render after a load it
deep-copies each fast tokenizer for FLUX.1 / FLUX.1-Kontext (T5 bucket
key) and SDXL (textual-inversion key) into `_KEY_TOKENIZERS`, so the
copy lands on the first image's latency and in `generation_seconds`.

The only reader of those copies is `coalesce_prompt_key`, reached only
from `coalesce_plan`. `coalesce_plan` returns None whenever
`request_batching()` is serial, and a load with `offload_policy ==
"none"` is always serial (`_denoiser_streams_from_host` returns False).
`offload_policy` is a field of the frozen `_LoadState` and is only set
when a load builds a new state, so a resident load can never start
coalescing without a reload. The copies made for a resident load are
never read.

On transformers 5.x (Studio pins 5.5.4 on Python 3.10+) diffusers'
`CLIPTokenizer` is the fast tokenizer, so FLUX.1 copies two tokenizers
and SDXL copies two. On 4.57.6 `CLIPTokenizer` is the slow class, so
only FLUX.1's T5 tokenizer is copied and SDXL copies nothing.

## Change

`prime_coalesce_tokenizers_for(state)` calls `prime_coalesce_tokenizers`
only when `_denoiser_streams_from_host(state)` is true, the same
predicate `request_batching()` uses for its resident/serial decision.
`generate` calls it in place of the direct call. Resident loads,
including group-offloaded loads whose denoiser groups are all pinned
resident (also served serially), skip the copies; streamed,
model-offloaded and partially or fully streamed group-offloaded loads
prime exactly as before. Pixels, batching decisions, errors and status
output are unchanged.

## Results

`prime_coalesce_tokenizers` as run by `generate` on the first render of
a fresh load, with the real tokenizer objects diffusers builds from each
repo's `model_index.json` (tokenizer subfolders only, stub pipeline),
CPU, 5 repeats per arm, median ms. Base was run twice (A/A).

| transformers | family | tokenizers copied (base) | base A | base B |
head resident | saved |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| 4.57.6 | FLUX.1-schnell | T5 | 29.6 | 31.0 | 0.01 | ~30 |
| 4.57.6 | FLUX.1-Kontext | T5 | 30.4 | 29.8 | 0.01 | ~30 |
| 4.57.6 | SDXL | none (slow CLIP) | 0.02 | 0.02 | 0.01 | 0 |
| 5.5.4 | FLUX.1-schnell | CLIP + T5 | 186.1 | 196.8 | 0.01 | ~190 |
| 5.5.4 | FLUX.1-Kontext | CLIP + T5 | 246.0 | 243.8 | 0.01 | ~245 |
| 5.5.4 | SDXL | CLIP + CLIP | 409.1 | 414.7 | 0.01 | ~410 |
| 5.18.0 | FLUX.1-schnell | CLIP + T5 | 198.5 | 187.5 | 0.01 | ~190 |
| 5.18.0 | FLUX.1-Kontext | CLIP + T5 | 212.1 | 200.0 | 0.01 | ~205 |
| 5.18.0 | SDXL | CLIP + CLIP | 251.9 | 217.2 | 0.01 | ~235 |

Streamed loads (`offload_policy="sequential"`): head still copies the
same tokenizers in the same time as base, and `coalesce_plan` over five
prompts (short, long, weighted, over-length) returns identical keys on
both arms for all three families and all three transformers versions.
`request_batching()` modes are identical on both arms (resident
`serial`, streamed `any`).

## Tests

- New in `tests/test_image_batching_followups.py`: a group-offloaded
load copies nothing while its denoiser is pinned resident and primes
once it streams; a resident FLUX.1 / SDXL load makes no copy and leaves
`_KEY_TOKENIZERS` untouched while `coalesce_plan` stays None; a streamed
/ model-offloaded load primes and yields the same keys as the direct
prime; `generate` primes through the gate. They fail on base (the gate
does not exist there).
- Related backend tests (diffusion backend, hires, detailer, slot
release, eject ownership, image batching / concurrency, OpenAI images

`test_diffusion_hires.py::test_timestep_rule_reads_each_pipelines_rounding`
failure and 7 setup errors from the local diffusers install); head adds
5 passing tests.

Keep the earlier GGUF when a re-export fails (#19572)

Running `save_pretrained_gguf` again into a folder that already holds a
working GGUF overwrote that file in place. llama-quantize empties its
output file as soon as it starts, so if the second run died partway (out
of memory, disk full, a killed kernel), the working Q4_K_M was left as a
short, broken file that llama.cpp refuses to load.
`save_pretrained_ggml` had the same problem for LoRA GGUF files.

Each quantized GGUF and each LoRA GGUF is now written to a temporary
file next to the final one and moved into place only once it is
complete. A failed run leaves the earlier file exactly as it was and
removes the temporary file. While a re-export runs, the folder needs
room for the old file and the new one at the same time.

Studio video: batch LTX-2.5 clips across requests (per-clip noise, encode, upsample and audio) (#19937)

## Summary

Follows #19831 (queued Wan clips share one denoise), now on main. Queued
LTX-2.5 text-to-video clips can now share one denoise too, on the
distilled DiT, through one stage or both stages of the reference recipe.
The engine contract is #19831's: only the clips contiguous behind the
head in FairOrder join, with the same canvas, frames, fps, steps,
guidance, flow shift and audio flow shift, and no first frame, keyframe,
reference or continuation. A single clip, or a head with nobody
compatible behind it, renders exactly as before.

What LTX-2.5 needed on top of the Wan path:

- **Per-row renoise.** The distilled DiT samples euler-ancestral, which
draws fresh noise at every step from `noise_generator`. With riders it
holds one generator per clip, and `randn_tensor` draws row i from
generator i at the one-clip shape: exactly what that clip draws alone,
for both the video and the audio stream (the audio scheduler copy shares
the same generator list, so each clip's stream continues in its solo
order). The sampler says so (`per_row_noise`), so #19831's refusal of
samplers that renoise from a shared stream no longer catches it.
- **`keep_tokens` per row.** The sampler's deterministic-step tokens (an
image-conditioned first frame) can be one entry per row. Conditioned
clips still render alone in this PR, so every batched row has none
today; the per-row form is there and tested for when they join.
- **Per-row text encode.** The Gemma 4 encoder worker sees one prompt
per call, as in each clip's own render (the LTX-2.5 encode returns four
parts, embeds and masks for both branches, and all four are stacked).
- **Two stages.** Stage one's latents go through the latent upsampler
one clip at a time, then stage two denoises the batch; stage two's noise
is per row too.
- **Per-row decode, video and audio.** The video VAE, the audio VAE and
the vocoder each decode one clip at a time (decode peak stays one clip),
and each rider's mp4 carries its own soundtrack.
- **Residency.** #19831's batch term applies unchanged: rows x the
largest one-clip denoise peak recorded for the load (else the base
overhead), decode floor one clip; a batch that would not fit raises
`BatchDoesNotFit` and its clips render one at a time.

## When it batches (Auto)

`UNSLOTH_VIDEO_BATCH=auto|off|force`, as in #19831. Auto batches LTX-2.5
only where it was measured faster **and** passed the paired quality
gate: a Low VRAM load running eager, on the reference two-stage recipe,
**2 or 4 clips at a time**. A sealed batch of another size (3) renders
its clips one at a time in the same job (before any denoise, nothing
lost or rendered twice). Everything else renders one clip at a time:
- the default load and every placement whose DiT stays on the card (an
eager batch loses to one compiled clip there);
- the one-stage recipe (`UNSLOTH_LTX25_TWO_STAGE=0`): its batch of 2 did
not pass the quality gate;
- a compiled Low VRAM load (default speed mode): batched eager is 2.8x
faster there, but its quality gate (compiled solo against an eager
batch) was not run;
- the dev DiT (CFG plus STG over 30+ steps), which renders alone even
under `force`.

`force` batches any eligible load at any size; a compiled load batches
eager, never compiling or capturing on a user's request.

## Measurements

A100-80 (Colab), Diffusers pack through the unsloth mirror, 768x512, 49
frames, 24 fps, the distilled recipe (8 + 3 steps), 4 to 8 prompts with
their own soundtrack cues x 2 seeds, in a warm process (first clip
excluded), one card. Seconds per clip; speedup = serial over batched in
the same load, with a bootstrap 95% lower bound. The serial and batched
passes ran in A/B then B/A order.

| Load | Serial s/clip | Batched by 2 | Batched by 4 | Speedup by 2 / by
4 (95% lower bound) |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Low VRAM, bf16 DiT streamed, eager, two stages | 39.9 (n=16) | 21.8 |
12.9 | 1.83x (1.80x) / 3.09x (3.04x) |
| same, second VM | 39.6 (n=16) | 21.7 | 12.7 | 1.83x (1.80x) / 3.15x
(3.10x) |
| same, third and fourth VMs (G2c runs) | 39.6 / 42.6 (n=24 each) | 21.7
/ 24.7 | | 1.83x (1.81x) / 1.72x (1.70x) |
| Low VRAM, eager, one stage (`UNSLOTH_LTX25_TWO_STAGE=0`) | 30.1 (n=8);
29.3 (n=24) | 17.2; 16.7 | 10.6 | 1.80x (1.71x), 1.77x (1.75x) / 2.91x
(2.77x) |
| Low VRAM, default speed mode (compiled), batch forced eager | 27.8
(n=8) | | 10.1 | / 2.80x (2.71x) |

Peak allocated VRAM in the server process (the Gemma 4 encoder worker is

The win is where the DiT streams its weights for every call: a batch
pays the transfer once for all its clips, so 4 clips take 52 s where one

**One clip unchanged (G1).** Main vs this branch, same VM, one seeded

## Tests

`studio/backend/tests/test_video_batch_ltx25.py` (14 tests). The numeric
ones run a tiny real Diffusers LTX-2 pipeline on the CPU (random
weights, with LTX-2.5's own euler-ancestral sampler, render and latent
upsampler; a stub stands in for the Gemma 4 encoder worker, which is

- the sampler draws each row's renoise from its own generator (batched

- the Auto policy (Low VRAM two-stage loads only, sizes 2 and 4; a batch
of 3 under Auto renders each clip alone, through the real backend), the

Studio CUDA graphs: report why Krea-2 calls decline a graph instead of blaming a non-tensor argument (#19960)

## Summary

On Krea-2 the CUDA graph layer is armed, but every denoiser call runs
eager. That part is intended: #19208 declines graphs for any call with a
non-zero key start. What is wrong is the reporting. Nothing is logged,
and the status reason says the calls had "a non-tensor argument". This
PR counts the decline separately, logs it once, and puts the real reason
in the `cuda_graph` status.

## Why the graphs never record

- `diffusion_krea2_text_trim.py` lays each text row out as `[pad |
valid]` in buckets of 128 rows when the prefix processors are installed.
Each row's key start is its pad count, `rows - valid`, so it is non-zero
for any prompt whose valid length is not an exact multiple of 128.
- `diffusion_krea2_prefix_kv.py` (`install`, the `_key` hook) raises
`PlanNotRecordable` for any non-zero start. The op reads the start on
the host, so a recorded graph would freeze it. #19208 says an earlier
version keyed graphs on the start, and on an RTX PRO 6000 that hit the
graph cap of 4 within a few prompts.
- `GraphedForward.__call__` calls that hook inside the same `try` as
`graph_key`. The raise therefore fell into the "unhashable tree"
handler: `refused_object += 1`, eager, no log. `never_engaged` then
reported `armed, but all 48 denoiser call(s) so far ran eager (48 with a
non-tensor argument)`.

On a G4 (Krea-2-Turbo, transformer_quant none, 1024px, 8 steps, Auto)
the deferred profile lists `cuda_graph` from generation 3. Graph
engagement then reads `captures 0, replays 0, eager_calls 48`, and there
are zero process-wide `CUDAGraph.capture_begin` calls.

## What changes

- `diffusion_cuda_graph.py`: an exception from the branch-key hook
(`_unsloth_graph_key_extra`) is counted as `refused_branch`, separate
from `refused_object`. The reason is logged once at info
(`diffusion.cuda_graph: Krea2Transformer2DModel runs eager: ...`) and
`never_engaged` names it. The reason comes from the exception's
`graph_decline` attribute, or from its type when that attribute is
missing. `refused_branch` is added to `stats()`.
- `diffusion_krea2_prefix_kv.py`: `PlanNotRecordable.graph_decline`
gives the reason text, "declined by Krea 2 prefix K/V attention (the
per-prompt key start is read on the host, a CUDA graph would freeze
it)".
- `diffusion_block_graph.py`: the per-block layer uses the same
`refused_branch` counter and label.

Whether a call graphs or runs eager is unchanged, so no render changes.

## Tests

- New
`test_live_status_names_a_branch_key_decline_not_a_non_tensor_argument`
(fake torch, CPU). It fails on main with `KeyError: 'refused_branch'`
and passes here.
- `test_a_planned_call_is_never_recorded_by_a_cuda_graph` now also
checks the decline text.

Studio video: load DiffSynth raw-layout MiniMax-H3 LoRAs with per-head fused QKV rows (#19934)

## Summary

MiniMax-H3 video LoRAs trained with DiffSynth-Studio load on main, but
their fused `attn.qkv_proj` B matrix is split the wrong way. Weights
land on the wrong heads and the wrong projections, and nothing reports
an error.

Background:
- The raw H3 DiT reads its fused qkv output per head, as `[heads, 3,
head_dim]`. DiffSynth-Studio trains on that model and saves PEFT names
(`blocks.N.attn.qkv_proj.lora_B.default.weight`), so the B rows are per
head: `[h0: q k v, h1: q k v, ...]`.
- #19818 added the community layout map, which splits qkv B into three
contiguous thirds for `to_q` / `to_k` / `to_v`. That is right for the
ai-toolkit / ComfyUI files #19818 checked
(`diffusion_model.*.lora_B.weight`). Those files follow the Comfy-Org
repack, which reads qkv as `[3, heads, head_dim]`.
- `video_lora.py` folds `.lora_B.default.weight` into the same suffix
list as `.lora_B.weight`, so the DiffSynth files take the thirds split
too.

## Evidence for the layout

DiffSynth-Studio at `13046f3065e766ec372e1531fc6a35a8e11f2a0b`:
- `diffsynth/models/minimax_h3_dit.py:127`: `MiniMaxH3Attention` has one
`qkv_proj = nn.Linear(hidden, 3 * inner)`. Lines 134-138 read its output
with `qkv.view(total, self.num_heads, 3, self.head_dim)`, then `q =
qkv[:, :, 0]`, `k = qkv[:, :, 1]`, `v = qkv[:, :, 2]`.
- `diffsynth/models/minimax_h3_dit_comfy.py:17-23`: the Comfy-Org
variant reads `qkv.view(total, 3, self.num_heads, self.head_dim)`, which
is contiguous thirds.
- `diffsynth/configs/model_configs.py:1603-1606`: the raw
`MiniMaxAI/MiniMax-H3` `FL2VA/transformer` shards load into
`MiniMaxH3DiT` with no state-dict converter, so the released qkv rows
are per head. `:1642-1646` does the same for
`DiffSynth-Studio/MiniMax-H3-NF4` `minimax-h3-ref2va-nf4`.
- `diffsynth/utils/lora/minimax_h3.py:85-96`: DiffSynth's own
diffusers-to-DiffSynth LoRA converter writes `to_q` / `to_k` / `to_v`
rows at `head * 384 + {0, 128, 256}` into
`qkv_proj.lora_B.default.weight`.
- `diffsynth/diffusion/training_module.py:95-101` injects PEFT LoRA
(adapter `default`), and `diffsynth/diffusion/logger.py:125-133` saves
those parameter names as they are, so `.default.` stays in the keys.
- The raw config (`MiniMaxAI/MiniMax-H3`
`FL2VA/transformer/config.json`) has 56 heads x 128 = 7168, which gives
qkv B 21504 rows.

The published DiffSynth H3 LoRA,
`DiffSynth-Studio/MiniMax-H3-LoRA-LineartAnime`, is the only `.default`
H3 LoRA I found among 57 H3 LoRA search hits. Its README loads it on
`minimax-h3-ref2va-nf4` (raw `MiniMaxH3DiT`). Mean |B row| of its qkv
tensors (fp32, rank 32), read without downloading the file:

| tensor | contiguous thirds [q, k, v] | per head [q, k, v] |
|---|---|---|
| blocks.0 | 0.0098, 0.0103, 0.0097 | 0.0114, 0.0099, 0.0085 |
| blocks.40 | 0.0114, 0.0119, 0.0122 | 0.0128, 0.0135, 0.0091 |
| token_refiner.blocks.0 | 0.0095, 0.0092, 0.0093 | 0.0089, 0.0086,
0.0106 |

Grouped per head, the v slice stands apart. Grouped by thirds, the three
segments are flat. That is what a per-head layout looks like when read
as thirds.

## Fix

`h3_community_key_map(..., per_head_qkv = True)` gives each projection
the 128-row slice `head * 384 + i * 128` of every head. `read_deltas`
records whether B came from `.lora_B.default.weight` and passes it
through. Nothing else changes:
- `mlp.fc1` [gate; value] to `ff.net.0.proj` [value; gate] is the same
in both layouts (DiffSynth's converter does the same swap,
`minimax_h3.py:104-107`).
- `out_proj`, `fc2`, `adaln_proj.linear` and `token_refiner` renames are
unchanged.
- `diffusion_model.*.lora_B.weight` and unprefixed `.lora_B.weight`
files keep the contiguous thirds. That covers all six public files
#19818 lists.

Known limit: DiffSynth's training scripts can also train on a Comfy-Org
base (for example
`examples/minimax_h3/model_training/lora/MiniMax-H3-Pruned-Ref2VA.sh`).
A file trained that way carries the same `.default` keys but contiguous
rows, and the keys cannot tell the two apart. I found no such file
published. DiffSynth itself applies its LoRAs in the raw layout
(`minimax_h3.py:85-96`), so this change matches DiffSynth's own reading.

## Tests

New `studio/backend/tests/test_video_lora_h3_diffsynth_qkv.py`, CPU
only:
- `test_diffsynth_fused_qkv_matches_the_raw_module` (blocks 0 and 7,
token_refiner 1): a random fused LoRA in the raw layout. The reference
applies `B @ A` the way `MiniMaxH3Attention.forward` does (view `[heads,
3, head_dim]`), and Studio's per-projection deltas must be `torch.equal`
to it.
- `test_diffsynth_rows_match_diffsynths_own_layout`: builds the fused
file with DiffSynth's converter formula. Each projection must read back
its own `B @ A`.
- `test_community_files_keep_the_contiguous_thirds`,
`test_diffsynth_fc1_and_out_proj_are_unchanged`,
`test_per_head_qkv_needs_whole_heads`.

On main, 5 of the 7 fail: the three raw-module cases, the DiffSynth
converter case and the head-width check. The other 2 pass by design
(contiguous thirds, fc1 / out_proj).

`test_video_lora_h3_community_keys.py` (#19818): the real-row check
against the released weights now runs on `diffusion_model.*`,
`diffusion_model.*` with `.alpha`, and unprefixed `.lora_{A,B}.weight`.
Its third case used to be an unprefixed `.default` copy of the community
file, which is not a layout any tool writes.

All `test_video_lora*.py` suites: 84 passed, 2 skipped.

feat(studio): live prompt progress and generation details for MLX chats (#19738)

## Summary

MLX chats in Unsloth Studio showed "Working..." for the whole prompt
read and had no live decode line: only the GGUF stream fed the
`generation_progress` frames added in #14909, and only GGUF showed the
status between tool rounds and the compacting label from #16608. This
makes MLX chats (text and vision, single reply and resident batch) send
the same frames, so the UI shows "Processing prompt N% · Xs left", the
live "N tokens · tok/s" line with Generation details on, the round
status and the compacting label. The frontend is unchanged: it already
consumes these frames without knowing the backend.

## Changes

- **Single text reply** (`mlx_inference._LiveProgress`, worker,
orchestrator, route): the MLX worker reports llama-server-shaped samples
for a reply that asks (`generation_progress` on the command): a prefill
sample per mlx-lm chunk counted past the prompt-cache prefix, so a
follow-up starts at 0%, with its elapsed `time_ms` for the UI's
time-left fit, and decode figures timed from the first token (mlx-lm's
`generation_tps` counts the first token over the time after it, which
roughly doubles a short reply's rate). The orchestrator hands samples to
a `perf_callback` out of band of the token stream, and the safetensors
chat and server-tool streams reuse `_PrefillProgressSignal` and
`_stall_wait_frames`, so framing and throttling are shared with GGUF.
Only a single reply asks; `n > 1` does not.
- **Resident text batch**: plain MLX chats are batched by default. A
watched row reports the same samples from mlx-lm's `BatchGenerator`
prompt responses and its own decode. A single-image row is prefilled by
Unsloth Studio as it is admitted; with an unsloth-zoo whose
`prefill_image_prompt` takes `progress`, it reports those chunks, else
decode only (never a fake 1/1 prefill).
- **Vision models**: the single path reports chunks through
unsloth-zoo's `vlm_prefill_progress`; a resident vision batch row passes
`GenerationRequest.prompt_progress` when it is the watched reply. A
speculative row prefills inside `BatchStream.add()`, so the worker now
attaches a reply's live sink before admitting it (both batch sessions
hold a sink for a reply not yet admitted), and a speculative row passes
the callback only where unsloth-zoo's
`speculative_prompt_progress_unavailable_reason()` is None. The cached
prefix is what the forward actually resumed from: the prompt-cache
session's `resumed_tokens` on the single path, and for a batch row the
prefix unsloth-zoo reports with each chunk, since a queued row may be
reopened at a longer prefix. Both hooks are feature-detected: with an
unsloth-zoo without them, vision chats report decode only, as before.
- **Tool rounds and compaction**: the safetensors tool stream calls
`round_ended()` on `tool_end`, and `compact_chat_context` forwards an
`on_compacting` hook to the same `_fit_with_instruction_pins` fit GGUF
uses, reported by the tool loop's per-turn refit and the plain chat's
fit. GGUF behaviour is unchanged.

Companion unsloth-zoo PR: unslothai/unsloth-zoo#2830 (adds the vision
hooks). This PR does not depend on it landing first.

## Risks / tradeoffs

- Decode samples are throttled in the backend to the route's
decode-frame interval (0.25 s) before the IPC hop; prefill sends one per
chunk.
- Non-MLX safetensors backends take the same route path; they send no
samples, so nothing changes for them.
- With `prefill_batch_size > 1`, vision batch progress counts padded
columns. Media rows that Unsloth itself produces fall outside the live
total.

## Validation

```text
tests/test_live_generation_progress.py, test_mlx_resident_batch.py, test_mlx_context_compaction.py,
test_mlx_vlm_prompt_cache.py, test_mlx_inference_backend.py (non real-model)
  702 passed with the companion unsloth-zoo branch; with unsloth-zoo main the hooks are feature-detected and the targeted batch/progress tests pass (145)
```

Real models through the backend after rebasing on current main:
- Llama-3.2-3B-Instruct-4bit, ~7K-token prompt, single and resident
batch: prefill at 2048 / 4096 / 6144 / 7041 / 7042, then decode; the
follow-up turn reports from the 7064-token cached prefix.
- Qwen3.5-0.8B (mlx-vlm), single and batched: 2048 / 4096 / 6144 / 7909
of 7910, then decode; follow-up from the 6144-token resumed prefix. With
n-gram speculation, a resident batch row reports the same 2048 / 4096 /
6144 / 7909 before decode.
- Unsloth Studio API with Qwen3-4B-4bit at a 3072-token context: a chat
past the window streams `compacting` → prefill → decode; a two-call tool
loop streams a prefill and decode per round with `tool_start`/`tool_end`
between.
- In the UI, the prompt label and decode line appear as on GGUF
("Processing prompt 20% · 5s left · 2,048 / 10,233 tokens · 1,708
tok/s", then "225 tokens · 87.8 tok/s").

An A/B against main showed no end-to-end time difference (all cases
within 1%).

Studio: Keep QLoRA selected for cached 4-bit models on CUDA (#19852)

Selecting a model that is already cached in bitsandbytes 4-bit can make
Studio switch the training method to LoRA. That can send the run to the
larger base checkpoint and make it run out of GPU memory even though the
cached 4-bit model fits.

Read the quantization metadata from the cached checkpoint Studio
selected and use it to keep QLoRA as the default on CUDA. The user can
still choose another training method.

### Before and after

The browser replays the same cached Qwen3 8B checkpoint metadata and RTX
3080 Ti memory readings on both builds. With 11.33 GiB free, the default
changes from LoRA to QLoRA.
