Studio](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/NilayYadav/unsloth/72a3f0c4b64d60121f87402c5b263daa7f445563/21-cached-qlora.png)

The same misjudgement happens when a bitsandbytes 4-bit repo is picked
from the Hub rather than the cache: the hardware check sizes LoRA by the

the config.json of whatever target the worker loads (cached snapshot,
Hub repo or local folder), so both paths keep QLoRA on CUDA. The config
read is the same memoized one the route already made, so model selection
makes no extra request.

Apply qat_scheme for models that load through FastModel (#19587)

FastLanguageModel.get_peft_model accepted qat_scheme but did not pass it
on when it handed the model to FastModel, which happens for Gemma 3,
Qwen3.5 and other models that load through FastModel, and for any model
loaded after a FastModel load in the same process. QAT was silently

Studio: map more Hugging Face repos and whole vendor orgs to their ModelScope copies (#19883)

## Summary

With ModelScope as the hub source, Unsloth Studio resolves a Hugging
Face id through `upstream_id()`. Until now that meant 18 hand-written
aliases, and every other repo ModelScope hosts under a different org
(for example `zai-org/GLM-5.3` → `ZhipuAI/GLM-5.3`, `nvidia/*` →
`nv-community/*`) answered 404, so it could not be browsed, downloaded
or opened from Unsloth Studio. This PR makes those repos reachable
without anyone maintaining a growing per-repo table.

## What changed

- **More exact aliases** (`_ALIASES`): 122 models and 36 datasets, up
from 18 entries in all. They cover repos Unsloth Studio's own code uses
(GLM, MiniMax, gpt-oss, Nemotron, Hy3, Yi, gte, …) and popular models
and datasets (CLIP, t5, TinyLlama, gpqa, hellaswag, AIME, NuminaMath,
…).
- **Org aliases for models** (`_ORG_ALIASES`): every model of
`MiniMaxAI`, `OpenMOSS-Team`, `zai-org`, `01-ai`, `tencent`, `openai`,
`nvidia` and `Alibaba-NLP` maps to the ModelScope org that holds them
under the same names (`MiniMax`, `openmoss`, `ZhipuAI`, `01ai`,
`tencent-community`, `openai-mirror`, `nv-community`, `iic`). Precedence
is exact alias → `_ORG_KEPT` (the model keeps its own id) → org rule →
unchanged. Datasets get exact aliases only.
- **`_ORG_KEPT`** lists the 127 models of those orgs whose ModelScope
copy has different or missing weights, configs, remote code or tokenizer
files, or is a private copy, so the org rule never sends them to a wrong
copy. A model with no copy at the target isn't listed: the alias answers
404 just as the original id would.
- **Frontend:** `/api/health`'s `modelscope_pages` now carries `{base,
aliases, orgs}`. `hubWebUrl()` applies the same precedence for models,
and its lookup tables have no prototype, so an id like `constructor/...`
can't read an inherited property.
- **Opt-in network test** (`tests/test_modelscope_org_aliases.py`, run
with `UNSLOTH_MODELSCOPE_ORG_ALIAS_NETWORK=1`):
- It lists every Hugging Face model of each aliased org and checks every
one the rules map elsewhere.
- It fails when the ModelScope copy's loaded files differ, or when
ModelScope starts hosting the model under its own id, and prints the ids
to add to `_ORG_KEPT`.
- A model that isn't mirrored yet passes, since it answers 404 with or
without the alias.
- Throttled lookups count as inconclusive and fail the run only above
5%.
  - `HF_TOKEN`, when set, is sent to huggingface.co only.

## How aliases were verified

- **Metadata only**, no weights downloaded. Every file Unsloth Studio
may load must exist on ModelScope with an equal LFS sha256, or an equal
size for files outside LFS.
- **Which files count as loaded:** for exact aliases, everything except
READMEs, licences, repository bookkeeping, and in models docs and media.
For org-rule models (`_ORG_KEPT` and the network test), an allow-list of
weights, JSON/YAML configs, Python remote code and tokenizer files, with
hidden files ignored. ModelScope-only extra files are allowed only when
nothing loads them.
- **Owner check:** an alias points only to a vendor's own ModelScope org
(`ZhipuAI`, `MiniMax`, `Tencent-Hunyuan`, …), a ModelScope-run vendor
mirror (`nv-community`, `openai-mirror`, …), or a ModelScope team org
(`AI-ModelScope`, `modelscope`, …). Copies under personal or third-party
namespaces were rejected.
- **Source repos:** only official upstream Hugging Face repos get exact
aliases, never re-uploads.
- **No hidden copies:** no aliased id has a ModelScope repo under its
own id, so no alias hides a same-id copy.
- **Large repos:** repos beyond the adapter's 100k-file listing limit
get no alias.

## Risks and tradeoffs

- An org rule maps future uploads before anyone checks them. The network
test is how drift gets caught.
- Small non-LFS files (configs, tokenizers) are compared by size only:
Hugging Face exposes no content hash for them.
- A few very large dataset copies (for example `AI-MO/olympiads`) take

Studio RAG test: the connection gate test holds on a sqlite3 without extension loading (macos-15) (#19980)

## Problem


`studio/backend/tests/test_rag_vec_cache.py::test_the_builder_opens_and_closes_through_the_connection_gate`
(added in #16607) fails on the macos-15 leg of the cross-platform runs:

```
AttributeError: 'GatedConnection' object has no attribute 'enable_load_extension'
```

The python.org Python on that runner builds `sqlite3` without extension
loading. The product handles this: RAG reports itself unavailable. The
other RAG tests skip there through the `rag_conn` fixture ("an
interpreter whose sqlite3 cannot load extensions (the macos-15 runner's)
never has RAG"). This test calls `vec_cache._connect` directly, so it
bypasses that gate and fails on any PR whose macOS leg runs the file.
The latest example is #19891's cross-platform run.

## Fix

On a `sqlite3` without `enable_load_extension`, the test checks what
still holds there instead of skipping:
- the open goes through `sqlite_gate.connect` exactly once;
- `_connect` raises the `enable_load_extension` error;
- the connection it opened is closed, through the gated `close`.

Everywhere else the test is unchanged.

## Verification

- `studio/backend/tests/test_rag_vec_cache.py`: 20 passed on Linux.
- macOS behaviour, simulated on Linux: `enable_load_extension` was made
to raise `AttributeError` on `GatedConnection`, and the test module's
`sqlite3` was replaced with one whose `Connection` has no such
attribute.
- Main's test fails with the same `AttributeError` as the macos-15 job.
  - This version passes.
- Not run on a real macOS runner in this PR.

Skip the adapter_config.json Hub request when the cache already records it as missing for the resolved commit (#19890)

## Problem

`FastLanguageModel.from_pretrained` and `FastModel.from_pretrained`
probe every load with `PeftConfig.from_pretrained(model_name, ...)` to
tell an adapter repo from a base model. For a plain base model on the
Hub, `huggingface_hub` sends a HEAD for `adapter_config.json` on the
branch ref every time, even though it already wrote a `.no_exist` marker
for the commit after the first 404. `hf_hub_download` never reads that
marker for a branch ref, so every warm online load pays one extra Hub
round trip that can only answer "still not there".

transformers avoids the same cost in `cached_file`: once the commit is
known (`_commit_hash` on 4.x, a `ResolvedRevision` via
`_pinned_commit_hash` on 5.18+), it serves a file the cache records as
missing without calling the Hub.

## Change

- `loader_utils._cached_missing_adapter_error` mirrors that shortcut. It
takes the commit the config probe already used (the memoized
`ResolvedRevision` on transformers >= 5.18, a sha `revision`, or
`config._commit_hash` on older transformers) and calls
`try_to_load_from_cache(model_name, "adapter_config.json", revision =
commit)`. If that returns `_CACHED_NO_EXIST`, it returns the same
`ValueError` text peft raises (`Can't find 'adapter_config.json' at
'<repo>'`), and the loader raises it inside the existing `try`, so the
existing `except` handles it as before.
- Anything it cannot settle falls through to the existing probe
unchanged: config probe failed, local folder, `local_files_only`,
offline env, no known commit, marker missing, file cached,
`FastModel(config = ...)` (a user config says nothing about the repo),
and a revision vLLM dropped for the base (the adapter probe keeps its
own ref).
- No new Hub requests: the resolve is a memo hit from the config probe,
and outside a load scope it is a pass-through.
- `_refuse_network_share_raw_adapter_base` is untouched.

## Results

Warm online load of `hf-internal-testing/tiny-random-LlamaForCausalLM`
up to model dispatch (weights stubbed, CPU), HTTP requests counted at
the `requests` / `httpx` layer. 5 measured loads after one warm-up, 2
sessions per arm (10 loads), base = merge base.

| transformers / hub | entry | requests per load (base -> head) |
adapter_config.json HEADs | PeftConfig probe ms (median) | to-dispatch
ms median, base sessions -> head sessions |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| 4.57.6 / 0.36.2 | FastLanguageModel | 4 -> 3 | 2 -> 1 | 43.2 -> 0 |
143.7, 122.7 -> 87.5, 88.5 |
| 4.57.6 / 0.36.2 | FastModel | 4 -> 3 | 2 -> 1 | 43.5 -> 0 | 197.3,
179.6 -> 154.5, 132.9 |
| 5.18.0 / 1.33.0 | FastLanguageModel | 2 -> 1 | 1 -> 0 | 41.7 -> 0 |
89.4, 88.1 -> 50.5, 49.5 |
| 5.18.0 / 1.33.0 | FastModel | 2 -> 1 | 1 -> 0 | 42.5 -> 0 | 139.3,
203.1 -> 125.4, 116.8 |

Request counts were identical across all repeats. The FastModel wall
time spread between base sessions is larger than the delta, so the
request count and the removed probe time are the result there. The
remaining `adapter_config.json` HEAD on 4.57.6 is the network share

Tests: test_pp_native_fused_ce leaked UNSLOTH_FORCE_CPU=1 into its whole CPU shard (15 reds on unrelated PRs) (#19974)

## Problem

`Repo tests (CPU, rest)` fails the same 15 tests on unrelated PRs (for
example #19518 and #19957). Every failure traces back to one test file
added in #19959, `tests/test_pp_native_fused_ce.py`:

1. **It sets `UNSLOTH_FORCE_CPU=1` at module level and never restores
it.** Collecting the file is enough. From then on, every test in that
pytest worker and every interpreter those tests spawn takes the CPU
route. That breaks tests that rely on the CUDA spoof or on the GPU
import path:
- `test_fp8_full_finetune_dequant.py`: the child goes down the CPU
loader, so no `FineGrainedFP8Config` is passed (`{'cls': 'NoneType',
'dequantize': None}`)
- `test_allow_cpu_import_driverless.py`: `import unsloth` with
`UNSLOTH_DISABLE_CPU_FALLBACK=1` now succeeds ("a device is visible;
this file proves nothing here")
- `test_lazy_openai_import_check.py`, `test_triton_optional_import.py`:
the child prints the CPU banner and the CPU-only warnings their output
checks do not expect
2. **Its own six tests fail even when run alone.** `build()` creates a
DeepSeek-V4.1 model from a config. With unsloth_zoo present, the engram
tables are parameter-free frozen tables that need a checkpoint, and none
is ever bound, so the forward raises `frozen table deepseek_v41 engram
layer 1 is not bound to its checkpoint`. The other DeepSeek-V4.1 tests
that build from a config (`test_deepseek_v41_native.py`,
`test_parallel_deepseek_v41_gloo.py`) call `set_engram_table` first.

Reproduced on main (`60248e78de`) with transformers 5.18.0, PEFT 0.22.0
and TRL 1.19.0, using both the released unsloth_zoo and zoo main:
- The four files together: 14 failed.
- `test_fp8_full_finetune_dequant.py` alone passes. With
`test_pp_native_fused_ce.py` only collected (not selected),
`test_lora_load_keeps_fp8` fails.

## Fix

- `tests/test_pp_native_fused_ce.py`:
- Sets `UNSLOTH_FORCE_CPU` only around the imports that need it
(unsloth_zoo, `pp_native`, the DeepSeek-V4.1 modules), then restores the
previous value.
- `build()` gives each engram table rows with `set_engram_table`, as the
other config-built DeepSeek-V4.1 tests do.
- `tests/conftest.py`, a guard against this kind of leak:
- A `pytest_make_collect_report` wrapper compares the device-route
variables after each test module is collected: `UNSLOTH_FORCE_CPU`,
`UNSLOTH_ALLOW_CPU`, `UNSLOTH_DISABLE_CPU_FALLBACK`,
`UNSLOTH_FORCE_GPU_PATH` and `CUDA_VISIBLE_DEVICES`.
- A module that leaves one changed fails its collection with a message
naming the module and the variable.
- The guard restores the variable, so the leak does not reach the rest
of the run.

## Verification

- `tests/test_pp_native_fused_ce.py`: 7 passed, with CUDA hidden and
with it visible. Before: 6 failed alone.
- The five affected files together, with CUDA hidden as on the CPU
runners: 18 passed, 9 skipped. Before: 14 failed.
- Collecting the whole `tests/` tree with the guard (`--collect-only`,
CUDA hidden): clean, no module trips it.
- Sabotage, with main's `test_pp_native_fused_ce.py` restored and the
guard kept: collection fails with `tests/test_pp_native_fused_ce.py
changed the device route for every later test while it was imported
(UNSLOTH_FORCE_CPU: None -> '1')`.
- `tests/python/test_conftest_bitsandbytes_preimport.py` and
`tests/python/test_accelerator_skip_guards.py`, which read the conftest:
passed.

Studio images: batch MOSS-Image layer by layer so a streamed block uploads once per batch (#19957)

## Studio images: MOSS-Image runs a streamed batch layer-major

Part of the image batching program (Phase 3 item 3). MOSS-Image was the
one family that SGLang and vLLM-Omni batch while Studio did not really
fuse it: `MOSSImageTransformer.forward` looped over the samples outside
the layer loop. On a streamed (offloaded) DiT every block was uploaded
once per row instead of once per batch, so a batch of 4 paid 4 full
weight streams per step, and the batch matrix measured 1.00x.

### What changes

- **Layer loop outer, rows inner.** For a batch of 2 or more on an
offloaded DiT, each `_Block` is called once with a tuple of rows, so its
offload hook moves the block's weights once per call. Inside the block
each row runs the unchanged solo computation at its own shape: its own
text length, its own text refinement, its own mask slice and its own
RoPE table. Nothing is padded and nothing is shared across rows except
the uploaded weights.
- **AdaLN modulation at batch 1.** The timestep MLP and the shared block
/ head modulation now run at batch 1 in this path (once for a shared
timestep, once per row for per-row timesteps). The batch-B GEMM there
was the only thing that made a batched row differ from its solo render
(latent max abs up to 3.0 on main).
- **When it engages.** Only when every block is reached through offload
hooks that move weights and arguments only (diffusers group offload, its
lazy-prefetch tracker, accelerate hooks). Resident weights, compiled
blocks, CUDA-graph or cache wrappers, module forward hooks and gradient
checkpointing keep main's per-sample forward. `layer_major_stats()`
counts layer-major forwards, rows, and the per-sample fallbacks by
reason.
- **Kill switch.** `UNSLOTH_MOSS_LAYER_MAJOR=0` restores main's order
for every batch.
- **Admission.** `coalesce_prompt_key` no longer refuses MOSS outright.
It asks `coalesce_key(pipe)`, which returns a key only for a load that
runs layer-major on a card with a serving verdict in
`MEASURED_BATCH_WINS`. Rows may differ in prompt length. The table holds
one measured entry, `NVIDIA A100-SXM4-80GB`; every other card, and every
resident or compiled load, keeps rendering concurrent MOSS requests one
at a time.

### G1, and why batch bytes change

- A single-image request (N=1) is byte-identical to main, resident and
streamed: N=1 never enters the new path.
- A `batch_size` > 1 request on a streamed load now shares one
layer-major pass, and its bytes change by design. On main each image of
such a batch drifted from the image its own seed renders alone, because
the modulation ran as one batch-B GEMM. Now each image is its own solo
render bit for bit, so a returned seed replays exactly. That path is
gated by G2a, G2c and the row-0 gate below instead of by byte equality
with main.
- Resident batches are unchanged from main (they keep the per-sample
forward).

### Gate table

One Colab A100-SXM4-80GB (torch 2.14.1, diffusers 0.42.1, transformers
5.15.1), weights `unsloth/MOSS-Image-SFT-FP8` (bf16 `transformer/`,
`text_encoder/`, `vae/`), SFT defaults, CFG 2.5, bf16 eager. Main and
head ran in the same process on the same card, interleaved. Streamed =
diffusers block-level group offload, one block per group, with streams.
Gates at 512 px; speed at 1024 px, 10 steps, 3 ABBA repeats.

| Gate | Check | Main | Head | Verdict |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| G1 | N=1 latents, 4 prompts, resident and streamed | | sha256 equal to
main, all 8 | PASS |
| G1 | resident N=2 / N=4 batch latents | | sha256 equal to main
(per-sample kept) | PASS |
| G1 | streamed N=2 / N=4 batch latents | | differ from main by design
(see above) | by design |
| Row 0 | batch rows vs their own solo renders, streamed | max abs 2.75
(N=2 row 0), 2.92 (N=4 row 0) | bit-identical, every row of N=2 and N=4
| PASS |
| Row 0 | same, resident | max abs up to 3.01 | same as main (per-sample
kept) | not promoted |
| G2a | streamed batch of 4, neighbour prompt (other length) or seed

Vision DPO collator: reuse TRL's converted pixel rows for Qwen-VL grids on TRL < 0.29 (#19902)

## Problem

On TRL < 0.29 with Qwen2-VL, Qwen2.5-VL or Qwen3-VL, the vision DPO
collator pays a host side cost twice on the main thread every
micro-batch. The `DataCollatorForPreference` patch from #19857 calls
TRL's own `torch_call`, which already runs
`torch.tensor(example["pixel_values"])` on every row and right pads them
into `(batch, max_patches, dim)`. The grid branch then threw that tensor
away and ran `torch.as_tensor` again on the same nested lists.
Converting the lists is most of the collator's time, so it was paid
twice.

## Change

`rl_replacements.py`, grid branch of the collator patch: slice each row
back out of TRL's padded tensor (`padded[i, :len(rows_i)]`) and
concatenate. The fast path only runs when the padded tensor is 3D with
the batch on dim 0, has the row's trailing shape and dtype, and has the
row's first and last patch row exactly where right padding puts them.
Anything else falls back to converting the rows as before. TRL 0.22.2,
0.25.1 and 0.28.0 all build this tensor with `pad(pixel_values,
padding_value=0.0)` (right padding).
The patch is idempotent.

The tensors reaching the model are bitwise identical to before (keys,
key order, dtypes, shapes, values). No loss math changes.

images, rows written to and fetched from a `datasets` Arrow dataset
(`__getitems__`, as the DataLoader does). Collator wall time per
micro-batch: median of 7 repeats, min to max in brackets. Base is the
merge base, A/A is the base run again. "equal" is `torch.equal` + dtype
+ shape on every output tensor and identical key order.

Studio training: skip unchanged diffusion status replies and the duplicate Train page status poll (#19892)

## Problem

Two Studio status pollers were doing work nobody could see.

1. **Images / Video Train tab.** `DiffusionTrainPanel` polls `GET
/api/train/diffusion/status` every 1.5 s while the tab is open. The
backend keeps a finished run's status, full metric history included,
until the next start. So once a run had finished, every poll returned
the same reply (about 206 KB for a 4000-step run with 6 series and 40
samples). The panel parsed it, rebuilt the loss and grad-norm series and
re-rendered the charts 40 times a minute. It also kept polling at that
rate in a hidden tab.
2. **Train page.** `useTrainingCompletionWatch` (mounted in the sidebar
on every route) polls `/api/train/status` every 6 s during a run. On the
Train page, `useTrainingRuntimeLifecycle` already polls the same
endpoint every 3 s. The single-flight only joins requests that are in
flight at the same moment, so the Train page sent about 30 status
requests a minute instead of 20. Each reply carries the full
`metric_history`.

## Change

Three commits:

- **Diffusion status poll** (`use-diffusion-training-status.ts`, moved
out of the panel unchanged apart from the following):
- The reply is read as text. A reply that is byte-identical to the last
applied one is dropped before parsing, so the status object, its
memoised series and the panel stay as they are.
- When the tab is hidden and the last status is settled (no live worker
and `idle` / `completed` / `stopped` / `error`), the interval skips its
tick. It polls once as soon as the tab is shown again, and only if a
tick was skipped.
- A live run keeps polling at 1.5 s while hidden, so
`onTrainingComplete` (LoRA list refresh) fires at the same time as
before.
- **Completion keyed by job** (`diffusion-train-panel.tsx`): the
completion notice and the run-list refetch also key on `job_id`. A run
started from another tab or client that finishes while this tab is
hidden and skipping settled polls is never seen as `running` here;
keying by job id keeps the LoRA picker and the run history refreshing
when the tab is shown, as before.
- **Train status poller ownership** (`training-status-poll-owner.ts`):
the lifecycle hook registers a predicate that is true exactly when its 3
s status timer polls (mounted, hydrated, not idle, signed in). The
completion watch skips its tick only while that predicate is true. A
pending start (phase still idle), an unhydrated page and every other
route keep the watch as it was. Native notifications still come only
from the lifecycle poll.

## Results

Measured with the real hooks and the real `DiffusionTrainPanel` render
body on both arms (base = merge base), fake timers and a mocked backend.

**Diffusion Train tab, 60 s after a completed 4000-point run**

| Case | Requests base | Requests head | Status applies (panel
re-renders) base | head |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Idle, visible | 41 | 41 | 41 | 1 |
| Idle, hidden | 41 | 1 | 41 | 1 |
| Idle, hidden then shown at 30 s | 41 | 22 | 41 | 1 |
| Running, visible (every reply differs) | 41 | 41 | 41 | 41 |
| Running hidden, completes at 30 s | 41 | 22 | 41 | 22 |

The completed status is applied at 31.5 s on both arms in the last case.
Each skipped apply saves about 1.0 to 1.2 ms of JSON parse plus series
rebuild per poll (206 KB reply). The string compare costs about 0.02 ms.
Chart re-render time is extra and not included.

**Train status, 5 minute run (completes at 4:30)**

| Case | Status requests/min during run, base | head | Native
notifications base | head |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Train page throughout | 29.9 | 20.1 | 1 at 4:30.02 | 1 at 4:30.02 |
| Another route throughout | 9.8 | 9.8 | 0 | 0 |
| Leave Train at 2:00, back at 4:00 | 21.2 | 15.9 | 1 at 4:30.02 | 1 at
4:30.02 |
| Leave Train at 4:00 (completes away) | 27.7 | 19.0 | 0 | 0 |
| Open Train at 4:00 | 12.3 | 11.2 | 1 at 4:30.02 | 1 at 4:30.02 |

One case differs on purpose. If the watch is the first poll to see the
completion while on the Train page, base applies it before the lifecycle
poll can compare before and after, so the "Training finished"
notification is never sent. Head sends it once, on the next lifecycle
poll (2 s later in that case).

## Tests

- `tests/diffusion-train-status-poll.test.ts`: an unchanged finished
status is applied once, a hidden settled tab sends no polls and polls
once on return, a live run keeps polling while hidden and its completion
is applied once.
- `tests/training-status-single-poller.test.ts`: 20 status requests a
minute on the Train page with the watch active, 10 a minute after
leaving, one completion notification after coming back, and the watch
still polls a pending start.
- `tests/training-hidden-tab-polls.test.ts`: stub added for the new
import.
- `npm test`: same failing test IDs on both arms (one KaTeX Vite test
that fails here because `node_modules` is a symlink). `npm run
typecheck` and `npm run build` pass.

Studio images: compress large PNGs in parallel strips, identical pixels (#19933)

## Summary

Studio's fast PNG path (`png_encode.py`) filters rows on a helper
thread, but every image still goes through one `zlib.compressobj`. So
one large PNG deflates on a single core. On a 2048x2048 render that is
about 240 ms of the gallery save.

This PR deflates large images in strips, in parallel, using the layout
pigz uses:
- Each strip of filtered rows is a raw deflate stream. All strips but
the last end with `Z_SYNC_FLUSH`, which leaves a byte-aligned, non-final
block. The last strip ends with `Z_FINISH`.
- Each strip is primed (`zdict`) with the previous strip's last 32 KiB
of filtered rows, so the compression ratio stays the same as one stream.
- Concatenated with the zlib header and the combined Adler-32
(`adler32_combine`), the IDAT data is one standard zlib stream. Any
inflater reads it, and the filtered rows it inflates to are
byte-identical to Pillow's.

Scope:
- Only images of at least 2 MiB of pixel bytes take strips (for RGB that
starts a little above 1024x682). Smaller images keep the existing path,
whose bytes are identical to Pillow's.
- Strip bounds depend only on the image size, never on the thread count,
so the output is deterministic.
- `save_many` splits the CPU count across the encodes it runs at once
(`cpus // workers`), so a batch does not oversubscribe the machine.
Threads per encode are capped at 8.
- Kill switch: `UNSLOTH_IMAGE_PNG_STRIPS=0` restores the single-stream
path, which matches Pillow byte for byte. `UNSLOTH_IMAGE_PNG_FAST=0`
still turns the whole fast path off.
- Any exception still falls back to Pillow.

## Output validity

Large images no longer match Pillow byte for byte. They do match on
decoded pixels and on every non-IDAT chunk. Checked with:
- PIL: same `tobytes()`, mode, size and `info` text chunks.
- `zlib.decompress` of the concatenated IDAT payload. This checks the
header and the Adler-32, and the result equals the inflated Pillow
stream.
- libpng (OpenCV `imdecode`): same pixels for RGB, RGBA, L and LA, with
27 to 47 IDAT chunks.
- ffmpeg's PNG decoder: same raw pixels for all four modes, and nothing
on stderr.

## Speed (CPU only, Xeon Platinum 8559C)

Median of 5, compress level 1 (the Studio default), PngInfo with two
text chunks, smooth image with noise:

| Image | Pillow | fast path, one stream (main) | strips (this PR) | vs
main | size |
|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| 1024x1024 RGB | 118 ms | 61 ms | 24-26 ms | 2.4-2.6x | +0.003% |
| 1024x1024 RGBA | 158 ms | 81 ms | 25-26 ms | 3.1-3.3x | +0.003% |
| 2048x2048 RGB | 474-493 ms | 236-239 ms | 62-63 ms | 3.8x | +0.003% |
| 2048x2048 RGBA | 636 ms | 311 ms | 81-86 ms | 3.6-3.8x | +0.003% |

The numbers come from two repeated runs; the main column moved less than
2% between them. Against Pillow itself the gain is 5-8x.

A batch of four 2048x2048 RGB images, encoded side by side the way
`save_many` does it:

| CPUs available | threads per encode | batch time |
|---|---:|---:|
| 8 | 1 (main) | 374 ms |
| 8 | 2 (this PR) | 356 ms |
| 16 | 1 (main) | 282 ms |
| 16 | 4 (this PR) | 231 ms |

`png_encode` is used only by the image gallery (`image_gallery.py`).
Video frames do not go through it, so there is no video arm.

## Tests

`studio/backend/tests/test_png_encode.py`:
- `test_strips_decode_to_the_same_pixels_and_chunks`: L / LA / RGB /
RGBA x 1 / 5000 / 64 KiB / one-strip sizes. Checks the same pixels and
the same non-IDAT chunks as Pillow, that `zlib.decompress` of the IDAT
equals Pillow's inflated stream, size within +8%, and identical bytes
for 2 and 4 threads.
- `test_large_images_take_strips_small_ones_stay_pillow_exact`: a small
image stays byte-equal to Pillow and never enters the strip path. A
large one takes it and decodes the same. `threads = 1` and the kill
switch give Pillow's bytes again.
- `test_adler32_combine_matches_zlib`, and
`test_save_many_splits_the_cpus_across_its_encodes`.
- The existing "across IDAT buffers" test covers a 40x20000 RGB image,
which is now past the threshold. It now checks Pillow-exact bytes with
`threads = 1`, and pixels plus chunks with strips.

`test_png_encode.py`, `test_image_gallery.py` and the other gallery /
PNG / image route suites: 661 passed.

Studio: render MLX image chats on string-only chat templates (#19912)

## Problem

On the MLX backend, every image chat with
`mlx-community/llava-v1.6-mistral-7b-4bit` failed before generation with
`TypeError: can only concatenate str (not "list") to str`. The single,
resident and batch generation paths all hit it, and so did
`count_chat_tokens`. Text-only chats were unaffected.

## Root cause

This checkpoint ships the old Mistral chat template, which only accepts
string content: `'[INST] ' + message['content'] + ' [/INST]'`. Vision
chats send every message's content as a part list, so
`apply_chat_template_for_generation` raised. Its only `TypeError`
fallback handles tool-call argument normalization, so nothing turned the
parts back into a string. The existing model-aware recovery cannot help
here. It goes through mlx-vlm's `prompt_utils.apply_chat_template`,
which formats `llava_next` as a part list too and hits the same template
error.

## Fix

- `apply_chat_template_for_generation` takes a new optional
`image_marker`. After every existing render attempt and fallback
candidate has failed, it retries once with each part list flattened to a
string. It uses the new helper `flatten_part_lists`.
  - Parts keep their order and are joined with `\n`.
- Each image part becomes `image_marker`. For llava_next this gives
`[INST] <image>\nWhat color? [/INST]`, the same form as the list
template llava-hf ships for this model.
- If the text already contains a typed copy of the marker, it is spaced
out (`< image>`). Otherwise one attached image would produce two
markers. The control-markup sweep builds its marker list from the
template text, and a string-only template never names the image tag, so
the sweep leaves it alone.
- `MLXInferenceBackend._render_vlm_prompt` passes the processor's
declared image token as `image_marker`.

## Risk and tradeoffs

- A template that already renders part lists never reaches the retry, so
its output is byte-identical.

Studio Data Recipes: default Data Designer usage telemetry to off in the recipe worker (#19895)

## Problem

Data Designer 0.5.4 (the version pinned in
`studio/backend/requirements/single-env/data-designer.txt`) has usage
telemetry on by default. After every preview and after every batch of a
full run that used an LLM column,
`ColumnWiseDatasetBuilder._emit_batch_inference_events` enters a
`TelemetryHandler`. Its exit sends one synchronous POST (a fresh
`httpx.AsyncClient`, default 5 s timeouts) to
`events.telemetry.data.nvidia.com`. The payload holds the model name and
token counts. The recipe worker waits for this request to finish before
it reports `job.completed`.

Studio never sets `NEMO_TELEMETRY_ENABLED`, so every Studio recipe pays
one round trip per preview and per batch. On a network that silently
drops outbound traffic, it pays the full 5 s connect timeout.

## Change

`run_job_process` in `studio/backend/core/data_recipe/jobs/worker.py`
now runs `os.environ.setdefault("NEMO_TELEMETRY_ENABLED", "false")` as
its first statement. That is before any `data_designer` import, which
matters because `data_designer.engine.models.telemetry` reads the
variable once at import time. Previews and full runs both go through
this spawned worker, so one line covers both paths.

Because it is `setdefault`, a user who exports
`NEMO_TELEMETRY_ENABLED=true` (or `1`, `yes`) before starting Studio
keeps the current behaviour. The variable is only set in the worker
child process, so the server's own environment does not change. Studio
already does the same for Hugging Face Hub telemetry in its download
subprocesses (`HF_HUB_DISABLE_TELEMETRY=1`).

## Results

Setup: a CPU host, a recipe with one seed file and one `llm-text`
column, 5 rows, served by a local stub OpenAI-compatible endpoint. The
telemetry endpoint was pointed at a local stub
(`NEMO_TELEMETRY_ENDPOINT`) or at an unroutable IP, so no data left the
host. The worker is spawned exactly as `jobs/manager.py` does it. Base
is the merge base `18ba95a`. All numbers are medians over 5 interleaved
repeats with [min, max].

| Case | Metric | Base | This PR | Saved |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Telemetry endpoint responds in 300 ms, preview | end of generation to
usage summary (in worker) | 316.0 ms [315.9, 328.3] | 1.3 ms [1.2, 1.8]
| 315 ms |
| Telemetry endpoint responds in 300 ms, full run | end of generation to
usage summary (in worker) | 324.2 ms [320.9, 332.3] | 6.1 ms [5.8, 8.1]
| 318 ms |
| Telemetry endpoint drops traffic, preview | job start to
`job.completed` | 7.46 s [7.31, 8.36] | 2.40 s [1.76, 2.56] | 5.07 s |
| Telemetry endpoint drops traffic, full run | job start to
`job.completed` | 7.58 s [6.85, 9.20] | 2.37 s [1.86, 2.98] | 5.21 s |

Studio Images: list the gallery in one scandir pass, like the video and audio galleries (#19651)

## Problem

`image_gallery.list_images()` lists the folder with `Path.glob("*.png")`
and then runs `Path.stat()` on every PNG just to sort by mtime. That
runs on every `GET /images/gallery` page, every resync page, twice per
Library listing (one per shelf) and on every drag-reorder (`move()` does
the same glob + per-file stat over the whole shelf). A page reads at
most `offset + limit + 1` recipes, but pays one `Path` object and one
stat for every image in the gallery.

On Windows each `Path.stat()` opens a handle to the file (roughly 20 to
60 us each), so a 2000 image gallery spends tens of milliseconds per
page on stats the page never uses. The video gallery (#16372) and the
audio gallery (#16367) already list with one `os.scandir` pass.

## Change

Port the video gallery pattern to images:

- `_listed_pngs()`: one `os.scandir` pass with `Path.glob("*.png")`'s
exact matching: case folded on Windows only (`_GLOB_FOLDS_CASE`),
`Path(name).stem` for dot-led names (`.png`, `..png`, `.hidden.png`),
directory order kept, a failed or partial scan lists nothing (as glob
did).
- The sort key comes from `DirEntry.stat()` (follows symlinks like
`Path.stat`). It is free on Windows and the same single stat per file on
POSIX.
- The recipe cache key (dev, ino, size, mtime_ns, ctime_ns) on POSIX is
that same stat result, so cache hits and misses are unchanged. On
Windows, where `DirEntry.stat()` reports `st_ino` / `st_dev` as 0, a
real `os.stat` is taken just before the read, and only for the records
the page actually reads.
- `move()` builds its shelf order from the same scan.

Unchanged: ids, order (equal mtimes keep directory order, as the stable
sort over glob's output did), records, `order_at`, pin / archive
shelves, `has_more`, the `valid` filter, error handling (unlistable
folder lists nothing, a PNG whose stat fails sorts as mtime 0 and is
read uncached, a PNG deleted before its keying stat is skipped).
`clear()` and `delete()` are untouched.

repeats (range = per-process medians). Base A and Base B are the same
base tree run twice (A/A).

(19.9-23.7) | 23.9 ms (23.6-24.1) | 12.0 ms (7.4-13.5) |

On Linux the kernel still sees one stat per file (`strace -c`: base 4000

Studio: share one forced llama.cpp update check across hook copies and one release fetch per status pass (#19658)

## Problem

Every non-passive copy of `useLlamaUpdateCheck` forces a check one
second after it becomes enabled. The corner update card does that on
each page load, and the Audio page keeps its copy mounted and toggles
`enabled` with the tab, so every entry into the Audio tab forces again.
Landing on `/audio` forces twice at the same moment, since nothing
shares a read in flight.

On the server, a forced `GET /api/llama/update-status` refreshes the
llama.cpp, whisper.cpp and audio.cpp release lists
(`releases?per_page=30` on the GitHub API, once per repo). In the common
state (automatic backend, no update pending) it also passes
`force_refresh` into `_pending_backend_migration`, which skips the 24 h
`_backends_memo` and spawns `install_llama_prebuilt.py
--resolve-backends latest`. Measured locally, that child takes 3.7 s
wall, peaks at 665 MB RSS and sends 6 more HTTP requests to GitHub
hosts. When an update is available, each component sends the same
`releases?per_page=30` request twice in one pass: once for the tag
(`latest_published_release`) and once for the asset sizes
(`latest_release_assets`). Anonymous GitHub API calls are limited to 60
per hour per IP, so this pattern spends that budget quickly.

## Change

Frontend (`use-llama-update-check.ts`):
- Hook copies share one module-level forced read while it is in flight.
- An automatic check (first check after enable, hourly reminder, snooze
expiry, cross-tab resync) that comes within 5 minutes of a successful
forced read reads the cached status (`GET /api/llama/update-status` with
no `force_refresh`). The server has just refreshed those caches, so it
returns the same answer without calling GitHub or running the resolver.
The timestamp is also kept in `localStorage`, so a reload inside the
window reuses it too.
- `refresh()` (the Settings Check button) always forces. A failed or
unauthenticated forced read is not recorded, so the next automatic check
forces again. A recorded time in the future (clock moved back) is
ignored.

Backend (`freshness_flow.py`, `llama_cpp_update.py`):
- `shared_release_fetches()` scopes one `get_update_status` pass. Inside
it, the tag lookup and the asset-size lookup for the same repo read one
release object, picked by the same newest-published selection. Both
memos are filled exactly as two fetches would fill them. Failures are
not shared, each pass (each request) still fetches fresh, nested passes
join the outer one, and outside a pass nothing changes.

The backend-migration resolver keeps its current behaviour: an explicit
check and the first automatic check in a window still force it. Only the
redundant automatic repeats are gone, so a backend migration is detected
exactly when it was before.

real hook and backend code run against a fake llama.cpp + whisper.cpp +
audio.cpp install. Requests are counted per user scenario, base

Studio Translate: one cached-model listing per disk probe, and no re-probe on RAM-only system updates (#19644)

## Problem

Translate checks which of its models are already on disk after every
mount and after every run. Two things made it send more of those
requests than it needs:

1. `withStableSchemes` in `use-gpu-info.ts` keeps the previous
`denseQuantSchemes` array when a new `/api/system` snapshot has the same
contents, but `checkpointQuantFormats` is rebuilt by
`normalizeDenseQuantSchemes` on every snapshot, even when it is empty.
So any snapshot that moves free RAM by more than the 0.25 GiB drift
tolerance hands out a new array. Translate's `offeredModels` memo
depends on it, so the disk probe effect aborts and sends all of its
probes again (3 GGUF variant listings, plus 3 `/api/hub/cached-models`
reads on FP8 GPUs). The FP8 fallback effect and the Hub page's
`diffusionQuantFormats` / `filteredDiscoverRows` memos also recompute
for nothing.
2. On FP8 GPUs each of the 3 FP8 rows calls `listCachedModels()` on its
own, so one probe pass sends 3 identical `/api/hub/cached-models`
requests.

## Change

- `withStableSchemes` now holds the previous `checkpointQuantFormats`
array when its contents and order match, with the same rule it already
used for `denseQuantSchemes`. Each list is held on its own; a real
change is still published as the new array. Every consumer (Translate,
Hub, the chat model picker, the model selector) reads it through
`useMemo` / `useEffect` deps or a `join(",")` key, so equal contents
give the same output.
- `translate-runner.ts` adds `sharedCachedModelsListing(signal)`, a lazy
one-shot listing, and `translateModelDownloaded` takes it as an optional
`cachedModels` option. The page's probe pass creates one per pass, so
the FP8 rows share one request. Each row still gets `true` / `false` /
`null` exactly as before, and a failed or aborted listing still gives
every row `null`. Other callers (the pre-run check and the download
check) keep their own read.
- The page's disk probe also re-runs when the app's model inventory
version changes (`useInventoryVersion`, the signal the Audio page and
Translate's own downloaded list already use). Before this change a
download that finished while Translate was open only refreshed the
badges by accident, when the system monitor's RAM poll republished the
format list; now a finished download, a delete or another tab refreshes
them directly, and ordinary reads still do not.

## Results

Harness: the real `useGpuInfo` hook, `/api/system` subscription,
`translateModelDownloaded`, `quantOnDisk` and chat API client, bundled
from each tree and rendered in jsdom with a mocked `fetch`; the page's
memo and probe effect copied verbatim from each tree. Base is the merge
base.

| Scenario | Request | Base | Head |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| FP8 GPU, mount | `/api/hub/cached-models` | 3 | 1 |
| FP8 GPU, mount | GGUF variant listings | 5 | 5 |
| FP8 GPU, per run end (x3) | `/api/hub/cached-models` | 3 | 1 |
| FP8 GPU, per run end (x3) | GGUF variant listings | 4 | 4 |
| FP8 GPU, 5 snapshots moving RAM by 1 GiB each |
`/api/hub/cached-models` | 15 | 0 |
| FP8 GPU, 5 snapshots moving RAM by 1 GiB each | GGUF variant listings
| 20 | 0 |
| FP8 GPU, 5 snapshots | probe passes run | 6 | 1 |
| Non-FP8 GPU, 5 snapshots | GGUF variant listings | 20 | 0 |
| FP8 GPU, cached-models returns 500, per run end |
`/api/hub/cached-models` | 3 | 1 |

The offered model menu and the per-model on-disk map are identical
between base and head in every scenario, including the failing listing
(FP8 rows stay unknown in both).

## Tests

- `tests/translate-probe-dedupe.test.ts`: one listing per pass for the 3
FP8 rows, identical per-row results with and without sharing, a failed
listing and an aborted pass give `null` for every row, no listing when
no FP8 row asks, separate callers keep their own read, and the page
wires one listing per pass.
- `tests/dense-quant-schemes-identity.test.ts`: a RAM-only move keeps
the `checkpointQuantFormats` identity (including an empty list), a real
change is published, and the two lists are held independently.
- Full frontend `npm test`, `npm run typecheck` and `npm run build`
compared against the merge base.

Studio: remember the install source until the unsloth dist-info changes (#19643)

## Problem

`detect_install_source()` in `studio/backend/utils/update_status.py`
runs on every request to `/api/studio/update-status` (fetched twice per
web page load, by the sidebar and the update banner) and
`/api/studio/install-source` (every About tab open). For a plain PyPI
install there is no `direct_url.json`, so each call parses `RECORD` and
calls `Path(dist.locate_file(f)).resolve()` on every `unsloth/`,
`unsloth_cli/` and `studio/` entry before answering `pypi`. The
2026.11.12 wheel has 2738 such entries, so every request pays about 0.2
s of filesystem work on a threadpool worker on Linux. On Windows each
`resolve()` opens a file handle, so it is expected to be several times
slower there (not measured).

## Change

- Memoize the answer per process, keyed on the dist-info path plus
`(st_mtime_ns, st_size, st_ino)` of `RECORD`, `direct_url.json`,
`installed-files.txt` and `SOURCES.txt` (absence included). A reinstall,
upgrade or downgrade rewrites or moves these, so the answer is
recomputed.
- `direct_url.json` (PEP 610) is still read on every call, as before,
and wins when present; only the `RECORD` file scan is memoized, and its
result is stored only when a second stat after the scan still matches
the key, so metadata rewritten mid-scan is never pinned.
- `distribution("unsloth")` still runs per call, so a missing
distribution or a changed `sys.path` is seen immediately; the
missing-distribution branch is not memoized.
- Answers that depend on a Git checkout on disk (package files outside
`site-packages` / `dist-packages`) are never memoized, since `.git` is
not part of the key. A distribution without a filesystem path, or a
metadata `stat` error other than not-found, also skips the memo.
- `UNSLOTH_DISABLE_UPDATE_CHECK` and `UNSLOTH_STUDIO_FAKE_UPDATE` are
still read on every call after detection; nothing env-dependent is
cached.
- Frontend unchanged.

## Results

Real PyPI-style install (`uv pip install --no-deps unsloth==2026.11.12`,
Python 3.12, Linux x86_64), 5 processes per arm, 20 warm calls each:

| Arm | First call | Warm call (median of medians) | Warm range across
processes | `resolve()` per warm call |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| base, A/A run 1 (5 procs) | 220 to 255 ms | 218 ms | 211 to 221 ms |
2738 |
| base, A/A run 2 (3 procs) | 232 to 253 ms | 233 ms | 225 to 240 ms |
2738 |
| head (5 procs) | 233 to 314 ms | 0.08 ms | 0.079 to 0.107 ms | 0 |

Saved per request after the first: about 215 ms on Linux, so roughly 0.4
s per web page load and 0.2 s per About tab open. The first call per
process does the same work as before.

Answer parity, base vs head, in both a PyPI venv and a `uv pip install
-e` editable venv (21 scenarios each, all identical): real install,
`UNSLOTH_DISABLE_UPDATE_CHECK=1`, `UNSLOTH_STUDIO_FAKE_UPDATE`, env
cleared again, crafted dist-info with git `vcs_info`, editable
`dir_info`, `file:` archive, malformed `direct_url.json`,
`direct_url.json` removed, `RECORD` rewritten, `RECORD` removed, legacy
checkout outside site-packages with and without `.git` (and `.git`
removed again), distribution missing. A real in-process downgrade (`uv
pip install --reinstall unsloth==2026.11.11` between two calls)
recomputes and still answers `pypi`.

## Tests

- New `studio/backend/tests/test_install_source_memo.py` (13 tests): a
`direct_url.json` seen only mid-detection is not reused, `RECORD`
rewritten mid-scan is not memoized, memo hit without rescanning,
`RECORD` rewrite recomputes, `direct_url.json` added / rewritten /
removed for editable, vcs, local path and unknown URLs, Git-checkout
answer not memoized and flips with `.git`, missing distribution not

per call after a memo hit.

`tests/studio/test_studiobench_ci_update_checks_off.py`: 285 passed on

Studio RAG: keep the warm vector cache when a document is ingested (#19885)

## Problem

Every Studio RAG upload threw away the warm dense vector cache for its
scope, so the append fast path from #15961 never ran on a real ingest.

`ingestion._run` calls `store.set_document_embedding_model(conn,
document_id, identity)` after encoding. In the normal case `identity`
matches what `start_ingestion` already wrote through
`create_document(embedding_model=effective_identity)`, but the function
still ran `UPDATE documents SET embedding_model=? WHERE id=?`. The
`rag_vec_epoch_document_model` trigger (`AFTER UPDATE OF
embedding_model`, no `WHEN` clause) fires whenever the column is in the
SET list, even if the value is unchanged. That bumped the scope epoch
before `add_chunks` read `epoch_before`. Then `vec_cache.note_append`
and `_note_ann_append` saw `entry.epoch != before` and dropped the
entry. The next search fell back to a vec0 scan and queued a full
rebuild. On scopes at or above `RAG_VEC_ANN_MIN_ROWS`, every uploaded
file caused a full usearch HNSW rebuild plus an index write.

## Change

`set_document_embedding_model` now only writes when the value changes:

```sql
UPDATE documents SET embedding_model=? WHERE id=? AND embedding_model IS NOT ?
```

The row ends up the same as before. A real identity change (backend swap
mid-job, a NULL legacy identity, or a `vectors-dropped:` prefix) still
updates the row, so the trigger still bumps the epoch. The trigger
itself is unchanged, so this needs no schema migration. A `WHEN OLD IS
NOT NEW` clause on the trigger would not be equivalent:
`replace_document_vectors` (re-embed) deletes and rewrites `chunks_vec`
rows, which has no trigger, and it depends on its same-identity UPDATE
to bump the epoch.

## Results

Setup: synthetic `rag.db` scope built through `store.create_document` /
`add_chunks`, 384-dim stub encoder, CPU only. The cache is warmed with
one search, then one small `.txt` goes through the real
`ingestion.start_ingestion` path. After that I count `vec_cache._build`
/ `vec_ann.new_index` / `vec_ann.save` calls and time the next 3
searches, querying with the new document's own vector. 3 repeats per
cell. Medians are shown with the [min, max] of the first search. The
host was shared and loaded, so absolute times are noisy, but the gaps
are far larger than the spread between repeats.

| Scope | Arm | Epoch bumped | Cache entry kept | Rebuilds | HNSW
new_index / save | Rebuild time (s) | 1st search ms | 3rd search ms |
Searches served by vec0 |

19.2] | 15.4 | 3 of 3 |

Studio chat: send pasted text exactly as pasted, not re-decoded by its XML charset (#19695) ## Problem When a long paste is turned into a text attachment, `TextAttachmentAdapter.add` and `send` (`studio/frontend/src/features/chat/runtime-provider.tsx`) called `readTextAttachmentOnce(file)`, which reads the paste's bytes back and decodes them like an uploaded file. That decoder honours an XML declaration, so a paste that starts with an XML prolog is re-decoded in whatever charset the prolog names, even though the bytes were written as UTF-8 by the browser a moment earlier. - Pasting `café` (plus enough text to cross the paste threshold) sends `cafÃ©` to the model. - Pasting a prolog whose charset the browser has no decoder for (for example `encoding="x-bogus-charset"`) fails the paste entirely with "Could not attach the pasted text" and a "not UTF-8 text" toast. - The composer chip preview (`file.text()`) and the pure-paste queue path (`pastedTextOf`) both show the original text, so the preview, a queued message and a sent message disagreed. ## Change `readTextAttachmentOnce` takes an optional `pasted` string. When it is given, the cached attachment text is that string as a UTF-8 encode and decode would leave it (one leading U+FEFF dropped, lone surrogates become U+FFFD), with no read or decode of the File. The text adapter passes `pastedTextOf(file)` in both `add` and `send`; for anything that is not a paste it is `undefined`, so uploaded and dropped files go through the existing byte decoder unchanged. Because the cache is seeded with the same string, the mixed-attachment queue snapshot (`snapshotQueuedTextAttachments`, which reads `cachedTextAttachment`) also carries the exact pasted text. Restored paste drafts are recreated with `createPastedTextFile`, so they keep the paste marker and get the same behaviour after a reload. As a side benefit, a multi-megabyte paste is no longer read back from the Blob and decoded a second time. `text-attachment-accept.ts` still has no runtime imports, which keeps it out of the chat barrel cycle guard. No UI, toasts for real files, size limits, paste threshold, chip rendering or draft persistence changed. ## Results | Case | Before | After | | --- | --- | --- | | Paste with `encoding="ISO-8859-1"` prolog and `café` | sent `cafÃ©` | sent `café` | | Paste with `encoding="x-bogus-charset"` prolog | paste refused, two error toasts, nothing sent | attached and sent verbatim | | Mixed queue snapshot (paste + uploaded file) | pasted part `cafÃ©` | pasted part `café` | | Plain UTF-8, leading U+FEFF, lone surrogates paste | UTF-8 byte decode | identical to the byte decode | | Uploaded `.xml` declaring ISO-8859-1 | decoded as ISO-8859-1 | unchanged | | Uploaded UTF-8 `.xml` declaring ISO-8859-1 | `cafÃ©` | unchanged | The first two rows were also checked in headless Chromium against the built frontend with a mocked backend: a synthetic paste of the XML text, Enter, and the persisted message body captured from the `PUT /api/chat/threads/.../messages` request on both builds. ## Tests - New `studio/frontend/tests/pasted-text-original-string.test.ts`: 4 tests fail before this change and pass after (ISO-8859-1 paste, unsupported charset paste, mixed queue snapshot, adapter wiring); the plain UTF-8, U+FEFF, lone surrogate and uploaded `.xml` cases pass on both sides and compare against the byte decode. - `npm test`, `npm run typecheck`, `npm run build` in `studio/frontend`. ## Before / after Two isolated Studio installs (merge base `a14868116` left, head `455f51320` right), no model: a keyless external checkpoint lets the composer send. First a long paste starting with `` and `café` is sent (BEFORE posts `cafÃ©`, AFTER posts `café`), then a long paste declaring `encoding="x-bogus-charset"` is left in the composer: BEFORE refuses it with two error toasts and no chip, AFTER attaches it. ![Pasted XML text before and after](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/danielhanchen/unsloth-staging-2/pr-media/pr/19695/pr19695_ui-c75deda71143.png)

Tests: give the from_pretrained precision harness the real _gguf_load helpers (rest red on main) (#19963)

## Summary

`Repo tests (CPU, rest)` is red on `main` since #19947. All 20 tests in
`tests/test_optimized_precision_conflicts.py` fail:

```
AssertionError: from_pretrained reached `from .._gguf_load import require_gguf_package`: stub it in the loader fixture
```

The test compiles `FastLanguageModel.from_pretrained` out of `loader.py`
without importing the package. It rewrites each relative import to read
the name from its fixture environment, and fails by name when the
fixture lacks one. #19947 added `from .._gguf_load import
require_gguf_package` at the top of `from_pretrained`, so every case now
stops there. The code is right; the fixture just did not know the new
module. This is the same failure #19917 fixed for
`gguf_drop_bitsandbytes` from #19889.

## Fix

The fixture loads `unsloth/_gguf_load.py` itself, which imports only
`importlib` and `os`, and offers every function in it with `setdefault`,
so an explicit stub still wins. The real `require_gguf_package` runs. No
case passes `gguf_file`, so it returns at once. Helpers added to
`_gguf_load.py` later are covered without another fixture change, which
is the robust part: one-name-at-a-time stubbing is what broke twice.

## Verification

`main`: 20 failed, the error above.

GGUF loads: keep the load hook first, and fix the MLX harness for the new relative import (rest-2 red on main) (#19961)

## Summary

`Repo tests (CPU, rest-2)` is red on `main` since #19947, with 11
failures in two files:

```
tests/test_import_keeps_plain_model_backends.py::test_every_from_pretrained_starts_with_the_load_hook
E   AssertionError: ('unsloth/models/loader.py', 'FastLanguageModel')
E   assert '_unsloth_load_begins' in ['require_gguf_package']

tests/test_mlx_bf16_gpu_family.py::test_loader_default_dtype_follows_gpu_family[...]   (10 cases)
unsloth/__init__.py:419: in _mlx_from_pretrained
    from ._gguf_load import refuse_gguf_on_mlx
E   KeyError: "'__name__' not in globals"
```

Two separate causes:

1. **Load hook order.** In both `FastLanguageModel.from_pretrained` and
`FastModel.from_pretrained`, #19947 put `require_gguf_package(...)`
ahead of `_unsloth_load_begins()`. The guard requires every
`from_pretrained` to start with the load hook. Here the code is wrong
and the guard is right: the hook only applies the cuDNN SDPA settings
for an Unsloth load and loads nothing, so running it first costs the
GGUF check nothing.
2. **MLX test harness.** `test_mlx_bf16_gpu_family.py` compiles
`_mlx_from_pretrained` out of `unsloth/__init__.py` and execs it in a
bare namespace, so the package is never imported. #19947 added a
relative `from ._gguf_load import refuse_gguf_on_mlx` inside that
function. A relative import needs `__package__` in the function's
globals. The code is right and the harness is wrong.

## Fix

- `unsloth/models/loader.py`: `_unsloth_load_begins()` first, then
`require_gguf_package(...)`, in both loaders. Same checks, same order of
anything that can fail.
- `tests/test_mlx_bf16_gpu_family.py`: the harness loads the real
`unsloth/_gguf_load.py` as `unsloth._gguf_load`, without importing the
package, and execs the function with `__name__` / `__package__` =
`"unsloth"`, so the relative import resolves as it does in production.

Studio setup (Windows): a custom-home install no longer repoints another install's inductor cache (#19927)

## Summary

`studio/setup.ps1` writes `TORCHINDUCTOR_CACHE_DIR` to the USER
environment, and the value comes from whichever Studio home the run
used. A second install with a custom `UNSLOTH_STUDIO_HOME` (a test
install, a portable copy) therefore repointed the real install's
inductor cache for every later process on the account. We saw this on a
DGX Spark class Windows box: a scratch run moved the value from `C:\tc`
to `C:\work\0023\studio_home_emul\cache\torchinductor`. Studio launches
then compiled into the scratch tree, and once that tree was cleaned up
the stray directory came back.

## Fix

A new helper, `Test-TorchCacheMayPersist`, now gates the USER write:

- Default home: it persists as before. That install owns the
account-wide value, so rerunning setup also fixes an account the old
behaviour already hijacked.
- Custom home: it persists only when the USER value is unset, already
equals the value being written, or already points inside this same home
(an earlier run of this install wrote it).
- Otherwise the value is set for this run's process only, and setup
prints a line naming the value it kept.

Staged installs (`UNSLOTH_STUDIO_STAGE_ROOT`) still never persist.

The MAX_PATH reason for the setting still holds. The path selection
(long paths on: `<home>\cache\torchinductor`; long paths off: `C:\tc`;
whitespace and apostrophe refusals) is unchanged. When a custom-home
install skips the write, its launches inherit the other install's value,
and an earlier setup chose that value to avoid MAX_PATH too.

## Why not drop the persistence

I looked at the other option: stop persisting and let every Studio entry
point set the variable for its own process. The backend resolver
(`storage_roots._setup_cache_env`) already pins
`TORCHINDUCTOR_CACHE_DIR` to `cache_root()/torchinductor` when the
variable is unset, and the Tauri env list forwards it. But the resolver
has no long-paths awareness. On a machine with long paths off, the
persisted `C:\tc` is the only thing that carries the MAX_PATH fallback,
so dropping it would bring back the MAX_PATH failures the setting exists
to prevent. Moving that logic into the resolver is a bigger change, and
it would also need care for the uninstaller's cleanup of persisted
values.

## Other platforms

`install.sh` and `studio/setup.sh` do not persist any inductor or cache
variable into shell profiles or `launchctl`, so macOS and Linux do not
have this bug. `install.ps1` only writes probe values at USER scope and
clears them right away.

## Tests

`tests/test_setup_master_root.py`:

- `test_a_custom_home_never_repoints_another_installs_inductor_cache`
runs the shipped function in pwsh. It covers the reported case, another
install's tree, a user's own directory, a sibling-prefix home, unset /
same / inside-home values, and the default home healing a hijacked
value.
- `test_the_user_inductor_cache_write_is_gated_on_ownership` checks that
the only USER write of the value sits behind the check and that the
check is passed `$StudioHomeIsCustom`.

Both fail on `main` and pass here. The full file passes (48), as does
`studio/backend/tests/test_setup_cache_env_containment.py`, and
`setup.ps1` parses cleanly.

Studio desktop: clear the composer drop overlay when the window loses focus or is hidden (#19373)

Related to #19346

**Problem.** On the desktop app, the composer's "Drop files here"
overlay follows the native Tauri drag state (`useNativeModelDrop`). Only
a `leave` or `drop` event clears it. If neither arrives, the overlay
stays over the composer: the report shows the model name and tools
hidden under it, with the controls still responding to the cursor but
invisible.

**Root cause (Linux, reproduced).** The reporter is on Ubuntu, so the
webview is WebKitGTK. wry 0.57.0's GTK handler emits `Enter` from
`drag-data-received` and only acts on `drag-leave` when it has already
seen an `Enter`. When the file list reaches the window after the pointer
has left it, `drag-leave` is ignored and the late `Enter` is never
followed by anything. A minimal wry 0.57.0 app under Xvfb (webkit2gtk
2.50.4, a separate GTK drag source, pointer driven by XTest) shows it:

| Drag | Last wry event |
|---|---|
| file dragged in, moved, dragged out (control) | `Leave` |
| same, pointer passes over the window for 20 ms | `Leave` (3 of 3 runs)
|
| pointer crosses the window with no dwell, no added delay | `Enter {
paths: [...] }`, nothing after it |
| source answers in 50 ms, pointer passes for 20 ms | `Enter { paths:
[...] }`, nothing after it |
| source answers in 1.5 s, released outside or cancelled with Escape |
`Enter { paths: [...] }`, nothing after it |

So a file dragged across the app on its way somewhere else is enough;
the user never dropped anything on it.

**Change.** The overlay state is reset to idle on window `blur`, `focus`
and `pointerdown`, and on document `visibilitychange`. None of these can
happen during a native drag, so a stuck overlay clears as soon as the
user clicks in the app, switches windows, or minimizes and restores. If
a drag really is still over the window, its next `over` event brings the
overlay back from the paths kept from `enter`. The drop itself reads the
paths from its own event, so nothing is lost. The listeners are removed
in the effect's cleanup. The browser build is unchanged (the effect
returns before adding them).

**Tests.** `tests/native-drop-overlay-clears-off-window.test.ts` drives
the real hook with a fake webview, with `window` and `document` stubbed
separately so a listener on the wrong target fails:
- after `enter` then `blur` / `focus` / `pointerdown` /
`visibilitychange`, the overlay is idle. These 4 fail on the merge base
(the overlay stays `attach`) and pass here.
- a drag still over the window shows the overlay again on its next
`over`.
- every listener is removed on cleanup.

Results: full frontend suite 17225 pass, 0 fail; `npm run typecheck`
clean; Biome and ESLint report the same diagnostics on the changed file
as on main.


**Before / after (real Unsloth Desktop on Linux, WebKitGTK).** Both
sides are a debug build of the app under Xvfb, with the same backend.
BEFORE is main `dba2cd170`, AFTER is this PR `a1b20cf43`. A GTK file
drag crosses the window without stopping (the wry race above, triggered
for real, not injected), then a real click lands on an empty part of the
chat page. Row 1: both sides are stuck under "Drop files here". Row 2:
after the click, main is still stuck and this PR shows the normal
composer. The greeting text is picked at random, and the audio-runtime
toast on the left is unrelated.

after](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/danielhanchen/unsloth-staging-2/pr-media/pr/19373/composite-eb6744541732.png)

Studio: show the Thinking switch for llama.cpp models served by repo id (#19501)

Related to https://github.com/unslothai/unsloth/issues/19486

## Problem

`llama-server -hf unsloth/Qwen3-8B-GGUF:Q4_K_M` reports its model as
`unsloth/Qwen3-8B-GGUF:Q4_K_M` (llama.cpp uses the `-hf` repo as the
model alias, `common_params_model::get_name`). Studio looks llama.cpp
and vLLM models up in the model catalog by bare name, and that lookup
never strips the `-GGUF` repo suffix, so every model served straight
from a GGUF repo was treated as a non-reasoning model and the composer
showed no Thinking switch. The same model loaded with `-m
Qwen3-8B-Q4_K_M.gguf` got the switch. Windows `-m` paths, sharded files
(`-00001-of-00009.gguf`) and dated checkpoints such as
`DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash-1017` missed the same way.

## Fix

A local-server lookup (`resolveLocalServerCatalogEntry`) used only by
the llama.cpp / vLLM path:
- treats `\` as a path separator, drops a trailing `-GGUF` (with or
without a `:QUANT` tag) and a `-NNNNN-of-NNNNN` shard suffix before the
existing name lookup;
- when that still misses, retries once without a trailing 4-digit date
tag, so `DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash-1017` resolves to `deepseek-v4.1-flash`.

Ollama keeps the existing lookup untouched. Nothing about the request
wire changes: the backend already forwards `enable_thinking` /
`reasoning_effort` as `chat_template_kwargs` for llama.cpp, the switch
was just never shown.

## Evidence

- Live, llama.cpp b12722 CPU build, `llama-server -hf
unsloth/Qwen3-0.6B-GGUF:Q4_K_M --jinja`: `/v1/models` id is
`unsloth/Qwen3-0.6B-GGUF:Q4_K_M`; `chat_template_kwargs:
{enable_thinking: true}` returns 608 chars of `reasoning_content`,
`false` returns none and the answer directly. Before this change that id
resolves to `supportsReasoning: false`, after it resolves exactly like
`Qwen3-0.6B-Q4_K_M.gguf`.
- Differential over all 396 public `unsloth/*-GGUF` repos, each as repo
id, `repo:UD-Q4_K_XL`, two file names and a shard name, for `llama_cpp`,
`vllm` and `ollama` (5940 cells): 586 cells move, all from no switch to
a switch, 0 Ollama cells move, 0 cells that already had reasoning
change, and every moved repo id now resolves identically to its plain
file name.
- New test in `tests/model-catalog.test.ts` fails on main and passes
here; the full frontend `node --test` failure set is identical before
and after.


## Before / after

Same CPU llama-server (`-hf unsloth/Qwen3-0.6B-GGUF:Q4_K_M --jinja`)
added as a llama.cpp connection on a Studio built from the merge base
and one built from this branch. Before, the composer model picker for
`unsloth/Qwen3-0.6B-GGUF:Q4_K_M` offers only "Preserve thinking"; after,
it offers the Thinking switch and the chip reads "Thinking". (The extra
llama icon in the after tab bar is the connection tab finishing loading,
not part of this change.)

![Before / after: Thinking switch for a llama.cpp
connection](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/danielhanchen/unsloth-staging-2/pr-media/pr/19501/pr19501_before_after-78eb4cbd7c95.png)

setup.ps1: pin the elevation probe in the unattended-UAC tests (red on elevated Windows runners) (#19926)

## Summary

`setup.ps1 units, no-VS resolve, VC++ round-trip (windows-latest)`
(Studio Windows installer smoke) fails on `main` since #19864, and the
same three tests failed on #19864's own run:

```
[-] UNSLOTH_NONINTERACTIVE=1 answers True     Expected $true, but got $false.
[-] UNSLOTH_NONINTERACTIVE=yes answers True   Expected $true, but got $false.
[-] a CI run cannot answer a prompt           Expected $true, but got $false.
```

`Test-SetupUacUnanswerable` in `studio/setup.ps1` returns `$false` early
when the process is already elevated. That is correct, since an elevated
process never sees a UAC prompt. But GitHub's Windows runners run
elevated, so on a runner the function never reaches the
`UNSLOTH_NONINTERACTIVE` / `CI` logic the tests check.

The code is right and the test is wrong: it depended on the elevation of
whatever machine runs it. The `install.ps1` copy
(`Test-InstallUacUnanswerable -Elevated ...`) avoids this by taking
elevation as a parameter. On Linux the probe throws and is treated as
not elevated, which is why the tests pass locally.

## Fix

- `studio/setup.ps1`: the elevation probe moves into its own function,
`Test-SetupProcessElevated`, with the same
`WindowsPrincipal.IsInRole(Administrator)` check and the same
not-elevated answer when the probe throws. `Test-SetupUacUnanswerable`
calls it at the same point as before, so behaviour is unchanged.
- `tests/studio_setup_ps1/Studio.Setup.UnattendedUac.Tests.ps1`:
- Each test pins elevation through a stub of that function, `$false` by
default.
- New: an elevated run answers `$false` even with
`UNSLOTH_NONINTERACTIVE=1` or `CI=true`. The elevated branch was
untested before.
- New: `Test-SetupUacUnanswerable` must call `Test-SetupProcessElevated`
and contain no direct `IsInRole`, so the stub cannot silently stop being
consulted.
  - New: the real probe returns a `[bool]`.

## Verification

- `Invoke-Pester Studio.Setup.UnattendedUac.Tests.ps1` (pwsh 7, Linux):
26 passed, 0 failed.
- `Invoke-Pester Studio.Setup.SelfRerun.Tests.ps1`, which also loads
`setup.ps1` functions: 39 passed.
- Runner condition reproduced: with the stub defaulted to elevated,
exactly the three tests that fail on the Windows runner fail
(`UNSLOTH_NONINTERACTIVE=1`, `=yes`, `a CI run cannot answer a prompt`),
and the other 23 pass.

Not run here: the real elevated Windows runner. This PR's own Windows
installer smoke job covers that.

Studio: headless image and video API requests no longer build a live preview (#19928)

## Summary

Headless image and video API requests now pass `live_preview=False`, so
the engine no longer builds the per-step latent previewer for renders
that nothing displays.

## The bug

- `/v1/images/generations` reaches the engine two ways, and neither
passed `live_preview`:
  - the coalesced batch kwargs in `_batched_openai_images`;
  - the solo fallback in `_generate_openai_images`.
- `generate(live_preview=None)` then hits `preview_wanted(None)`, which
returns True unless `UNSLOTH_DIFFUSION_PREVIEW=0` is set
(`core/inference/diffusion_preview.py`).
- On CUDA, every API render therefore built a `LatentPreviewer`. That
means per-step `project()` work on the GPU plus the publish path, for a
caller that never polls `generate-progress`.
- `/v1/videos` had the same gap in `_start_openai_video`. The chat video
tool and MCP video jobs start there too.
`VideoBackend.begin_generate(live_preview=None)` builds the same
previewer.

The fix reuses the existing pattern: the Detailer pass and cross-account
batches already pass `_live_preview_kwarg(backend.generate, False)`. For
engines without the parameter (sd.cpp), the helper still passes nothing,
so their call shape is unchanged.

## What does not change

- The output. The previewer only reads the step latents and never writes
them back.
- The Images and Video pages. They still send their own `live_preview`
and keep their previews.
- Coalescing. `live_preview` is already in `_COALESCE_KEY_IGNORED`.
- An API request that leads a batch now shows no preview for that batch.
  - Before, that preview was row 0, which is the API caller's own image.

## Other entry points checked

- Studio has no OpenAI edits, variations or batch image routes.
`/v1/images/generations` is the only headless image route.
- The chat `generate_image` tool goes through
`_generate_diffusion_image_core` with `live_preview=None`, so it still
builds a previewer. It is left as is here and can be a follow-up.

## Tests

New tests fail on the merge base and pass here:

-
`test_openai_images_generations_route.py::test_headless_requests_never_build_the_live_previewer`:
solo path. Base gives `[(None, True)]`.
-
`test_openai_images_batching.py::test_a_coalesced_headless_batch_never_builds_the_live_previewer`:
coalesced path, with two requests in one batch.
-
`test_openai_videos_route.py::test_headless_video_jobs_never_build_the_live_previewer`:
the `/v1/videos` job reaches `generate` with `live_preview=False`.


`test_openai_videos_controls.py::test_a_plain_openai_request_sends_the_old_kwargs_plus_a_seed`
pins the exact kwarg set. It now allows `live_preview` and asserts that
it is False.

Related suites: 22 files, including the OpenAI image/video routes, image
batching and concurrency, MCP video, video queue, media auto-switch,
account isolation and the preview tests. Result: 689 passed, 9 skipped.
The batching test was rerun 5 times and stayed green.

## Not measured

The GPU time saved per step was not measured. On CPU the previewer is
never built (`LatentPreviewer.create` returns None off CUDA), so a CPU
number would not mean anything. A CUDA A/B would check `emitted == 0`
and equal PNG hashes, for example Z-Image-Turbo at 1024px with
concurrent b64 requests.


## Device results

NVIDIA RTX PRO 6000 Blackwell (Colab G4), torch 2.14.1+cu130, diffusers
0.42.1. Base is the merge base `532afbed81` and head is `59a8e757c7`,

alternating, 3 processes per arm.

Each process runs the real `/v1/images/generations` route in process
against a loaded `unsloth/FLUX.2-klein-4B`: 1024x1024, 4 steps, fixed
seed, b64_json. Each process sends 1 warmup and then 3 timed requests.

| delta |

| per-image wall (ms) | 747.6 | 2.4 | 744.4 | 3.1 | -3.2 (-0.4%) |

/ 0 | | |

Studio diffusion: Z-Image and Krea-2 prompt encodes skip the KV cache and keep only the hidden states they read (#19929)

## Summary

Z-Image and Krea 2 prompt encodes no longer build a text-encoder K/V
cache nobody reads, and they keep only the hidden states the pipeline
consumes. #17118 and #17182 shipped the same pattern for Qwen-Image-2.1
and FLUX.3. The prompt embeddings are bit-identical.

## The gap

In diffusers 0.42.1 (the Studio pin), the shipped transformers 5.5.4 and
also 4.57.6:

- **`ZImagePipeline._encode_prompt`** calls `text_encoder(...,
output_hidden_states=True).hidden_states[-2]`. The Img2Img, Inpaint,
ControlNet and Omni variants use the same code.
- **`Krea2Pipeline.get_text_hidden_states`** calls `text_encoder(...,
output_hidden_states=True)` and stacks `hidden_states[i] for i in
text_encoder_select_layers`. With the default select layers that is 12
entries.

Neither passes `use_cache`. The `Qwen3Model` / `Qwen3VLModel` config
default (`use_cache=True`) therefore builds a `DynamicCache` for a
single forward. The forward also keeps all `num_hidden_layers + 1`
hidden states alive until the helper returns.

## The change

- **New `core/inference/diffusion_te_lean.py`.**
`lean_text_encode(pipe)` wraps whichever of the two helpers the pipeline
has:
- A forward pre-hook sets `use_cache=False` for that call only. A direct
forward of the same encoder still caches as configured.
- `diffusion_te_select.run_selected` records only the read entries:
`(-2,)` for Z-Image, and `pipe.text_encoder_select_layers` (read at call
time) for Krea 2.
- Anything unexpected re-runs the stock call. That includes an index
outside the plan, a recorder that did not fire, and a forward that still
built the full tuple.
- **The wrapper is installed only when the class method's source still
has the expected call.** Other pipelines are left alone.
- **It reads `pipe.text_encoder` at call time,** so a later quantised
swap is covered. It composes with the dead-tail truncation: passthrough
slots keep the stack length.
- **It is marked transparent for the prompt cache.**
- **Installed in `diffusion.py`** next to the Qwen-Image-2.1 hooks:
after TE truncation and quantisation, before `cond_cache` and
`prompt_cache`.
- **Kill switches:**
  - `UNSLOTH_DIFFUSION_TE_NO_KV=0` turns the wrapper off.
- `UNSLOTH_DIFFUSION_TE_SELECT_HIDDEN=0` (existing) keeps the stock
hidden states but still skips the cache.

## Exactness

`tests/test_diffusion_te_lean.py` runs the real diffusers helper methods
on hand-built instances with tiny random Qwen3 / Qwen3-VL encoders on
CPU (6 layers, offline):

- The stock call builds a cache; the lean call builds none.
- The selective encode engages: `diffusion_te_select.call_count()` goes
up by one, so there was no silent fallback.
- The outputs are bitwise equal (`view(torch.int32)`). For Z-Image that
is the per-prompt masked embeddings; for Krea 2, the stacked states and
the mask.
- Install is idempotent, the wrapper is prompt-cache transparent, both
kill switches behave, and unrelated pipelines are untouched.

Passes on transformers 5.5.4 + diffusers 0.42.1 (the shipped pin) and on
transformers 5.17.0 + diffusers 0.42.1 (latest). On 4.57.6 the
encoder-level check (stock `hidden_states[i]` vs the selective encode
with `use_cache=False`) is bitwise equal for both encoders. The
diffusers-level test could not be imported there, because that
environment's diffusers does not import.

## CPU measurement

Method: real pipeline helpers, transformers 5.5.4, fp32, 8 threads, one
process per arm, run twice in ABAB order. RSS peak is a coarse proxy,
because the CPU allocator keeps freed pages.

| family | shape (H, layers, B, L) | stock median s | lean median s |
stock peak RSS MiB | lean peak RSS MiB |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| Z-Image | 64, 6, 1, 512 | 0.0060 / 0.0059 | 0.0047 / 0.0047 | 382 |
379 |
| Z-Image | 64, 6, 8, 512 | 0.0298 / 0.0316 | 0.0300 / 0.0273 | 415 |
394 |
| Krea 2 | 64, 6, 8, 512 | 0.0162 / 0.0158 | 0.0130 / 0.0124 | 422 | 405
|
| Z-Image | 1024, 12, 1, 512 | 0.216 / 0.228 | 0.180 / 0.186 | 1141 |
1083 |
| Z-Image | 1024, 12, 8, 512 | 1.995 / 1.703 | 1.543 / 1.441 | 1664 |
1343 |
| Krea 2 | 1024, 12, 1, 512 | 0.210 / 0.180 | 0.206 / 0.250 | 1190 |
1189 |
| Krea 2 | 1024, 12, 8, 512 | 1.449 / 1.448 | 1.482 / 1.477 | 1651 |
1422 |

- Peak memory drops wherever the saved tensors are large enough to show
in RSS: up to 321 MiB for Z-Image and 229 MiB for Krea 2 at B=8.
- Z-Image encode time drops by 10 to 20 percent.
- Krea 2 time is flat within noise, about +2 percent at B=8. Krea 2
still keeps 12 states, and its B=1 runs are noisy.

Assuming 36-layer, 2560-hidden, 8-KV-head bf16 encoders (not checked
against the real configs here), the arithmetic gives these
per-prompt-row savings at L=512:

- about 75 MB of K/V cache for both families;
- about 94 MB of hidden states for Z-Image (36 of 37 dropped);
- about 65 MB of hidden states for Krea 2 (25 of 37 dropped).

These are estimates, not GPU measurements.

## Not covered

- No GPU run. The CUDA peak and encode time at the real encoder sizes
are not measured here.
- The diffusers-level test does not run on transformers 4.57.6; only the
encoder-level check does.
- The trainers' own Z-Image caption encode
(`core/training/diffusion_lora_trainer.py`) is untouched.


## Device results

Tests: stop test_css_culprit leaking its synthetic CSS tree into the cached scan (#19950)

## Summary

`Repo tests (CPU, studio)` can fail on `main` since #19932, depending on
how xdist places the files:

```
tests/studio/test_sibling_rules_have_a_key.py::test_no_frontend_rule_ends_a_sibling_relation_on_a_keyless_compound
E   AssertionError: found too few CSS rules under studio/frontend/src to trust the scan
E   assert 4 > 1000
```

Seen on the staging runs for #19837 and #19903.
`tests/studio/_css_culprit.py`'s `css_rules()` is `lru_cache`d per
process. `test_css_culprit.py` points `SRC` at a synthetic tree and
clears the cache. When its `monkeypatch` restores `SRC`, the cache still
holds the synthetic tree's four rules, so a later scan of the real CSS
on the same worker reads those instead. The minimum-count assertion in
#19932's test is the check that caught it. Before, `test_css_culprit.py`
was the cache's only user.

## Fix

- `test_css_culprit.py`: an autouse fixture clears the cache after each
test, so the synthetic tree cannot outlive the test that made it.
- `test_sibling_rules_have_a_key.py`: clears the cache before scanning
and asserts that every rule comes from `studio/frontend/src/`, so a
stale or foreign cache fails loudly instead of passing on a handful of
rules.

## Verification

- `pytest tests/studio/test_css_culprit.py
tests/studio/test_sibling_rules_have_a_key.py`, in this order: 21
passed. On `main`: 1 failed, the error above.
- The reverse order: 21 passed on both.
- Each half alone is enough: with only the `test_css_culprit.py` change,
or only the scan-side change, the failing order passes.
