Studio ROCm gfx1151: Linear weight row pitch K + 64 outside TunableOp-covered GEMMs (Wan -7% s/step, Krea-2 -19%) (#19874) ## Summary On ROCm gfx11 cards, Studio can now store the denoiser's 16-bit `nn.Linear` weights with a padded row pitch: each weight becomes a view of an `[N, K + 64]` buffer, re-stored once on the first forward. On Strix Halo (gfx1151), hipBLASLt runs these GEMMs faster when the weight's leading dimension is not a power-of-two stride. The GEMM is the same one with another leading dimension, and the output was `torch.equal` on every GEMM measured. A TunableOp row is keyed on the leading dimension, so a padded weight misses Studio's shipped gfx1151 table and takes another solution. Off the table it is 0.90-0.94x on the Qwen-Image-2.1 / FLUX.3 klein GEMMs, and the render is no longer byte-identical to main. The default therefore never pads a weight whose `(N, K)` has a row in the loaded TunableOp results, for any family. Every GEMM that main served from the table keeps its solution, and every padded GEMM is one that main ran untuned. So the default render is byte-identical to main. ## What changes - New `diffusion_rocm_weight_pitch.py`, installed from `diffusion_speed.apply_speed_optims` on ROCm targets only, for `transformer`, `transformer_2` and `unet`. - Eligible: a plain `nn.Linear` with a contiguous bf16 / fp16 weight on the card and `in_features >= 1024`. - Never touched: - INT8 / FP8 / torchao weights, by dtype and tensor type; - `nn.Linear` subclasses; - offloaded weights; - weights already strided; - calls under torch.compile tracing. - Table rule, read from the rows TunableOp actually holds (`torch.cuda.tunable.get_results()`): - **Default (env unset):** every weight whose `(N, K)` has a `tn_*` row stays contiguous, for any family. If the table is active but unreadable, nothing is padded. - **`UNSLOTH_DIFFUSION_ROCM_WEIGHT_PITCH=

` (explicit):** only the family rule applies. A family the shipped tables were tuned on (`qwen-image-2.1`, `flux.3-klein`, `flux.3-klein-base`, `flux.2-klein`) keeps its covered weights. So does any family while the user tunes (`UNSLOTH_DIFFUSION_ROCM_TUNABLEOP=tune`) or has a local tuned cache. Other families pad every eligible weight. This is faster on Wan, but some small Wan GEMMs leave their tuned rows (see below). - After the re-store, the replaced contiguous weights go back to the driver (`empty_cache`, never while a stream is capturing). Without that, the caching allocator held about 5 GiB more reserved memory on Wan 5B, which is system RAM on an APU. - Arch gate: gfx11 only. On by default for gfx1151, the measured arch; other gfx11 cards only through the env var. - Engagement counts are kept in `STATS` (`padded`, `skipped_table`, `skipped_other`, `bytes`). The first forward logs one line. Env: `UNSLOTH_DIFFUSION_ROCM_WEIGHT_PITCH=0` turns it off; `=

` (a multiple of 8) forces pitch P on any gfx11 card with the family rule. Weight memory grows by P / K, which is 0.4-2%. ## Measurements AMD CI gfx1151 (Strix Halo). Linux stack: torch 2.11.0+rocm7.13.0, Triton 3.6.0; Windows: torch 2.11.0+rocm7.14.0. Each arm ran in a fresh process, ABBA over 3 rounds, after one untimed warm-up arm. Values are medians, and the spread is the range across rounds. | | main | pitch | change | frames vs main | |---|---|---|---|---| | Real diffusers `Krea2TransformerBlock`, 4608 tokens | 250.5 ms | 206.7 ms | 1.21x | `torch.equal` | | Wan 2.2 5B 832x480x49 Windows (no table rows hit), s/step | 6.76 s | 6.38 s | -5.6% | byte-identical | | Wan 2.2 5B Windows, wall | 85.58 s | 82.82 s | -3.2% | | | Wan 2.2 5B Linux, explicit pitch (family rule), s/step | 5.28 s (spread 0.3%) | 4.85 s (0.1%) | -8.2% | LPIPS 0.119 (small GEMMs left the shipped table) | | FLUX.3 klein 1024^2 Linux, table active, default rule | 23.63 s | 23.67 s | +0.2% (spread 0.5%) | byte-identical; 269 kept for the table, 0 padded | | Qwen-Image-2.1 1024^2 Linux, table active (INT8 default) | 27.24 s | 27.23 s | 0.0% | byte-identical; 6 kept, 0 padded | - **Why Wan on Linux drifts with the explicit pitch:** main's shipped klein / Qwen table also holds rows that Wan 5B hits: its 3072 x 3072 projections at the text length, and the M = 1 timestep rows. Padding those weights moves the GEMMs to an untuned solution, which gives the 0.119 LPIPS after 8 steps. Same-arm repeats are byte-identical. - **What the default keeps on Linux Wan:** those shapes stay contiguous, and only the uncovered weights (the FFN) are padded. Linux rerun (run with this branch's final default rule): | | main | this PR (default) | change | frames vs main | counts | |---|---|---|---|---|---| | Wan 2.2 5B 832x480x49, s/step | 5.14 s (spread 0.2%) | 4.78 s (0.4%) | -7.0% | byte-identical | 62 padded, 242 kept for the table | | Wan 2.2 5B, wall | 64.88 s | 62.06 s | -4.3% | | | | Wan 2.2 5B, peak reserved | 24.05 GiB | 24.47 GiB | +0.4 GiB (was +5.2 GiB before the storage release) | | | | Krea-2 Turbo 1024^2, 8 steps (Studio default: bf16 DiT, INT8 text encoder) | 49.08 s wall, 6.00 s/step | 39.85 s, 4.84 s/step | -18.8% wall, -19.2% denoise | byte-identical | 261 padded, 0 kept | The explicit pitch (family rule) on the same Wan run was -8.2% denoise with LPIPS 0.096 against main, so it stays opt-in. Krea-2 is the same either way: its GEMMs have no table rows. ## Kernel checklist This ships no kernel: it re-stores existing weights through torch (`torch.empty` plus `copy_`) and every GEMM stays on hipBLASLt. The rules that still apply: - **Exactness:** - Every GEMM is `torch.equal` padded vs contiguous on gfx1151 (smoke: 9 DiT shapes, Linux and Windows). - With the default rule, renders are byte-identical to main (klein and Qwen-Image-2.1 with the shipped table, Wan on Windows). - **Kill switch:** `UNSLOTH_DIFFUSION_ROCM_WEIGHT_PITCH=0` installs no hook. With env unset it is on only for gfx1151, and GPU detection only widens. - **Compile:** the re-store runs in the denoiser's first-forward pre-hook, before any compiled block traces, and is skipped while compiling. The measured product flow compiles the Wan denoiser and pads 304 Linears. - **Inference mode:** the padded buffers are allocated under `inference_mode(False)`, so a first forward inside `inference_mode` cannot turn the weights into inference tensors. A test runs backward afterwards. - **Memory:** the replaced storage goes back to the driver once (`empty_cache`, skipped while a stream is capturing). Weight memory grows by P / K. - **Device / dtype:** the arch is read per weight device. bf16 / fp16 dense weights only; INT8 / FP8 / torchao tensor subclasses are skipped by dtype and type. - **Engagement:** `STATS` (padded, kept for the table, other skips) and a log line, checked through Studio's real load path on both OSes. Gaps: - gfx11 cards other than gfx1151 are opt-in and unmeasured. - A LoRA fused into the weights after the first forward drops the pitch (correct, just unpadded). ## Tests `studio/backend/tests/test_diffusion_rocm_weight_pitch.py` (CPU, no GPU), 18 tests. They fail on main (the module does not exist) and pass here. They cover: - the arch / env gate; - exact re-store and counts; - the one-time storage release, and a first forward under `inference_mode`; - INT8 / fp32 / subclass / strided skips; - the default rule: every covered `(N, K)` kept for any family; - the explicit family rule: table family kept, other family padded; - no table, tune mode, local cache, unreadable table; - that every shipped table name maps to `TABLE_FAMILIES`; - the first-forward hook; - the ROCm-only wiring. ## Not covered - gfx11 cards other than gfx1151 (opt-in only). - LTX-2.5 and H3 end to end (model size on this harness). In the untuned micro, LTX-2.5's Linear sums were 1.30x faster. - LoRA fused into the weights after the first forward replaces the padded storage with a contiguous one (correct, just unpadded).

Studio: Use file-scoped links for chat downloads (#19846)

Downloading a generated chat file put the session credential in the download URL, which browsers keep in download history. Downloads now use a short-lived (5 minute) HMAC link scoped to one sandbox session, file and account, minted by POST /api/inference/sandbox-download-link for UI sessions only (API-key and keyless callers get a 403 and download with their bearer header). The download route still runs its containment, O_NOFOLLOW and inode checks under the minting account. Studio: stop every modal open and close from restyling the whole page in long chats with math (#19932)

## Summary

Opening or closing any modal (Settings, dialogs, modal menus) restyled
the whole page in Chromium once the chat had KaTeX math in it. This
fixes the cause instead of the limit: the area matrix's
`length:settings=5` allowance from #17466 is removed and Settings is
held to the default 2.0x again.

## Cause

Two rules ended a sibling relation on a compound with no class, id or
attribute:

- `.composer-run-settings :has(+ [data-pinned-footer])`
- `.browser-web-toolbar > form ~ div` (inside the narrow `@container
browser` block)

Chromium matches a rule like that against every element of that kind
(every element for the bare `:has()`, every `div` for `~ div`).
Evaluating the sibling part marks the element's parent as having
children styled by their siblings, whether or not the rule then matches.
`<body>` got marked as soon as a portal child was styled.

Once a chat contains math, Chromium's MathML stylesheet is loaded, and
its `mmultiscripts > mprescripts ~ :nth-child(...)` rules make the
sibling invalidation for a marked parent cover its whole subtree. Radix
inserts its focus guards before `#root` on every modal open and removes
them on close, and the overlay is removed while the content after it is
still there. Each of those steps restyled the entire document, thread
included.

Reproduced in isolation: a plain page with `.a ~ div {}` and one
`<math>` element restyles 3,006 elements when a child is inserted at the
start of `<body>`. Without the math it restyles 1.

## Fix

- `index.css`: `.composer-run-settings [data-pinned-footer-above]` and
`.browser-web-toolbar > .browser-web-toolbar-trailing`, each keyed on a
marker.
- `model-config-page.tsx`: the row above the pinned footer carries
`data-pinned-footer-above`, under the same `variant === "page"`
condition as the footer.
- `browser-panel.tsx`: the web toolbar's trailing actions carry
`browser-web-toolbar-trailing`. That is the only `div` after the address
form.
- `tests/studio/_area_matrix.py`: `length:settings=5` is removed from
`KNOWN_DEFAULT`.
- New `tests/studio/test_sibling_rules_have_a_key.py`:
- Fails on any rule under `studio/frontend/src` whose last compound has
no class, id or attribute and has `+` / `~` before it or a `:has(+ ...)`
/ `:has(~ ...)` in it. An `:is()` / `:where()` with only keyed arguments
counts as a key.
  - Self-tests the check on known keyed and keyless selectors.
- Pins that the new markers are still rendered where the old selectors
matched.

## Evidence

Chromium (Playwright), the gate's own page and fixture, separate
`vite.long-thread.config.ts` production builds of the merge base
`28e0714de9` and this branch. Main was measured twice per round (A/A),
alternating with this branch, 3 rounds. Each cell is the median over
rounds of the median of 3 Settings opens on one page, with the min and
max of those per-round medians in brackets.

| Settings open + close | turns | main (A/A, n=6) | this PR (n=3) |
|---|---|---|---|
| elements restyled, default | 40 | 5,732 (5,723-5,737) | 2,444
(2,442-3,234) |
| elements restyled, default | 200 | 6,369 (6,363-6,376) | 2,448
(2,442-2,448) |
| elements restyled, liquid-3d | 40 | 5,764 (5,763-5,779) | 2,472
(2,471-2,478) |
| elements restyled, liquid-3d | 200 | 6,412 (6,403-6,419) | 2,471
(2,471-2,478) |
| style recalc ms, default | 200 | 116 (113-120) | 55 (53-56) |
| style recalc ms, liquid-3d | 200 | 175 (161-185) | 74 (73-77) |
| CPU ms, default | 200 | 386 (361-427) | 311 (301-318) |
| CPU ms, liquid-3d | 200 | 545 (518-580) | 412 (411-433) |

Every row is outside main's A/A spread, apart from default CPU at 40
turns, where the ranges touch: 365 (334-385) on main, 303 (297-338)
here.

Path engagement: after one Settings open, inserting an element at the
start of `<body>` restyles 1,585 elements on main and 1 on this branch.
Deleting only these two rules from main's live page has the same effect,
and deleting the other 107 sibling rules does not.

Full area matrix (`LONG_THREAD_ONLY_AREAS=1`,
`LONG_THREAD_AREAS_KNOWN=""`, so every allowance is off): passes on this
branch. Settings is 2,533 -> 2,532 elements from 40 to 200 turns (main

5,924).

Layout is unchanged. Both rules were laid out with each build's own CSS:
- The row above the pinned footer keeps its 20px bottom margin, and gets
0px on this branch without the marker.
- The narrow toolbar's trailing actions stay right-aligned, 6px from the
edge, and move next to the nav buttons on this branch without the
marker.

The Settings dialog over a 200-turn chat renders pixel-identically: both
screenshots have the same md5. Focus is in the dialog while it is open,
Escape closes it, and focus returns to the page, the same on both
builds.

The new test fails on `main`, flagging exactly these two rules, and
passes here (21 passed with `test_css_culprit.py`).

## Not proven here

- **The 2.0x length check itself.** At this merge base, main also passes
it, because the whole-page restyle already happens at 40 turns (5,732
elements), so the ratio stays near 1.1x. The limit was set from a run
where the 40-turn reading happened to be cheap. What this PR removes is
the cost itself, about 3,300 to 3,900 fewer elements restyled per open
and close at both lengths. It does not turn a failing length ratio into
a passing one.
- **Other engines.** WebKit and Firefox were not measured. The mechanism
is Chromium's invalidation, and the WebKit browser-pane and overlay
allowances are separate work.

Studio: Keep whole attachments available after chat compaction (#19841)

When a local GGUF chat compacts, the document auto-search now retries whole-document retrieval against the compacted prompt instead of the pre-compaction history, so an attachment that fits once older turns are gone is sent whole instead of as ranked excerpts. The retry is accepted only within the fit's own target (headroom, plus the recall reserve on rolling fits) and, when it grows the prompt, within the unfitted size admission already priced; conversation recall and the transcript link are counted inside that bound. Chats with audio or video, which no fit prices, keep the excerpts. Source cards are deferred until after the fit so they show what was actually sent.

Studio diffusion: reuse the text-encoder dead-tail verdict across loads, settle unified memory on stable reads (#19919)

## Summary

Two changes to the diffusion load path, both with zero output change:

1. **Text-encoder dead-tail probe verdict is cached across loads.**
`truncate_text_encoders` runs several `encode_prompt` forwards on the
host before placement to find how many decoder layers the DiT reads
(FLUX.2 klein 4B: 27 of 36). A sampling profile of a FLUX.2 klein 4B
bf16 load put this at about 23% of the load on an RTX Spark (about 6.7 s
of 29.5 s, the matmuls run on the ARM CPU in bf16) and about 5% on an
RTX 5090 desktop. The verdict is structural, so it is now stored in
`<studio cache>/diffusion_te_truncate.json` and reused when nothing it
depends on has changed.
2. **Unified-memory settle stops on stable reads.**
`settled_snapshot_device_memory` takes up to three reads one second
apart and keeps the maximum. On unified memory the idle early exit never
fires (host RAM in use keeps free below total minus the reserve), so
every load on an integrated GPU waited 2 s (8% of the Spark load). Two
consecutive unified reads that agree within max(256 MiB, total/200) now
end the settle.

## Cache key

`core/inference/diffusion_te_truncate_cache.py` keys a verdict on
everything the probe can depend on:

- the pipeline class and the code of every method on its MRO, plus
instance attributes (callables by code, simple values by repr), so an
instance-level patch or a different reader is a different key
- per text encoder: class, `name_or_path`, config JSON, the forward code
of every module class inside it, per-module instance attributes, and
parameter and buffer names, shapes, dtypes plus the first values of each
(views only, never a full copy)
- the pipeline config and model path, the family, Python, torch,
transformers and diffusers versions, `UNSLOTH_DIFFUSION_TE*` /
`UNSLOTH_FUSED_FORWARD` env, and a digest of the probe's own source
files

A miss, an unkeyable pipeline (function-local shims such as the LTX-2.5
worker's, meta or opaque tensors, opaque callables), explicit
`encode_kwargs`, a failed probe, a tampered or unreadable file, or an
encoder the probe would now skip all fall back to probing as before.
Only successful probes are stored. Building the key takes about 15 ms
for a 36-layer encoder. `UNSLOTH_DIFFUSION_TE_TRUNCATE_CACHE=0` turns it
off.

The probe still runs before placement on a miss: running it after
placement would place the layers it exists to drop (1.7 to 2.4 GiB on
FLUX.2 klein 4B).

## Settle change scope

Only `unified_memory` / `system_memory` readings take the stable stop. A
rise or a fall between reads keeps waiting, so a release or a tenant in
flight is still waited out. Discrete VRAM keeps the full spacing, since
a transient tenant on a busy card is what that spacing is for.
`UNSLOTH_SETTLE_UNIFIED_STABLE_STOP=0` restores the old behaviour.

## What the profile's import share was

The profile attributed 38 to 61% of the load to imports, about a third
of it `unsloth/__init__`. That part does not happen in Studio: the
profiler imported `core.inference.diffusion` without the
`UNSLOTH_IS_PRESENT=1` that `main.py` and `run.py` set, so
`diffusion_patch_backend._helpers()` imported the whole `unsloth`
package to set it. In Studio's environment the same install only imports
`unsloth_zoo.temporary_patches.utils`:

| fresh process, CPU, median of 5 | eager patch install | single-file
fp32 wrapper | `unsloth` imported |
|---|---|---|---|
| profiler environment (no `UNSLOTH_IS_PRESENT`) | 2.71 s | 4.18 s | yes
|
| Studio environment | 0.55 s | 4.06 s | no |

The single-file wrapper's time is the first import of diffusers
(quantizers, bitsandbytes, transformers), which the load needs anyway
and which the opt-in "media" startup warm already moves to server start.
Studio's own patch installs take about 1 ms and its source inspection
about 3 ms of a load, so this PR does not change them.

## Tests

- `tests/test_diffusion_te_truncate_cache.py` (new): second load reuses
the verdict and stays byte-identical; the key is stable across
processes; a weights, config, reader, family, layer count, source or env
change is a miss; a changed reader gets its own correct verdict; kill
switch, corrupt or tampered file, explicit `encode_kwargs`,
function-local shims and declined probes are never cached; meta weights
are unkeyable.
- `tests/test_diffusion_settle_unified_stable.py` (new): stable unified
reads stop after one wait and keep the max; rising or falling reads,
discrete VRAM and the kill switch keep every read; tolerance bounds.
- `tests/test_diffusion_load_settle_reuse.py`: the unified case of
`test_other_cuda_memory_kinds_keep_settling` turns the stable stop off,
since it tests the resident-replan shortcut, not the read count.
- Both new files fail on the base commit and pass here. The related
suites (truncate, settle, memory, diffusion and video backend, prewarm,
prequant, LTX) fail the same 2 tests on base and head and nothing else
(head 2189 passed, base 2152 passed without the new files)

Studio FP8: fused Triton row-wise GEMM on Windows cards without row-wise _scaled_mm (#19898)

Stacked on #19871 (base branch
`studio-fp8-rowwise-cublas-not-supported`).

## Problem

Windows torch wheels have no row-wise fp8 `_scaled_mm`. Since #19665,
Studio runs every fp8 GEMM on those cards as a tensorwise `_scaled_mm`
at scale 1 with an fp32 output, followed by a separate row/column scale
epilogue. The fp32 `[M, N]` round trip costs FLUX.2 Klein 4B about 25%
per denoise step in eager mode and 15% compiled, compared with the Linux
row-wise CUTLASS kernel.

## Fix

On those cards (and only on sm_89 and sm_12x), the GEMM and the epilogue
run as one Triton kernel
(`core/inference/diffusion_fp8_triton_gemm.py`):

- fp32 accumulator, then `acc * a_scale * b_scale + bias`, the same fp32
operations in the same order as `_scale_epilogue`. Each step is pinned
to round-to-nearest (`libdevice.mul_rn` / `add_rn`, no FMA contraction,
eager or re-emitted by Inductor), with one rounding to bf16 / fp16.
- Eager calls launch the autotuned kernel directly. Under
`torch.compile` it is a `torch.library.triton_op`, which Inductor
inlines, so there is no graph break and no extern GEMM.
- Per arch:
  - sm_12x (RTX 50xx, RTX PRO 6000, RTX Spark): eager and compiled.
- sm_89: eager only. On an L4 the compiled fallback is as fast or faster
at 512 rows on some shapes (kernel up to 1.24x slower there), so a trace
keeps today's route.
- Every other arch, ROCm, and cards that have the row-wise kernel:
unchanged.
- Accumulate mode: fast-accumulate calls take it everywhere it runs (the
kernel matched cuBLAS's fast-accumulate output bit for bit).
Precise-accumulate calls take it only on a card whose accumulator check
passed; elsewhere they keep cuBLAS. That matters for Studio's own FP8
load: it seeds the hosted pre-quantized denoiser
(`unsloth/FLUX.2-klein-4B-FP8`), whose Float8Tensors are baked with
`use_fast_accum=False`.
- Accumulator check (per card, at install): rows whose exact product is
0, so only the accumulator's rounding residue survives (about 2**-22 of
the largest partial sum for fp32, 2**-11 for a 14-bit accumulator). It
passes when the kernel's residue is within 4x cuBLAS precise
accumulate's, or under 2**-16.
- Operand gate: 2-D e4m3 activation (row-major) and weight (torchao's
column-major `weight.t()`), scales `[M, 1]` / `[1, N]`, optional 1-D
bias, bf16 / fp16 output. Every offset the kernel forms must fit in 32
bits, strided views included. Anything else keeps the tensorwise route.
- Self-check: at install, every card in use runs every shipped config,
with and without bias, on integer-valued operands with power-of-two
scales, where every step is exact in fp32. The result must match the
fp32 reference bit for bit. fp16 output is checked on its first eager
call.
- A mismatch, or a config that cannot compile, keeps the tensorwise
route for that dtype.
- An OOM during the check is no verdict: the check runs again on the
next call.
- A failed launch turns the kernel off for that card and falls back for
the same call. An OOM while autotuning keeps that one shape on the
fallback.
- Setting up the kernel can never fail the install: today's route stays
installed.
- Autotuning uses 6 fixed configs. The key is rows rounded up to a power
of two (capped at 8192), N and K; Triton >= 3.3 caches the choice on
disk. A shape that is not yet tuned is never launched inside a CUDA
graph capture, where it would sync to benchmark: that call takes the
fallback. A traced call only takes the kernel for a dtype the self-check
has already passed.
- Kill switch: `UNSLOTH_DIFFUSION_FP8_TRITON_GEMM=0`. It is registered
as a compile-graph switch.
- Compile cache key: an install with the compiled kernel appends
`:gemm=triton-<cards>-<sha256[:12] of the kernel file>`. torch's FX /
AOT caches key a `triton_op` without its source, so an edited kernel can
never be served stale. Eager-only installs (sm_89) keep their old key.
- `fp8_gemm` status gains `triton_gemm: {eager, compiled,
precise_accumulate}` and a `triton_gemm` call count.

Builds with the row-wise kernel (Linux) never import the module or
Triton through it. Their routing, compile key and output are unchanged.
ModelOpt FP8's own unit-scale GEMM (`diffusion_modelopt_fp8.py`) is not
touched here.

Studio: read safetensors with pread on integrated NVIDIA GPUs (#19905)

## Summary

Image and video loads onto an integrated NVIDIA GPU (DGX Spark, RTX
Spark, Jetson) now read every safetensors shard with the `pread` backend
instead of mmap, on Windows and Linux, for both transformers and
diffusers components.

On unified memory, mmap is the slow path. A mapped shard faults in page
by page while its tensors are copied into the same RAM, and the mapping
stays in the working set until the load ends. `pread` reads each tensor
straight into its buffer.

Measured with the same microbenchmark (FLUX.2 klein 4B bf16 shards, warm
cache, safetensors 0.8.0, ABBA order, `safe_open(backend=...)` then
`.copy_()` into preallocated CUDA tensors):

| Device | Component | mmap | pread | Peak working set |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| RTX Spark (Windows ARM64, `is_integrated` True) | transformer, 7.75 GB
| 3.96 s | 2.18 s (1.81x) | 8.1 GB to 0.87 GB |
| RTX Spark | text encoder, 8.05 GB | 4.76 s | 2.17 s (2.20x) | |
| RTX 5090 (Windows x64, discrete) | both | faster | 1.32x / 1.45x
slower | 10x lower |
| DGX Spark (Linux, user report) | | 19.6 s | 0.84 s | |

Discrete cards are faster with mmap, so they keep it.

## Changes

- `host_pinning.cuda_is_integrated(device)`: reads
`torch.cuda.get_device_properties(index).is_integrated` for the load's
own target device, through the existing cached
`device_integrated_status`. It returns False on ROCm builds, on non-CUDA
devices and on any error.
- `safetensors_pread.pread_wanted(integrated_cuda=False)`: an explicit
`UNSLOTH_SAFETENSORS_PREAD=0|1` still wins. Otherwise the default is
Windows, or any OS when the target is an integrated NVIDIA GPU.
- `pread_safetensors(..., integrated_cuda=False)`: when set, every shard
goes through `pread`. The scope also wraps diffusers' `load_state_dict`
(in `model_loading_utils` and `modeling_utils`), so diffusers model
shards such as the image transformer are read the same way. The wrapper
binds the call through diffusers' own signature, so it works on 0.40
(which still has `dduf_entries`) and 0.42 alike. It only acts on the
plain per-shard call: a `.safetensors` file loaded to the host, with
mmap enabled and no DDUF archive. If the pread read fails, diffusers'
own read runs. Without an integrated-CUDA rule, diffusers shards keep
diffusers' own read, so the Windows converting-load rule is still
transformers-only.
- Call sites pass the load's target device:
- `diffusion.py`: the three pipeline `from_pretrained` scopes, via
`_converted_shards_pread(dtype, small_host, device)`
  - `video.py`: the `_run_load` scope, using the load's `gpu_ordinal`
  - `diffusion_hidream.py`: the Llama TE4 scope

Unchanged:
- Discrete NVIDIA, CPU, MPS and ROCm (including AMD APUs, whose timing
is still being measured) keep their current backend on every OS.
- The Intel Arc iGPU rule from #17137 still applies to transformers
shards only.
- Components the small-host route loads at their stored dtype stay
memory-mapped.
- safetensors without the `backend` keyword (< 0.8) stays on mmap.
- `UNSLOTH_SAFETENSORS_PREAD=0` turns it off.

The pread and mmap backends read the same bytes, so the loaded weights
do not change.

## Tests

Studio: do not pin the Krea 2 compiled caption pad at batch size 1 (#19901)

## Summary

Compiled Krea 2 LoRA runs pinned every step's text to the dataset's
longest valid caption (`qwen_pad_to`). At batch size 1 that pin is not
needed: a single sample's valid rows need no mask, `_krea2_collate`
already returns `mask=None` for an unpadded batch, and the regional
compile runs with `dynamic=True`, so a new caption length does not
recompile.

This change stops pinning Krea 2 at batch size 1
(`_compiled_text_pad_to`). Batches above 1 keep the pin, and Qwen-Image
is unchanged.

With the pin, a dataset with one long caption pads every step to that
length and runs masked attention. The step whose caption is the longest
one comes up unmasked, which flips the `attention_mask` guard and
compiles a second graph.

## Measurements

Krea-2-Raw (`unsloth/Krea-2-Raw`), 512 px, bf16 base, compiled, rank 32,
lr 3e-4, batch size 1, seed 0. The dataset is 16 tarot images with
long-tail captions: 38 to 372 text rows per caption, median 54.5 rows
per step. Each arm ran 50 steps in a fresh process with a fresh inductor
cache, in ABBA order. s/step is the median over steps 11 to 50. Card:
RTX PRO 6000 Blackwell (sm120), torch 2.13.0+cu130, diffusers 0.42.1.

| Arm | s/step (median) | s/step (mean) | Recompiles | Graphs | Masked
steps |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| pinned 1 | 0.2811 | 0.2809 | 1 | 2 | 47 / 50 |
| batch-local 1 | 0.2160 | 0.2292 | 0 | 1 | 0 / 50 |
| batch-local 2 | 0.2159 | 0.2198 | 0 | 1 | 0 / 50 |
| pinned 2 | 0.2816 | 0.2813 | 1 | 2 | 47 / 50 |

- Speedup: 1.303x. The A/A spread is 0.16% for the pinned pair and 0.08%
for the batch-local pair.
- Recompile reason in the pinned arms: `expected type of
'attention_mask' to be a tensor type, but found NoneType`, raised when
the 372-row caption came up unpadded.
- Loss: the step-1 loss differs by 4.5e-6 between pinned and
batch-local. Over 50 steps the largest per-step gap is 2.3e-3, against
an A/A gap of 7.7e-4 between the two pinned runs. Masked padded keys
contribute nothing to the softmax, so the two arms compute the same math
up to kernel choice.
- Peak memory: 36.38 GB in the pinned arms, 36.36 to 36.38 GB in the
batch-local arms.

The speedup was measured on sm120 only. The masked SDPA call (pinned)
and the unmasked one (batch-local) choose different backends, and how
much that matters can differ on sm80 / sm89 cards and on ROCm.

## Tests

- `tests/test_diffusion_krea2_text_trim.py`: two new tests, both passing
on CPU.
- `_compiled_text_pad_to` returns None for Krea 2 at batch size 1, the
longest valid length at batch size 2, the longest length for Qwen-Image,
and None when not compiled.
  - Batch-size-1 Krea 2 collate is unmasked at every caption length.
- `test_krea2_collate_and_forward_roundtrip` and
`test_trimmed_forward_matches_the_padded_masked_forward` fail the same
way before and after this change on the CPU host used:
`diffusers.pipelines.krea2` does not import there because of a
`huggingface_hub` version mismatch.

Studio: run the Qwen-VL patch embed Conv3d as a matmul on torch 2.9 with cuDNN 9.8-9.14 (#19862)

## Summary

On torch 2.9.0 / 2.9.1 the Qwen-VL vision `patch_embed.proj` Conv3d runs
on the slow native kernel. That makes each Qwen-Image-2.1 edit encode
take about 40 s on an L4 instead of 0.5 s. This PR runs that conv as one
`F.linear`, and only on the affected torch / cuDNN range.

## Cause

In torch 2.9, `use_cudnn` (`aten/src/ATen/native/Convolution.cpp`,
commented "broken on cuDNN 9.8 - 9.14") refuses cuDNN for a contiguous
bf16 / fp16 5-D convolution with a non-1 kernel when the runtime cuDNN
is in [9.8, 9.15). The torch 2.9.0 and 2.9.1 pip wheels ship cuDNN
9.10.2, so the conv falls back to `slow_conv3d` on every call, not only
the first. Turning `cudnn.benchmark` on or off makes no difference, and
neither does `torch.backends.cudnn.enabled = False`. torch 2.8 has no
such check, and torch 2.10 removed it.

`patch_embed.proj` is still `nn.Conv3d` in transformers 4.52.4, 4.57.6,
5.18.0 and 5.24.1. Each input row is exactly one patch (kernel ==
stride, no padding), so the conv is a matmul over the flattened patch.

## Change

- `studio/backend/core/inference/diffusion_patch_embed.py`:
`install_patch_embed_linear(pipe, target)`. It replaces `forward` on the
`proj` of every `*PatchEmbed` module in the pipeline whose conv is a
pure patchify Conv3d.
- It installs only on CUDA when torch is 2.9.x and the runtime cuDNN is
in [9.8, 9.15), which is the same window as upstream.
- The matmul path is taken only for bf16 / fp16 CUDA inputs of shape
`[N, *weight.shape[1:]]`. Everything else calls the stock
`Conv3d.forward`.
- `UNSLOTH_PATCH_EMBED_LINEAR=0` keeps the stock conv. `=1` installs it
on any CUDA torch.
- `diffusion.py`: the load path calls it after the VAE hooks. A failure
there is logged and leaves the stock conv in place.

## Measurements (NVIDIA L4, bf16)

Patch embed alone, per call (real kernel / stride / width from the
configs). All numbers are ms except the two `s` cells, which are
seconds.

| Model | Patches | torch 2.9.1 + cuDNN 9.10.2, Conv3d | torch 2.9.1 +
cuDNN 9.28.1, Conv3d | torch 2.14.1 + cuDNN 9.28.0, Conv3d | F.linear
(any) |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| Qwen3-VL (Qwen-Image-2.1) | 576 | 5.3 s | 0.70 | 0.70 | 0.08 |
| Qwen3-VL | 4096 (1024x1024 reference) | 37 s | 2.1 | 2.1 | 0.23 |
| Qwen3-VL | 16384 | over 90 s (timed out) | 10.2 | 10.0 | 0.86 |
| Qwen2.5-VL (Qwen-Image / Edit) | 784 | 22.5 | 0.57 | 0.56 | 0.10 |
| Qwen2.5-VL | 5476 | 161 | 2.2 | 2.2 | 0.28 |
| Qwen2.5-VL | 16384 | 645 | 7.4 | 7.6 | 0.81 |

torch 2.9.0 + cuDNN 9.10.2 gives the same numbers as 2.9.1. The 2.9.1
rows were each measured twice (in separate processes), and the two runs
were within 3%.

One real Qwen-Image-2.1 edit-style encode: the `unsloth/Qwen-Image-2.1`
text encoder (Qwen3-VL), a 1024x1024 reference (4096 patches, 1046
tokens), and `model.model(...)` timed after a warm-up:

| torch / cuDNN | Stock Conv3d, call 1 / call 2 | With this change, call
1 / call 2 |
|---|---|---|
| 2.9.1 / 9.10.2 | 40.2 s / 39.1 s | 0.50 s / 0.52 s |
| 2.14.1 / 9.28.0 (not gated) | 0.87 s / 0.52 s | 0.52 s / 0.52 s |

## Accuracy

The baseline is an fp64 patch embed rounded once to bf16.

- **Patch embed output:** the matmul's max abs error against the fp64
baseline is 0.0156, and its mean abs error is 3e-7. For the stock conv
the max abs error is 0.0039 on the native kernel and 0.0156 on cuDNN
9.28.
- **fp32 strict (no TF32):** conv and matmul differ by at most 5e-6.
- **Final hidden state:** the matmul is as close to the fp64 baseline as
either stock conv is:

| Path | Mean abs diff | Median cosine |
|---|---|---|
| Matmul | 0.280 | 0.9944 |
| Native-kernel conv | 0.270 | 0.9947 |
| cuDNN 9.28 conv | 0.327 | 0.9924 |

A one-ulp change in the patch embed moves the bf16 36-layer output by
that much on any path. Repeating the same path gives a bit-identical
result.

## Tests

`studio/backend/tests/test_diffusion_patch_embed.py` (CPU, 19 tests):

- the torch / cuDNN gate table;
- matmul against Conv3d in fp32, fp64 and bf16 at the Qwen2.5-VL and
Qwen3-VL shapes;
- the patched forward takes the matmul only for half-precision CUDA
patch rows (counted);
- install gating, the env switch and idempotence;
- non-patchify convs and other classes are left alone;
- the real transformers `Qwen2_5_VisionPatchEmbed` /
`Qwen3VLVisionPatchEmbed` are matched;
- the load path calls it.

Reverting the matmul makes the engagement test fail, and removing the
call from `diffusion.py` makes the wiring test fail.
`tests/test_diffusion_device.py` still passes.

## Not covered

- Only image pipelines (`diffusion.py`) install it, not the video load
path.
- Unsloth Core vision fine-tuning of Qwen2.5-VL / Qwen3-VL on torch 2.9
hits the same fallback, including in backward. That is out of scope
here.
- Hardware: measured on an L4 only. The fallback comes from torch's
version check, not from the GPU, so other NVIDIA cards should behave the
same way; that was not measured.

Studio images: per-load Merge LoRA for speed option (Auto keeps today's unfolded default) (#19868)

## Summary

Adds a per-load opt-in for folding an unchanged diffusion LoRA set into
the denoiser weights, so users can get the render speedup measured on
DGX Spark (median render 3.145 s to 2.559 s with folding on) without
changing the accurate default.

Folding has been off by default since #18983, because the merged `W +
scale * B @ A` rounded to bf16 lands further from an fp32 reference than
PEFT's unfolded branch (mean LPIPS 0.0149 vs 0.0109 on L4, FLUX.2 klein
4B). Until now the only way to turn it on was the install-wide
`UNSLOTH_DIFFUSION_LORA_FUSE=1`.

## What changes

Backend
- `DiffusionLoadRequest.lora_fuse`: `auto` | `on` | `off`, default unset
(= `auto`).
- Precedence: an explicit per-load `on` / `off` beats
`UNSLOTH_DIFFUSION_LORA_FUSE`, which beats the default (off). `auto` is
exactly today's behaviour: the env switch is still read at fold time.
- `on` folds on a resident load, and on a group offload load where every
denoiser sits whole on the card (the same gate the env switch opens).
Weights that move every render (model / streaming / sequential offload,
`low_vram`) still stay unfolded, as does an explicit Speed mode Off
(bit-exact) and a quantized bake.
- `off` never folds on that load, even with the env switch set.
- The choice is stored on `_LoadState`, so every later fold (deferred
compile, a LoRA change) keeps it.
- `status()["resolved"]["lora_fuse"]` reports the choice: `value`
on/off, `source` explicit/auto (the existing ResolvedBadge contract) and
a new `origin`: `per_load`, `env` or `default`. The existing `lora_fuse`
outcome field (fused / disabled / offload / ...) is unchanged.
- The route forwards `lora_fuse` only when it is `on` / `off`, and only
to an engine whose `begin_load` takes it (sd.cpp and MLX do not).

Frontend
- A "Merge LoRA for speed" select (Auto / On / Off) under the LoRA list
on the Images page, with a hint that it is faster but slightly less
exact. It is sent only when not Auto, carries a ResolvedBadge for
`lora_fuse`, and reseeds from the loaded build.
- The "Not fused (fusion off)" detail now points at the new control as
well as the env switch.

## Default behaviour is unchanged

On main, with the env switch unset, no load folds (the env gate in
`_fuse_constant_loras` runs before the offload check, so an
`OFFLOAD_NONE` load does not fold either). With no per-load choice, the
fold decision is identical to main: a differential script enumerating
1344 cells (env value x offload policy x memory mode x speed mode x
speed source x on-card x quantized bake) produces byte-identical status
and fold-call output on main and on this branch.

## Tests

- `tests/test_diffusion_lora_fuse_per_load.py` (new): precedence, `on`
folding a resident group offload load, `off` suppressing the env fold on
`OFFLOAD_NONE` and group loads, `on` still refusing moving weights and
Speed mode Off, persistence across `dataclasses.replace`, the resolved
entry and its origin, request validation, route forwarding.
- `tests/test_diffusion_backend.py`: an end-to-end fake load that checks
the state keeps the choice and the status reports its origin.
- Against main: 33 of the new backend tests fail (the API does not exist
there); the 5 that pass on main pin the default and env-only behaviour.
- On this branch: 85 passed in the LoRA fuse suites. A wider run of 79
LoRA / load / status test files shows the same failing test IDs on main
and on this branch (pre-existing on main), and no new failures.
- Frontend: `npm run typecheck` passes,
`tests/image-lora-fuse-control.test.ts` added, ESLint reports no new
problems in the touched files.

## Not covered

- No GPU timing or LPIPS run on this branch: the fold code itself is
unchanged, only its gate. The speed and accuracy numbers above are the
earlier measurements.
- The video page keeps its own LoRA path (merged at load) and does not
get this control.

## GPU check (NVIDIA L4)

FLUX.2 klein 4B bf16 (`transformer_quant="none"`, group offload as
Studio picked it), 1024x1024, 4 steps, a random rank-32 adapter on 100
attention modules (no unsloth/* klein LoRA exists). Fresh process per
arm, order main, auto, on, off, off, on, auto, main; each arm imported
its own tree.

| arm | s/step, renders 2 to 4 (rep 1 / rep 2) | wall per render | fold
outcome | `resolved.lora_fuse` |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| main (env unset) | 0.868 / 0.880 | 4.49 / 4.54 s | disabled | absent |
| head auto | 0.875 / 0.881 | 4.51 / 4.53 s | disabled | off, auto,
default |
| head on | 0.715 / 0.719 | 3.87 / 3.89 s | fused | on, explicit,
per_load |
| head off | 0.877 / 0.880 | 4.53 / 4.55 s | disabled | off, explicit,
per_load |

- `on` is about 18% faster per step against a 1.4% main-vs-main spread;
the render that folds costs about 8.2 s instead of 4.6 s, once per load.
- Head auto and head off are byte-identical to main on every render of

- LPIPS on vs auto: render 1 identical (no fold yet), renders 2 to 4

Not run: pure Studio defaults on L4 (an int8 DiT bakes the LoRA and

Studio int8: pair-check MiniMax-H3-Image's large-row CUTLASS races (power-capped Ada at 2048) (#19879)

## Summary

MiniMax-H3-Image at 2048x2048 on the RTX 6000 Ada (300 W) runs about 5%
slower with the prebuilt int8 CUTLASS GEMM than with
`UNSLOTH_DIFFUSION_INT8_CUTLASS=0`. #19807 fixed the same loss on H3
video with the paired check (`paired_cost_us`: each race winner re-timed
as (tile, today's path) pairs, the clock a denoise step actually
shares), but only for the 16384-row race. H3-Image's calls run about
4100 rows, so its races never reach the pair check. Turning pairs on for
every image race cost FLUX.2 klein and Qwen-Image-2.1 up to 3% on L4, so
this PR opts in the MiniMax-H3-Image family only.

## Changes

- `diffusion_int8_cutlass.py`: `PAIRED_ROW_FAMILIES =
("MiniMaxH3ImageTransformer2DModel",)`, a per-card switch
(`set_paired_rows` / `paired_rows`), and `paired_for(m, index)`: the
16384-row race as before, plus the large-row races (1024 to 8191 rows)
on a card whose last int8 swap was a paired family. `race()` passes its
card index. The old `info.get("sustained")` guard is dropped because at
16384 rows the sustained timings always decide, so H3 video behaves
exactly as before.
- `diffusion_int8_gemm.py`: `_swap_on` sets the switch from the DiT
class before anything plans, including its early returns, so a FLUX.2
load after an H3-Image load on the same card races unpaired again. While
the switch is on, the race cache key gets a `|paired_rows` suffix. H3
video uses the same 5 weight shapes and races them unpaired at image
rows, so the two families never read each other's image-row verdicts.
Every other load keeps its key. The new names are in `_RACE_SOURCES`.
- Same kill switch as H3 video:
`UNSLOTH_DIFFUSION_INT8_CUTLASS_PAIRED=0` (and
`UNSLOTH_DIFFUSION_INT8_CUTLASS_SUSTAINED=0` / `=huge`) keeps every
winner.

The race code digest changes, so every card re-races its cached CUTLASS
verdicts once after this update. That is the same one-time cost as any
race-code edit. The verdicts for other families come out the same.

## Tests

`tests/test_diffusion_int8_cutlass_paired_rows.py` (CPU) runs the real
`_cutlass_plan`, `race`, `pick`, `paired_cost_us`, `_live_row_race` and
`slot`, with the timers replaced by a card model. The model uses the L4
72 W and RTX 6000 Ada 300 W clocks from #19807 / R9, applied to every
call of 1024 rows or more.

| Cell | origin/main | this PR |
|---|---|---|
| Ada, H3-Image at ~4100 rows: Linears on CUTLASS | 300 | 0 (9 races
paired) |
| Ada, H3-Image with `..._PAIRED=0` | 300 | 300 |
| L4, H3-Image | unchanged, no pair timing | unchanged, no pair timing |
| Ada / L4, FLUX.2 klein and Qwen-Image-2.1: routing, race inputs |
golden | same golden, 0 image-row pair timings |

On origin/main, 4 of the 9 tests fail: the Ada routing cell (300 vs 0)
and the three that use the new switch. On this branch all 9 pass. The
existing int8 CUTLASS suites (`test_diffusion_int8_cutlass*.py`,
`test_diffusion_gpu_lever_matrix.py`, `test_diffusion_int8_gemm*.py` and
the rest that touch the race) also pass. The 5
`test_diffusion_backend.py::test_download_plan_for_minimax_h3_image_*`
failures happen on origin/main too and are not related to this change.

## GPU check (Colab L4, 72 W)

This runs the real race through each tree, base (origin/main) and head,
in separate interpreters, with today's Triton path as the incumbent. It
covers H3's 5 int8 weight shapes at 4096 rows (load race) and 4160 rows

Studio: bound Windows integrated NVIDIA GPU diffusion memory by system commit (RTX Spark) (#19881)

## Summary

On Windows with an integrated NVIDIA GPU (RTX Spark N1X, Windows ARM64),
the diffusion memory planner credited about 109.5 GiB of free memory on
a machine whose real ceiling is about 58 GiB. This PR bounds the credit
on that platform by the Windows system commit charge.

## What was measured

Measured on an RTX Spark Windows ARM64 machine:

| Reading | Value |
|---|---|
| `get_device_properties(0).is_integrated` | 1 (`.integrated` is absent)
|
| `mem_get_info()` free / total | 109.52 / 109.72 GiB |
| OS-visible RAM | 64 GB |
| psutil `available` | 50.67 GiB, does not move as the GPU allocates |
| `GlobalMemoryStatusEx.ullAvailPageFile` (commit available) | 58.14 GiB
idle, 17.70 GiB while holding 40 GiB on the GPU |
| Commit limit | 74,733 MB |

The GPU has a dedicated carve-out the OS does not see, plus up to about
48 GB of shared OS RAM, and `mem_get_info` reports both. Every GPU byte,
dedicated or shared, is charged to system commit 1:1 (also with
random-filled tensors, so it is not memory compression), while psutil's
available RAM stays flat. Commit is the binding limit.

Today `_cuda_memory()` marks the device `unified_memory` and
`_unified_reclaimable_memory_mib` credits `max(cuda_free,
min(os_available, cuda_total))` = `max(109.52, min(50.67, 109.72))` =
109.5 GiB, with capacity 109.7 GiB.

## Change

- `utils/host_memory.py`: `windows_commit_mib()` reads
`(ullAvailPageFile, ullTotalPageFile)` via `GlobalMemoryStatusEx`;
returns None off Windows or on any failure.
- `core/inference/diffusion_memory.py`: only when `sys.platform ==
"win32"`, the CUDA device is integrated, and torch is not ROCm:
  - free = `min(cuda_free, commit_available)`
  - capacity = `min(cuda_total, commit_limit)`
- No extra reserve is taken at the credit: the planner already keeps
`_reserve_mib("unified_memory", capacity)` (20% of the commit-capped
capacity) of this free, so subtracting it at the credit too would
reserve twice. On the measured numbers the auto budget is 58.14 GiB
minus 14.6 GiB, about 43.5 GiB, instead of about 87 GiB.
  - Any failed commit reading falls back to the existing rule.
- Kill switch: `UNSLOTH_DIFFUSION_WIN_IGPU_COMMIT_CAP=0` restores the
previous credit.
- `DeviceMemory` gains an optional `credit_basis` field. It is
`"windows_commit"` when the commit reading bounded the pair, and it then
appears in the plan's public `device_memory` dict. Everywhere else it is
None and the dict is unchanged.

Linux integrated GPUs (DGX Spark, Jetson), macOS, discrete GPUs and ROCm
never reach the new path.

## Tests

`studio/backend/tests/test_windows_integrated_gpu_commit_memory.py`
mocks torch props, `mem_get_info`, psutil available and the commit
reading with the measured numbers:

- Windows integrated: credited free is commit available (58.14 GiB),
capacity is the commit limit, the planner budget is that minus the
unified reserve (not 109.5 GiB), and `credit_basis` is reported.
- Kill switch and an unreadable or raising commit reading restore the
previous credit.
- Linux integrated, Windows discrete and Windows ROCm APU are unchanged,
and the commit reader is never called.
- The credit never exceeds the driver's free.
- `windows_commit_mib()` parses `GlobalMemoryStatusEx`, and returns None
on a failed call, a missing kernel32, or a non-Windows platform.

## Not covered

- Not yet run on the device itself; a follow-up load of an image model
will read the planner's credited figure with and without the fix.
- Allocations past the dedicated carve-out (where WDDM starts placing
them in shared OS RAM) were not measured; the capture held up to 40 GiB.
- `/api/system` reporting (`_reconcile_cuda_integrated_memory`) still
widens the device total to the torch figure; that is a reporting path,
not the planner, and is left for a separate change.

## Device check (RTX Spark, Windows 11 ARM64, Studio venv torch
2.14.0+cu134, driver 621.14)

The real `GlobalMemoryStatusEx` path, main `234e89701f` against this
head, each tree imported from its own checkout:

| build | free_mib | total_mib | credit_basis |
|---|---:|---:|---|
| main | 112,150 | 112,350 | none (CUDA's figure) |
| head | 59,748 | 74,732 | windows_commit |
| head, `UNSLOTH_DIFFUSION_WIN_IGPU_COMMIT_CAP=0` | 112,150 | 112,350 |
none |

A 2 GiB step allocation loop stopped at 54 GiB held with Windows commit
down to 4.3 GiB, while CUDA still reported 56.9 GiB free: the commit
reading, not CUDA's, is where allocation runs out on this machine.

Studio FP8: treat torch 2.10's cuBLASLt row-wise refusal on sm_12x as a missing kernel (#19871)

## Summary

#19665 sends every fp8 GEMM to the tensorwise unit-scale path on a card
whose torch build has no row-wise `_scaled_mm`, but it only recognises
the missing kernel by torch's "not supported" text. On a real RTX 5090
(sm_120) with the Windows `torch 2.10.0+cu130` wheel that Studio
installs, the row-wise call fails differently:

```
RuntimeError: CUDA error: CUBLAS_STATUS_NOT_SUPPORTED when calling cublasLtMatmulAlgoGetHeuristic(...)
```

`_is_unsupported` matched none of its words (the status code is spelled
with underscores), so the probe returned no verdict, the fallback never
installed, and FP8 loads stayed broken on that card.

## Cause

In torch 2.10, `_scaled_mm_out_cuda`
(`aten/src/ATen/native/cuda/ScaledBlas.cpp` at v2.10.0) sends row-wise
scales to CUTLASS only when `dprops->major == 10`; sm_12x with cuBLAS
12.9+ goes to cuBLASLt, which refuses row-wise scaling there. Newer
torch (`rowwise_uses_cublas`, main) checks `major < 10` instead, so
sm_12x reaches CUTLASS, which the Windows wheels do not build. Either
way there is no row-wise fp8 GEMM on these cards; only the error text
differs.

## Change

- `diffusion_fp8_unit_scale.py`: `cublas_status_not_supported` joins
`_UNSUPPORTED_WORDS`. The probe still requires the tensorwise GEMM to
run first, so a card with no fp8 GEMM at all, an OOM, or another cuBLAS
failure (`CUBLAS_STATUS_EXECUTION_FAILED`, already a test case) is still
no verdict.
- `test_the_torch_210_cublas_rowwise_refusal_is_a_missing_kernel`: the
exact message from the RTX 5090 makes the card a fallback card with
`gemm_path` `unit_scale_fallback`. It fails on main.

## Evidence

Device probe on the RTX 5090, Windows 11 x64, driver 616.56, Studio venv
torch 2.10.0+cu130, cuDNN 9.12, triton 3.6.0, 8192^3:

| kernel | ms | TFLOP/s |
|---|---|---|
| bf16 matmul | 4.98 | 220.7 |
| fp8 tensorwise, bf16 out | 2.50 | 439.6 |
| fp8 tensorwise, fp32 out | 2.51 | 437.9 |
| fp8 row-wise | `CUBLAS_STATUS_NOT_SUPPORTED` | |

The fp32-output tensorwise GEMM the fallback uses runs at the same rate
as bf16 output, about 2x bf16.

Tests: `test_diffusion_fp8_rowwise_fallback.py` and
`test_diffusion_fp8_unit_scale.py`, 89 passed, 1 skipped; the new test
fails on main.

## Not covered

A Studio FP8 render on the RTX 5090 with this change (queued as a device
check). Linux and newer torch builds take the same path as before: their
row-wise kernel either runs or raises torch's own "not supported" text.

## Hermetic unit-scale tests

The first RTX Spark device run (Windows 11 ARM64, torch 2.14.0+cu134, no
row-wise kernel) found 9 head failures in
`test_diffusion_fp8_unit_scale.py`. The fixture mocks `_device_caps` but
left the real per-card probe running. On a card with no row-wise kernel,
the probe made every install a fallback install, so `install()` returned
True where the test expected the mocked arch to be left alone. The two
cache-tag tests also saw the `:rowwise-missing=0:acc32=0` suffix.

- The autouse fixture now stubs `_probe_rowwise` to report row-wise as
available. The persisted verdict was already stubbed. The missing-kernel
path keeps its own tests in `test_diffusion_fp8_rowwise_fallback.py`. On
a row-wise host the tag stays `unsloth_fp8_unit_scale=<rows>` (with
`:force` when forced), which is what the tests assert.
- `test_compiled_graph_after_a_cached_rowwise_one_uses_the_dispatcher`
skips when the real card has no row-wise kernel, because its base arm
compiles that GEMM. Its child processes also run with
`UNSLOTH_DIFFUSION_PROBE_CACHE=0`, so they cannot read this host's
persisted verdict.

To reproduce on a CPU host, a pytest plugin makes the real probe answer
"missing" for the current card, which is what the RTX Spark returned.
Results for `test_diffusion_fp8_unit_scale.py` under that plugin: before
this commit, 10 failed. These are the 8 device failures that can run
without a GPU, plus `test_epilogue_matches_rowwise_math[False|True]`.
After this commit, 29 passed and 1 skipped. Without the plugin, both
files pass before and after (89 passed, 1 skipped).

Studio: keep Triton's bundled ptxas-blackwell when importing flashinfer 0.7.3 (CUDA 13.0 toolkit on PATH) (#19882)

## Summary

`flashinfer/triton/__init__.py` runs `_patch_triton_ptxas_blackwell()`
at import. It sets `TRITON_PTXAS_BLACKWELL_PATH` to the `ptxas` on PATH
whenever that ptxas reports CUDA >= 13, without comparing it to the
`ptxas-blackwell` Triton bundles. The variable is process wide, so after
Studio's first flashinfer import every later Triton compile on sm_100 /
sm_120 (int8 attention and GEMM, NVFP4 Triton, the inline-asm kernels,
video kernels) assembles with the system toolkit instead.

On flashinfer 0.7.3 (the release Studio's NVFP4 installer picks first),
plain `import flashinfer` reaches it: `flashinfer/__init__.py` imports
`flashinfer.mamba`, whose `ssd_combined` imports
`flashinfer.triton.kernels` at module level. On 0.6.6 only lazy call
paths import `flashinfer.triton`, and none of them are ones Studio uses.

Torch 2.13 (new CUDA 13 installs) pins Triton 3.7.1, which bundles
ptxas-blackwell 13.1. A CUDA 13.0 toolkit on PATH is common, and with it
the bundled 13.1 is downgraded to 13.0.

Upstream fix: flashinfer-ai/flashinfer#10079 (open) only takes a system
ptxas that is strictly newer than the bundled one. This PR does the same
on Studio's side until a flashinfer release with that fix is the one
installed.

## Change

- New `core/inference/flashinfer_import.py`: `import_flashinfer()`
imports flashinfer and records whether `TRITON_PTXAS_BLACKWELL_PATH` was
set beforehand. If it was unset and the import set it to a ptxas that is
not newer (major.minor from `--version`) than
`triton.backends.nvidia.compiler.get_ptxas(100)` with the variable
unset, it is unset again. It logs this once. The cleanup also runs when
the import fails partway through.
- The override stays when the system ptxas is newer, when Triton's
bundled version cannot be read, and always when the variable was set
before the import (a user's choice is never touched).
- Every function in the NVFP4 modules
(`diffusion_nvfp4_dispatch/ops/linear/tactics.py`) and in
`video_minimax_h3_flashinfer.py` calls `import_flashinfer()` before its
first flashinfer import. Once flashinfer is in `sys.modules`, the call
does nothing.

## Testing

- `tests/test_flashinfer_import.py` (CPU, 11 tests): fake ptxas scripts,
a fake Triton compiler module, and a fake flashinfer package that runs
the 0.7.3 patch verbatim. Covered cases: older and equal system ptxas
restored, newer kept, CUDA 12 untouched, unknown bundled version kept, a
user-set value untouched, a failed import still restored, the
already-imported fast path, logging once, and an AST check that every
Studio function importing flashinfer calls the guard first.
- Real packages (flashinfer-python 0.7.3, Triton 3.7.1, fake 13.0 ptxas
first on PATH): `import flashinfer.gemm.gemm_base` changes Triton's
Blackwell ptxas from the bundled 13.1 to the 13.0 one. Through
`import_flashinfer()` the variable ends unset and Triton reports its
bundled 13.1. With flashinfer 0.6.6 the same import leaves the variable
unset.
- Existing NVFP4 and H3 flashinfer suites pass.
`test_diffusion_nvfp4_weight_quant.py::test_4over6_layout_scale_top_and_error`
also fails on main and is unrelated.

## Not covered

- No GPU compile run showing a kernel that needs PTX ISA 9.1 failing
under the 13.0 ptxas. The env-level effect above is what the guard
targets.
- A flashinfer import made outside Studio's own modules (for example
inside a third-party library imported first) does not go through the
guard.

Studio images: MiniMax-H3-Image sequential lockstep batching, opt-in batched forward (#19880)

## Summary

MiniMax-H3-Image has never run a batched forward. Its lockstep mode runs
each image as its own batch-1 call through every block, and only the
streamed weight upload is shared. This PR adds a real batched forward
behind `UNSLOTH_H3_IMAGE_BATCHED=1`. It is off by default, because it
wins only on some device and size combinations.

- **Rows that share a packed layout** run every block as ONE call over
all rows. The layout is the canvas, text token count and tags, reference
grids and steps. Rows with other layouts still share the forward, as
separate block calls, so the streamed upload stays one per step.
- **Each row keeps its own state:** noise, reference noise, refined text
and scheduler. Per-row reference images come in through `row_images`.
- **The fp32 patch projection and the output head run per row.** Without
that, a 1e-7 batch-shape rounding in the head grew through the 6 steps
to up to 0.24 LPIPS per image. With it, a batched row is bit-identical
to its own solo render.
- **The row-mod kernel** runs over the flattened rows, with the index
repeated per image. Batch 1 calls the original forward.
- **A block call takes at most `UNSLOTH_H3_IMAGE_BATCH_TOKENS` (4608)
packed rows.** At 2048 px one image already fills that budget, so each
image runs in its own call there.

It also lets the sequential tier denoise a request's images together. On
that tier (one big component on the card at a time), every image used to
bring the DiT onto the card and back on its own. Now the DiT comes in
once for the group, and each image runs each block as its own batch-1
call (lockstep), so its pixels are those of its own render. This is on
by default. `UNSLOTH_H3_IMAGE_LOCKSTEP=0` keeps one render after
another.

`row_layout_key(pipe, prompt, ...)` in
`diffusion_minimax_h3_image_batch.py` is the match key for a
cross-request batcher. It uses only the tokenizer.

Based on main; it needs nothing from the image batching infrastructure
(#19837). The sequential lockstep is on by default; the batched forward
stays behind its env flag.

Studio sd.cpp: one sd-server per card while image requests queue (#19863)

## Summary

On a host with two or more GPUs, a GGUF image model on Studio's native
engine (sd.cpp) now runs one `sd-server` per card once requests start to
queue. Waiting requests go, in arrival order, to whichever server frees
first. A single user keeps today's path: an idle engine sends the
request straight to the one server it already has, with the same argv,
env and payload.

Auto applies this only where the primary already runs on one card (for
example Qwen-Image-2.1 Q4_K_M on a T4). Loads where Auto picks a
companion split (for example Z-Image Q8_0 on a T4) keep main's split
argv and placement; one-card servers for them are opt-in with
`UNSLOTH_SD_CPP_REPLICAS=N`.

On Kaggle 2x T4 with 4 concurrent clients this measured 2.00x the
images/min of main for Qwen-Image-2.1 Q4_K_M, with p95 halved and the
same pixels.

## How it works

- **Scope.** A pool is built only for an sd-server load on CUDA under
Automatic card selection (no `gpu_ids`), with no offload policy flags
and at least one other card. The pool covers every card that can hold
the diffusion model resident. Everything else (one card, explicit
offload, a block split, Vulkan / ROCm / Metal, one-shot `sd-cli`) has no
pool and keeps main's code path.
- **Lazy start.** Nothing extra starts at load. The first time a request
has to wait for a busy server, one more `sd-server` starts per card.
Each one is masked to its card with `CUDA_VISIBLE_DEVICES` and gets no
`--backend` pin: it runs the argv a one-card Studio runs. Replicas stay
up until unload or the next load.
- **Dispatch.** Requests wait in a FIFO line. Only the head can take a
server (the primary first, then the first ready replica), so nothing is
passed over. A replica renders through the same generate code as the
primary, with its own LoRA scratch dir and progress.
- **Host RAM pricing.** When the whole model does not fit one card,
auto-fit leaves the text encoders (then the VAE) on the host. Without
`--mmap` that spill is copied into pinned host memory, about 7.5 GiB per
server for Z-Image's BF16 Qwen3-4B. It is priced 1:1, plus 1.5 GiB per
server process, against cgroup-aware available RAM less the small-host
reserve. Each replica is priced one at a time, after the ones before it
reserved their share:
  - pinned when the host holds the spill;
- else `--mmap`, which keeps the spill in the file's shared page cache
(measured 0.22 GB, about 1% slower);
  - else refused, with the reason in status.
- **Companion split.** Auto picks a companion split (DiT on cuda:0,
encoders + VAE on cuda:1) when one card cannot hold everything. Auto
keeps it, with main's argv and no replicas: one-card servers would leave
the encoder in pinned host memory (about +7.5 GB host RAM and +0.7%
latency for a single Z-Image user). With an explicit
`UNSLOTH_SD_CPP_REPLICAS=N`, the load instead runs one-card servers per
card when the host holds the primary's pinned spill plus one replica. A
block split (no card holds the DiT) always keeps one server.
- **Failures.**
- A replica that dies, times out or runs out of VRAM is retired
(stopped, status `dead` with the reason). Its request goes back to the
head of the line and renders once more on another server. The failed
render returned nothing, so nothing is duplicated.
- A job error on a healthy replica is the request's error, as it would
be on the primary.
- Unload, a new load, a dead primary or a primary restart stop every
replica, and requests still in the line get the usual not-loaded error.
- Stop, account retire and the account-scoped unload guard all see
renders on replicas.
- **Kill switch.** `UNSLOTH_SD_CPP_REPLICAS=off` (or `0` / `1`) keeps
one server. `auto` is the default (one-card primaries only). `N` caps
the number of servers, also turns a companion split into one-card
servers, and applies to an explicit multi-card pick.
- **Status.** `/images/status` gains a `replicas` block, present only
when the load has a pool. It has a row per card (role, status, `--mmap`,
host MiB priced, requests dispatched, reason) plus waiting, in-flight
and failover counts.

- a replica dying mid-render, and one exiting while idle;

- Auto keeps main's companion split argv, env and status at N=1 and
starts nothing when a queue forms;
- the kill switch (`off`, `0`, `1`) keeps main's split, and a server
count applies to an explicit pick;
- host pricing (pinned, `--mmap`, refused), and a companion split
replaced or kept;

All 23 fail on the merge base. The sd.cpp suites pass (519 tests). Two

`test_sd_cpp_torch_vae.py::test_decode_matches_the_diffusers_pipeline_decode`.

## Not covered

- The Queue on the Images page still runs one job at a time and waits
for direct runs. Replicas serve concurrent `/images/generate` calls, for
example several users or API clients.
- Replicas hold their cards until unload. The memory sampler for other
models counts only the primary's VRAM, and the detailer / segmenter
passes that take the primary's lock do not wait for replica renders.
- Companion-split loads (Z-Image on a T4) get no replicas under Auto.
There is no on-demand re-placement from the split to one-card servers
when a queue forms. With `UNSLOTH_SD_CPP_REPLICAS=N` they run one-card
from the load on, at about +7.5 GB host RAM and +0.7% N=1 latency
against main's split, measured with one main repeat.
- Auto keeping the split is covered by a CPU test (same argv, env and
status as replicas off). It was not re-run on a GPU: the code path is
main's.
- One VM, one repeat of the branch per model, equal-cost requests only.
Not measured: mixed shapes, LoRA, edits, hires and the `--mmap` replica
(exercised only by CPU tests).
- No other hardware: more than two cards, Windows, or a host whose RAM
forces the `--mmap` or refusal paths.

Tests: state host RAM in the auto-offload placement matrix instead of reading the runner (#19896)

## Summary


`studio/backend/tests/test_auto_offload_ctx_platform_matrix.py::test_manual_memory_mode_bypasses_both_sites_on_a_gpu_box[*-windows]`
fails on CI runners with little free RAM since #19784:

```
RuntimeError: This model and context need about 15 GB of system RAM outside the GPU, and only about 7 GB is free after keeping 2 GB for the rest of the system ...
```

#19784's Windows commit pre-check is correct: it refuses a load whose
CPU-resident share would exhaust host memory. When the caller does not
pass a reading, it falls back to `_available_system_memory_mib()`, the
real host. #19784's conftest neutralised the real commit-headroom
reading for tests, but the placement matrix fakes GPU memory, model size
and KV cost and never states host RAM. Its Windows cells that put layers
on the CPU therefore pass on a machine with plenty of free memory and
fail on a GitHub runner with about 9 GB. Seen on the `(Python 3.13,
a-f)` leg for #19888, which does not touch this code.

## Change

- `cell_backend` pins `LlamaCppBackend._available_system_memory_mib` to
a stated `HOST_RAM_MIB` (256 GiB). The matrix is about which placement
arm runs, so host RAM is an input it now declares instead of reading
from the machine.
- The pre-check's own behaviour is covered by
`test_windows_host_commit_precheck.py`, which fakes its own readings,
and is unchanged.

studio/backend/tests/test_auto_offload_ctx_platform_matrix.py` normally
and with a plugin that fakes the host at 9 GB available:
