Studio video: queued Wan clips can share one denoise (#19831)

## Summary

Queued Wan text-to-video clips can now share one denoise. When the video
queue starts its head clip and the clips right behind it ask for the
same render (same canvas, frames, fps, steps, guidance, guidance_2 and
flow shift, no first frame / last frame / references / continuation),
the engine takes them as riders of that one denoise:

- one seeded `torch.Generator` per row, so row i draws exactly the noise
its own solo render draws;
- each clip's prompt and negative prompt are encoded alone (a per-row
`encode_prompt`), so UMT5 sees one prompt per call, as in that clip's
solo render, and the text embeddings carry no batch-shape difference;
- one denoiser call per step and guidance branch holds every clip (Wan
2.2 A14B: both experts switch at the same step for the whole batch,
since every row shares the timestep grid);
- each clip is still decoded on its own (an outermost per-row
`vae.decode` layer, so the decode peak stays one clip's), encoded, saved
under its own id and recipe, and settled on its own.

A single clip, or a head with nobody compatible behind it, starts
exactly as before: no gathering, no wait, the same calibration key,
admission, stream encode, preview and save path.

## Who joins, and the queue

- The fair queue stays the only order. Only the clips **contiguous**
behind the head in FairOrder join, up to `UNSLOTH_VIDEO_BATCH_MAX`
(default 4), so no waiting clip is ever started ahead of an earlier one
that could not join. Each rider takes its FairOrder turn as it starts.
- A clip the engine refuses (another shape after resolution, the batch
already sealed, the head already stopped) stays queued with its place,
exactly like a busy engine.
- The three entry points (Video page, `/v1/videos`, chat tool) go
through the same start functions; a rider's start runs the same access
checks under its own account.

## Stop, progress, outcome

- A rider's Stop settles that clip at once (its frames are discarded);
the shared denoise keeps going for the others. The job's own Stop does
the same for the job's clip, before or after the batch is sealed. The
render ends early only when every clip in it stopped, or on an unload /
superseding load.
- `/video/generate-progress`, `/v1/videos/{id}`, delete and the chat
tool read a rider's own record (`member_progress`,
`progress_for_video`); an account-wide stop (deleted account) reaches
its riders; an unload is refused while another account's clip rides the
batch.
- A batch that runs out of memory, or whose denoise would not fit beside
the load's weights, renders its clips one at a time in the same job,
each saved as it finishes: no clip is lost or rendered twice, and an
unseeded rider keeps the seed drawn for the batch.

## When it batches (Auto)

`UNSLOTH_VIDEO_BATCH=auto|off|force`. Auto batches only the placement
measured faster: a Wan load under Low VRAM that runs eager (speed mode
off, no compile, no CUDA graphs). Everything else renders one clip at a
time; `force` batches any eligible load. It renders one clip at a time
when any of these holds:
- the denoiser is compiled, or CUDA graphs are captured: one compiled
clip is faster than an eager batch (measured below). Under `force` such
a load batches eager (`torch.compiler.set_stance("force_eager")`, graphs
bypassed, not dropped), so a batch never compiles or captures on a
user's request;
- activation scales come from the whole call (dynamic NVFP4);
- a step cache is on, or Auto would engage one at this step count
(FBCache from 20 steps): FBCache's residual test and the static step
skip's timestep (`amax`) and history span the whole batch, so one clip
would decide another's skips. A cache that engages at request time
anyway, after the batch is sealed, sends the clips one at a time before
any denoise;
- the sampler draws fresh noise every step (an ancestral / SDE / LCM /
DDPM scheduler, or `stochastic_sampling`): the pipeline steps it without
a generator, so a batch would share one noise stream. Wan's UniPC draws
noise only at the start, one generator per row;
- the load is split across cards, a background compile is pending, or
the checkpoint is a DMD student;
- the load is not Low VRAM (resident, the default group offload whose
groups mostly stay on the card, and the unmeasured streaming /
sequential tiers).

Measured with Wan 2.2 TI2V-5B, 960x544, 33 frames, 12 steps, 4 different
prompts and seeds, 2 interleaved repeats per cell, in a warm process
(first clip excluded), one card each. Seconds per clip; the speedup is
serial over batched in the same load.

| Card | Load | Serial s/clip | Batched s/clip, N=2 / N=4 | Speedup N=2
/ N=4 | Auto |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| A100-40 | resident, compiled (default) | 7.72 | not run (Auto
declines) | | serial |
| A100-80 | resident, compiled (default), batch forced eager | 7.6 | 9.8
/ 9.6 | 0.78x / 0.79x | serial |
| A100-40 | group offload, eager (speed off) | 16.5 | 16.8 / 16.4 |
0.98x / 1.00x | serial |
| A100-40 | Low VRAM, INT8, compiled + graphs (default) | 12.2 | | |
serial |
| A100-80 | same, batch forced eager | 12.2 | 14.3 / 14.0 | 0.86x /
0.87x | serial |
| A100-40 | Low VRAM, eager (speed off) | 27.7-28.3 | 18.6 / 17.0 |
1.50x / 1.65x | **batched** |
| A100-40 (quality run) | Low VRAM, eager (speed off), 8 clips, one pass
| 28.2 | 18.1 / 16.6 | 1.56x / 1.70x | **batched** |
| T4 (Kaggle) | group offload, eager (default on T4) | 91.6 | 99.8 /
116.7 | 0.92x / 0.78x | serial |
| T4 (Kaggle) | group offload, eager (speed off) | 250.0 | 251.3 / 257.5
(N=4: one repeat) | 1.00x / 0.97x | serial |

**Latency trade-off.** A batch finishes all of its clips together, so
the first clip in it waits longer. Four clips under Low VRAM, eager, on
the A100-40: one at a time, they finish at about 28, 56, 84 and 112 s;
as one batch, all four finish at about 68 s. The first clip waits 68 s
instead of 28 s, the last 68 s instead of 112 s, and the four take 68 s
instead of 112 s in total.

The one placement where a batch wins is the one where every denoiser
call streams the whole DiT and nothing else amortises it: the batch pays
the transfer once for every clip in it. Wherever the weights mostly stay
on the card, the denoise is compute bound and a batch at best matches
serial; against a compiled clip (with or without CUDA graphs) an eager
batch loses.

## Memory

Peak allocated VRAM over each timed arm (denoise and decode), serial vs
batched, same runs as the table above:

| Card / load | Serial | Batched N=2 | Batched N=4 |
|---|---|---|---|
| A100-40, Low VRAM, eager | 4,760 MiB | 5,663 MiB | 7,468 MiB |
| A100-40, group offload, eager | 13,830 MiB | 14,312 MiB | 15,897 MiB |
| A100-80, resident compiled, forced eager batch | 24,670 MiB | 24,802
MiB | 25,861 MiB |
| T4, group offload (default) | 10,357 MiB | 10,489 MiB | 10,128 MiB |

The extra is the denoise activations of the added rows; the decode runs
one clip at a time, so it adds only the decoded clips that are already
done.

The denoise admission and the residency fit get a batch term: each row
is priced at the largest one-clip denoise peak recorded for the load
(else the base overhead), linear in rows. The decode floor stays one
clip, since decode is per clip. A batch has its own learned-peak key
(`batch=N`), so one-clip keys and peaks are unchanged.

## Not batched (yet)

- **LTX-2.5:** the Euler-ancestral renoise draws from one scheduler-held
generator for the whole call (`video_ltx25.py`, `noise_generator`), so
no row would match its solo render; `keep_tokens` is scheduler state;
two stages, the upsampler, audio latents and the remote text encoder all
need per-row plumbing.
- **MiniMax-H3 video:** batch-1 noise (`h3_reference_noise`), one shared
`position_ids` / `token_tags` / `timestep_indices` layout for every row,
the row-mod kernel turns itself off at batch > 1, and the modular
workflow renders one clip per call. For step-level batching later: the
INT8 attention's exact-start window (first 4 steps in 16-bit) is one
flag per denoiser, set each forward from the one video scheduler's
`_step_index`, so rows at different steps would need the call split by
phase.
- **Image-conditioned Wan clips** (first frame per row) still render
alone.
- **For a future LTX batch:** guidance rescale is off today
(`guidance_rescale` and `audio_guidance_rescale` are 0.0 in
`_guidance_off`); if it is ever nonzero, its std has to be per row and
leave padded audio tokens out.

## Tests

`studio/backend/tests/test_video_batch.py` (24 tests). The numeric ones
run a tiny real Diffusers Wan pipeline on the CPU through the real
`VideoBackend`:
- every batched clip is byte-identical to its solo render; one denoiser
call per step holds both rows; the text encoder sees one prompt per
call; each clip decodes alone;
- Auto batches a guided clip on a Low VRAM eager load and keeps every
other placement serial;
- neighbour invariance with the target first, middle and last: changing
only the neighbours' prompts and seeds leaves the target's frames
bit-identical;
- two experts: the high-noise expert runs first, the low-noise one
after, every call holds both clips, and each clip matches its solo
render;
- a step cache: Auto's cache refuses a join at its step count, and one
engaged after the seal renders the clips one at a time, each its own
solo render;
- out-of-memory fallback, a rider's Stop, the job's own Stop (before and
after the seal), everyone stopping, refused joins, no wait for a single
clip;
- the Auto policy, the batch price, and the drainer's contiguous
hand-over.

Related suites (video backend, routes, queue, `/v1/videos`, MCP,
accounts, residency): unchanged results; the three account test failures
are red on main too.

## Accuracy on the GPU

**Quality gate (G2c), on the placement Auto batches.** Wan 2.2 TI2V-5B,
A100-40, 960x544, 33 frames, 12 steps, default guidance (CFG 5), 4
prompts x 2 seeds. Reference: each clip rendered alone with the DiT
resident in bf16 (memory mode fast, speed off), in its own fresh
process. Floor: each clip rendered alone under Low VRAM, speed off.
Candidates: the same 8 clips in batches of 2 and of 4 under Low VRAM,
speed off. Per-frame LPIPS (alex) of each clip against its reference,
then the paired non-inferiority gate (eps +0.01 on the mean, +0.10 on
the worst pair, one-sided 95% bound, larger of the t and bootstrap
bounds):

| Batch | Per-clip statistic | Mean difference | 95% upper bound | Worst
pair | Rows worse | Verdict |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| 2 clips | mean-frame LPIPS | 0.0000 | 0.0000 | 0.0000 | 0/8 | PASS |
| 2 clips | worst-frame LPIPS | 0.0000 | 0.0000 | 0.0000 | 0/8 | PASS |
| 4 clips | mean-frame LPIPS | 0.0000 | 0.0000 | 0.0000 | 0/8 | PASS |
| 4 clips | worst-frame LPIPS | 0.0000 | 0.0000 | 0.0000 | 0/8 | PASS |

The batched clips are byte-identical to their solo renders (8 of 8 at
both sizes), and the solo renders byte-identical to the resident
reference. Controls in the same scorer: another prompt's clip scores
0.85 mean LPIPS, the same prompt at another seed 0.56. With each clip's
prompt encoded alone, the batched DiT and VAE produce exactly the solo
clip here. An earlier run that encoded the batch's prompts in one UMT5
call drifted by 0.08 mean and 0.165 worst-frame LPIPS from the solo
render, so the drift came from the batched text encode.

Speed in the same run (one pass each, 8 clips): 28.2 s per clip one at a
time, 18.1 s in batches of 2 (1.56x), 16.6 s in batches of 4 (1.70x).

**Other runs (before the per-clip encode):**

- **G1, one clip unchanged:** with no riders the decoded frames of a
seeded clip are byte-identical to main in the same process and card
(SHA-256 of the raw uint8 frames): A100-40 twice (two VMs) and T4; same
peak VRAM, same time.
- **Neighbour invariance:** with the shape fixed (2 clips), changing
only the neighbour's prompt and seed leaves the target clip's frames
bit-identical (max pixel difference 0, LPIPS 0); rerunning the identical
batch is bit-identical too. Every load above.
- **Identity:** each batched clip against its own solo render: worst
frame LPIPS 0.165, mean 0.08 (eager loads); against any other clip's
solo render the closest is 0.60. A forced eager batch on a compiled load
drifts more from its compiled solo (worst frame 0.27 to 0.31) for the
same reason a compiled clip differs from an eager one; identity still
holds (0.60 to the nearest other clip).
- In those runs a batched clip was not bit-identical to its solo render;
that difference went away with the per-clip encode (above).

Studio Windows installer: unattended runs skip UAC prompts, ARM64 shows the real CUDA tag and flags emulated shells (#19864)

## Summary

Unattended Windows installs of Unsloth Studio can no longer hang on a
UAC prompt that nobody is there to answer. The CUDA torch label now
names the build Windows on ARM actually installs. Elevated or
x64-emulated shells on Windows on ARM now print a command that reopens
PowerShell natively as the normal user.

## Device evidence

The official one-liner (`irm https://unsloth.ai/install.ps1 | iex`) was
run on a Windows 11 ARM64 machine with an NVIDIA RTX Spark, in Windows
PowerShell 5.1.

- **Native, non-elevated run:** exited 0 with "Unsloth Studio Setup
Complete" (`shell: proc=Arm64 ... elevated=False`). The Studio venv
ended up with torch `2.14.0+cu134`, CUDA available, ARM64 interpreter.
That run needed two UAC approvals, and nobody was at the machine:
1. `winget install astral-sh.uv` pulled its
`Microsoft.VCRedist.2015+.arm64` dependency, which printed "The
installer will request to run as administrator. Expect a prompt." and
then waited. One unattended attempt sat on this prompt for about 30
minutes.
2. setup.ps1 started `reg.exe add ...\FileSystem /v LongPathsEnabled
...` with `-Verb RunAs`. This also waited on UAC until the prompt was
dismissed. The installer then logged its existing decline message and
continued.
- **Mislabelled step:** the log said `installing PyTorch with CUDA
support (cu130)...` right after `windows on arm: pinning the CUDA build
this index publishes (2.14.0+cu134).` The `cu130` came from the x64
CuTag leaf, not from what was installed.
- **Elevated, x64-emulated run:** started from an elevated x64-emulated
shell (`shell: X64 ... env AMD64`), the installer printed only the
generic "Running as administrator" warning. It said nothing about the
emulation and gave no command to relaunch natively.

## Changes

**install.ps1**
- New `Test-InstallUacUnanswerable`. A run counts as unattended when any
of these holds:
- there is no interactive desktop (`[Environment]::UserInteractive` is
false)
- stdin is redirected (the same test that already suppresses the "Start
Unsloth Studio now?" question)
  - PowerShell was started with `-NonInteractive`
  - `CI` is set
  - `UNSLOTH_NONINTERACTIVE=1`

`UNSLOTH_NONINTERACTIVE=0` forces the old prompting behaviour. Unsloth
Desktop (`--tauri`) and already-elevated shells are never treated as
unattended: Desktop explains each prompt itself, and an elevated shell
triggers no prompt.
- Unattended runs install uv from its pinned release archive, which is
the existing non-winget path. winget would raise UAC for the VC++ Arm64
runtime dependency.
- The decision reaches setup.ps1 through `UNSLOTH_NONINTERACTIVE`. The
variable is only set for the child process and is removed afterwards.
- New `Write-Arm64ShellNotice`. It runs only when the machine is ARM64
and the shell is emulated or elevated. It prints `explorer.exe
"%SystemRoot%\System32\WindowsPowerShell\v1.0\powershell.exe"` (the
actual path, expanded), which opens a native, non-elevated PowerShell,
or points to the Start menu. x64 Windows prints nothing new, and install
logic is unchanged.

**studio/setup.ps1**
- New `Test-SetupUacUnanswerable`, the same rules as install.ps1 except
one: it does not read setup's own `-NonInteractive`, because the CLI
adds that flag whenever it pipes stdout.
- LongPathsEnabled: unattended runs skip the elevated `reg.exe` and
print the exact `reg add` command for an Admin terminal. This is the
same outcome as a declined prompt.
- `Ensure-VCRedist`: unattended runs skip the winget and direct-download
installers, which both raise UAC. They print the `winget install --id
Microsoft.VCRedist.2015+.x64 ...` command and the download URL instead.
- `Get-CudaTorchInstallLabel`: on Windows on ARM, the step label is the
`+cuXXX` tag of the pinned win_arm64 build (for example `cu134`). Other
platforms still print `$CuTag`.

Interactive runs behave exactly as before. install.sh and setup.sh are
untouched.

## Tests

- New `tests/studio_setup_ps1/Studio.Setup.UnattendedUac.Tests.ps1`
(Pester, 22 cases):
  - the unattended detection matrix (env knob, CI, Desktop, elevated)
- `Ensure-VCRedist` neither downloads nor starts an installer when
unattended, but still tries when attended
- the LongPaths branch is chosen before the elevated `reg.exe` and
prints the `reg add` command
- the CUDA label is `cu134` for the win_arm64 pin and `cu128` stays
`cu128` on x64
  - the uv winget gate and the hand-off to setup.ps1
- the ARM64 shell notice: emulated, elevated native, silent when native
and non-elevated, silent on x64

On main all 22 fail, because the functions do not exist. On this branch
all 22 pass.
- `Studio.Setup.SelfRerun.Tests.ps1` now stubs the new check as an
attended run, so its prompt-count assertions keep testing the attended
path under CI (`CI=true`).
- The whole `tests/studio_setup_ps1` suite passes (267 cases), with and
without `CI=true`. The Python installer text tests that read install.ps1
/ setup.ps1 also pass.

## Not verified here

- A real unattended run on Windows on ARM: that UAC is no longer raised,
that uv installs from the release archive, and that the printed commands
work.
- The new notice and `explorer.exe` relaunch from an elevated
x64-emulated shell.
- `[Environment]::UserInteractive` / redirected-stdin values under a
scheduled task or an SSH session.

Tests: read diffusion.py as UTF-8 in the MOSS hosted int8 Auto test (#19887)

## Summary


`tests/test_source_read_encoding.py::test_checked_in_file_reads_name_an_encoding`
is red on main since #19860. The new
`studio/backend/tests/test_diffusion_fp16_hosted_int8_moss_auto.py`
reads `core/inference/diffusion.py` with a bare `read_text()`, which
uses the platform default codec (cp1252 on Windows) and fails the
encoding guard:

```
AssertionError: 1 file reads in the test trees touch a checked-in file with the platform default encoding ...
  'studio/backend/tests/test_diffusion_fp16_hosted_int8_moss_auto.py:216: read_text()'
```

It fails `Repo tests (CPU, rest-2)` on every PR based on main after
#19860 (for example the staging runs for #19863 and #19878).

## Change

- Pass `encoding = "utf-8"` to that one read. The guard is correct as
written and is unchanged.

gives 1 failed, 15 passed, naming line 216.
- With this change: 16 passed.
- `pytest
studio/backend/tests/test_diffusion_fp16_hosted_int8_moss_auto.py`: 42
passed.

commits.message:
feat(verify-pr): add host capability probes and per-round VM staging (#18552)

* feat(verify-pr): add host capability probes and per-round VM staging

* fix(verify-pr): harden host staging vault, seatbelt, FIFO, and CLI guards

* fix(verify-pr): re-verify vfkit profile pre-spawn and canonicalize roots/vault

fix(ci): fail closed on authority-surface PRs and ambient credential probes (#18370)

* fix(ci): fail closed on authority-surface PRs and ambient credential probes

The precheck admitted two fork PRs that probed the review automation: one added
an environment dump and a cloud metadata credential walk to a script CI executes
after checkout, the other instructed the reviewing agent to run commands and
paste their raw output into a public comment. Neither named a GitHub secret, so
the sink/name pairs could not see them, and the manual fork-approval setting does
not cover the privileged trigger these lanes run on.

Judge reachable authority instead of known-bad wording: hold untrusted changes
to CI and agent instruction surfaces, treat ambient credential sources as a
signal on their own, and fail closed when the diff had to be truncated. Holding
rather than closing keeps a maintainer able to opt in, and closing could not
preempt lanes that start within a second of the PR being opened.

* fix(ci): close the env-dump, credential-boundary and metadata gaps in the precheck

Review of the first commit found four ways the new gate still admitted a probe:
the env rule only knew env/printenv/export -p, so set, declare -x, env -0 and a
shell -c wrapper walked past it; .credentials had no boundary and gated an
ordinary object spread; two instruction slots the loader reads under folder
trust were unprotected; and a failed metadata call substituted an empty body,
which silently stopped scanning the channel the gate exists for.

Cover every enumerated dump form, bound .credentials at a path or whitespace
edge, protect the two latent slots, and fail closed on unreadable metadata with
its own reason code. An adversarial pass over this fix caught three problems in
it: combined shell flags, a regression that dropped relative .credentials reads,
and a lone set identifier false positive. The first two are closed, the third is
recorded as accepted.

Also withdraws the design claim that the reviewer loads project context from the
checked-out contribution: that job checks out the default branch and leaves
folder trust off, so the path rule is deliberately broader than the live
channel.

* fix(ci): pin the fail-closed flags and close the wrapper and boundary gaps

Review of the second commit found five more gaps. The credential boundary had
dropped the quoted relative read; the shell -c branch carried no terminator test
and so gated ordinary wrappers such as sh -c "set -euo pipefail; make"; flags
preceding -c were unrecognised; the per-task proc path was unlisted; and neither
fail-closed CLI flag was pinned by any committed test, so renaming one left the
suite green while the arm went dark.

Give the wrapper the same terminator test as the bare branch, allow flags before
-c, enumerate the credential boundary instead of negating it, cover the per-task
proc path, and add committed cases that drive the real CLI plus a contract case
that derives the flag names from the CLI source and requires the workflow to
pass each one. Renaming a flag on either side now reds the suite.

An adversarial pass over this fix caught one more problem in it: a negated
boundary class also admits ? and ), which gated ordinary TypeScript optional
chaining and parenthesized property access. The allowed set is now enumerated and
both shapes are pinned.

* fix(ci): close the code-span, second-command and substitution credential forms

Review of the third commit found six more admitted shapes and one blind pin.

The boundary enumerated two of the three quote characters, so a markdown code
span around .credentials was admitted. The bare branch accepted no closing quote
as a terminator, so a dump after the first command of a -c string escaped both
branches. An assignment with no utility is itself an env dump, and the precision
fix that released wrapper false positives released that spelling too. The $( )
and ( ) anchors were inert because the terminator had no closing paren. Flags of
the --flag=value form were not stepped over. And the flag pin accepted an echo in
the trusted branch, so deleting the untrusted write stayed green.

Share one terminator lookahead outside the dump alternation, allow an assignment
prefix, enumerate the backtick alongside the other quotes, add the closing paren
and inline flag values, and pin the untrusted echo specifically.

Also widens the mutation harness: it now mirrors the repository layout so the
workflow-contract case cannot red for a missing file, and adds an unmutated
control that must stay green before any kill in the run is worth reading.

Discloses rather than chases the option and prefix grammar that is outside this
rule's enumerated forms: env -u NAME, env "FOO=bar", and command prefixes such as
time env or command env.

* fix(ci): protect output-language.md and stop the CLI exiting silently on odd paths

Two findings from review.

The project output-language file is an instruction input of the same class as the
context filenames, but the CLI selects it independently and appends it through
getExtensionContextFilePaths(), outside the hierarchical memory loader, so it
belongs in the protected set on its own.

The entry guard compared import.meta.url with a hand-built URL. A checkout path
containing a space, or a symlink, never matched, so the child exited 0 with no
output and the caller saw a clean-looking empty stdout instead of a decision.
Resolve the argument the same way the sibling scripts do, and pin both launch
shapes.

Review also corrected this design's trust rationale, which had been withdrawn on
a wrong premise. folderTrust is an opt-in hardened mode: measured by calling
isWorkspaceTrusted, an unset or disabled flag returns isTrusted = true, and only
enabled-with-no-stored-decision returns undefined. Project context therefore loads
by default and those slots are live, not latent. What insulates the review job is
that it checks out the default branch and starts the CLI there, not the flag.

* fix(ci): stop the paren terminator holding ordinary calls and tolerate imports

Review of the fifth commit found three more items, and one defect of my own.

Adding ) to the terminator set also held ordinary source whose last argument is
env or set: load(env), .then(set), map(set). A bare ( matched a function call as
readily as a subshell, so the paren anchor is now a subshell anchor whose
lookbehind excludes a preceding word character. Release cases are committed for
all four call shapes and a restoration arm reds them.

The code comment still asserted the trust premise the design docs had corrected,
so it disagreed with the same commit's own documentation. Rewritten in place.

The entry guard also had to learn to be imported: resolving process.argv[1] when
it is absent threw before any assertion, which is exactly how the suite and every
direct probe loads the module. Guarded and pinned with a child-process import.

Also corrects two earlier statements: env FOO="bar baz" belongs to the disclosed
option-grammar residual, and the entry fix does not remove the need to keep an
older arm's script inside the checkout when replaying a base or previous head.

* docs(ci): disclose the inline-code-span residual without gating prose

Review of the sixth commit found that `env` and its sibling dump commands written
as inline markdown code spans are still admitted. Measuring a candidate that
closes the backtick confirms that it also holds ordinary prose naming `env` or
`set` in a code span, with no evidence separating an instruction from a symbol
mention. Keep the rule behavior and record the residual and that boundary in both
design languages rather than manufacture the false positives.

Also reconcile the solution count: the four additions already have four numbered
subsections, including fail-closed handling for unreadable PR metadata.

The mutation harness now reverts to the previous head rather than HEAD. Its old

* fix(serve): fail closed on unreadable worktree sidecars during session deletion

Session deletion used `fs.existsSync` in two places before worktree
preclassification, so a dangling symlink, symlink loop, or unreadable
sidecar parent fell onto the lock-free fast path without emitting a

already introduced for archive moves across both archive and delete fast
paths (dropping the redundant wrapper in `session-archive.ts` and keeping
the synchronous coordinator prefix for genuine `ENOENT` sessions), and
switch `removeWorktreeSidecars` to a non-following `lstatSync` existence
check that absorbs parent stat errors such as `ENOTDIR`/`EACCES` so
sibling sidecar cleanup is never interrupted after transcript removal.

fix(core): stop worktree snapshot capture from freezing the daemon event loop (#18494)

* fix(core): stop worktree snapshot capture from freezing the daemon event loop

Worktree retention (#18009) captures a snapshot before deleting a checkout.
Three defects there could pin the daemon's event loop for minutes and make a
single checkout produce a multi-GB archive (#18489).

- The post-capture checkout check looked up each hashed entry with
  `regularFiles.includes()`, an O(N^2) scan inside one synchronous microtask.
  On 300k files that is a 42s stall with no timer tick; a Set lookup is 14ms.
- The archive had no bound on Qwen's own regenerable state: a checkout's
  nested `.qwen/worktrees/` (other checkouts) and `.qwen/tmp`/`.qwen/logs`
  caches were archived in full. They are now excluded through the same
  matcher the post-capture check uses, so the two geometries cannot disagree.
  `.qwen/skills`, `commands`, settings and drafts stay snapshot subjects.
- The retention sweep read `worktree.maxRetained` only once per sweep, so
  disabling retention mid-sweep still captured and then discarded every
  remaining candidate. The limit is re-read before each capture.

Verified with a mechanism witness against the real capture path: the reported
scan shape stalls 41.9s at 300k members (4.5s at 30k), the Set lookup 14ms;
a 300k-entry nested `.qwen` tree leaves a 7-member archive instead of 300,013.

* fix(core): unbreak the build and make the liveness case able to fail

- `computeCarriedIdentities` took `readonly string[]` while the caller now hands
  it the `Set` it already built for the O(1) membership check, so
  `tsc --build` failed with TS2345 and took the whole build graph with it.
  Widen the parameter to `Iterable<string>`: the body only iterates, so the
  type change adds no behaviour and every existing array caller still checks.
- The liveness case asserted `ticks > 0`, which the capture's own async work
  satisfies whether or not the membership check is a linear scan — reverting
  `regularFileSet.has(...)` to `regularFiles.includes(...)` left it green
  (measured: 34ms with the Set, 645ms with `includes`, on the same fixture).
  Repeat the genuine identities through a wrapped `computeCarriedIdentities`
  so the loop runs 3e5 times while the hashes stay real and the capture still
  completes, then bound the longest synchronous gap. The includes() arm now
  fails the bound (715ms against 200ms).

* test(core): time the membership stall only after the archive is written

The bound covered the whole capture, so tar and its disk I/O set it: with six
busy loops on ten cores the green arm moved from 34ms to 85ms, leaving a
shared runner free to cross it.

Arm the interval from `captureTiming.afterCreate` and clear it in `finally`, so
the window holds only the hashing and the membership loop. Measured on this
fixture (3000 files x 100 repeats = 3e5 identities), longest synchronous gap:

                       idle      6 busy loops / 10 cores
  Set membership       54ms      53ms
  regularFiles.includes 1529ms   1901ms

The green arm no longer moves under load, 200ms leaves >3x on it, and the
linear scan still misses the bound by >7x.

* fix(core): never drop work that the archive excludes from a snapshot

The `neverDirs` exclusions were unconditional: `.qwen/tmp/`, `.qwen/logs/` and
the whole `.qwen/worktrees/` tree were dropped from every archive while the
has-work gate counted a tracked edit (or an unregistered nested checkout) there
as work. The capture then reported `checkoutMatchesCapture: true` — the same
matcher feeds the post-capture check — the checkout was deleted, and the work
existed nowhere.

- `.qwen/tmp` and `.qwen/logs` are now disposable only where git ignores them:
  `isDisposableIgnoredEntry` recognises the two cache subtrees, so the archive
  skips them exactly when the gate waives them, and a tracked or non-ignored
  file there is archived and restored. A collapsed `.qwen/` rule still covers
  them, so a broad ignore rule keeps the original multi-GB protection.
- A nested checkout under `.qwen/worktrees/` is excluded only when it holds no
  work; one that does now refuses the capture, which makes every caller
  preserve the checkout instead of deleting it with the parent.
- The docstrings state the invariant the service actually holds, and each
  entry point gains a behaviour assertion (archive membership, restored
  content, and the refusal) rather than a timing one.

* test(core): make a nested checkout that gains work during capture visible

The post-archive check reused the pre-tar exclusion list, so a clean nested
checkout that gained a draft while tar ran was skipped on both sides and
reported as a faithful match (18494 F-5). Re-read the exclusions for that
check and pin it with the mid-capture fixture.

Co-authored-by: Qwen-Coder <qwen-coder@alibabacloud.com>

* fix(core): treat a cache container holding a checkout as work, not cache

`.qwen/tmp` and `.qwen/logs` were excluded by prefix whenever git ignored them,
but `.qwen/tmp/review-pr-<n>` is a linked worktree this repository's own review
tooling creates. The parent's status collapses to one `!! .qwen/tmp/`, so the
prefix exclusion dropped every member, `checkoutMatchesCapture` agreed (same
matcher), and `isDisposableIgnoredEntry` waived the same entry for the has-work
gate and the change digest — both removal guards read the parent as clean, and a
`requireSnapshot: false` path deleted it without a snapshot at all.

- The cache containers are now scanned as containers: a `.git` FILE is a linked
  worktree (work → refuse the capture, clean → exclude that child by path), a
  `.git` DIRECTORY is an independent repository that is never excluded, and the
  prefix goes only when the container holds no checkout at all, which keeps the
  multi-GB cache protection.
- The ignore-derived `dirs`/`files` geometry skips the same containers, so the
  archive cannot exclude by prefix what the container scan declined to exclude.
- `isWaivableIgnoredEntry` makes the waiver container-aware, and both guards —
  `worktreeHasWork`/`hasNonCarriedWork` and the cleanup change digest — use it.

* fix(core): refuse a capture before it creates the snapshot directory

Moving `readSnapshotExclusions` into the archive callback (the mid-capture
re-read) also moved the first refusal after `fs.mkdir(snapshotDir)`, so a FIFO,
a case-variant path or a non-UTF-8 symlink target left an empty archive
directory behind for a capture that produced nothing. Two existing cases assert
that directory is absent and went red.

Run the exclusion table once as a pre-flight, before the directory exists. The
callback still re-reads it for the tar filter and `checkoutMatchesCapture` still
uses a fresh read, so the race hardening this was added for is unchanged.

* fix(core): never exclude a checkout the archive cannot rebuild

- A nested checkout is excludable only when its .git is a file naming a
  git dir outside this checkout AND its HEAD is a branch; a git dir
  inside the tree being deleted, a .git directory, or a detached HEAD
  is archived instead, because the parent deletion is the last copy.
- An ignored .qwen cache that directly holds a checkout is not
  regenerable: the review tooling puts its worktrees under .qwen/tmp,
  whose drafts exist nowhere else.
- Verification compares against the archive's own members, so an archive
  written before the exclusion still verifies instead of tripping the
  capture-time refusal.
- The exclusion preflight runs before the snapshot directory is created,
  so a refusal leaves no empty directory behind.

* fix(core): preserve nested git stores/checkouts under ignored caches and fix post-tar verification

- Replace the one-level cache container check with recursive, non-following
  `inspectCacheContainer`: finds nested checkouts at any depth (including
  `.qwen/tmp` itself and `.qwen/tmp/runs/inner`), bare / `--separate-git-dir`
  object stores (`.qwen/tmp/inner-git`), and unreadable subtrees (fail-closed).
- Cache container inspections per status/digest call in `worktreeHasWork`,
  `hasNonCarriedWork`, and `checkoutChangeDigest` to eliminate O(N^2) scans
  under `.qwen/tmp/*`.
- Add `preservedDirs` to the snapshot exclusion matcher so independent repos
  and in-tree `--separate-git-dir` object stores stay archived while sibling
  plain cache files remain excluded, and check legacy `archived` membership at
  each child checkout path rather than skipping the whole cache container
  (fixing repeated retention sweeps accumulating redundant snapshots when a
  clean linked worktree sits inside `.qwen/tmp`).
- Refuse capture on external linked worktrees with detached HEAD, missing
  branch ref, or metadata inside this worktree's own admin dir so parent
  deletion plus `git worktree prune --expire=now` cannot break HEAD or strand
  detached commits.
- Check `.qwen/worktrees` with `lstat` before scanning so a symlinked
  `.qwen/worktrees` is archived as a link without inspecting external targets.
- Skip the pre-tar case-variant protected-path throw on the post-tar
  exclusion re-read so late `.GIT` arrivals report `checkoutMatchesCapture:
  false` as expected on Linux while late nested-checkout work still refuses.

* test(core): give the stall-bound case an explicit timeout

The case asserts the longest synchronous gap stays under 200ms; it does not
assert how long the capture takes. That duration now follows the capture path
(about 1s when it was written, 5s after the newest refactor, and 16.4s on one
cold run), so the runner's default 15s was doing double duty as an implicit
duration assertion and a slow host read as a regression to the linear scan.

Raise it to 60s and say why beside the assertion.

* fix(core): close nested ignored-dir, separate-git-dir verify, O(depth) matcher, and digest/limit gaps

- Inspect ignored directories of a candidate excludable nested checkout before
  excluding it wholesale (`nestedCheckoutHasIgnoredGitState`), so a third-level
  worktree or git store inside e.g. `inner/dist/vendor-demo` refuses capture
  and preserves its draft.
- Preserve in-tree `--separate-git-dir` store paths (`resolveInTreeGitStorePaths`)
  during post-capture verification even when the archive already carries the
  nested checkout directory, so late commits/branches in ignored `dist/inner.git`
  fail verification and preserve the parent checkout.
- Replace linear `matcher.dirs.some` / `neverDirs.some` / `preservedDirs` prefix
  scans with O(depth) ancestor-set lookups (`matchesDirSet` + precomputed
  `preservedAncestors` / `ignoredAncestors`), cutting 6,000-dir `.qwen/tmp/*`
  event-loop lag from ~1s down to ~13ms.
- Classify untracked nested repo entries (`?? <dir>/` from `--untracked-files=all`)
  so detached external worktrees mounted directly on `.qwen/tmp` refuse capture
  even under `.qwen/tmp/*` or without an ignore rule.
- Align `checkoutChangeDigest` with the archive by waiving clean regenerable
  `.qwen/tmp/` and `.qwen/logs/` subtrees under broad `.qwen/` rules or beside
  nested checkouts (R2-5), abort in-flight retention sweeps when `maxRetained`
  changes to a different limit (R1-2), tighten the O(N^2) liveness timer window
  (R1-3), and document the cache waivers on `worktreeHasWork` (R2-4).

* fix(core): classify unignored repos beside ignored cache dirs and archive standalone external --separate-git-dir repos

- Mark `handledCheckouts` only after confirming a cache-container checkout is
  covered by an ignore rule, so an unignored repo such as `.qwen/tmp/review`
  beside an ignored (even empty) `.qwen/tmp/cache/` still reaches
  `untrackedRepoDirs` to preserve its `--separate-git-dir` store (e.g.
  `dist/inner.git`) or refuse an external detached linked worktree.
- Distinguish prunable external linked worktrees (`commondir` or `gitdir`
  back-pointer present inside `realGitDir`, fail-closed on non-ENOENT errors)
  from standalone external `--separate-git-dir` repos so e.g. `vendor/inner`
  with uncommitted drafts archives cleanly instead of blocking retention
  sweeps, and survives `git worktree prune --expire=now` plus restore.

* fix(core): trace symlinked git objects, alternates, and in-tree gitdir links during snapshot capture and verification

- Add step-by-step symlink resolution tracing (`tracePathResolution` +
  `traceGitStoreDependencies`) for nested repositories (both `.git` files and
  `.git` directories): inspects `rawGitDir`, `commondir`, `HEAD`, `objects/`,
  `objects/pack`, `objects/info`, `objects/info/alternates` (up to depth 5),
  `refs/`, `reftable/`, `packed-refs`, `config`, `index`, and `logs`.
- Preserve every in-tree symlink or object-store path needed to resolve `.git`
  and its objects (e.g. an external `--separate-git-dir` whose `objects/`
  symlinks into `.qwen/tmp/git-objects/`, a `.git` file traversing a symlink
  inside `.qwen/tmp/`, or a shared clone borrowing objects from ignored
  `dist/`) during both capture and post-capture verification.
- Fail closed (refuse capture) when store resolution hits the unarchivable
  top-level `.git` root, the parent worktree's own admin dir, unreadable or
  looping symlinks, or when an external linked worktree resolves git metadata
  through paths inside the checkout being deleted.

* fix(core): scan symlinks inside git stores, resolve .. in POSIX symlink order, and handle quoted alternates fail-closed

- Recursively scan `objects/`, `refs/`, and `reftable/` (`scanDirSymlinks`) so
  individual symlinked pack files (e.g. after `git repack -ad` moving `.pack`
  into ignored `.qwen/tmp/`), loose objects, or ref files are preserved across
  capture, verification, and restore.
- Reimplement `tracePathResolution` with a raw segment queue following POSIX
  `path_resolution(7)` order (never folding `route/..` lexically before
  following symlink `route`), and preserve in-tree directory anchors stepped
  through before `..` (e.g. `.qwen/tmp/anchor` for `route/../refs`) in
  `preservedAncestors` without pulling in unrelated cache children.
- Parse Git C-quoted paths in `objects/info/alternates` (`unquoteGitPath`),
  and check `targets.unreadableDependency` before `if (targets.insideWorktree)`
  so unreadable or malformed alternates inside an in-tree `--separate-git-dir`
  refuse capture fail-closed rather than silently dropping objects.

* fix(core): canonicalize on-disk entry spelling for case-insensitive aliases and fail-close verification on unreadable git stores

- Add `resolveActualEntryName` (with per-traversal `CachedDirEntries` lookup)
  inside `tracePathResolution`: exact matches return in O(1) so case-sensitive
  volumes keep distinguishing distinct files differing only in case, while
  case-insensitive/Unicode-normalizing aliases (e.g. `.QWEN/TMP/git-objects`
  or `.QWEN/TMP/*.pack` on APFS) canonicalize to the on-disk directory entry
  spelling observed by `readdir`/`tar`.
- Return `{ deps, unverifiable }` from `resolveInTreeGitStorePaths` and
  propagate `unverifiableDependency` through `boundedSnapshotExclusions` and
  `DisposableIgnoredMatcher` so `verifyRestoredWorktreeSnapshot` returns
  `false` when an object directory (e.g. `objects/<2hex>/` set to `0111`
  after capture) cannot be enumerated before deletion.

Per review feedback (#18494 comment 7223070238), restore the baseline
(94b1d9dc) snapshot archive exclusion, has-work waiver, and cleanup digest
scope so cache slimming can land separately once provably-regenerable rules
are defined without risking main-repo, nested-repo, or user state.

Net changes in this PR relative to merge-base 94b1d9dc:
- Replace the synchronous O(N^2) `regularFiles.includes(entry.path)` scan in
  `checkoutMatchesCapture` with a `Set` lookup (`regularFileSet.has`), plus
  the liveness regression test.
- Re-read `worktree.maxRetained` before each retention candidate in
  `sweepWorktreeRetentionOnceInStorage` and stop immediately when disabled
  (`0`) or changed (`sweepLimit !== scope.limit`), plus both regression tests.

If `worktree.maxRetained` is disabled (`0`) or changed while a retention
candidate is queued on the worktree ownership lock, re-read the limit under

ci(lint): share the content-verified pnpm store across runs (#18548)

* ci(lint): share the content-verified pnpm store across runs

The two ungated lanes publish a run-unique HOME to keep a fork's ~/.npmrc
from reaching the next job on the registration. pnpm resolves its store
through XDG_DATA_HOME, so that store sat inside the per-run home and was
reclaimed with it: every run refetched all ~2300 packages. The cost was
accepted at ~900 s, but the tail is long -- five green lint runs on
2026-11-27 spent 6m32s-24m35s in the install step, and PR #18543's run
(job 140553347054) hit the step's 30-minute cap two packages short of
done, skipping all 20 lint steps. Registry egress compounds it: the same
12 MB tarball measured 86 KB/s direct from Hangzhou vs 19 MB/s via HK.

Point XDG_DATA_HOME at the persistent tool cache instead. Sharing is
licensed by the same property that already makes the linter-archive cache
shareable: pnpm re-verifies every store entry on a warm hit. Measured on
pnpm 11.24.0 with a three-arm probe -- pristine store reuses, an
equal-length tamper is rejected and refetched, and only
verify-store-integrity=false adopts the tampered bytes. HOME stays
run-unique, and COREPACK_HOME stays inside it because corepack does not
re-verify on hit.

The routing battery pins both halves of that argument (the shared path,
and .npmrc not disabling the check), plus the coupling to
reap-isolated-home.sh: XDG_DATA_HOME joins HOME_KEYS so a daemon holding
that path stays reaper-selectable if the path ever moves back inside the
home. Four mutation arms confirm the pins discriminate.

* ci(lint): gate the shared pnpm store on trusted writers, not on verification

Review disproved the safety argument in d4d893e. pnpm's store check is a
corruption check, not a trust boundary: verifyFile() skips the digest read
whenever size and mtime still match the index, and pnpm's own source says
verification "does not make a store writable by untrusted users safe".

The original three-arm probe could not see this because writing the tamper
bumped mtime. Re-run with a fresh store per arm and mtime restored, an
equal-length write lands the poisoned bytes (reused 1, downloaded 0) through
in-place r+b, truncate AND atomic replace; only leaving mtime bumped
triggers a refetch. So a store on a pool that admits forks is a cross-job
poisoning channel regardless of the integrity setting.

Gate sharing on trust instead. SHARED_STORE_ELIGIBLE requires the persistent
self-hosted fleet and excludes the ephemeral pool pick_runner assigns to
untrusted forks; both the mkdir and the publish sit inside that guard, and
nothing touches the shared path outside it. Forks keep a per-run store.

Also close the second review finding: the assertion only scanned .npmrc,
but pnpm reads verifyStoreIntegrity from pnpm-workspace.yaml too (confirmed
via pnpm config list --json on 11.24.0), so flipping it there would have
left the test green. Both surfaces are now pinned.

The battery pins the gate by value (both halves of the expression), the
guard's structure, and both config surfaces. Mutation arms: dropping the
ephemeral exclusion, moving the publish outside the guard, and setting
verifyStoreIntegrity: false in pnpm-workspace.yaml each turn it red.

Both design language versions now state the corrected mechanism, record
that the first draft's justification was disproved, and name the two
properties that remain unenforced for the store path: no ownership recovery
and no disk floor of its own.

ci(web-shell): isolate browser smoke in a loopback-only netns on self-hosted runners (#18547)

* ci(web-shell): isolate browser smoke in a loopback-only netns on self-hosted runners

On shared self-hosted ECS hosts, sibling Docker-backed jobs (such as
sandbox:docker E2E) create and remove bridge-networked containers every
few seconds, emitting host-level docker0/veth netlink events that cause
Chromium's NetworkChangeNotifierLinux to abort in-flight localhost Vite
ESM module requests with net::ERR_NETWORK_CHANGED.

Wrap `Run web-shell browser smoke` in `bwrap --unshare-net` on
self-hosted runners (fail-closed if bwrap cannot isolate, stripping
unreachable host loopback proxy env vars, and keeping a pre-merge `-f`
guard for open PR heads that predate the script). Leave
`Run transcript document browser gate` outside the loopback-only netns
since it fetches the pinned legacy renderer from unpkg/npm.

Also split the four-width sidebar reload loop out of the update
lifecycle smoke test in `web-shell.update.spec.ts` so neither test stacks
six full reloads inside a single 60s timeout budget on busy hosts.

* fix(ci): drop --die-with-parent from bwrap to avoid SIGKILL on Runner.Worker thread exit

On Linux, `bwrap --die-with-parent` sets `PR_SET_PDEATHSIG(SIGKILL)`,
which fires when the spawning *thread* exits rather than the parent
process. Because the workflow step `exec`s `bwrap` directly under the
multi-threaded `.NET Runner.Worker`, ThreadPool worker-thread retirement
killed `bwrap` with exit code 137 after 3m50s (job 140587110681) while
leaving npm and Chromium alive for post-job cleanup.

Remove `--die-with-parent` (GitHub Actions already tracks and reaps step
processes via `RUNNER_TRACKING_ID`) and pin its absence in the unit
suite.

* test(web-shell): deduplicate sidebar widths and assert no update POSTs on reload

Address review feedback on the split sidebar-width update smoke test:
- Replace `[220, 343, 360, 260]` (where both `220` and `260` clamp to the
  276px rail-layout minimum) with the three distinct rendered widths
  (`220 -> 276px`, `343 -> 343px`, `360 -> 360px`) and assert the rendered
  sidebar width via `toHaveCSS('width', ...)` on each pass.
- Match the real daemon's `ready` state (`canInstall: false`) in the mock
  handler and assert that reloading a ready page sends zero `POST` requests
  to `/daemon/update`.

feat(cli): Push an ingested Turn's events from the Harness (#18519)

* docs(managed-agent): Propose Harness event ingest

Let the Hosted Harness deliver an admitted Turn's committed events to any
control-plane instance, so no Java instance stays attached to the Turn's
event stream. The admission hands the Turn's dispatch lease to the
Harness, whose ingest requests renew it; existing guards, the sweep and
recovery paths keep working unchanged.

* feat(managed-agent): Add the Harness event ingest route

A Hosted Harness that holds a Turn's dispatch lease can push the Turn's
committed event envelopes to any control-plane instance. The route
authenticates the Session's writer, live or, for a park marker,
clean-sealed; records the envelopes by the stream consumer's rules; and
renews the lease. The stream consumer's per-envelope logic moves to a
shared recorder so both paths record identically. Nothing requests
ingest yet.

* docs(managed-agent): Align the ingest design with its route

The request names the Harness by its writer ID, which is the boot ID,
and an end marker that cannot apply answers
managed_event_ingest_end_refused. Mark the first slice as implemented.

* feat(managed-agent): Report terminal settlement in ingest replies

The pusher needs a defined stop signal once its batch settles the Turn,
so the ingest receipt now carries terminal: true for that request.

* docs(managed-agent): Address the event ingest design review

Correct the recording lock order, qualify the kill-Java and
pre-admission failure rows, define the terminal reply, record the
heartbeat-versus-recording window and the sealed-marker outcome, state
the cross-instance clock exposure, and tighten the current-state
summary.

* feat(cli): Push an ingested Turn's events from the Harness

A prompt submission that asks for event ingest starts a pusher. The
pusher sends the Turn's committed envelopes to the Session Store from
the admission cursor, follows the cursor the control plane reports,
renews the Turn lease with heartbeats, and stops when the reply settles
the Turn or the Harness no longer holds it. It posts the
recovery-blocked marker when the control plane's probe would, and an
Action-parked suspension posts the park marker between the seal and the
placement release. The Harness advertises event-ingest/1.

* docs(managed-agent): Record the Harness pusher's admission and suspension rules

A malformed ingest request is refused before admission, and a Session
without an HTTP Session Store answers a retryable conflict. A pusher
counts as an open event stream for suspension. There is one pusher per
ingest admission, and the first two slices are now implemented.

* test(managed-agent): Pin the event ingest facade entry

ManagedStoreDecompositionTest compares a closed inventory with every
non-private method of the Session Store facade, so the new
authenticateEventIngest entry belongs in it.

* docs(managed-agent): Address the second event ingest review round

Say that the cancel take-back ignores the lease deadline and the retry
delay, that a success after an end marker stops the pusher, and list
the feature token and submit-body files. Restore the recording lock
order: the Session read locks the event stream before the Turn.

fix(core): point at the JSON error when a tool arg arrives as broken text (#18481)

* fix(core): point at the JSON error when a tool arg arrives as broken text

When a model writes an array or object argument with a syntax error,
DashScope (with tool_stream off) sends the value on as a string. The
schema then fails with "params/docs must be array", which does not say
the text itself is broken, so the model resends the same text until it
gives up.

When a type error expects an array or object and the value is a string
that starts like JSON but does not parse, the error now adds the parse
error, the text near it with the exact spot marked, and asks for the
value as JSON rather than a string.

* fix(core): keep the quoted JSON excerpt on character boundaries

The excerpt around the parse error is cut by UTF-16 index, so an edge
could fall inside a surrogate pair and quote half a character. Drop the
stray half at either edge. Also cover a plain object-typed field on its
own, not only under anyOf.

then failed with "Failed to create release, \"workflow\" scope may be
required", leaving no tag or GitHub release behind (issue #18493).

The neighbouring steps (commit/push and release PR creation) already use
secrets.CI_BOT_PAT; use the same token for the release so the step can
complete after the package is already published.

Adds a regression test pinning the step's token so a revert is caught
before a future release.

* fix(ci): keep SDK releases out of the CLI release consumers

Creating the SDK release with CI_BOT_PAT (issue #18493) makes it emit
`release: published`, which GITHUB_TOKEN-created releases never did. Every
`sdk-typescript-*` tag now reaches the workflows watching that event, and two
of them cannot succeed on it: finalize-release exits 1 at "Validate stable
release tag", and sync-release-to-oss holds its single concurrency lock while
`gh release download` finds the assets an SDK release does not ship. Both
failures are observable on the PAT-created sdk-typescript-v0.1.29 release
(Finalize Stable Release and Sync Release to Aliyun OSS), and
dsw-swe-verified-release also starts a self-hosted gate job that only no-ops.

Guard all three job `if`s with the tag prefix their siblings already use
(release-managed-runtime.yml, release-vscode-companion.yml), keeping the
workflow_dispatch arm each declares. One test pins all three guards.

* fix(ci): keep SDK releases out of CLI release consumers

* fix(ci): keep dsw-eas release-event smokes in the benchmark gate

The v-prefix guard added for sdk-typescript-* tags also excluded the
workflow's own dsw-eas-smoke/tb-smoke/full prerelease tags, whose only
trigger is the release event, silently turning benchmark smokes into
green no-op runs.

* test(ci): pin the release guard expressions exactly

Replace the disjoint substring assertions with one normalized
full-expression table so an operator flip or negated startsWith goes
red, and drop the weaker duplicate copies from the other two test
files.

* fix(ci): exclude only the SDK tag family from the benchmark gate

Enumerating allowed families (`v*` or `dsw-eas-*`) silently deletes
whatever release family is added next, which is the failure the
previous commit repaired. Excluding only `sdk-typescript-*` leaves
every other release event reaching the gate exactly as it did before
the guard existed.

* test(ci): name the guard test for what it pins

The DSW gate is not a CLI consumer, so a title claiming it fans only
to CLI tags is the misreading that made the over-broad prefix look safe.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

fix(ios): match app names in SpringBoard's captions up to punctuation

walkShowsHome took an app's name from a caption by parseCaption, which
splits at ", " and "，" only. What follows an icon's name is the phone's
language's, and what a Japanese phone puts there, likely "、", has not
been seen: an icon with a badge or a trait would then name no app, and a
Japanese home screen could fall short of three names and fail to read on
the inspector path.

A caption now names an app when it begins with one of the app's names
followed by its end or a punctuation mark (unicode.IsPunct), the longest
such name when several are (captionApp). So "Mail-Box, 1 new item" names
Mail-Box rather than Mail, a name may hold a punctuation mark ("Yahoo!"),
and "Notesheet" does not name Notes. splitCaption stays as it is: Chinese
text uses "、" inside a label too.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

fix(ios): name SpringBoard's walk the home screen only with its icons

When remoteAXService fails, a read falls back to the inspector's walk.
A walk whose elements were mostly SpringBoard's was named the home
screen, which the gateway lets be pictured, also when SpringBoard only
drew over an app: Face ID's prompt or its fade-out, an alert, a banner.
The picture could then take in the app beneath, a blocked one included.

The walk gives no element types, and nothing recorded tells an icon by
its caption or identifier. So a walk of SpringBoard's elements is now
the home screen only on a locked phone or when their captions begin with
the names of 3 different apps in the catalog, which has the home
screen's names in the phone's language (walkShowsHome). Otherwise the
walk names no app: the read gets the app knownFront allows, as a partial
read, or none, and then takes no picture and fails with errAppUnknown.
A home screen named from the walk is recorded for knownFront, as
screenApp's is on the remoteAXService path. AXDevice.Observe, below
iOS 27, follows the same rule.

fix(standalone): never take the task before for the one that starts

Before the agent connects, the core finds its gateway task by when it
started, allowing a second before the agent's start. A task that ended
within that second, as one does when the next starts right after it,
was taken for the new one: the task screen showed its steps under the
new task, and a new task that ended before it connected, such as with
no key, wrote its end over the earlier task's in runs.json, so Activity
showed that task as not started. The gateway starts the task when the
agent connects, after the agent started, so the slack is not needed.

fix(ios): mask a password on an iPhone while it is shown

A field with no label of its own, such as a web page's password field
named only by its placeholder, is named by its text once it holds some,
and a password field the person shows is an ordinary text field. The
policy saw no name in it: the password stayed in history's screen text
and typing into it skipped the password switch. Keep the placeholder as
the field's hint, as the Android drivers keep theirs.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

docs: release notes for the stuck accessibility service on iPhones (#248)

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

fix(ios): tell when axauditd is stuck, and stop guessing the home screen (#248)

In #248 an iPhone 18 Pro on iOS 27.2, used over Wi-Fi, answered none
of over 280 screen reads in more than two hours: remoteAXService's
handshake got no answer within 5 s, and the inspector walk that stands
in for it timed out on its first focus request. Screenshots, OCR, the
live picture, taps and app launches went on working; restarting Pinky
and a new tunnel did not help. Both services are axauditd's. When it
was seen stuck before, only restarting the iPhone brought it back.

Those reads were named the home screen. A read without a tree took its
app from the inspector session's app states, which fall back to
SpringBoard when the session has heard of no app (on iOS 27 it has not
of one in front since before it connected), or, after web content, from
the last read remoteAXService answered, however long ago. The gateway
then let the read take and read its picture as the home screen's,
whatever app was on screen, a blocked one included. Those states cannot
tell the app on screen anyway: iOS reports apps it wakes in the
background in the foreground too.

Now such a read (no elements, none of a process Pinky can name, or no
walk after web content) names only the app the last read able to tell
named (knownfront.go): remoteAXService's frontmost home screen app, or
SpringBoard with the home screen's icons (screenApp's new named
result), or the home screen app that owns a walk's elements (walkApp,
which also names a web view's host). It does so for 30 s at most, while
the inspector session has listened since before that read, answered
during this one (its walk, or a 2 s ping when there is no walk), and
heard of no other app coming to the foreground, nor of that one
leaving it. Such a read is partial and does not renew the record.
Otherwise it names no app, so the gateway lets it take no picture, and
it fails with what failed. A read that finds the phone locked drops the
record. AXDevice.Observe follows the same rules.

axstuck.go finds the daemon stuck when remoteAXService timed out
(errRAXTimeout) and the inspector did not answer either (its handshake,
a ping or a walk's first requests), while lockdown answered and the
phone is unlocked: three such reads in a row over at least two minutes,
no two more than five minutes apart, while the phone gives pictures (a
screenshot or video frame within a minute, else one taken to see, at
most every 30 s, and not read). Any read the daemon answers clears it.
While it lasts, each read fails with words for the agent: the service
stopped answering; screenshots and taps still work; restarting
Pinky or reconnecting the iPhone does not help, restarting it does; so
call phone_handoff and ask the person to restart it. The error wraps
nothing, so the gateway passes it on instead of its own words for a
deadline. pinky.log says when it is found and when the daemon answers
again; a read's own line has stuck_for and the read's own error.

The checkup of an iPhone on iOS 27 gets a Reading the screen item
(driver.CheckReading) that asks the phone nothing: it fails with
driver.FixRestartStuck while reads find the daemon stuck, and the
client says to restart the iPhone, with no button. Its words are in
English, Simplified Chinese and Japanese.

Nothing keeps the daemon from getting stuck (what does is not known),
and Pinky never restarts the phone. Tested with fakes only
(knownfront_test.go, axstuck_test.go, the gateway's stuckread_test.go
and the checkup's tests), not on a phone.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

fix(ios): build the Simulator's WebDriverAgent without files Xcode lacks

WebDriverAgent 16.15.3's runner embeds files of the Simulator platform
and leaves some of them out by Xcode's major version: with any Xcode 26
it embeds lib_TestingInterop.dylib, which Xcode 26.2 (17C52) and 26.3
do not have. The build stopped at the copy (lstat: No such file or
directory), so Simulators could not be used with those versions (#245).
WDA has no newer release and no fix upstream.

Before building, missingPlatformFiles reads the project's references to
the platform's files (sourceTree PLATFORM_DIR) and lstats each in the
Xcode, as the copy does. Those missing go on the command line as
EXCLUDED_SOURCE_FILE_NAMES=$(inherited) <names> (wdaBuildArgs), which
keeps the project's own list for the SDK and leaves the checked source
untouched, and pinky.log says so. With an Xcode that has them all, the
arguments do not change. buildWDA takes the provider's logger for that.

On Xcode 27.2 the override reaches the runner's copy phase: the build
succeeded without lib_TestingInterop.dylib and wrote the .xctestrun.
Not run on 26.2 or 26.3; the reporter ran a runner built without the
file on 26.2.

docs: release notes for the still-screen video restarts

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

fix(ios): stop restarting the video stream on a still screen

Idle probes asked a watched stream for a key frame after 5 s without a
frame and failed it when none came within 2 s, on the premise that a
working phone answers such a request, still screen or not. It does not:
the owner's log has 43 such restarts (37 from the iPhone 13 mini on
2026-11-24 and 25, 6 from the iPad on 2026-11-26), all why=idle, 40 of
them with no RTP after the last frame and nothing lost, and #235's
iPhone 17 had 43 more. Idle probes go (probeIdle, probeIdleMax, the
watched case and the doubling); input probes, probeHold and the
dark-screen check stay.

A frame that comes while the probe decides (screenDark asks the phone,
which takes a while) now answers the probe instead of failing the
stream, as it did twice in the owner's log (since_frame=-100ms).

The log line's sr_sent_since_frame subtracted the count of the last
sender report before the last frame, which can be a second older than
the frame, so it counted packets that came (180 in #235's line, which
lost none). sr_missing replaces it: the packet count of the phone's last
sender report minus the RTP packets that had come when that report did,
recorded in onRTCP under the stats' lock. frameCounts.srSent goes. The
why field, always input now, gives way to since_input.

test(pilot): stop waiting for the idle lock poll in TestUnlockWindowSkipsUnattendedRuns

test(pilot): stop waiting for the idle lock poll in TestUnlockWindowSkipsUnattendedRuns

The test locked the demo phone and waited up to 2 s for the gateway to
list it locked, before any task ran. With no task on a phone, the
gateway reads its lock only every idleLockEvery (6 s). When that read
ran between the phone showing up and SetLocked, the next one came after
the deadline, and the test failed with "the gateway did not see the
phone locked".

The wait is not needed: the scheduled run's first read sees the lock
on its own, which is what the test checks. Without the Unattended check
in windowOpenForLocked, the test still fails.

fix(langfuse): upload base64 media and export its reference from the langfuse callback (#53934)

* fix(langfuse): upload base64 media and export its reference from the langfuse callback

The v2 SDK replaced base64 payloads in a trace's input, output and metadata with
Langfuse media references and uploaded the bytes before ingestion. The v4 export
channel sends spans through litellm's own exporter, which had no such step, so
images reached Langfuse inline and multiplied the stored trace size on servers
that do not extract them.

The export channel now replaces data URIs and the Anthropic and Vertex typed
blocks with the same references and uploads the bytes through the Langfuse media
REST API on one background thread per channel.

* fix(langfuse): bound queued media by bytes and stop trusting the storage response

Media the uploader has no room for now stays inline in the span, the cap counts
decoded bytes, and a failed upload makes flush report failure. The storage PUT
no longer follows redirects and Langfuse is told the storage status without the
storage response body. A data URI followed by text is left as it is, trace level
media is registered without an observation, and queued uploads get five seconds
to finish at shutdown.

* fix(langfuse): validate upload URLs for request-supplied hosts and queue an attribute's media as a whole

A Langfuse host that comes with a key's or team's credentials now has the upload
URLs it returns checked with validate_url, so it cannot point the upload at an
internal address. A host the operator configured keeps naming its own storage.
The media of one attribute is queued all together or not at all, so an attribute
that stays inline no longer leaves part of its media uploading.

* fix(langfuse): keep media inline while Langfuse cannot store it

A Langfuse with no media route or bucket, or one whose upload URL is refused, answers the same
way for every payload. After the first such answer the uploader turns media away, so the exporter
keeps it inline, and one upload per pause checks whether Langfuse takes media again.

* fix(langfuse): re-send a media registration that does not reach Langfuse

The span export keeps trying through a short Langfuse outage, so a trace could arrive with a
reference whose single registration attempt had failed. Registration now waits out the same delays.

* fix(langfuse): replace base64 media in model parameters

A call rejected before the provider, such as an unknown model or a failed key check, is logged
with its request body as the model parameters, which left the image inline in those traces.

* Revert "fix(langfuse): replace base64 media in model parameters"

This reverts commit 3a4894c78eb58ca47c1aa3f28d1eeed26a059d0d.

* fix(langfuse): leave the media storage response body unread

Only the status of the storage PUT is used, and an upload URL can answer with a body of any size.

* fix(langfuse): always export the media reference, as the Langfuse SDK does

Drops the pause that kept media inline after the media API failed. A self-hosted Langfuse needs a media bucket, as its docs state.

* fix(langfuse): read the HTTP client from the handler on every media upload

litellm closes a pooled client once its cache entry expires (one hour plus
the close grace) and the handler opens another. The uploader held the first
client, so later uploads raised 'client has been closed' and traces kept a
reference with no file. The span exporter already reads handler.client per
request.

* perf(langfuse): skip the media parse for values that only mention base64

extract_media parsed and walked any value that held the text base64 or
mime_type. It now parses only a value that holds a base64 data URI, or a
content type key next to a data key, which every payload it replaces has.

* test(langfuse): check media-free values by their output only

* fix(langfuse): stop validating the media upload URL for key and team hosts

The Langfuse host on a key or team is not validated by default, so checking only the
upload URL it returns added no protection. The check resolved DNS on the proxy and
refused storage that is private or reachable only through an egress proxy, which left
the trace with a media reference and no file.

* fix(langfuse): restart the media upload thread in a forked child

A fork copies the upload queue but none of the parent's threads, so a child forked after
the first logged call wrote media references that nothing uploaded. The child now gets
its own queue and thread, and the parent keeps uploading what it had queued.

* fix(langfuse): upload Gemini inline_data parts as media

The Langfuse SDK replaces Gemini inline_data and inlineData parts with a media reference. The callback now does the same, so a Gemini-native request with an image no longer stores its base64 inline.

* fix(langfuse): size the media upload queue from an env setting and stop keeping media inline when it is full

LANGFUSE_MEDIA_QUEUE_MAX_BYTES sets how many decoded bytes wait for upload per
export channel, 100 MB when unset. Media that does not fit is no longer kept
inline in the span: the span carries the reference, the upload is skipped with
a warning and counted as failed, as the Langfuse SDK does when its queue is
full.

* fix(langfuse): give a forked child its own failure lock

A lock a parent thread held at the fork stays locked in the child. The queue
test now holds the first upload until the second has been turned away.

refactor(rust): log from the core crates with tracing instead of host calls (#54788)

* refactor(rust): log from the core crates with tracing instead of host calls

router-core asked its host to write two model info log lines through an
awaited lookup, and the model capacity engine asked its host for every
warning and error line plus a fixed "unlicensed priority" line. A log line
is not something only the host can answer, so both crates now emit these
lines with tracing and the three host surfaces are gone from the traits,
from the native and Python hosts and from the Python answering code.

The Python proxy still gets the same lines at the same level on the same
logger. The bridge already delivers tracing events to Python logging, so
its target table now sends the capacity crate to "LiteLLM Proxy" and
router-core's model info module to "LiteLLM Router", and a model info
query runs under the calling request's logger so a level change is seen
at once.

A line logged on a runtime task is queued and handed to Python from the
blocking pool, so it can land after the call that logged it returns. The
bridge gains native_log_lines_delivered(), an awaitable that resolves once
the queued lines are delivered, and the capacity tests await it before
reading each step's lines.

* refactor(rust): name the log delivery wait rust_log_lines_delivered

The Rust workspace says "Rust", not "Native", for something written in Rust.

* fix(proxy): deliver queued Rust log lines before the proxy shuts down

A log line a Rust runtime task queued could be lost when the proxy stopped
before the queue was drained. Shutdown now waits for the queue, after the
steps that can still log.

The queue also reported its dropped-line count only when a later batch
arrived, so a drop during the last batch was never reported. It is now
reported once the queue is empty, and a delivery wait ends only after that
report.

* fix(proxy): bound the shutdown wait for queued Rust log lines

The wait had no timeout, so a log handler that stalled would hold worker
shutdown until an outside kill. It now gives up after five seconds or when
the graceful shutdown window runs out, whichever comes first. A timeout is
not logged, because a stalled handler holds its lock and the warning would
block on it too.

The native stub's __all__ was missing the three cost-map refresh classes that the

test(unit): make 21 flaky unit tests deterministic (#54785)

* test(unit): make 20 flaky unit tests deterministic

These tests failed on main and on PR reruns over the last two weeks without a code change. Each fix keeps
what the test proves and only removes the timing, clock or shared-state dependency.

Router usage tests now read usage with usage_since, because the Rust core stamps usage with its own system
clock, so a read in the next minute missed the write. The header parity test checks the remaining count
against the minute the header was read in. The websocket admission test pins the usage-based-routing-v2
clock, and the deployment rpm test freezes time with time-machine because its old patch never reached the
clock bound as a default argument.

The bedrock realtime test stubs AWS signing like its sibling. The swagger test stubs FastAPI's schema
builder. The prisma span scan skips files that cannot hold a call site. The http, live session and custom
code bounds are tied to the timeout constants they guard.

The vertex test reads only LiteLLM log records, the agentops test reads only its own route's requests, the
redis test picks a port whose shared breaker is closed, and the SAML test freezes the clock and now asserts
the exact TTL.

* test(bedrock): stub the boto3 session instead of our own signing helper

Greptile flagged that the realtime guardrail fixture replaced run_aws_signing, which tests/unit/AGENTS.md
forbids. The CI timeout was resolve_credentials building a real boto3.Session on the signing pool, so the
fixture now swaps boto3.Session for a static-key session and the real signing path runs.

* test(s3): keep the short upload deadline for the timeout case only

The dropped-connection case also ran under the 0.3s per-attempt deadline. When the fake bucket's handler
thread answered one attempt late on a loaded runner, that attempt was retried as a timeout instead of a
dropped connection, so the test counted 5 PUTs instead of 6. Only the timeout case needs the short deadline.

Harden BLE ingress, padding, scan duty, panic wipe, and remove NostrPoW bypass (#1924)

* Harden BLE ingress, padding, scan duty, panic wipe, and remove NostrPoW bypass

Tier 0 security, privacy, and battery fixes:
- Return early on unverified announces in BLEAnnounceHandler so spoofed
  announces cannot trigger dedup marks, UI refreshes, or forced announce-backs.
- Validate 0x25 group message framing and freshness before admitting to gossip,
  relay, or UI; drop unknown MessageType values instead of relaying up to 128 KiB.
- Remove NostrPoW and the 8-bit rateLimitBypassBits sender-bucket bypass;
  sign geohash kind-20000 events synchronously without cooperative-pool spin loops.
- Zeroize NoiseSymmetricState chainingKey and hash in place via memset_s.
- Use a 256-byte bucket stride in MessagePadding so every 1..2048 B frame pads
  within single-byte PKCS#7 limits (0..255 B) with no unpadded gaps.
- Duty-cycle active idle BLE scanning for solo and 1-2 peer meshes and disable
  AllowDuplicates when central links are saturated.
- Make TorManager panic directory wipe synchronous, restore userTorEnabled=true
  on panic, clear remaining in-memory caches/clipboard, mark clipboard local-only
  with expiry, and cover all connected iOS scenes in PrivacyScreen.
- Require explicit confirmation before Cashu clearnet web redeem, gate
  bitchat:// deep links during panicWipeBlocked, dedup BoardStore tombstones by
  (postID, authorSigningKey), protect Favorites/GroupStore against locked-boot
  overwrites, synchronize SecureLogger DateFormatter, and preserve image
  orientation + AFU file protection in ImageUtils.
