annotation: fixes from a review pass

Determinism. A lasso bent round a neighbour when a product landed just
above a threshold, and the product could differ in its last bit between
arm64 and amd64. Snap such values before comparing them, and measure
lengths with a sqrt of unfused products in place of math.Hypot, which
differs across architectures too.

Paint. A pen is one color: the compiler now rejects a gradient, which
the SVG never defined and the rasteriser could not stroke. A raw render
target can no longer carry a paint server in an annotation's stroke or
font color.

Lasso. Group by the class or glob that gave the lasso, recorded when the
shape is compiled, and not by where it was written; an import or a
variable spread no longer joins shapes. The loop takes its note and pen
from the first member that sets one. A caption's link does not ring a
shape a lasso holds. The loop no longer crosses itself round a shape
that reaches right across it.

Notes. Set every note in the board's font, the one it was measured in,
so that a note beside a mono shape fits its box. Place what is being
erased and what is being drawn apart, so a note no longer reserves room
beside the one it replaces. Find Markdown and LaTeX where the renderers
center it. Stop at the first side with nothing in the way and skip marks
and routes that are nowhere near: a thousand annotated shapes render in
under a second, down from fourteen.

Animation. Pace marks to the frames a step has, so they finish when a
short grid transition does. Add no frames to erase a mark whose shape
the step removed. Erase nothing on a layer, which is a page of its own.

Language. An annotation that a glob gives a shape now holds on every
board, as one from a class does. A caption can link to a key with a
space in it through angle brackets. A list is not an annotation.

Also: one opacity per mark in SVG, as in the raster output, so strokes
that overlap do not double up; d2oracle.Set rewrites a note in place.

annotation: highlight, arrow and lasso

Three more marks.

highlight runs a highlighter over the label of a shape or a connection,
one pass per line of text. It is yellow unless style.stroke says
otherwise, and its strokes end square.

arrow stands the note off from its target, wherever there is room, and
joins the two with a hand-drawn arrow. It works on shapes and on
connections, and without a note.

lasso draws one loop round every shape that one declaration gives it to,
which is what a class or a filtered glob does. The exporter groups those
shapes: the first carries the annotation and names the rest in a new
Members field. The loop is the convex hull of the members with its
corners rounded, bent inward round another shape that pokes into it from
the side. A shape that sits right among the members stays inside.

A highlighter is too pale to write with, so a highlight's note is in the
default pen. style.font-color, new here, colors any note or caption
apart from its mark.

one of its strokes it turns just far enough for that stroke to cross the
route instead of lying along it. Which way it turns is decided on the
tenth-of-a-pixel grid, so every architecture decides it the same way.

and the simplifier decides on whole numbers, with each product rounded
before the subtraction so it cannot be fused. A value exactly halfway
between two tenths is nudged the same way everywhere. The pen position of
a partly drawn mark is snapped to the same grid, and the fraction drawn
is kept to four places, because it feeds the diagram hash and through it
every ID in an animated SVG.

Compiling with -gcflags=all=-d=fmahash=n turns fused multiply-add off on
arm64 and reproduces the CI failure before this change. After it, the
goldens and all four example renders are byte-identical in both modes.

annotation: draw and erase marks between steps

With `animate-duration`, a step's marks are drawn by hand and the
previous step's are erased from where they began. New marks follow one
another, each starting when the one before it is half done. Marks that a
caption links to go first, in the order the caption names them. An
annotation declared again unchanged keeps its ink.

Annotations are planned in a pass of their own. The existing planners
compare consecutive boards shape by shape to decide what moved, and an
annotation that changes every step would make each annotated shape look
changed. So annotations are lifted off the board tree before
sampleBoardTransitions runs and put back afterwards, sampled onto
whatever frames it produced. A step with no other transition gets frames
for its marks alone.

An animation also pins every caption to one lower third, since all boards
share a viewport, and holds each board for as long as its caption and
notes take to read. `animate-interval` stays the floor.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Fable 5.2 <noreply@anthropic.com>

annotation: marks, notes and captions drawn over a diagram

`annotation` draws a pen mark and a Markdown note over a shape or a
connection without taking part in layout:

    db.r2.annotation: 4 s behind
    db.r2.annotation.shape: box
    (api -> cache)[0].annotation: 2 ms

The marks are circle, box, underline, brace and cross for shapes, and
trace and cross for connections. With no shape named, a container gets a
brace, bare text an underline, any other shape a ring, and a connection a
trace. The note is placed on whichever side of the mark covers the least,
or where `near` says. `style.stroke` sets the pen.

On a board's root, `annotation` is the caption, drawn under the diagram.
A Markdown link to a shape, `[the replica](db.r2)`, becomes emphasis and
marks that shape.

An annotation belongs to the board that declares it. Steps and scenarios
start from another board without its annotations, so each step can point
at something new. Classes keep theirs.

Both renderers draw the same geometry from d2target, so SVG, PNG, PDF and
PPTX agree, and the viewport grows to hold marks, notes and the caption.

`annotation` is now reserved. A shape with that name must be quoted, and
the compiler says so when it meets one.

changelog: globs over boards

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

d2ir: apply globs over boards to every board they select, once

A glob over layers, scenarios or steps applied only to the first board
it reached: scenarios: {w: {b}; v: {c}; *: {a}} added a to w only, and
so did layers and steps, scenarios.*.a, ** inside a board, edge
selectors such as scenarios.*.(x -> y)[0] and *: @f. Glob contexts
record what they applied to by BoardIDA, which is empty for a board
itself and repeats inside different boards, so every board after the
first looked done. Keys are now per board (appliedKey): BoardIDA for
nodes in the glob's own board, as before, and the absolute path for a
board and for anything inside another board, shared by the glob's
copies so that inheritance never applies a glob twice.

Making every board reachable exposed and fixes these:
- A glob written in a board group's map (layers, scenarios or steps)
  selects the boards and no longer also acts inside each board as if
  written there: scenarios: {*: {a}; w: {b}} no longer gives w.b an a,
  and scenarios: {*.style.fill: red} fills each scenario's background,
  not its objects (** does that). A connection glob there whose
  endpoints are one element other than ** (* -> hub,
  (* -> *)[*].style.stroke) cannot connect boards, so it still applies
  inside each board, including boards declared before it and their
  scenarios and steps, once; scenarios: {* -> hub} used to be an error.
- Edge globs skip endpoint pairs in different boards, as ** already
  did: scenarios.*.x -> scenarios.*.y connects within each board, and a
  glob whose pairs all cross boards (scenarios.*.a -> x) creates nothing
  instead of failing with "cannot create edges between boards".
- A scenario or step that a glob reaches before it has a map starts as
  a copy of its base board, as it does when its own map comes first;
  a step without a map copies the step before it once the glob has
  finished that step. A failing filter no longer stops that copy.
- Each step's copy of a glob records its own applications, starting
  from the previous step's, so a step no longer stops its board's globs
  from reaching a later object of the same name.
- A glob no longer applies again to what its own import added
  (**: @f; a gives a one p, not p.p, and no false cyclic import), the
  importer's own fields get the import (x; *: @f; p), and *** no longer
  applies a second time to objects a scenario or step inherits. Two
  triple-glob golden files lose the duplicate references this made.

Programs without boards compile to the same IR (6,100 random programs
and the repository's .d2 files). On generated board programs: 0 of
18,000 repeat an edge that only a double application could create (622
before), and an oracle that checks every board a glob selects finds 0
misses (12,566 before). Because globs now reach every board, a diagram
with many glob connections can reach the expansion limits sooner.
TestBoardGlobs has 118 subtests.

commits.message:
Honor declared filesystem permissions in Windows sandboxes (#64416)

## Why

MXC volume expansion can generate child grants that override restrictions on
directory aliases. The restricted-token backend can also reject valid workspace
policies because its compatibility check assumes the working directory is
writable.

## What changed

- Check directory identity before MXC expands writable volume roots. Suppress
  generated write grants that conflict with read-only aliases, including through
  junctions on other volumes, while preserving narrower explicit grants.
  Reject launch if a writable volume is also denied or its relationship to a
  restricted directory cannot be determined.
- Let the restricted-token backend accept the supplied workspace roots when
  the working directory has no explicit write grant, while retaining exact
  root matching for filesystem-root write grants.

## Testing

Add regression coverage for restricted volume aliases, junctions across
writable roots, explicit drive-root denials, and restricted-token workspace
roots with nested or read-only working directories or an empty root list.

GitOrigin-RevId: 0cd880b52185d0a38c479df17ae48aa68d45eeb1

Preserve Linux sandbox restrictions across writable symlink aliases (#64415)

## Why

Ordering writable binds by the spelled paths can put a parent mount
after a child mount when symlinks are involved. The later bind can cover
deny masks and read-only mounts that the sandbox already applied.

## What changed

Group writable roots by their resolved mount destinations and bind each
destination once, with parents before descendants. Map deny rules under
writable aliases to their physical paths and apply them after read-only
mounts. Reapply read-only mounts below each writable bind while
preserving explicit write grants for narrower paths.

## Testing

Add `bwrap` regression cases for a symlink to `/` paired with a project
alias and for aliases to nested project directories. The cases check
that denied files stay unreadable, read-only files resist writes, and
explicitly writable children remain usable under restricted parents.

GitOrigin-RevId: e8c677cbccae1d7b62cb566609074f8c8c14ddeb

Fit the Agent Command Center grouping header to the panel (#64411)

## Why

The full header can clip the current grouping and its shortcut in
narrow panels.

## What changed

Use shorter header labels as space runs out and show just the grouping
in the narrowest layout. Account for the longest grouping name and the
configured shortcut when choosing a layout so the title stays stable
as users cycle groupings or move focus. Show the shortcut when it is
available and fits.

## Testing

Add snapshot coverage for Directory grouping with a custom `f11 g`
shortcut at 24, 36, and 60 columns.

GitOrigin-RevId: 9d4efe8d483d9431ff75c163a1a0ce96b7886894

Fix TUI Markdown line breaks before inline code (#64400)

## Why

When a paragraph starts with inline code after a heading in a list
item, the renderer can append the code to the heading's line.

## What changed

Honor pending line breaks before rendering inline code using the same
line-start logic as links. Table cells keep their inline layout.

## Testing

Extend the rendering and transcript copy snapshots to cover a list
item with a heading followed by inline code. The copy cases cover
both the full item and a selection within the code span.

GitOrigin-RevId: bcc480cb9aa2cbf7ab0738f1ec3667677445987a

Seal synthetic mounts in read-restricted Linux sandboxes (#64398)

## Why

Read-restricted sandboxes build a synthetic filesystem around paths
granted by policy. Leaving the backing mounts writable lets commands
modify synthetic directories outside explicitly writable paths.

## What changed

Remount the synthetic root, minimal `/dev`, and applicable WSL masks
read-only after bubblewrap finishes setting up mounts. The remounts
are nonrecursive, so explicitly writable child mounts stay writable.

## Testing

Extend the sandbox regression test to check that commands can read an
approved file through a symlink, write to `/dev/null`, and write to an
allowed subdirectory under a denied parent. The test also checks that
commands cannot rename the synthetic directory containing the approved
file or create an ungranted directory under `/dev`.

GitOrigin-RevId: e2ddc6c4a215d052adf12e2644480a2eb9c72640

Show confirmed thread permissions in TUI status (#64396)

## Why

The TUI used its local configuration to report permissions and approvals.
Pending profile selections could make those values differ from the
settings confirmed for the displayed thread. Legacy sandbox policies
can also hide restrictions of named profiles.

## What changed

- Use the displayed thread's confirmed permissions and approval settings
  in `/status`, the built-in status line, and status line provider data.
  Show unknown values in the UI when the thread has no confirmed settings.
- For named custom profiles, show the profile name and approval mode in
  `/status`, including workspace roots where applicable.
- Omit ambiguous enforcement from provider data unless the embedded app
  server can resolve it. Report confirmed approval settings independently.

## Testing

Add regression coverage for switching threads, retaining confirmed
settings after a rejected profile selection, and resolving enforcement
for a full-disk profile with networking disabled.

GitOrigin-RevId: f7b6c005d640ae9ede4bd132090b835ca6b7ea1f

Track server-confirmed thread permissions in the TUI (#64393)

## Why

Embedded sessions can use a local execution profile that differs from
the sandbox policy reported by the app server. The TUI needs a
server-confirmed snapshot for permission displays.

## What changed

Capture the server-reported sandbox profile, active profile, approval
settings, working directory, and workspace roots when a thread starts,
resumes, forks, or receives a live settings update. Restore the snapshot
from cached sessions and preserve it during transcript replay. Leave the
snapshot unset when session settings are inferred.

## Testing

Extend tests to cover differing server and local profiles, workspace
roots from live settings updates, and snapshot preservation during
transcript replay.

GitOrigin-RevId: 525fdfa1b526f5d799bca01c955ac7cfc3e60774

Remove dim styling from hook details in the TUI (#64391)

Use the default text style for single-line and wrapped values in the
hooks browser detail pane.

## Testing

Extend the wrapped hook command test to check that every detail span
uses the default style while still checking the full hyperlink destination.

GitOrigin-RevId: 77041a3bd95ad1f9fa71aa38857208c59ba44f9b

Bind Linux sandbox paths before shell snapshot replay (#64388)

## Why

Linux filesystem rules that depend on `TMPDIR` or `HOME` need to keep
the same meaning when shell snapshot replay changes the command environment.

## What changed

Resolve `:tmpdir` entries and home-relative read-deny globs against the
prepared launch environment. Omit `:tmpdir` entries when `TMPDIR` is
unset or empty. Resolve relative temporary directories from the physical
command working directory and verify that directory before and after
bubblewrap sets up its mounts.

Preserve process confinement when resolving paths makes the filesystem
rules appear to grant full-disk access. Reject bindings that would change
the grants enforced by legacy Landlock.

## Testing

Add regression coverage for shell snapshot replay, working-directory
changes, and preservation of Linux process confinement.

GitOrigin-RevId: 07d4698ca7b30b0259193513145233ae1bdc7f19

Report pending startup dialogs through terminal program status (#64384)

## Why

Terminal hosts need to know when Codex is waiting for a startup decision, including while a chat status record is active.

## What changed

Emit a separate `OSC 7501` blocked record while waiting for directory trust, startup hook review, or an update decision. Report trust and hook review as permission prompts and the update prompt as a question.

Clear the dialog record when the prompt closes or Codex suspends. Report it again if Codex resumes waiting for input. Dialog records can coexist with the chat status record.

## Testing

Extend the connected directory trust PTY test to check blocked and clear records for consent and hook review. Exercise Ctrl-Z in a PTY without a controlling terminal and verify that the pending trust record stays active until the prompt is answered.

GitOrigin-RevId: 9801e03b28a19b75f62a09e3e927de0dd59c5448

Clean up unused TUI image paste files on exit (#64382)

## Why

Pasting an image or an image file path could leave a temporary copy on disk
even if the image never reached the app server. Drafts still need those
copies during the session, and saved turns can reference them after exit.

## What changed

Track pasted-image copies for the lifetime of the TUI session, including
across backend switches and reconnects. Delete the remaining tracked copies
on exit. Preserve copies when a turn is admitted or when a lost response
leaves admission uncertain.

Check model support before writing a clipboard image for an ordinary
composer paste. In WSL, read PNG bytes from PowerShell's standard output
so the fallback uses the same cleanup path.

## Testing

Extend paste tests to verify that a copied image survives changes to the
source file and a change of event sender, and that cleanup removes the
copy while preserving the source. Verify that queueing a submission still
leaves the copy eligible for cleanup.

GitOrigin-RevId: 36d51af242901306be0ff319949d26a01ca71200

Respect sandbox read restrictions in remote plugin approvals (#64369)

## Why

Remote command approvals could attribute a command to a plugin by reading
a script that the turn's filesystem permissions denied access to.

## What changed

Use the remote environment's sandbox policy and stored permission grants
when resolving script paths, checking file metadata, and reading scripts
for approval attribution. If the lookup is denied, the approval prompt
still appears without plugin attribution.

## Testing

Add a regression test that checks for an approval prompt without a plugin
ID or script path when either the environment policy or a stored turn
grant denies reads of an otherwise matching plugin script.

GitOrigin-RevId: 123fd72c14cd31121d271fa800f005d3fc41a366

Interrupt running commands promptly when approval is canceled (#64368)

## Why

Recording a declined command can block on history writes. If turn
cancellation waits for that write, sibling commands can keep running.
The same write can also delay recording results from commands that
already finished.

## What changed

Signal cancellation before recording the declined command and publish
the decline before `TurnAborted`. Start the task's shutdown grace period
after publication so it has time to record completed tool results.

## Testing

Add a regression test that blocks publication of the decline, verifies
that a running sibling stops while publication is blocked, and checks
that another sibling's completed output reaches the next model request.

GitOrigin-RevId: c0b2e40e711ffe5ee46b76b110410518d2191041

Finish approved remote one-shot commands after startup interruption (#64367)

## Why

Interrupting an approved one-shot command while remote plugin attribution
is pending can stall session shutdown and leave the command without a
terminal record. An open elicitation can also delay output collection.

## What changed

On interruption, skip the pending remote attribution lookup and optional
plugin metrics read, and bypass the elicitation pause during output
collection. Keep session history open until the command's terminal event
is published, including when the exit watcher publishes it.

## Testing

Extend the remote startup interruption test to cover resumable commands
and approved one-shots. Verify process termination and session shutdown
with the attribution request still pending, and check that the approved
one-shot records exactly one failed completion with an unrelated
elicitation still open.

GitOrigin-RevId: e9b78290544d634797876119006540150a7672b1

Share tool approval logic across initial attempts and retries (#64355)

## What changed

Build `ApprovalContext` and submit approval requests through shared
code. Retry requests add the retry reason and any network approval
context, while the initial request retains its approval source for
later execution decisions.

GitOrigin-RevId: a8210c7b32fcc1414141198bdacfe55fff39b9b6

Preserve command approval items through turn interruption (#64349)

## Why

The app server could show a command awaiting approval before core had
recorded its start. Interrupting the turn or abandoning launch after
approval could leave the live command item and saved history out of sync.

## What changed

Have core publish the command item before prompting for approval and
retain it across approval and sandbox retries until execution takes over.
Complete abandoned items as declined when interrupted while awaiting
approval, or as failed when interrupted after approval but before launch.
Wait for pending approval item writes during shutdown.

## Testing

Extend the app-server interrupt test to restart the server and verify
that the interrupted turn contains exactly one declined command item with
the original approval item ID.

GitOrigin-RevId: c9f027fc7096d091dc8cf1936c88aa69d3eed8c1

Drain unified exec launch failure events before session shutdown (#64346)

## Why

A launch failure can still be publishing its command events after the turn
is interrupted. If the session shuts down during publication, the failed
command can be lost from persisted thread history.

## What changed

Track in-flight launch failure publications and wait for them to finish
before running session-end hooks and emitting the thread-stop event.
Once shutdown closes the tracker, skip new launch failure publications.

## Testing

Add a regression test that pauses publication for a command with a missing
working directory, interrupts the turn, and requests shutdown. It checks
that shutdown waits and that persisted history records the command as failed
in the interrupted turn.

GitOrigin-RevId: 1fb33d1fd3c11939c0013f5feb4edb737702b0ad

Gate hosted Guardian test helpers to non-Windows builds (#64345)

The hosted Guardian scenarios are already excluded on Windows, leaving
their reload and stall helpers unused in Windows test builds.

Apply the same platform gate to the `Reloaded` and `Stalled` read modes
and the stall notification. Make the root snapshot mutable only in
the reload branch.

GitOrigin-RevId: 1f517e56ba6ce436b96c6e44c4dc4731b94e1e97

Persist command completions when approval is declined or fails (#64341)

## Why

The app server completed command items for rejected approval responses
directly in the live stream. That bypassed core's history recording, so
clients could see a completed command live and lose it when reloading
the turn.

## What changed

Keep top-level command items with their pending approvals in core.
Record and emit the command completion before unblocking the turn.
Declines and cancellations produce a `declined` item, while invalid
responses and approval request failures produce a `failed` item.

## Testing

App-server integration tests cover cancellation, decline, and malformed
responses. They check that `item/completed` precedes `turn/completed`
and that paginated history returns the same command item after restart.

GitOrigin-RevId: d3d95272c8a6af2fa65fa980f312260313cc5e32

Compute the Responses WebSocket privacy flag before building the request (#64324)

GitOrigin-RevId: bced2fd4db353e13da74ae50707d4d8e3e640259

Fix lifecycle hook dispatch for hosted subagents (#64310)

## Why

Hosted workers keep the host's session source, so hook dispatch
can mistake them for root sessions and run `SessionStart` and
`Stop` on worker turns.

## What changed

Recognize host-managed workers by their inherited session ID and
dispatch `SubagentStart` and `SubagentStop` for them. Resolve the
parent transcript for `SubagentStop` using the immediate parent
thread ID when available.

## Testing

Add a regression test that verifies a hosted worker runs only the
subagent lifecycle hooks, receives start-hook context, and reports
its own transcript and final message in the stop hook.

GitOrigin-RevId: 272d29d275120a1b020b1a00a0db2e00402ebe06

Resolve Command Center worktree groups in the background (#64259)

## Why

Git lookups for saved session directories can stall the Command Center
when a filesystem mount is slow or unresponsive.

## What changed

Group sessions by their saved working directories immediately. When
worktree support is enabled, resolve local paths with up to four
background workers and refresh the view as grouping changes arrive.
Reopening the Command Center retries completed lookups without
duplicating pending work.

## Testing

Extend the worktree grouping test to check that the initial view shows
directory groups, related worktrees regroup under their project, and
the selected session stays selected.

GitOrigin-RevId: c1411749c9db31dec5827c78cb89fe94255f0c7e

Open `/diff` in a TUI sidebar tab (#64258)

## Why

The full-screen diff pager takes the conversation off screen. A sidebar tab lets users review working-tree changes alongside the conversation.

## What changed

- Open a read-only `Diff` tab when the sidebar is available, and fall back to the full-screen pager otherwise.
- Reuse the tab on repeated runs. Keep the previous patch visible while Git runs, preserve the reading position on refresh, and apply only the latest result without stealing focus.
- Render large patches in chunks and derive scroll indicators from visible rows so redraws can skip layout of the off-screen tail.

## Testing

Cover tab reuse, stale result handling, and the visibility of the last hunk across resize and refresh. Verify that scroll indicators render without laying out the off-screen tail.

feat(pbl): support course-defined role narration voices (#2436)

## Summary

Course authors can assign a narration voice to each PBL role in
`project.json`. The workbench uses the speaking role’s voice for its
live replies, including queued speech. This extends the workbench
narration introduced in #2382.

Each binding names a provider and voice, with an optional model. It
applies when compatible with the active speech service. A missing or
incompatible binding uses the platform narrator. Existing studies read
their pinned project version. If Doubao refuses a role’s speaker,
playback retries the same line with an available narrator and uses it
for queued lines bound to that speaker. Other roles keep their own
voice.

## Verification

- Imported a project with separate role voices into PostgreSQL, replaced
the classroom’s project revision, and reopened the study. It kept the
original voices. An older package without bindings kept the platform
narrator.
- Queued speech from all four roles, including two sharing a voice. Each
segment requested the expected voice once. Checked provider and model
mismatches, a restricted voice catalogue, and browser speech.
- Replayed a speaker refusal through the synthesis route and player. The
current line played once, a queued role sharing the refused voice used
the narrator, and the next role retained its own voice. Covered paused
playback, changed speech accounts, an unavailable fallback, and ordinary
service errors.
- Local regression runs passed for PBL, audio, model settings, and the
PostgreSQL teaching runtime. TypeScript, formatting and lint checks
passed for the changes.

AI-assisted implementation and review.

commits.message:
docs(sql): document text and JSON descriptions

Apply the reviewed DESCRIBE TEXT and JSON contract.

fix: explain Function catalog SDK compatibility errors (#5250)

An older Function catalog can reject the query generated by
`get_function` at `FORMAT`, or by `list_functions` at `LIMIT`. When the
operation receives its exact trailing-input diagnostic at submission,
append guidance on matching the Python SDK to the Enterprise build. Keep
the original SQL error, request ID, gRPC status and any build metadata
supplied by the server.

Compared 24 loopback Flight responses through the public synchronous and
asynchronous Python APIs against the published b38 wheel. Eight lookups
and listings gained the pairing guidance. The other 16 responses
preserved their error types and diagnostics, including authorization,
missing resources and unrelated parser failures. The candidate passed
122 Python tests and four Rust tests. Current catalog reads and opaque
continuation tokens also worked after build discovery returned 404.

fix(python): preserve omitted Function GPU counts (#5249)

`@function(gpu=True)` currently serializes `gpus_per_worker: 1` even
when the caller omits `gpu_count`. This prevents registration on servers
that support single-GPU Functions but reject an explicit GPU count
field.

Preserve omission through registration and runtime digest calculation.
The effective default is still one GPU per worker. With an explicit
`gpu_count=1` or `gpu_count=2`, the request and digest include the
declared count. As a result, the omitted and explicit-one forms now have
distinct runtime digests even though both request one GPU in practice.

The regression test captures the Flight SQL `CREATE FUNCTION` request
for CPU, omitted GPU count, and explicit counts of one and two. Only the
omitted-count case failed on the base revision. All 34 focused Python
tests and Ruff checks passed on the candidate Python source with a
compatible native extension. Local replay of the captured requests
against the registration admission code confirmed that the older
implementation accepts the omitted count and that the current
implementation resolves the four effective counts to 0, 1, 1 and 2.

perf: raise the default Blob V2 direct-read threshold to 32 MiB (#5248)

Enterprise SDKs use an inclusive 32 MiB default for eligible Blob V2
direct reads. The paired field comparison with the 10 MiB SDK default
measured higher direct-read latency at 10 and 16 MiB. At 32 MiB, the
interval for the latency difference spanned zero. [SDK version used in
the field comparison](https://github.com/lancedb/lancedb/pull/5247)

The earlier mixed-load test measured lower Plan Executor cache pressure
with direct reads enabled at the 10 MiB cutoff. That result covers the
tested size mix. With the 32 MiB cutoff, reads from 10 MiB up to (but
excluding) 32 MiB go through the proxy, so the impact on executor
traffic and cache pressure depends on the workload's size distribution.

The existing internal override still takes precedence. Direct reads keep
the 16 MiB part size. The Node binding test verifies proxy routing one
byte below the default and two contiguous object-store ranges with a
matching SHA-256 at exactly 32 MiB.

perf: improve presigned Blob V2 reads (#5247)

## Behavior

Presigned Blob V2 reads retry an idempotent ranged GET once after a
recognized disconnect or timeout before the complete response headers
arrive. This includes an abrupt TLS EOF while receiving the headers. A
retry preserves the physical Range and the still-valid URL. Expiry
triggers resolution on the pinned snapshot. Once the complete headers
arrive, the existing status and body paths handle the response.
Enterprise connections default to a 300-second pool idle timeout and
presigned object-store connections default to 30 seconds. The existing
override applies to both pools.

Loopback TCP tests exercise FIN and RST on a reused connection, both
with zero response bytes and after a partial header. They verify the
send count with retries enabled and disabled, the exact replayed Range
and the payload digest. A truncated body after complete headers returns
an error after one send.

Direct reads over 16 MiB stream bounded physical ranges into their
corresponding slices of the final buffer. The per-read fan-out uses
Lance's `LANCE_IO_THREADS`, capped by the connection's existing
`LANCE_CLIENT_BLOB_REQUEST_CONCURRENCY` limit (8 by default). Each
request retains its permit through body consumption. The 10 MiB routing
threshold continues to apply to the full logical read.

The connection can reuse unexpired presigned locations for verified rows
under the same table, column, snapshot and request credentials. Range
offsets and sizes come from the resolver. The existing batch request
covers the requested rows of a shared Packed or Managed sidecar.
Reopening a verified row uses its prior resolution, and the first open
of each unseen SQL descriptor still authorizes just that row. The public
API and REST response format are unchanged.
chore: update lance dependency to v16.0.0-beta.5

feat(node): accept Expr values in select() (#4878)

Closes #3042.

Node `select()` now takes `Expr` values, the same expression builder
that `where()` already accepts. A `Map` or a plain object can mix `Expr`
values and SQL strings:

```ts
import { col } from "@lancedb/lancedb";

const rows = await table
  .query()
  .select({
    id: "id",
    name: col("firstName"),
    total: col("unitPrice").mul(col("quantity")),
  })
  .toArray();
```

This works on every query with `select()`: `query()`, `vectorSearch()`,
`search()` and the take queries. The parameter type is now `Map<string,
string | Expr>` and `Record<string, string | Expr>`. Nothing else in the
TypeScript API changes.

### How it works

`select()` turns each `Expr` into SQL with `toSql()` and passes the
pairs to the native `select` that SQL strings already use. `where()`
handles an `Expr` the same way, so Node treats expressions alike in both
places. `toSql()` quotes camelCase names and SQL keywords with
backticks, so `col("firstName")` reads `firstName`.

I also looked at passing the expressions to Rust as `Select::Expr`, as
Python's `select_expr` does. I didn't go that way:

- Before a local or remote query runs, Rust turns `Select::Expr` back
into SQL with the same `expr_to_sql_string`. The query is the same
either way.
- A map that mixes SQL strings and expressions can't become a
`Select::Expr` without parsing the strings. Python's `AsyncQuery.select`
sends a mixed dict through `select_expr` and wraps each string with
`lit()` (`_coerce`), so `select({"id": "id", "doubled": col("score") *
lit(2)})` returns the string `'id'` in the `id` column. Sending SQL
keeps every string a SQL expression.
- I found one path that accepts `Select::Expr` and rejects
`Select::Dynamic`: namespace `QueryTable` pushdown. Node can't turn
pushdown on today, so nothing changes yet. If Node gets that option,
`select()` can send `Select::Expr` when every value is an `Expr`.

`blobMode: "bytes"` (#4353) finds blob columns by name in the `[output,
source]` list of the selection. For a camelCase column, `toSql()` gives
`` `imageData` ``, which doesn't match `imageData`. So when an `Expr` is
a bare column reference, the match uses its plain name. For this, the
native `Expr` gets a small `columnName()` helper, like `column_name()`
in the Python bindings, which Python uses for the same match. A blob
renamed with `col()` gets its bytes, as with a SQL string. Other
expressions are not filled with bytes, as before.

A value that is neither a string nor an `Expr` now throws a `TypeError`
that names the key, instead of the native conversion error.

### Tests

New tests in `expr.test.ts`:

- a `Map` that mixes SQL strings with `col("firstName")` and
`col("unitPrice").mul(2)` on a plain query, with the column order
- a `Record` with `upper()`, `func("lower", ...)` and a SQL string,
filtered with an `Expr` in `where()`
- `Expr` values on a vector query, an automatic `search()` (full-text
search) and a take query
- `blobMode: "bytes"` with a camelCase blob column selected with
`col()`: renamed, next to a computed `Expr` column, and in a take query
- a number as a value throws a `TypeError`

The whole Node suite passes. The Node docs under `docs/src/js` are
regenerated. The `@example` in the middle of the `select()` docstring
used to swallow the two paragraphs after it into the code block, so I
moved the example to the end, which is why each query class page
changes.

Left out: `Expr` items in the plain column list (`select([col("a")])`),
because an expression needs an output name. The `select` of a
materialized view still takes SQL strings only.

fix(python): give tied FTS scores full weight in hybrid normalization (#4858)

## Why

Hybrid search normalizes FTS scores with min-max. When all FTS scores
are equal (one match, or a tie), the range is 0 and every score became
0. `LinearCombinationReranker` treats 0 as a missing FTS match. So a
lone keyword match could rank below documents without the keyword. Fixes
#4857.

## What changed

- `_normalize_scores` takes a `tie_value` for the zero-range case. The
default stays 0, so vector distances are unchanged.
- The FTS leg passes `tie_value=1.0`, so tied FTS matches count as the
best FTS result.

## Scope

- Covers the zero-range case for both `normalize="score"` and
`normalize="rank"`.
- Leaves out how `_rank` breaks ties among equal scores. That is a
separate question.

## Blast Radius

The change only affects hybrid queries where every FTS hit has the same
score. RRF and MRR use list position, so their results don't change.
LinearCombination and custom score-based rerankers now give those hits
full FTS weight.

## Verification

- A new test in `test_hybrid_query.py` fails on main in both normalize
modes and passes with the fix.
- `pytest python/tests -m "not slow and not s3_test"`: 3272 passed, 167
skipped.
- `ruff format --check` and `ruff check` (0.9.9, the version pinned by
pre-commit) pass.

[ci] fix: remove retired in-cluster pypi mirror from Ascend workflows (#8804)

### What does this PR do?

The self-hosted Ascend CI runners no longer use the in-cluster nginx
pypi/apt mirror (`cache-service.nginx-pypi-cache.svc.cluster.local`).
Public indexes are now reached through the cluster-level squid caching
proxy, so the hard-coded internal-mirror env vars are dead
configuration. This PR removes them, letting pip/uv fall back to the
public indexes already configured in these workflows (e.g.
`mirrors.huaweicloud.com`, `pypi.org`).

This is not a duplicate: `gh pr list -R verl-project/verl --state open
--search "nginx-pypi-cache in:title,body"` (and `cluster.local`, `pypi
mirror ascend`) returned no matching open PR.

### Files touched (15) and lines removed (78)

Removed only env vars whose value was a cache-service URL:
- `PIP_INDEX_URL`, `PIP_TRUSTED_HOST` (27 each)
- `UV_INDEX_URL`, `UV_INSECURE_HOST` (12 each)

Files:
- `.github/workflows/sgl_ascend.yml`
- `.github/workflows/e2e_ascend.yml`
- `.github/workflows/model_ascend.yml`
- `.github/workflows/reward_model_sglang_ascend.yml`
- `.github/workflows/reward_model_vllm_ascend.yml`

- `.github/workflows/e2e_ppo_trainer_megatron_sglang_2_ascend.yml`

No apt/yum sed rewrites or `pip config set` lines referencing
cache-service exist in this repo. Public indexes and unrelated settings
(e.g. `UV_EXTRA_INDEX_URL`, `UV_INDEX_STRATEGY`) are left intact. No
consumers of the removed vars exist in these workflows, so no fallbacks
were required.

### Test / validation

- `grep -rIn "cache-service\|nginx-pypi-cache" --exclude-dir=.git .` →
no matches.
- All changed workflow YAML files parse successfully with
`yaml.safe_load` (PyYAML).
- No shell scripts changed, so `bash -n` is not applicable.

### Checklist Before Submitting

- [x] Read the Contribute Guide.
- [x] Searched for similar PRs (no duplicates).
- [x] No user-facing docs require updates (CI-only env cleanup).
- [x] No new tests needed; this is CI configuration cleanup and CI
itself exercises these workflows.

AI assistance was used to prepare this change; the submitter has
reviewed every changed line.

Signed-off-by: chenqi49 <479148871@qq.com>

[ci] test: enable R3 in Ascend Qwen E2E cases (#8779)

Enable R3 by default in the two existing Ascend Qwen E2E launchers. Both
now set actor_rollout_ref.actor.megatron.router_replay.mode=R3 and
actor_rollout_ref.rollout.enable_rollout_routing_replay=True. Select
VLLM_USE_V2_MODEL_RUNNER=1 in the launcher and explicitly forward its
string value through Ray runtime_env, addressing the routed-expert
capture startup failure in this CI stack. Remove the obsolete
VLLM_USE_V1 setting from the 35B launcher and preserve quoted caller
arguments in the 30B launcher.

The final diff changes only the two launch scripts. Temporary
baseline/R3 comparison loops and artifact-upload additions have been
removed from this PR. Existing workflow model sizes and step counts stay
in effect: 30B uses the existing reduced random two-layer CI fixture;
35B uses the full pretrained model. This enables execution coverage, not
a guarantee of learning or route-value correctness.

Validation:

latest rerun, the LLM E2E; the VLM job was cancelled.
- The isolated reduced 30B comparison in #8799 passed. It reported zero
rewards and gradients, so it does not validate meaningful task learning
or full-model training.

result; full 30B validation is not claimed.

passed.
- Mocked execution of both actual launchers with Hydra parsing passed:
no caller overrides defaults to R3/capture=True, the launcher and Ray
both select V2, and explicit disabled/R3 overrides still work.
- Real NPU execution and Linux CI must rerun on the final revision.
Local mocked checks do not execute training.

Related work: this is the streamlined final form of this existing PR,
rather than another duplicate PR. #8799 is a separate isolation
experiment and #6585 proposes nightly coverage.

zcode: the mover's min is 0.1.74, which asks ZCode's Start Plan as the installed ZCode, 4.0.0 at the least (plugins#1635, #1639)

Since ZCode 4.0.0 shipped, zcode.z.ai answers a Start Plan request asked
as 3.17.2 with a bare 200 {"code":0,"msg":"","logid":...} and no
stream. The plugin threw "did not stream" and magpie answered 502
(cdredfox on plugins#1635, shenchuhannb on #1639).

plugins 46ba1e4e (zcode 0.1.74, Linmord's plugins#1641 with a review
fix-up) asks as the ZCode installed here, read from every platform
folder of .zcode/v2/runtime/provider, and never as a version older than
4.0.0. A machine with no ZCode, or an old one, asks as 4.0.0. That empty
answer is now a 400 that names the version, not a 502. Only the version
changes: ZCode 4.0.0's own engine (Resources/glm/zcode.cjs) builds Start
Plan headers as 3.17.2's does and signs no Start Plan request. Raising
the min updates moved users (keepMovedCurrent).

npm: npm view @magpie-community/opencode-zcode-auth version
--prefer-online is 0.1.74 (served about 19 minutes after the publish step). The plugins publish run (46093372220) is red
only for middleware-system-prompt and middleware-think-tags (E404,
trusted publisher), as before; its log has
"+ @magpie-community/opencode-zcode-auth@0.1.74".

Run at this change on origin/main 36c4ee039, on mica (Go 1.26.8), then
rebased onto 96ee42fb4, which changes no internal/provider file:
- go test ./internal/provider -count=1 -timeout 45m: ok (146s).
- GOOS=linux and GOOS=windows go vet ./internal/provider: ok. gofmt -l:
  clean.
- Plugin side, at plugins b966fef5 on mica with HOME=$(mktemp -d):
  packages/zcode 298 pass; root bun test 9609 pass, 0 fail; the new
  version and start tests are red at the PR's first head and at main.
Not run: a full go test ./... (this change is one string in the mover).
Not tried: a Start Plan request on a real account (no real-account
probes). Linmord and shenchuhannb saw 4.0.0 stream on their own

update: the app magpie runs from is kept until nothing runs from it, so the restart comes back on macOS 13 (#4983)

Cause (#4983, #2362): Install moved the running app to
.magpie-update/old, swapped the new one in, and removed
.magpie-update, deleting the program the running magpie is.
InstallAsAdmin rm -rf'd it too (and moved it to the cache, on
another volume: a copy and a delete). On macOS 13, syspolicyd ends
every program a process whose program file is gone starts, before
its first instruction ("Unable (errno: 2) to read file", "Security
policy would not allow process"), while fork/exec report success. So
the handover's `open -n` died unseen and the hello wait ran its 60s
out ("context deadline exceeded" in the reporter's log), the fallback
Relaunch's shell died before writing a line to relaunch.log (which
the reporter never had), Start said nil, and magpie quit with nothing
to bring it back. danbo610 found the early delete and reproduced it on
macOS 13.7.5 Intel (9b3bea5d, #2362); tlerbao's report is the same.
macOS 26 and 27 don't do this, which is why we never saw it.

Change:
- Install and InstallAsAdmin move the old app to
  <app dir>/.magpie-old/<pid>-<random>: on the app's volume (a rename,
  the running file stays the same file), outside stageDir (Stage's
  RemoveAll never reaches it), and not named .app (#3965). swapScript
  no longer rm -rf's it.
- RemoveRetired removes a kept copy only when lsof finds no process
  with a program in its Contents/MacOS open (lsof exit 1 and no
  output; a timeout or anything else keeps it). It runs at start and
  every 30 minutes (KeepRetiredClear). The admin install removes the
  unused copies in its own script, since they are root's.
- startShell (Relaunch's runAfterExit and OpenBeside): the shell
  writes a byte to fd 3 before anything else. EOF first, or nothing
  in 10s, is an error ("the shell that opens the new version didn't
  run"). restartInto then stays up, and so does a handover whose
  fallback can't start. Both now set Updates' "installed but couldn't
  be started" (notRestarted). Before, the handover's fallback failing
  logged only.
- docs/subsystems/gui-shell.md: the handover's step 4 and the kept app.

magpie web (the reporter's launchd job, and its 502s): StartWeb runs
its own updater, and followReplaced makes the app and the web follow
each other's installs, so whichever installed first deleted the image
the other runs from. On macOS 13 the web's later forks (agents,
plugin hosts) then die, and its toGateway proxy answers 502 while the
app's gateway is gone after its restart vanished. The kept copy covers
the web as well: lsof sees it running the old program, so the copy

gateway: Share on local network turned off elsewhere moves the serving gateway off [::] (rael_tao on X)

rael_tao on X: "how do I stop public listening on 3425? I changed the
config, restarted the gateway, and it listens on [::] again".

Cause: the magpie serving the gateway never followed a sharing or port
change made outside its own process. Only the GUI's own
/api/settings/lan called Relisten, and only when that GUI served the
gateway itself. With `magpie serve`, a daemon or another magpie serving,
Share off in the window or `magpie web`, or a hand edit of
settings.json, saved lan:false while the socket stayed on 0.0.0.0
(lsof: IPv6 *:P, Linux/Windows: [::]:P), until that process restarted.
Relisten also compared "[::]:P" with "0.0.0.0:P" as strings, so every
call closed and reopened a socket already where it should be.

  writes, and on OthersEvery as a fallback, and Relistens when
  listenAddr() differs from the socket; a failed move is logged once
  per target.

- Settings: with MAGPIE_ADDR on the network (Docker's image, a daemon
  installed with it), Share showed Off while the gateway listened
  everywhere. The row now shows On, disabled, and says what to change:
  MAGPIE_ADDR to 127.0.0.1:P or unset, or in a container
  -p 127.0.0.1:P:P. Strings in all five languages.

gateway: a client's tool search keeps the cached prefix where the upstream can load late tools (tourweint on X)

@tourweint on X, with pi's tool search (Responses tool_search with
execution "client"): only a Codex account kept the prompt-cache prefix;
DeepSeek's own API and OpenCode lost it on every search.

Cause: every Responses upstream but the ChatGPT backend is sent the
search as a function (searchAsFunction), and the tools each
tool_search_output found were added to the top-level tools. A search
changed the tools, so the next request's prompt changed from its first
bytes. TestToolSearchKeepsThePrefix recorded the bodies of turns 1 to 3
(deepseek-flash on api.deepseek.com, OpenAI's API, a relay with
additional-tools=on): on the old code each one's turn-2 tools gained
the mcp__cal namespace. The Codex account kept the prefix before and
after (TestToolSearchKeepsThePrefixOnCodex, green on both).

What each upstream gets now:
- Codex account: unchanged, the body as Codex sent it.
- DeepSeek's own API (api.deepseek.com), deepseek-flash and
  deepseek-v4.1-flash*: the search as the client sent it
  (searchesAsSent): the tool_search tool, tool_search_call,
  tool_search_output and the found tools' defer_loading. DeepSeek's
  Responses docs (api-docs.deepseek.com, Responses compatibility and
  its tool search guide) list these for V4.1 Flash only and load the
  found tools after the history; deepseek-v4-pro ignores them and its
  Chat API has no deferred loading, so those keep the function form.
  A 400/422 naming tool_search is asked again at once with the
  function form and remembered (clientSearchRefused).
- An upstream that loads in place (loadsInPlace: OpenAI's API with a
  key, additional-tools=on): the function form, with the found tools
  in an additional_tools item right after the output that found them,
  once, and tools as turn 1 sent them (searchAsFunctionIn). A 400/422
  naming additional_tools is asked again with them in tools (loadedUp)
  and remembered, as the translated route already does.
- A translated request: a tool_search_output's tools are
  Tool.Deferred and its result Part.Loads, so buildResponses places
  them in additional_tools where Request.LoadedInPlace is set
  (OpenAI's API, a Codex account, additional-tools=on), as Claude
  Code's ToolSearch loads already are (#2660).
- Unchanged: other relays, deepseek-v4-pro, Chat upstreams (OpenCode
  Go's, DeepSeek's Chat) and the Anthropic route. Chat has no place
  for a late tool, so a search there still changes tools. pi not
  reading a tool_search_call that comes back is pi's side.

No text is added to any prompt; the function's output text is as before.

gateway: xAI's Messages and chat go without stop sequences (#3392)

guqing ran Claude Code 2.1.326 in auto mode against api.x.ai. Its
auto-mode classifier asks with "stop_sequences": ["</block>"], and
xAI's /v1/messages answers that with 400 "Model grok-4.7 does not

hid the required error. guqing also tested straight against api.x.ai:
/v1/messages and /v1/chat/completions refuse any non-empty stop and take
an empty one, and /v1/responses takes it.

max_tokens still bounds the reply. A chat client that set its own stop
for xAI gets a reply that does not stop there. That is the trade for no

usage: a first start's spans begin on the oldest row's local day (#8000)

coldSpans took the oldest row's calendar day from the row's own time and
built that day's midnight in the cut's zone. A row keeps the zone it was
written in: a reported call's "t" and a session file's timestamps are
UTC. West of UTC, a row early on a UTC day is still the day before
locally, so the first span began hours after it and the row was in no
span. The page's kept cells before the cut (page-v1.json), the heatmap's
first day and Codex's effort before the cut all come from these spans,
so such a row was listed on All but counted in none of its totals.

Before d2ef36c17 the gap was hidden: a page with fewer rows since the cut
than it shows paired every chunk and counted all of it again. Since that
commit it keeps the cells and reaches back only for its rows, so the
totals lost the row, and TestUsageIngestTellsSpeed (a reported call at
2026-10-17T00:24Z) went red in PST and green in UTC and UTC+8.

The oldest row's time is now read in the cut's zone, as ledger.go's
chart already does (first.In(now.Location())). The three callers
(pageCold, the heatmap's and Codex effort's cold builds) share the line.

Who it reached: a user west of UTC whose oldest row is a reported or
session-file call in their evening. The cells are written to
page-v1.json, heat and effort files under a key of the settled chunks,
so wrong cells already written stay until that key changes (a new
settled chunk, the next day's cut).

TestColdSpansBeginOnTheOldestRowsLocalDay holds time.Local at UTC-8 and
a call at 00:24Z: All's page of one row, the heatmap's first day, and
both against a pairing of every chunk. Red on the old code ("page: 3

mcpauth: a renewal whose token endpoint is down keeps the sign-in and waits before asking again (#7915)

Since #7451 a renewal that gets 429 waits and shows "renewal
rate-limited". A token endpoint that answered 5xx or couldn't be
reached still ran the sign-in out, so the server showed "needs sign-in"
while the sign-in was fine.

Now a 5xx or a transport failure (not a cancelled ctx) keeps the record,
sets a wait (Retry-After, else the backoff from the record's own
counts) and returns ErrRenewalUnavailable; a token that hasn't run out
is still used. The MCP proxy answers 503 with Retry-After, the Library
check says "renewal failed, retrying" and keeps "Signed in" (zh, zh-TW,
ja, de). invalid_grant and 401 still run the sign-in out. library.md and
mcp-router.md say so.

Ported from Q's fix/mcpauth-renewal-transient-retry (a6c588e20), with
these changes: markRetry takes the backoff from the record inside the
update instead of a copy read before it; the fake's RenewalStatus field
became FailRenewals(status) under its lock (the field raced with the
handler under -race); a GUI case for the new state; the library.md
sentence is rewritten. ArvinChen9539's patch for the same issue
(fix/7915-mcp-temporary-renewal-failure, 77f5c5fdf) is not taken; it

gateway: an account signed in after the gateway started has its models listed without a restart (#7945)

serve() ran FetchNew at start and each minute only while a list was
missing, then stopped. An account signed in later from another process
(magpie accounts add through docker exec beside magpie serve) reached
the serving process through logins.json, but nothing there fetched its
list, so it had no models (and no web-search take-over) until a restart.

provider.KeepNewListed runs for as long as the gateway serves, in every
front end: each minute it fetches the lists of accounts that have none,
under a TryLock so it never waits on another FetchNew, with a 20s bound

gateway: an https download through a proxy the user chose asks for the host by name (#7869)

publicTransport pins the address it resolved, so a fetched video,
picture or drawing went out as CONNECT <address>:443 through an HTTP
proxy. A proxy that takes host names only refused that with 400, and
WorkBuddy's finished video answered 502 "couldn't be fetched".

user (a request's own choice, Settings, or HTTPS_PROXY and friends) or
picked up from the system. For an https URL given by name, through an
http(s) proxy that the user chose or that runs on this computer, the
CONNECT goes by name when every address the name resolved to is public.

the proxy the user set; a system proxy, a SOCKS proxy and an address
written in the URL still get the pinned address. gateway-routing.md
says so.

sessions: read Dim alpha's sessions from its own store (#7990)

Dim alpha (dima, npm dimcode-alpha, agent id dim) was missing from
Sessions and session usage: nothing read its store. internal/sessions/
dim.go reads $DIMCODE_HOME/rust/dimcode.sqlite (else .dimcode-alpha in
the home folder, USERPROFILE on Windows), store format 53, as Dim's
dim-app-server writes it: agent_sessions, session_metadata,
session_catalog and timeline_events. This is the Dim agent's local
store only: no Dim subscription, sign-in or proxying of Dim's service.

- A session is listed once it has an input/message with data.user (as
  Dim's catalog counts prompts). Agents' messages and members' reports
  are raw blocks and don't count.
- A collaboration member (leader_session_id) is filed under its leader:
  its tools and tokens count there, its task doesn't. A fork's main line
  copies its source's through session/forked, so those rows count in the
  source only. Events with parent_call_id are no prompt or reply.
- Tokens: model/usage once per (session, request_id), the model from its
  model/call. promptTokens includes cache reads and writes, so Input is
  what is left of it.
- A <dim-...> runtime block after the first (skill, hook context; the
  MARKERS of Dim's markup.rs) is not the user's words.
- Transcript: the main line's prompts, thinking, replies, tool uses and
  each call's result once.
- Strictly read only: provider.OpenReadOnly (mode=ro) and one read-only
  transaction a listing or parse; never written, locked or migrated. A
  read that fails (Dim's daemon holding the file) is unknown, not "no
  sessions": the last listing stands with cold set, and parseDim (a grow
  parser) hands back the last parse.
- Found() adds dim, so `magpie sessions read` lists it. internal/agent's
  dimDir now calls sessions.DimDirIn, so both find the folder the same way.

Gateway matching: not possible. Dim sends no session header and no
prompt_cache_key; its session and request ids stay in aimux's local
recording (plugin.rs metadata). So its gateway requests stay agent=dim
with no session. The docs page says so.

Fixtures come from Dim's source (sqlite.rs CREATE statements, timeline.rs
Row, events.rs). No real Dim store was on HQ, mote or mica.

usage: a page of rows older than cut reaches back for them, not the whole history

A page whose newest rows are older than the last two days (opening the
app after a few days away, or a filter for a model not used since)
fell back to pairing every chunk of the history, while its cells were
already kept in page-v1.json. On the real-data HOME that held ~30 MB
more heap, steady after the page was built.

Now such a page keeps the cut's cells and reaches back for its rows in
steps of 7, 30 and 120 days before cut, each further only when the one
before keeps fewer rows than the page takes. Each reach counts only the
rows the filter keeps (keptParts), which is what ps.newest reads; the
counts still come from old.cells and the recent parts. Only when the
last reach is still short, or reaches the period's start, does the page
pair every chunk as before.

egress: the Claude editor shows the way out without a Check (mamba on Discord)

mamba asked why the Claude editor's Way out row read "Not looked up
yet" until Check was clicked. Two causes:

- A window whose gateway another magpie serves (the service, magpie
  serve, another copy) never ran egress.Keep: Keep was started only by
  the gateway's ListenAndServe, and the page reads the lookups of its
  own process (egress.Worst in providers.go). Check ran a lookup in the
  window's process, so the address showed only after it. The window's
  startBackend now starts a Keep too. Keep holds a one-slot semaphore,
  so the gateway's and the window's in one process run one at a time:
  one lookup per change, as before, and the second takes over when the
  first ends (a gateway restarted, or ended).
- The Providers list is read once, often before the first lookup ends

agent: PowerShell's agy reads `magpie agy env` from the GUI magpie.exe (CyberCaius on Discord)

On Windows a new terminal's agy started on the user's own sign-in with
none of magpie's models. The function magpie writes into $PROFILE ran
`foreach ($l in @(& 'C:\...\magpie.exe' agy env))`. magpie.exe is linked
as a GUI program, and PowerShell runs a Windows application that ends
its pipeline in the background: NativeCommandProcessor sets
_isRunningInBackground = isWindowsApplication when the command is last
in its pipeline, then neither waits for it nor reads its output, so
$start stayed empty and the function fell through to `& $real @args`.
A native command in the middle of a pipeline is never run in the
background, so the call is now piped into ForEach-Object, which fills
$start. That works with or without the magpie.com beside the app
(magpie.com is written only when the folder is on PATH). The GUI app
leaves a redirected stdout alone (cli/console_windows.go), so the lines
reach the pipe.

The same line was in the function a plugin's agent gets
(plugged_launch.go, agent-agy and any plugin with a Launch). Both now
use psReadEnv.

Old profiles: the block is rewritten on every agent Sync while agy is
on a magpie model (agy.go Sync -> agyShell, plugged.go lsh.set), so the
first start of the new version replaces it. A terminal that is already

copilot: GitHub's Terms of Service 403 rests the account instead of signing it out (yidasanqian on X)

GitHub answered a Copilot account's token trade with 403 "Resource not
accessible by integration. For more on scraping GitHub and how it may
affect your rights, please review our Terms of Service (...)". That tail
is GitHub's wording for its abuse and rate limits (the same tail as its
"API rate limit exceeded ... 403"). A revoked token gets 401 "Bad
credentials" instead. GitHub suspends Copilot for scripted or heavy use
(ericc-ch/copilot-api#84). magpie read the 403 as a refused sign-in:
- copilotRefuse marked the account signed out ("GitHub 拒绝了这个 Copilot
  登录，请重新登录"), and signing in again does not fix that.
- The Sign error became a 502, which the gateway retried as busy.
- Each try traded the token again: one request made 15 trades in 37s.
  That is the reporter's "502 after 37.489s", sent to GitHub from an
  account it had just turned away for its use.

Changes:
- provider/copilot_tos.go: a 403 or 429 whose body has GitHub's
  ToS/rate-limit words holds the token. GitHub is not asked with it again
  until Retry-After, an X-Ratelimit-Reset with none remaining, or an hour
  (clamped to 1m..24h).
- The hold covers the trade (copilotToken), the CLI's copilot_internal/user
  (copilotDirect) and the usage read (copilotSubscriptionUsage).
- Such a refusal is not a sign-out. An earlier signed-out mark it left is
  cleared (copilotSessionDone, login_usage).
- The error ends in CopilotToSHint, which says what happened and what the
  user can do: look for GitHub's mail about the account, or ask GitHub
  Support.
- account.go: a token GitHub refused with 401/403 is not traded again for
  5 minutes. The same error is given meanwhile, so a retry loop can't
  hammer GitHub with a dead token either.
- gateway: restrictedSaid reads the hint, so the account rests as
  restricted (failRestricted, 2h, liftable on Routing). passing() does not
  retry it in place as busy. riskRefused leaves the provider's other
  accounts in play, since GitHub refused the token before any request was
  sent.
- Routing page: the hint is split from GitHub's words and translated
  (zh, zh-TW, ja, de).

Not changed: VS Code sends X-GitHub-Api-Version 2025-04-01 on the trade
and on copilot_internal/user, and magpie sends none there. It can't be
tried without a real account, and it isn't what GitHub's words are about.
The allowance read can reach copilot_internal/user about once a minute
while routing asks, where VS Code reads it about every 25 minutes. That
is left as it was.

redact: a name in code and a TRON address go as written, and Never mask takes a pattern (#7973)

StringKe's patch, narrowed in review. The local model took names in
code for secrets (Illuminate, Speechmatics, JazzCash, dev_worker5,
edge-san-jose-01, Mozilla/5.0, PaymentClient.merchant_api_key) and
USDT's TRON contract, and the agent read a placeholder where each was.

What lands:
- codeName: a Pascal or camel name, an identifier, a dashed host or
  route name, a user agent's version, a field read through a class, of
  8 characters or more, goes as written when the model calls it a
  secret. Digits only as a short number at a word's end
  (scatteredDigits) and capitals at most a third of it, so a key's
  random run (key-3ax6xnjp…, k3xq9vb2mz-…, XkQpLmZnBv, a Discord
  token's dotted shape) is masked still.
- credentialAt: such a name is masked where a password goes: given a
  secret's name or called one, a pw/auth/login/cred cue, after user:
  or user%, or as any command flag's value (mysql -p, redis-cli -a,
  --pass).
- tronAddress: a TRON address with its 0x41 byte and checksum goes as
  written unless called a key.
- Never mask: a value with * is a pattern (*-singapore-*, binedge-*).
- Keep a key's form: a word with no key's head and no digit goes as a
  placeholder, not a made-up word.

Changed from the patch:
- Solana public keys are not exempt: a 32-byte seed in base58 has the
  same shape, so no check tells them apart.
- The name shapes reject scattered digits, long numbers and random
  capitals; as sent, hostNameRe and snakeIdentRe let a lowercase key
  with digits go (key-3ax6xnjp29jd6fds4gc373sgvjxteol0).
- credentialAt added: as sent, PurpleMonkey after mysql -p,
  sshpass -p, redis-cli -a, curl -u admin:, smbclient admin% or
  "pw": went out.
- relPathRe dropped: slugRe already lets config/service.key go.
- A pattern needs 4 characters besides its stars (* alone matched
  everything), and lets go only personal data, network names and
  model/name-found SECRETs (wildKind). A vendor key, a crypto key or
  a value of the user's own rule goes only written out in full.
- Shape keeps the made-up key for a headless key with digits (hex
  keys, random keys): only digit-free words go as placeholders, so
  Shape users' hex keys still pass a form check.

gateway: an account near its cap is held by the turns not in a reading, not every turn since usage last moved (gakiclin1 on X)

gakiclin1 on X: a Claude Code account capped at 70% was held at 41%,
"its next turn would take it past its 70% cap: a turn there has spent
up to 30 points".

Cause: turnSpends.ahead counted out + (turns - s.turns) turns at the
learned per-turn spend, where s.turns is the turn count of the last
reading that moved the usage. Turns a later reading already had, but
that left a whole-point usage where it was, were still counted as if no
reading had them, one learned spend each. On a big plan one turn moves
a whole-point usage, then dozens don't: 40% -> 41% over one turn
learned a point a turn, the next 29 turns read at 41% made ahead 29,
own() added the turn's 1, and CapHeldWithin held 41 > 70 - 30. Once held
no turn goes there, so nothing moves the reading and the hold stays
until the window renews. The same rule with nothing learned already
capped those turns at a point between them (guess's 1/n each); the
learned path didn't.

Fix: ahead counts out + (turns - s.read) at the guess, the turns no
reading has, and at most a point for the s.read - s.turns turns a
reading has that didn't move it (they spent under a point between
them, the remainder a whole-point reading hides). With nothing learned
the result is unchanged (g*n = 1 there). The near-cap hold is now the
turn's learned spend plus the turns truly not in a reading, plus that
point at most.

The held reason told CapTurn (own + ahead) as one turn's spend. capHold
and the trace's Weighed carry CapAhead too, and the reason now says "a
turn there has spent up to X points, and turns its last reading doesn't
have yet are taken to spend Y points" (either half alone when the other
is 0). docs/subsystems/gateway-routing.md says the same.

which says the reading has it; it now passes read=2, as its comment
says (6 as before). New steps: 29 turns read at 41% after a 40 -> 41
turn are 1 point ahead, and 1 + 3 with three unread.
TestNearCapHeldByTurnsNotRead feeds Server.nearCapOf/nearCapHeld the
reported sequence on a Claude account capped at 70% (allowances
stubbed), wants it let in at 41% and held at 69% with an unread turn
(2 points, 1 of them ahead), and checks the reason's wording.

call's id (signedID, __tsk16__<key>). namelessEncoder (streamed) and
namelessResult (whole) drop that call, and its id with it, so the named
call reached the client with a plain id. On the next turn it had no
Signature: a relay serving Gemini got neither extra_content nor
skip_thought_signature_validator and answered 400 "Function call is
missing a thought_signature"; Google's own host was sent the skip in
place of the real signature. The history drops (withoutNamelessCalls,
namelessItemsOut, namelessChatCallsOut) lost it the same way for a
client that kept the nameless call.

Fix: each drop hands the left-out call's signature to the next named
call of the same step that carries none of its own, in the form it
carries there: the reply's call id (namelessEncoder, namelessResult),
Part.Signature (withoutNamelessCalls), and a relayed history's call id
with its answer's call_id/tool_call_id renamed to match
(namelessItemsOut, namelessChatCallsOut), or a Chat call's
extra_content. Only ids carrying sigMark (or a google thought_signature
in extra_content) hand anything on, so other vendors' replies and
histories are unchanged. docs/subsystems/gateway-routing.md says so.

sessions: an Antigravity call a subagent shares with its parent counts once (Taytay_19891213 on X)

Cause: readAntigravityCalls gave each call the id
"antigravity:<conversation>:<step>". Usage counts a call id once over
every file (callsFor's seen map, the Requests page's visibleLocal), but
a subagent's call written in its own conversation database and in its
parent's had two ids, one per conversation, so it was counted twice
(the report: 728 calls / 177M tokens in a day where 424 / 95M were made).

The data: the step's metadata field 9.11 is the vendor's response id,
already read by antigravityRead (it folds one response's steps in one
database into one call). #2190's real rows carry it on every model
step. #6022 independently describes subagent and forked-worker
conversations as databases of their own, a fork's parent_references
naming the step it forked at. No real Antigravity database was on any
of our machines, so the shared id itself is the reporter's word.

Fix: antigravityCallID. A call whose step names a response id has the
id "antigravity:response:<id>" (Insiders' "antigravity:insiders-
response:<id>", keeping the two stores apart as
TestAntigravityInsidersSessions requires), so the first file's copy is counted and
the other left out. A step with no response id keeps the old
conversation-and-step id. Two calls with different response ids never
share an id, even with equal tokens and times.

Old data: callParseVersions' antigravity goes 2 -> 3, so every
Antigravity call shard is read again from its database on the next
read, and usage's requests and heatmap caches, keyed by
CallCacheVersion, are rebuilt. Nothing double-counted is kept: every
user's history is counted once again as long as the databases are on
disk. A shared call is counted under the conversation whose file is
older (usually the subagent's), and a one-session call list asked for
the other conversation no longer shows it.

Not changed, filed as #7980: the Sessions page sums each
conversation's calls into its own totals, so the overview still counts
a shared call in both; the agy CLI keys its calls by conversation and
step too, not checked for the same sharing.

and images and drops thinking, tool calls, tool results and context
