commits.message:
iOS: a conversation's failed read is an error seen only from an empty chat on screen

Production 2026.11.1 (163) posted error_shown area=conversation_load for
about a quarter of iOS direct-connection users a day, and Android none.
Conversation.failed posted every failed history read: over the rows the
phone kept, off screen in a warm chat, and again at every backoff retry,
though iOS shows no error for any of them and asks again by itself. Only
an empty chat on screen now posts it, as Android's Conversation.reload
does ("only an empty chat says it").

A direct connection's tunnel errors (TailcatError, TransportError,
TailcatTransportError, NWError) were all Problem.unknown. They are named
now: a Tailcat client that can't connect in its 20 seconds, the
`unknown` errors seen 20-30 s after an open, is a timeout.

A bootstrap whose mode, draft, context or a subagent this build can't
read decoded to nothing, and the conversation's read failed with
invalid_response on every try. Only the agent is required now, as in
Android's Bootstrap.parse.

android: a message or agent state too big for a cursor window is stored cut, and one stored before reads as null

Build 2026.11.1 (167) crashed on one install seven times: SQLiteBlobTooBigException
and OutOfMemoryError in HappyStore.messages (MessageSync's chat flow) and
HappyStore.sessions (home), plus an OOM stringifying a JsonObject. The store
kept every decrypted document whole. A relay tool output of megabytes made a
message row past the 2 MB CursorWindow, which throws on every read of that
chat; the old CLI's agent state keeps every completedRequests entry with its
arguments, so a long session's row grew the same way and home read it for
every session.

Write side (StoredJson): a message's content and a session's agent state are
measured before they are written out; over 512 KB, long strings are cut
(16K, then 1K, then 128 chars), and an agent state still too big loses
completedRequests. A message that can't fit is stored with null content, as
one that doesn't open. RecordDecoder and LiveUpdates' agent-state path use it.

Read side (HappyStore): metadata, agent_state and message content longer
than 768 KB read as null, in SQL, so rows already stored can't crash or
fill memory; the next write of the record replaces them.

fix(android): a cold start's foreground reaches the relay sender, so sends don't fail at once as "failed in background after 30s"

AccountSync.start() told MessageSender the foreground from one read and
watched later changes with `foreground.drop(1)` in a coroutine on io. When
MainActivity started between that read and the watcher's first collection
(the account opens on Default while the activity resumes after graphReady),
the flip to foreground was the dropped value: the sender stayed "in the
background since start", and from 30 s on its watchdog failed every send,
and every Retry, the moment it was queued, with BACKGROUND_FAILURE, until
the app went behind and came back or was killed.

The watcher now drops only values equal to the one the sender was given.

MessageSenderTest holds the account's io dispatcher through start(), flips
the foreground, then sends a minute later: before, the row failed with
"Message failed to send in background after 30s"; now it goes on the retry.

happy-android: a terminal code without a key makes no account, and a failed key restore says which step failed

sign_in_failed on 2026.11.1 (167), traced code by code:

- relay_create/unknown: Add (and a terminal link with no Happy account)
  called createAccount before reading the terminal's key. POST /v1/auth
  made an account on the server, then approveTerminal's base64url decode
  or encryptBox threw IllegalArgumentException for a key that isn't 32
  bytes, which relaySignIn has no step for. The person saw "Failed to
  connect terminal" and the server kept an account no phone has.
  terminalPublicKey() now reads the key first, as iOS's LegacyPairingLink
  does (base64url or standard base64; a line break or space inside it, as
  a wrapped terminal line copies, is dropped), and createAccountForTerminal
  turns a code without one away before any account is made, as "Invalid
  authentication URL", with no sign_in_failed.
- relay_restore, secret key: every failure read "Invalid secret key",
  so a right key offline or during a server error sent people retyping
  it. The alert now follows the step (restoreFailureMessage): a key that
  isn't one or one the server refused says check the key; no network,
  the server's error, keeping the credentials say that.

Not changed: relay_restore/server_error came from three Android 11 test
devices (one in Google's 74.125/16, two with device-farm fingerprints)
and one transient 5xx for a signed-in person who carried on; the same
request against production answers 200, and nothing in the client can
make the server answer 5xx for it.

iOS: the iPhone's drawer, home of bots and tasks, Plugins in Settings

On an iPhone, home's account face (and a swipe in from the leading edge)
opens a drawer: the account switcher at its top, then Home, Activity,
Artifacts, Documents, TODOs, Plugins, Pipelines, a divider and the other
Surfaces, with Settings pinned at its foot. Picking a place makes it the
stack's root with a menu button where back would be; Home is kept and
comes back as it was. Home on an iPhone lists the shared bot, the bots and
the tasks alone; its bar has no settings gear. Links, the call's "home"
and Pipelines going away land on the drawer's home whatever place is the
root. The iPad keeps its sidebar.

Plugins and Pipelines now follow TODOs on the sidebar, and an agent's
Settings ends its Agents group with Plugins where the server serves them,
as desktop's Settings has it.

DrawerLayout with exact-frame tests, Drawer's rows in HappyCore tests,
HostedPhoneDrawerTests on a simulator.

iOS: Documents and TODOs sections on home, as desktop's sidebar has them

Home's first group gets two fixed rows after Pipelines, "Documents" and
"TODOs" (replacing "Todos"). Each pushes a list of every Surface of its
type in the computer's catalog, by name; a todo list shows what it has
left while it has some, read from the computer for lists never opened
here. The bar's + makes only that section's kind and opens it.

No document or todo list is a home row of its own any more, whether
joined or a space's target; what the person is in stays in
HomeSnapshot.sectionedRows so search, a Surface chat's title and the
open todos search reads keep treating them as the person's own. Stored
joins, order keys and spaces are untouched.

TodoListsViewController becomes SurfaceListViewController over a
SurfaceSection (documents, todos).

android: Plugins in the agent's Settings too, last in Agents

Where the server serves plugins, Settings' Agents group ends with Plugins
(after Usage; desktop's place for it, after its Secrets), opening the same
plugins page over Settings. The drawer and the tablet card keep their
Plugins row: desktop has it in Settings only, phones in both (Steve).

android: home keeps the instance's picture on its bar, opening the drawer

Steve: the account's avatar stays at the bar's start on a phone; it opens
the drawer (whose header still switches accounts) instead of a ☰.

android: a navigation drawer on phones, home its bots and tasks

An agent connection's phone has a modal drawer from the start edge: the
account and its menu in the header; Home, Activity, Artifacts, Documents,
TODOs, Plugins and Pipelines, then the other joined Surfaces; Settings at
the foot. A pick is the stack's new root at once, whose back is the ☰;
the drawer opens from ☰ and by a swipe on a root. Home's bar is ☰, the
name and search; home lists the shared bot, bots and tasks. The places
card takes the drawer's order on the tablet too. Agreed with iOS.

android: Documents and TODOs rows on home, each opening a list of its Surfaces

Desktop's sections, without tabs: home's places get fixed Documents and
TODOs rows after Pipelines; a document or todo list is no longer a home row
of its own (the feed keeps the joined ones in AgentFeed.lists for search).
Each row opens every Surface of that kind, joined or not, by name; a todo
list trails its open count when there is one. + makes one of that kind and
opens it; an item opens the Surface's page, Back returning to the list.

android: home's places in desktop's order, the shared bot last

Activity, Artifacts, Plugins, Pipelines, Todos, the joined Surfaces, then
Happy Cloud's shared bot (happy-desktop #215's top group).

android: Happy Cloud's shared and personal bots

A cluster bot carries `kind`. The shared bot (only owners get it) is the
first row of home's places card, above Artifacts; personal bots stay in
Bots, each opening the caller's own conversation. Placement follows
`kind` alone, editing `editable` alone, never `isAdmin`; a Happy Agent
daemon's bots, which have no kind, are listed as before.

On Happy Cloud, or wherever a bot carries a kind, new work is a task: the
Task | Bot choice is gone and a kept Bot choice becomes a task.

An editable bot's agent page opens Bot Settings: picture (PUT/DELETE
/v0/bots/:id/avatar), name and multiline instructions, saved with
PATCH /v0/bots/:id (If-Match, only what changed, once more over a 409's
newer version). Back with unsaved changes asks first. The shared bot is
read-only. Debug builds have BotsFixturesActivity for the scenes.

iOS: place Happy Cloud bots by kind and edit personal bots in Bot Settings

A Happy Cloud server's bots now carry `kind` (shared or personal) and
`editable`. Home places a bot by its kind alone, never `isAdmin` or
`systemKey`: the shared bot (only owners receive it) closes the first
group, after Activity, Artifacts, Plugins, Pipelines, Todos and the
Surfaces, as desktop orders it, and is never moved or hidden; personal
bots stay among the bots, each opening the reader's own conversation.
The first group now leads with Activity, as desktop's does. A daemon's
bots carry no kind and are listed as before.

New work on a Happy Cloud server is a task: the Task | Bot choice is
gone, and a bot asked for falls back to a task, since its bots come
from its admin bot.

A bot whose `editable` is true gets a Bot Settings row on its profile:
picture, name and multiline instructions (32 KiB). Save sends only what
changed with `PATCH /v0/bots/:id` over the version read (If-Match), the
picture on its own route; a stale save reads the bot again and retries
once unless someone else changed the same field. A shared bot has no
edit affordance.

Decoding is lossy for the new fields, so a field this build can't read
never loses the bootstrap. Tests: BotKindTests (decoding, owner, member
and daemon sectioning, kind independent of admin), BotEditTests (the
form, the PATCH and avatar requests, conflict handling) and
BotSettingsLayoutTests. The cluster harness gains `-botkinds`.

mobile: say under About that developer mode is on and how to turn it off

While developer mode is on, About's footer on iOS and Android opens with
"Developer mode is on. Tap Version ten times to turn it off." Ten taps
on Version already toggle it both ways; the line says so. Turning it off
hides the Happy Cloud switch again and leaves its value as it was.

mobile: show the Happy Cloud switch in developer mode only

Outside developer mode Settings has no Happy Cloud card, footer or search
result on iOS and Android, and home's search on iOS no longer indexes it.
Defaults are unchanged (on in debug/preview, off in production), still
kept only once the switch is turned; entering or leaving developer mode
changes only whether the switch shows.

iOS, Android: Happy Cloud's switch is Settings' alone, defaulting by build

Kirill: the switch lives in Settings only. Start's Get help no longer
offers Turn On / Turn Off Happy Cloud, on either app, and nothing else on
Start or in onboarding does.

Its default is the build's, computed in code: on in dev and preview
builds, off in the store's (Android HappyCloud.offeredByDefault, debug
and preview; iOS HappyCloud.isOfferedByDefault, development and preview).
The stored value is an override written only by the switch's own change
(same keys: Android prefs happy-cloud/offered, iOS UserDefaults
happy-cloud); until it is turned nothing is kept, so a phone follows each
build's default across updates. Android's invite-link alias follows the
effective value.

iOS, Android: the H in the Happy Cloud mark is solid black

Kirill: the H was a hole showing the sky, and on the light sky the
contrast was way off. As desktop's liquidMetalShader.ts (happy-desktop
#214): cloud.svg's H cut-out as a signed distance, max(rounded square,
-notches), grown by 2 texels of the 512 field, adds coverage under the
metal and no colour, alpha = opacity + hole * (1 - opacity), so the
metal's soft inner bevel blends onto #000 in light and dark alike. In the
AGSL program, which the pre-Android-13 GL still is translated from, and
the Metal one.

iOS, Android: Happy Cloud behind a Settings switch, off until turned on

Android: a device-wide HappyCloudSetting (prefs "happy-cloud", kept for
every account), off on every build. Every build now has Happy Cloud's
addresses; the switch decides whether its ways in are offered: Start's
Use Happy Cloud, the account menu's Connect to Happy Cloud and Unlock
Failed's (LocalCloudConnect), and invite links. The invite intent filters
move from the debug/preview overlays to a disabled HappyCloudLinks alias
in the main manifest that the switch enables, so while it is off the
links stay the browser's; DeepLinkEffect also drops a Cloud invite while
Cloud isn't offered.

iOS: HappyCloud.isOffered reads UserDefaults "happy-cloud", on by default
in the preview app only (AppVariant from Info.plist HappyAppVariant),
off in development and production until changed; setOffered posts
offeredChanged and Start shows or hides Use Happy Cloud live.

Both: the switch is a card above Privacy on both kinds of Settings, and,
since Settings can't be reached before an account, the first screen's
Get help offers Turn On / Turn Off Happy Cloud. Servers already on the
phone keep working either way.

iOS, Android: the sky and the Happy Cloud mark are always the shaders' own, with no flat stand-in or fade

The onboarding sky (Grain Gradient) and the Happy Cloud mark (Liquid Metal)
now look the same on every client: grain and metal always, a still frame 0
on lower-spec hardware, and no transition into the shader.

iOS: GrainGradientView and LiquidMetalView draw their first frame as they
go on screen and present it with the transaction that shows them
(presentsWithTransaction), instead of flashing the flat back colour or
nothing until an async frame lands. They hold frame 0 under ShaderMotion:
Reduce Motion, Low Power Mode, thermal state serious or critical.

Android: GrainGradient no longer fades in over a flat radial-gradient
stand-in; until its grain field is ready it draws the whole shader (the
same picture), and programs not yet warmed are compiled where they are
needed. LiquidMetalMark no longer shows the flat tinted cloud while it
warms. Both hold frame 0 under rememberShadersMove: animations removed,
Battery Saver, a low-RAM phone, thermal status severe or worse. Before
Android 13 ShaderStills draws frame 0 of both with OpenGL ES 2 from the
same AGSL sources, so older phones get grain and metal instead of a flat
gradient and a flat cloud.

iOS: voice calls from a Happy account (Happy CLI sessions) (#2126)

* iOS: voice calls from a Happy account (Happy CLI sessions)

The call button is back on a Happy account's home, on the same call as an
agent connection's: one bar, lifecycle, mute and end, analytics, and the
device's free minutes or paid hours (CallAllowance) shared between both.
No relay voice token: the hosted v3 agent, injected at build time.

- LegacyCallTarget: home's sessions as the call's directory (newest
  created first, under project and worktree headings, an unnamed session
  "New chat" as its row says), status, reads with turn failures, and
  what a send may change.
- LegacyCallTargets: list, read, send (refused on a session that can't
  take one), model and effort through the composer's own chips (a
  locked model refused), new work through NewSessionLaunch with the
  refusals the call speaks, and navigation.
- CallContext.HappyCLI: the prompt lines and refusals for this account.
- CallScreens and the history file shared by both accounts; the binding
  names the account so a switch ends the call.
- Settings: Voice on a Happy account too.
- AccountSwitcherLayout: a third header button takes its whole width, so
  iOS doesn't fold them into a menu while a status widens the switcher.
- Debug: HAPPY_CALL_TYPE types turns into a silent live call; steps can
  mute and end.
- docs/agent-voice-call.md: the Happy CLI section (with Android's
  notes) and the paid limit as the code has it (2 h a paid month).

* iOS: relay voice sends never go twice, recheck after a switch; follows reserved; new work per kind

- A send is held under its message ID before it waits: a retry after
  "uncertain" shares it, a new-work start included; a refused one can
  be tried again.
- After a model switch, the call, the deadline and the session's record
  are checked again right before the message is queued.
- A follow holds its feed before reading the composer's chips, so two
  follows can't start two observers and close cancels it.
- The first context checks tasks and bots one at a time.
- The locked-model refusal ends "Nothing was sent.", as Android's.

* iOS: relay voice sends judged in the keeping transaction; voice starts on their own spawn requests, stopped by End

- A voice send is kept only if the session's stored row, read in the
  transaction that enqueues it, can take it (LocalStore
  enqueueAcceptedSend admitting, LegacySyncEngine.accept, OutboxSender).
- Each voice start runs under its own SpawnRequests, never compose's, so
  two starts can't share a session; closing the call closes them, so a
  pending start keeps nothing once End is tapped.
- LegacyCallTargets.Relay: the relay and outbox as one seam, the live
  account's or a test's.
- Tests: HostedLegacyCallTargetsTests (same-ID retries, new-work retry,
  the checks after the switch, follow setup races, own spawn requests and
  End stopping a start) and the transactional refusal in
  SendingDeliveryMetaTests.

* iOS: a voice start's first message and End race through one gate; its spawn slot under the account's

- VoiceStartGate: End and the first message's keeping, decided in the
  outbox's transaction (VoiceStartSender, admitting). Ended first, the
  message is refused and the start put down; kept first, End leaves the
  session.
- Each voice start's spawn requests are a child of the account's
  (SpawnRequests.Role.voiceStart), so opening the new chat adopts it and
  the account's teardown reaches it, without compose's slot.
- Tests against the real SessionStarter: End before and after the first
  message is kept, and an adopted chat outliving End.

fix: the Claude model chip names the model the session runs (#2127)

* fix: the Claude model chip names the model the session runs

A terminal-started Claude session has no model pick. The Android and iOS
chips fell back to the code default (Opus 5.5), but for Claude the message
meta sent no model, and the CLI then let Claude Code pick its own default:
Sonnet 5.5 on accounts where that is the default. So the chip read Opus
while every turn ran Sonnet.

The CLI now reports the model in session metadata (`currentModelCode`):
the configured one at start (--model, ANTHROPIC_MODEL, then the project's
and the user's settings `model`), and on every turn the model from the
SDK's init message. A reconnect starts the value over.

The apps resolve an unpicked Claude session's model as: the user's default
(sent), else what the CLI reports (shown, not sent, so a running session
is never re-modeled), else the code default, which now goes out with the
message instead of being shown and never sent. A pick on the chip still
goes out as before.

* fix: resume without the model default, pass happy --model to local Claude

Review follow-ups to the model chip fix:

- A resume sends only a model pick or the user's default, never Claude's
  code default: the new process reports the model its own configuration
  names, and a message sends the default only if it reports none.
- `happy --model` is consumed by Happy, so the interactive (and offline)
  local Claude never got it while the session already advertised it.
  It now goes on to the local Claude unless its args carry a --model.
- The configured-model lookup reads the user settings from the config dir
  Claude is given (--claude-env CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR), not the parent's.

* fix: always send the model the Claude chip shows

Kirill's call: whatever the composer chip shows goes out as the model, on
every message and on resume. The chip is the session's pick, then the
user's default, then the model the CLI reports (currentModelCode), then
the code default. Sending the reported model is a no-op for the running
process; overriding the machine's own Claude config when nothing else is
known is accepted. Drops the "shown but not sent" case and the resume
special case on Android and iOS.

* fix: publish the model local Claude turns run; keep Claude's default alias

A terminal /model switch now reaches the app: the local launcher publishes
currentModelCode from main-thread assistant transcript entries (not
subagents or <synthetic>), keeping a published [1m] variant of the same model.

A reported `default` (happy --model default) gets its own chip row and is
sent as itself on messages and resume; a picked `default` stays the app's
reset and still goes out as null.

* fix: publish only live local turns' model; scan Claude's own config dir

Replayed transcript entries (--continue, reconnect) still reach the chat but
no longer set currentModelCode: only main-thread assistant entries written
after this local launch count, so --model is not undone by older turns.

The local scanner and claudeLocal's project dir now use the env Claude runs
with, so --claude-env CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR transcripts are found.

Co-authored-by: Kirill Dubovitskiy <kirill2003de@gmail.com>

Android: voice for Happy CLI sessions (the agent connection's call) (#2124)

* Android: voice for Happy CLI sessions, the agent connection's call

The relay home gets the agent home's voice button (left of compose, the
tablet sidebar's foot) and nothing else: no chat or composer has one. It
starts the same call (CallController.startCli) with the same hosted v3
agent, prompt, four tools, sheets and one device-local CallAllowance.
LegacyCallTargets reads home's sessions (bots, tasks, then projects, each
newest made first), each chat as ChatFeed reduces it, sends through the
composer's sender marked voice, switches model and effort as the chips do
(refused only when the computer locks them), and starts tasks and named
bots through Happy Agent's spawn on compose's computer. A failed turn-end
is now AgentEvent.TurnFailed, so a call reads Happy Agent's failed runs.

The old relay voice (voice/, ui/voice/, VoiceEngine, its server usage,
settings page and Required sheet) is deleted. Settings' Voice row opens
the shared Voice page.

* Android: an unnamed relay session reads New chat; only an online one takes the call's sends

As iOS: the call names an unnamed session as its home row does, and a
stopped or offline session is read, never sent to.

* Android relay call: check sends where they enqueue, keep a draft's ref, gate the live check

- A voice send is checked again inside the sender's outbox step: the
  account, local archiving, the session's archived state and, for an
  existing session, that it is online. A just-spawned session's first
  message is checked for archiving only (its presence may lag).
- Sends run in the call's own scope, keyed by message ID: a tool deadline
  no longer cancels one mid-way, and the same ID again waits for it.
- A session the call's new work made is listed, followed and told under
  the draft's ref, so replies to a follow-up reach the call.
- LegacyCallLiveDeviceCheck runs only with -e live 1 and logs nothing.

* Android relay call: live presence at enqueue, the draft's ref from spawn, no content logs by default

- A voice send is online by live presence, else the stored flag, as the
  chat has it, checked again at enqueue. New work's first message waits
  (up to 15 s) for its session to come online, then the same check.
- The draft's ref takes over the new session as soon as the spawn
  answers, before home lists it, and the directory is told at once.
- Freshness is read by the session's own ID; the draft's ref goes only
  on what the call is told.
- CallProbe keeps and logs nothing unless a live check turns capture on;
  LegacyCallLiveDeviceCheck writes live.txt only with -e capture 1.

* Android relay call: a session home listed before spawn answered keeps the ref the call gave it

The server tells of a new session before the spawn RPC returns, so home can
list it, and the call hand out a ref for it, before the draft's alias goes in.
Such a session now keeps its own ID in the directory and the draft's ref names
it too; both refs read and send to the one session. Unit test for the
event-before-RPC-response ordering through CallContext.

commits.message:
[Core] Default new authenticated users to the user role (#11521)

* [Core] Default new authenticated users to the user role

With rbac.default_role unset, every new identity was seeded as admin.
Authenticated identities (SSO, auth proxy, API-server basic auth) and
service accounts created without a role now get `user`; requests that
reach the server unauthenticated keep `admin`. While no authenticated
user or service account holds admin, the first new login through an
auth proxy or OAuth2 proxy becomes admin, so a deployment is never left
without one.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

* [Core] Count untyped admins with a password as existing admins

Rows from before user types existed have no type. One with a password was
authenticated, so it stops the first-admin bootstrap. An `sa-` id is not
counted: a client without authentication chooses its own user id.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

* [Core] Count only admins who can still log in before bootstrapping

An admin that can no longer authenticate left a deployment with no usable
admin and no bootstrap: a basic-auth admin after the API server's basic
auth is turned off (for example after moving to SSO), or a service
account whose tokens have all expired. Basic-auth admins now count only
while ENABLE_BASIC_AUTH is on, and service-account admins only while
service accounts are enabled and they hold an unexpired token. A token
also lets an untyped sa- row count, since only authenticated endpoints
write tokens.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

* [Docs] Name only ingress basic auth as the unauthenticated example

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

* [Core] Bootstrap the first admin only when rbac.default_role is unset

A configured default role never produced an admin before; keep it that
way. The bootstrap still covers deployments that leave the default unset,
which used to make every new user an admin.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

Co-authored-by: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

[Jobs] Page the managed jobs queue from an index and compute its counts only when asked (#11522)

* [Jobs] Page the managed jobs queue from an index and compute its counts only when asked

A queue page selects its top-level jobs, and follows its cursor, along an
index on job_info's coalesce(root_job_id, spot_job_id), alone and under the
user and workspace scopes (migration 032), and reads its rows through the
same index. `/jobs/queue/v2` takes `include_counts` (default true): without
it the server skips total, total_no_filter, status_counts and infra_options,
each of which reads every matching job. It is threaded through the
GetJobTable proto, the codegen (MANAGED_JOBS_VERSION 30) and the runner
protocol; a controller or runner that predates it computes the counts.
API_VERSION 74, SKYLET_VERSION 48.

The SDK fetches the queue in pages only from API 74, asks for the counts on
the first page and takes them from it. queue_v2 takes include_counts, and
callers that discard the counts pass false.

* [Jobs] Format migration 032, bump the dashboard client API version, and update queue tests

* [Jobs] Take paged counts from the first page's value; one source for the tree-root index expression

* [Jobs] Return no counts from a queue that matches no user or workspace when they were skipped

* [Jobs] Note why migration 032 builds its indexes without CONCURRENTLY

[Dashboard] Send reads as sync calls and fetch the cluster, volume and recipe lists in pages (#11504)

The dashboard reads `sync_call_max_limit` and `api_version` from `/api/health` (after early-init plugins; a failed probe is tried again on the next call) and sends `X-SkyPilot-Sync` on `apiClient.fetch` and on the reads that schedule a request themselves, for a request with a `limit` only within the server's maximum. A refused sync call is sent again without the header; a busy one is retried per `Retry-After` (1 s when missing, at most 5 s, 5 tries), then runs as a background request. A result answered in the response is read without `/api/get`. The `window.__skyApiFetch` plugin hook is removed.

On API 72+, `getClusters`, `getVolumes` and `getRecipes` fetch their list as sync calls of the server's maximum size, following the cursor until a page comes back empty (pinned recipes still first). A page that is refused, busy, not answered in its response or repeats a row sends the list to one unpaged call, and nothing is queued for that page. Status for named clusters that fit one page, none a glob pattern, is one sync call.

The Python SDK's `sdk.status`, `sdk.storage_ls` and `sky.volumes.ls` detect a dropped cursor by a repeated row instead of byte order, since the server orders names in its database collation. `sdk.status` for named clusters that fit one page is one sync call.

fix(coding-agent): keep $ in exported HTML (#12609)

Closes #12608.

**Problem.** `generateHtml` inserts the viewer script, the vendor
scripts and the CSS with `String.prototype.replace` and a string as the
replacement, which expands `$$` to `$` and `$&` to the matched text. The
viewer writes the cost as `$${totalCost.toFixed(3)}`, so the exported
header showed `Cost: 0.300`. `highlight.min.js` contains both patterns
as well: the exported copy had `{{HIGHLIGHT_JS}}` in the R operator
regex in place of `$&`, and the Swift variable rule lost a `$`.

**Fix.** Every value is passed through a function (`.replace("{{JS}}",
() => templateJs)`), which inserts it as is. Applied to all ten
replacements, the CSS ones included, so a value with a `$` in it can no
longer change.

The chained replacements could also replace a placeholder that an
earlier inserted file contains. No inserted file contains one today, so
this PR does not change that; a single `replace(/\{\{(\w+)\}\}/g, ...)`
pass would rule it out if wanted.

fix(coding-agent): detect WSL without the WSL environment variables (#12634)

## Problem

Pi detects WSL in several places, with two different checks:

| Place | Check |
|---|---|
| `utils/wsl.ts` `isWSL()` (clipboard) | `WSL_DISTRO_NAME \|\| WSLENV`,
then `/proc/version` |
| `core/keybindings.ts` `useWindowsKeybindings()` | `WSL_DISTRO_NAME
\|\| WSL_INTEROP` only |
| `core/footer-data-provider.ts` `isWslEnvironment()` | `WSL_DISTRO_NAME
\|\| WSL_INTEROP` only |
| p2 `hosts/tui-local-preferences.ts` `launcherCapabilities()` |
`WSL_DISTRO_NAME \|\| WSL_INTEROP` only |
| p2 `hosts/tui-clipboard.ts` `isWSL()` | copy of the first one |

The WSL variables are only set in shells started through `wsl.exe`. A
terminal that runs as a systemd user service inside WSL (seen with the
Rex terminal) starts shells without them. In that case:

- Keybindings: pi uses the plain Linux defaults. Image paste is bound
only to `ctrl+v`, which the Windows-side terminal handles as its own
paste, so pasting an image does nothing. The Windows/WSL defaults
(`alt+v` + `ctrl+v`, `ctrl+q` follow-up, ...) never apply.
- Footer: for repos under `/mnt/<drive>`, pi watches `.git/HEAD` instead
of polling it, and file watching does not work across the Windows mount,
so the branch shown can go stale.
- The clipboard code still detects WSL (it falls back to
`/proc/version`), so the two checks disagree in the same process.

Nothing in the history suggests the split was intentional: the env-only
checks were added later than `isWSL()` without reusing it. Cost is not a
reason either: the `/proc/version` read is a few microseconds and runs
only when the variables are missing, a few times per session.

## Changes

- `utils/wsl.ts`: `isWSL(platform, env)` is the single check. False off
Linux; true for any of `WSL_DISTRO_NAME`, `WSL_INTEROP`, `WSLENV`; else
`/proc/version` matches `microsoft|wsl`. It takes `platform` so callers
stop repeating `platform === "linux" &&`, and so a Windows process with
`WSLENV` in its environment is never reported as WSL.
- `useWindowsKeybindings`, the footer's `shouldPollGitHead`, and both
clipboard modules call it.
- p2 cannot import coding-agent internals and already keeps copies of
its clipboard helpers, so `hosts/tui-wsl.ts` is a copy of `isWSL`, used
by `tui-clipboard.ts` (replacing its private copy) and
`launcherCapabilities().windowsKeys`.

## Tests

- New `test/wsl.test.ts`: each variable alone, the `/proc/version`
fallback without variables (the systemd-service case), plain Linux,
unreadable `/proc/version`, other platforms with WSL variables set.
- `keybindings.test.ts` stubs `isWSL`, so its expectations no longer
depend on the host.
- `clipboard.test.ts` / `clipboard-image.test.ts`: 12 tests failed on
`main` when run on a WSL host because they read the real
`/proc/version`. They now hide it and clear `WSL_INTEROP`, and pass on
WSL hosts with and without the WSL variables.
- New p2 `test/p2/tui-wsl.test.ts`: variable and platform cases for the
copy and `launcherCapabilities`.
- Manual: on a WSL2 host with the variables unset,
`useWindowsKeybindings()` now returns `true` and image paste defaults to
`["alt+v", "ctrl+v"]` (was `false` / `"ctrl+v"`).

`npm run check` and `cd apps/p2 && npm run check` pass.

gtk: use GraphicsOffload for background blur lag (#15371)

I was getting mouse and typing lag while running Codex on Intel/Wayland.
I have narrowed this down to background blur, even with a fully opaque
background. The minimal config is:

```ini
background-blur = 32
```

Without blur, mouse movement and typing are smooth. Enabling blur again
brings the lag back.

My setup is CachyOS (Linux 7.3.5), MangoWM 0.18.6 on Wayland, Intel
Raptor Lake integrated graphics with Mesa 26.3.1, GTK 4.24.1, and
libadwaita 1.10.0. The screen is 2560×1600 at 240 Hz with 1.625×
scaling. The laptop also has an RTX 4090 Laptop GPU but I'm using the
iGPU for Ghostty.

This patch wraps the terminal's render surface in `GtkGraphicsOffload`
to improve responsiveness with blur enabled.

Measured latency on my system went from around 105–133 ms to 62–70 ms
with an opaque background, and the mouse stopped lagging.

This has only been tested on my laptop, including the container and
headless sessions. These checks passed:

- Intel and NVIDIA on Wayland, plus X11 with software GL and Cairo:
keyboard, mouse reporting, resize, tabs, splits, and search focus.
- Transparency reloads and opaque background colors, including padding,
matched the original rendering.
- Headless Weston rendering at scales 1 and 2 with GL and Cairo.
- Builds with GTK 4.18.6 and 4.24.1, all 121 selected GTK tests, and
formatting checks.

Codex with GPT6.2-Sol Extra High thinking wrote the patch and ran the
checks, with my feedback.

commits.message:
[CONNEX] Add gateway for Dimplex Connex heaters (nRF24L01) (#2430)

* Add Connex gateway for Dimplex Connex heaters (nRF24L01)

- gatewayCONNEX / config_CONNEX: passive RX of wall controller frames,
  controller ID learn, per-zone setpoint TX bursts, HA climate discovery
- esp32dev-connex environment (RF24 + BME280)
- BME280_I2C_ADDR can be overridden at build time

CONNEX: announce only zones that have been used

A zone gets its Home Assistant climate entity once it has a last setpoint
(paired, commanded or heard from the wall controller); the entity is
announced on first use. Zones never used have their entity removed with an
empty retained config, and erase clears the zones and removes all of them.

docs: add Dimplex Connex gateway setup page

Wiring with pin build flags, firmware, learning an existing wall controller,
pairing heaters, setting temperatures, what the gateway can and can't know,
configuration commands and build flags. Linked under Hardware setup.

CONNEX: single status topic, last setpoints, power and burst options

- Publish everything on one retained CONNEXtoMQTT/gateway topic; drop the
  per-zone topics. The status lists each zone's last setpoint (sent or heard
  from the wall controller) with frames sent/acked and age in seconds.
- Save last setpoints to NVS; after a reboot they are reported with
  "restored":true and "age":null, and are not resent.
- Age uses the core uptime(); no NTP in the module.
- Configurable transmit power: CONNEX_PA_LEVEL / {"power":"min|low|high|max"}.
- End a burst after CONNEX_BURST_ACKS (default 10) acked frames;
  {"acks":n}, 0 sends the full burst.
- Home Assistant climate discovery reads zone setpoints from the gateway
  status. Configs trimmed (device ids only, default availability payloads)
  so they fit the publish queue's re-parse buffer and are no longer dropped.
- erase also clears saved setpoints.
- Harness: default base topic home/OpenMQTTGateway, power and acks options,
  zone checks read the gateway status, test restores zone 1 afterwards.

CONNEX: two-byte setpoint, 0-30 C range

The setpoint is 16-bit big-endian tenths of a degree in frame bytes 5-6.
The wall controller never went above 25.5 C, so byte 5 was always 0x00.
Heaters were tested to follow 0, 26 and 30 C, matching their own controls.

- encode/decode the setpoint as two bytes (TX, RX and frame validation)
- default range 0.0-30.0 C; CONNEX_MIN_TEMP / CONNEX_MAX_TEMP overridable
- harness test: reject 30.5 and -1 C, send 26 and 30 C for a display check

CONNEX: make minimum setpoint a build flag

CONNEX_MIN_TEMP can now be overridden at build time (default stays 5.0 C),
and encodeSetpoint() uses it instead of a hard-coded 50 (5.0 C) floor.
Testing showed the heaters accept setpoints down to 0 C.

CONNEX: fix set commands routed to setpoint handler

cmpToMainTopic is a prefix match, so MQTTtoCONNEXset also matched
MQTTtoCONNEX and every set command (learn, pair, id, ...) was dropped.

CONNEX: add MQTT test harness script

CONNEX: add pair command

Generates and saves a controller ID if none is set, then sends a setpoint
frame for the heater in sync mode to adopt.

esp32dev-connex: add BH1750, 115200 upload, OTA env
Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

* [CONNEX] Fix erase, round setpoints to 0.5 C, accept zone as string

- erase now also clears the controller ID and settings in RAM (after
  removing the zone climate entities), cancels learn and restores the
  default transmit power
- setpoints are rounded to CONNEX_TEMP_STEP (0.5 C) for commands and pairing
- "zone" and "pair" accept numeric strings ("1") as well as numbers

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

* [CONNEX] Apply clang-format

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

* [CONNEX] Address review: input validation, failed bursts, radio retry

- Reject null, boolean and non-numeric temperatures (setpoint and pair)
  instead of reading them as 0 C
- An unacked burst keeps the zone's known setpoint and is reported as
  status "failed" with failed_setpoint
- Reject commands while the radio is down and retry radio init every 30 s
- Rejected commands publish a non-retained state with an "error" field
- erase/init cancel the active burst, pending setpoints and learn mode;

Let Companion.spawn_tcp_server set the companion's debugserver port

Summary:
`idb_companion` takes `--debug-port`, the port the debugserver it starts for `idb debugserver start` listens on, and uses 10881 without it. `Companion.spawn_tcp_server` had no way to set it, so every companion launched through it uses 10881, and two companions on one host that both start a debugserver want the same port.

`spawn_tcp_server` now takes an optional `debug_port` and passes `--debug-port <debug_port>` when it is set. When it is not set the command line is unchanged.

An older companion that predates `--debug-port` ignores unknown arguments, so it keeps listening on 10881.

commits.message:
[gym][scan][snapshot] Make disallow_xcodebuild_settings_lookup work end to end (#30379)

* [gym] Archive and export without build settings when the destination names the platform

Fixes #30365. With `disallow_xcodebuild_settings_lookup` on, an iOS archive
could not finish. After `xcodebuild archive`, `Gym::Runner#run` called
`building_for_ipa?`, which always read `SUPPORTS_MACCATALYST`, and then
`watchos?`, and no option avoided either. With the issue's own options gym
stopped even earlier, on the app name used for the log file.

- The platform checks answer from the configuration first. A destination
  that names an iOS, tvOS, watchOS or visionOS platform, in any case as
  xcodebuild accepts, with no `sdk` or `catalyst_platform` for macOS, rules
  out a macOS build. Anything else falls through to the project as before.
- The Mac Catalyst checks test `catalyst_platform`/`sdk` before asking if the
  project supports Mac Catalyst. The results are the same, and the
  provisioning profile mapping no longer fails at setup.
- The `watchos?` check moves into the opt-in generic archive fix it guards.
  When build settings can't be read, it goes by the destination.
- Without build settings, the log file is named after `output_name`, which
  is always set by then, instead of failing when `app_name` isn't set.
- Values that can't be avoided fail at setup, before the archive, and the
  error names the option to set: `destination`, `output_name`,
  `configuration`. A macOS export needs build settings to tell an app from a
  command-line tool, so it fails at setup too, unless `skip_archive` is set.
- Installer certificates only sign macOS packages. They aren't looked for
  without build settings, and installerSigningCertificate is only written
  for a package export.

In fastlane_core, `xcodebuild_settings_lookup_disallowed_by` is now public,
so callers can check it before a lookup they can do without. The new
`verify_xcodebuild_settings_lookup_allowed!` raises the lookup error naming
the option that replaces the value. This follows the pattern gym already
uses of checking the configuration before the project, rather than adding a
keyword to `build_settings`.

With the option off, results change in three cases only. A macOS-only
project given an iOS-family destination, which xcodebuild can't archive,
now reads as IPA. `building_for_ios?` is true for an iOS-family destination,
so `generate_appstore_info` also runs for a multiplatform project exported
without an `sdk`, as it already does for a single-platform one. And an IPA's
export options no longer include installerSigningCertificate, whose
selectors are Mac-only.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

* [gym] Report the build failure when the SDK can't be read for it

When a build or export fails, gym prints a summary of the build environment,
including the SDK, before raising the failure. Reading the SDK fetches the
project's build settings. With `disallow_xcodebuild_settings_lookup` on, that
raised the lookup error, so a failed archive was reported as a missing
SDKROOT build setting, telling the user to set an option that doesn't exist,
instead of as the build failure. A `-showBuildSettings` timeout at that point
replaced the failure the same way.

The summary now leaves the SDK out when it can't be read, and the failure is
raised as before. A local `rescue` fits here, unlike at call sites that can
act on the error: the summary is best-effort, and any error reading it would
otherwise hide the one that matters.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

* [scan] Test without build settings when the device or destination is given

With `disallow_xcodebuild_settings_lookup` on, scan only worked with `device`
or `devices`, and even then it read build settings for a deployment target
under an empty key. With `destination` alone it failed at setup, picking a
default simulator from the project's supported platforms that it didn't
need. Names derived from the app name failed after the tests had run.

- With `device`/`devices`, there is no deployment target to read, so the
  empty key isn't looked up. That also saves a `-showBuildSettings` run with
  the option off.
- With `destination` alone, no default simulator is picked, as for a Mac or
  Swift package target. The options that act on the simulators scan picks
  (`reset_simulator`, `reinstall_app`, `prelaunch_simulator`,
  `include_simulator_logs`) then fail at setup, asking for `device` or
  `devices`. Before, two of them crashed and two did nothing.
- Lookups that can't be avoided fail at setup and name the option to set:
  `device`, `devices` or `destination`, `derived_data_path`, and
  `destination` for a Mac Catalyst build.
- Without build settings, the log file and the Slack message are named after
  the scheme, as they are for a Swift package, unless `app_name` is set.

Builds on the fastlane_core helpers from the gym change for #30365.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

* [snapshot] Take screenshots without build settings when devices are given

With `disallow_xcodebuild_settings_lookup` on, snapshot couldn't run at all.
Every log file name started with the project's app name, read from the
build settings, before the first xcodebuild ran. Unlike gym and scan,
snapshot has no `app_name` option to provide it.

Without build settings, the log files are now named after the scheme
alone, as scan names a Swift package's. That avoids a new option for a
log file name. When `devices` isn't set, picking the default devices still
reads the build settings, and that error now names `devices`.

Builds on the fastlane_core helpers from the gym change for #30365.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

* [gym][scan] Skip the new specs that need Xcode where it isn't installed

The ubuntu CI job failed with "Unable to locate Xcode" and "No such file or
directory - xcrun". scan's setup reads the Xcode version and the default
simulator OS version, and gym's export options generator reads the Xcode
version, so these examples can't run without Xcode. Tag them with
`requires_xcode`, as the existing specs for the same code are, so they are
skipped there and still run on macOS.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

* [scan] Clear the simulators an earlier run picked when only the destination is given

`Scan.devices` lives on the module and is only set when scan picks
simulators. When build setting lookups are disallowed and only
`destination` is given, scan skips picking them, so a second `run_tests`
in the same lane kept the first run's simulators. `Runner#test_app` then
applied `disable_slide_to_type`, which is on by default, to a simulator
the run doesn't test on. Clear them on that path.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

* [scan] Don't reuse the project or simulators found by an earlier run

`Scan.project` and `Scan.devices` are kept on the module, and setup only
sets them when a run has them. Several `run_tests` calls in one lane share
them, so a run that needs neither kept the previous run's values:

- A macOS project tested after an iOS run got the previous simulator as
  its destination (`platform=iOS Simulator,id=...`) instead of
  `platform=macOS`, and the runner applied `disable_slide_to_type`, on by
  default, and the other simulator options to that simulator.
- A Swift package (`package_path`) tested after an Xcode project run kept
  that project. Setup then read the old project's build settings to pick
  simulators and to find the derived data path.

Setup now starts each run without them.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

* [fastlane_core][gym][scan][snapshot] Share the app name fallback, and fix review nits

Review feedback on the branch:

- gym's log name, scan's log name and Slack message, and snapshot's log
  names each repeated "the project's app name, unless build settings can't
  be read" in a slightly different way. `Project#app_name_if_lookup_allowed`
  now returns the app name, or nil when the lookup is disallowed, and each
  tool keeps its own fallback: `output_name` in gym, the scheme in scan and
  snapshot. snapshot's own helper for this is gone.
- scan's Slack message no longer crashes for a Swift package. There is no
  project then, and with `slack_url` set and no `app_name` the message read
  the app name from nil, as it does on master. It now names the scheme, as
  the log file does.
- The `Scan.devices = nil` in scan's destination-only path is gone. Setup
  now clears it at the start of every run.
- When several options can replace a lookup, the error now says "set one of
  the `device`, `devices` or `destination` options".

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

* [fastlane_core][gym][snapshot] Comment the less obvious parts of the build settings guard

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

* [gym][scan] Keep more of the environment out of the new specs, and cover destination with devices

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

* [gym][scan][snapshot] Use the same description for disallow_xcodebuild_settings_lookup

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

* [scan][snapshot] Clear the workspace and lookup switches in the new specs

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

* [scan] Don't crash on reinstall_app or include_simulator_logs without simulators

A Swift package, or a project that doesn't test on a simulator, leaves
Scan.devices nil, and both options called `each` on it. They now skip like
reset_simulator, disable_slide_to_type and prelaunch_simulator already do.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

* [gym] Check the installer certificate search through the security gem

gym now searches with Security::Certificate.find (#30309), so the spec's

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

* [spec] Clear every option's environment variable in the new specs

Listing the variables one by one kept missing some, so the specs now clear
everything a tool's options read, with a FastlaneSpec::Env helper, and list
only the variables read outside the options.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

* [gym] Report the packaging failure when the build log can't be named

When only exporting with `output_name` given, naming the build log is the
first build settings lookup, and a timeout there replaced the packaging
error being reported.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

* [spec] Drop with_option_env_values_cleared now that the suite unsets option variables

#30632 unsets every variable an option reads before the first example, so the
new specs only clear the two variables read outside the options.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

* [spec] Clear the global build settings lookup switch in specs that read build settings

FASTLANE_DISALLOW_XCODEBUILD_SETTINGS_LOOKUP isn't an option's variable, so
the suite leaves it set, and with it exported 226 examples in 17 files failed.
Each of those files now clears it, which makes the PR's narrower hooks in

mfdes: align storage size in dump view

PM5 FPGA: command SPI set up once, not before every command

FpgaSendCommand() set up SPI3 again before every command: clock, four
pins and peripheral, about 19 us each time. Because of it, hf 14a sim
answered late and hf 14a reader sent its SELECT and listened for
answers 256 carrier periods late. SPI3 is now set up once, and again
after the FPGA JTAG, which shares its pins, has used them.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

fileutils: add generic saveFileVCD() helper

Lets any feature write a VCD waveform file through one entry point,
same pattern as saveFileEx()/saveFileWAVE()/saveFilePM3(). Takes a
generic (timestamp, channel, 8-bit value) sample array and channel
names, not a feature-specific struct.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Sonnet 5 <noreply@anthropic.com>
Claude-Session: https://claude.ai/code/session_01EmXoNJg9UMjcCdM48wNwqo

hf 14a info: SAK 20 with a non-NXP UID is not MIFARE Classic

Double/triple UIDs outside the NXP, ST and Infineon ranges default to
MIFARE Classic. SAK 0x20 has bit 3 clear, so it can't be one. A JCOP
like card (UID 3F 10 00 03 29 CE 55) got the `hf mf info` hint, the
Classic magic, static nonce and PRNG probes, and `hf search -v` on PM5
ran `hf mf info` on it.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

hf 14a magic ident: 10 ms field resets instead of 90 ms

mf_reset_card() kept the field off for 40 ms and iso14443a_setup()
then waited 50 ms after switching it back on. Use 10 ms for each, twice
the ISO14443-3 minimums (5.1 ms reset, 5 ms guard time), through a new
iso14443a_setup_ex() with a settle time. The first setup in
MifareCIdent() follows a dropped field as well and gets the same 10 ms.
Magic ident on an Ultralight 371 -> ~130 ms on RDV4 and PM5. The
MIFARE Classic path does 7 resets and saves more.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

graph: temporary markers, uint32_t count and NUL-terminated labels

g_TempMarkerSize was uint8_t: the 256th marker wrapped it to 0, so the
next add calloc'd a fresh array and leaked the old one. A 30+ char
label was strncpy'd into label[30] without a terminator, which
draw_marker() then read past.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

lf sniff: reply timeout follows the capture time

Same fixed 2.5 s wait as `lf read` had, so a plain `lf sniff` on PM5
always timed out. Use the shared capture time helper, renamed to
lf_capture_timeout_ms(), and say lf_sniff in the timeout message.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

lf read: reply timeout follows the capture time

A plain `lf read` fills the whole BigBuf. On PM5 that is 395700
samples, ~3.2 s at 125 kHz, longer than the fixed 2.5 s wait, so the
client always reported a timeout and 0 samples while the device still
finished. Wait 2.5 s plus the capture time from the sample config
(samples, bits per sample, decimation, skip, divisor).

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

Merge pull request #3935 from matrix/fix-i2c-read-result

I2C: a timed-out read no longer counts as a success

fpga: bit-bang the bitstream from RAM

Flash wait states dominated the loop. Send each run of bytes from a
RAMFUNC (208 bytes of RAM). RDV4 bit-bang ~127 -> ~80 ms per bitstream
swap. A single PIO_ODSR store for DIN and CCLK gained only ~4 ms more
and was left out.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

gpio: plain writes to the AT91 PIO set/clear registers

PIO_SODR/PIO_CODR are write-only and only act on the bits written as 1,
so other pins are never touched. The |= added a useless volatile read
to every pin change. FPGA bitstream bit-bang on RDV4 ~290 -> ~140 ms.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

fpga: 1 ms PROGRAM pulse, power-up wait only on the first download

Spartan-II/3E need 300/500 ns on PROGRAM, and INIT is polled after
release anyway (high ~4 us after a 1 ms pulse on RDV4). FPGA power is
never switched off, so the 50 ms power-up wait is only needed once.
Saves ~100 ms per bitstream swap.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

fpga: skip the other interleaved bitstreams a block at a time

The combined image interleaves all bitstreams in 288 byte chunks. Each
byte read ran a software division and modulo to find its chunk and
skipped foreign bytes one call at a time. Track the chunk position with
counters, skip foreign chunks by moving the ring buffer pointer and
send contiguous runs straight to the FPGA. RDV4 bitstream download
1339 -> ~520 ms.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

I2C: a timed-out read no longer counts as a success

I2C_BufferRead() and I2C_AdaptiveRead() return -1 or -2 when SCL
times out. Five PM5 callers stored the result in a bool, and the RDV4
SIM module version read in a uint8_t, so a timeout counted as a good
read (CEP attach, hw qc_pm5, hw ant_pm5, hw factorydata, hw status on
an RDV4). They now test > 0, as bwm_charger.c does, or use an
int16_t; the 28 bool calls in at32_unit_test.c test > 0 too.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

hf iclass/seos/mf/mfdes sam -v: accept one more HID SAM ATR

With -v these commands check the SAM ATR against the list of
IsHIDSamPresent() and stop with "Not detecting a SAM" when it is not
there. A HID SAM answering 3B 95 97 80 11 FC 47 72 61 63 65 3D was
refused; the ATR is now in the list.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

PM5 USB: clear DIEPTSIZ on discard, macro argument lacked parentheses

4e95850ee made async_usb_write_discard() clear DIEPTSIZ, passing
`USBD_CDC_BULK_IN_EPT & 0x7F` as the endpoint number of USB_INEPT().
The macro multiplies its argument without parentheses around it, so
the zero went to address 0x00000990 and DIEPTSIZ kept its value. The
CMake build of the PM5 firmware stopped on that line with
-Werror=parentheses. The argument is now in parentheses, as in the
other three uses of USB_INEPT() in the file.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Mythos 5.2 <noreply@anthropic.com>

trace list -t iclass: CHECK SUCCESS only on the card MAC

After a CHECK the lister labelled the next tag frame CHECK SUCCESS,
whatever it was. When the card did not answer the CHECK, the answer
to the following READ or READ4 got the label. READ, IDENTIFY and
READ4 now end the CHECK state, and only the 4-byte card MAC that
answers the CHECK is labelled. A pm3_tests.sh test checks that label
in traces/hf_iclass_sniff.trace.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

hf iclass sim: CRC check, PAGESEL page bound

The simulation answered READ, READ4, UPDATE and PAGESEL whatever
their CRC, and wrote a damaged UPDATE to the emulator memory. A real
PicoPass 2K drops a READ4 with a wrong CRC, as ISO/IEC 15693-3 asks
of every request. The four frames are now dropped when their CRC is
wrong.

In non-secure mode PAGESEL took any page number, so READ4 and UPDATE
then worked past the emulator memory. It now takes only the pages
the card has, as in secure mode.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

hf 14a simaid, hf seos/secc/mfdes sim: ISO/IEC 14443-4 fixes

An Elatec TWN4 reported none of these simulations. It deselects the
card after its SELECTs and activates it again with WUPA: simaid and
seos ended there, secc did not answer S(DESELECT), mfdes ignored the
WUPA. The TWN4, a HID OMNIKEY 5427CK and an ACR122U check with
R(NAK) that the card is still there: simaid, seos and secc did not
answer, mfdes left out the CID.

The four simulations now answer S(DESELECT), WUPA and R-blocks as
ISO/IEC 14443-3 and 14443-4 say, with the R-block and PPS code of
hf 14a sim. simaid and seos no longer end at an HLTA either.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

fix(message): ignore the pre-release part in the version handshake (#4342)

* fix(message): ignore the pre-release part in the version handshake

`versions_compatible` turned each side's version into a caret
`VersionReq`, and semver only lets a requirement match a pre-release of
its own `major.minor.patch`. So `1.2.0-rc.1` and `1.1.0` rejected each
other at node register, daemon register and the CLI `Hello`, although
both speak the 1.x protocol: an rc CLI could not run a node built
against the stable `dora-node-api` or the stable `dora-rs` wheel, which
pip and cargo pick by default.

Compare the `major.minor.patch` parts only. A 1.1 component still
rejects an rc peer when it is the side doing the check, since its own
code is unchanged.

Pokopia: enable NVN_DIRTY_SPLIT so overlapping memory pools stay tracked

Pokopia 2.0.1 registers a texture pool whose first page overlaps an
already-tracked range. With NVN_DIRTY_SPLIT disabled, nvn_dirty_add_range()
declines the whole overlapping pool, leaving every texture in it untracked:
the same static BC texture is re-uploaded on every submission (~170 MB/frame).

nvn_dirty.c already documents this failure mode for BOTW, AOCX, P5R and OOT
and ships the split-range fix; GAME_POKOPIA was simply missing from the
enable list. This one-line change adds it.

Measured on the same save/route: re-uploads 16.00 -> 1.00 per frame (-93.75%),
Output FPS 28.5 -> 55.89 with frame interpolation off, peak footprint -3.0 GiB.
Image quality unchanged; dynamic textures still re-upload (~1/frame).

  compose, which the twin writes as literals; another layout is refused, not given a different saturation.

commits.message:
Report a desynced pair outside the repo instead of crashing (#1195)

check_notebook_pair_sync.py accepts paths, so the natural way to reproduce a CI
pair-sync failure is to extract a PR head into a scratch directory and check it
there. Doing that found the desync, then died in the reporting loop on
`nb.relative_to(REPO_ROOT)`, printing a traceback where the gate had already
computed the answer.

The gate itself was never wrong - every path it sees in CI and in pre-commit is
inside the repo. It just could not say what it found when handed one that was not.

Compound the simulated path in Monte Carlo VaR instead of summing it (#1194)

* Compound the simulated path in Monte Carlo VaR instead of summing it

Returns in 01_var_cvar are simple (close/close.shift(1) - 1), so a path over
`horizon` days accumulates as prod(1 + r) - 1. `monte_carlo_var` summed the
daily draws instead, which is the log-return convention applied to simple
returns. Reported as #1192.

The two conventions agree to rounding at one day and diverge as the horizon
grows: on the SPY sample, the 95% figure goes 3.861% -> 3.863% at five days.
A fitted Student-t is unbounded below, so compounding also has to respect the
-100% floor on a simple return; the sampler now refuses its own invalid draws,
the same commitment 06_stress_testing makes for its 20-day horizon. On this
data a t fitted with df=2.39 does produce such a draw past about ten days, and
the error says so and names the alternative.

No published value moves. The notebook calls `monte_carlo_var` only at
horizon=1, where prod(1 + r) - 1 and sum(r) differ in the sixteenth
significant digit:

  90%  1.0549359940998295 -> 1.0549359940998317
  95%  1.6462944383025744 -> 1.6462944383025722
  99%  3.7499640439519624 -> 3.749964043951958

Figure 19.2 and var_method_comparison.parquet are unchanged at every precision
a reader sees. Re-executed because source that computes changed, not because a
result did.

Two of the three new tests fail on the summing implementation. The multi-period
one asserts what only compounding can satisfy: a long-only wealth path cannot
lose more than the capital committed, and summing reports a 216% loss over 100
days. The third exists to catch the opposite error, a support guard aggressive
enough to reject the notebook's own one-day call.

* Say the support bound in words, not as a numeral

The guards job runs check_prose_numerals.py, which is not in the pre-commit
config, so the local hooks passed and CI did not: clause N1/N2 refuses a numeral
typed into notebook prose, and the markdown stated the floor on a simple return
as one. The bound is definitional rather than a result, but the gate reads text,
and 06_stress_testing already states the same commitment in words.

Markdown only, folded in with `notebook_provenance.py sync-prose`. Every output
and the original executed_at are unchanged.

sheet, so changing a copied PivotTable before the next reload failed with

its value fields match by name on reload.

mock_command: add new_command_with_env so compiler children get only the client environment (#3016)

* mock_command: add new_command_with_env for explicit child environments

Every compiler invocation had to remember to call env_clear() before
envs(), and forgetting it silently leaks the server's environment into
the compiler. new_command_with_env does both, and all the call sites
that pass the client's environment now go through it. The few places
that deliberately layer onto the server environment (direct client
compile, compiler/assembler detection) are left alone.

MockCommand now records env, env_clear and current_dir so tests can see
what a command would have run with.

Fixes #95

deps: bump which from 6 to 8

which 8 drops its rustix 0.38, home and winsafe dependencies.

It also resolves relative PATH entries against the cwd passed to
which_in and returns an absolute path. That fixes server-side lookups
(assembler, nvcc) that previously resolved them against the server's
cwd, but broke the argv[0] masquerade check in cmdline.rs, which
removed sccache's own directory by comparing against raw PATH entries.

commits.message:
ci: install pytest directly in tox, not via dev-requirements

tox's -rscripts/dev-requirements.txt pulls in 'pygobject-stubs
--config-settings=config=Gtk3,Gdk3', whose inline option is mishandled
on py310 and leaks --config-settings into pytest's argv, failing the run.
Install pytest>=8.0 directly; dev-requirements still carries the stubs
and tooling for local development.

test: skip fidelity tier when no display is available

Fidelity builds a real KlipperScreen panel against the fakes and asserts
on the resulting widget tree, so it needs a Gdk display connection;
without one GTK3/PyGObject segfaults during widget construction -- a hard
failure on headless CI (ubuntu-latest has no display server).

Skip the whole fidelity tier when no Wayland/X display is reachable,
mirroring the render tier's graceful skip when Weston is absent, so the
suite stays green headless while still validating the fakes wherever a
display exists.

ci: run tests via pytest with pytest installed in tox

The render/fidelity test modules import pytest at collection time, but tox
only installed the install requirements, so 'unittest discover' failed with
ModuleNotFoundError. Switch the runner to pytest (already configured in
pyproject) and install it through dev-requirements.txt.

test: add real-GTK fit tests under headless Weston

Verify panels fit their target resolution when rendered through the real
base-panel (titlebar + action bar + injected panel) under a headless
Weston compositor.

- tests/preview_panel.py: interactive 'open a panel to view it' tool plus a
  --sweep mode driving the faithful build+measure path (real chrome, shipped
  CSS/theme, realistic live data, clean teardown). The 'layout won't fit'
  signal is the host main_grid minimum preferred size vs. resolution.
- tests/render/: 9 passing panels x 6 resolutions x 5 fonts matrix (fits_res);
- tests/render/fit.py: check_fit() clip metric + realize().
- tests/fidelity/: in-process checks that the fakes reflect reality first.
- tests/fakes/runtime.py: thin but faithful fakes.
- tests/conftest.py + tests/render/conftest.py: import/translation setup, a
  session-scoped headless Weston fixture, bounded GLib pump, per-panel summary.

package/pkg-generic.mk: fix <pkg>_OVERRIDE_SRCDIR_RSYNC_EXCLUSIONS for host package

Host packages already default to using <pkg>_OVERRIDE_SRCDIR from the
matching target package. However, this did not apply to
<pkg>_OVERRIDE_SRCDIR_RSYNC_EXCLUSIONS. This meant the host package
might rsync files that should be excluded (typically build artifacts)
to the build directory, and users need to define both
<pkg>_OVERRIDE_SRCDIR_RSYNC_EXCLUSIONS and
HOST_<pkg>_OVERRIDE_SRCDIR_RSYNC_EXCLUSIONS to avoid that.

Fix that, so both <pkg>_OVERRIDE_SRCDIR and
<pkg>_OVERRIDE_SRCDIR_RSYNC_EXCLUSIONS are the same for target and
host package, unless different values are explicitly set for the host
package.

fix(wifi): fix DUT stuck on redundant opmode change during WPS scan

Issuing a redundant esp_wifi_set_mode() while a WPS scan is in progress
made the DUT unresponsive. hostapd_cleanup() runs in the Wi-Fi task
context and called the blocking esp_wifi_ap_wps_disable(), which posts
WPS work to the wpa_supplicant eloop and blocks on s_wps_api_sem. When
the eloop is being torn down this self-deadlocks the Wi-Fi task
(wps_reg_eloop_post_block -> eloop_register_timeout_blocking), leaving
the device stuck.

The WPS type/status globals are shared between the enrollee (STA) and
registrar (AP) paths, so a mode change during an enrollee WPS scan also
corrupted registrar state, causing spurious 802.1x/WPS handling on the
AP side. STA SAE commit used that same status, so an AP registrar
session suppressed the station handshake. Restrict the SAE check to
WPS_OWNER_ENROLLEE.

Free the concatenated WPS IE when PBC overlap rejects an association.
That buffer is not stored on the station.

Co-authored-by: Cursor <cursoragent@cursor.com>

fix(esp32p4): lower MSPI speed during boot CPU freq switch

On ESP32-P4, calibrating CPLL inside rtc_clk_cpu_freq_set_config()

corrupting external memory.

Suspending the external-memory cache around the switch avoided the
corruption, but also blocked Flash XIP (shared L2 cache) and forced
RTC_CLK_FUNC_IN_IRAM to remain permanently enabled on ESP32-P4.

Instead, use the lightweight early-init helpers
mspi_timing_enter_low_speed_early() and mspi_timing_enter_high_speed_early()
around rtc_clk_cpu_freq_set_config() when CONFIG_SPIRAM is enabled.
This switches PSRAM to a fixed 20 MHz clock (supporting CPU frequencies
down to 20 MHz) while keeping external-memory XIP accessible, allowing
RTC_CLK_FUNC_IN_IRAM_ESP32P4 to be removed.

fix(esp_system): reset Wi-Fi and BT modules on ESP32-C2 exit

esp_system_reset_modules_on_exit() only wrote 0 to SYSTEM_CORE_RST_EN_REG,
without first asserting the Wi-Fi / BT reset bits. Every other target pulses
them first (see esp32c3), so on ESP32-C2 a software reset that skips the
esp_wifi_stop() shutdown handler -- for example a Task WDT abort leading to
esp_restart_noos() -- left the Wi-Fi MAC and its RX DMA running. The DMA kept
writing received frames into the previous boot's RX descriptor ring, which by
then belongs to the new boot's heap, corrupting the TLSF free list and
crashing the next wifi init.

C3 resets plus SYSTEM_BTMAC_RST, which ESP32-C2 defines separately.

commits.message:
fix: keep per-query options off the HTTP server-info query (#2125)

* fix: keep per-query options off the HTTP server-info query

Important: Change affects how server timezone is handled. Previously it was set to result of `timezone()` what
returns server or session timezone. Today it is result of `serverTimezone()` that returns configured server timezone. 

The HTTP handshake ran its server-info query with the caller's context, so
per-query settings, the query id, the quota key and parameters were sent on
that internal statement. session_timezone was then stored as the connection
timezone, and settings that change Native encoding made the handshake
response undecodable.

Run the handshake with the caller's cancellation and deadline but with empty
query options. Connection-level settings stay on the connection URL.

Fixes #2123

* fix: keep the per-query JWT on the HTTP handshake

The handshake context dropped every query option, including the JWT.
dial uses the first query's context, so HTTPS with WithJWT and no
connection GetJWT sent the server-info request without Authorization
and the connection failed.

Keep the JWT. Drop settings, parameters, the query id, external tables
and the user location. quota_key is a query parameter and initial_user
is native-only, so those stay off the handshake too.

Fixes #2123

* fix: use serverTimezone() in the HTTP server-info query

* test: align HTTP handshake settings with context deadlines

fix(column): parse Tuple element names that contain a space (#2074)

* fix(column): parse Tuple element names that contain a space

A backquoted element name such as `a b` Int64 was split at its first
space, giving name "`a" and type "b` Int64". When the name is
backquoted, split at the first space after the closing backtick.

Fixes #2073

* fix(column): parse Tuple element names that contain parentheses or commas

The guard that tells a name from an unnamed type such as
Decimal(10, 2) looked for a parenthesis before the first space, so
`price (usd)` Float64 was read as a type. The element split also
counted brackets and commas inside a backquoted name.

Apply the guard only to unquoted names, and do not split inside a
backquoted name that opens an element.

* refactor(column): split Tuple elements with indexTopLevelComma

The Tuple parser carried its own copy of the bracket and quote-aware
comma split. indexTopLevelComma in map.go already handles backquoted
names, quoted strings and backslash escapes, so use it and drop the
name and escape state kept here. The existing Tuple rows pass as
before. Because indexTopLevelComma also skips single-quoted strings,
a parenthesis inside a quoted Enum value no longer ends the element;
a test row covers it.

* refactor(column): read a quoted Tuple name up to its closing quote

splitTupleElement takes a name in backticks or double quotes as the
text between the quotes, unescaped, and the rest of the element as
the type. The second search for a space is gone, so a newline, a tab
or no separator after the closing quote works, and an unquoted name
ends at any whitespace. Inside the quotes a backslash escapes the
next character, and \t, \n, \r, \b, \f and \0 decode to the control
characters the server writes that way.

* fix(column): reuse quoted-parameter parsing in Variant and Nested

Signed-off-by: spicysharkco <321699413+spicysharkco@users.noreply.github.com>

* test(column): cover quoted names across composite types

Signed-off-by: spicysharkco <321699413+spicysharkco@users.noreply.github.com>

Add experimental-firebase-limit to limit Firebase messages per visitor and topic (#2250)

FCM has an undocumented, non-adjustable hourly limit on topic fanout, which ntfy.sh now hits
