commits.message:
fix: refuse a storage key that climbs above the base dir (#907)

ConfineJoin refused keys that started by climbing but clamped ones that
climbed later, so a/../../x resolved to x and named a different object than
the key asked for. Any key whose dot segments climb past the base is now
refused, which is what the comment claimed.

docs: drop the unimplemented HTTPS_ONLY option

The security page documented HTTP_LOADER_HTTPS_ONLY as a way to refuse
plain-HTTP sources, but no such flag exists. Removed from the allowed-sources
section and from the production example.

fix: do not delete a stored object when its save fails (#906)

A failed Put used to be followed by a Delete of the same key, to clean up the
partial object an in-place write could leave. That cleanup is what made the
storages look atomic, so the storages are made atomic instead: GCS abandons
the upload on a short or failed copy rather than committing it, the file
storage refuses a body shorter than its declared size, and a failed Put now
leaves the previous object in place.

fix: write the file storage target atomically (#905)

Put wrote straight to the destination, so a concurrent read of a source being
fetched found a file that was still growing, and libvips filled the missing
scanlines with grey and cached the result. The body is now written to a
dot-prefixed temporary file beside the target and renamed into place, with
SaveErrIfExists using a link so an existing target is never replaced.
build: update go deps

fix: serve only image bytes on raw-on-error, with the sniffed type (#902)

* fix: serve only image bytes on raw-on-error, with the sniffed type

The raw-on-error response wrote the error status before its headers, so the
source type the loader reported decided how the browser read the body: an
attacker's HTML source was served as text/html on the imagor origin with no
CSP, which is the open advisory. The headers now go out first, the body is
only served when the sniffed type is an image, and the type is taken from the
bytes rather than from the loader's claim.

* fix: serve only image bytes on raw-on-error, with the sniffed type

The raw-on-error response wrote the error status before its headers, so the
source type the loader reported decided how the browser read the body: an
attacker's HTML source was served as text/html on the imagor origin with no
CSP. Headers now go out before the status and the response carries the
sandbox policy; the body is refused when its type is markup, including the
XML types an XHTML document hides in, and the type is taken from the bytes
whenever they are a recognised image.

fix: keep storage keys inside the configured base dir (#903)

The S3 and GCS storages joined the key with filepath.Join, so a key such as
../other/photo.jpg, which survives imagorpath.Normalize, resolved outside the
base dir. Both now use imagorpath.ConfineJoin, which refuses a key that names
its way out even when no base dir is set, and a key that resolves to nothing.

fix: block the unspecified NAT64 local-use address (#900)

64:ff9b:1:: is the local-use encoding of 0.0.0.0, but every layout of it reads
as zero, and the all-zero readings were dropped as artifacts of a different
prefix length, so the address passed BlockLoopbackNetworks while 64:ff9b::
was blocked. The address is now read as 0.0.0.0 when no layout yields anything
else.

Reading every layout is deliberate: RFC 6052 says a translator ignores a
non-zero suffix, so gating on a zero suffix let an address such as
64:ff9b:1:a9fe:a9:fe00:808:808 read as 8.8.8.8 instead of 169.254.169.254.

fix: serve the main HEIF image, not its embedded thumbnail (#901)

Moving GIF, AVIF and HEIF to the image route carried options.Thumbnail through
to heifload, which returns the embedded thumbnail when it is set. libvips' own
thumbnail path overrides that setting and only picks the thumbnail when it is
large enough to still be shrunk, so the move silently served the thumbnail for
every larger request: a 2000x2000 HEIC with a 320x320 embedded thumbnail
answered fit-in/1000x1000 with 320x320, and fit-in/3000x3000 with 320x320 too.

The image route now asks for the main image, as the other formats do.

fix: base URL confinement and the raw-on-error panic (#899)

* fix: report a failed source instead of panicking on raw-on-error

The reader was taken after the error status had been written and its error was
dropped, so a source that produced no reader left writeBody with nil: a
recovered panic, a 404 status and a JSON 500 body. The reader is now taken
before the status, and a source with nothing to serve is reported as an error.
A source that does return a body with its error still serves it raw.

* fix: reject a base URL path that climbs out of the base

JoinPath resolves dot segments before the request is made, so with a base URL
that has a path, an image path such as ../../../other.jpg reached a sibling of
the base and was served. The joined path is now checked to stay under the base.

* docs: list the ranges the block flags do not cover

BlockPrivateNetworks follows net.IP.IsPrivate, so carrier-grade NAT, IETF
protocol assignments, benchmarking and reserved space are not covered. The
docs now give the list to pass to HTTP_LOADER_BLOCK_NETWORKS, and mention that
a proxy changes which address the blocks see. Also fix the BLOCK_NETWORKS flag
help, which described the link-local option.

fix: check the declared size before decoding formats without shrink-on-load (#898)

vips_thumbnail_source pre-shrinks or scales only jpeg/uhdr, webp, svg/pdf,
jp2k, tiff and openslide (libvips resample/thumbnail.c). gif, avif and heif
open the full image and are resized afterwards, so the source loader saved
nothing there and the resolution limits were only ever applied to the output:
a 705-byte 4000x4000 avif held 297MB while producing a 10x10 thumbnail.

Those three now go through the image route, which checks the declared
dimensions before the first pixel is read, reading sequentially so memory
matches what the source loader used.

fix: enforce the HTTP loader size limit on the response body (#897)

MAX_ALLOWED_SIZE read the Content-Length of a HEAD answer and nothing else: the
status check beside it could never fire, a missing length read as zero, the GET
body was never limited, and a gzip body was decompressed unbounded. The limit
now applies to the body stream after decompression, and the HEAD length is only
trusted when that answer is successful.

fix: extract embedded IPv4 from the remaining IPv6 transition prefixes (#895)

extractEmbeddedIPv4 recognised the NAT64 well-known prefix, 6to4 and Teredo,
so the network block flags applied to the IPv4 address a translator or tunnel
would reach. The RFC 8215 local-use prefix 64:ff9b:1::/48 was not recognised,
and neither were the deprecated IPv4-translated ::ffff:0:0/96 and
IPv4-compatible ::/96 forms, so the embedded target passed the block checks
untouched.

A translation prefix inside the local-use /48 may be /48, /56, /64 or /96 long
(RFC 6052) and the address does not say which, so every IPv4 it could carry is
extracted and classified.

commits.message:
patch: Continue streams after unsigned Messages thinking (#2563) ## Why Anthropic-compatible providers that send thinking without a signature (#2544) could not be continued or handed off after a mid-stream disconnect. Messages stream recovery treated every `thinking` block, `thinking_delta` and `signature_delta` as signed, so: - any thinking set `unsafe_reason = "signed_thinking"` and recovery stopped, - a completed unsigned block was never cleared from pending reasoning, - a replacement attempt failed with "cannot be combined" as soon as it started its own thinking block, - an empty `signature_delta` marked the delivered prefix `opaque_delta`. Fixes #2550. ## How - `providers/continuation.py`: in the Messages branch of `SourceRecoveryState.observe`, only real protected state is unsafe: `redacted_thinking`, or a non-empty `signature` or `extra_content` on a block start or delta. Stream pieces are not decoded as FCC replay records, because a record can be split across deltas and a readable record would keep the untrimmed thought in a continuation. - It still runs on each raw event as it arrives, so protected state is seen before anything queued behind or beside it is published. - Thinking blocks are tracked as open until `content_block_stop`, signed or not. An open block is reported as `open_thinking`, both in the attempt's own snapshot and in the evidence a local retry inherits for model fallback. - `core/delivered_response.py`: an empty accumulated signature no longer marks the prefix opaque. - Tests cover: - completed unsigned thinking, with and without an empty `signature_delta`, continuing over Messages and Responses wires with both thoughts delivered once - a disconnect inside an open thinking block stopping - a split signature not aborting a healthy stream - a replacement with a readable record failing instead of combining - a tool call not being published before later redacted thinking - citations stopping recovery - a retry keeping earlier open thinking for fallback Accepted tradeoffs: - A thinking block still open at disconnect stops recovery. The signature arrives last, so an open block cannot be shown to be unsigned. - A replacement attempt streams thinking normally and fails with the existing "cannot be combined" error only when protected state actually appears. Nothing is buffered. - A chained FCC upstream that sends a readable replay record as a signature stops recovery, as it did before. - Only shapes real providers send are classified. These are not detected: - an event named only by its SSE `event:` line - invented or typeless delta types - unknown fields such as `encrypted_content` on thinking - malformed `message_start`, block or delta objects Main only caught some of them because it refused all thinking. No handoff test was added. Messages cannot hand off because a tool call only completes at `message_delta`, which already marks the normal stop. 🤖 Generated with [Claude Code](https://claude.com/claude-code)

Confidence Score: 5/5 · The PR appears safe to merge within its stated provider-shape limits.Confidence Score: 5/5

The PR appears safe to merge within its stated provider-shape limits.

Summary

 The PR lets streams continue after a completed unsigned Messages thinking block. Open thinking and non-empty signatures still stop recovery. - Completed unsigned thinking can continue after a stream disconnect. No new actionable issues were found.

Diagram

 ```mermaid %%{init: {'theme': 'neutral'}}%% flowchart TD A[Messages thinking starts] --> B[Track the open block] B --> C{Protected state arrives?} C -->|Yes| D[Stop recovery] C -->|No| E{Block closes before disconnect?} E -->|No| D E -->|Yes| F[Allow continuation after disconnect] F --> G[Remove repeated output] G --> H[Continue one public response] ```

patch: Ignore OpenAI request hints when translating to other protocols (#2562) ## Why OpenAI clients such as OpenCode send `prompt_cache_key` to help OpenAI reuse its prompt cache (#2541). When FCC translated those requests to Gemini or Anthropic Messages, it rejected the field with a 400, so the request never reached the provider. Chat Completions clients hit the same error going to Messages, Responses or Gemini. OpenAI has three sibling fields with the same property: `prompt_cache_retention`, `safety_identifier` and `user`. None of them change the model's answer. ## How - `core/openai_request_hints.py` defines these four fields once as `OPENAI_REQUEST_HINTS`. - Chat ingress, Responses to Gemini and Responses to Messages accept them. Messages and Gemini leave them out of the provider request because they have no equivalent. Every other unknown field is still rejected. - Chat to Responses forwards all four, since Responses supports them. This keeps a client's choice such as `prompt_cache_retention: "in_memory"` instead of falling back to OpenAI's default. - Tests check that Messages and Gemini requests with the hints translate exactly like the same request without them, and that Responses receives every hint. Accepted tradeoffs: - Messages and Gemini have no per-request retention setting, so `prompt_cache_retention` is ignored there and those providers apply their own caching rules. - `safety_identifier` and `user` are not copied into Anthropic `metadata.user_id`. The client gave that identifier to OpenAI, and `user` often holds an email address. - `prompt_cache_options` is still rejected on these paths. It can skip generation (`prewarm`) or depend on per-block breakpoints that FCC does not carry. Fixes #2541. 🤖 Generated with [Claude Code](https://claude.com/claude-code)

Confidence Score: 5/5 · The PR appears safe to merge; no actionable defects were found.Confidence Score: 5/5

The PR appears safe to merge; no actionable defects were found.

Summary

 The PR accepts four OpenAI request hints without rejecting otherwise valid requests. - Messages and Gemini conversions ignore four OpenAI request hints. - Chat Completions conversion forwards all four hints to Responses. No actionable issues were found. Tests were reviewed but not run.

Diagram

 ```mermaid %%{init: {'theme': 'neutral'}}%% flowchart LR A[Chat requests with OpenAI hints] --> B{Destination} C[Responses requests with OpenAI hints] --> D{Destination} B -->|Messages or Gemini| E[Build request without hints] D -->|Messages or Gemini| E B -->|Responses| F[Forward all four hints] ```

Merge pull request #4621 from mikeysklar/dwc2-fs-interrupt-nak-retry

dwc2/hcd: keep a USB keyboard working on ESP32-P4 host

Merge pull request #4603 from emincan2000/msc-host-capacity-wrap

msc host: keep block count at its maximum when last LBA is 0xFFFFFFFF

Merge pull request #4591 from hathach/osal-none-fast-queue

osal_none: fixed-item queue with a lock-free reader

osal_none: the queue reader masks the interrupt on multi-core MCUs

With OSAL_MUTEX_REQUIRED (OPT_OS_NONE on an MCU with TUP_MCU_MULTIPLE_CORE, e.g. RP2040 built without OPT_OS_PICO) the reader takes the writers' interrupt mask, as this queue always did before the lock-free reader: its publish order has no memory barrier. The mask acts on the calling core only, so the USB ISR and the task must still share a core; the queue comment says so. Single-core builds keep the lock-free reader.

test_osal_none_queue_mc runs the queue tests again with TUP_MCU_MULTIPLE_CORE=1 and checks the reader's mask/unmask pair.

dcd: dcd_event_bus_signal() zeroes the SOF frame count

DCDs without a frame counter (ci_fs, musb, samx7x, ...) report
DCD_EVENT_SOF through dcd_event_bus_signal(), which set only rhport and
event_id, and usbd's SOF case reads sof.frame_count. GCC 14.2 with LTO
flagged it on frdm_mcxa153 (make, -Werror=maybe-uninitialized) once
queue_event() moved out of line. Those DCDs now report frame 0.

Only an SOF event stores the count: eid is a constant at almost every
call site, so the others cost nothing (clearing the whole event at each
inlined call site added 16..148 B per DCD).

dwc2/hcd: keep a USB keyboard working on ESP32-P4 host

After a NAK halt the core can leave HCTSIZ.DoPing set. The bInterval=1
retry re-enables the channel without rewriting HCTSIZ, so an interrupt IN
channel goes out with DoPing set and is never serviced again: HCCHAR stays
enabled, HCINT stays 0 and GINTSTS reports an incomplete periodic transfer.

Seen on an ESP32-P4 (buffer DMA) with a full-speed keyboard on the
high-speed root port. Clearing DoPing keeps the immediate retry.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

commits.message:
perf(settings): search results are worked out once per query, after typing pauses

Each keystroke in Settings search matched every terminal setting, and
parsed every shortcut in use, twice (once to decide whether anything
matched, once to draw it), and again on every redraw. The results are now a
value, TerminalSettingsSearch, made once per query; Settings keeps it in
state and makes the next one 150 ms after the query stops changing (the
first query shows at once).

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

perf(terminal): installed fonts and themes load off the main actor at launch

The first visit to a terminal settings page read every installed font
through CoreText and decoded and sorted 633 themes on the main thread
(100-300 ms on a Mac with many fonts). Both are now static lets that a
utility task asks for at launch; a page that gets there first only waits
for the one setup in progress. Fonts are indexed by family, so a family's
faces and whether it is monospaced are a lookup, not a scan of every face.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

perf(terminal): applying a setting validates it once, in the shared terminal configuration

Each apply built up to two throwaway TerminalControllers, a whole Ghostty
app and config each, only to check the light and dark renderings, then had
setTheme load the configuration again. setTheme already validates and keeps
the old configuration when Ghostty reports a problem, and the two
appearances differ only in theme colors, so its check is the only one
needed. A slider drag applies about four times a second; this removes two
Ghostty config loads from each.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

feat(terminal): Import from Ghostty… takes the options Rayon's terminal uses from Ghostty's configuration

With the settings no longer a Ghostty-syntax file, people who set up
Ghostty.app first need a way to bring that setup over. The Mac's terminal
settings tools read Ghostty's own config files (XDG config home, then
Application Support, as Ghostty reads them), set the catalog options they
name as one undoable change, and say which options were skipped because
Rayon's terminal does not use them.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

refactor(terminal): terminal settings are Rayon data, saved as JSON, not a config.ghostty file

The settings are now each Ghostty option's values by key, kept in memory as
a dictionary and saved as terminal-settings.json in Application Support.
libghostty gets config text rendered from them when they are applied, and
the file is written off the main actor, each save after the one before. No UI
ever showed config.ghostty, and sync already treated the settings as
key/value data, so the file was only weight: a comment-preserving line
editor, an outside-edit watcher, an unreadable-file path that sync had to
guard against, and a migration from the UserDefaults blob before it.

On the first launch after the update, an existing config.ghostty is read
once into the settings, with its time as theirs so sync still weighs them
by when they were made, and then removed. Options not in the catalog (the
ones Rayon's terminal does not use, among them those pruned from Settings)
are dropped. New preference backups carry the settings as JSON; a backup
that holds config.ghostty text still restores.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

perf(settings): sidebar badges are counted once when the set keys change

Each sidebar row counted its category's set keys on every redraw, and
read the config to do it, so every change (each slider step) redrew
every row of the sidebar. TerminalSettings now keeps the counts
per category, recounts them only when the set of keys in the file
changes, and publishes them only when a count differs. A row reads only
its count, so a value change no longer touches the sidebar.

Measured in rayon-qa, as in the previous commits. With the parse index
in place a recount is cheap, so the gain is within the bench's noise. In
two runs, median busy ms of one font-size change (n=5), before -> after:
  Text 63/56 -> 57/59, Colors 24/25 -> 37/24, Cursor 13/13 -> 25/14,
  Window 10/9 -> 13/11, Keyboard 18/19 -> 20/24.
Page switches, median busy ms: Colors 285 -> 275, Keyboard 198 -> 186,
Advanced 126 -> 125.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

perf(terminal): config.ghostty is parsed once per change, not on every read

Every row reads its key through values(_:), isSet(_:) or value(_:), and each
call parsed every line of the file. A config after a shortcut edit holds
about 70 keybind lines, so one redraw parsed the file hundreds of times,
and the sidebar's badges added one parse per known key on every change.
The text now keeps a key-to-values index, rebuilt once whenever its lines
change; set(_:_:) assigns the lines once, so it rebuilds it once. The set
of keys main keeps for the badges is now read from the same index.

Measured in rayon-qa with the 88-line seeded config. In-app bench, median
main-thread busy ms of one font-size change inside the apply debounce
(n=5), before -> after:
  Text 81 -> 63, Colors 57 -> 24, Cursor 48 -> 13, Window 46 -> 10,
  Mouse & Clipboard 35 -> 16, Keyboard 37 -> 18, Advanced 35 -> 13.
Page switches, median busy ms: Text 365 -> 344, Colors 301 -> 285,
Mouse & Clipboard 194 -> 168. GhosttyConfigText frames in the click
samples: Colors 35 -> 0, Text 11 -> 0.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

perf(settings): one terminal preview outlives page switches

Each terminal page made its own preview inside the page, under
`.id(selected)`, so every switch between Text, Colors, Cursor, Window,
Mouse & Clipboard and Advanced tore down a Ghostty surface and made a new
one (makeNSView, TerminalController.createSurface, ghostty_surface_new).
The preview now sits around the page switch, in Settings and in the
package's own shell, and holds one terminal from its first showing. The
page keeps its id, so a new page starts at its top; its rows are all new
either way, and dropping the id measured no faster.

Measured in rayon-qa, as in the previous commit. Main-thread samples of
ghostty_surface_new per page visit: Text 3 -> 0, Colors 1 -> 0,
Cursor 1 -> 0, Window 1 -> 0. In-app bench, median busy ms per page switch
(n=5), before -> after:
  Text 387 -> 365, Colors 328 -> 301, Cursor 163 -> 141,
  Window 129 -> 112, Advanced 149 -> 133, About 92 -> 84.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

perf(settings): the terminal settings issue floats over the page instead of insetting it

The issue bar was a safeAreaInset around all of Settings. To place an inset
SwiftUI asks the content for its minimum length, and a grouped Form answers
by measuring every row. Samples of each page switch showed that measuring
under InsetViewLayout.primaryMinimum. As an overlay the bar takes no space

fix(ssh): a cancelled forward returns without waiting for its connection to close

untilClosed raced the forward against the connection's closeFuture in a
task group. Waiting on a future ignores cancellation and a group waits for
all its tasks, so stopping a forward left runForward and runRemoteForward
blocked until the connection itself closed: the port-forward round never
released its lease, which kept the pooled connection open.

The live test mirrors QA's crash: -L and -D clients connect through a
frozen server and hang up, the forwards are stopped and awaited, the
server thaws and a new forward on the same connection carries data. It
crashed on the late channel confirmations before the openChannel fix.

fix(ssh): a forward's waiting connections are bare channels until they are bridged

The -L listener and the -R forward wrapped each connection in a
NIOAsyncChannel as soon as it arrived. A channel lets go of the async
channel's writer once it is active, so a wrapper still waiting in the
listener's queue or the remote forward's stream when either ended was
dropped unfinished and tripped NIO's "Deinited NIOAsyncWriter" precondition.
It happened whenever signing in failed after a client had connected to a
-L port (the listener listens first), the case QA hit with a paused jump
host.

Waiting connections are now held as bare channels that read nothing; they
become async channels only when bridged, after which the pipeline keeps the
writer. Closing a listener closes the connections it took. A SOCKS client
that leaves after its channel opened finishes that channel instead of
dropping it.

fix(ssh): a channel confirmed after it was given up on is closed without an async channel

openChannel ran its setup, which wraps the child in a NIOAsyncChannel, in
the child's initializer, before the server confirms. When the open timed
out or its task was cancelled (a frozen jump host, a curl that gave up) and
the server confirmed later, the child channel took the writer's last
reference off on activation and the unused NIOAsyncChannel was dropped
unfinished: NIO's "Deinited NIOAsyncWriter without calling finish()"
precondition, which crashes Release builds too.

The handlers are still added in the initializer, but the result is now
made only once the server confirms and only while the open is still
wanted; a late channel is closed instead. A wrapper made after activation
is kept by the channel's pipeline until it closes, so even an unused one
can no longer trip the check.

The live test freezes the server, times out and cancels channel opens,
then thaws it; it crashed in debug and release before this change.

fix(forward): a local or SOCKS forward listens before signing in, and says when its port is taken

A forward listening on this side signed in first and only then tried to
listen. With its port taken by another program it failed, waited three
seconds and signed in again, for as long as the switch stayed on: a
connection and a sign-in every three seconds, and the row only said the
forward had ended. SSHForwardListener now binds the port before the
round leases a connection; a port in use ends the round as "Port in
use" without signing in, and the next round only tries to listen again.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

fix(ssh): leases waiting on a connect that fails share its failure

A lease that found the server's connection still connecting waited for
it before counting itself. When the connect failed, the lease that had
started it could resume first (a terminal at a higher priority than a
forward reconnecting in the background), see itself as the last one and
drop the entry; the waiting leases then connected again, and asked about
the host key a second time. The lease is now counted before waiting.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

fix(terminal): the local terminal never blocks on input and closes its descriptor last

Typed input was written in a loop that retried every millisecond until
the terminal took all of it. A paste larger than the terminal's input
queue, into a program that was not reading, held the loop for good:
nothing else was typed, resizing stopped, and closing the tab could not
end it. Closing also cancelled the output reader and closed the
descriptor at once, while the reader could still be reading it, and by
then its number could belong to another file of the app.

PseudoTerminalIO now reads and writes the terminal on dispatch sources:
input it cannot take waits and goes out when the terminal has room,
closing drops it, and the descriptor is closed only after both sources
have finished cancelling.

new test is the review's harness in Swift: a SIGWINCH handler that marks
when it runs outside the test process, and a thread resizing the

fix(files): a download writes only inside the folder it goes to

A folder download named each local file after what the server listed.
A malicious or compromised server listing "../../.zshrc" had it write
outside the destination, over the person's own files (the scp flaw
CVE-2019-6111). Listings now leave out every name a file cannot have:
empty, ".", ".." and anything with a slash. Without a slash, a name
appended to the destination stays directly inside it.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

fix(files): deleting an item asks the server about it, not its parent's listing

removeItem listed the whole parent folder to find out whether the item
was a folder, a file or a link: one listing per deletion of a folder
that may hold thousands of entries, and one more handle left open while
Citadel did not close them. It now asks with lstat, which describes a
link itself, so a link to a folder is still removed and never followed.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

fix(ssh): signing in may take the connection's whole timeout

Citadel gave the handshake and sign-in a fixed 10 seconds, whatever the
connection's timeout. A slow server, or an agent waiting for Touch ID or
a confirmation for longer, failed with "Timed out signing in" and the
server was then reported unreachable. Citadel's timeout is now turned
off; SSHConnection's own deadline, which is the configured timeout plus
the time the agent waited, bounds signing in.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

fix(ssh): listing a folder closes the handle it opens

Citadel's listDirectory opened a folder handle and never closed it, so
every listing kept one open on the server for the rest of the session.
OpenSSH's sftp-server holds only a few hundred, each an open descriptor,
and after enough browsing opening files and folders failed. No Citadel
release fixes it (upstream PRs #137 and #142 are open), and 0.12.1 pins
an unvetted swift-nio-ssh fork, so Citadel now comes from Rayon's fork
(mizorewww/Citadel, branch rayon): 0.12.0 with the handle closed, the
login timeout left to the caller, and an lstat.

The test runs Citadel's own SSH server in the test process with an SFTP
file system the test makes up, and counts the folder handles left open.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

fix(ssh): a connection's own event loop lives as long as the connection

A connection that signs in through the agent gets an event loop of its
own, which was shut down as soon as its channel closed. Everything that
touched the channel afterwards needs that loop: closing it (the pool
releasing its last lease), waiting for it to close (a file transfer
reconnecting, answers(within:)) never returned, and NIO logged
"Cannot schedule tasks on an EventLoop that has already shut down".
makeChannel now hands the loop to its caller, and SSHConnection shuts
it down in deinit, once nothing can use the channel.

commits.message:
fix(realtime)!: fail a channel the server shuts down with the server's reason (#1896)

* fix(realtime)!: fail a channel the server shuts down with the server's reason

Before it stops a channel, Realtime pushes a `system` message with
`extension: "system"`, `status: "error"` and the reason (`shutdown_response/2`
in `realtime_channel.ex`), then `phx_close`. The client reported that reason as
`replicationFailed`, moved a subscribed channel to `.unsubscribed`, and failed
pending pushes with "closed by the server while subscribing".

Now the channel keeps the reason of a `system` error on its current join. The
`phx_close` that follows moves it to `.failed` with a `RealtimeError` of kind
`.channelClosed`, whose message is the reason and whose code is parsed from a
`"<Code>: <message>"` reason. A waiting subscribe and pending pushes fail with
the same error. The channel is still spent and does not rejoin, as the
capability spec says of `phx_close`.

`replicationFailed` fires only while a join with `waitsForReplication` waits
for the replication report. A `phx_close` with no reason keeps the old
behavior, and `RealtimeError.channelClosedByServer` no longer says "while
subscribing".

Found by skirmish-bot when the local tenant passed `max_events_per_second`.

BREAKING CHANGE: a channel the server shuts down for a reason now becomes
`.failed(error)` with `error.kind == .channelClosed` instead of
`.unsubscribed`, and `events()` no longer emits `replicationFailed` for
shutdowns that are not a replication timeout.

* fix(realtime): keep the replication wait of a rejoin for new bindings

A replication `system` ok can confirm a join that rejoins at once for a new
binding. The flag was cleared after the confirmation, so it cleared the new
join's wait too, and a shutdown of that join emitted no `replicationFailed`.
Clear it before the confirmation.

Document that any shutdown before `replicationReady` emits `replicationFailed`
with its reason, since the client does not parse the server's reason. Cover a
`phx_error` without `join_ref` on a channel that left.

fix(strategies): report the world size as `num_replicas` for DDP and FSDP (#22016)

`DDPStrategy` and `FSDPStrategy` computed `distributed_sampler_kwargs["num_replicas"]`
as `num_nodes * num_processes`. That is only correct when every node in the cluster
holds the same number of devices. With heterogeneous nodes -- e.g. two nodes with 2 and
1 devices, as in the report -- each node derives a different value (4 on the first, 2 on
the second) even though the world size is a single number shared by all ranks, so
`DistributedSampler` shards the dataset inconsistently.

Return `self.world_size` instead, which is what the sibling strategies already do:
`DeepSpeedStrategy` and `XLAStrategy` both use `self.world_size`, and
`TorchElasticEnvironment.world_size()` reads `WORLD_SIZE` directly (its
`set_world_size` is a documented no-op), so under `torchrun` the value is the real total.

No behavior change when the nodes are homogeneous, because there
`num_nodes * num_processes == world_size`.

Fixes #19898

Fix ModelPruning iterative reuse RuntimeError on non-leaf tensors (#21717)

* Fix ModelPruning iterative reuse RuntimeError on non-leaf tensors

When ModelPruning with use_lottery_ticket_hypothesis=True is reused
across multiple trainer.fit() calls, setup() is called again each run.
After the first pass, _copy_param sets dst.data = src.data, making the
parameters non-leaf tensors. The subsequent deepcopy(module) then raises:

  RuntimeError: Only Tensors created explicitly by the user (graph
  leaves) support the deepcopy protocol at the moment

Fix by adding _deepcopy_for_pruning(), a helper that temporarily
replaces non-leaf parameters with detached clones before deepcopy and
restores the originals afterward. Also explicitly set _original_layers
to None before re-populating in setup() so the previous run's tensor
references are released before new copies are allocated.

Fixes #8542

* Fix _deepcopy_for_pruning to patch __dict__ not _parameters

The actual non-leaf tensor after pruning is module.weight stored in
module.__dict__ by the forward pre-hook (weight_orig * weight_mask),
not in module._parameters. Patching _parameters had two problems:

1. Did not fix the RuntimeError (wrong dict being patched)
2. Caused mypy errors: assigning Tensor to Parameter | None

Switch to iterating module.__dict__ instead, which correctly captures
the hook-written non-leaf weight attribute.

Keep the protocol on last-checkpoint paths from a remote dirpath (#21936)

* Keep the protocol on the last checkpoint paths from a remote dirpath

`_find_last_checkpoints` ran `os.path.normpath` over what `self._fs.ls`
returned. On a remote filesystem `ls` gives paths without their protocol,
and `normpath` would collapse one anyway ("gs://bucket" -> "gs:/bucket"),
so the checkpoint connector resolved every candidate against the local
filesystem, dropped them all, and warned that no last checkpoint exists.
`ckpt_path="last"` then trained from scratch.

Keep `normpath` for local paths and reattach the protocol otherwise.

* Drop the end-to-end remote resume test

It failed on Windows, where checkpoint paths under a remote dirpath are
joined with a backslash, and on the oldest fsspec, whose memory
filesystem has no modified(). test_find_last_checkpoints_remote_keeps_protocol
still covers the fix.

Broadcast time-based `val_check_interval` decision across ranks to prevent DDP deadlock (#22209)

* Broadcast time-based val_check_interval decision across ranks

In _TrainingEpochLoop._should_check_val_fx(), time-based validation
(when val_check_interval is configured as a timedelta, str, or dict)
evaluated 'now - self.trainer._last_val_time >= interval' independently
on each rank's local monotonic clock without cross-rank synchronization.

In multi-process distributed training (DDP / FSDP), per-step timing jitter
or rank-0 result printing in _EvaluationLoop (which updates _last_val_time
after _print_results on rank 0) can cause one rank to cross the time
threshold a batch earlier than another rank. The rank that sees >= interval
enters val_loop.run() while the other rank proceeds to the next training
batch, causing a collective mismatch / NCCL deadlock.

Broadcast the time-based validation decision via self.trainer.strategy.broadcast
(matching Timer._check_time_remaining) so all ranks run validation in lockstep.

Fix ViTamin-XL-384 image_size (256 -> 384)

The config was built for vitamin_xlarge_384 and loads the 384px

inference ran at 256px. ViTamin has no learned pos embed, so this
ran silently. Upstream's config.json / preprocessor_config.json and

fix(subtitle): 修复智能上下文被 YouTube 页面简介误判跳过并放宽字幕长度上限 (#1418)

开启 YouTube 字幕「增强智能上下文」后，实际播放新视频时不会发出智能上下文请求。原因是 `#ensureCaptionContext` 通过 `if (this.#docInfo.summary) return Promise.resolve();` 判断是否已完成上下文分析，但 `getDocInfo()` 在 YouTube 页面上本来就会把 DOM 中的视频简介或 meta 描述填入 `docInfo.summary`，导致绝大多数视频直接提前返回、跳过了 `#enrichDocInfoWithAI`。此外，`#enrichDocInfoWithAI` 原先仅校验 `API_SPE_TYPES.ai`（拦截了具备 `summarize` 能力的插件服务和内置 AI），且把字幕硬截断在前 8000 字符。

- 在 `src/subtitle/YouTubeCaptionProvider.js` 中新增独立状态位 `#captionContextEnriched`，替代对 `this.#docInfo.summary` 的判空，并在切视频、重新获取字幕、切换上下文服务和恢复原生字幕时正确重置。
- 在 `#enrichDocInfoWithAI` 中补充 `supportsApiCapability(contextApiSetting, summarize)` 判断，与设置页筛选逻辑保持一致。
- 将 `#enrichDocInfoWithAI` 的字幕原稿长度限制从硬截断前 8000 字符放宽为 60000 字符，超出 60000 字符时通过 `sampleTranscriptForContext` 按首/中/尾三段均匀采样并以 `\n...\n` 连接，兼顾长视频覆盖率与小上下文模型稳定性。
- 在 `src/subtitle/YouTubeCaptionProvider.test.js` 中补充回归测试，验证 `getDocInfo()` 已带 DOM `summary` 时仍正常调用 `apiSummarizeContext`，以及超过 60000 字符时会按首/中/尾采样。

- **开启「增强智能上下文」的 YouTube 用户**：新视频可正常发起智能上下文总结请求，常规长视频可传入完整字幕，超长视频自动首/中/尾采样控制在 60000 字符内；使用插件 AI 服务或内置 AI 作为上下文服务时也可生效。
- **未开启该功能的用户**：行为不变。

- 运行 `pnpm test -- --watchAll=false src/subtitle/YouTubeCaptionProvider.test.js`，69/69 用例全部通过。

perf(conv/esp32): MAC16 convolution and depthwise on ESP32

Conv and depthwise run on the ESP32 MAC16 unit:
- Conv uses an s16 im2col band and a MAC16 dot loop
  (esp_nn_conv_mac16_esp32.S). Rows up to 256 samples loop over the
  output channels in asm. The fused loop is unrolled per row length for
  out_offset -128, and longer rows use a x256 dot.
- 3x3 depthwise runs on MAC16 (esp_nn_depthwise_conv_mac16_esp32.S).
  Stride 1 runs two output rows and three columns per pass. Channels go
  in chunks of a multiple of 4.
- The requant is fused into the dot loops. Filters are widened as
  f * 256, so the requant takes one mulsh.
- NN_ESP32_MAC16 (Kconfig, default y) selects these kernels. With it
  off, ESP32 keeps the generic kernels and the smaller scratch of 1.5.x.
- conv_s8_mac16 and dw_s8_mac16 are noinline, so the generic fallback
  does not carry their stack frames.
- include/esp_nn_esp32.h maps conv and depthwise to the ESP32 entries.
  They run the generic kernels for shapes MAC16 does not take, without a
  scratch buffer, with CONFIG_NN_SKIP_NUDGE, and for PSRAM buffers or a
  PSRAM task stack when CONFIG_SPIRAM_CACHE_WORKAROUND is set.
- MAC16 conv takes a layer only when it has input and output channels
  and every output window has input columns and input rows.
- The x256 fused paths need in_offset >= -127, so |in + offset| <= 255
  and the bias limits hold. TFLite input offsets are in [-127, 128].
- The shape rules and the 16 KB scratch budgets are in
  esp_nn_conv_dispatch_esp32.h. The kernels and the scratch getters
  (esp_nn_scratch_sizes_esp32.c) share it, and the getters build on a
  host.
- esp_nn_get_fc_batch_scratch_size returns 0 on targets without the
  batched FC 1x1 path. The plain batch call on ESP32 does not use the
  MAC16 conv scratch.
- Test cases:
  - conv: 3x3 with stride 1 and 2, 1x1 with 32- and 128-sample rows,
    out_offset -128 and 7, in_offset 128, 5 and -3, all with the full
    activation range;
  - conv 96: a 1x1 with explicit output dims one row taller than the
    input;
  - conv 97 and depthwise 57: in_offset -128 with every input and filter
    -128 and a bias near the x256 limit;
  - conv 101 and 102 (ESP32 only): no output channels and no input
    channels, where the scratch getter returns 0;
  - conv and depthwise gate cases: bias at the x256 limits and at
    2^28, +-1, shifts -15/-16 and -20/-21, and shifts 0 and 1;
  - depthwise: stride 1 and 2, ch_mult 2, out_offset -128 and 3,
    in_offset 128, 9 output rows and 10 columns;
  - the batched FC scratch getter is 0 on targets without the 1x1 path.

- On one core the PIE 1x1 wins from a batch of 16, which is one 16-pixel

  kernel.

test(conv): cases for the PIE lanes-as-channels kernel and tile stores

- 2-byte and 31-byte window rows, the shortest and longest the kernel
  takes, with a final batch of fewer than 16 pixels.
- SAME stride 2 with only a trailing pad, on 3 input channels.
- A shift outside the fast requant range on one of 48 channels.
- The kernel limits: 256 pixels in each dual-core half, 255 output
  pixels, 32 and 64 output channels, and a dual-core split whose halves
  take the batch.
- The kernel cases keep at least 256 pixels in each dual-core half, so
  they reach the kernel with the worker active.
- 8-byte tile stores to outputs 4 and 1 bytes off a 16-byte boundary,
  with 20 and 24 output channels.

perf(conv/pie): faster int8 convolution on ESP32-P4

- Requant: one multiply per output, an asm requant with esp.addx2 and
  esp.sat, and per-channel constants built into a table once per call.
  A negative multiplier takes the exact requant.
- 1x1 and im2col paths: a QACC MAC loop of 2.25 instructions per tap,
  the transpose staged on PIE once per batch, and padded raster batches.
- 16-pixel QACC batches requant as one tile on PIE.
- A lanes-as-channels kernel (esp_nn_conv_oc16_riscv_pie.c) for short
  window rows, 2 to 31 bytes, on 16, 32 or 48 output channels and maps
  of at least 256 output pixels. This covers 3x3 layers on 3 to 10
  input channels, such as a first layer on RGB input. It transposes the
  filter on each call, so other shapes take the 16-pixel batch.
  esp_nn_conv_oc16_ok() holds the rule and the measurements behind it.
  Its MAC is inline asm that jumps into a 31-slot sequence. Its 16 x 16
  sums, requant row and tile are in the work scratch, not on the stack,
  as it can run on the dual-core worker.
- On the im2col batch paths the requant table follows the 16-pixel
  staging or the oc16 work area. esp_nn_conv_im2col_tab_offset() in
  esp_nn_conv_dispatch_riscv_pie.h gives its place to the kernel and to
  the scratch getter.
- For oc16 layers the table has 4 words per channel, with the shift
  term, and the oc16 kernel reads it in place.

The staged 3x3 path splits positions only from two chunks of positions
up. Smaller maps, such as 6x6, split the output channels instead.
Each core stages the same windows and runs its channels through the
panel driver at the full output stride. The chunk size and work area
come from the full layer shape, which the scratch getter sized.

perf(conv/s3): split the small-map 3x3 conv by output channels

The main core builds the padded map. Then each core runs half of the
output channels over it. The ACCX kernel takes an output stride, so a
core can write a channel range of the NHWC output.

perf(conv/s3): split batched 1x1 and im2col convs across both cores

With dual core on, these paths give each core half of the output
positions:
- the batched 1x1 path, at a multiple of 8 positions. Over 96 channels
  each half keeps at least 32 positions for the ACCX kernel.
- the im2col path. The main core builds the filter copy once. Both cores
  read it and stage their windows into their own buffers.

The worker's work area comes from esp_nn_dual_core_scratch(). The scratch
getter is unchanged.

Each split site claims the worker with esp_nn_dual_core_begin() before it
takes the worker scratch, and calls esp_nn_dual_core_end() on every path.
The worker's job sits in a static slot, which the claim makes
single-owner. This core runs its half with a direct call. So the
caller's stack holds no job struct.

ci: run the ESP32-P4 rev < v3 code paths on esp-emu

- test_app takes -D ESP_NN_TEST_REV_LT_V3_PATHS=1. It sets
  ESP_NN_HWLOOP_MAX_COUNT to 7 and ESP_NN_VLDBC_IP_BROKEN to 1 on a rev v3
  build, and the app prints the two values.
- build_idf_master_p4_rev_lt_v3_paths builds that image for ESP32-P4 and
  stages it for the emulator stage.
- run_emulator_tests.py fails an image staged under that name when the app
  does not print the line.

fix(avg_pool/pie): split long window rows on ESP32-P4 rev < v3

- ESP32-P4 before rev v3.0 keeps only the low 12 bits of the esp.lp.setup
  count. A window row of 4096 or more positions stopped early.
- On P4 builds for rev < v3, a layer whose filter is wider than
  ESP_NN_HWLOOP_MAX_COUNT runs avg_pool_long_rows: the same kernel, with
  each row in chunks that all add to the QACC. Other layers and other
  builds keep the existing loop.
- Test cases on P4 and S31: 1x4200 windows of random input and of all
  -128, and 70x70 windows of all 127 and all -128.

fix(softmax/pie): split the row max loop on ESP32-P4 rev < v3

- ESP32-P4 before rev v3.0 keeps only the low 12 bits of the esp.lp.setup
  count. A row of 65552 or more values got its max from the first groups
  only.
- The row max is softmax_row_max_pie. On P4 builds for rev < v3 it runs on
  chunks of at most 4096 groups of 16, and the chunk maxima are combined in
  C. Other builds make one call.
- Test case on P4 and S31: one row of 4098 groups plus 5, every value at
  most 0 except the last value of the last full group, which is 127.

fix(add/pie): run long adds in chunks on ESP32-P4 rev < v3

- The add loop runs one step per 8 elements. From 32768 elements the step
  count passes the rev < v3 hardware loop limit.
- On P4 builds for rev < v3, ADD_PIE_LOOP_N runs the steps in chunks of
  ESP_NN_HWLOOP_MAX_COUNT. Other builds compile the same code as before.

fix(mean/pie): split the mean loop on ESP32-P4 rev < v3

- ESP32-P4 before rev v3.0 keeps only the low 12 bits of the esp.lp.setup
  count. A mean over 4096 or more positions stopped early.
- New ESP_NN_HWLOOP_MAX_COUNT in common_functions.h: 4095 on P4 builds for
  rev < v3, no limit on other builds. A build can set a smaller value.
- The mean loop runs in chunks of at most that many positions. Later chunks
  add to the QACC.
- Test cases 10 to 13: 64x64 and 65x65 maps, and 65x65 maps of all 127
  and all -128.

docs: elementwise add cycles on ESP32-S3, ESP32-P4 and ESP32-S31

- Update the elementwise add rows.
- Add rows with TFLite parameters, which take the P4/S31 vector path.

test(add): cases for the P4/S31 PIE add

- Cases 10-21 use TFLite-like parameters with left shift 14 to 20: sizes
  of 8, 13 and 56x56x24, unaligned inputs and output, an output that
  aliases input 1, all shifts 0, the largest shifts and multipliers the
  fast path takes, int32 and narrowed activation limits, and offset edges.
- Case 18 and cases 22-28 each put one parameter just outside the fast
  path: an input or output multiplier at 0x7fff8000, left shift 21 and 13,
  input offset -128, an input or output shift of -21, and output offset
  128.

perf(add/pie): vector requant for elementwise add on P4 and S31

- 8 elements per step in a hardware loop. Offsets, both input requants,
  the rounding shifts, the output offset and the clamp run on PIE vectors.
- Each input requant is two 16x16 bit products: the input plus offset has
  at most 9 bits, and the multiplier splits into a high and a low 16-bit
  half. esp.vmul.s32.s16xs16 shifts the low product by SAR, which gives
  the floor the rounding needs.
- Only the output requant's 32x32 bit high multiply is scalar, one mulhsu
  per element.
- The clamp runs on s32 lanes before narrowing, so any activation limits
  give the reference result.
- A tail below 8 elements runs one more step on the last 8 elements into a
  buffer and keeps the last bytes, so an output that aliases an input
  stays correct.
- Inputs in external memory are prefetched 384 bytes ahead.
- Fewer than 8 elements, and parameters outside the fast path (left shift
  outside 14..20, a multiplier of 0x7fff8000 or more, shifts below -20),
  take the scalar code.

bench_app: time ADD with TFLite parameters and MobileNetV2 shapes

- add_tflm rows use left shift 20 and the multiplier and shift ranges of a
  MobileNetV2 residual add, at 1615 elements and the five MobileNetV2
  residual add sizes, 56x56x24 down to 7x7x160.

fix(max_pool/pie): long bands and windows on ESP32-P4 rev < v3

- ESP32-P4 before rev v3.0 keeps only the low 12 bits of the esp.lp.setup
  count. A band of 4096 or more pixels or 16-byte blocks stopped early,
  and so did a window of 4096 or more taps on 33 or more channels.
- New ESP_NN_HWLOOP_MAX_COUNT in common_functions.h: 4095 on P4 builds for
  rev < v3, no limit on other builds.
- On those builds, a layer whose output row, output row in 16-byte
  blocks, or filter side is above that count runs the reference. Every
  other layer, and every layer on other builds, runs the same code as
  before.
- Test cases on P4 and S31: 1x2 and 2x2 bands of 4199 blocks, a 2x2 band
  of 4100 pixels, a 3x3 band of 4100 blocks, and 1x4200 windows on 48 and
  40 channels with the max in the last pixel. At 40 channels the last of
  the 3 blocks overlaps the one before.

docs(max_pool/pie): update the ESP32-P4 and ESP32-S31 max pooling cycles

- docs/performance.md: ESP32-P4 and ESP32-S31 rows for input 16x16x16,
  3x3 filter, pad 1, stride 1, from bench_app. The P4 row notes its chip
  revision and 400 MHz clock.
- README.md: ESP32-P4 and ESP32-S31 ratios in the kernel summary row.
docs(max_pool/pie): note why the 16-byte input over-read is safe

test(max_pool): add boundary cases for the PIE fast paths

- Take the output size as an argument, so tests can ask for the extra
  right/bottom output of TFLite SAME padding.
- Print the output size and buffer offsets when a case fails.
- Add exact-match cases for 1xK and 1x2 line bands that read input,
  width-1 inputs with real data, SAME padding on the right/bottom only,
  channels < 16 with unaligned buffers, and the 3-block generic window
  with 16 < d < 32.

perf(max_pool/pie): fast paths for 2x2 and 3x3 windows, row bands

- Unclipped 2x2 and 3x3 windows unroll their taps. A hardware loop runs
  over the 16-byte blocks of a pixel, or over the pixels of a row band.
- Rows whose windows fit the row width form one band per block offset.
  With stride 1 the band is one byte run, done in 16-byte blocks for any
  channel count.
- 1xK line filters and width-1 inputs run as bands too.
- The generic clipped window does three 16-channel blocks per pass.
- Channel tails reuse an overlapping last block. Pixels whose 16-byte
  accesses would leave the buffers use a scalar loop.
- Windows that miss the input give INT8_MIN, clamped, without entering a
  hardware loop.
- Every hardware loop uses ESP_NN_HWLOOP_BEGIN/LAST/END. The
  two-instruction tap loops run as software loops when
  ESP_NN_HWLOOP_PADDED is 1.

Merge branch 'perf/p4_depthwise_pie' into 'master'

perf(depthwise/pie): faster int8 depthwise convolution on ESP32-P4

See merge request espressif/esp-nn!95

Merge branch 'ci/esp_emu_latest' into 'master'

See merge request espressif/esp-nn!91

Merge branch 'perf/s3_conv_r2_mr' into 'master'

perf(conv/s3): s8 MAC path and faster requant for the 1x1 and 3x3 kernels

See merge request espressif/esp-nn!86

Merge branch 'perf/p4_mul_pie' into 'master'

perf(mul/pie): vector requant for elementwise and broadcast multiply

See merge request espressif/esp-nn!81

test(depthwise): edge strips wider than the edge slab

- Case 84: 400x40x32, a 3x3 filter and pad 1. The top and bottom strips
  are over DW_PIE_SLAB_MAX, so they run in chunks of columns.

perf(depthwise/pie): skip the slab for 16-channel layers without edges

- A layer of one full 16-channel block whose windows all lie inside the
  input runs on the non-slab path. It reads the input once there too, so
  it needs no slab scratch.
- A partial block (8-15 channels) keeps the slab, as the non-slab path
  would run it in scalar C.

refactor(depthwise/pie): keep the position arrays in the layer scratch

- The output position arrays of a batch take 832 bytes. They move from
  the stack of depthwise_conv_s8_ch1_pie_impl into the layer scratch, so
  the inference task and the dual-core worker need less stack.
- dw_pie_ch1_scratch_size adds DW_PIE_POS_BYTES.

test(depthwise): a moved last block across blocks 63 and 64

- Case 83: 10x10x1032, a 3x3 filter and no pad. Channel 1020 is past the
  PIE requant, and the moved last block covers channels 1016-1031.

fix(depthwise/pie): size the slab scratch the same on every device

- The slab size depended on the L2 cache size. A size computed without
  the device's sdkconfig, for example on a host, could be smaller than the
  band the kernel ran, and the kernel wrote past the scratch.
- dw_pie_slab_band and dw_pie_slab_size do not read the L2 size. The
  kernel caps the band to the L2 cache in dw_pie_slab_band_l2. The cap only
  shortens the band, so the slab fits the scratch the getter gave.
- When one band of output rows needs more than DW_PIE_SLAB_MAX, the slab
  path is off. A 1-D map does not ask for a slab of its whole width.
- The dispatch header does not include sdkconfig.h, so the scratch getters
  build on a host.
- Test case 82: a 1100x1x16 map with a 9-tap filter. On P4 and S31 its
  scratch must stay under 4 KB.

fix(depthwise/pie): end the last channel block at the last channel

- Off the slab path, a last block of 8-15 channels loaded 16 bytes per
  tap and pixel. The last filter tap and the last input pixel read up to 8
  bytes past the end of their tensors.
- dw_pie_tail_block moves that block back to end at the last channel. Its
  first channels repeat the block before, with the same results. All 16
  lanes are valid, so the block can take the fused requant loop.
- The block moves only when it stays in the channels of the call and
  starts on an 8-channel group. Otherwise those channels run in scalar C.
- dw_pie_block_slow checks both 16-channel blocks that a moved block
  spans, and no shift goes past the 64-bit mask.
- Block 64 has no bit. With channels past block 63, a channel of block 63
  outside the PIE requant turns the PIE requant off for the layer, as the
  moved last block can span blocks 63 and 64.

docs: depthwise conv cycles on ESP32-P4 and ESP32-S31

- Update the ESP32-P4 and ESP32-S31 depthwise rows, and add rows for the
  3x3 shapes with padding and the strided 1x3 shapes.
- README: add a 3x3 depthwise row.
test(depthwise): two-core channel split cases

perf(depthwise/pie): split maps of under 8 rows across cores by channels

- The kernel runs a channel range [c_beg, c_end) of the layer.
- With under 8 output rows, the worker takes the first half of the
  16-channel blocks and this core the rest, over every position. Each core
  builds the per-channel table of its own channels only.
- Larger maps keep the output-row split.
test(depthwise): edge strips of the non-slab 3x3 path

perf(depthwise/pie): run 3x3 edge positions from padded slabs

- Without the slab path, the top and bottom rows and the left and right
  columns of a 3x3 layer run from padded copies of their input, through the
  fused loop, when all channels are in fused 16-channel blocks.
- dw_pie_edge_size gives the scratch for these copies. The scratch getter,
  the dispatcher and the dual-core worker use it.

- The edge slab is sized only for whole 16-channel blocks, the case that
  takes it, and only up to DW_PIE_SLAB_MAX. Wider top and bottom strips
  run in chunks of columns.
test(depthwise): non-slab cases for the fused 3x3 loop

perf(depthwise/pie): one loop for window, requant and store of 3x3 blocks

- Full 16-channel blocks of a 3x3 window with the PIE requant run window,
  requant and store per position in one asm loop.
- The non-slab path runs inner positions in chunks of up to 32 in raster
  order, every channel block per chunk.
- The slab path runs a whole band of such a block in one call.
- The clamp uses vsat, so the lo and hi vectors of the table are not loaded.
- Per-channel filter sums run on PIE for full 16-channel blocks.

perf(depthwise/pie): scalar requant only for the 16-channel block that needs it

- The PIE requant gate is checked per 16-channel block. A channel outside
  its range (multiplier of 0x7fff8000 or more, shift outside -20..-1,
  a large combined bias) sends only its own block to the scalar requant.
  The other blocks keep the PIE requant.
- Past 64 blocks such a channel still turns the PIE requant off for the
  whole layer.
- Test cases 70 and 71: one out-of-range multiplier in a full 16-channel
  block (stride 1) and in a partial block (stride 2).

test(depthwise): slab path on maps larger than the L2 cache

- Case 67: 28x28x96, pad 1, stride 1. The band is capped to 5 rows.
- Case 68: 37x37x96 to 19x19, stride 2. The last band is shorter.
- Case 69: 9x9x960, over the L2 size, where a capped band would be a
  single row, so the band is not capped.

perf(depthwise/pie): cap the slab band when the map is larger than the L2 cache

- The slab path runs every 16-channel block over the whole band. Each
  block reads every input row and writes every output row of the band
  with 16-byte strides.
- When the input and output of the map, all channels, are larger than
  the L2 cache, those rows fall out of the cache between blocks and
  every block streams them from PSRAM again.
- The band is then capped so its input and output rows, all channels,
  take a quarter of the L2 cache. The cap is skipped when it would leave
  a single row. Maps that fit the L2 keep the long band.
- The L2 size comes from CONFIG_CACHE_L2_CACHE_SIZE, 128 KB if undefined.
  The dispatch header includes sdkconfig.h, so the scratch getter and the
  kernel see the same size.
- A dual-core slice also bounds its band by the slab size of the full
  call, so it never needs more scratch than the getter gave.
- The arithmetic per output is unchanged, so the result is bit-identical.

test(depthwise): cases for the PIE ch_mult 1 kernel

- Square 5x5 filters, with 32 and 25 channels.
- Partial channel blocks: 25, 20 and 44 channels. Their 16-byte output
  stores land at odd addresses.
- The edges of the vector requant: shifts of -15 to -20, multipliers
  on both sides of its limit, and one shift of -21, which takes the
  scalar requant.
- in_offset 128 with padding, so pad taps are -128.

perf(depthwise/pie): faster int8 depthwise convolution on ESP32-P4

For ch_mult 1 with an input offset in [-127, 128]:
- Windows MAC in inline asm (esp_nn_depthwise_conv_mac_riscv_pie.h)
  with unrolled 3x3 and 5x5 pipelines. Edge windows also run on QACC.
  The window routine steps through the output positions itself.
- Edge-heavy layers and layers with one 16-channel block copy the input
  into a padded slab per block, in bands of output rows of at most
  16 KB. Every window is then inside the slab. The slab path runs
  batches of 32 positions.
- Requant, clamp and store run on PIE: 16x16-bit partial products in
  the 64-bit QACC lanes, a per-lane shift, then vmax/vmin and one
  16-byte store per position. It is exact for |acc + comb| < 2^26,
  mult < 2^31 - 2^15 and shift in [-20, -1]. Other layers take the
  scalar requant.
- The dual-core split gives each core its own scratch of the same size.
- The scratch size rules are in esp_nn_conv_dispatch_riscv_pie.h. The
  getter and the kernel share the inner-window range helpers there.
- ESP_NN_QACC_LOAD_S32 loads QACC from an array, the reverse of
  ESP_NN_QACC_EXTRACT_S32.

ci: expect the fc_dual_core_s8 suite in the emulator runs

- fc_dual_core_s8 joins EXPECTED_SUITES, so a run without it fails.

ci: emulate the ESP32-S3 test_app

- esp32s3 joins the emulated targets. esp-emu runs the S3 ee.* SIMD
  kernels, so the S3 images run in the emulator job like the RISC-V
  ones.

ci: pick the esp-emu release of the emulator tests

- ESP_EMU_VERSION in the GitLab and GitHub emulator jobs picks the

- The jobs download install.sh to a file and then run it, so a failed

  stamps it into the report rows.
- It stops before the first image when esp-emu is older than 1.0.0, the
  oldest release that runs every test image.
- The CI comments give the time budget of each emulator job.

commits.message:
chore: bench: replay saved sampled CPU audits

# Summary

Make CPU qualification and calibration recoverable from their saved
artifacts, with results written separately from the original study.

# Details

The calibration phase previously guessed its parent audit helper's path
from the phase directory and failed after recording completed. Resolve
pinned dependencies from each protocol and use an explicit phase plan so
recovery also works from another working directory.

Keep qualification gates and signed calibration estimates intact. Record
terminal phase states so an audit failure cannot look like a running
measurement. Compile pinned validators with assertions enabled even when
Python itself runs with optimization.

Reject unknown phases so a misspelled calibration cannot appear complete
with an empty set of qualification comparisons.

chore: bench: compile the durable node with the rocks feature again

# Summary

`benchmarks/durable` did not compile with `--features rocks`: its
RocksDB backend's `follower_read` handler still called the follower-read
API that f3e840d9 changed. Call it as the other examples do, with
`FOLLOWER_READ_TIMEOUT`, and name the error type's `TypeConfig`.

# Details

- f3e840d9 made `App::ensure_follower_read_ready()` take a timeout and
  `FollowerReadError` generic over the type config, and updated every
  example's handler but this one.
- No CI job and no `make verify*` target that CI runs builds this
  feature, so the break showed only in `make verify-bench-durable-rocks`.

fix: openraft: preserve the deadline when retrying a transfer

# Summary

Retrying a leadership transfer to the same node keeps the original
recovery deadline, even if the deadline has already passed.

# Details

A retry still sends the transfer request again so a target that missed
it has another chance to take over. Changing the target starts a new
attempt with its own deadline. This prevents repeated calls for the
same target from indefinitely delaying the source's recovery election.

Refs: #2178

docs: bench: record the heartbeat batching results of grpc-groups

# Summary

`results.md` of grpc-groups gains the runs of #2543: 3 rounds of
`steady` and `crash` at a324507f without batching, with
`--batch-heartbeats`, and with `--node-heartbeat-timer` as well. The
README explains why `ack_age` does not compare between runs with the
node timer and runs without it.

# Details

- With batching, `rpcs/s` fell from 39,124 to 529 and 224 in `steady`,
  and `cpu%` from 253 to 123 and 116, with about the same round trips.
- With `--node-heartbeat-timer`, the leaders of a node send their
  heartbeats in step, so the 100 ms samples of `ack_age` all fall at
  one point of the 50 ms interval, which differs from run to run.
  `ack_age_p50_ms` was 16.2 to 45.8 ms in those runs, against 28.9 to
  29.7 ms without the option.

Refs: #2516

chore: bench: measure apply lag of durable WAL nodes on real disk

# Summary

Add OpenRaft runtime stats and a slow-apply option to
`benchmarks/durable`, and use them to measure apply lag with the WAL
backend's real fsync through `process_profile.py`. Add a report of a
grid of three `apply()` costs and three write rates.

# Details

- The durable node builds with a new default `runtime-stats` feature
  and serves `/benchmark/runtime_stats`: its role, its per-entry stage
  latencies over the last 1,024 log ranges, and the entries of its
  `apply()` calls. `process_profile.py` builds the node with the
  feature and records every node's stats after the workload.
- `--apply-delay-us` makes every `apply()` call of the WAL backend's
  state machine take that much longer, on a blocking-pool thread
  before the call applies its entries. The WAL backend wraps
  `sm-mem`'s store in `SlowApply` and serves its own copies of the
  example's three read handlers, which are typed on the unwrapped
  store. The driver passes the option to every owned WAL node and
  checks that each node reports it.
- Findings: the WAL append took 19 to 21 ms on the leader, so commit
  took about 20 ms. Committed to applied took 0.02 ms with the
  in-memory state machine, 2.3 to 2.5 ms with 2 ms calls (1.2 calls)
  and 17 to 18 ms with 10 ms calls (1.8 calls), at 500 to 4,000
  writes/s. With 10 ms calls apply was 44 to 47% of a write's time on
  the leader. 25 of 45 runs stalled for about a second in every row,
  with or without an apply delay; the traced stall coincided with
  AppendEntries timeouts to both followers.
- The driver now waits for the new leader to apply its first entry
  before it adds learners. It had sent `/add-learner` as soon as the
  node was leader, and on this disk one run of 22 failed with
  `UncommittedLeaderLog`.

commits.message:
Merge pull request #2236 from doronz88/refactor/dedup

Remove six repeated blocks (RTP handling, websocket relay, tunnel start-up, certificates, DTX wait)

core_device: Share the RTP and RTCP handling of serve-web and serve-vnc

Each server read the RTP header, tracked the extended highest sequence number and built the
receiver report, SDES and PLI packets with its own copy, for the video and again for the audio.
They are now functions of `core_device.rtp`, and `is_key_nal` is the one of screen_stream.

Nothing sent or accepted changes: the packets are byte for byte the ones built before, and
serve-vnc still sends its audio receiver report without an SDES.

tunneld: Relay a websocket to its peer with one helper

The `/connect` bridge to a tunnel and the one to an upstream tunneld each ran the same pair of
forwarders and the same cleanup around them. `_relay_websocket` does it for both, given how to
send to and receive from the peer.

tunnel_service: Establish a TCP tunnel in one place

`RemotePairingProtocol` and `CoreDeviceTunnelProxy` each connect a stream their own way, then
establish the tunnel over it, yield its result and stop it with the same lines. Those are now
`StartTcpTunnel._established`.

dtx: Wait for a service and for a proxied service with one loop

`wait_for_service` and `wait_for_proxied_service` each turned the predicate into a function and
looped over the services under the condition. They now differ only by the services they look
at. The new tests pass on the code as it was.

ca: Build the host and device certificates from one builder

The two leaf certificates of a pairing differ only by the subject key identifier of the device
one. The certificates are byte for byte what they were.

lockdown: Drop the RemoteLockdownClient constructor which only called its parent

It took the eight parameters of `LockdownClient.__init__` and passed them on unchanged.

pyproject: Require pycrashreport 2.8.0

pyproject: Require pycrashreport 2.8.0

Merge pull request #2234 from Cassian433/afc-walk-pull-errors

afc: Fix dirlist depth and unreadable entries in walk() and pull()

afc: Let pull --ignore-errors skip an entry that vanished

resolve_path ran outside the try, so an entry deleted between READ_DIR and
the pull aborted the whole pull even with ignore_errors. A dropped
connection still aborts it.

afc: Skip subdirectories walk() cannot list

An unreadable directory inside the requested depth still made walk()
raise, the case #1963 left open: /PhotoData/UBF answers READ_DIR with
PERM_DENIED, so afc ls -r /PhotoData failed. The listed root still
raises, same split as dvt ls in #2015. An entry walk() cannot stat
(deleted after READ_DIR, or a dangling link) stays in the file list, as
os.walk keeps it, instead of failing the walk.

afc: Count dirlist depth from the listed root

dirlist() counted separators in the full path, so depth only matched the
listing depth for "/" and one-component relative roots: dirlist("/a", 2)
never returned /a/b/c. crash ls -d goes through it.

commits.message:
fix(editor): a drop keeps a quote's lazy line in it, a failed copy leaves no empty line

Three low items the release review left open, closed before the release.

A plain line right under a quote's paragraph is part of the quote in
cmark-gfm. A drop on the quote put the link between the two and pulled
that line out; a drop on the line put the link inside the quote. Both
now go after the whole quote. A line that opens a heading, list, code,
table or formula ends the quote as before.

A file dropped on the empty line between two paragraphs gets a break
on each side. When its copy failed later only the first went back out
with the link; the second does too.

The attachment path pattern still started a match on the slash of each
`../`, so 20,000 of them with no attachment after took 26s. A match no
longer starts there; the randomized comparison with the plain pattern
still holds.

Verified: the new assertions fail on the old sources, swift test for
MiaoYanCore (151) and the whole xcodebuild test (633, 1 skipped) pass,
SwiftLint and swift-format strict pass.
Revert: git revert this commit.

docs(rules): load the upload and drop rules with their files, I-114 to I-116

editor.md's paths did not match Helpers/ClipboardManager.swift,
S3Uploader.swift or TextFormatter.swift, so the upload, drop and
secret rules were not loaded when those files were edited. It now
lists them, and records the drop placement and S3 rules as fixed
today, and that a toast whose English changes is translated again
rather than carried over (the same keys were fixed three times).

storage.md names AttachmentLinks and UnusedAttachments and says the
Mac and iPhone walks change together; AGENTS.md lists DropPlacement in
MiaoYanCore, points to editor.md for image upload, and says CI runs on
macOS 15, where a test measuring a system layout has to guard itself
(62043f56 failed there). ARCHITECTURE.md names NoteVersionFiles; the
audit prompt says five variant groups, as the project has; the audit's
Open list drops decide 1125-22, which landed.

incidents.md: I-114 (uPic and Picsee trashed a picture the note still
linked, shipped until 79e97c7f), I-115 and I-116 (fixed in 7065a4ee).
check_incidents.py: 116 incidents, 0 problems.

fix(settings): name the iCloud folder as Finder does in every language

Note Location named the app's own container with the localized app
name, 妙言 on a Chinese or Japanese system, while Finder shows the
folder by NSUbiquitousContainerName, MiaoYan everywhere. It now asks
the system for the folder's display name, as it did for other apps'
containers.

FontConfiguration's defaultEditorFont, defaultInterfaceFont and
defaultPreviewFont lost their last caller in f696be48 and go; the
tests read fallbackFont.

Verified: xcodebuild test (633 passed), with
testNoteLocationNamesICloudFoldersAsFinderDoes. Not looked at on a
Chinese system.

fix(storage): clean attachments through a linked folder, keep old versions at the budget

macOS 27 refuses to list the URL of a linked folder (ENOTDIR), so
Clean Unused Attachments could not read a library holding one and
cleaned nothing. Both walks, Storage.noteFiles(below:) and
UnusedAttachments in MiaoYanCore, list a folder by its path. The Mac
walk also refuses while a note is not current in iCloud, which only
the iPhone walk did.

The attachment path pattern read a long run of / or ../ again from
each of its characters (8000 slashes took 2.8s on the main thread). A
match never starts right after a slash or on the second dot of ../,
and the pattern now says so; it finds exactly what the plain one
found, compared over 20000 made-up texts in the test and over three
million more in review.

The trim to nine tenths of the version budget (97f97bc3) took every
older version of every note whenever the newest versions alone were
above nine tenths. It then stops at the budget itself.

Restore's exact save (I-112) had no test in the app: taking exact
out left every test green. testRestoreKeepsACurrentTextThatDiffersOnlyInIndentation
runs the panel's restore, which no longer dismisses a panel that was
never presented.

Verified: swift test (151 passed) and xcodebuild test (633 passed).
Each new test was run red with its fix taken out; the linked-folder
test is red only on macOS 27, CI's macOS 15 lists the URL either way.
Nothing here deletes a file the old code kept: the walks can only
refuse more often, and the trim never removes more than before.
Revert: git revert this commit.

fix(upload): save the S3 secret first, refuse remote http, say why an upload failed

The S3 / R2 sheet wrote the address, key id and public URL before the
Keychain took the secret, so a refused save left new settings beside
the old secret and every upload answered 403. The secret goes first
now and nothing else is written when it is refused.

Plain http to a host outside the local network could be saved, and
then failed on every paste: Info.plist allows local networking only.
Save stays off for it (S3UploadConfig.isLoadable), and for a public IP
address too, where the picture would cross the internet in the clear.

A bucket's refusal and a public URL that does not serve the image
each have a toast of their own, with the S3 error code; a first setup
only ever saw "Upload failed" and no hint which field was wrong.

The settings row reads its host from the defaults, without a Keychain
read each time Settings opens, and its plain description is back in
the PrefsFitTests width check. Public URL stays in English like the
other three labels, as R2's dashboard names them. zh-Hant's
"Uploading image…" gets the ellipsis ja and es got in 6499759e.

Verified: xcodebuild test (633 passed), with
testPlainHTTPIsTakenForTheLocalNetworkOnly and
testARefusalAndAPrivateAddressEachHaveTheirOwnToast; plutil -lint on the
four Localizable.strings. No upload was run against a real bucket.
Revert: git revert this commit; saved settings keep working either way.

fix(editor): a drop in a table, quote or any code block stays out of it

A file dropped inside a table went right under its last row with one
line break, and cmark-gfm takes any line there for one more row, the
result 325125b8 meant to prevent; its test held that text as right.
A fence of tildes, one indented under a list item, a $$ formula and a
quote were not seen as blocks, so the link landed inside them.

DropPlacement.spot now answers the offset and the line breaks around
the link: two after a table or a quote, one after code (told by the
table commands' scan, TableEditing.codeBlockEnd), and on an empty line
a break on each side that holds text, so the line that kept two
paragraphs apart still does. An empty line inside code goes after the
block, a line of spaces alone gets a break first, and an empty line
above an indented line is left alone so a list item keeps its
paragraph. lineEnd keeps its signature for the iPhone editor, which
still has to move to spot to leave the same empty lines.

The drag test used a one-line note, where every drop point gave the
same text; it now drops on the second of two lines.

Verified: swift test for MiaoYanCore (151 passed) and xcodebuild test
(633 passed, 1 skipped). testADropLeavesAnEmptyLineWhereTheLinkWouldJoinABlock
and the tilde and formula cases of testADropGoesAfterItsLineTableOrCodeBlock
were run red with each rule taken out. A second review of this diff
found the three empty-line cases above. Not run in the built app.
Revert: git revert this commit.

fix(l10n): retranslate toasts left on their old wording in zh-Hant, ja and es

ee3b1647 shortened eleven English toasts and updated zh-Hans; d21f3df3
later fixed part of the rest. Still on the old sentence: "Install and set
up %@ first" in zh-Hant, ja and es (ja ungrammatical, es without the set-up
step), the upload failure toast that S3 / R2 uploads now show (ja told the
reader to "use local", es read "using local"), "Uploading image…" in ja and
es, "Several notes share this title" in ja and es (es dropped the search
results half), "Note link copied" in ja and es (es still said the URL was
copied successfully, use it anywhere), "Separate slides with ---" in ja
(missing particle), "Press ⌘⇧W" in zh-Hant and es, and "Exit preview to
format" in es. zh-Hant and ja follow zh-Hans' current wording; Apple's own
zh_TW strings use 密鑰, so the Keychain sentence keeps it.

Found by an agy review of the S3 / R2 strings plus a sweep of every key
ee3b1647 renamed, across the three languages. Verified: plutil -lint on the
three files; full app suite 630 tests pass.

commits.message:
Handle invalid peer keys in ECDH key agreement (#848)

Wasefire's Public::import stores peer coordinates without validating
that the point lies on P-256 and defers validation to Shared::new.
Because SecretKey::diffie_hellman unwrapped Shared::new, an off-curve
ClientPIN or hmac-secret key agreement key panicked the authenticator
instead of returning CTAP1_ERR_INVALID_PARAMETER.

Make ecdh::SecretKey::diffie_hellman return Option<Self::SharedSecret>,
propagate Shared::new errors as None in the Wasefire environment, and
map None to CTAP1_ERR_INVALID_PARAMETER in PinProtocol::decapsulate.
