commits.message:
Merge pull request #1615 from twmb/kfake-kip360-last-epoch

kfake, kgo: fix KIP-360 fencing and EndTxn recovery

kgo: document not purging topics in an active transaction

PurgeTopicsFromClient, and so PurgeTopicsFromProducing, forgets that a
purged partition joined the open transaction. EndTransaction then sees
no partition in the transaction and returns without ending it below
transaction version 2. At transaction version 2, if a produce in the
transaction succeeded, EndTransaction(TryCommit) aborts the transaction
and returns nil.

kgo: do not reload a transactional producer ID after truncation

A transactional producer whose produce gets UNKNOWN_PRODUCER_ID or
OUT_OF_ORDER_SEQUENCE_NUMBER after the log start moved past its last
acknowledged offset now fails the producer ID with that error, as it
does for those errors otherwise. Previously, it took the idempotent
producer's recovery: it marked the producer ID for reload and retried
the batch. The reload's InitProducerID aborted the open transaction,
including records it had acknowledged in other partitions, and at
transaction version 2 the retried batch joined a new transaction that
the next commit committed without them.

The changed test fails without the fix.

kgo: repeat End's error after an unknown EndTxn outcome

GroupTransactSession.End now returns the same error again, without
sending anything, after an End that did not learn whether its commit or
abort happened. End's documentation says its errors are not retryable,
apart from the error after a recreated topic. Previously, a second End
reran the offset commit, which fails until EndTransaction learns the
outcome, and then tried TryAbort. After a commit EndTransaction did not
learn the outcome of, End returned EndTransaction's refusal of TryAbort
instead of the error about the unknown outcome.

The changed test rows fail without the fix.

kgo: fence on INVALID_PRODUCER_EPOCH from transaction requests

An EndTxn, AddPartitionsToTxn, or AddOffsetsToTxn answered with
INVALID_PRODUCER_EPOCH now fails the producer ID with PRODUCER_FENCED,
which is fatal, as Java does. Kafka answers a fenced request of these
kinds with INVALID_PRODUCER_EPOCH below v2. Previously, below
transaction version 2, the client treated the error as recoverable
(KIP-588) and reloaded the producer ID, whose InitProducerID could
abort the transaction of the producer that had fenced it.

The new test rows fail without the fix.

kgo: do not hold the producer mutex across a producer ID reload

maybeRecoverProducerID no longer holds the producer mutex across its
InitProducerID round trip. A HookBrokerRead or HookBrokerE2E that calls
BufferedProduceRecords locks the same mutex, and kgo runs those hooks
before it hands a response over, so a transactional client's first
BeginTransaction deadlocked. Every caller already holds the transaction
mutex. The lock came with EndAndBeginTransaction's concurrent mode,
EndBeginTxnUnsafe, which is now a no-op.

The changed test waits at most 5s for BeginTransaction, so that it
fails without the fix instead of hanging on the deadlock.

kgo: fence on INVALID_PRODUCER_EPOCH from InitProducerID v4+

An InitProducerID answered with INVALID_PRODUCER_EPOCH at v4+ now fails
the producer ID with PRODUCER_FENCED, which is fatal. Previously, a
client without KIP-890 part 2 treated the error as recoverable
(KIP-588). BeginTransaction succeeded, and each produce sent another
InitProducerID and failed with INVALID_PRODUCER_EPOCH, without the
client ever reporting that it was fenced.

Kafka answers a fenced InitProducerID with PRODUCER_FENCED from v4, and
with INVALID_PRODUCER_EPOCH only below v4. The new test row fails
without the fix.

kgo: recover from TRANSACTION_ABORTABLE below transaction version 2

TRANSACTION_ABORTABLE is now recoverable at every transaction version,
as Java does: EndTransaction(ctx, TryAbort) aborts at the producer ID
and then reloads it. Previously, below transaction version 2, the
producer ID stayed failed with TRANSACTION_ABORTABLE after the abort,
and every later BeginTransaction failed as fatal. Kafka's coordinator
does not send TRANSACTION_ABORTABLE for EndTxn or AddOffsetsToTxn, but
other brokers can.

The new test rows fail without the fix.

kgo: abort at the failed producer ID before reloading it

EndTransaction(ctx, TryAbort), with the producer ID failed with a
recoverable error or flagged for reload during an open transaction, now
sends EndTxn(abort) at the stored producer ID and epoch first, as Java
does. The producer ID is recovered afterward only if the abort ends the
transaction or the coordinator answers INVALID_PRODUCER_ID_MAPPING,
which means it has no transaction for us. Any other definitive answer,
such as PRODUCER_FENCED or TRANSACTIONAL_ID_AUTHORIZATION_FAILED, fails
the producer ID and is returned, with nothing more sent. Previously,
the abort reloaded the producer ID without sending EndTxn, or flagged
it for the next BeginTransaction to reload. If another producer had
taken over the transactional ID, the reload's InitProducerID aborted
the other producer's open transaction.

Nothing reloads the producer ID while the abort is in flight. A resent
abort that ends the transaction, or that the coordinator answers
INVALID_PRODUCER_ID_MAPPING, recovers the producer ID as the first
abort does.

The new and changed test rows fail without the fix.

kgo: do not treat a definitive EndTxn answer as unknown

A definitive EndTxn answer, such as PRODUCER_FENCED, now ends the
EndTransaction attempt: the transaction state is consumed, and
EndTransaction does not treat the outcome as unknown. Previously, since
v1.21.6, every EndTxn error restored the state and treated the outcome
as unknown. After PRODUCER_FENCED, BeginTransaction then returned
"invalid attempt to begin a transaction while already in a transaction"
instead of the fence. TRANSACTION_ABORTABLE still keeps the transaction
state, because the caller must abort, and TryAbort after it is not
refused.

EndTransaction(ctx, TryAbort) with no transaction state left now
returns the stored producer ID error when that error is fatal, as Java
does. A recoverable error is left for BeginTransaction to recover from.

The new and changed test rows fail without the fix.

kgo: do not fail the producer ID on CONCURRENT_TRANSACTIONS

An EndTxn or AddOffsetsToTxn that still gets CONCURRENT_TRANSACTIONS
when the context ends no longer fails the producer ID with it.
EndTransaction did not learn whether that EndTxn's commit or abort
happened, and resends the EndTxn when the caller calls EndTransaction
again with the same TransactionEndTry. The AddOffsetsToTxn applied
nothing, and the producer ID stays as it was. Previously, the producer
ID was failed with CONCURRENT_TRANSACTIONS, which kerr marks
non-retryable and which maybeRecoverProducerID did not recover from, so
every later BeginTransaction failed as fatal.

maybeRecoverProducerID now treats CONCURRENT_TRANSACTIONS like a
retryable error, including as the last answer to a reload that ran
until its context ended: it marks the producer ID for reload rather
than reporting a fatal error that it never stored.

The new test row fails without the fix.

kgo: bound GroupTransactSession.End's resends before KIP-447

GroupTransactSession.End now stops resending EndTxn after the rebalance
timeout when its offset commit ran below KIP-447 (Kafka before 2.5).
End then does not learn whether the commit happened, and the session
fails. Previously, End resent EndTxn until its context ended. Without
KIP-447's RequireStable, a member that takes over our partitions does
not wait for our open transaction, so a commit that arrives after the
group moved the partitions duplicates what that member processes.

The new test row fails without the fix.

kgo: resend EndTxn when its outcome is unknown

When EndTransaction did not learn whether the commit or abort happened,
it now resends the same EndTxn, with the producer ID and epoch it used,
when the caller calls EndTransaction again with the same
TransactionEndTry, as Java does: EndTransaction(ctx, TryCommit) resends
a commit whose outcome it did not learn, and EndTransaction(ctx,
TryAbort) resends an abort whose outcome it did not learn. TryAbort is
refused after a commit EndTransaction did not learn the outcome of, and
TryCommit is refused after such an abort. Until EndTransaction learns
the outcome, nothing reloads the producer ID, and ProducerID returns an
error. Previously, the retry reloaded the producer ID with a KIP-360
InitProducerID, which aborted the transaction, and then refused a
commit. The reload failed in two ways:

* Without KIP-890 part 2, if the lost EndTxn never reached the
  coordinator, the reload's abort cleared the epoch that the reload
  retries from, and Kafka fenced the retry with PRODUCER_FENCED.
* If another producer had taken over the transactional ID and opened a
  transaction, the reload aborted that producer's transaction: Kafka
  checks only the producer ID before it aborts an ongoing transaction.

A resent EndTxn that succeeds needs no reload, and kgo reports a commit
only then. An answer to the resend is as definitive as an answer to a
first attempt: INVALID_TXN_STATE fails the producer ID, and for a commit
the error says the commit did not happen. PRODUCER_FENCED leaves the
other producer's transaction open. If EndTransaction does not learn the
outcome of a resend either, the caller can call EndTransaction again.
After a commit EndTransaction did not learn the outcome of, the next
call resends the commit even if no partition is left in the transaction,
such as after a purge. After a commit EndTransaction did not learn the
outcome of, in a transaction whose topic was recreated, both TryCommit
and TryAbort are refused, and the error says to close the client.

GroupTransactSession.End now calls EndTransaction again with the same
TransactionEndTry after UNKNOWN_SERVER_ERROR while EndTransaction has
not learned the outcome, and reports a commit if the resent commit
succeeds. Previously, End retried a commit EndTransaction did not learn
the outcome of as an abort.

errReloadProducerID and errEndTxnUnconfirmed now live in errors.go, and
the EndTransaction doc is rewritten, with the retry rule as a list and
the list of errors BeginTransaction recovers from moved to
BeginTransaction's doc.

The new and changed test rows fail without the fix.
